name: Andalen Plantation
why_founding: Andalen Plantation was a House Dres saltrice enterprise. It had a great house, a drying floor, a counting room and a labour row. It was abandoned at the secession. The workers stopped work. The owning family never came back.
why_site_advantages: The plantation stands on prime saltrice ground beside slack water. It has a private landing for shipping the crop.
why_occupants_motive: The house stands unoccupied. People from the labour rows down the road work the fields. They take the crop off the land and stop at the drying floor.
why_pressures: The house is intact and unlooted after two centuries. Unnamed hands keep that arrangement in place. The field-holder says House Dres sees to it, but that claim cannot be true.
why_would_change_if: The house would be occupied once the field-holders decided the taboo was over. The house is worth more than the whole village.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the ex-Imperial agricultural belt
vibe_silhouette: The house is a two-storey Dunmer great house. A colonnaded drying floor stands beside it. The house stands whole and shuttered in the middle of worked fields.
vibe_palette: The stonework is Dres grey and the crop is saltrice green. The crop grows right up to the walls. The shutter paint has not been renewed since the secession.
vibe_materials: The house is built of cut basalt with Dunmer joinery, entirely unaltered. Nothing has been rebuilt in Argonian style.
vibe_signature_feature: The house is unlooted after two hundred years. The roof is sound. The shutters are unbroken. The fields are farmed up to the doorstep.
vibe_condition: The house is remarkably sound for a building that has been shut for two centuries.
vibe_mood: The field-holders avoid the house but do not call it haunted. They insist firmly on that distinction.
vibe_approach: The way in runs through worked fields towards the shut house. The field hands do not look up as visitors pass.
vibe_senses: Crop noise fills the fields on all sides. The noise drops away at the walls.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An unlooted Dunmer great house stands in worked fields. The counting room holds the records of who was owned here.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: TA03 · tier-2; LD37 · tier-3; PP06 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Andalen is a Dunmer plantation that failed with the crop still in the ground. The house ledgers name whose fault it was.

name: Bogmother
why_founding: Bogmother is a sacred site south-west of Stormhold. It has been ruined for centuries but is still kept. Moving the relics in it has never been proposed, because the relics are that old.
why_site_advantages: It lies at the far end of a stone causeway from Stormhold. The causeway was built to reach it.
why_occupants_motive: A few caretakers keep it swept and the relics in place. The city of Stormhold funds the caretakers. The city does this to avoid being seen letting the site go unkept.
why_pressures: Crocodiles have moved inside the threshold. The caretakers feed them on the days they sweep.
why_would_change_if: The site would be robbed if the caretakers left.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it
vibe_silhouette: Terraced stone stands half-sunk in bog. It is swept clean above the waterline and green below it. It has wide flooded courts.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone and black water. The caretakers wear white cloth. Green growth reaches up to the height of the flood.
vibe_materials: The terraces are built of old Argonian terrace stone. The caretakers bring brooms and cloth. They take the brooms and cloth back down the causeway.
vibe_signature_feature: The relics stand in place in an open chamber. The ruin has no door.
vibe_condition: The site has been ruined for centuries. The caretakers sweep it every morning.
vibe_mood: The mood is reverent. Crocodiles lie in the flooded courts.
vibe_approach: The causeway runs straight at the site over open bog. The terraces are visible for the last four hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear brooms sweeping the stone. Water is displaced by something large. Birds do not sing inside the walls.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The sacred ruin stands at the end of the causeway.
why_site_won: saddle in firm lowland (danger band 4), 327 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, region, parent.
player_purpose_hook: Bogmother is a stone xanmeer at the end of Stormhold's causeway. Pilgrims sweep the outer terraces. Crocodiles hold the flooded courts inside.

name: Broken Boom
why_founding: A field-owner's hired guard was stood down without pay at the end of a bad season. The guards walked as far as the channel boom. They took the keeper's lodge. The boom now opens for people who have settled with them.
why_site_advantages: The lodge stands on a firm bank within two hundred metres of the boom's anchor. The bank is high enough that the keeper is not flooded out.
why_occupants_motive: The guards levy what they were owed, one hull at a time. Their sergeant can quote the wage clause that gives her the right to collect.
why_pressures: Every boat crew in the district has stopped using the channel. The levy is falling. The guards stopped a Thorn factor's boat last month. They would not have done that in spring.
why_would_change_if: The gang would break up if the field-owners paid the arrears. The field-owners will not pay.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with a crossing, landing or light
vibe_silhouette: One stout house stands at the water with a horn-bracket on the gable. A winch platform stands at the water. No other building stands close.
vibe_palette: The timber is tarred black. The channel water is green. A brass horn gleams, polished daily as part of the keeper's duties.
vibe_materials: The timber is heavier than a village house uses. It was built to the boom's standard, which is Stormhold's.
vibe_signature_feature: A brass channel-horn hangs on the gable. Boat crews downstream know what one note from it means.
vibe_condition: The lodge is solid and isolated. It is over-built for one person.
vibe_approach: The boom first reads as a line on the water. The lodge is the small structure at one end of it.
vibe_senses: A winch pawl clicks. Water piles against timber. One horn note, rarely sounded, carries a long way.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The boom can be opened or refused. It is a route that travellers must negotiate.
why_site_won: headland in firm lowland (danger band 3), 11 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The boom only opens for boats that have settled with the men holding it. The men set the price on the day.

name: Branchmont
why_founding: Branchmont is an Archein saltrice estate south-west of Thorn. Its owners embezzled until the family ended. The estate was left as a village with no landlord.
why_site_advantages: It has the best saltrice ground outside Thorn's own fields. The ground is level. It can be flooded on demand.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers work the estate as their own. Three separate claimants say otherwise. One of the claimants is Dunmer.
why_pressures: The dispute has been in Thorn's title court for eleven years. The village has paid no rent in eleven years.
why_would_change_if: The dispute would be settled violently. That happens the first time a claimant arrives with armed men in place of papers.
siting_prefs_water_relation: controls a crossing or a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: holds the crossing that its neighbours must use
vibe_silhouette: A shuttered estate house stands empty. It stands in the middle of fields that are visibly worked.
vibe_palette: The saltrice crop is silver-green. The estate house is white going grey. The old worker rows have new thatch.
vibe_materials: The estate house is Archein masonry and unoccupied. The worker rows have been re-roofed and extended in reed.
vibe_signature_feature: The house is swept and shuttered. The house has no residents. The villagers maintain the house more carefully than their own houses.
vibe_condition: The fields are excellent. The rows are improved. The house is unchanged.
vibe_approach: The white house stands empty. It shows across flat fields for a kilometre.
vibe_senses: Water runs in the sluices. Work songs carry over the fields. The shutters of the empty house can be heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The contested estate village sends two sets of goods to the port under one seal. It pays two wages for the same day's work. That arrangement cannot last the season.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD93 · tier-3; LV16 · tier-3; LV17 · tier-3; LV18 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 165 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Branchmont is a contested estate village with two owners and one market. Both sides are hiring.

name: Breathes-Underneath
why_founding: Breathes-Underneath is a chamber under the Loriasel shelf. Air is trapped in its crown. The way in is a slot in the rock. The slot is a sump for two months a year and a squeeze for the rest of the year. It opens on an empty air chamber.
why_site_advantages: It is a limestone void with no drain out of it. Its own roof seals it. It has one opening, the width of a person.
why_occupants_motive: The divers who use the landing know about the chamber. The divers treat it as a test and not as a resource.
why_pressures: The slot floods in the monsoon. The divers argue about how long the crown's air lasts. Two people have tested it and one came back.
why_would_change_if: The chamber would become lethal if the slot silted. It is already frightening. The channel above the slot is silting.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a dry throat under a spring shelf
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: hidden; discovered by exploring water
vibe_silhouette: A slot in the rock lies above the shelf. Beyond it is a domed chamber. The air in the chamber is still and dead.
vibe_palette: The water is black. The underside of the air pocket is mercury-bright.
vibe_materials: The rock is bare wet limestone. No surface is worked. The rock is natural.
vibe_signature_feature: Divers surface inside solid rock. They surface in a room of trapped air.
vibe_condition: Bare rock, unchanged.
vibe_mood: The chamber has one way out. It is the size of a hut.
vibe_approach: The site has no approach. A marked slot lies in the shelf and leads to the water.
vibe_senses: The water around the slot is silent. Then breathing sounds in a small hard room.
quest_hooks_opportunity: This is a pure dive challenge. The air budget is survivable but finite.
why_site_won: spring head in border mountains (danger band 3), 1323 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: Divers dive under the rock and surface inside it. The chamber holds trapped air.

name: Buried Blades
why_founding: In 1E 2836 the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War overnight. In the north they buried the proof. A whole district's weapons were oiled, wrapped and put in one pit. Stopping the war could then not easily be undone.
why_site_advantages: The pit lies in a dry gravel lens under a low rise. It was chosen because the gravel drains. That is why the contents are still recognisable.
why_occupants_motive: No guard stands over the pit. Four villages have known where it is for sixteen hundred years. Children are told about the pit as they are told about the deep channel.
why_pressures: An-Xileel interest in the province's armament has made the pit awkward. One of the four villages has started asking what the other three would do.
why_would_change_if: Opening the pit would change the north's politics in a week. It has stayed shut for sixteen centuries.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a battlefield or a village of the period
vibe_silhouette: A low grassed rise has a single upright stone at one end. It has no other feature for four hundred metres.
vibe_palette: Grass grows over gravel and one upright stone is grey. If the turf is cut, wrapped iron shows black and oil-brown.
vibe_materials: The pit is lined with clay. The bundles are wrapped in oiled hide. The weapons were buried with care.
vibe_signature_feature: The bundles lie in courses on the clay floor. They are stacked square to the pit walls.
vibe_condition: The pit is undisturbed. The bundles are better preserved than sixteen centuries should allow.
vibe_approach: The site is a rise on a plain. It is easy to walk past.
vibe_senses: Silence lies over the rise. Wind moves in the grass.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A district's worth of weapons was buried on purpose. The An-Xileel want those weapons. It is a four-village secret with one member wavering.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 1044 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A whole district's weapons were buried in one pit when the Blackwater War stopped. The An-Xileel have begun asking where it is.

name: Channel Cross
why_founding: Two navigable channels cross here. Traffic stops. A village stands on the crossing itself.
why_site_advantages: The site is the junction of the trunk channel and the Bogmother feeder. Every boat in the district passes through it.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers earn their living from pilotage. The channels split into braided arms. Which arm is open changes with the season.
why_pressures: The pilots now charge one fee for the whole season. They used to charge for each trip. The boat crews call that a toll.
why_would_change_if: The village would be irrelevant if the pilots dredged and marked the braids properly.
siting_prefs_water_relation: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial
vibe_silhouette: A tall pilot's platform stands at the middle of a water crossroads. The village is built outward from it in four arms.
vibe_palette: Black water lies in four directions. Reed roofs cover the buildings. One raised platform carries a lamp.
vibe_materials: The buildings are stilt construction. One structure is built deliberately too tall. No other building in the district stands so high.
vibe_signature_feature: The pilot platform is high enough to see up all four channels at once.
vibe_condition: The village is sound. The platform is the best-maintained structure for kilometres.
vibe_approach: The platform lamp is visible up all four channels at night.
vibe_senses: Water sounds come from four directions. A horn sounds to summon pilots. Poles are heard at work.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The villagers of this tie-up village hear the boat gossip first. A lie planted here reaches four districts by morning. A ferry family will cross for any boat except one household's. The ferry family gives no reason.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV19 · tier-3; LV20 · tier-3; LV21 · tier-3
why_site_won: ford in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 446 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, hinterland, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-lightning-yard (+1.29).
player_purpose_hook: Every boat in the district ties up here. The walkway is where the district's news is traded.

name: Climbs-To-See
why_founding: The north marsh has no rises and no sightlines. The villages built a stack of platforms up a stand of trees. The platforms are high enough to show a flood a day before it arrives.
why_site_advantages: Three trunks stand close enough to brace against each other. The trunks stand on root mat that is firm enough to take the base frame.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages pay a flood-watcher through the wet season. Out of season, travellers climb the tower for the view.
why_pressures: The bracing between the trunks is the weak point. The trees move independently in wind. Two platforms have been rebuilt after storms in a decade.
why_would_change_if: The tower would be abandoned if one of the three trunks came down. Two trunks cannot brace the frame.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: placed where a viewshed pass shows a dead zone
vibe_silhouette: A lattice of platforms climbs three trunks and tapers as it rises. A small railed cage sits at the top above the leaves.
vibe_palette: The tower is green-black below the leaf line. Above the leaf line lie grey sky and silver water to the horizon.
vibe_materials: Lashed frames are braced between three living trunks. A rope hoist lifts loads that are heavier than a person.
vibe_signature_feature: Eleven metres of enclosed green lead up to a hatch. The hatch opens onto the top cage. The whole north marsh is visible from the top cage.
vibe_condition: The tower is rebuilt in patches. The top cage is the newest part of it.
vibe_mood: The tower feels workmanlike below the leaves. Wind is loud above the leaves.
vibe_approach: From the ground the tower looks like plain canopy. The structure can be read only from underneath, looking up.
vibe_senses: The frame creaks and sways. Insects are loud below the leaves and only wind sounds above. The hoist rope runs.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The top cage shows the north marsh as a landscape. A flood warning can be carried or suppressed.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 30 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, culture-clump, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: The place is a lashed tower up three trunks. The channel network is visible as a whole from the top cage.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at this position. The record sits on the Argonian marsh side of the region, where two zones interleave. The place is catalogued with the north. Its trade, levies and neighbours are northern.

name: Crystalgate
why_founding: Stormhold's crystal has to be cut, graded and sold outside the city. The city taxes what passes its gates.
why_site_advantages: The town stands on the road between the diggings and the Tear road. It stands at the first spring outside Stormhold's jurisdiction.
why_occupants_motive: The cutting houses are guild-like and hereditary. The town depends on a single trade.
why_pressures: The vicecanons want the cutting done inside the walls. They have tried tariffs twice.
why_would_change_if: The town would collapse into a road village if the Silyanorn seams ran out. The diggers say that is a generation away.
siting_prefs_water_relation: at its resource and its haul route
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: paired with a diggings, salt pans, clay pit or fishery
vibe_silhouette: The town is long low sheds that all face the same way. The sheds have north-facing window slots. A single tall grading hall stands among them.
vibe_palette: Blue-green crystal dust lies over the sheds. The sheds are shed-timber grey. One hall is whitewashed.
vibe_materials: The sheds are mud-brick and timber. All the sheds are built to one plan.
vibe_signature_feature: Every shed faces north for the light. The streets run parallel because of the orientation of the sheds.
vibe_condition: The town is purpose-built and well kept. It is monotonous by local standards.
vibe_mood: The town is insular. Dust hangs in the air at any hour.
vibe_approach: From the road above, the town reads as a grid of parallel roofs.
vibe_senses: Small chinking sounds run continuously. Water wheels turn. A grader calls grades aloud.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The town offers a graded, traceable crystal supply that can be entered, corrupted or audited. The hereditary craft guild has a succession problem. A strong room is worth robbing. The strong room has a guard who is better avoided than fought.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD66 · tier-3; LD67 · tier-3; LD68 · tier-3; LD69 · tier-3; LD70 · tier-3; LD71 · tier-3; LD72 · tier-3; LD73 · tier-3; LD74 · tier-3; LD75 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 609 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The cutting houses buy raw crystal and sell finished work. The cutting houses do not ask which digging produced the crystal.

name: Cut-And-Stack
why_founding: Peat is the only fuel in the north that is not brought from elsewhere. Peat banks are cut in the dry months and stacked to dry. Three villages with no timber worth burning work the banks.
why_site_advantages: The site is a raised bog on the plain edge. The bog is deep enough to cut for three generations. It is dry enough for stacking.
why_occupants_motive: The peat is fuel. A stack of turves is also a village's savings.
why_pressures: The cut face is a wall of exposed peat. In a dry year the face catches and burns underground for months. It has done that twice. The strips exist because of those fires.
why_would_change_if: The place would be abandoned as too dangerous if a fire reached a stack. A fire that reaches only a face does not end the cutting.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the burn country, or supplying a village's fires
vibe_silhouette: A stepped brown face two metres high runs a hundred metres across a bog. Stacked turves lie in herringbone rows behind the face.
vibe_palette: The colours are peat brown-black, stack shadow and the pale straw of the cut-strip boundaries.
vibe_materials: The stacks are turves built from the peat that is being cut.
vibe_signature_feature: Unworked baulks of peat stand between the faces and break up the cut. The baulks are firebreaks. They were left after two years of underground fire.
vibe_condition: The bog is actively worked in the dry season. It holds standing water in the wet season.
vibe_mood: The work is laborious and sooty. The cutters are proud of the strip system.
vibe_approach: From a distance the stacks look like a village. Close up they are rows of drying turf.
vibe_senses: Spades strike wet peat. The bog has a silence of its own. Smoke smells of earth and not of wood.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Three villages depend on this fuel supply. A fire can be started in the peat.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 133 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-freed-rows (+0.77).
player_purpose_hook: The crew cuts peat and dries fuel. The crew trades peat and fuel for news from the road.

name: Cut-In-The-Wall
why_founding: The Stormhold ravine system has more wall than floor. Households left unhoused by the terraced city cut their own dwellings into the face of a side ravine. The dwellings lie outside the walls and outside the rents.
why_site_advantages: A soft band in the ravine wall is easy to cut. The band lies above the wet-season torrent. The city's lights are visible round the bend.
why_occupants_motive: Residents pay no rent here. The residents call the place a neighbourhood. The surveys of the vicecanons call it an encroachment.
why_pressures: The vicecanons twice sent surveyors to learn whether the cuttings lie within the city's boundary. Both surveyors were treated hospitably. Both reports were inconclusive.
why_would_change_if: Once a survey came back conclusive, the city would take the place inside its boundary and tax it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: commands a stretch of river; the corridor's signature settlement
vibe_silhouette: Two dozen square-cut openings lie in a ravine wall on three levels. Cut ledges join the levels. Laundry lines run between the levels.
vibe_palette: The rock is wet grey. The shuttered fronts are warm brown. Washing strung across the gorge adds bright colour.
vibe_materials: The chambers are rock-cut with timber fronts. All the load-bearing timber was scavenged.
vibe_signature_feature: Each level has a continuous cut walkway that is wide enough for two. Rails have been added where children have fallen.
vibe_condition: The cuttings are sound. A new opening is usually being cut somewhere along the wall.
vibe_approach: From the ravine floor a whole neighbourhood shows overhead. From the rim there is no sign of it.
vibe_senses: Voices arrive from above. Water runs in the ravine below. A cutter taps while cutting a new room.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Residents of the neighbourhood pay no rent. The city cannot decide whether it owns the neighbourhood. It is a vertical residential district that is reached by ledge and ladder.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD11 · tier-3; LV48 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 847 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, hinterland, danger.
player_purpose_hook: Houses are cut into the ravine wall below Stormhold. They offer a bed, a fire and the city's lights round the bend.

name: Draws-The-Herds
why_founding: When the northern plain under the rim dries, every animal walks to the same three tree-islands for water. For two months this ground holds more wild animals than anywhere else in the region. Predators and hunters follow the herds.
why_site_advantages: Three spring-fed pools hold the last standing water on the plain. The pools lie under tree cover at the foot of the rim. They do not fail in a normal dry year.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages hunt the ground under an allocation. They renegotiate the allocation every year at Wolk Market. The four villages settle their other disputes in the same week.
why_pressures: A long dry year concentrates the herds harder. Then the allocation stops holding. The last time it failed, two villages did not speak for a decade.
why_would_change_if: If the springs failed, the villages' year would end as they organise it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: the last water in a drying landscape
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the region's ecological engine; villages time their year on it
vibe_silhouette: Out of season the site is three ordinary tree stands on a wet plain. In season the ground is bare and trodden for two hundred metres around them. A haze of dust and birds hangs over it in season.
vibe_palette: Out of season the site is green and grey. In season it is dust ochre with churned black mud at the pools. In season there is a great deal of movement.
vibe_materials: The only structures are the hunting stands of four villages. The villages put up the stands and take them down each year.
vibe_signature_feature: Bare ground, the trodden ring, extends two hundred metres around the pools. The pools hold water for two months of the year.
vibe_condition: The site is unbuilt. Between seasons a bare ring and a line of post-holes for the stands remain.
vibe_mood: In season this is the most dangerous ground in the north.
vibe_approach: The smell of the site carries further than the sight of it. The birds above it show for kilometres.
vibe_senses: Out of season the site is quiet. In season the animals make an unbroken noise. Silence falls intermittently when a predator moves.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The north's year depends on the two months of the dry season. An allocation dispute has a hunting ground under it.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1457 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-tear-wreck (+0.38).
player_purpose_hook: In the dry months every animal on the plain comes to these three pools. The predators that follow the animals come too.
siting_note: The region raster reads the northern rim basin as 'border mountains'. The classification of the rim covers the lake and fen floor inside it. The water identity of the record and the raster class describe the same ground.

name: Dreams-By-The-Ash
why_founding: Dreams-By-The-Ash is a wallow and a hut on the Dunmer frontier. An Argonian rite is practised there. Dunmer clients now attend the Argonian rite. The holdings' people come for visions that their own tradition does not offer. Dunmer clients pay better than the villages do.
why_site_advantages: The site is a warm seep in an ash-fall hollow. Ash keeps the trees in the hollow low. The hollow is dark and quiet within twenty paces of the rim.
why_occupants_motive: One keeper runs the wallow. The keeper is wealthy. Neither the Argonians nor the Dunmer have forgiven her wealth.
why_pressures: The holdings' elders disapprove of the rite. The holdings' children attend the rite anyway. The nearest Argonian village calls the arrangement a sale of something unsellable.
why_would_change_if: The village would close the wallow if the keeper took a Dunmer apprentice. The holdings would not close the wallow.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a short walk from a village, out of its sight
vibe_silhouette: The site is a grey ash hollow. One reed hut stands on the rim. A fenced wallow of pale warm mud lies at the bottom.
vibe_palette: The ground is ash grey. The warm mud is a shade paler than the ash. A single red Dunmer client's cloak hangs on the fence.
vibe_materials: The hut is built of reed in an ash hollow. The building is Argonian on ground that looks like Morrowind's.
vibe_signature_feature: The fence rail is the signature feature. Clients leave a token on the rail. Half of the clients are Argonian and half are Dunmer.
vibe_condition: The wallow is simple and kept. It is better provisioned than a village keeper's would be.
vibe_mood: The wallow is quiet and lucrative. Both cultures disapprove of it.
vibe_approach: The hollow comes into view suddenly in flat ash country. Noise fades on the way down into the hollow.
vibe_senses: Visitors feel ash underfoot and warm mud. Two languages are whispered at different times of day.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A rite is sold across the cultural line. Two communities object to the sale.
why_site_won: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 1004 m from the nearest route; won on culture-clump, hinterland, danger.
player_purpose_hook: The warm seep can be used for sleep. The keeper reads the dream back. Her clients are Dunmer as often as Argonian.

name: Dry-Under-Water
why_founding: Dry-Under-Water is a second air pocket in the drowned terrace's undercroft. The air pocket is big enough to hold a standing diver. It is dry enough for storage. The divers' landing uses it as a store. The store can be reached only by divers. Land travellers cannot reach it.
why_site_advantages: The site is a xanmeer undercroft. Its vault held when the terrace sank. The room has a floor above the water line.
why_occupants_motive: The divers keep salvage here between lifts. A store that needs a dive to reach is safe from robbers.
why_pressures: The vault is holding. The terrace above the vault is failing. Every season more of the ceiling falls to the floor.
why_would_change_if: The divers would give up the store if a lift brought up ceiling. The older divers say such a lift is overdue.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: hidden; discovered by exploring water
vibe_silhouette: Only a marked buoy shows from above. Below it, a doorway opens in a submerged wall. A lit room lies behind the doorway.
vibe_palette: The passage has green underwater light. The room has lamp-yellow light. The xanmeer stone is pale grey.
vibe_materials: The walls are worked xanmeer block, dry above the water line. The divers have laid a plank floor over the silt.
vibe_signature_feature: The room is a warehouse reached by swimming. It holds crates, a lamp shelf and a tally board. The room can be reached only by water.
vibe_condition: The vault is sound. Ceiling stone is falling. The divers' fittings are new.
vibe_mood: The room has a businesslike air. It serves no natural business use.
vibe_approach: The route runs from a buoy, through a dive and a doorway, to air.
vibe_senses: Water laps inside a stone room. A lamp burns there. The room has the echo of a vaulted store.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The cache can only be reached by swimming. Only a diver can rob it.
player_purpose_hook: The site is a dry room under a drowned terrace. It can only be reached by diving. Divers use it as a store and do not trust their neighbours on land.
siting_note: Dry-Under-Water is held in reserve. Its identity is a vault under The Drowned Terrace. It cannot fill an off-route gap elsewhere. The note is dated 2026-09-04.

name: Feeds-The-North
why_founding: Feeds-The-North is a deep bend where the northern river slows. Fish hold in the bend. It is the most productive water in the region. Four villages' boats work it. All four villages have argued over it for longer than living memory records.
why_site_advantages: The site is a scoured hole below a gravel shoulder. The hole is deep and cold. It reliably holds fish. No other water in the north matches it.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages depend on the water for food. Three of those villages stand where they do because of it. The boats work it in a rotation held in memory. Every crew can recite the rotation.
why_pressures: The rotation has held for generations. Stormhold's market buyers pay for volume. The buyers do not ask whose week it is.
why_would_change_if: The water would be fished out in three seasons if the rotation broke. Every fisher on it knows the number.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: contested between two coastal settlements
vibe_silhouette: The site is open brown water with a gravel shoulder on one side. Four villages' floats mark it in four colours. Most mornings six boats work there.
vibe_palette: The river is brown and the gravel is pale. Boat crews read the four float colours at four hundred metres.
vibe_materials: Floats and a marker post mark the shoulder. The weeks are cut into the post.
vibe_signature_feature: The signature feature is a stake on the bank. The rotation is cut into the stake in notches. It is the nearest thing to written law on this river.
vibe_condition: Crews fish the water hard. Fish stocks are steady. Every crew on the water keeps a lookout.
vibe_mood: The water is busy. The crews watch the other villages' boats.
vibe_approach: Floats show before the water is deep enough to matter. The boats keep their distance.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear oars and nets going over. Fishers from four villages do not talk to each other.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A common resource has an unwritten rota. A buyer is breaking the rota.
why_site_won: cove in firm lowland (danger band 3), 200 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: It is the deepest hole in the northern water. It is seldom empty. A stake on the bank carries the four villages' rotation.

name: Anachronistic Library
why_founding: The library is a collection inside an Ayleid tomb. It holds books written long after the tomb was sealed. Books are still being added to it.
why_site_advantages: The library is the deepest dry chamber of the fenlord's complex. Paper survives nowhere else in the north.
why_occupants_motive: The shelves stand unattended. The collection is still catalogued. The catalogue hand changes every few centuries.
why_pressures: The Conclave of Baal at Stormhold reads the Elder Scrolls with a tablet. The tablet is older than the Conclave. The tablet's provenance traces to the library.
why_would_change_if: The library would be the most valuable room in the province. That holds only if its books could be carried out.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a ruin, or in a northern city
vibe_silhouette: The library is a dry vaulted room of shelves. Blue light fills the room. The books come from every century, including this one.
vibe_palette: Welkynd blue light falls on white stone. The bindings are leather. The paper should have rotted four thousand years ago.
vibe_materials: The Ayleid shelving is cut from the wall itself. The complex is Ayleid throughout, except for the books.
vibe_signature_feature: The catalogue is continuously maintained. Several hands have written it. The most recent entry is very recent.
vibe_condition: The library is bone dry. It stands in a building in a fen.
vibe_approach: Visitors reach the library last, through the flooded levels.
vibe_senses: The library is entirely free of water sound.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The hook concerns the tablet's provenance. It also concerns the Conclave's source.
why_site_won: cliff bench in border mountains (danger band 3), 1491 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, bound.
player_purpose_hook: The library is a room in the north where paper survived. What it says about the Duskfall is in no other book.

name: Gandranen Ruins
why_founding: Gandranen Ruins is a Barsaebic Ayleid fenlord's tomb. Undead guard the tomb. Books have kept arriving in its library since the tomb was sealed.
why_site_advantages: The tomb is sunk in fen on the least accessible ground near Stormhold. The fenlord chose privacy.
why_occupants_motive: The dead still hold the office they held. No living claimant has taken their place.
why_pressures: Books keep arriving. How they arrive remains unexplained. The Conclave at Stormhold has sent three parties. None of the three parties has published a report.
why_would_change_if: The Synod would prize the tomb if an agent proved the collection movable.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a Barsaebic compound
vibe_silhouette: White Ayleid stonework rises out of black fen water. Half of it is below the surface. The whole structure is lit from inside.
vibe_palette: The colours are bone white, welkynd blue and black water.
vibe_materials: The masonry is Barsaebic Ayleid and the lighting is welkynd. Both are entirely intact. It is the best-preserved Ayleid work in the province.
vibe_signature_feature: The lit windows are the signature feature. The tomb has been lit inside without interruption for four thousand years.
vibe_condition: The structure is perfect. The lowest level is completely submerged.
vibe_approach: The blue light on the water is visible at night for six hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear water against stone. The welkynd stones hum. A second set of footsteps sounds in step with the visitor's.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1421 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: The site is a fenlord's tomb sunk in the fen. Its own dead guard it. The library below it is still dry.
siting_note: The northern rim basin reads 'border mountains' on the region raster. The rim's classification covers the lake and fen floor inside it. The record's water identity and the raster class describe the same ground.

name: Greylight
why_founding: A Hist stands at Greylight, so a village stands there. The north's Hist are fewer and further apart than the interior's. That makes each northern Hist political.
why_site_advantages: Greylight stands on a firm hummock in the Shadowfen channels. No other firm hummock lies within half a day.
why_occupants_motive: The village mediates for four water-villages. Those four villages have no tree of their own. The mediation gives Greylight standing among them.
why_pressures: Stormhold's officials want the tree's sanction for things on which the tree holds no opinion. Stormhold's gifts arrive twice a year regardless.
why_would_change_if: The village would not move, because a Hist village does not. Its politics could change in a season.
siting_prefs_water_relation: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage
vibe_silhouette: A pale crown stands over the channel canopy. Four landing stages surround the hummock beneath it. Each stage serves one village.
vibe_palette: The colours are Hist grey-white and channel black. The four mooring posts carry four different carvings.
vibe_materials: The buildings are mud and wattle roofed in reed. Each of the four stages is built in a visiting village's own style.
vibe_signature_feature: The four stages are the signature feature. Which stages are maintained shows which villages still speak to Greylight.
vibe_condition: The village is rebuilt on the usual cycle. The stages vary widely in condition.
vibe_approach: The crown is visible over the canopy from the channels at a kilometre.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear poles arriving and the uxith. Four dialects are spoken on one hummock.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Hist here will answer an outsider. People pay outsiders to ask on their behalf. The village minders forbid a stretch of drowned ruin that they cannot patrol.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LQ26 · tier-3; LV22 · tier-3; LV23 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 455 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Greylight is firm ground, with none other for half a day. The Hist here will take a stranger's question.

name: Hackwing Wall
why_founding: Hackwing Wall is a cliff above the channel. Carrion birds roost there in hundreds. The village below keeps the roost. The village puts its dead animals out for the birds. In return it gets a clean bone-yard.
why_site_advantages: The wall faces south and has ledges at every height. It is warm in the afternoon. It stands above water that is left unfarmed anyway.
why_occupants_motive: The village feeds the roost deliberately. The birds dispose of carcasses. The birds warn of anyone on the ridge path. Villagers have used the birds as a weapon twice.
why_pressures: Travellers on the ridge path who do not know the arrangement have been badly frightened. Some of those travellers were injured.
why_would_change_if: The roost would empty in a season if the village stopped putting carcasses out. The village would then have to bury things.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: downwind of a lair, a battlefield or a midden
vibe_silhouette: The cliff is a hundred metres high. Droppings have whitened it. Ledges run from top to bottom. Large birds circulate slowly above it permanently.
vibe_palette: The rock is grey under white streaking. The birds are dull brown-black. The feeding ledge at the base is red.
vibe_materials: The feeding ledge stands alone as a built structure. It is a low stone shelf at the foot of the wall. It is swept clean between carcasses.
vibe_signature_feature: The feeding ledge and its bell are the signature feature. The keeper rings the bell when a carcass is put out. The birds come off the wall together.
vibe_condition: The site is kept. The whitening is fresh. The ledge is swept.
vibe_approach: The wall is audible from the last bend. The road runs directly beneath it.
vibe_senses: Several hundred birds shift at once. The bell rings out. Wingbeats sound directly overhead.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The village maintains a hazard on purpose. Any traveller who reaches the bell can ring it.
why_site_won: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 2), 70 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The village feeds its dead animals to the birds on this wall. Walking under the wall unannounced makes the birds come down.

name: Hatching Pools
why_founding: Hatching Pools is the regional hatchery. It was rebuilt after Umbriel. It was also rebuilt once before Umbriel, after a massacre. The counting stones record the massacre but do not date it. A depopulating province cannot let the hatchery lapse.
why_site_advantages: The pools are warm shallows at a constant temperature. They are screened on every side. They were found, not dug.
why_occupants_motive: The Keepers of the Shell stay so that each generation is born. Some Keepers have died at the pools and did not leave.
why_pressures: Hatching Pools has been attacked twice in living memory. The Keepers defend it heavily. Outsiders are not welcome at the pools. A woman with a name in the roll can vouch for an outsider.
why_would_change_if: Losing Hatching Pools would be the greatest loss that the north could suffer. It is the most defended site in the province outside the cities.
siting_prefs_water_relation: warm still water, no flood risk
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: serves 4-8 villages; approaches watched
vibe_silhouette: A stockade of stakes surrounds a bowl of steaming pale-green pools. Low sheds stand on the rim. No structure here stands taller than a stake.
vibe_palette: The colours are pool jade-green, steam white, stockade black and shell pale.
vibe_materials: The stockade is made of pikes. The sheds are built of mud and reed. The pools themselves are untouched ground.
vibe_signature_feature: Counting stones stand on the rim, with one stone for each clutch. The stones go back further than the current stockade. One course of stones is cut differently. That course marks a year with no clutches at all.
vibe_condition: The stockade was rebuilt twice within living memory. Each course of stakes belongs to a different rebuild.
vibe_mood: The mood is reverent and guarded. The pools hold their heat all night, so the place is warm.
vibe_approach: Wardens stop visitors a long way out. A warden meets visitors first.
vibe_senses: The water is at blood heat. Steam rises from the pools. A constant low chorus sounds across the water. The chorus is not frogs.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Hatching Pools is the regional hatchery. The Keepers of the Shell run the hatchery.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ04 · tier-0; MR02 · tier-2; LV24 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 44 m from the nearest route; no free 'spring-head' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: The Keepers guard the warm shallows at the pools. A stranger is admitted when a member named in the roll vouches for them.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at this position. The record sits on the region's Argonian marsh side, where two zones interleave. The place is catalogued with the north. Its trade, its levies and its neighbours are northern.

name: Hissmir
why_founding: Hissmir exists to receive comers that it may not refuse. The Trials of the Burnished Scales reconnect the Hist-less. The trials are open to lukiul, exiles and non-Argonians.
why_site_advantages: Hissmir stands on firm ground at the head of a pilgrim water route in Shadowfen. It is deliberately reachable, because its function depends on being easy to find.
why_occupants_motive: Trial marshals and stewards administer the trials and do not defend the town. The Zaht stones of Hist amber do the defending. The Hist has not made a new Zaht stone in four hundred years.
why_pressures: The lodging was built for traffic that the town no longer has. The Mages and Fighters Guild halls that housed pilgrims were dissolved in the Fourth Era. Their dormitories now hold people who came for a trial and stayed.
why_would_change_if: The An-Xileel could declare the trials invalid. The province's only route back to a Hist would then close. Every Hist-less settlement in the north would have nowhere to send its own.
vibe_silhouette: Hissmir is a low town. Its lodging blocks are three times the size of its houses. A walled Hist stands behind the lodging blocks.
vibe_palette: The colours are amber Zaht stone and wet green-black canopy. Pale mud render and faded foreign heraldry complete the palette.
vibe_materials: The houses are mud and wattle over xanmeer footings. The trial stones are Hist amber. The imported guild-hall masonry has gone green.
vibe_signature_feature: Dead foreign guild insignia of the Mages and Fighters still hang over the dormitory doors. Argonian pilgrims who failed the trial sleep under them.
vibe_condition: The town of Hissmir is kept maintained. It is visibly over-built for its population.
vibe_approach: The trial ground comes before the village. It is waymarked and watched. It lies out in bad water.
vibe_senses: Chant is counted in sets. The air is sap-sweet. Boots dry in rows.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Root Stewards cannot refuse a comer. The remedy that LW01 needs comes on a certificate that the registry will not accept. The Trials of the Burnished Scales are a three-day ordeal. The ordeal has a physical route through it.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LW01 · tier-2; LD76 · tier-3; LD77 · tier-3; LD78 · tier-3; LD79 · tier-3; LD80 · tier-3; LD81 · tier-3; LD82 · tier-3; LD83 · tier-3; LD84 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 419 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: Hissmir is the pilgrims' first firm ground. It offers beds and a trial to enter. Every steward here has walked the route themselves.
singular_claim: Hissmir has countBand [1,1]. The lore names a single settlement whose institution is the Trials of the Burnished Scales.

name: Hixinoag
why_founding: Hixinoag is the province's one drifting village. It is a jumble of huts half-sunk in mud. The mud moves with the flood cycle along the northern caravan route.
why_site_advantages: The village occupies two or three fixed moorings in turn. Each mooring is good at a different water level.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers move because moving is cheaper than repairing. Being hard to find has also been good for them.
why_pressures: Caravans that miss the mooring lose a day. The village charges a day's worth to guide caravans to the mooring.
why_would_change_if: The village would settle permanently only if one mooring became good in every season. The hydrology forbids that.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: its moorings are on a caravan or boat route
vibe_silhouette: Forty huts are jammed together at whatever angle the mud allowed. The huts are half-sunk. The mooring posts of the last site stand empty two hours away.
vibe_palette: Everything is mud brown. The only colour comes from the roof thatch, most of it askew.
vibe_materials: The huts are mud and reed, built to be abandoned. They use rope lashings only, with no fixed joints.
vibe_signature_feature: The empty mooring has posts, flattened ground and hearth rings. It stands on its own when the village is elsewhere.
vibe_condition: The huts are deliberately shoddy. Nothing is built to outlast one move.
vibe_approach: Travellers are told where the village was last moored. Finding it is the travellers' own work.
vibe_senses: Mud sucks at feet. The huts settle audibly. The villagers talk a great deal.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Hixinoag is a village that actually moves. It uses two or three fixed moorings.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD84 · tier-3; LV49 · tier-3; tier-0 protected
why_site_won: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 47 m from the nearest route; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, ring.
player_purpose_hook: The village moves with the water level. When it is found at the right mooring, it carries a passenger onward.

name: Hutan-Tzel
why_founding: Hutan-Tzel is an old tribal village on the Panther River. It stands where the river drains into its basin. It holds the western approach to the north. It has its own tribe and its own elder naheesh. The xanmeer Xal Irasotl stands close enough to be the tribe's charge.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on the basin edge. It has still water for the village and running water for the trip downstream. A rock shelf stands above every flood on record. The Imperial maps call the place Rockguard after the shelf.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe stays because the Hist speaks here. The totem line is the tribe's to keep. The tribe has dealt carefully with outsiders since the 2E. Few interior tribes deal with outsiders at all.
why_pressures: Tampering with the rune-carved totems attracts dangerous things. Outsiders tamper with the totems. The tribe has a 3E rivalry with Glenbridge across the fringe. In bad years the rivalry costs the tribe a season's trade. The tribe takes in Su-Zahleel survivors who fled the Xit-Xaht. It takes them in without making them kin.
why_would_change_if: The village would close to outsiders entirely. That would follow the first meddled totem that killed a villager. The western approach would close with it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on the basin where the river slows, with a rock shelf above the flood
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: first friendly village on the western approach; its xanmeer lies 300-600 m off and is watched, not entered
vibe_silhouette: A Hist stands over a low village on a rock shelf. A ring of carved posts stands further out than the houses.
vibe_palette: The colours are river brown, shelf grey and the red Hist flower. The cut faces of the totems are paler than the wood around them. The tribe recuts the totems every year.
vibe_materials: The village is reed and mud on a stone shelf. Crocodile skulls hang on the totems. No quarried block is used in the village. The xanmeer's stone is left where it stands.
vibe_signature_feature: The rune line is a row of posts carved in a script that the tribe reads. No other village reads the script. The gaps between posts are as deliberate as the posts. Every creature in the basin goes round the line.
vibe_condition: The village has been kept without a break for centuries. The houses are young. The totems are the old part.
vibe_mood: The villagers are watchful and courteous. They expect to talk to strangers.
vibe_approach: The totem line stands a full two minutes out from the first house. The villagers let arrivals wait there.
vibe_senses: The basin's frogs chirp. The vossa-satl copies the chirp. Recut wood gives off its smell. The low note of the Hist carries in the water, not the air.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Hutan-Tzel is the first friendly interior village on the western approach. Its speaking tribal Hist is reachable without a city's permission. Rune totems punish tampering. A visitor can cause that hazard.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ04 · tier-0; LV25 · tier-3; LV26 · tier-3; LV27 · tier-3
why_site_won: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 3), 230 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, region, landform.
player_purpose_hook: Still water lies on one side and running water on the other. Boats leave downstream every morning.

name: Keeps-The-Second-Hammock
why_founding: Keeps-The-Second-Hammock is the north marsh's second tree hammock. It is half the size of the first hammock and twice as awkward. Its settlers could not get standing room on the first hammock. They have been defined by that for three generations.
why_site_advantages: The ground is a thin cap of soil over root mat. The soil is dry most years. The hammock is out of the first hammock's line of sight. Its people consider that an advantage.
why_occupants_motive: The islanders rent nothing and admit no outsiders. That is a policy, not a shortage. The islanders say so themselves.
why_pressures: The soil cap is thin and the burials are shallow. The hammock floods about one year in seven. When it floods, the islanders have to ask for help.
why_would_change_if: The islanders would give up the policy the second time it floods in a decade. The islanders of the first hammock are counting the floods too.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a lower hammock, wet underfoot most of the year
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a local centre; neighbours come here in flood
vibe_silhouette: The hammock is a smaller, scrappier dome of trees. Roofs are built up into the branches, not under them. There is no landing stage at all.
vibe_palette: The marsh grey is the same as at the first hammock. The green is thinner and yellower. No pale ground is visible anywhere. Soil is never seen here.
vibe_materials: The houses are reed and lashed timber carried up into branch forks. The ground is left for the dead and the water.
vibe_signature_feature: No villager lives at ground level. The whole village is two to five metres up. The soil below is a graveyard. The houses stand over the graveyard.
vibe_condition: The village is improvised and well maintained. It is poorer than the first hammock.
vibe_mood: The islanders are prickly. They have a long memory for a refusal.
vibe_approach: Arrivals wade the last thirty metres because there is no stage. The islanders watch them wade.
vibe_senses: Everything in the village is overhead. Ladders connect the houses. Water lies underfoot where a village floor should be.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The village has no ground floor. It is an entirely climbed settlement. It has a three-generation grudge with a visible physical cause.
player_purpose_hook: The smaller hammock rents nothing and admits no outsiders. The islanders say so at length before a visitor has asked.

name: The Let Upper Floor
why_founding: The Let Upper Floor is a rented upper floor over the counting room of a Velothi factor. The counting room is on the Tear road. A party whom the landlord has not met took the floor on a three-year lease. The Dominion keeps no post in Black Marsh. The Thalmor are still one of the standing explanations for the Accession War.
why_site_advantages: The room overlooks the weighbridge on the Morrowind road. Every cart off the Morrowind road is broken open and counted there. A tenant can count northern traffic in ore, saltrice and people through a shuttered window. The tenant need not leave the room.
why_occupants_motive: The tenant wants to know what the An-Xileel are moving north before Morrowind does. The room can be emptied in an hour if a step sounds on the stair.
why_pressures: The landlord's grandson resents the tenant. The tenant pays a year in advance. The tenant burns a lamp all night. The grandson has tried the door twice.
why_would_change_if: An hour's warning empties the room completely. The lease is in a dead Dunmer's name. The ledgers are in wax. Only a cold lamp and a good chair would be left in the room.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: The place stands inside another owner's working building, on a trunk road.
vibe_silhouette: The building is an ordinary two-storey Velothi counting house on the road. One upper window stays shuttered. The outside stair is used after dark.
vibe_palette: The lower walls are ash-grey render and bitumen-black timber. Above, one warm slot of lamplight shows behind the shutters. The lamplight is visible only from the weighbridge side.
vibe_materials: The walls are rendered chitin-and-ash brick. The shutters are bitumen-sealed. The room has a bare boarded floor and a stack of wax tablets. It holds one very good chair that the factor's household could never afford.
vibe_signature_feature: The chair cost far more than everything else in the room. It stands where a person can watch the weighbridge all day unseen.
vibe_condition: The room is immaculate and impersonal. It is cleaner than the rest of the house.
vibe_approach: Most traffic walks straight past the building. It stands on the road out of Morrowind. Its shutters are closed like every window on either side.
vibe_senses: The room smells of lamp oil where cooking should be. It has no smell of a person, though a person plainly lives on the floor.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A foreign account of northern traffic exists that the Dominion keeps off any register. The lease is in a dead Dunmer's name. The payer behind the lease is unknown.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 87 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The room is a rented upper room over the weighbridge at Stormhold. Its shutter gives a count of every cart out of Morrowind.

name: Sings-Under-Water
why_founding: Lamias hold the flooded caverns beneath Loriasel. Loriasel is a Barsaebic Ayleid site raised to the Ten Ancestors. The nest is older than the local memory of it. The ruin above is the reason the cavern was opened at all.
why_site_advantages: The system is spring-fed and lies under Ayleid foundations. It is half-flooded and has one dry mouth. The dry mouth is the only way in that a person can use.
why_occupants_motive: The lamias form a nest. The nest sings. The nest is not a person. The lamias keep everything they take in one heap.
why_pressures: Antiquarians keep reaching the ruin above the caverns. They keep hearing the singing come up through the floor. The count of those who went down is kept at the mouth.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the nest would open an Ayleid undercroft that is still unrobbed. The undercroft stays unrobbed until the nest is cleared.
vibe_silhouette: The cavern mouth is black and sits under white Ayleid footings. Water stands three steps inside the mouth.
vibe_palette: The Ayleid stone above is bone-white. The water below is green-black. One cold blue mineral glow lights the place.
vibe_materials: The materials are Ayleid block, ship's timber and standing water. The lamias drag bone in as nest material.
vibe_signature_feature: The victims' effects are sorted, with boots beside boots and buckles beside buckles. The lamias sort them without understanding their use.
vibe_condition: The nest is undisturbed. Every sorted effect lies where the lamias left it.
vibe_mood: A singing nest sits in standing water.
vibe_approach: The singing is heard at the ruin above before the stair is found.
vibe_senses: The singing carries up through stone. The air off the water is cold. The bone is wet.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A flooded Ayleid system lies beneath the citadel. The system is a dive dungeon. A Barsaebic inscription lies at the bottom.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 653 m from the nearest route; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, remote; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: The Ayleid system is half-flooded and has one dry mouth. Something in it sings under the water.
singular_claim: countBand [1,1] marks the cavern as unique. The lore places lamia caverns at Loriasel specifically. The lore places them at no other site in the province.

name: Mazzatun
why_founding: The Xit-Xaht built in stone against the Duskfall prohibition. A Hist directed the building. The Xit-Xaht had enslaved that Hist with sap.
why_site_advantages: Mazzatun lies deep in the north-east swamp. The surrounding tribes avoid the ground. Rootland screens it. What the neighbours say about the place screens it too.
why_occupants_motive: Tsono-Xuhil has not woken from its convalescent sleep. Three and a half centuries later, the Amber Plasm seep has resumed. The Xit-Xaht restarted the building along with the seep.
why_pressures: The neighbours say only 'the Hist is crazy' and stay away. Three centuries of that talk have not stopped the building.
why_would_change_if: It would become a province-wide emergency if another tribe accepted the Xit-Xaht's invitation to help.
siting_prefs_water_relation: stone source and a haul water
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: raids its neighbours for labour
vibe_silhouette: A city is being built out of stone in a province that stopped building. Scaffolds and half-cut blocks fill the site. A great tree at the centre carries tubes.
vibe_palette: The stone is wet green-black. The sap is amber. The workers look sick and pale.
vibe_materials: The materials are cut stone and cane scaffolding. The sap conduits are hollowed root. No other Argonian settlement in the province uses that technique.
vibe_signature_feature: The conduits are amber tubes running from the Hist into the works. They feed the labour and do not feed the tree.
vibe_condition: The city is under construction, three and a half centuries late. The mortar in the newest courses is a decade old.
vibe_mood: The mood is industrious. The work goes on through the night shift in silence.
vibe_approach: The sound of stone being cut carries a long way through the swamp. The province has not heard that noise since the Duskfall.
vibe_senses: Chisels ring. The conduits drip wetly. The workers do not talk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Hist is enslaved and the building is a stone heresy. The building has resumed.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV28 · tier-3; LV29 · tier-3; LV30 · tier-3; tier-0 protected
why_site_won: Pinned by the Part 6 meso siting (world/sources/blueprints/place.dunmer-north.mazzatun.json): The rock shelf at the ridge end: 68 m x 42 m of ground between 198.3 m and 209 m, falling ~8.5 m north to south in three readable steps, flood band 0, 4.1 m above the water table, a headwater stream along its southern lip and a 55 m escarpment on the east. 85 m from Tsono-Xuhil and 296 m from the Gideon-Stormhold road. Every parcel measured on this ground fits the slope ladder at plinth, pad or dug-in; none needs a graded pad over 2 m.
player_purpose_hook: The Xit-Xaht build in stone. They welcome visitors in to help.

name: Tsono-Xuhil
why_founding: Sap coerced a Hist into directing a city's construction. The Hist was left in a convalescent sleep. It has not woken from that sleep.
why_site_advantages: Tsono-Xuhil stands where it always stood. The Xit-Xaht built the city around the Hist.
why_occupants_motive: The Xit-Xaht tend the Hist as a farmer tends a crop. The Xit-Xaht call their tending devotion.
why_pressures: The Amber Plasm seep has resumed, slowly. Either the Hist is healing or it is dreaming again.
why_would_change_if: The whole north would change if the Hist woke. A mnemic egg here might show whether it is healing or dreaming.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village
vibe_silhouette: The Hist has a vast crown, greyer than a Hist should be. Amber runs down its bark in fixed channels.
vibe_palette: The bark is sick grey with amber. The canopy is thinner than the trees around it.
vibe_materials: The place is made of the tree and the tubes that run out of it.
vibe_signature_feature: An amber egg sits cradled in the first fork. The egg is a memory put away for safekeeping.
vibe_condition: The Hist is alive and harmed. It may be recovering.
vibe_mood: The mood is grievous. The workers keep their backs to the Hist.
vibe_approach: The crown shows above the canopy from a kilometre away. It is greyer than any other crown.
vibe_senses: Sap drips. The canopy is silent where birdsong should be.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The harmed Hist will describe its own injury. It tells this to any visitor who can bear to listen.
why_site_won: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 253 m from the nearest route; won on culture-clump, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: The Hist has been harmed and knows it. It will say what was done to it. It tells this to a listener who can stand the telling.

name: Murkwater
why_founding: Murkwater is a Shadowfen village with a Shadowscale association. The Shadowscales liberated it in 2E 582. The village still tells the story.
why_site_advantages: A Hist stands on a firm hummock in the channel network. Water approaches reach the hummock on every side.
why_occupants_motive: The village stays because the Hist is here. The villagers keep their Shadowscale connection because it has twice saved the village.
why_pressures: The Archon sanctuary closed in 4E 187. The surviving ku-vastei who lives here is the last of an institution.
why_would_change_if: Murkwater would become a pilgrimage site on the day the Shadowscales were publicly ended. The villagers would hate that.
siting_prefs_water_relation: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage
vibe_silhouette: A Hist crown rises over reed roofs on a hummock. One house stands apart on its own small island.
vibe_palette: The Hist is grey-white. The reeds are gold. The channel water is black. The separate house has a single black door.
vibe_materials: The buildings are Argonian mud, wattle and reed. The separate house is built like the rest, except that it has a door.
vibe_signature_feature: One house stands apart on its own island at the edge of the hummock.
vibe_condition: The village is well kept. Its people rebuild it on the usual cycle. The centre is older.
vibe_approach: By boat the crown appears first. The separate house is the last thing a visitor notices.
vibe_senses: Poles move in water. The uxith is present. The villagers lower their voices near one house.
quest_hooks_opportunity: People who know what she was ask a retired executioner for one more piece of work. The villagers can see the tempering ground from their own water. The villagers then insist that they cannot.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV31 · tier-3; LV32 · tier-3; LV33 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 614 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Murkwater is a Hist village on a hummock with water on every side. A retired executioner lives here and kept her tools.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at this position. The record sits on the region's Argonian marsh side, where the two zones interleave. Murkwater is catalogued with the north. Its trade, its levies and its neighbours are northern.

name: Murkwater Tempering Ground
why_founding: Children born under the Shadow were given up and made into something else. The making happened on set ground, away from the village.
why_site_advantages: The ground is a screened hollow about 51 m from Murkwater. The villagers heard sounds from the hollow at no time.
why_occupants_motive: The ku-vastei who ran the ground retired and never came back. The Archon sanctuary closed in 4E 187. The course has stood as it was left since then.
why_pressures: The equipment is still here. The ku-vastei in the village has not come back to remove it.
why_would_change_if: The ground would be destroyed on the day a decision was made against reconstituting the institution. That decision has not been made.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a hatchery and a major city, deliberately unremarkable
vibe_silhouette: A hollow holds a course still laid out in it. The course has beams, ropes and pits. The beams, ropes and pits are rotted and still in position.
vibe_palette: The rope is rotted grey. The overgrowth is green. One pale stone stands at the entrance.
vibe_materials: The materials are timber, rope and pits. One piece of stone is the delivery stone.
vibe_signature_feature: The delivery stone is flat and waist-high. It stands at the entrance. It is worn smooth in one place.
vibe_condition: The ground has been abandoned for fourteen years. It is rotting fast. It is entirely undisturbed.
vibe_approach: The path has vanished. Visitors who are told where the ground stands can find it.
vibe_senses: Rope creaks on an empty beam. Birds call. The hollow has an odd flat acoustic.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tempering ground has its equipment intact. That draws a visitor who wants to start the tempering again. The villagers can see the tempering ground from their own water. The villagers then insist that they cannot.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ23 · tier-0; SS03 · tier-2; LD26 · tier-3; LV32 · tier-3
why_site_won: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 2), 591 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The screened hollow is where Shadowscale children were tempered. The fittings are still bolted to the trees.

name: Names-The-Year
why_founding: The northern villages hold their naming-day together on one flat, once a year. A name given in front of four villages cannot later be disputed by a fifth.
why_site_advantages: The site is a dry meadow equidistant from four villages. A single old tree stands at one end. Every naming has happened under that tree.
why_occupants_motive: The meadow stands empty outside the fortnight. The ground belongs to the naming. Grazing the meadow is rude but not illegal, so it is grazed.
why_pressures: The meadow is safe for the fortnight during which the moot sits in it. For the rest of the year it is open ground a long way from any village. The moot posts a watch before it posts a speaker.
why_would_change_if: The meadow would lose its whole point if the registry issued the names. Now the registry records them and does nothing more.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: serves a settlement cluster
vibe_silhouette: The meadow is empty. One broad old tree stands at the north end. A ring of worn ground lies under the tree.
vibe_palette: The meadow is green under one dark crown. The ring is a pale scuff. The ring does not quite grow back between years.
vibe_materials: The meadow has no buildings of any kind. The tree is the venue. The ring worn under it is the floor.
vibe_signature_feature: The ring under the tree is worn by one day's standing a year. It is older than the registrar can date.
vibe_condition: The meadow is untouched. It is worn in one place.
vibe_mood: The mood is warm and formal. The meadow is newly watched.
vibe_approach: The tree stands alone on the skyline for a kilometre either way.
vibe_senses: Out of season, wind moves in one tree. In season, four villages say the same words at slightly different speeds.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A naming can be witnessed, sponsored or disrupted. The registry is encroaching on a village rite.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 543 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Four villages meet under one tree to name the year. This year they cannot agree what to call it.

name: Nine Fords
why_founding: Nine shallow crossings lie within one kilometre. One family built a gate on the crossing that stays passable in the wet. The town grew around the gate and became larger than the single crossing from which it began.
why_site_advantages: One of the nine crossings has a gravel bottom. A loaded cart can use that crossing for four months of the year.
why_occupants_motive: The toll family collects a toll at the gate. Stabling, warehousing, a tradehouse and a moneylender grew up around the toll. Two people move goods around the gate for a price.
why_pressures: The other eight fords are usable in the dry. The toll generates income for four months of the year and nothing for eight. Debts in Nine Fords are written to fall due in the wet.
why_would_change_if: Nine Fords would shrink to a village if a bridge went up. Stormhold has proposed a bridge twice. The townspeople have bought off the proposal both times.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a road or boat lane; day-travel spacing from the next
vibe_silhouette: A gate house stands astride the road at the river crossing. The town is strung along one bank. Eight unused fords are visible upstream and downstream.
vibe_palette: Road dust, river brown and black-tarred gate-house timber set the colours. The tradehouse has bright paint because it is doing well.
vibe_materials: The houses are built of mud-brick and timber. The gate house is the single building made of Stormhold terrace stone. The townspeople paid for that stone and resent it.
vibe_signature_feature: Eight fords stand empty. In the dry season the townspeople watch traffic cross the river two hundred metres away.
vibe_condition: Nine Fords is prosperous but seasonal. It is visibly over-built for eight months of the year.
vibe_approach: The gate house is on the road and cannot be avoided. Travellers notice the fords only after they pass the gate house.
vibe_senses: Cart wheels sound on gravel. Townspeople argue over a toll. The dry season brings an unsettling quiet.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A toll at the gate can be paid, avoided or broken. Eight alternative fords are visible from the road. The townspeople keep buying off a bridge proposal.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV34 · tier-3; LV35 · tier-3; PP13 · tier-3; Reed track · tier-2; LD95 · tier-3; LD96 · tier-3; LD97 · tier-3; LD98 · tier-3; LD99 · tier-3; LV01 · tier-3; LV02 · tier-3; LV03 · tier-3; LV04 · tier-3; LV05 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 71 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: One ford can carry a loaded cart in the wet. A toll matches that ford. Carters resent the ford and the toll.

name: Nine Marks
why_founding: Nine identical marks are cut into nine separate boulders across two kilometres of open upland. The script matches no Ayleid, Jel or Daedric writing. The ninth mark is a stroke short. The district has agreed to leave it that way.
why_site_advantages: The erratic boulders stand on open upland hills and are visible from each other. That is presumably why whoever cut the marks chose these nine.
why_occupants_motive: The boulders have no residents. The nearest village keeps the grass down around each boulder. Villagers describe the mowing as tidiness.
why_pressures: A Whispers scholar found that one mark is unfinished. She asked to finish it. Every village within a day refused in writing.
why_would_change_if: The ninth mark would be finished if the scholar found a willing office-holder. The office-holder would need to sign. The scholar is still looking.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately unrelated to its surroundings
vibe_silhouette: Nine grey boulders stand on open grass. Each boulder carries the same three-stroke mark on its north face. The grass around each boulder is mown.
vibe_palette: The colours are grass green and boulder grey. Each mark is darker than the stone because it holds water.
vibe_materials: No building of any kind stands here. Mowing is the work done here. Four people need two days to mow all nine boulders.
vibe_signature_feature: The ninth mark is unfinished, one stroke short. Travellers rub it and copy the missing stroke.
vibe_condition: The marks are weathered but legible. The ground around them is kept clear.
vibe_approach: One boulder can be found from the track. The other eight take about an hour to walk.
vibe_senses: Wind moves over the open grass. A hand on cut stone makes a disproportionate sound.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The nine marks form a puzzle that can be completed. The district has asked visitors to stay out.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 304 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: Nine cut boulders stand in sight of each other. Read in order, the marks form a route. The route can still be walked.

name: Nine-Stone Bench
why_founding: A cutter set up small diggings and a polishing bench outside Crystalgate. The bench works the stones for which the province is famous. The grading houses refused the cutter. She has worked the bench for nine years.
why_site_advantages: The site is a gravel terrace with garnet and jasper in the wash. Clean spring water serves the polishing wheel. Crystalgate's own water is too silty for cutting.
why_occupants_motive: The bench has one cutter and two apprentices. The cutter sells ungraded stone to any buyer. Crystalgate calls that heresy. Buyers come to the bench because it sells ungraded stone.
