why_pressures: The grading houses twice had the bench's output declared uncertified at Wolk Market. Both times the stone sold. The second time it sold for more.
why_would_change_if: The grading houses could buy out and close the bench. They would need to offer money where they have so far offered censure.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: supplies an artisan village's jewellers
vibe_silhouette: A gravel bank holds a water-driven wheel. An open-sided shed covers a stone bench. Nine finished stones are set in the lintel.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey gravel, clear spring water and grey timber. Nine points of hard colour show in the timber.
vibe_materials: The shed is built of rough timber. The stone bench is very good. All the money spent here went into the working surface.
vibe_signature_feature: Nine stones are set into the shed's beam. One stone is added per year. Each is the best piece cut that year.
vibe_condition: The bench is rough and precise. Its work is improving.
vibe_approach: The noise of the wheel carries up the terrace. The shed lies below the path and comes into view late.
vibe_senses: A wet wheel turns. Stone grinds on stone at a very fine grade. The cutter corrects the two apprentices.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Ungraded stones are sold without a certificate. Crystalgate wants that trade stopped. The cutter will work a stone brought to her without questions.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD05 · tier-3; LD66 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: ravine in firm lowland (danger band 3), 88 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Garnet and jasper come out of the wash. The stones are cut and polished on site. They are sold under Crystalgate's price.

name: One-House-High
why_founding: One household lives on a rise too small for a second house. The household has taken in travellers for four generations. No other stop lies between the pass and the plain.
why_site_advantages: A pinnacle of firm ground lies where the pass road meets the flood plain. It holds one house's worth of ground and no more.
why_occupants_motive: The household are innkeepers by geography, not by trade. They say frankly that they would prefer not to be.
why_pressures: Too many travellers arrive at one house. The road delivers them at the worst hours. The household has begun turning people away. Travellers on the road have begun to resent that.
why_would_change_if: It would become a road station with a garrison. That happens if Stormhold notices how many people sleep in the yard.
siting_prefs_water_relation: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: refuge for its neighbours in flood
vibe_silhouette: One tall narrow house stands on a green rise. A yard fence encloses more space than the house does.
vibe_palette: The colours are reed-thatch gold and mud-wall brown. The yard is trodden bare earth that takes more feet than it should.
vibe_materials: The house is ordinary village building, one house's worth. The yard fence is rebuilt annually because strangers lean on it.
vibe_signature_feature: The yard is the place, not the house. It is a fenced acre of trodden ground. Forty people can sleep there. One household can watch them.
vibe_condition: The house is well kept. The yard is permanently worn to bare earth.
vibe_approach: The house stands out of the plain from a long way off. From every distance it looks as small as it is.
vibe_senses: Many voices fill the yard. One household's cooking is stretched thin. A dog in the yard reacts to the crowd.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A bed may or may not be available. A refusal has to be got past.
player_purpose_hook: One house stands between the pass and the plain. The household takes travellers in grudgingly, for a price.

name: Puts-Down-The-Cup
why_founding: Stormhold's crystal trade pays in coin. Stormhold's dockside takes the coin straight back in exchange for daril. Stormhold's cutters send those who cannot stop to this terrace-road house.
why_site_advantages: The house is far up the terrace road. Walking back down for a drink takes two hours. That distance is most of the cure.
why_occupants_motive: A former cutter with a shaking hand runs the house. The cutting houses pay a levy that funds it. The cutting houses call the levy charity, though it is insurance.
why_pressures: The cutting houses want the house to take anyone they send. The keeper wants to choose the residents. The levy is renegotiated every year. Both sides use the levy as a bargaining lever.
why_would_change_if: The house would close inside a season if the levy stopped. The cutting houses know what that would cost them.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: just outside a settlement, near sap country
vibe_silhouette: A terrace house stands on the uphill side of the road. Its lower windows are barred and its door is open.
vibe_palette: The terrace stone is grey. The shutters are painted the blue of a grading hall's shutters. A lamp is left lit all night on purpose.
vibe_materials: The house is Stormhold terrace masonry. Only the bars are new. The household argued about the bars.
vibe_signature_feature: The door is never shut. The windows are always barred. The open door and barred windows show that the household guards against residents leaving.
vibe_condition: The house is sound and plain. Its staff have time on their hands and care for it.
vibe_approach: Going up the terrace road, it is the last lit house. Coming down, it is the first lit house.
vibe_senses: A resident plays the same four notes badly. A kettle sounds in the house. The road lies below. The city lies below that.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The house gives the northern road what a healer would give it. The levy is really insurance. It also gives the cutting houses bargaining power.
player_purpose_hook: The house is a withdrawal house, two hours' walk above the nearest drink. It takes strangers in to dry out.

name: Reedmoor
why_founding: Shadowfen's channels have no dry ground fit for building. Villages there stand on legs over the water.
why_site_advantages: The reach is wide and slow. It has a firm bed for piling. The bed matters more than the bank here.
why_occupants_motive: Villagers fish and cut reed. They pole cargo out to the trunk boat lane. The lane passes a few minutes' push from the landing.
why_pressures: The bed is silting. The piles are driven shorter at each rebuild. The elders discuss this constantly.
why_would_change_if: Reedmoor would move two hundred metres downstream, entire. Shadowfen villages have rebuilt themselves that way for generations.
siting_prefs_water_relation: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial
vibe_silhouette: Forty reed houses stand on legs over open water. A single broad platform stands at the centre. Boats are racked beneath the walkways.
vibe_palette: Reed gold lies above and black water below. New-cut piles are pale.
vibe_materials: The houses are stilt shells joined by elevated walkways. The piles run straight into the bed. No bank lies beneath any of it.
vibe_signature_feature: A forest of piles stands below the village. Two centuries of abandoned piles still stand there.
vibe_condition: Reedmoor is continuously rebuilt. The newest houses are at the downstream end.
vibe_mood: Reedmoor feels buoyant and noisy. Its people are at ease with water.
vibe_approach: From four hundred metres along the channel, the village shows as roofs. The roofs appear to float on open water.
vibe_senses: Water moves under the floors. Villagers push their boats with poles. Children are in the water constantly.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A warning bell sounds nightly with the water flat calm. A landlord who left the district let one stilt house to two households.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LQ03 · tier-3; LV36 · tier-3; LV37 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 118 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.riverwalk (+0.38).
player_purpose_hook: A stilt village stands over slow water. It offers reed, fish and a bed on legs. Poled cargo leaves at dawn.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at Reedmoor's position. The record sits on the region's Argonian marsh side, where the two culture zones interleave. Reedmoor is catalogued with the north. Its trade, levies and neighbours are northern.

name: Rimfield
why_founding: Rimfield stands on the rim shelf above the pass. The marsh rules stop on the rim shelf. The water at Rimfield is clean and the nights are cold, so grain keeps well there. Rimfield sells its surplus grain down to the lowland, which cannot store grain.
why_site_advantages: The site is a broad south-facing shelf. A spring rises at the back of the shelf. The shelf lies above the fever line and below the snow.
why_occupants_motive: Rimfield trades in grain, wool and pass supplies. Parties crossing the rim buy food at Rimfield. This saves them from carrying four days of food up the mountain.
why_pressures: The shelf is small and the village fills all of it. Rimfield's young people go down to Stormhold. The ground above Rimfield is worse than the ground below it.
why_would_change_if: Rimfield would become a summer grazing station within two generations. That change follows from the current rate of leaving.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a pass or an upland route; isolated
vibe_silhouette: Terraced fields climb in six steps below the village. A tight cluster of stone-based houses stands above the terraces. The rim wall stands behind the whole village.
vibe_palette: The palette is hard upland green and dry-stone grey. The roofs are grey slate. Slate roofs exist nowhere in the lowland.
vibe_materials: The house bases are dry stone with reed walling above. Reed alone does not suffice at this height.
vibe_signature_feature: The roof slate is split off the rim itself. No other roofs in the region are slate. From the lowland the slate reads as a hard grey mark on the shelf.
vibe_condition: Old and complete; emptying.
vibe_approach: The last hour of the pass road runs below the terraces. The whole village is in full view from that road.
vibe_senses: The wind blows across the shelf, with few insects. A hand-quern grinds grain in the village. Sheep graze here. The lowland cannot keep sheep.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Rimfield is the last resupply before the rim crossing. It is a village that is visibly losing its young to the city.
why_site_won: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 926 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Rimfield is a terrace village above the fever line. Its nights are cold enough to break a fever.

name: Riverwalk
why_founding: Riverwalk is a halt in a sheltered sea cove. The cove lies at the mouth of the pilgrim water, the channel up to Hissmir. Boats off the Padomaic run put in at Riverwalk. The houses stand on the shore. A plank walk runs from the houses across the cove to an islet. The ferry stage moors at the islet.
why_site_advantages: Riverwalk has the only sheltered water on this stretch of coast. It lies under a kilometre east of Thorn by the Tear road, which leaves Riverwalk westward. Canoes leave the ferry stage for Hissmir and Murkwater.
why_occupants_motive: Riverwalk lives on the ferry stage and the toll on boats entering the pilgrim water. The villagers feed and lodge the boat crews. The village grows no food of its own.
why_pressures: Thorn's field-owners say the toll on the pilgrim water is theirs. The stewards of Hissmir also say the toll on the pilgrim water is theirs.
why_would_change_if: Boats would bypass Riverwalk if the cove silted up. For that reason the villagers sound the way across the cove to the ferry stage every morning.
siting_prefs_water_relation: crosses water rather than sitting beside it
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: often the only dry route through its stretch
vibe_silhouette: Two houses and a totem stand on the shore. The long house stands on piles in the shallows beside them. A plank walk runs across the cove to a tent on a low islet. The ferry stage is moored off the islet's far side.
vibe_palette: The palette is silver weathered plank, black water and reed thatch.
vibe_materials: Piles and planks carry the village over the water. The crews' house and the family house are plank houses on posts. Both plank houses stand on dry ground at the shore. The long house stands on piles in the shallows beside them.
vibe_signature_feature: The plank walk is the only way between the shore and the ferry stage. It crosses open water. All who land at the stage walk past the toll-holder's post at the shore end.
vibe_condition: The villagers re-plank the walk constantly. The boards are all different ages. They record the order in which the village was built.
vibe_approach: Boats come in off the Padomaic run. Crews pole across the cove to the ferry stage off the islet.
vibe_senses: Boards run underfoot from the shore to the islet. Poles push into the mud. Talk carries over still water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Thorn and Hissmir both tax the cove village at the mouth of the pilgrim water. Paying either one counts as taking its side. The nightly toll argument can turn into a provable accusation.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV38 · tier-3; LV39 · tier-3; LV40 · tier-3
why_site_won: sheltered sea cove (danger band 0), 692 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, hinterland, route; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.reedmoor-stilts (+0.38).
player_purpose_hook: Riverwalk is the cove where boats put in off the Padomaic run. The toll is argued nightly, since Thorn and Hissmir both claim it.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at this position. The record sits on the region's Argonian marsh side, where two zones interleave. The village is catalogued with the north. Its trade, its levies and its neighbours are northern.
watch_reason: The toll office on the pilgrim water is an An-Xileel levy; the toll-holder and the toll hands stop a wrongdoer at the spit.

name: Saltmarch
why_founding: Saltmarch is a field village of Argonians and Dunmer. Both peoples work the same crop. The village was founded when the estates broke up and the labour stayed.
why_site_advantages: The village stands in the middle of the terraces. It stands on a single rise that the flood does not reach. The rise is equidistant from four banks.
why_occupants_motive: The households farm together and marry separately. That arrangement has lasted three generations.
why_pressures: Thorn's title court could dissolve the common holding with a single ruling. The households know this.
why_would_change_if: Saltmarch would split cleanly in two along a line that both households already name. That split happens if Thorn's title court forces the question.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a city's agricultural hinterland
vibe_silhouette: Round Argonian houses and square lacquered Dunmer houses alternate along a single street. The village has a single shared threshing floor.
vibe_palette: The palette is thatch gold and lacquer red. Saltrice silver shows on every horizon.
vibe_materials: Argonian and Dunmer architecture are interleaved house by house. Neither style borrows from the other.
vibe_signature_feature: The shared threshing floor has two shrine niches on opposite walls. Both shrine niches are in use.
vibe_condition: Saltmarch is prosperous. The residents keep extending it in both styles.
vibe_mood: The mood is practical and mixed. The residents are proud of the mixed village.
vibe_approach: The alternating roof shapes show from the terrace banks.
vibe_senses: Threshing goes on in the village. Two languages are spoken. Two kinds of cooking go on at once.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Four banks give four accounts of the same night. None of the accounts agree. A grassland field turns up a weapon. The weapon reopens a settled inheritance.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LQ21 · tier-3; LV41 · tier-3; LV42 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 382 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: Saltmarch has grass and dry beds on a single rise that the flood does not cover. Gossip from four banks runs through the village.

name: Seam-Chasers
why_founding: Failed Silyanorn hopefuls end up on the rim. Four unlicensed claims are worked out of a single camp. The camp lies above the cold root gallery. Each prospector is convinced that the seam runs north. None of the four holds a licence to prove it.
why_site_advantages: The site has exposed country rock on the rim's shoulder. The gallery's first chamber below serves as a store. Spring water is within reach. The site lies far from the licensed diggings. The hoist master's men do not patrol the site.
why_occupants_motive: Four independent prospectors live here. They cooperate on food. Each has marked a claim in a way that the other three do not recognise.
why_pressures: The diggings' hoist master reports the camps annually. The vicecanons sit on the report. The four now treat the approach as theirs. They drive strangers on the claim lines off with tools first.
why_would_change_if: A real strike would make the camp a licensed working. Whichever office signs first would hold the licence. The four prospectors would not be named on that licence.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a known extraction district
vibe_silhouette: Four scrappy camps stand within shouting distance. Four differently-cut claim stakes mark the claims. A single shared cook fire burns in the middle.
vibe_palette: Grey scree lies under four colours of salvaged canvas. Blue-green dust off the ravine has settled on everything.
vibe_materials: The camps use salvage from the diggings, mostly stolen. Four people assembled it in four ways. The four will not share a design.
vibe_signature_feature: There is a single fire and four camps. The four eat together and stake their claims apart.
vibe_condition: The camps are marginal and ingenious. Each prospector is about a season from finished.
vibe_approach: Four hammers are audible before the camps show. The hammers keep four unsynchronised rhythms.
vibe_senses: Four hammers ring across the camps. A single cook pot serves the four. An argument about water rights goes on across a gully.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Four claims lie over a single seam. It is unclear which of the four found the seam. The licensed diggings would pay to know. They would pay more to keep it quiet.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 2056 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: Four unlicensed claims lie across the ravine from the real diggings. All four prospectors are certain that the seam turns their way.
siting_note: The camp is sited at the D3 hostility gap point on the north-west rim. hostility-frequency.md records that gap point. The Cold Gallery's record already describes a prospectors' camp holding this ground above it.

name: Silyanorn Diggings
why_founding: Stormhold's crystal trade comes out of a Barsaebic Ayleid undercity. The city has quarried that undercity for centuries.
why_site_advantages: The ravine walls below the city expose the Ayleid galleries directly. The diggings are the ruin, entered sideways.
why_occupants_motive: The vicecanons license the diggings because crystal sales fund the border offices. The diggers dig because the Owing says so.
why_pressures: Every season takes more of an Ayleid structure. The Synod would pay handsomely to study that structure intact.
why_would_change_if: Any authority that valued the ruin above the revenue would close the diggings. The north has no such authority.
siting_prefs_water_relation: drainage problems are the mine's whole story
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: feeds a northern city's crystal trade
vibe_silhouette: Timber hoists run down a ravine wall. They end at square white doorways. The doorways are plainly not natural.
vibe_palette: The palette is Ayleid bone-white and ravine black. Welkynd blue shows in the depths. The timber is grey.
vibe_materials: The galleries are Ayleid ashlar. Modern timber shoring is driven straight through the carving.
vibe_signature_feature: Diggers paid by the load hammer props into the reliefs. The reliefs are four thousand years old.
vibe_condition: The Ayleid work is perfect. The modern shoring that is driven through it is already failing.
vibe_mood: The mood is industrious and blue-lit. The diggers commit sacrilege without noticing.
vibe_approach: The city terraces above look straight down into the gallery mouths.
vibe_senses: Hoists creak and picks strike stone. A welkynd hum sounds under the noise.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A crystal cutter is found in the diggings' water channel. Graded stones are sewn into his coat. Four unlicensed prospectors work on the rim. One of the four has actually found the seam.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD02 · tier-3; LD12 · tier-3; LD67 · tier-3
why_site_won: saddle in upland hills (danger band 3), 717 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The diggings are the Ayleid galleries, entered sideways. Crystal can be taken past the licensed face.

name: Sings-For-The-Pipes
why_founding: The Panther basin's frogs have the chirp that the vossa-satl copies. Three generations ago a farmer worked out that the tone breeds true. The farm culls frogs by ear.
why_site_advantages: The site has six spring-fed ponds. The ponds sit at slightly different temperatures. That lets the farm hold six different tones on a single site.
why_occupants_motive: The pipe-makers in Thorn pay by tone. A matched set of six carries the highest price of all.
why_pressures: The tone drifts if the pond temperature drifts. The farm's craft is holding six ponds at six temperatures. A hot year ruins a decade of selection.
why_would_change_if: The farm would lose its stock in a single season to a spring failure. The selection could not be redone in under thirty years.
siting_prefs_water_relation: still, warm, separated from the channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: supplies a named artisan village
vibe_silhouette: Six small ponds step down in terraces. Reed screens stand between the ponds. A single low shed stands at the top of the fall.
vibe_palette: The ponds are green in six perceptibly different shades. The screen-reed is gold. The channels dividing the ponds are wet black.
vibe_materials: The farm uses reed screens, timber sluices and clay-lined ponds. Each part holds the temperature of one pond steady.
vibe_signature_feature: Each pond is screened from the next. The farmer can stand between two ponds and hear the difference.
vibe_condition: The farm is quiet and kept to the inch. The sluices are better built than the house.
vibe_approach: The farm is heard long before it is seen. Six chords carry from the ponds. No two of the chords are in tune.
vibe_senses: Six frog choruses sound at once. Each chorus is in tune with itself but not with the others. Water runs over sluice boards.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The farm supplies the raw material for the vossa-satl. The supply is audible from the road.
why_site_won: waterfall in seasonal floodplain (danger band 2), 6 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The farm breeds frogs from six ponds by ear. A matched set of six tones is worth more than the farm.

name: Sits-Above-The-Flood
why_founding: Six houses stand on one rise that stands a kilometre from any other. The hamlet has no other reason to exist.
why_site_advantages: The site is a gravel rise two metres above the plain. The rise has stayed dry in every flood on record. It lies on the line that villagers walk between the terraces and the north road.
why_occupants_motive: The households farm the plain and sleep on the rise. In flood season they farm nothing. In flood season they take in everyone whose ground is under water, for a price.
why_pressures: The rise is finite and the flood is not. Two of the six houses stand on made ground. The households carried that ground up themselves, basket by basket.
why_would_change_if: The hamlet would double in size and halve in dryness if the flood took the next rise downstream. Floodwater is already cutting at that next rise.
siting_prefs_water_relation: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: refuge for its neighbours in flood
vibe_silhouette: Six roofs stand in a tight line on a low green swell. The plain runs flat to the horizon on both sides.
vibe_palette: Gravel grey shows under everything. Flood-silt brown reaches the edge of the yards. The roofs are kept pale so that travellers can see them across water.
vibe_materials: The houses are built of reed and mud on a base course of river gravel. The only stone in the hamlet lies under the houses. The households carried that stone to the rise.
vibe_signature_feature: Two houses stand on a metre of basket-carried gravel. The households that carried the gravel still say whose baskets they were.
vibe_condition: The hamlet is poor and durable. Nothing in it is new and nothing has failed.
vibe_approach: The roofs sit on the horizon for an hour before a traveller arrives. They grow very slowly.
vibe_senses: The frogs are loud enough to be difficult to bear. Woodsmoke hangs in the air because the plain has no slope down which it can run.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A floodable route can cut a traveller off. One dry place lies on it.
player_purpose_hook: Six houses stand on a gravel rise. Their households take in everyone that the flood turns out, for a price.

name: Stands-On-The-Hammock
why_founding: A tree hammock in the north marsh carries an acre of soil that stays above the flood. A village stands on the hammock.
why_site_advantages: The marsh on every side is too soft to walk and too shallow to row. A boat cannot arrive in a hurry. The ground on top is dry enough for burial and for crops. The raft villages cannot manage burial or crops.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers own the permanent ground for two kilometres in every direction. During the flood they rent standing room. Those who rent it resent the price but pay it.
why_pressures: The hammock is not getting bigger. The flood season is getting longer. The crown terrace is filling faster than the ground below it.
why_would_change_if: The village would have to stop burying its dead in the soil. That argument is splitting the village now.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a raised hammock ringed by marsh, above the flood
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a local centre; neighbours come here in flood
vibe_silhouette: A dome of dark trees stands out of flat marsh. Roofs stand inside the dome and a landing stage lies on one side. The hammock reads as a single object at any distance.
vibe_palette: Water-sky grey surrounds the hammock on all sides. The hammock itself is a hard green-black. One gap of pale ground shows through the trunks.
vibe_materials: The village is built of timber and reed on real soil. The houses have floors.
vibe_signature_feature: The soil is a metre of actual earth. It is fenced, planted and dug for graves.
vibe_condition: The village is prosperous and tight-packed. It is running out of room.
vibe_approach: The hammock sits on the marsh and grows for an hour without changing shape. The trees close overhead at the end of the approach.
vibe_senses: Water noise stops at the landing. Feet on dry ground make an entirely different sound. A burial argument is in progress.
quest_hooks_opportunity: All the dry ground for two kilometres around is rented. The price can rise beyond a traveller's reach. The village is split over whether to stop burying in the ground.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV43 · tier-3; LV44 · tier-3; LV45 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 365 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: The hammock holds real soil in a marsh. The village can bury its dead and grow its own food.

name: Stillrise Village
why_founding: The village took a Daedric bargain to survive the Knahaten Flu. Its villagers are technically dead and are sustained by a soul-gem array.
why_site_advantages: Stillrise stands east of Stormhold on ground that the Flu emptied around it. Nothing else on that ground is still inhabited.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers maintain the illusions because the alternative is to stop. The same argument has run for centuries and has moved neither side.
why_pressures: The villagers kept the array intact in 2E 582 and did not destroy it. The argument that started then is still running, with the same participants. The villagers stay here under Clavicus Vile's bargain. The argument will end with the villagers.
why_would_change_if: The argument would end the day a villager broke the array. Half the village would thank whoever broke it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: shunned by its neighbours, who nevertheless maintain the markers
vibe_silhouette: From a distance Stillrise reads as an ordinary village. At about thirty metres the illusion stops covering the detail.
vibe_palette: Warm ochre and thatch show at distance. Bone and grey-green show at close range.
vibe_materials: The houses are ordinary mud-and-reed houses. The villagers, who do not need to eat, maintain them. The thatch is perfect and has gone unrepaired for centuries.
vibe_signature_feature: The array stands in the meeting house. It is soul gems in a frame, humming. It is the whole village's life support.
vibe_condition: Stillrise is unchanged since 2E 582 in every particular.
vibe_approach: From the path Stillrise reads as a normal village. The detail fails at close range.
vibe_senses: The villagers' voices sound slightly too dry. The array hums. There are no cooking smells at all.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The soul-gem array is preserved. The 2E 582 argument is unresolved.
why_site_won: island in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 508 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, remote.
player_purpose_hook: The Flu passed over Stillrise. A humming frame of soul gems in the meeting house explains why.

name: Stormhold
why_founding: Stormhold stands on ravine-severed mounds above a waterfall. It sits over a Barsaebic Ayleid crystal undercity. The city has mined the undercity since its founding and mines it now.
why_site_advantages: Stormhold is the head of navigation on the northern river. Every boat out of Morrowind stops here. The ravines make each mound its own defensible quarter.
why_occupants_motive: The vicecanons are plural and rivals. They run the state's only working border offices. The river trade pays for the offices.
why_pressures: The Knahaten Flu began at Stormhold. Four provinces still say so aloud when petitions from Stormhold come before them. People with no other option work the Silyanorn tunnels below.
why_would_change_if: Stormhold would lose its purpose if the Morrowind trade failed. It would lose its shape if the waterfall cut back past the first mound.
siting_prefs_water_relation: astride a navigable river above the falls
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the northern hinge: Tenmar Wall east, Bogmother south-west, the Morrowind road north
vibe_silhouette: Three terraced mounds step above a white waterfall. Bridges link the mounds. Black ravine slots lie between them.
vibe_palette: The terrace stone is wet grey and the water is white. The ravines are dark. The undercity mouths show crystal-blue points at night.
vibe_materials: Argonian terrace construction stands over Barsaebic Ayleid foundations. Dunmer-frontier timber balconies stand on the trade quarter.
vibe_signature_feature: Three worked openings, the undercity mouths, cut the ravine walls. They are lit blue. Hoists run into them.
vibe_condition: The top terraces are prosperous. Below the waterline of the ravines the workings are worked out and propped.
vibe_mood: The city is layered and damp. Every quarter stands above or below another.
vibe_approach: By river the approach is to the falls, with the city stacked above. By road the approach arrives at the top and overlooks the city below.
vibe_senses: A waterfall sounds constantly under the terraces. Hoists creak. Three languages are spoken. Each mound has a bell.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Conclave of Baal locates Murkwood by reading the Elder Scrolls with an Ayleid tablet. The Cyrodilic Collections alcove is a hook. The Silyanorn crystal undercity is a hook. The ground where the Knahaten Flu began is a hook.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ03 · tier-0; SA03 · tier-2; LD01 · tier-3; LD02 · tier-3; LD03 · tier-3; LD04 · tier-3; LD05 · tier-3; LD06 · tier-3; LD07 · tier-3; LD08 · tier-3; LD09 · tier-3; LD10 · tier-3; LD11 · tier-3; LD12 · tier-3; LD13 · tier-3; LD14 · tier-3; LD15 · tier-3; LD16 · tier-3; LD17 · tier-3; LD18 · tier-3; LD19 · tier-3; LD20 · tier-3; LD21 · tier-3; LD22 · tier-3; LD23 · tier-3; LD24 · tier-3; LD25 · tier-3; LD26 · tier-3; LD27 · tier-3; LD28 · tier-3; LD29 · tier-3; LD30 · tier-3; LD31 · tier-3; LD32 · tier-3; LD33 · tier-3
why_site_won: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'stormhold' (world/sources/anchors); the anchor pixel is the city gate on the main road. The record sits at the solved city centre (cityLayout, owner rule 2026-09-18).
player_purpose_hook: Stormhold is the north's border city. It has offices, boats to everywhere and a crystal undercity underfoot. Two vicecanons who hate each other rule it.
complexity_justification: Stormhold is a major city on ravine-severed mounds with an undercity. It has three district clusters, bridges and a vertical layer. Placement stays Morrowind-level. The mound, bridge and undercity structure justifies the budget.

name: Bogmother Causeway
why_founding: Stormhold built a stone causeway to Bogmother. The pilgrimage had to run in every season.
why_site_advantages: The site is the shortest line of shallow bog between the city's south gate and the sacred ground.
why_occupants_motive: Stormhold maintains the causeway as a civic duty. The maintenance gang is a hereditary office with a bad reputation.
why_pressures: The causeway is stone. Since the Duskfall, locals count stone building as a moral compromise. The pilgrimage is why locals tolerate the causeway.
why_would_change_if: Stormhold would replace the causeway with timber if it ever failed completely. The caretakers would prefer timber and the city would not.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: links two named places directly
vibe_silhouette: A raised stone road three paces wide runs dead straight over open bog. It has no rail of any kind.
vibe_palette: Grey stone and brown bog fill the view. A very large amount of sky shows for this province.
vibe_materials: The causeway is cut stone slabs on a rubble core. It is the largest piece of stone construction that the north has built since the Duskfall.
vibe_signature_feature: Whole sections of the causeway tilt from subsidence. The causeway reads as a line of slightly wrong angles.
vibe_condition: Gangs repair the causeway continuously. It sinks continuously.
vibe_mood: The causeway is exposed and is used for processions. Locals regard it as improper.
vibe_approach: It runs flat to the horizon out of the city's south gate. It is the only straight line for kilometres in either direction.
vibe_senses: Feet on stone make an unfamiliar sound here. Bog gas hangs over the bog. Wind crosses open ground.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The causeway ferry is late every dusk, on the Bogmother side each time.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 121 m from the nearest route; no free 'isthmus' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: A stone causeway crosses the bog to Bogmother. It is three paces wide, dead level and dry underfoot.

name: Tear Road Stage
why_founding: The Tear road is one of the province's two roads out. A road to Morrowind needs a last stage on the Argonian side.
why_site_advantages: The stage stands where the road leaves the marsh for the pass. Above it there is no fodder and no level ground.
why_occupants_motive: A family runs the stage. The family takes payment in both coin and salt and prefers salt.
why_pressures: Dunmer caravans and Argonian porters use the same yard. They keep to opposite sides of it.
why_would_change_if: The stage would become a border town if the traffic doubled. The stage family can name the year in which they think that will happen.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road
vibe_silhouette: Two walled yards share one gate and one well. A fodder barn stands between the yards and divides them.
vibe_palette: The yards are dusty. Velothi red marks one side of the yard and Argonian ochre the other. A grey barn divides the two sides.
vibe_materials: The buildings are mud-brick and reed. The stone well is Dunmer work. The caravans paid for the well over the family's objection.
vibe_signature_feature: The barn works as a wall between the yards. The family built it across the yard on purpose. The family says it was for the fodder.
vibe_condition: Busy, worn, well provisioned.
vibe_mood: The stage is cordial and segregated. It is profitable to both sides.
vibe_approach: The road climbs. The yards appear in the last hollow before the pass.
vibe_senses: Guar and pack-beasts of two kinds stand in the yards. Two languages are spoken. A well windlass creaks.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A caravan sits at the road stage. It is waiting for a guarantee from Tear. Tear refused the guarantee a week ago.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 291 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The stage offers the last fodder and water before the road climbs to Morrowind.

name: Tearmouth
why_founding: Cargo changes hulls where the north river meets navigable water. A two-culture port grew at the transfer point. Argonians hold the water side and Dunmer hold the bank. Each half claims to be the port.
why_site_advantages: Tearmouth stands at the head of deep-draught navigation. A keeled hull can float below the town. Only shallow craft can pass above it. Two dredging schemes have failed to move the line.
why_occupants_motive: The town lives on transfer fees and warehousing. A customs post run out of Thorn has two clerks. Much of the business is kept from those two clerks.
why_pressures: Both halves of the town want the customs house on the other side of the water. A bridge is needed on the Thorn road. Residents leave for six weeks when the river runs too hard to transfer cargo.
why_would_change_if: Tearmouth would lose half its trade to a deeper channel. It would lose all its trade to a bridge. The town has resisted both for a century.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: feeder to a major port
vibe_silhouette: A stone quay stands on one bank. A raft-and-pier town stands on the other bank. The customs house stands on a mid-channel island that neither side wanted.
vibe_palette: Dres grey stone shows on the north bank. Weathered raft-timber shows on the south bank. The water between is brown. One whitewashed customs house stands in the middle.
vibe_materials: The quay is cut stone. The piers are lashed timber. The quay and the piers meet at a mid-channel island.
vibe_signature_feature: The customs house on the mid-channel island is reachable only by boat. The two clerks inside ask for a lift home every night.
vibe_condition: The town is working and prosperous. It is also structurally divided.
vibe_mood: The townsfolk speak two languages and drive hard bargains. They argue permanently.
vibe_approach: The town has two entirely different waterfronts. An arriving crew chooses a bank before tying up.
vibe_senses: Two languages are spoken across one channel. Cargo swings on the cranes. Both banks ignore the customs bell.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Cargo transfers at Tearmouth on every northern route. Smuggling, seizure or delay can occur there. A customs house on an island is staffed by two clerks. The two clerks cannot leave without help.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD85 · tier-3; LD86 · tier-3; LD87 · tier-3; LD88 · tier-3; LD89 · tier-3; LD90 · tier-3; LD91 · tier-3; LD92 · tier-3; LD93 · tier-3; LD94 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: isthmus in firm lowland (danger band 3), 385 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Cargo changes hulls at Tearmouth. The town has two half-towns and one customs house. A berth of any kind goes to whoever asks the right half.

name: Ten-Maur-Wolk
why_founding: Dunmer dissidents who fled the Tribunal raised a temple to Boethiah and Vaermina. They later abandoned the temple. The Third Empire's surveyors recorded a different name for the site. Northern carters and market clerks still use the Dunmer name. The market with the shortened name grew half a morning's walk away. It grew where the carters' tracks bend, which was the closest point they were willing to build.
why_site_advantages: The site lies off the road, in a hollow that the tracks curve to avoid. Every carter in the north can point at the hollow from the bend.
why_occupants_motive: No people live in the shrine. The marker posts around it are maintained.
why_pressures: The market town that borrowed the name lives off the road. The market town treats the ruin as another party's business. The second atrocity on this ground is the Dres slave road that ran past the district. The dissidents did not commit that atrocity.
why_would_change_if: The site would draw a cult if the markers stopped being renewed.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately avoided by every route
vibe_silhouette: A black stone shrine stands in a clearing. White-painted posts ring it at forty metres. The posts are obviously new.
vibe_palette: The site shows black stone and white posts. The grass inside the ring is a different green.
vibe_materials: The shrine is Daedric black basalt. The outbuildings beside it are ordinary Dunmer-cut stone, the dissidents' own work. The outbuildings are easier to read than the shrine.
vibe_signature_feature: The marker ring is repainted every year. Wolk Market pays for the whitewash out of the market fund. The entry is not itemised.
vibe_condition: The site is intact. Nothing has fallen down in two thousand years.
vibe_approach: The site lies off the road. The marker posts start well before the stone does.
vibe_senses: Silence holds inside the ring. Ordinary marsh noise sounds outside it.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A white marker ring surrounds a Daedric ruin. A market fund pays for the ring. The market clerk will not itemise the entry.
why_site_won: box canyon in upland hills (danger band 3), 1146 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: A Daedric shrine is ringed with white posts. The posts were painted this year.
siting_note: The shrine stands over 400 m from any track. The hollow is ground that the routes bend to avoid. The route distance is a requirement and not a fault.

name: Ten-Thousand-Nests
why_founding: A stand of dead trees stands in shallow water. The north's wading birds nest there in large numbers. The birds make the stand uninhabitable. The ground beneath is the richest fertiliser source in the region.
why_site_advantages: The dead standing timber is over water, with no route in for predators. Forty years of guano lie beneath it.
why_occupants_motive: The villages take guano for the terraces in one licensed month. They stay away for eleven months. The smell keeps them away more than any warden does.
why_pressures: The saltrice growers want more than one month. The villages that eat the eggs want no collecting at all. The stand is rotting and falling tree by tree.
why_would_change_if: The birds would relocate entirely if the stand came down. The licensors have never traced where the birds go.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: worked seasonally from a nearby settlement
vibe_silhouette: White dead trunks stand over water. Every branch is loaded with nests. A haze of birds above the stand does not settle.
vibe_palette: Guano whitens every trunk and branch. The water is black. Ten thousand birds make a grey-brown churn.
vibe_materials: Nothing is built at the stand. Collectors bring punts and scoops for a month and leave.
vibe_signature_feature: The trees are white from the top down. The whiteness stops at the waterline in a hard edge.
vibe_condition: The stand rots steadily. Two or three trunks fall into the water most years.
vibe_mood: The stand is overwhelming. It is unpleasant at close range.
vibe_approach: The noise of the birds can be heard a kilometre out. It is heard before the trees are seen.
vibe_senses: The birds roar continuously. The air smells of ammonia. A falling trunk makes a distinct slap.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The guano is a resource with an enforced season. Poaching it is a crime with witnesses.
why_site_won: gorge in firm lowland (danger band 3), 106 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on route, hinterland, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: Forty years of guano lie under dead standing timber. The guano is worth money. The colony above will not agree to its removal.

name: Tenmar Wall
why_founding: A town grew at the junction of the roads to Helstrom, Stormhold and Alten Corimont. Three roads meet here and nowhere else in the north.
why_site_advantages: The ground is firm where three approaches converge. There is water enough for a market. The roads on either side flood and the town does not.
why_occupants_motive: The town takes a cut of everything passing between the interior, the border city and the smugglers' port.
why_pressures: The town is prosperous and indefensible. It stands next door to a Daedric ruin, which its people refuse to discuss.
why_would_change_if: The town would be fought over once any of the three roads mattered militarily.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a junction of navigable waters, or a road crossing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the hinge of a district; several villages depend on it
vibe_silhouette: The square town has three gates and no fourth wall. The market square lays its pitches out in three wedges.
vibe_palette: The town shows dust ochre. Awnings come in colours from three different regions. The black ruin is visible past the eastern gate.
vibe_materials: The town is built of mud-brick and reed. An interior-style uxith stands on the west side. Stormhold terrace stone stands at the north gate.
vibe_signature_feature: Goods from each road sell in their own third of the square. Mixing the goods is a fine.
vibe_condition: The town is well kept and expanding. It is entirely unfortified.
vibe_mood: The town is cosmopolitan by northern standards. Its people are superstitious and sharp.
vibe_approach: All three roads run at the town. The market noise carries further than the roofs do.
vibe_senses: Three dialects are spoken. Guar and porters crowd the town. A market bell rings at each of three gates.
player_purpose_hook: The ground is firm where three approaches converge. There is water enough for a market. The roads on either side flood and the town does not.
deferred_why: Tenmar Wall was merged into place.dunmer-north.ten-maur-wolk after lore critique L1. Lore:Ten-Maur-Wolk states that Tenmar Wall is the Imperial exonym for the Daedric site. A separate town at the same junction under a canonical name was therefore a duplicate. The name is now an alias on the ruin. The road-hinge market town survives as place.dunmer-north.wolk-market. The wolk-market town has a name that is not canonical and a provenance implied by the lore.

name: Ash Causeway
why_founding: The Dres built a stone causeway north from their frontier holdings towards the Tear road. The Argonians who inherited it keep it. Stone holds firm across four kilometres of bog that would drown anything else.
why_site_advantages: The causeway follows the line of a buried gravel ridge. The Dres surveyed the ridge. The road has followed the survey ever since.
why_occupants_motive: The holdings at either end maintain the causeway jointly. Both holdings dislike the arrangement and both keep it.
why_pressures: The causeway is Dunmer work in a province that reads stone as a moral error. Travellers use it constantly and speak of it badly. Three sections have been let go deliberately.
why_would_change_if: The causeway would be let go entirely if the northern holdings emptied. The north would then lose its only dry winter road.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: links two named places directly
vibe_silhouette: A straight stone way two carts wide runs dead level across sinking ground. Three visible gaps mark sections abandoned to the sink.
vibe_palette: The stone is Dres grey basalt. The sink water on either side is black. Raw brown timber decking covers the gaps.
vibe_materials: The causeway is cut Dunmer basalt. Argonian lashed-timber decking bridges the failures.
vibe_signature_feature: Three lengths of proper Dres masonry are deliberately not repaired. They are decked over in wood. The causeway alternates between two cultures every few hundred metres.
vibe_condition: The Dres sections are structurally excellent. The sections where timber decking bridges the gaps are seasonal.
vibe_approach: The causeway shows as a line on the water from a kilometre out. It looks the same underfoot as it does at that distance.
vibe_senses: Boots sound on stone, then on hollow timber, then on stone again.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The causeway is a hard road across ground that cannot otherwise be crossed in winter.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 8 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, nearPoint, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A Dres-surveyed gravel line crosses wet ground. It is the fast way over the plain for traffic that keeps to it.

name: Ash Holding
why_founding: The Dres household kept the holding for two generations. The upland ground then gave way under the compound in a single wet season.
why_site_advantages: The same spring and grazing that drew the family in undercut the ground beneath the compound.
why_occupants_motive: The sunk cellars were never resettled. Whatever hunts there now came up through the joined cellars after the houses went down.
why_pressures: The herders who once worked for the family will not go near the stair-throat. The compound used to stand there.
why_would_change_if: Shoring up the collapse would close the stair-throat. No herder has attempted it since the ground went.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Tear road and the Morrowind frontier
vibe_silhouette: A sunk depression marks where the walled compound used to stand. A stair-throat lies at the low point.
vibe_palette: The ash-grey render is broken and tilted. A black tomb door still stands upright at the compound's old edge. The brown grazing has gone to scrub.
vibe_materials: Velothi stonework is cracked and dropped at odd angles. Roof timbers have fallen through into the cellars below. The tomb door is intact where the ground held.
vibe_signature_feature: The compound's walls tilt into the collapse at every angle. The stair-throat lies at the deepest point.
vibe_condition: The compound is sunk and broken. The cellars below are undisturbed.
vibe_mood: The site feels unsettled. The ground moves underfoot.
vibe_approach: The tilted walls are visible on the ridge. The extent of the collapse is seen only later.
vibe_senses: Loose stone shifts underfoot. The ground sounds hollow where it should be solid. Guar bones are scattered at the collapse edge.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A Dunmer holding's cellars joined into a single warren when the ground gave way. Something then moved into the cellars.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 949 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: A Dunmer holding's ground gave way in one season. Its cellars are now joined into a single warren under the collapse.

name: Black Stage
why_founding: The Bogmother causeway ends at a channel that is too deep to bridge in stone. A ferry makes the last two hundred metres of the crossing.
why_site_advantages: The stage stands at the narrowest point of the channel. Stormhold's builders raised the causeway up to that point and stopped there.
why_occupants_motive: The ferry family are cousins of the causeway gang. Both sides inherited the arrangement. Neither side chose it.
why_pressures: Pilgrims who arrive at dusk often find the ferry on the far side.
why_would_change_if: Stormhold would replace the ferry with a span once it decided to spend the money. The span has been on the works list for sixty years.
siting_prefs_water_relation: across water too deep or wide to ford
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage
vibe_silhouette: A stone causeway ends at the water. The stage has a slipway, a bell post and a raft. The raft is usually on the wrong side.
vibe_palette: The stage is grey stone and black water. A rope runs down into the water.
vibe_materials: The slipway is cut stone and the ferry is tarred plank. Stormhold built the approach. The village built the crossing.
vibe_signature_feature: The last slab of the causeway is cut square. The square end suggests that the builders expected to continue.
vibe_condition: The slipway is sound. The ferry is patched. The bell rope is frayed.
vibe_mood: The ferry family are resigned to their situation. They obstruct travellers when it suits them.
vibe_approach: A kilometre of straight stone ends at the water. A bell stands at the water's edge.
vibe_senses: The bell rings for a long time. Water surrounds the stage. The ferry sets out from the far bank.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The causeway ferry is late every dusk, because the boat always comes from the far bank. The ferry family have refused to carry one household for five years.
why_site_won: ravine in upland hills (danger band 3), 330 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, route, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'eviction-repair'.
player_purpose_hook: The causeway ends and a ferry family begins. At dusk the boat is usually on the wrong bank.
siting_note: The terrainRequests of the record supply its named landform. Part 6's meso compiler carves that landform. The plotted landform class is the pre-carve ground.

name: Carries-Them-North
why_founding: Argonians die in Morrowind, in Tear's yards and in the Owings. Their bones are carried back down the pass.
why_site_advantages: This is the first stage on the Argonian side of the pass. The carry down from Tear is long. It ends here. The vault below the stage holds what the carriers cannot place. The vault has been filling for two hundred years.
why_occupants_motive: The keepers meet the carriers at the border post and take custody there. Both sides negotiated the arrangement. Both sides keep to it.
why_pressures: More bones come down the pass each year. Thorn's assembly was asked about it twice. The assembly has minuted neither question.
why_would_change_if: It would be a scandal if the border post refused a carrier. The border post has not yet refused a carrier.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a walked or poled route
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: between a carceral site and the interior
vibe_silhouette: A house and a bone house stand with a stone between them. They stand on the first flat ground below the pass.
vibe_palette: The bone house is limewash white. The other house is thatch. The pass is grey above both.
vibe_materials: The houses are mud and reed. The bone house is limewashed. A single dressed receiving stone stands between them.
vibe_signature_feature: A count board inside records how many came down the pass. It lists each year for the past sixty years. The last nine entries each top the year before.
vibe_condition: The stage is well kept. The keepers renew the limewash monthly, as the rite requires.
vibe_mood: The keepers are formal and gentle. The count alarms them.
vibe_approach: It is the first roof below the pass. There are two roofs, with a gap between them.
vibe_senses: Wind comes off the pass. Low talk carries. The carriers set their bundles down carefully.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Bone-carriers put down their bundles at the first rest. This season the count is wrong.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 271 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The stage is the first rest on the Argonian side of the pass. Bone-carriers set down their bundles and count them there.

name: Borrowed Tomb
why_founding: A Dunmer wayside tomb stands on the Tear road. Its own family emptied it when they left. A road family with nowhere else to go has lived in it since.
why_site_advantages: The tomb is dry, stone-built, roofed and beside the road. No other shelter on a three-hour stretch of road is free to use. The inner door has not been opened in forty years. The chambers behind it run further back than the antechamber suggests.
why_occupants_motive: The family live in the antechamber. The inner door stays shut. The family mention this to every guest within a minute of meeting.
why_pressures: Passing Dunmer find the occupation obscene. Passing Argonians find the scruple about the inner door unnecessary.
why_would_change_if: The family would vacate instantly and apologetically if any Dres heir arrived.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: inside any ruin type
vibe_silhouette: A stone tomb doorway stands beside the road. Washing hangs across the doorway. A cooking fire burns in the antechamber.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey Velothi stone. Domestic colour shows in the doorway. Road dust covers the ground.
vibe_materials: The tomb is Velothi masonry. The family added a reed lean-to at the door.
vibe_signature_feature: The inner door is swept clean and still shut. The family leave a bowl in front of it every evening.
vibe_condition: The structure is excellent. The domestic fittings are improvised.
vibe_mood: The family are homely and hospitable. They are a little nervous.
vibe_approach: From the road it looks like a tomb door. Laundry hangs on the door.
vibe_senses: Cooking echoes in a stone chamber. A child can be heard. The road lies outside.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A household returns to bury its dead in the tomb where a road family has lived for years. The occupant can name the household that owns the tomb, which is why he is not turned out.
why_site_won: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 181 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The tomb is a dry Dunmer tomb. Its occupant prefers that the fact goes unmentioned.

name: The Bound Urns
why_founding: The dead who are denied return to the Hist are bound into urns. The urns must be kept where a stray footstep will not break one.
why_site_advantages: The site is a dry rock shelter on the rim above the swamp. It is dry enough to keep clay. It is remote enough to be forgotten deliberately.
why_occupants_motive: An officeholder from Greylight visits twice a year to check the seals. Afterwards the officeholder says nothing about the visit.
why_pressures: Some urns here are from the last decade. The punishment is therefore still being handed down.
why_would_change_if: The shelter would be emptied if Greylight ruled the sentences complete. No officeholder has claimed that authority.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately outside a village's normal ground
vibe_silhouette: A dry overhang holds two hundred sealed clay urns. The urns stand in rows on ledges. The oldest are at the back and the newest at the front.
vibe_palette: The urns are red-brown clay. The rock is grey. The seals are black wax.
vibe_materials: The urns are fired clay sealed with wax. The ledges are cut minimally into the rock.
vibe_signature_feature: The urns carry dates. The front row was sealed in the last decade.
vibe_condition: Dry, ordered, inspected.
vibe_mood: The mood of the shelter is punitive and patient. The shelter is still in use.
vibe_approach: The overhang cannot be seen from below. It is reached by a climb. The rows extend back into the dark.
vibe_senses: The air is very dry. Voices are deadened. A faint sound comes from the front row.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One officeholder, whose count is the only record there is, counts the sealed urn shelter twice a year. Her count comes back one urn light.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 113 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The sealed urn shelter stands on the rim. An officeholder counts it twice a year and keeps the tally in her head.

name: Causeway Hearth
why_founding: A kilometre of open stone causeway in a province of storms needs one place to stop. The obligation supplies that place.
why_site_advantages: The hearth stands at the mid-point of the causeway. It is built out sideways on its own small platform.
why_occupants_motive: Families from Stormhold's south quarter keep the hearth by rota. They regard the duty as an honour and compete for it.
why_pressures: Pilgrim numbers have risen. The rota families are out of pocket.
why_would_change_if: It would embarrass the whole city if the hearth were found cold.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities
vibe_silhouette: A single small room is built out from the side of a stone causeway. It has a lamp bracket and no door.
vibe_palette: The hearth is grey stone and lamp yellow. Open bog lies in every direction.
vibe_materials: The lower walls are stone, which matches the construction of the causeway. The upper walls are reed and mud.
vibe_signature_feature: The fuel store is bigger than the room that it heats.
vibe_condition: The hearth is immaculate. The rota families compete on the quality of the fuel.
vibe_mood: The hearth is safe and exposed. It is free to anyone.
vibe_approach: It stands alone on a kilometre of straight stone. It is visible from both ends.
vibe_senses: Wind drops inside the room. A fire burns. Passing feet make the causeway ring.
player_purpose_hook: A fire and a roof stand at the mid-point of the causeway. The hearth is free. It has no beds. Travellers are not questioned there.

name: Causeway Lodge
why_founding: The Dres built a lodge at the midpoint of the Ash Causeway for a road-warden. An Argonian family now occupies it. The family inherited the duty along with the walls.
why_site_advantages: The lodge stands on the causeway's one widening. The widening is a stone apron that is large enough for a building. Surveyors put the apron there because they assumed that a warden would always be needed.
why_occupants_motive: Both end-holdings pay the family to keep the decked gaps passable. The causeway still works because of the family.
why_pressures: The lodge is a Dunmer building that the family cannot alter without admitting that they live in one. The interior is Argonian and the shell is Dres. The join between them is the whole domestic life of the family.
why_would_change_if: The lodge would fall to the dispute between the holdings if the family had no heir. The causeway would fall with it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with a crossing, landing or light
vibe_silhouette: A squat basalt block sits on a stone apron. The apron lies in the middle of a straight road across water. A reed lean-to is attached to the lee side of the block.
vibe_palette: The basalt is near-black Dres stone. The reed lean-to is gold. Grey sink water lies on both horizons.
vibe_materials: The masonry is cut Dunmer stone. An Argonian reed structure is built against the stone and never into it. The two materials are stacked and never blended.
vibe_signature_feature: The family live in the reed half of the lean-to. They store tools in the stone half. They have done so for four generations.
vibe_condition: The stone is perfect. The reed is renewed annually.
vibe_mood: The family are dutiful and isolated. They make dry jokes about the arrangement.
vibe_approach: The lodge stands alone on four kilometres of straight road. It takes an hour to reach from either end.
vibe_senses: Wind blows with nothing to break it. A plane works on timber. Water laps on stone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A hereditary duty is about to lapse. A road depends on that duty.
player_purpose_hook: The lodge is the warden's lodge on the causeway apron and holds one household and one boat. The household keeps a long list of who passed.

name: Charge Pond
why_founding: A wamasu holds a deep pond. The wamasu curses all the water around the pond to deadly convulsions.
why_site_advantages: The pond is deep still water. It is fed from below. Its outflow is too weak to clear it.
why_occupants_motive: The wamasu lives here because the pond is deep and quiet. Other creatures reach the pond only by accident and briefly.
why_pressures: The offerings of the villages have made people approach the pond on purpose. That approach is new and unwise.
why_would_change_if: Nothing would change. The pond stays lethal whatever arrives at it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a held pond, still and avoided
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a district hazard; villages route around it
vibe_silhouette: A black pond lies still. Dead standing trees ring it. No debris floats on it. The surface stays unbroken.
vibe_palette: The water is black. The timber is bleached and dead. A blue-white flash shows occasionally under the surface.
vibe_materials: Nothing is built here. The dead trees form the setting.
vibe_signature_feature: A ring of dead trees surrounds the pond. Every tree within ten metres of the water is dead and standing. Trees beyond that line are alive.
vibe_condition: Unchanging.
vibe_approach: The dead ring of trees is visible for two hundred metres.
vibe_senses: The pond is absolutely silent, then a crack sounds. The air smells of a storm on a clear day.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A wamasu pond kills two carriers. The shrine wardens see the animal only afterwards.
why_site_won: spring head in border mountains (danger band 3), 1109 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, remote, parent; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: Still black water holds a wamasu. The charge comes up through the water before the animal does.

name: Charge Works
why_founding: A wamasu is worth more dead than three ordinary game animals combined. Each wamasu taken has to be processed by a works.
why_site_advantages: The works stands on a spit downwind of the village. The spit is also downstream, so the water carries the waste away.
why_occupants_motive: The works family holds the sap-insulation technique. They have taken no apprentice from outside the family in four generations.
why_pressures: Charge-holding bone is the north's most valuable export after crystal. Stormhold's enchanters have offered to buy the whole output three years running.
why_would_change_if: The works would end with the family unless the daughter changes her mind. The technique would end with the family too.
siting_prefs_water_relation: near but not on a wamasu pond
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the only reason to live this close to that water
vibe_silhouette: Racks of translucent hide dry in rows. A bone store stands raised on posts. Amber sap wraps the posts.
vibe_palette: The hide is translucent grey-blue. The post wraps are amber. The organ jars give a faint constant glow.
vibe_materials: The buildings are timber and reed on insulated footings. The sap wrapping distinguishes the works from a fish shed.
vibe_signature_feature: The organ jars are the works' sole light source. The organ jars glow without fire.
vibe_condition: The works is clean and exact. A mistake in the work is fatal.
vibe_mood: The works feels precise and secretive. The works family is well off.
vibe_approach: At night the jar glow shows through the reed walls. The glow is visible from two hundred metres.
vibe_senses: The bone store gives off a faint crackle. Scraping sounds carry across the works. There are no open flames anywhere.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Two charged-goods works bid for the same wamasu stock. The bidding lasts until the hunters stop selling to either works.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 214 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: The works turns wamasu hide and gland into charged goods. It is the north's sole source of charged goods. The works buys raw stock.

name: Cold Holding
why_founding: The failed Dres holding stood empty for years. The family's heir did not come to reclaim it. A fire went through the compound before any blackguard band arrived.
why_site_advantages: A walled square and a sealed tomb behind it form a defensible base. The base has one door worth watching.
why_occupants_motive: The blackguard band moved in after the fire. The band uses the standing half as a base for work on the Tear road. The holding is close enough to reach the road and far enough to hide from it.
why_pressures: The tomb door is still sealed. The band has not opened the tomb door. The band will not touch a Dres ancestor tomb.
why_would_change_if: A Dres heir who arrives to reclaim the holding would have to deal with the band first.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Tear road and the Morrowind frontier
vibe_silhouette: A scorched walled square has lost half its roof. The tomb door stands untouched at the far end.
vibe_palette: The stone is scorched grey with black soot streaks. The tomb door is still black and clean.
vibe_materials: The Velothi stonework is cracked and smoke-blackened. The roof timbers burned through on one side. The fire left the tomb door untouched.
vibe_signature_feature: Fire gutted half the compound. The band re-roofed the other half roughly and occupies it.
vibe_condition: The holding is burned on one side. The band rebuilt the other side roughly.
vibe_approach: The scorch marks show on the ridge before the walls do.
vibe_senses: An old smoke smell lingers in the stone. A dog barks somewhere behind the walls. The tomb door beneath the holding is silent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A blackguard band works out of a burned holding. The holding is close enough for the band to hit the Tear road twice a season.
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 818 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, nearPoint, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The holding is a burned Dunmer holding. A blackguard band works its standing half. The band is close enough to reach the Tear road.
siting_note: The catalogue moved the holding onto the rim gap at (5473, 406). It is a hostile, dungeon-like place at least 320 m from every route. It is at least 450 m from every other fight. It fills the region's listed off-route D3 gap. The gap is listed in hostility-frequency.md, dated 2026-09-04.

name: Crown Terrace
why_founding: On a hammock the ground is precious and the crown is dry. The households put their dead in the canopy and not in the ground. The terrace is a platform in that canopy, above the houses and above the flood. It stands an hour up the hammock from Last Landing. It lies within a day's traffic of Thorn.
why_site_advantages: The terrace stands in the hammock's tallest stand of trees. Three trunks are close enough to carry a terrace. The canopy is dense enough to hide the terrace from the marsh.
why_occupants_motive: The hammock's whole population tends the terrace by turns. Tending the terrace is a rotating duty. A household that refuses its turn is put off the hammock.
why_pressures: The terrace is full. The village is arguing over three options. The options are to build a second terrace, extend this one, or bury in the soil after all.
why_would_change_if: Within five years the village must choose one of the options. Both answers cost the village something.
siting_prefs_water_relation: above the flood, in the crown of a hammock's tallest stand
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one per inhabited hammock; the region's signature sacred form
vibe_silhouette: A railed timber platform stands in the crown of three trees. It is invisible from the marsh. It is impossible to miss from inside the village. Wrapped forms lie in rows on the platform.
vibe_palette: The canopy is green-black. The wrapping cloth is bleached. The timber is pale bone-grey from long exposure.
vibe_materials: The platform timber is lashed and renewed by rotation. The wrappings are the hammock's own cloth. Everything on the terrace came from the hammock.
vibe_signature_feature: The dead are laid in rows in the order they went up. The terrace records the order of the village's deaths.
vibe_condition: The terrace is kept to the inch. The terrace is completely full.
vibe_mood: The terrace feels reverent and crowded. The terrace is under pressure.
vibe_approach: The climb starts inside the village. The terrace appears overhead through the leaves.
vibe_senses: Wind moves through the canopy. Cloth moves in the wind. The village below is silent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The terrace is a burial ground where a visitor is either admitted or trespassing. It shows the island's unresolvable argument in physical form.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 155 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The island puts its dead up in the canopy. The terrace is full. The village has not agreed what to do next.
siting_note: The record's terrainRequests supply the landform it names. Part 6's meso compiler carves that landform. The plotted landform class is the pre-carve ground.

name: The Jumped Claim
why_founding: A licensed party proved a garnet seam on the rim scree. Four men who had followed them up ran them off it. The claim still belongs legally to the licensed party. The Crystalgate register has not been altered.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the rim scree above the root gallery. The rock there is exposed, so seams would show if they were there.
why_occupants_motive: The claim-jumpers work the seam by day. They hold the approach by night. They treat a climber on the scree as a claim-jumper by default.
why_pressures: The cutting houses buy the claim-jumpers' stone anyway. The arrangement would have failed within two seasons without those sales.
why_would_change_if: The camp would empty overnight if a seam were struck. Crystalgate would move to the new seam.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a known extraction district
vibe_silhouette: Test pits are scattered across a scree slope, each with a stake. One cook shelter is shared by four men who are competitors.
vibe_palette: The scree is grey. The stake wood is pale. There is one canvas awning.
vibe_materials: The camp uses canvas, stakes and stacked stone wind-breaks. Nothing in the camp is meant to last a winter.
vibe_signature_feature: Forty claim stakes stand across the slope. Each stake carries a name and a date. Most of the dates are old.
vibe_condition: The camp is provisional and failing. It is four seasons deep.
vibe_mood: The camp feels watchful and dug-in. The claim-jumpers are short with strangers.
vibe_approach: The white stakes on the grey scree can be read from the valley track at a kilometre.
vibe_senses: Hammering on rock sounds at intervals. Wind blows across the scree. The claim-jumpers share a kettle.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Claim-jumpers on the scree hold ground. They cannot legally sell from that ground.
why_site_won: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 1271 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Claim-jumpers hold the rim scree. They ran the licensed party off. They hold the approach at night.

name: The Delta Byre
why_founding: The Tear road runs on guar. The delta breeds Glowgill, the strain that will work wet ground without foundering.
why_site_advantages: The byre has brackish delta grazing on firm islands. The grazing is poor for crops and ideal for a Glowgill herd.
why_occupants_motive: The byre breeds guar and sells to the caravans of both provinces. That makes the byre the least political business in the north.
why_pressures: The breeding family owns the Glowgill strain. A Dres factor has twice tried to buy the breeding stock outright.
why_would_change_if: The byre would be bought out within a decade. It stays independent if the family keeps refusing. The daughter may not keep refusing.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: serves a coastal settlement's transport
vibe_silhouette: Rail pens stand on three low islands. Guar swim between the islands. The byre is built out over the water on piles.
vibe_palette: Guar hide is green-grey. The water is silver. The rail timber is black with salt.
vibe_materials: The pens use split rail and piled timber. The pens are half in the water.
vibe_signature_feature: Herders drive the herd from island to island through the channel. The swimming crossings happen twice a day.
vibe_condition: Salt corrodes the timber and herders constantly replace it. Nothing at the byre lasts five years.
vibe_approach: Swimming guar are visible before any structure is.
vibe_senses: Guar call across the water. Splashing sounds from the channel. The air smells of salt and dung.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A herder will part with a glowgill guar for a service. The herder accepts a service in place of coin.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 143 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Glowgill guar graze on brackish islands. The byre offers mounts and milk. A herder will trade a beast for the right favour.

name: Diggings Ladder
why_founding: The Silyanorn diggings run down into the ravine. The crystal comes out on ropes. Builders put a ladder tower up the ravine wall. The tower gets the hands down and the stone up without using the road.
why_site_advantages: The ravine wall has enough ledge to seat platforms every four metres. A working face lies directly below.
why_occupants_motive: Hoist crews use the tower and are paid by weight. The tower is the fastest way in and out of the diggings. The hoist crews use it whatever its condition.
