why_pressures: The tower is a works structure and the diggings treat it as one. Crews repair it when it fails. The diggings' ledger records each failure as lost time.
why_would_change_if: The tower would be replaced with a proper stair. That happens the year Stormhold's vicecanons price the lost time honestly.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: placed where a viewshed pass shows a dead zone
vibe_silhouette: Timber platforms and ladders zigzag up a ravine wall. A hoist frame stands at the top. A working face of raw rock lies below.
vibe_palette: Crystal dust coats every surface blue-green. The timber is grey. The ravine floor is wet black.
vibe_materials: The timber is pinned to rock and is not lashed. Dunmer taught the mine work, unlike the marsh's basketry.
vibe_signature_feature: Blue-green crystal dust coats every platform. It also coats every hand that works there. The diggings' crews are identifiable at a distance.
vibe_condition: The tower is hard-used. Crews patch it after a failure. The failures are on a list.
vibe_approach: The hoist is audible before the ravine shows. On arrival the tower stands below the rim.
vibe_senses: A hoist ratchet clicks. Workers trim rock. A worker coughs.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tower is a fast, unsafe way in and out of the diggings.
why_site_won: ravine in upland hills (danger band 3), 836 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, bound; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Platforms stand every four metres down a ravine wall. The tower is the fast way to the working face. It works if the ladders hold.
siting_note: The tower is bound to Silyanorn Diggings. It exists as the diggings' hoist route. It is sited on the ravine wall above the working face and is not plotted freely. Its regionClasses now describe the ravine ground at the diggings. The semantic audit will read a region mismatch until the next plot moves it off its old north-marsh position.

name: Divers' Landing
why_founding: A lake with a drowned xanmeer in it produces divers. The landing is where the divers sort and sell what they raise.
why_site_advantages: The landing stands on the nearest firm bank to the drowned terrace. Deep water lies two boat-lengths out.
why_occupants_motive: The divers work the terrace. They argue in public and constantly about which chambers are permissible.
why_pressures: Greylight's minders have declared parts of the terrace off limits. The landing cannot enforce that ban. Ignoring the ban is no easier.
why_would_change_if: The villages together would shut the landing if a Hist chamber were ever stripped.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with drowned ground it works
vibe_silhouette: Two shelves stand under a reed roof. One shelf is long and full and one is short and almost empty. The lake goes dark green ten metres out.
vibe_palette: Wet stone is grey. Weed is green. The reed roof and lake water darken every surface.
vibe_materials: The landing has timber racks and a reed shelter. Every object under the shelter came up from below.
vibe_signature_feature: Two shelves hold what may be sold and what must go back.
vibe_condition: Working and permanently wet.
vibe_mood: The landing feels argumentative and amphibious. The divers are scrupulous under strain.
vibe_approach: The reed shore runs unbroken for a kilometre except at the landing. From the water the break is unmistakable.
vibe_senses: Water drips. A diver surfaces. Divers argue about a fitting.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The divers argue in public about which drowned rooms may be stripped. Then one room is stripped. The village minders forbid a stretch of drowned ruin. The minders cannot patrol that stretch.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 701 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, nearPoint, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: The divers work the drowned terrace. They sell what they bring up. They hire divers who can hold their breath long enough.

name: The Drawdown Flats
why_founding: The northern lake drops three metres in the dry season. The drop exposes ground that is underwater for most of the year.
why_site_advantages: The flats lie on a shallow shelf on the north side of the lake. The shelf is the largest area that the annual drawdown exposes.
why_occupants_motive: No household lives on the flats. Gleaners work the exposed ground for the eight weeks that it exists.
why_pressures: Each year the drawdown exposes different things. In some years the things exposed are ones that people would prefer to leave covered.
why_would_change_if: The flats would become permanent ground if the lake fell for good. The villages dread that outcome.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the lake region's signature seasonal event
vibe_silhouette: The flats are a wide plain of cracked grey mud. The lake lies a long way out. Objects that are not rocks stand up out of the mud.
vibe_palette: The colours are crack-pattern grey, weed black drying to brown and distant water.
vibe_materials: Nothing is built on the flats. Each year the lake leaves a different set of objects on the mud.
vibe_signature_feature: The strandline is a curve of debris that marks where the water stopped this year. Last year's strandline lies above this year's.
vibe_condition: Reset annually.
vibe_mood: The mood is bleak, with open mud to the horizon.
vibe_approach: From the shore the water lies far out across the flats.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear mud cracking underfoot. Gulls call a long way off. Wind crosses the open mud.
why_site_won: open water in border mountains (danger band 3), 708 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: For a few weeks each year the lake pulls back. A drain hole opens in the mud during those weeks. After the weeks end, the hole lies under three metres of water.
siting_note: The northern rim basin reads 'border mountains' on the region raster. The classification of the rim covers the lake and the fen floor inside it. The water identity in the record and the raster class describe the same ground.

name: Dres Rows
why_founding: House Dres built the rows as labour quarters for a saltrice plantation. House Dres owned the people who lived in them. Since the secession their descendants have lived in the rows. Those descendants now own the fields.
why_site_advantages: The rows stand between the fields and the water, which is where a plantation puts its labour. The site is convenient for the work and damp. Residents cannot leave quickly when the flood comes.
why_occupants_motive: Residents stay because moving would mean building new homes. The rows work well enough. Every winter the households discuss what living in the rows means. The talk changes nothing.
why_pressures: Dunmer built the rows. Every household has altered its own unit. The terrace shows a two-hundred-year argument over how much of the original to keep.
why_would_change_if: The rows would be pulled down once the field titles were settled. The Owings have not agreed to settle the titles with any household.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a road that stopped being used
vibe_silhouette: Two long parallel terraces of identical stone-based units face each other across a beaten yard. Each unit is altered differently above the door line.
vibe_palette: The stone is Dres grey below. Above it the households chose reed, plank, paint and one tiled roof. Saltrice green lies beyond both ends.
vibe_materials: The lower walls are Dunmer masonry. The upper walls are Argonian work, done unit by unit.
vibe_signature_feature: At waist height the building changes culture. The line runs along the whole length of both terraces.
vibe_condition: The structure is excellent. The domestic fittings are improvised.
vibe_mood: The mood is ambivalent and industrious. The households joke about their situation.
vibe_approach: The entrance is at the end of the yard. The two terraces run away in a symmetry that the alterations then break.
vibe_senses: Two hundred people fill the hard-surfaced yard. The households tread saltrice. The residents use a Dunmeris word or two without noticing.
quest_hooks_opportunity: TA03 uses the labourers' quarters. Freed households hold fields under the Owings. The building shows the history of the province in one elevation.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: BC01 · tier-2; LD38 · tier-3; MQ12 · tier-3; province system · tier-1
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 362 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The rows are plantation quarters between the fields and the water. The people who were once housed here own the fields now. The ledger is kept badly.

name: Drover Camp
why_founding: The Naga range further north in the wet season than the road wardens will put in writing. The Gideon-Stormhold caravan road through wet ground is a hunting lane.
why_site_advantages: The camp lies where the delta section of the Gideon-Stormhold road runs between two channels. The road has no way out of that section.
why_occupants_motive: The Naga camp here for the season and take what passes. The road wardens do not class this as ordinary banditry.
why_pressures: Thorn's levy sweeps the section twice a year. Both times the levy finds an empty camp.
why_would_change_if: The camp would not exist in a dry year. The road wardens forget the camp between wet seasons.
siting_prefs_water_relation: commands traffic and offers an escape
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a route with traffic worth robbing
vibe_silhouette: The road looks empty. In the reeds beside it are trampled beds, drying racks and much bone.
vibe_palette: The colours are reed gold and bone white over black water.
vibe_materials: The camp has no structure. The Naga press beds into the reeds and lash racks together from cane.
vibe_signature_feature: The racks hold goods taken off the road. The goods dry in plain sight, thirty metres from the road.
vibe_condition: The camp is seasonal. The Naga remake it each wet season in a slightly different reed bed.
vibe_mood: The mood is predatory and unhurried. The Naga are at home here.
vibe_approach: From the road the camp looks like an ordinary reed bank. The smell of drying meat then arrives from the wrong side.
vibe_senses: Reeds move against the wind. No voices are heard. Water runs nearby.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A Naga camp stands where the road has no way round the channels. Thorn's levy finds the camp empty twice a year.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 325 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A Naga camp stands where the road cannot leave the channels. The Naga take what passes. By the dry season they are gone.

name: The Drowned Terrace
why_founding: The ground of a xanmeer subsided into the lake. The subsidence took a complete Merethic building down intact.
why_site_advantages: The terrace lies in a lake basin over soft ground. Subsidence is common in that basin.
why_occupants_motive: The building is empty. Divers from the nearest village take stone fittings from it. The divers see this as different from looting a standing xanmeer.
why_pressures: Greylight does not accept the distinction that the divers make. Greylight has said so twice at the market.
why_would_change_if: A serious quarrel would start if a diver brought up a fitting from a Hist chamber.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in drowned country; often near a drowned village
vibe_silhouette: One corner of a terrace breaks the lake surface like a step. Beneath it lies a whole building in green light.
vibe_palette: The colours are surface silver, green underwater light and pale stone going blue with depth.
vibe_materials: The walls are xanmeer ashlar, entirely intact. Lake weed picks out every carved line.
vibe_signature_feature: The building is complete. Swimmers can pass its stairs and doorways as built.
vibe_condition: The building is perfectly preserved by the water.
vibe_approach: From the surface the terrace is one stone step in open water. The rest of the building lies beneath it.
vibe_senses: Underwater silence surrounds the swimmer. Divers hold their breath. The stone is felt under the hands.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The divers argue in public about which drowned rooms may be stripped. Then one room is stripped.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 894 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: One stone step shows in open water. A whole building lies beneath it in green light.

name: Empty Socket
why_founding: Builders raised a small Barsaebic structure around a single stone socket. The stone is gone. The record cut beside the socket says that the stone was taken in the same generation in which the building went up.
why_site_advantages: The site is a rock knoll clear of the flood. It lies close enough to the Silyanorn system to belong to it. The crews of the diggings have stopped checking it.
why_occupants_motive: Searchers have gone through the chamber from top to bottom. Only the socket and the record remain in it.
why_pressures: The record beside the socket is legible. It gives the name of the person who took the stone. The Whispers scholars have found that name in no other source.
why_would_change_if: The chamber would be the most important room in the north if the stone were put back. The Whispers scholars say so often.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one of a set; the set is the puzzle
vibe_silhouette: A single low domed chamber of Ayleid block stands on a knoll. It has one square doorway and no other opening.
vibe_palette: The block is pale outside. Inside, wet stone gives a green half-light. One black square marks the socket.
vibe_materials: The walls are unornamented Barsaebic block work. The chamber is single-celled and was built for one purpose.
vibe_signature_feature: The socket is a cut cube recess at waist height. A name is cut into the wall beside it. The Whispers scholars have not matched the name to any record.
vibe_condition: Intact and completely empty.
vibe_mood: The mood is bare. The chamber holds only the socket.
vibe_approach: The dome shows above the scrub from one direction only.
vibe_senses: Water drips in a small hard room. Otherwise the chamber is silent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The chamber is a lock with the key missing. The record names a thief. The Whispers scholars have not found the stone.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD31 · tier-3; LD70 · tier-3; tier-1 owned
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 358 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The chamber is an Ayleid keystone chamber with the keystone gone. The diggings below have not cut through to it yet.

name: Field-Edge Hearth
why_founding: The hearth obligation applies in field country too. In field country the people who come are mostly those who have just lost an Owing case.
why_site_advantages: The hearth stands at the edge of the terraces. The road from the court of Thorn comes out into the fields there.
why_occupants_motive: The rota of Saltmarch keeps the hearth. The Dunmer households take their turn. That arrangement took a generation to reach.
why_pressures: The field-owners regard the hearth as a shelter for runaways and have said so. The villages have declined to discuss it.
why_would_change_if: The hearth would become a flashpoint the first time that an overseer took a person out of it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities
vibe_silhouette: A round house stands at a field corner. Its door faces the court road. A fire is always laid.
vibe_palette: The thatch is pale, with saltrice silver on three sides. Road dust lies on the fourth side.
vibe_materials: The walls are mud, wattle and reed. The Dunmer rota added a lacquered lintel. The households do not remark on it.
vibe_signature_feature: The lacquered lintel is the mark of a foreign household. It sits on a house that belongs to no single household.
vibe_condition: Eight households keep the house up in turn. The repairs are in eight different hands.
vibe_mood: The mood is quiet and watchful.
vibe_approach: The house sits at a field corner in the open. Its door faces the court road.
vibe_senses: Wind passes through the saltrice. A fire burns. Visitors do not explain why they are here.
player_purpose_hook: The hearth stands where the road of Thorn comes out into the fields. It is open to anyone who works.

name: Field Gate
why_founding: The field-owners of Thorn keep a levy. The levy must be quartered where the fields end and the road to Morrowind begins.
why_site_advantages: The town lies in the gap between the terrace country and the pass road. An approach from the north has to cross that gap.
why_occupants_motive: The levy exists to protect titles. Its officers are the sons of the field-owners.
why_pressures: Half the levy are Dunmer. Observers call that either sensible recruiting or a serious mistake.
why_would_change_if: The levy would be disbanded the year after the title disputes of Thorn were settled. The field-owners show no sign of settling them.
siting_prefs_water_relation: at a crossing or a road
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with a fort, occupied or not
vibe_silhouette: A drill ground has a town on three sides. Open fields lie on the fourth side. Shellback armour dries on every rail.
vibe_palette: The colours are shell-plate grey-brown, saltrice silver beyond and dust.
vibe_materials: Mud-brick billets surround a beaten drill square. The only fortification is a fence.
vibe_signature_feature: The shell racks stand outside the billets. The levy grows its armour and racks it outside to cure in the sun.
vibe_condition: The garrison is serviceable and crowded. It has no wall.
vibe_approach: The drill counting carries across the open fields for a kilometre. The drill ground itself comes into view after that.
vibe_senses: Soldiers drill. Shell plates knock together. Two languages of complaint are heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The border garrison is the physical crossing between Argonian and Dunmer claims on the saltrice ground. It runs a pass-and-permit regime that can be used, forged or broken. The security pact of the Accord needs a place where it visibly succeeds or fails.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD95 · tier-3; LD96 · tier-3; LD97 · tier-3; LD98 · tier-3; LD99 · tier-3; LV01 · tier-3; LV02 · tier-3; LV03 · tier-3; LV04 · tier-3; LV05 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
player_purpose_hook: Guards stop and inspect every northern cart here. A market has grown up around the waiting.

name: First-Counted
why_founding: The Flu filled this ground first, in the first season. Stormhold did not yet understand how the Flu spread.
why_site_advantages: The ground is the terrace below Stormhold's south gate. The mowing gangs could carry the dead no further. The dead of the first season went into a cut in the terrace. They were not placed in graves. The cut goes down three levels.
why_occupants_motive: Stormhold's authorities maintain the ground. The mowing gang works between the second and fourth hours. That working slot has stood in the gang's warrant for a century.
why_pressures: Kothringi dead are buried here alongside Argonian dead. Neither people's rite permits the mixing. Both peoples accepted it.
why_would_change_if: The ground would become the north's central memorial. That happens only if the people of Stormhold could bear to make it one.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village
vibe_silhouette: The ground is a wide flat terrace of grass. A field of driven poles stands at one end. Kothringi cairns stand at the other end. A strip of unmarked grass lies between them.
vibe_palette: The poles and cairns are weathered grey. The grass is green. The terraces of Stormhold rise above the whole ground.
vibe_materials: The poles and the cairns stand in the same ground. The markers of neither tradition were adapted to the other.
vibe_signature_feature: An empty middle strip of unmarked grass separates the two traditions. The two peoples were buried side by side.
vibe_condition: The grass is mown and edged. The mowing gang works at night.
vibe_mood: The mood is heavy and unresolved. The people of Stormhold are ashamed of the ground.
vibe_approach: The ground is the first outside Stormhold's south gate. The people of Stormhold do not discuss it.
vibe_senses: The terraces of Stormhold loom above the ground. Poles knock against one another in the wind.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An unknown person adds names to the count of the Flu memorial. The names are cut in new stone, at night. A grassland field turns up a weapon. The weapon settles an inheritance that two families have fought over.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 140 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The ground holds the first Flu dead, counted and stacked. It lies below Stormhold's south gate. The count is still legible.

name: Fish Boon Ground
why_founding: Hissmir's Fish Boon Feast needs a place to happen. The pilgrimage xanmeer is not that place. This tidal flat below the village has hosted the feast since it began.
why_site_advantages: The site is a wide gravel flat where the tide slows. The water is shallow enough for netting from the bank. The flat is wide enough for the whole village and its pilgrims. Every flood scours the flat clean.
why_occupants_motive: The flat is empty outside the feast. It carries no buildings. The flood scours it every year. The village expects the yearly scouring.
why_pressures: Pilgrim numbers have grown past what the flat can feed. The Root Stewards may not turn a comer away. The feast now runs three days where it once ran one.
why_would_change_if: The feast ground would move upstream if the channel shifted. The channel shifts about once a century. The last shift was in 4E 79.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: serves a settlement cluster
vibe_silhouette: The ground is a clean gravel flat beside slow water. A line of fire-scars marks the shingle. A stone fish-weir footing stands at the head of the flat.
vibe_palette: The shingle is wet grey and the tidal water is brown. In season a long line of fires burns on the flat. In season a great deal of silver fish lies on the stones.
vibe_materials: Only the weir footing stays standing all year. The village brings the rest down for the feast. The village carries the rest back up afterwards.
vibe_signature_feature: The fire-scars are a line of blackened patches in the shingle. The village renews them every year in the same places.
vibe_condition: The flood scours the flat clean each year. The feast marks the flat again.
vibe_mood: The mood is generous and crowded. The Root Stewards are anxious about the numbers.
vibe_approach: The pilgrim path comes down onto the flat. The whole feast lies laid out below the path.
vibe_senses: Out of season only the tidal water is heard. In season fires burn and fish are gutted at speed. In season there is a great deal of talking.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Fish Boon Feast is a place and a date. The calendar delivers the feast as a scene. A pilgrim crowd has outgrown its ground.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 269 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A netting festival is held on the gravel flat. A whole district gathers in one place, pilgrims included. The crowd is drunk by dusk.

name: The Flu Cordon
why_founding: The Flu began at Stormhold. The north cordoned itself off from its own city. No other line in the province was drawn from the inside out.
why_site_advantages: The cordon is a ring drawn at a day's walk from the city. On this side the ring falls on the rim ground. The rim villages never farmed that ground.
why_occupants_motive: The vicecanons pay a marker-walker to keep the cellar swept. The marker-walker sleeps in the cellar four nights a month.
why_pressures: No record in Stormhold admits that the line was drawn against Stormhold. The ledger of the vicecanons calls the line the northern works.
why_would_change_if: A re-marking of the cordon by the vicecanons would be a diplomatic incident. The markers stand unaltered for that reason.
siting_prefs_water_relation: uses water as part of the line where it can
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: encircles a plague-abandoned village or a cairn field
vibe_silhouette: Marker stones stand at intervals along the line. Their carved faces turn away from the city.
vibe_palette: Lichen grey, marsh green.
vibe_materials: The markers are undressed set stone. They match cordons elsewhere in the province. The markers of this cordon face inward.
vibe_signature_feature: Every marker faces out from Stormhold. The orientation shows which side the line was meant to hold.
vibe_condition: Markers have fallen in places. Fallen stone is left where it dropped. It is not re-set and it is not carried off.
vibe_approach: Traffic on the Tear road crosses the line unaware. The road then meets the next marker stone.
vibe_senses: The site offers wind and the road. Little else is present at this distance from the city.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The cordon cellar is the driest shelter on the rim. The rim villagers will not go near the cellar. An unknown person has taken the cellar over.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 346 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The rim villages avoid the cordon cellar. The cellar is dry and roofed. It is the safest floor within an hour of the rootworm ground.

name: The Freed Rows
why_founding: The pens emptied and the people in them had nowhere to be. A shelter grew where those people stopped walking.
why_site_advantages: The site lies a day south of the pen yard. A column of exhausted people got that far on the first day.
why_occupants_motive: The shelter persists because people still arrive. The arrivals are now Owing runaways and are no longer freed slaves. The board at the road does not distinguish between them.
why_pressures: The Owing brokers regard the shelter as a receiving house for stolen labour. They say so in Thorn's court.
why_would_change_if: A court order would close the shelter the day the Owing were ruled property. That case is being argued now.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: within a day of a hard owing district, out of its sight
vibe_silhouette: Three long open-sided shelters stand on the site. A board stands at the road end with names painted on it. The board carries hundreds of names.
vibe_palette: The roofs are thatch. The board is whitewashed. The names are painted by a hundred different hands.
vibe_materials: The shelters are built of mud, reed and open frames. By design, no shelter here has a door.
vibe_signature_feature: The name board holds hundreds of names. Residents wrote their own names where they can write. Others wrote the names of residents who cannot write.
vibe_condition: The shelters are well kept and constantly extended. The shelter is permanently under-provisioned.
vibe_approach: The board stands at the road edge. Visitors read the board before the shelters come into view.
vibe_senses: Many people sleep in the shelters. A cooking fire is kept in overnight. A resident reads names aloud.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The shelter of the Chainbreakers knows which northern house still works people. The Chainbreakers say they freed those people.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 460 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.cut-and-stack (+0.77).
player_purpose_hook: The shelter is where freed people got to on the first day. The Chainbreakers there know who is still holding whom.

name: Gravel Six
why_founding: A second rise lies half a day north of the first hamlet. Overflow from the first hamlet settled it two generations later. The two hamlets are related and competitive. Each thinks that the flood arrangements of the other are inadequate.
why_site_advantages: The rise is longer and lower than its neighbour's. That gives more ground and less margin against floods. The founders made that trade knowingly.
why_occupants_motive: The hamlet's residents live on saltrice from the plain. A ferry-rope crosses the channel. The ferry-rope operators earn only in the wet months, when the hamlet needs it.
why_pressures: In a bad year the rise goes under by a hand's depth. The hamlet then moves bodily to its rival's rise for three weeks. Neither hamlet enjoys the arrangement.
why_would_change_if: The hamlet would abandon the rise after two consecutive bad years. Every household has been counting since the last bad year.
siting_prefs_water_relation: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: refuge for its neighbours in flood
vibe_silhouette: Eight roofs form a long low string. A rope-ferry post stands at one end. The rise can be recognised as a rise only from a boat.
vibe_palette: Saltrice is green in season and silt grey out of season. The post of the ferry rope is tarred black.
vibe_materials: The houses are reed and mud. They use an unusual amount of tarred timber. The timber was salvaged off the channel traffic.
vibe_signature_feature: The rope post is tarred black and taller than any house. It is the hamlet's one vertical. It is the hamlet's one source of cash.
vibe_condition: The houses are serviceable and patched with river salvage. The hamlet is visibly poorer than its rival.
vibe_mood: The mood is chippy and hard-working. The residents are waiting on the water.
vibe_approach: From the channel the post shows first. The houses show only when a boat is level with them.
vibe_senses: A wet rope creaks under load. Saltrice is trodden. Two dogs never stop barking.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A rope ferry works only when the water is high. The route appears and disappears with the water.
player_purpose_hook: Six households live on a lower rise. A rope ferry works only in the wet. The hamlet feuds with the hamlet upstream.

name: Guar Ground
why_founding: The site is a second, smaller drying ground on the Thorn side. Dunmer holdings drive their guar here in the dry months. The saltrice ground stands bare in the dry months.
why_site_advantages: A shallow basin holds a skin of water two months longer than the plain. Its hard edges hold a herd.
why_occupants_motive: Two Dunmer holdings and one Argonian village use it in rotation. The Dres set the rotation. No holding has owned the ground since. The rotation still holds.
why_pressures: The guar and the wild herds need the same water in the same weeks. The holdings deal with that by killing whatever else arrives.
why_would_change_if: The rotation would break in the first year that a holding brought more guar than the basin can water. One of the two holdings is visibly building its herd to that size.
siting_prefs_water_relation: the last water in a drying landscape
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the region's ecological engine; villages time their year on it
vibe_silhouette: The ground is a shallow bowl of cracked mud. A skin of water lies in the middle. Driven stakes and a great many guar ring the bowl.
vibe_palette: The mud is cracked and pale. The water is brown. The guar hide is grey-green. Dunmer holding banners hang on the stakes in dull red.
vibe_materials: The builders used driven stakes and a rope line. The sole structure is a fence. The fence comes down when the rains come.
vibe_signature_feature: The rotation stakes carry three sets of marks on the same posts. There is one set of marks per user. The fence itself records whose weeks these are.
vibe_condition: Bare, hard-used, entirely temporary.
vibe_approach: The dust cloud shows from a long way off. The noise carries as far.
vibe_senses: The guar are constantly heard. The mud is cracked underfoot. A herder counts aloud in Dunmeris.
quest_hooks_opportunity: No single holding owns the rotation. Three users keep the rotation until one grows past its share.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1851 m from the nearest route; no free 'island' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, danger, landform.
player_purpose_hook: A basin holds water two months longer than the plain. Three herds' worth of marks stand on the same posts.

name: High Wrappings
why_founding: The site is the crown terrace of the second hammock. It is older and smaller than the terrace of the first hammock. Its people will not take charity from the first hammock. Their dead have been up there longer.
why_site_advantages: A single enormous trunk has a natural triple fork at fourteen metres. The fork needed almost no building to carry a terrace.
why_occupants_motive: The village tends the lower wrappings. The last climb past the third fork was two years ago. The trunk above the fork is hollow. A creature dens in the hollow trunk.
why_pressures: The trunk is dying from the top. The terrace is in the dying part. The village keeps that quiet.
why_would_change_if: The terrace would have to come down before the tree does. The village has not begun to plan for it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: above the flood, in one great trunk over the village
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one per inhabited hammock; the region's signature sacred form
vibe_silhouette: A dark platform is wedged in a triple fork high in one great trunk. Wrappings show from below through the leaves.
vibe_palette: The fork bark is black. The wrapping cloth has gone grey-brown with age. The leaves above are yellowing as they die.
vibe_materials: Little is built here. The fork carries the load. The timber forms a floor and is not a structure.
vibe_signature_feature: These wrappings are generations older than those of the first hammock. Both hammocks can state the difference in age.
vibe_condition: The terrace is older, plainer and better sited than its rival. It stands in a tree that is failing.
vibe_mood: The mood below the third fork is grave and proud.
vibe_approach: The climb is made only with the permission of the village.
vibe_senses: Wind blows at fourteen metres. Old cloth hangs on the fork. The drying leaves sound wrong.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A dying tree holds the dead of a village. The village has no plan for where the dead go next.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 1086 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.tunnel-rat-gallery (+0.76).
player_purpose_hook: The dead of the second island are wrapped fourteen metres up a triple fork. The hollow above them is occupied.

name: Last Landing
why_founding: The north-eastern river is navigable as far as Last Landing. Cargo that goes further inland is carried by porters.
why_site_advantages: A rock sill crosses the channel. Deep water lies below the sill. Boulders lie above the sill. The channel has a bank on both sides.
why_occupants_motive: Last Landing exists to change cargo from hull to back. Every trade at the landing follows from that change of cargo.
why_pressures: The porters and the boat crews price against each other twice a day. They bargain in public and loudly.
why_would_change_if: The landing would move upstream permanently if the sill were blasted. Two generations of residents have proposed blasting the sill.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node
vibe_silhouette: A quay with masts stands at the landing. A rock sill lies in white water just upstream. Above the sill is a porter yard with no boats.
vibe_palette: The river is green below the sill and white over it. The two halves of the settlement are quite different colours.
vibe_materials: The quay below the sill is stone. Above the sill the settlement is timber and reed.
vibe_signature_feature: The sill is the signature feature. A person who stands on the sill can touch a laden boat on one side. A laden porter is within reach on the other side.
vibe_condition: The landing is busy and worn. The sill divides the landing in two.
vibe_mood: The mood is competitive and loud. The work is hard on backs.
vibe_approach: The white water can be heard from a long way off. The masts appear below the white water.
vibe_senses: Water runs over rock. Ropes creak. Two crews shout rates at each other.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Boats stop at the head of navigation. The porters above the sill can hold the whole route to ransom.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 282 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Last Landing is the head of navigation. Boats stop below the sill. Porters work above it. Cargo and travellers alike change hands at the sill.

name: The Last Stone Course
why_founding: Builders stopped a xanmeer mid-course when the Duskfall came. The province has kept the xanmeer unfinished on purpose since then.
why_site_advantages: The site is a rise on the northern edge of the swamp. The rise is dry enough for stacking stone. The builders chose it while they still expected to finish.
why_occupants_motive: Villagers bring their young to the Last Stone Course. A teacher tells them why the province stopped building in stone.
why_pressures: Mazzatun is four days east of the site. Mazzatun is building in stone now. That makes the lesson of the Last Stone Course urgent again.
why_would_change_if: The Xit-Xaht would complete the xanmeer at once if they were offered it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in xanmeer country; contrasts directly with the tended and sealed ones
vibe_silhouette: Three terraces stand complete. A fourth terrace has its top course half laid. Blocks still lie on the ramp behind the fourth terrace.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey and the ramp is green. A sharp horizontal line shows where the building stops.
vibe_materials: The xanmeer is built of ashlar. The construction ramp is of earth and timber and is still in place. It has stood four thousand years as the builders left it.
vibe_signature_feature: The half-laid course is the signature feature. Five blocks are set. A sixth block was lifted but not placed. The sixth block lies where it was dropped.
vibe_condition: The site is preserved as it was abandoned. The preservation is deliberate.
vibe_approach: The flat top and the ramp stand out against the sky from the channels. The profile is wrong for a xanmeer.
vibe_senses: Wind crosses an open terrace. A teacher speaks. Children are quiet.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The xanmeer has been kept unfinished since the Duskfall. That draws those who want to finish it.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 20 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on nearPoint, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The Duskfall stopped a xanmeer mid-course. The province keeps it unfinished on purpose. The lifted block lies where it was dropped.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at this position. The record sits on the Argonian marsh side of the region. The two zones interleave there. The place is catalogued with the north. Its trade, its levies and its neighbours are northern.

name: Level Line
why_founding: Level Line was the camp of the surveyors who ran the levels of the North Cut. The camp is still pegged out. Its instrument stands are still in place. Surveyors abandoned it in the same week as the road.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on a knoll on the line of the cut. Surveyors chose it for inter-visibility with the next two stations.
why_occupants_motive: The camp is unoccupied. Villagers take the ranging rods for fence posts. Villagers do not touch the instrument stands, which they consider bad luck.
why_pressures: Two of the three onward stations are now in water. The third onward station is under scrub. The line that the camp served can no longer be walked.
why_would_change_if: Level Line would be the first place re-occupied if the cut resumed. The pegs would still be usable.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained along a planned route
vibe_silhouette: Three tripod-shaped stone instrument stands stand on a bare knoll. Tent scars mark the grass. A row of ranging-rod holes lies in the ground.
vibe_palette: The grass is bleached and the stone stands are grey. The iron pegs are rusted. The pegs have been in the ground two centuries.
vibe_materials: The survey furniture is Imperial and made to last. The stands are made of stone. The surveyors expected to come back.
vibe_signature_feature: The stone stands are the signature feature. Surveyors built permanent instrument mountings for a road that was abandoned within the year. The whole story can be read from this one object.
vibe_condition: The camp is untouched apart from the missing rods.
vibe_approach: The knoll is bare. The stands are visible from the cut. Travellers first see the stands from the cut.
vibe_senses: Wind blows on a bare knoll. Iron pegs ring underfoot.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The level book holds the number that killed the road. The level book can be found if anyone looks.
player_purpose_hook: Level Line is an Imperial survey camp abandoned on a knoll. The instruments are boxed. The levels prove that the road was never going to work.

name: Lightning Yard
why_founding: Lightning Yard is a second wamasu works on the northern channel. It takes the work that the Charge Works cannot handle. It specialises in the organ lanterns. It does not work the hide. The split happened because two brothers stopped speaking.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands on a channel bank with running water for flushing. A rock face stands at its back. It is far enough from the first works that the smells stay apart.
why_occupants_motive: The yard makes lanterns. The luminescent organs keep for a season if handled right. This yard handles them better than the other yard. The brother who runs it regards that as settled proof.
why_pressures: Both yards depend on the same hunters. The hunters play the yards against each other every season. The price of a live wamasu has doubled in five years.
why_would_change_if: The yard would merge with the Charge Works when either brother died. Both families know it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: near but not on a wamasu pond
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the only reason to live this close to that water
vibe_silhouette: An open yard stands against a rock face. Racks of drying hide stand in it. A flushing channel runs through it. A shed at the back glows blue after dark.
vibe_palette: Hide on the racks is grey-green. The stone is water-slick black. The lantern shed gives a cold blue light. The light can be seen from a kilometre away at night.
vibe_materials: The racks are timber. The flushing channel is stone-lined. The works is a plumbing arrangement with a shed attached.
vibe_signature_feature: The lantern shed at night is the signature feature. Organs light the whole building from inside, in blue. No fire or lamp is used on the site.
vibe_condition: The yard is well run and better equipped than its rival. The work is hard on the people who do it.
vibe_mood: The mood is competent and bitter. The yard does one thing very well.
vibe_approach: After dark the blue glow is the sole landmark on this channel. Boats from both yards steer by the glow.
vibe_senses: Water runs. Hide is scraped. A hum comes from the shed. It is not machinery.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Organ lanterns are a light source with a supply chain. A feud is attached to the supply chain. Two works share one set of hunters. The price keeps rising on both sides.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 574 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.channel-cross-village (+1.29).
player_purpose_hook: Lightning Yard is the second wamasu works. It sells charged goods. A rock face behind the yard is used as a working surface. Apprentices pay to be shown the work.

name: The Monsoon Boom
why_founding: The low road out of Thorn goes under in the monsoon. Thorn closes the road then. The alternative is the loss of caravans.
why_site_advantages: The boom stands at the lowest crossing of the terrace country. Water backs up there first.
why_occupants_motive: The paddy gate-holders work the barrier. They are already there for the gates.
why_pressures: Dunmer caravans have ignored the boom twice. On one of those occasions the road stayed sound.
why_would_change_if: The boom would be unnecessary if the road were embanked. Thorn's owners will not pay for a road that they do not own.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a road that has a wet-season alternative
vibe_silhouette: A floating timber boom crosses a road. Chains hold it at both ends. A depth gauge with painted bands stands beside it.
vibe_palette: The warning bands are white and black. The floodwater is brown. The sky is grey.
vibe_materials: The site holds a chained boom and one painted gauge post. These are the whole of its structure.
vibe_signature_feature: The top band of the gauge is painted in older paint than the rest. The band marks a level that the water reached once.
vibe_condition: Crude and functional.
vibe_approach: In the dry the boom is a chain lying in the dust. In the wet it is a boom on water with no road visible.
vibe_senses: Rain falls. The chain moves. Water flows over the road surface.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A depth gauge shows that the delta section has gone. The town must choose who crosses first.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 47 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A boom and a depth gauge stand across the lowest crossing of the road. When the boom is down, the delta section has already gone.

name: Moon Court
why_founding: Moon Court is a roofless alchemical court. Alchemists move the apparatus between fixed stations by moon phase. The work needs a clear sky. Stormhold has lamps, so the court stands outside the city.
why_site_advantages: The court stands on a dark upland flat. No light shows within four kilometres. A wall of rock to the north stops the wind without blocking the sky.
why_occupants_motive: Two alchemists live at the court. Stormhold practitioners book nights there in rotation. They pay for the darkness. One spoiled night voids the booking.
why_pressures: The cutting sheds at Crystalgate have begun to burn lamps late. The northern sky at the court is measurably worse than a decade ago.
why_would_change_if: The court would be worthless if a lit building went up on the ridge. The alchemists have started buying ridge land to prevent it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a settlement, above canopy where possible
vibe_silhouette: A roofless walled court stands on a bare upland flat. A ring of stone stations lies inside it. The court is open to the sky and unlit.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey by day. By night the working fires are the sole colour. The working fires are shielded on three sides.
vibe_materials: The court is dry stone with iron fittings. The apparatus is carried and is not fixed.
vibe_signature_feature: The stations are the signature feature. They form a ring of numbered stone pads. The apparatus stands on a different pad each phase. It is moved round the ring over a lunar month.
vibe_condition: The court is well kept and deliberately unlit. Its defences are directed against light.
vibe_mood: The mood is precise and nocturnal. The alchemists are obsessive about light.
vibe_approach: The court is a wall on a bare flat with no light showing. At night it is the hardest place in the north to find.
vibe_senses: Shielded fire burns. Something is ground very finely. Outside the court and inside it, the dark is complete.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Moon Court is a moon-phase workshop where a night can be booked. A booked darkness can be spoiled deliberately.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV13 · tier-3; PP14 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 392 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Moon Court is a calcinator court under a sky with no light for four kilometres. Its work can be done nowhere else.

name: Ninth Chapel
why_founding: An Imperial mission built a stone chapel on the north road. The mission died of swamp fever inside a year. It was the ninth attempt on this road. The mission numbered its own attempts. That numbering is why the other eight are remembered.
why_site_advantages: The chapel stands on a ready-made stone footing. The footing is the corner of something much older. The mission left the footing undug.
why_occupants_motive: Travellers used to sweep the floor and sleep in the nave. They stopped four years ago. The old cutting of the mission in the floor came open.
why_pressures: The roof is gone. The walls are sound. The Nisswo at the rest-house down the road calls it the failed one. The Nisswo says so aloud to travellers.
why_would_change_if: The chapel would be pulled down for its cut stone if the province had use for cut stone. The province has no use for cut stone.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: The place lies far inland, on land that other settlers passed over.
vibe_silhouette: Four roofless stone walls stand in scrub. The doorway faces the wrong way for the road.
vibe_palette: The grey stone has gone green on the north face. Sky shows where a roof should be. One carved number stands over the door.
vibe_materials: The walls are Imperial cut stone. The footing is older and better laid than the work of the mission. The mission built on the corner of another builder.
vibe_signature_feature: The number IX is cut over the door. The figures are Imperial. Local people cannot read them.
vibe_condition: The chapel is roofless with sound walls. Leaves have drifted over the floor since the last traveller slept there.
vibe_mood: The mood is bleak. The nave is safe as far as the cutting.
vibe_approach: Four stone walls stand up on a stretch where everything else is timber and reed. They can be seen from the road at half a kilometre.
vibe_senses: Wind passes through empty windows. Rain falls on a floor with no roof. The altar, icon and relic are gone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One carved number implies eight earlier missions. The eight missions form a chain to trace.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 89 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: Ninth Chapel is a failed Imperial chapel. It stands on the corner of something much older. The floor is open now.

name: North Post
why_founding: The Argonian keepers check the traffic that comes down the Tear road. They check for people being taken north.
why_site_advantages: The post stands below the pass on the Argonian side. It sits at the first point where a caravan can be stopped off a slope.
why_occupants_motive: The keepers count heads on the way out and heads on the way back. The practice began after the invasion. No order has repealed the count since.
why_pressures: House Dres's successors find the count insulting. The keepers find that satisfying.
why_would_change_if: The post would be abandoned if the Owing were ever abolished. The keepers keep the count for the Owing.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: spaced along the border; gaps are the point
vibe_silhouette: The post is a gate of two posts and a rope. It has a tally house. A notched stone stands beside the road.
vibe_palette: The post is made of rope and unpainted timber. It holds one very old notched stone.
vibe_materials: The buildings are timber and reed. All of them can be removed. The notched stone stays and is not a building.
vibe_signature_feature: The head-count stone carries notches for people going north. A shorter column of notches records people coming back.
vibe_condition: Simple, kept, undramatic.
vibe_approach: The rope across the road shows at fifty metres. The stone stands at knee height beside the rope.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear a tally called aloud. They hear caravan noise and the rope being lowered.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The head-counter logs each crossing by name. The book can prove who did not come back.
why_site_won: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 330 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: North Post is a head-count post below the pass. The head-counter logs each crossing in a book. Anyone can ask to read the book.

name: North Cut
why_founding: Imperial road-builders cut a hard road north from Stormhold toward the Tear road. The surveyors abandoned the cut after four kilometres. They had found what the plain villages already knew about the sink.
why_site_advantages: The cut is laid along a line that looks correct on a map. On the ground the cut is uphill for two hundred metres.
why_occupants_motive: The cut has no residents. The villagers quarry the metalling for their own yards. They consider the quarrying a form of restitution.
why_pressures: The cut has become a drainage channel. Water that used to reach the river now floods two fields and a hamlet's ground.
why_would_change_if: If its water reached the plain villages, the cut would become a serious problem in a generation. One village has started to notice.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the line of an abandoned Imperial road
vibe_silhouette: A dead-straight metalled cut is four kilometres long and ends in a sink. The last hundred metres lie under water. A spoil bank lies alongside.
vibe_palette: The colours are road-metal grey and sink black. A hard green line of different vegetation lies along the spoil bank, where drainage changed the ground.
vibe_materials: The road is Imperial road metal. The villagers have quarried it out in patches for hardcore. The engineered base under it is still level.
vibe_signature_feature: The road ends mid-formation. The pegs for the next section still stand in the ground beyond the waterline.
vibe_condition: The cut is level, sound and quarried. It now drains water. The surveyors did not design it for that.
vibe_mood: The cut is an expensive mistake that still does damage.
vibe_approach: The cut is the straightest thing on the plain. The whole of it shows at once from the spoil bank.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear water running where water should not be. Boots sound on metalled surface, then on mud, then silence.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An abandoned roadworks is flooding a hamlet two kilometres away. The villagers have not traced the water back to its source.
why_site_won: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 392 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent.
player_purpose_hook: An Imperial road ends mid-formation. The next pegs are still in the ground. The crew abandoned a half-bored culvert.
siting_note: The place was converted from a hostile place to a neutral ruin in the round 4 rebalance. Three other fights are already placed inside 250 m of the same route stretch. An abandoned roadworks suits an empty site.

name: The Waiting Hole
why_founding: Thorn's field-owners need somewhere to hold a debtor between the field and the court. The field-owners will not build a gaol. Argonians do not build gaols.
why_site_advantages: The pit lies in a field-owner's stock yard on the Thorn road. It is roofed and out of the weather. The field-owners mention this.
why_occupants_motive: The overseers use the pit for a night at a time. This is legal. They sometimes use it for longer. No court has been asked about the longer stays.
why_pressures: The Freed Rows keep a tally of who goes in and who comes out. The two counts often differ.
why_would_change_if: The pit would be filled in on the day that Thorn's court defined waiting. The Chainbreakers are building that case.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: attached to a hard-owing estate or crossing
vibe_silhouette: A roofed pit sits in the corner of a working stock yard. A plank floor covers the pit and leaves a gap for air.
vibe_palette: Straw and dung lie on timber in the pit. One dark gap lies at the bottom of the wall.
vibe_materials: The pit is timber and mud. It is older than the surrounding yard. The yard's owners cannot name who dug it.
vibe_signature_feature: The air gap is cut at boot height. An overseer can speak to a prisoner through it without being seen.
vibe_condition: In constant light use.
vibe_approach: The pit looks like a root store. The overseers call it a root store.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear yard work above. A voice can be heard at boot height.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A field-owner's roofed pit holds people who appear on no city record.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 132 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The Waiting Hole is a roofed holding pit in a field-owner's yard. It holds people who are on no charge sheet.

name: North Relay
why_founding: The two northern cities do not trust each other's messengers. Both cities pay a neutral relay that stands between them.
why_site_advantages: The relay stands midway on the northern road. It sits on ground that belongs to neither city's hinterland.
why_occupants_motive: The relay families keep neutrality as an inheritance. They refuse to read. They carry sealed writs unopened. They are paid twice.
why_pressures: Both cities have tried to buy an exception. The refusals are part of the family's standing.
why_would_change_if: The relay would fail if it were proven that one refusal had been sold.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay
vibe_silhouette: Two identical letter boxes stand on two posts. A hammock frame stands between them. Nothing else stands within a kilometre.
vibe_palette: The colours are weathered post grey and marsh green. The boxes carry two different city seals.
vibe_materials: The relay has two waxed boxes and a reed shelter. Nothing in it locks. The cities built none of it.
vibe_signature_feature: The two boxes are identical. Each box stands the same distance from the shelter. The symmetry is a policy.
vibe_condition: The relay families maintain the site daily. They replace the boxes together or not at all.
vibe_approach: Two posts stand on an empty road. A traveller would take them for a boundary marker.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear a person leaving at a run. They hear wind and a box lid.
player_purpose_hook: The courier relay stands midway on the northern road. Letters and remounts can be had there. Work is available for anyone who can carry.

name: The Cold Gallery
why_founding: The root layer ends here at its northern limit. It thins over cold rim ground. The galleries beneath it are colder and drier than any in the south.
why_site_advantages: The gallery lies between the swamp's edge and the rim's stone. Roots run over rock there. Mud lies under them elsewhere.
why_occupants_motive: No faction claims the gallery. The Seam-Chasers, unlicensed prospectors on the shoulder above, store gear in the first chamber. Their claim papers do not mention the gallery.
why_pressures: No other root gallery in the province has a stone floor. The stone floor makes the gallery walkable. It also makes a fall worse.
why_would_change_if: If it were fully mapped, the gallery would be the north's cave system. The prospectors have started mapping it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map
vibe_silhouette: The gallery has a living root ceiling and a bare rock floor.
vibe_palette: The colours are root brown above and grey stone below. Cold blue light shows at two collapses.
vibe_materials: The gallery has no construction beyond the prospectors' store boxes. The Seam-Chasers crew keeps the boxes here.
vibe_signature_feature: The floor is dry stone under a wet ceiling. Water drips onto rock all day, everywhere at once.
vibe_condition: The upper chambers are stable. The lower chambers change as roots shift.
vibe_mood: The gallery is cold and echoing. No other place underground in the province has the same feel.
vibe_approach: The mouth lies behind the prospectors' camp. It looks like a store. It partly is one.
vibe_senses: Water drips onto stone with a hard echo. Roots creak. A draught blows out of the deeper chambers.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Root galleries over bare stone are being mapped. The surveyor is paid in Stormhold coin. She cannot account for that coin.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 261 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Roots run over bare rock. Mud lies under them elsewhere. A gallery under them stays cold.

name: North Vista
why_founding: The rim gives Argonia a long view. From one ledge above the pass, the whole northern marsh can be seen.
why_site_advantages: The ledge sits on a ridge nose above the Tear road. It is high enough to clear the haze on a cold morning.
why_occupants_motive: A hackwing pair took the ledge and hold it. The villagers below know the view is worth a look. They do not know the climb.
why_pressures: The hackwing pair nest on the ledge. They hold it against climbers. Few of the villagers below have made the climb.
why_would_change_if: Would not change.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: placed where the visibility raster shows a dead zone
vibe_silhouette: A flat ledge the size of a room holds a cairn. Below it lies the whole northern marsh in bands of haze.
vibe_palette: The ground underfoot is rock grey. Below, every green that the province has fades blue toward the horizon.
vibe_materials: The ledge holds a single cairn and no other structure.
vibe_signature_feature: Each traveller leaves one small thing in the cairn.
vibe_condition: The ledge changes only as the cairn grows.
vibe_approach: The climb takes two hours with no view at all. At the top the whole northern marsh is in view at once.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear wind. The marsh lies too far below to be heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: From a ledge the whole channel network can be seen. Hackwings defend the ledge and will not share it.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: A ledge above the pass has the whole northern marsh below it. A hackwing pair hold the top.

name: Northern Rest
why_founding: The Nisswo walk the north too, less often. The villagers keep a house ready for a preacher who may not come this year.
why_site_advantages: The house stands on the Bogmother causeway road. Pilgrim traffic already passes there.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages take a month each in turn. Each village has kept its turn for forty years without a miss.
why_pressures: No Nisswo has come for three years. The villagers sweep the house every week.
why_would_change_if: The house would be maintained anyway, for as long as the villages take turns.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: between villages on a preaching circuit
vibe_silhouette: A small house has a black door. The door stands open. A bed is made and a fire is laid. The house has been unused for three years.
vibe_palette: The colours are a black door, an ochre wall and the pale of clean bedding.
vibe_materials: The house is plain mud and reed. The villagers sweep it to a standard that their own houses do not meet.
vibe_signature_feature: The made bed is turned down every week. Whichever village has the month has done so for three years.
vibe_condition: Immaculate and unused.
vibe_approach: A black door stands open on an empty road.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear wind through an open door. Otherwise the house is still.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A Sithis rest house is kept ready for a Nisswo who has not come in three years. The rest house on the pilgrim road is kept for a Nisswo whose route ended somewhere between two stages.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: NI07 · tier-2; LD64 · tier-3; LD81 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-opened-terrace (+0.34).
player_purpose_hook: Northern Rest is a Sithis rest house on the pilgrim road. A bed is made and a fire is laid for a Nisswo who has not come in three years.

name: The Opened Terrace
why_founding: A xanmeer was opened and looted, then left. People with no claim to it live in it now.
why_site_advantages: The terrace stands on the channel network. It is close enough that the carried trade can be heard passing. River patrols do not bother with it.
why_occupants_motive: River thieves live here. They wanted stone walls.
why_pressures: Greylight has asked twice for the terrace to be cleared. Stormhold has not answered.
why_would_change_if: The terrace would be tended again if a tribe with a claim took it back.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a district with other xanmeer, showing the range of states
vibe_silhouette: A stepped terrace has a hole in one face. The hole was knocked through the stone. Cook-smoke rises from the top of it.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone and black smoke. Washing is strung between two terraces.
vibe_materials: The terrace is xanmeer ashlar. Hide and stolen canvas are rigged across it on rope.
vibe_signature_feature: Domestic laundry hangs on a line across a sacred terrace.
vibe_condition: The terrace is structurally fine and casually inhabited.
vibe_approach: Smoke from a xanmeer terrace shows for a kilometre. The crews on the river read the smoke the same way every time.
vibe_senses: Visitors hear voices echoing in stone and a dog. A river thief cooks in a xanmeer that has no kitchen.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A broken-open xanmeer still holds what could not be carried. The second party came to take that.
why_site_won: ravine in upland hills (danger band 3), 145 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-northern-rest (+0.34).
player_purpose_hook: A xanmeer was broken open because it was easy to reach. The portable loot is gone. What could not be carried is still inside.

name: Outer Silyanorn
why_founding: Outer Silyanorn is the outer compound of the Barsaebic Ayleid settlement beneath Stormhold. The compound lies beyond the ravines of Stormhold.
why_site_advantages: Outer Silyanorn stands on the same dry shelf as Stormhold. The shelf continues north past the point where Stormhold stopped building.
why_occupants_motive: The surface work at Outer Silyanorn stands empty. Stormhold's diggers quarry the undercity and leave the surface work alone. The surviving structures stay intact because the diggers ignore them.
why_pressures: No licence covers this part of Silyanorn. The diggings office has not applied for one.
why_would_change_if: Stormhold's surveyors would quarry Outer Silyanorn if they found that the licence covers only the galleries.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the north and west, where the Barsaebic Ayleids went
vibe_silhouette: A white arcade stands in scrub within sight of Stormhold. The arcade is untouched while diggers empty the ground beneath Stormhold.
vibe_palette: The colours are bone white and scrub green. Stormhold's grey terraces show in the distance.
vibe_materials: The surface masonry is Barsaebic Ayleid work. It matches the galleries below Stormhold. It stands in daylight.
vibe_signature_feature: Unquarried Silyanorn stone stands in plain view of Stormhold. The stone is still coursed.
vibe_condition: Weathered but unrobbed.
vibe_approach: The compound is visible from Stormhold's north terrace. Stormhold's clerks assume that the compound has been dug.
vibe_senses: Wind passes through the arcade. Stormhold is faintly audible. The arcade has no other sound.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Ayleid surface work stands in daylight while Stormhold quarries beneath it. A party starts taking the surface stone. The stone is lifted from a compound that Stormhold has ignored for centuries.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: SA07 · tier-2; LD14 · tier-3; LD72 · tier-3
why_site_won: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 414 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Ayleid surface work stands in daylight. Stormhold's diggers quarry only downward and ignore the compound.

name: Pass Station
why_founding: The Tear road runs past the pass station. Winter kills travellers on this stretch of road. Both provinces pay for the station.
why_site_advantages: The station stands at the highest point of the road. The site has no lee at all.
why_occupants_motive: Two keepers hold the station under an arrangement between Thorn's field-owners and a Dres factor. No other cross-border arrangement in the north functions at all.
why_pressures: Neither province pays for the roof. The roof is the worst part of the building.
why_would_change_if: The station would collapse as an institution if either province stopped paying. The keepers expect that to happen.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the only crossings of the rim; each one is strategically singular
vibe_silhouette: A stone hut stands on bare ground. A line of tall poles runs away into cloud on both sides.
vibe_palette: The colours are stone grey and cloud white. The poles are painted alternately in the colours of two provinces.
vibe_materials: The hut is dry stone with a bad turf roof. The keepers maintain only the poles.
vibe_signature_feature: One half of the pole line is painted in Thorn's colours. The other half is painted in Tear's colours. The two halves meet at the hut.
vibe_condition: The walls are in excellent repair. The roof is in appalling repair. Everyone at the station has made the joke already.
vibe_mood: The mood is cold. The keepers are wry about being paid by two provinces.
vibe_approach: In weather, travellers follow the poles. The poles are the only guide.
vibe_senses: The wind never stops. In fog a keeper rings a bell on the hour. Two accents are heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A cross-border station will fail this winter. It survives only if one province admits that it wants the station.
player_purpose_hook: The station is the last chance to turn back. The site offers no shelter from weather.
siting_note: The record was cut in round 4 on 2026-09-04. The place was a pass station on a rim saddle of the Thorn–Tear road, but the Thorn–Tear road has no saddle. The high point of the road is 43 m in firm lowland, band 1. Two-Gate Bridge, 800 m away, already holds the border crossing. The region has no site where the pass station role exists. A pass station rewritten into a roadside hut would be a different place. Quest LD48 is re-anchored to place.dunmer-north.the-two-gate-bridge.

name: The Pen Yard
why_founding: Slavery ended. The buildings still stand. House Dres assembled people at this yard and shipped them north for four centuries.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands at the water's edge in mangrove forest. The nearest route is 282 m away. The yard lies below the pass on the old slave road.
why_occupants_motive: The yard stands empty of guards. A neighbouring holding uses the yard as a cattle pen. Opinion divides on whether that use is healing or obscene.
why_pressures: The yard is structurally excellent. The district argues over pulling the yard down.
why_would_change_if: The district would demolish the yard tomorrow if it could agree. The district cannot agree.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the old Morrowind-border trade line
vibe_silhouette: A stone-walled yard has a loading ramp at one end. Iron ring bolts sit in the walls at two heights.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey. Rust stains lie under every bolt. Green fodder is trodden into the floor.
vibe_materials: The walls are Velothi stonework built to last. The yard holds animals now.
vibe_signature_feature: The ring bolts sit at two heights, adult and child. Visitors work out the meaning without being told.
vibe_condition: The yard is in excellent repair because it is in use.
vibe_approach: From the road the yard looks like a stock yard. The bolts show only on closer approach.
vibe_senses: Cattle are heard. Wind blows through the walled yard. Iron rings knock against stone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A slaver's holding yard was abandoned with its paperwork intact. A party wants the yard burned.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD41 · tier-3; MQ12 · tier-3; PP06 · tier-3
why_site_won: open water in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 282 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, bound, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The Dres holding yard lies below the pass. The yard was abandoned with its fittings intact. The manifests are still nailed up.

name: Permit Dig
why_founding: Cyrodilic Collections keeps an alcove at Stormhold. The alcove implies a dig somewhere that the Collections can defend as lawful.
why_site_advantages: The dig stands on the parcel that the vicecanons agreed to licence. The parcel lies on firm ground, 23 m from the nearest route.
why_occupants_motive: The Collections dig to return antiquities. The vicecanons licence the dig to keep an eye on it. The diggers dig for wages.
why_pressures: The licensed parcel is the least interesting ground at Outer Silyanorn. The vicecanons chose the parcel. The director of the dig says so in her letters home.
why_would_change_if: The dig would move onto the Outer Silyanorn arcade once the licence widened. Stormhold will not widen the licence.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always beside a ruin
vibe_silhouette: A fenced parcel of trenches stands with a permit board at the gate.
vibe_palette: The colours are canvas white and spoil brown.
vibe_materials: The dig uses canvas and rope inside a woven fence.
vibe_signature_feature: The permit board has the licensed boundary drawn on it. The diggers take their meals at the fence, facing outward.
vibe_condition: Neat and frustrated.
vibe_mood: The diggers are diligent. The fence line confines them.
vibe_approach: The tent and the fence read from the road. The fence line is the first thing that visitors register.
vibe_senses: Trowels scrape. A clerk's pen scratches. Conversation turns on the fence.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Cyrodilic Collections keeps a northern alcove. The dig is licensed with a hard boundary.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 23 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Cyrodilic Collections runs a licensed dig that depends on Outer Silyanorn. The dig is short of hands. The hands that are available are short of honesty.
siting_note: The record was converted from hostile to guarded in the round 4 rebalance. Licensed diggers with a permit board are not an ambush. The stretch already carried two other fights.

name: The Pilots' Rest
why_founding: Boat crews on the through-boats need a bed that is not their own hull. The Pilots' Rest took that trade.
why_site_advantages: The tradehouse stands on firm ground in upland hills. The nearest route is 818 m away. A pool lies 341 m away.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper was a pilot and has retired from piloting. She still sells her knowledge of the channels.
why_pressures: The channel pilots at Channel Cross regard the keeper as competition. They regard her rates as a betrayal.
why_would_change_if: The pilots' families would buy out the Pilots' Rest if the keeper agreed to sell. The keeper will not sell.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: A long veranda on piles runs over a bend. It has six mooring rings, each with a lamp.
vibe_palette: The colours are lamp yellow and reed roof. The tradehouse looks its best at night.
vibe_materials: The tradehouse is built on stilts. Its veranda is unusually long and unbroken, because the mooring length sets its shape.
vibe_signature_feature: The keeper lights the six lamps in order as boats arrive. A crew can count how many boats are already tied up.
vibe_condition: The building is well built and wet. The keeper constantly re-decks the mooring edge.
vibe_mood: The mood is convivial and informed. The keeper charges for the information.
vibe_approach: The lamp count is readable from a distance.
vibe_senses: A hammock creaks. Talk turns on water levels.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The pilots price the channels by rumour. A party is deliberately planting one bad rumour. The nightly toll argument turns into an accusation that can be proved.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 818 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.waits-for-the-promise (+0.40).
player_purpose_hook: Pilots who know the channels meet at the Pilots' Rest. Their prices depend on how the last trip went.

name: The Quiet Landing
why_founding: The Quiet Landing is a marsh house on a private cut. Buyers bought the house through three names. The buyers needed a place on the north water that no ledger connects to them.
why_site_advantages: The cut reads as a dead end from the channel. The cellar stays dry. A second mouth into the reeds opens from inside.
why_occupants_motive: An Unbound Root cell stages northward from the house. The cell keeps records here. The work upriver cannot carry paper.
why_pressures: The neighbours have decided not to have noticed. The neighbours can reverse that decision.
why_would_change_if: A raid makes the house the best evidence that the Conclave has. Abandonment leaves an empty house with a shrine in the cellar. The cell that built the house will already be gone.
vibe_silhouette: One marsh house stands at the head of a cut. A boat sits under the house. The house has no landing stage.
