vibe_palette: The colours are grey weathered board and black water. One shuttered window shows light behind it.
vibe_materials: The house is plank and pile with reed thatch. A stone-lined cellar lies beneath it.
vibe_signature_feature: The cellar shrine is a cut root set in stone. The tools lie laid out beside the root.
vibe_condition: The house is deliberately unremarkable. The cell maintains it where it matters.
vibe_approach: The cut looks like a dead end from the channel.
vibe_senses: Cut sap and lamp oil can be smelled. There are no voices.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The landing is the first place where the cult can be caught with its own paper. The condition in which the landing is left afterwards is a second hook.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ08 · tier-0; MQ22 · tier-0; LD25 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 97 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, route.
player_purpose_hook: A house on a dead-end cut has a stone cellar under a reed roof. The cult keeps in the cellar what it cannot carry.

name: Rim Hermitage
why_founding: A Nisswo keeps a cell above the treeline. The Nisswo teaches that death is thought about more honestly in the cold than in the marsh.
why_site_advantages: The cell stands above the snowline on the leeward side of the ridge. Meltwater runs at the door. A village carries fuel up once a year. The village sends four people each year.
why_occupants_motive: One occupant lives here by choice. She receives climbers who reach the door. She sends no word down.
why_pressures: The village that does the carry is not sure that it believes any of it. The Nisswo is old.
why_would_change_if: The cell would stand empty and intact for a century. Nothing rots at that height.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the rim's signature dwelling; deliberately alone
vibe_silhouette: A single stone cell with a slab roof stands on a snow shoulder. A black doorway faces out. One line of footprints leads to it.
vibe_palette: The colours above the treeline are white, grey and black. The cell is a dark shape against the snow.
vibe_materials: The cell is dry stone and slab. One person built it over one summer. A Nisswo's mark is cut over the door. The rest of the stone is bare.
vibe_signature_feature: The doorway faces the province. The step gives a view of the entire north. The occupant has looked at that view for thirty years.
vibe_condition: The cell is in perfect repair. The cold keeps the slab and the door leather sound.
vibe_approach: The last four hundred metres are above the snow. The cell shows as a dark mark on a white shoulder.
vibe_senses: The quiet is absolute and thinner than marsh silence. The door leather creaks. A heartbeat is audible.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A Nisswo will talk about death with climbers who reach the door.
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 356 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: A hermit lives above the snowline. A village carries her fuel up once a year. The village sends four people to do it.

name: Rim Shelter
why_founding: The shelter stands above the treeline on the northern rim. The weather on the pass changes within minutes. The pass has no cover. The Dres built the shelter. The people of the north have kept it in use. Dunmer who work in the area meet with objection. The shelter is the exception. All parties accept it.
why_site_advantages: The shelter fills a rock notch on the leeward side of the col. The notch is out of the wind in every direction that the wind blows.
why_occupants_motive: The shelter has no residents. Each party that comes up restocks it for the next. Everyone follows the restocking rule. No authority enforces it.
why_pressures: Carriers bring the fuel up the pass. The stove is old. Twice in ten years a party arrived to find the fuel and stove gone. After the second time, three people did not come down.
why_would_change_if: If the habit of carrying fuel up lapsed, people would die at the shelter every year. At present people die there about once in ten years.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on an exposed stretch with no settlement
vibe_silhouette: The shelter is a stone hut shaped to fit its notch. Boulders weigh down the roof. The door opens inwards, for a reason.
vibe_palette: The stone is rock grey. Snow scour whitens the windward stones. The open door shows as a single warm rectangle.
vibe_materials: The hut is built of Dres-cut stone. Weighted slabs form the roof. An iron stove stands inside. It is older than any living grandmother.
vibe_signature_feature: The door opens inwards. Everyone who has spent a night here understands why.
vibe_condition: The hut is cold and sound. What the last party left is still inside.
vibe_approach: The hut cannot be seen until the col levels out. Then it stands directly ahead.
vibe_senses: The wind changes note on entering the notch. The iron stove ticks. Boots sound on stone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The shelter offers a survival beat on the rim crossing. A visiting character can be responsible for it either way, by stocking it or by leaving it bare.
player_purpose_hook: The shelter sits in a rock notch out of the wind from every direction. It holds a stove and whatever the last party left.

name: The Salt and Shell
why_founding: The tradehouse stands at the crossroads that it was built to serve. The cellar under it moves goods that never passed the toll.
why_site_advantages: The road junction draws travellers and off-duty levy. The levy watch the yard and do not watch the cellar door.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper cooks for anyone who walks in off the crossroads. The band that runs the cellar buys the keeper's cover and silence.
why_pressures: The levy drink upstairs most nights, ten feet from the cellar door. The keeper stands them their first round.
why_would_change_if: The arrangement would end if one off-duty patrol grew curious. The keeper knows this.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: The tradehouse is a long house with two smoking chimneys. A cellar door round the back is never shown to travellers.
vibe_palette: The walls are smoke-brown. Silver saltrice grows beyond the yard. The cellar door is unpainted and plain.
vibe_materials: The upper frame is patched Argonian-and-Dunmer work. Below, the cellar is built of unfinished plank and rope ladders.
vibe_signature_feature: The cellar door looks like a root store from the yard. It bolts from the inside.
vibe_condition: The upper floor is warm and busy. The cellar is cramped and dry.
vibe_mood: The mood upstairs is cheerful. The mood down the ladder is tense.
vibe_approach: Two chimneys smoke. Nothing at the front shows what lies under the floor.
vibe_senses: Two languages and one argument sound upstairs. Damp rope and packed crates fill the cellar. The door bolt slides when a patron gets too curious.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A crossroads tradehouse moves goods under a floor where the toll-holder drinks.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 76 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The tradehouse stands at the crossroads with a cellar under it. The toll-holder has not weighed what goes through the cellar.

name: The Salt Ledge
why_founding: The border post counts heads. That count is why an uncounted route over the rim exists.
why_site_advantages: A ledge line runs parallel to the pass, a kilometre east. It is wide enough for a person carrying a pack. It is too narrow for a beast.
why_occupants_motive: Carriers move salt north and, when the price is right, people. The border count was meant to stop that.
why_pressures: Both provinces know that the ledge is there. The officials of both provinces wish to avoid the diplomatic cost of closing it.
why_would_change_if: The ledge would close in a week if the head-count were dropped. That is the smugglers' argument.
siting_prefs_water_relation: none; this is the dry route
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: beside a pass, out of sight of its post
vibe_silhouette: The ledge is a pace wide and runs along a rock face. Spilled salt lies white in the cracks along its whole length.
vibe_palette: White salt lies in grey rock above a drop.
vibe_materials: The built things are rope anchors and a hide cache under an overhang. Nothing else on the ledge is built.
vibe_signature_feature: Spilled salt marks the ledge. Centuries of loads scraping the wall left a white line. The line can be followed in the dark.
vibe_condition: Unmaintained and heavily used.
vibe_approach: The white line is the path. It is invisible from anywhere except on it.
vibe_senses: Boots sound on grit. Wind blows. The pass bell sounds far below and to the west.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An uncounted ledge past the border post carries salt one way and people the other, for a fee.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 995 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger.
player_purpose_hook: The ledge is an uncounted route past the border post. It carries salt one way and people the other, for a fee.

name: Shell Ground
why_founding: Armoured shell-beasts work a stretch of gravel bar for the molluscs in it. The beasts moult where they work. The bar is the region's source of raw shell plate. Standing on the bar is dangerous.
why_site_advantages: The site is a long gravel bar with a mollusc bed under it. The bar is exposed for four hours either side of the drawdown. Water covers it the rest of the time.
why_occupants_motive: The bar has no residents. Gatherers come at the drawdown and take moult plate off it. They leave before the animals come back up.
why_pressures: The window is short and the plate is valuable. Every year a gatherer misjudges the window. The gatherers keep the count on a post at the landing.
why_would_change_if: The bar would stop producing plate if the mollusc bed were over-taken. The gatherers police the bed far more strictly than they police the timing.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: supplies a nearby craft works
vibe_silhouette: A long pale gravel bar lies exposed in dark water. Curved plates of shed shell litter it. Deep churned trenches show where something very large has been feeding.
vibe_palette: The bar is white-grey. Shed plate is iridescent. Black water lies on both sides. Trenched gravel is raw brown.
vibe_materials: Nothing is built on the bar. A post at the landing has a count cut into it. The post is the entire human presence.
vibe_signature_feature: The trenches are furrows a metre deep. The feeding animals ploughed them through the gravel.
vibe_condition: The tide reworks the bar twice daily. Nothing on the bar is more than a day old.
vibe_approach: Gatherers reach the landing. There they read the count on the post and judge the water.
vibe_senses: Water drains off the gravel. Shell plate rings when lifted. Something moves out of sight on the deep side.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Armour material is available on a timed window. The reason for the window is still in the water.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 581 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: Furrows a metre deep ploughed through gravel show the size of what made them. They show it well before the animal appears.

name: Shoal Bank
why_founding: A submerged bar off the delta concentrates fish. The people of the north get their protein from the bar.
why_site_advantages: The bank lies where the river's silt meets tidal water. It sits three metres down. It spans two hundred metres.
why_occupants_motive: Six villages fish the bank. They follow an oral marker system. The villages respect the system strictly.
why_pressures: The Dunmer boats out of Thorn have started fishing the bank. Their crews do not know the markers.
why_would_change_if: The bank would be fished out in a decade under any system that could not exclude newcomers.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: contested between two coastal settlements
vibe_silhouette: The bank shows as open water with a colour change in it. Four boats sit in a line along an unseen edge.
vibe_palette: Two greens meet in a line. Boat hulls and birds working the edge add detail.
vibe_materials: Nothing is built on the water. The marks are two poles and a tree on shore, lined up.
vibe_signature_feature: The fishers find the bank by a transit. They line a pole up with a tree on shore.
vibe_condition: The bank does not change. The fishers maintain the marks.
vibe_approach: The birds working the edge show before the boats do.
vibe_senses: Nets are heard. Gulls call. A hull knocks in a swell.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 527 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, hinterland; needs 1.5 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: Lining the pole up with the tree puts the bank underneath. A lighter sank on the bank and is still down there.
siting_note: The owner promoted this place from the reserve on 2026-09-04. It fills an off-route D3 gap at (3148, 1387). The aim is more fights off the road and fewer on it.

name: The Shut Village
why_founding: The village shut itself in during the Flu and survived. It has not opened since. The practice has outlived the reason by about nine centuries.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on a rise in the reedbeds. One causeway crosses to it. That single causeway made shutting the village possible.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers keep the practice because it worked once. They receive visitors at the outer end of the causeway and no closer.
why_pressures: The village is inbred and dwindling. The villagers know it. The Hatching Pools have sent word twice. The village has refused twice.
why_would_change_if: The village would end within a generation, either by opening or by running out.
siting_prefs_water_relation: cut off by reed and channel where possible
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately just out of reach of its neighbours
vibe_silhouette: The village is seen only across two hundred metres of causeway. A table is set at the near end.
vibe_palette: Distance haze, reed gold and brown water surround the village. A white cloth lies on the table.
vibe_materials: The buildings are ordinary mud and reed. The strangeness is social.
vibe_signature_feature: Goods are left on the table and taken from it. The receiver stays fifty metres back while a visitor is present.
vibe_condition: The village is well kept and thinning. More houses stand empty than are still roofed.
vibe_approach: The path ends at the table. The receiver tells arrivals, politely, that the path stops there.
vibe_senses: A voice calls across water. Wind blows. No children's noise can be heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A village shut behind its causeway for sixteen centuries wants one errand run, on its terms.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 785 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on nearPoint, landform, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: The village is shut in behind its one causeway. The village has stayed shut for about nine centuries. The villagers will talk through the gate.
siting_note: Danger is raised to D4 to match the band-5 reedbeds around the village. The causeway keeps the village itself safe. The reedbeds beyond the causeway are band 5.

name: Silyanorn Crown
why_founding: One block of the Outer Silyanorn stands to its full height. The stair inside fails two thirds of the way up. The last third of the ascent is a climb. The top gives a view over the ravine system. Other vantages near Stormhold lack that view.
why_site_advantages: The block stands at the compound's high corner, on the ravine rim. The diggings lie on one side and the city on the other.
why_occupants_motive: The diggings' hands used to eat their meal on top in the sun. They go elsewhere now. The failed stair dropped through into the inside of the block.
why_pressures: The failed section of stair is failing further. The diggers' favoured hold has visibly moved in a decade.
why_would_change_if: The block would lose its purpose if the last third became unclimbable. The block has no interior worth entering.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a canopy-breaking landmark in dense country
vibe_silhouette: A single Ayleid tower block stands above a low ruin field on a ravine rim. A stair visible inside it stops in mid-air.
vibe_palette: The stone is pale Barsaebic stone. Crystal dust, blue-green, blows up from the diggings. The top course is bleached white.
vibe_materials: The tower is Ayleid block-and-course. The failure of the internal stair is now the route. The way out is through the break.
vibe_signature_feature: The stair stops two thirds of the way up, in mid-air.
vibe_condition: The tower is standing. It loses a little of the climbable section each decade.
vibe_mood: The climb is casual as far as the break in the stair. Beyond the break it is not casual.
vibe_approach: From the diggings road the tower looks like a stump. From the ravine floor it looks like a tower.
vibe_senses: Wind blows at the top. The hoist ratchet sounds far below. Grit underfoot and a meal left by a digger are present.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The climb is short and has a view over the Stormhold ravines. The tower is the only standing tower in the compound.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 318 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, route, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The climb near Stormhold shows the diggings and the city at once. The way in is the break in the stair.
siting_note: Round 4 rebalance converted the place from hostile to a neutral climb. It stood 138 m off the route. Four other fights lay inside 250 m. Its value was the view. The fight was not its value.

name: The Slumped Hamlet
why_founding: The hamlet was built over a limestone void near the rim. The households took four generations to notice the void. They then left in a single season.
why_site_advantages: The ground was good and dry. The ground also had a spring. The void caused the spring. The households saw the connection only after the ground gave way.
why_occupants_motive: The old hamlet has no residents now. The households moved two hundred metres and rebuilt. Moving away is the province's standard answer to subsidence.
why_pressures: The old and new hamlets are in sight of each other. The old hamlet is still going down.
why_would_change_if: If the void runs as the rim's geology suggests, it would take the new hamlet too.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: above workings or burning peat
vibe_silhouette: Six houses lean at the same angle into a shallow bowl. The new hamlet's roofs show over the rise behind them.
vibe_palette: The thatch is gold at two angles, one right and one wrong. The bowl is green.
vibe_materials: The houses are built of ordinary mud and reed. Only the tilt sets them apart from any northern village.
vibe_signature_feature: Every house tilts the same way by the same amount. A uniform lean is far stranger than a random collapse.
vibe_condition: The houses are still standing and still moving. They sit measurably lower each decade.
vibe_approach: Both hamlets are visible together from the path to the new hamlet.
vibe_senses: Timber creaks under slow strain. Water runs somewhere below. Nothing living is in the houses.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Good ground with a spring on it fell into the void that fed the spring. The houses went first.
why_site_won: ford in border mountains (danger band 3), 670 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; bound to body.2879-340 within 60 m.
player_purpose_hook: The ground was good and had a spring on it. The void that fed the spring took six houses down with it.

name: The Standing Bid
why_founding: Stormhold taxes what crosses its weighbridge. Stormhold does not tax what is moored off its shore. The city's auctions moved onto the water two generations ago. They never moved back.
why_site_advantages: The mooring lies under the deck. The raft's own hull hides the mooring from the bank.
why_occupants_motive: Auctioneers run the sales and take a tenth of every lot. They ask about provenance only when a buyer makes them.
why_pressures: Half the lots are things that the city would seize if they came up the stair. The auctioneer's clerk knows which half.
why_would_change_if: One seizure on the deck would end the auctions. Two vicecanons have proposed a seizure. The vote has not been called.
vibe_silhouette: Three pontoon rafts are lashed into one floor. A single wide awning covers the floor. A lot-board stands at the head of the floor.
vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow light lies on wet planking. The water is black. Stormhold's grey terraces lie beyond the water.
vibe_materials: The raft is built of pontoon timber, tarred rope and a canvas awning. One iron lot-bell hangs there.
vibe_signature_feature: A trapdoor behind the auctioneer's table drops straight down into the water.
vibe_condition: The raft is prosperous and provisional. The crew replace the raft plank by plank.
vibe_approach: Arrival is alongside by boat. There is no way in on foot.
vibe_senses: Tar and lamp oil smell strongly. The lot-bell rings.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An auctioneer who never asks about provenance runs a room moored just outside the city's reach.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ07 · tier-0; LD01 · tier-3; LD06 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 12 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, bound.
player_purpose_hook: The auction sits on moored rafts. The city's law stops at the gangplank. The auctioneers do not ask about provenance.

name: Behind the Falls
why_founding: Stormhold's waterfall has undercut the rock. The undercut left a chamber behind the sheet of water. The chamber lies directly below the city.
why_site_advantages: The undercut is at the centre of the falls. A ledge from the south side of the ravine reaches it.
why_occupants_motive: The city's officials know about the chamber. The Conclave uses the chamber. There is no booking ledger.
why_pressures: None of the plans that the city holds shows this room.
why_would_change_if: The vicecanons would seal the chamber once they worked out who was using it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only
vibe_silhouette: The chamber is a room behind a curtain of falling water. The city's lights swim through the sheet.
vibe_palette: The water is white and the rock is black. The city's lamps refract into a moving smear of yellow.
vibe_materials: Only a stone bench and an iron lamp-hook driven into the rock are built. Both are old.
vibe_signature_feature: The view out shows the city through its own waterfall.
vibe_condition: The chamber is dry and swept. The chamber has been used more recently than it should be.
vibe_mood: The chamber is loud. The falls drown out any conversation.
vibe_approach: The ledge cannot be seen from above. The chamber cannot be seen from anywhere else.
vibe_senses: The water is loud enough to guarantee privacy. A lamp gutters. Footsteps cannot be heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Conclave wants the chamber behind the city's falls opened. The Conclave wants this done before the vicecanons hear of it.
why_site_won: ravine in upland hills (danger band 2), 196 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, bound, landform.
player_purpose_hook: A ledge behind Stormhold's falls leads into an undercut chamber. The chamber has no door.
siting_note: The terrainRequests of this record supply the landform that it names. Part 6's meso compiler carves that landform. The plotted landform class is the pre-carve ground.

name: The Stripped Village
why_founding: Umbriel passed north across the province in 4E 48. The village lay under its shadow. No bodies lie in the village.
why_site_advantages: The village lies directly on Umbriel's recorded track. The ground is good. The neighbouring villages keep off the ground by unspoken agreement.
why_occupants_motive: The houses stand empty. The neighbouring villages keep a vigil, which is a different thing from a taboo.
why_pressures: No graves lie here, because there were no bodies. The vigil-keepers find that harder than a massacre.
why_would_change_if: The village would be resettled if the Waiting Vigil closed its count of the dead. The Waiting Vigil has not closed its count.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Umbriel corridor, a legible line across the province
vibe_silhouette: The village is intact, with every roof sound and every door open. No burial pole stands in the village or around it.
vibe_palette: The thatch has faded to grey-gold. Green growth crowds the walls. The pole field is missing.
vibe_materials: The buildings are built of ordinary mud and reed. They decay only as fast as an unentered building does.
vibe_signature_feature: The pole field is absent. Every Argonian village drives poles for its dead. This ground is bare.
vibe_condition: The buildings are structurally sound after 150 years. The vigil-keepers have never let scavengers near the village.
vibe_approach: No path leads to the village. The village resolves out of the trees, whole.
vibe_senses: The village is silent. Every building is standing.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Umbriel passed over a village. The village stands intact with its pole field bare.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 214 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, bound.
player_purpose_hook: Umbriel passed over this village. The buildings are intact and the pole field is bare. There were no dead left to bury.

name: Sump Rows
why_founding: The Flu emptied the hamlet twice. The hamlet stands on the old Dres road. No family has resettled it since. The men working it now are what is left of a Dres holding-house. They take people off the road in ones and twos. They write each person down. A Dres crew that stops keeping the book stops being paid.
why_site_advantages: Some roofs still keep rain off. A walled stock pen stands there. The surrounding district has agreed not to walk this way.
why_occupants_motive: A house that no longer exists owes the crew wages. The crew trained in one trade. They take their wages in that trade.
why_pressures: Thorn's levy will not cross onto the old road. The Chainbreakers at the Freed Rows know that the camp is here. The Chainbreakers are two hands short of a raiding party.
why_would_change_if: The camp would empty in a night if a raider took the book. Without the book, the crew cannot prove a claim on any captive.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it
vibe_silhouette: The houses have Argonian footings. Velothi timber and lacquer are built up from the footings. Every gable has a shrine-niche.
vibe_palette: Dunmer red-brown lacquer covers Argonian mud-grey footings. The cloth is ash-grey. The sump is green.
vibe_materials: Two cultures are stacked vertically. The footings are Argonian. Everything above waist height is Dunmer.
vibe_signature_feature: The gable niches hold ancestor shrines. Each shrine sits on a house whose foundation belongs to the dead of another people.
vibe_condition: The hamlet has been maintained continuously for four generations. The footings are the oldest part and the best.
vibe_mood: The mood is settled and defensive. The residents are homesick for a place that none of them has seen.
vibe_approach: The path in is overgrown on the neighbours' side. It is clear on the road side.
vibe_senses: The residents speak a different language. Ash-cakes cook. A bell rings that is not an Argonian bell.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A crew with no house left takes people off the old road. The crew then keeps a book about it.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 260 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A Dres crew with no house left is still taking people off the old road. The crew still writes each person down.

name: The Tear Wreck
why_founding: A Dunmer trader out of Tear misread the delta bar in a storm. Her ship is still on the bar, forty years later.
why_site_advantages: The ship lies hard aground on the outer bar, upright. The tide covers the ship to the rail twice a day.
why_occupants_motive: The wreck has no salvagers. The cargo went in the first month. The hull is Dres property in a court that has never sat. Something took the flooded hold in the second year.
why_pressures: The delta villages still use the wreck as a navigation mark. The villagers pass the wreck wide at slack water.
why_would_change_if: The wreck would break up in one bad storm season. The villages would lose their best mark.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a shipping approach or a hazard
vibe_silhouette: A Dunmer hull sits upright on a bar. One mast still stands. The tide runs through her rail.
vibe_palette: The hull paint is weathered red. Black weed covers the hull to the waterline. The mast is bleached.
vibe_materials: The hull is Velothi ship timber, foreign in every line. No other Dunmer work is visible from open water in Argonia.
vibe_signature_feature: The mast stands upright. The villagers have twice re-stayed the mast because it is their mark.
vibe_condition: The wreck is sound below the waterline. Above the deck everything is gone except the mast.
vibe_mood: The wreck feels foreign and forlorn. Divers who go below do not go twice.
vibe_approach: The mast is the delta's principal seamark. The mast reads at three kilometres in clear weather.
vibe_senses: Water moves through the hull. No rigging remains. Birds sit on the rail.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A hull aground upright keeps her hold underwater. That is why the hold has not been emptied. The customs house condemned the hull. The hull went aground before it could be unloaded.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 106 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, hinterland; needs 1.5 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: A hull lies aground upright on the outer bar. Some of her cargo is still stowed. The hold is reached underwater.

name: Terrace Watch
why_founding: The saltrice crop is valuable enough to need watching. The terraces are flat enough that one tower sees all eleven banks.
why_site_advantages: The tower stands on the single knoll in the terrace country. Geology put the knoll there. People have used the knoll ever since.
why_occupants_motive: At harvest the villages set the watch in rotation. The rest of the year the field-owners set the watch.
why_pressures: In harvest the watch in the tower looks out for theft. Out of harvest the watch looks out for surveyors.
why_would_change_if: The villages would pull the tower down if the field-owners ever manned the tower year-round.
siting_prefs_water_relation: commands a route or a channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower
vibe_silhouette: A timber platform stands on four legs. The platform sits on the single knoll that breaks the flat terrace country. A bell hangs on the platform. The watch takes the ladder away.
vibe_palette: The timber is grey. Silver saltrice stretches in every direction. One bright bell hangs on the platform.
vibe_materials: The tower is built of timber and reed. It has no stone, deliberately, so that the watch can dismantle it in a night.
vibe_signature_feature: The ladder is removable. Whoever holds the tower carries the ladder away at dusk.
vibe_condition: The tower is simple and sound. The villages rebuild the tower every few years.
vibe_mood: The mood is watchful. The villages and the field-owners contest the tower at every harvest.
vibe_approach: The platform is the tallest thing in the terrace country. The platform shows from every bank.
vibe_senses: Wind moves through the standing crop. A bell rings. The watch carries the ladder away at dusk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The watch knoll reports a column. The garrison's own books say that the column cannot exist.
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 1766 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: Thorn's watch knoll has been manned every harvest for four generations. The platform sees all eleven banks.

name: Thorn Bond
why_founding: Saltrice goes north and Dunmer goods come south. Both cargoes need a lockable place to sit while the tolls are argued.
why_site_advantages: The bond stands on Thorn's river quay. Cargo is transferred there between the boats and the Tear road.
why_occupants_motive: The field-owners hold the bond jointly. No single owner can be named. Every field-owner audits it in turn.
why_pressures: Half of the north's smuggling passes through the bond legitimately. It then leaves by a different door.
why_would_change_if: Whichever faction won Thorn's title court outright would seize the bond.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: attached to a port or a wharf
vibe_silhouette: A long stone store stands on a quay. A great door is at one end. A small door at the other end carries no seal.
vibe_palette: The quay stone is wet and the timber is black. Red wax seals one door only.
vibe_materials: Dres builders raised the stone store. An Argonian reed-roofed office is bolted to its side.
vibe_signature_feature: The second door is unsealed and unlisted. Its handle is worn smooth.
vibe_condition: The store is sound and well used. The field-owners audit it more in name than in fact.
vibe_mood: The mood is commercial and complicit. Everyone is cheerful about both.
vibe_approach: The great door faces the quay. The small door faces an alley.
vibe_senses: Barrels stand about the store. A tally is called. A door is opened quietly at night.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Thorn's bonded warehouse has a night watchman. He is not on the watch roll.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, bound, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; needs 1.2 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: Thorn's bonded warehouse holds saltrice and Dunmer goods first. One hand on the night watch is not on the roll.

name: The Thousand Birds
why_founding: The north-east islands are flat and free of predators. Fishing water surrounds them. A bird colony has nested there since before the time of the oldest quota-keeper's grandmother.
why_site_advantages: The site is a cluster of low islets in the delta. None of the islets is big enough for a house. Birds have crusted each one white.
why_occupants_motive: The delta villages take eggs to a strict quota. The oldest woman in each village sets the quota. Each village enforces it absolutely.
why_pressures: The egging season and the fishing season overlap. The egg-gatherers' boats and the fishing boats work the same water.
why_would_change_if: The islets would be stripped in three seasons if the quota lapsed. Every village says so about every other village.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: worked seasonally from a nearby settlement
vibe_silhouette: Five low islets are so covered in birds that the land looks as if it is moving. A cloud of birds hangs above them.
vibe_palette: White birds sit on white ground over grey-green water. Birds spot the sky to a great height.
vibe_materials: A quota post on a stake in the water is the sole built object.
vibe_signature_feature: At dusk the whole colony rises at once. The sound reaches the listener a second later.
vibe_condition: Unchanging.
vibe_approach: The noise carries three kilometres over water.
vibe_senses: The noise makes speech impossible. Wings beat. Ammonia smells strongly.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A thief is taking eggs against a quota. Four villages enforce that quota absolutely.
why_site_won: island in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 609 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The delta islets are white with birds. At dusk the whole colony lifts at once.

name: Tide Fair
why_founding: Delta villages, upland holdings and Dunmer caravans can all reach one hard sand bank at low spring tide. There is no other place where the three meet.
why_site_advantages: The site is a firm sand flat. It is exposed for six hours twice a month. Two metres of water cover it for the rest of the time.
why_occupants_motive: Delta villages, upland holdings and caravans trade on the bank. Nothing is built there, because the tide covers the flat again after six hours.
why_pressures: The fair ends when the tide reaches the marker. The traders hold to that end time to the minute.
why_would_change_if: The fair would become impossible if the delta shifted. The delta shifts every few decades.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a landing, because most goods come by water
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: A hundred boats are drawn up on wet sand around a market. The market exists for six hours. It leaves no trace.
vibe_palette: The wet sand is silver. The boat hulls show a dozen colours. The sky is doubled in the sheet water.
vibe_materials: The fair has no structure at all. The market arrives by boat and leaves by boat.
vibe_signature_feature: The tide marker is a single pole. A horn is blown when the water reaches its second band.
vibe_condition: Utterly impermanent.
vibe_approach: Arrival is by water, onto ground that is dry for this one day only.
vibe_senses: A hundred hulls rest on the sand. A horn sounds. Water begins to run in the low channels.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A fair on a sand flat has six hours before two metres of water cover it. A seller will not close a sale. A seizure arrives at the fair with four hours of dry ground left.
why_site_won: cove in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 302 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The market runs for six hours on a sand flat. Then two metres of water cover it. A buyer must buy now or wait a fortnight.

name: Turning Stone
why_founding: A cut stone disc three paces wide sits flush in the marsh floor on a rise. The records of the four villages disagree about its orientation. Two of those records disagree within one lifetime.
why_site_advantages: A patch of bedrock reaches the surface. That is remarkable in this province. It is probably why the builders chose the spot.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages measure the disc separately. None of them claims it. The four villages dislike each other's answers.
why_pressures: The Nisswo say the disc is not their business. The College of Whispers outstation has asked to lift it. All four villages refused at once.
why_would_change_if: The disc would be lifted if a single village allowed it. The other three villages would carry it for a generation.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately unrelated to its surroundings
vibe_silhouette: A pale disc lies flush in dark ground on a low rise. One deep groove crosses it. The rise around it is bare marsh floor.
vibe_palette: Bleached stone lies against black peat. The groove holds water and reads as a black line.
vibe_materials: The disc is cut stone of a kind that does not outcrop within thirty kilometres. The four villages recognise no method by which it was dressed.
vibe_signature_feature: The groove runs off the rise in one direction. Four villages have set marker posts around it. The posts record four different bearings.
vibe_condition: The disc is untouched. It is unweathered in a way that stone this old should not be.
vibe_mood: The place feels patient and slightly wrong. Villagers who live near it are elaborately casual about it.
vibe_approach: The rise is bare. The disc does not show until the visitor is standing on it.
vibe_senses: The rise has no sound or smell of note. It is measurably quieter on the rise than off it. The villages have noticed this.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The disc is a genuine unexplained thing. Four communities will not let it be moved.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 967 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Bare bedrock has a turn cut into it. No other stone like it exists in the province. The cut is not weathered.

name: Two-Gate Bridge
why_founding: The Tear road crosses the north-eastern river once. The two banks belong to different interests.
why_site_advantages: A rock narrows the river, with abutments on each side. No other single span crosses this river.
why_occupants_motive: Each bank has built its own gate house. A cart driver pays twice or argues twice.
why_pressures: The two toll-holders have not spoken directly in nine years. They communicate by written notes that are carried between the gate houses.
why_would_change_if: The bridge would have one toll if either bank bought out the other. Both banks have refused on principle.
siting_prefs_water_relation: spans a channel at its narrowest
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight
vibe_silhouette: One bridge has two gate houses, one at each end. They are painted in different colours and face each other.
vibe_palette: The river below is green. The two gate houses are in deliberately clashing paint.
vibe_materials: Dres builders raised a stone span. Argonians added two timber gate houses at opposite ends.
vibe_signature_feature: The note line is a cord strung under the deck with a box on it. Messages are carried along it between people who will not meet.
vibe_condition: The bridge is sound. Both gate houses are over-built.
vibe_approach: Traffic pays the toll at the first gate house. The second gate house stands beyond the crossing.
vibe_senses: Two bells ring. The cord and box run under the deck. The river sounds below.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Two toll-holders on one bridge have not spoken in nine years. Their receipts have started matching.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LD47 · tier-3; LD48 · tier-3; PP13 · tier-3; Reed track · tier-2
why_site_won: gorge in firm lowland (danger band 2), 20 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: One span has a gate house at each end. Two toll-holders keep two tolls. They have not spoken in nine years.
siting_note: The terrainRequests of this record supply the landform that it names. Part 6's meso compiler carves that landform. The plotted landform class is the pre-carve ground.

name: The Two Hundred Roofs
why_founding: A large Kothringi-Argonian village stood here. The Flu emptied it in one season. Sixteen centuries later, it is still empty. The naming taboo keeps people out. The disease does not. The roofs have no lawful claimant left alive. In the north, ground passes only to a claimant who can say whose it was.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on good high ground on the channel network. Its emptiness is the most conspicuous thing in the district.
why_occupants_motive: Only the taboo remains in the village now. Habit maintains the taboo. Fear does not maintain it.
why_pressures: Boat crews use the village landing. The crews will not sleep above the landing steps. They observe that line without discussing it.
why_would_change_if: Newcomers who are unfamiliar with the taboo would resettle the village tomorrow.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it
vibe_silhouette: Two hundred roof frames with no thatch stand in rows on a rise. They are silhouetted like ribs.
vibe_palette: The timber is bare and grey. The ground is green. Sky shows through every roof.
vibe_materials: The frames are Argonian frames without their reed. The impermanent material went and the frames stayed.
vibe_signature_feature: The reed rotted within years of the village emptying. The timber frames have stood ever since.
vibe_condition: Skeletal, stable, unlooted.
vibe_approach: From the channel the rise looks like a fence of vertical timbers against the sky. It is visible at eight hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Wind blows through two hundred empty frames. It makes a sound like a single low note.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A newcomer claims two hundred empty roof frames. Northern custom holds that no living name can claim them.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 85 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; needs 0.6 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: Two hundred roof frames stand on the best ground in the district. Every one of them is empty.

name: The Veterans' Ridge
why_founding: Argonians went north into Morrowind in 4E 5–6 and came back. They settled together on the ridge. The pass through which they came home can be seen from the ridge.
why_site_advantages: The ridge is high ground with a clear line to the pass. The settlers chose it for the view. They did not choose it for the soil.
why_occupants_motive: The veterans' grandchildren hold the ridge as an institution. Here the invasion is remembered as a victory. Elsewhere in the province it is barely remembered.
why_pressures: The Dres holding is four hours away. Both households know precisely what the other is.
why_would_change_if: The ridge would lose its meaning when the last person to hear the story from a participant dies.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: toward the Morrowind border and the Tear road
vibe_silhouette: A long low hall stands on a ridge. Every house behind it faces north. Dunmer banners are nailed to the gable.
vibe_palette: The ridge is brown under thatch. The captured Velothi cloth is faded red.
vibe_materials: All construction is Argonian. Every trophy in the hall is Dunmer.
vibe_signature_feature: The gable banners were taken in 4E 6. The hall-holders rehang them every year. The banners are going to pieces.
vibe_condition: The hall is well kept. It is the best-built Argonian building in the district.
vibe_approach: The line of the ridge and the banners on the hall can be seen against the sky from the road below.
vibe_senses: A drum sounds in the evening. Wind blows on the ridge. Old men argue about a date.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Morrowind veterans hold a ridge against an order that was countermanded generations ago. A physician's treatment notes double as a record of who descends from whom.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LQ20 · tier-3; LV46 · tier-3; LV47 · tier-3
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 356 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Morrowind veterans hold a ridge for the view of the pass. They still expect an arrival.

name: Shrine of Haynekhtnamet
why_founding: Villagers left offerings to a wamasu of Shadowfen to stop the seasonal flooding. The stone shelf on the bank is where they left them.
why_site_advantages: The stone shelf stands on the bank above the pond that the creature is held to inhabit. The bank is at the highest point that the flood reaches.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages send offerings each wet season, in rotation. A headwoman who is asked why will say it is her turn.
why_pressures: The offerings are increasingly practical. They are tools and salt, not symbols. The older villagers find that embarrassing.
why_would_change_if: The villages would abandon the shelf in a dry decade. They would set it up again after the next bad flood.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: between a village and a lair
vibe_silhouette: A stone shelf stands on a bank above black water. Tools, salt and cord lie on it. All of it is slowly corroding.
vibe_palette: The water is green-black. The iron is corroded. The salt is white. Scorch marks cover the shelf.
vibe_materials: One dressed stone shelf is the whole construction.
vibe_signature_feature: Scorch marks cover the shelf. The shelf is struck. The offerings nearest the water are the most burnt.
vibe_condition: The shelf is older than the villages that use it. Most of what lies on it is from this year or last.
vibe_approach: Ozone can be smelled before the water comes into sight.
vibe_senses: Water sounds nearby. A dry crackle sounds with no flame behind it. Hair stands on end.
quest_hooks_opportunity: People still leave offerings above a pond that they say holds a leviathan. This year the flooding got worse.
why_site_won: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 613 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Villagers left offerings to stop the flooding. They still do. The offering shelf stands above a pond that people say holds Haynekhtnamet.
watch_reason: The shrine has no residents. Villagers come to leave offerings.

name: Unpermitted Cut
why_founding: A crew is digging on the far side of Outer Silyanorn without a permit. The crew digs at night. The crew is digging for something specific.
why_site_advantages: The cut lies behind the spoil ridge of the ruin. The fence of the licensed dig blocks the line of sight from the road.
why_occupants_motive: Hired diggers work the cut. The person who pays them is not here. That person sends written instructions.
why_pressures: The instructions name a chamber. None of the plans that the Collections holds shows that chamber.
why_would_change_if: The diggers would abandon the cut within an hour of discovery. They would burn the instructions.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Umbriel corridor, or at an unwatched ruin
vibe_silhouette: A cut runs into the spoil ridge. Hooded lamps burn in it. The diggers work it at night and cover it with brush by day.
vibe_palette: Lamp light is held down to a slot. The spoil is brown. Green brush lies over the spoil.
vibe_materials: The cut is an open excavation. It holds hooded lamps, brush screens and a rope ladder that leads down into it.
vibe_signature_feature: The instruction sheet is weighted with a stone at the edge of the cut. The diggers cannot read the handwriting.
vibe_condition: The diggers conceal the cut by day and work it by night. The cut is three weeks old.
vibe_approach: By day the cut looks like a brush pile. At night a light shows where no light should be.
vibe_senses: The diggers keep the digging deliberately quiet. A lamp hood is adjusted. The diggers do not talk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An unpermitted cut is being paid for from Leyawiin. The payer is known only as a name on a draft.
why_site_won: open water in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 182 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: An unpermitted cut lies behind the spoil ridge, out of sight of the licensed dig. The person who pays for it is not local.

name: White Pans
why_founding: Salt is the north's second currency. The Tear road stage prefers salt to coin. The delta makes salt for free, given sun and time.
why_site_advantages: The site is a flat tidal margin with high evaporation. A rock bar keeps the sea out of the pans except when the families open it to the sea water.
why_occupants_motive: Six families work the pans. The tide sets the rotation, not agreement. This avoids most quarrels.
why_pressures: The salt smugglers on the rim ledge buy here. The pan families weigh the salt and take the coin.
why_would_change_if: The pans would flood permanently if the rock bar were breached. Traders across the north would feel the loss of the barter economy.
siting_prefs_water_relation: tidal salt water, sun and wind
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: supplies a whole district's preservation
vibe_silhouette: A grid of shallow pans shows every stage from grey water to blinding white. Rakes stand in the finished pans.
vibe_palette: The pans are white on grey. A pink stain colours two of them.
vibe_materials: The pan walls are clay and the rakes are timber. The store is reed on a stone plinth.
vibe_signature_feature: Two pans of the grid go rose-coloured every summer. The families work them last, for luck.
vibe_condition: The families rebuild the pans each season. They re-puddle the pan walls every spring.
vibe_mood: The pans are bright and blinding. The work is slow.
vibe_approach: The white can be seen from a kilometre away in sunlight.
vibe_senses: Rakes scrape on crust. Gulls call. Wind carries salt into the mouth.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Salt is the north's second currency. One family controls where it comes ashore. Salt from the pans is paid out as wages. This suits the families who set the rate. It does not suit those who are paid in salt.
why_site_won: cove in ocean (danger band 0), 111 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A family that controls the rock bar works the salt pans. Salt is the north's second currency.

name: Wild Mouth
why_founding: The site is the tunnel mouth of an untamed rootworm. It lies two kilometres off the northern line of the Waykeepers. The animal is the same kind that the Waykeepers ride. This one has no rig and no handler.
why_site_advantages: The ground is soft and root-bound, which the animal can work. The site is close enough to the tamed line to worry the Waykeepers. It is far enough away that they do not act against it.
why_occupants_motive: Only the animal occupies the tunnel. It is territorial and large. It took a Waykeeper off a rigged worm two years ago.
why_pressures: The line of the Waykeepers runs close. A wild worm has cut across it twice in a decade.
why_would_change_if: The Waykeepers would have to deal with the worm, at expense, the first time it took the tunnel of a loaded transit worm.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on or beside the root-transit network, where the Waykeepers' loaded worms pass it
vibe_silhouette: A tunnel mouth two metres across opens in a root bank. Cut root ends rim it. The mouth has none of the timber facing that a tamed station would have.
vibe_palette: The roots are wet and brown. The tunnel is black. A pale ring of freshly cut root shows how recently the worm was working.
vibe_materials: The mouth is unfaced and unlit. It shows none of the signs that mark a Waykeeper station.
vibe_signature_feature: The cut ends are root that has been severed cleanly. Their size shows that the animal is bigger than the ones that people ride.
vibe_condition: The tunnel is active. The cut ring is fresh again within days.
vibe_mood: The mouth is frightening in a way that the tame stations are not.
vibe_approach: The ground gives differently within thirty metres of the mouth. That is the only warning.
vibe_senses: A working sound is felt through the soles of the feet, on and off. Above ground the site is silent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A very large animal lives in a tunnel. The tunnel lies two kilometres from the line that the worm has already cut twice.
why_site_won: flood high in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 707 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: A wild rootworm burrow lies close enough to the tamed line to worry the Waykeepers. It lies far enough away that they do not act against it.

name: Xanmeer Hold
why_founding: A tribe took a xanmeer's walls and the defences in them that still work. They have lived there ever since. It is the best-fortified hold in the north.
why_site_advantages: The hold is a terraced stone mass on firm ground in the channels. The mechanisms on the lower terraces still work.
why_occupants_motive: Sul-Xan and two later invasions have come through the north in four centuries. The walls held each time. That is why the tribe is still in them.
why_pressures: Living in stone is a compromise. The tribe's neighbours notice it. The tribe answers that they did not build it.
why_would_change_if: The hold would be the north's refuge of last resort in a real emergency. The tribe has said as much.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: dominates its immediate district
vibe_silhouette: A stepped stone mass carries reed houses on each terrace. Smoke rises from them. A barred stone gate stands at the bottom.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey, in terraces. The reed is gold, in horizontal bands. Smoke rises over both.
vibe_materials: The base is xanmeer stone. A present-day Argonian village of reed and mud is built onto it. Nothing is bonded into the stone. The villagers could take it all off in a week.
vibe_signature_feature: The living terraces carry houses that could be taken down in a day. The stone beneath is four thousand years old.
vibe_condition: The tribe maintains the stone where it defends the hold. They ignore it where it does not. They rebuild the reed on the usual cycle.
vibe_mood: The hold feels secure and watchful. It is a little smug.
vibe_approach: The stepped silhouette, with smoke rising from every level, can be seen over the canopy at a kilometre.
vibe_senses: A great many households live at close quarters. The gate mechanism is the loudest sound in the district.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The old mechanisms of a xanmeer that is held as a fort still work. Whoever holds the xanmeer this year can use them.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 1168 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger.
player_purpose_hook: A xanmeer is held as a fort. Whoever holds it can use the old mechanisms on the lower terraces, which still work.

name: Thorn
why_founding: Fields ring Thorn, which is a rarity in the north. The fields grow saltrice on temperate grassland. The farmers first grew it for House Dres. They now grow it for whoever holds the title.
why_site_advantages: Thorn stands on firm grassland above a delta. The Tear road runs out to Morrowind. River access runs down to the coast. No other place in Argonia has all three together.
why_occupants_motive: The vicecanon governs Thorn. The field-owners decide in practice. The Dunmer minority holds the trade. The Dunmer remember who used to hold the people.
why_pressures: Every field title is disputed. The smugglers pay the guards, who look away from the smuggling. Both sides of the argument are funded from the border tolls.
why_would_change_if: The people of Thorn would turn on one another if Morrowind pressed a claim. They know it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the northeastern frontier; Tear two days north, Alten Corimont west
vibe_silhouette: A low walled city stands in a sea of pale saltrice. One grey Hist crown stands outside the wall. Nothing inside the wall is as tall as the crown.
vibe_palette: The saltrice is silver-green. The wall is dun. The Dunmer quarter shows red lacquer. The Hist is pale grey.
vibe_materials: Inside the wall the buildings are Argonian mud and reed. The Dunmer quarter uses Velothi-influenced timber and lacquer. Where the two meet, the join is a street.
vibe_signature_feature: The Hist stands outside the walls. The people of Thorn depend on the tree. The builders deliberately did not enclose it.
vibe_condition: Thorn is prosperous. It is over-guarded at the gates and under-guarded everywhere else.
vibe_mood: Thorn is wealthy and litigious. Its people are conscious of how its fields were won.
vibe_approach: Across the fields the wall shows as a low line. The Hist crown shows above the wall long before any roof.
vibe_senses: Wind moves through standing saltrice. A Dunmer market bell rings. Guar caravans pass. Wet-season frogs call in the delta.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The field titles are disputed. A Dunmer frontier presence stands in the city. Border tolls and smuggling run through the city. The city is the venue of the Ash-Reed Accord. A magistracy, a Dunmer militia hall and a saltrice counting floor stand in one city. Vicecanon Neetra-Sei's boat hosts a meeting afloat. A delegate cannot storm out of that meeting. A memorial square carries two dates.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: TA02 · tier-2; LD34 · tier-3; LD35 · tier-3; LD36 · tier-3; LD37 · tier-3; LD38 · tier-3; LD39 · tier-3; LD40 · tier-3; LD41 · tier-3; LD42 · tier-3; LD43 · tier-3; LD44 · tier-3; LD45 · tier-3; LD46 · tier-3; LD47 · tier-3; LD48 · tier-3; LD49 · tier-3; LD50 · tier-3; LD51 · tier-3; LD52 · tier-3; LD53 · tier-3; LD54 · tier-3; LD55 · tier-3; LD56 · tier-3; LD57 · tier-3; LD58 · tier-3; LD59 · tier-3; LD60 · tier-3; LD61 · tier-3; LD62 · tier-3; LD63 · tier-3; LD64 · tier-3; LD65 · tier-3; LQ19 · tier-3; MQ12 · tier-3
why_site_won: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'thorn' (world/sources/anchors); the anchor pixel is the city gate on the main road. The record sits at the solved city centre (cityLayout, owner rule 2026-09-18).
player_purpose_hook: Thorn is the field-owners' city. It has a road to Morrowind and a river to the coast. Work is on offer there to those who do not ask about the fields.
complexity_justification: Thorn is a major city with a walled core. It has an unblended Dunmer trade quarter. A Hist stands outside the walls. A working field system must be compiled as landscape as well as settlement.

name: Thorn Terraces
why_founding: Saltrice is the north's cash crop. That is why a foreign house wanted this ground. The house pursued that ambition for four centuries. The terraces are the result.
why_site_advantages: The site is a shallow tilt of grassland above the delta. Farmers can admit salt water there in controlled amounts. Saltrice needs both the tilt and the salt water.
why_occupants_motive: The villages work the terraces. Whoever last won in Thorn's title court owns them on paper.
why_pressures: The salt gates are the whole system. One family holds three of the eleven gates. That family charges a fee for them.
why_would_change_if: If a delta shift took the salt gates, the crop would fail in two seasons.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a city's hinterland; owned
vibe_silhouette: Eleven wide terraces of standing water step down to a delta. Each terrace is a different shade. A stone gate stands at the head of every bank.
vibe_palette: The saltrice is silver-green. The water is brackish grey. Salt crust whitens the gate lips.
vibe_materials: The bunds are earth with cut stone gates. The rest of the terracing is earth, not stone. Dres builders raised the gates.
vibe_signature_feature: Every gate carries a white rime of salt crust. The rime shows how the gate is being worked.
vibe_condition: The bunds are immaculate. The gates are four centuries old. The villages patch the gates more each year.
vibe_mood: The mood is prosperous and calculating. The people are tense about water.
vibe_approach: From the Tear road the terraces flash in sequence during the descent.
vibe_senses: Water runs through the gates. Bird-scarers clatter. A great deal of standing water lies in the wind.
quest_hooks_opportunity: TA03 is saltrice ground. The fields are held under occupation. A counting house and a drying floor stand there. The boundary has gone unwalked for forty years.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 85 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, bound; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The terraces grow saltrice. The gate-holders let salt water in by hand. They decide the district's year.

name: Three-Ways-Over-Water
why_founding: The junction is a smaller one on the Thorn side. Three walkways meet at a single great trunk. The builders used the tree as the platform and built no platform of their own.
why_site_advantages: One tree is large enough to carry three walkway arms. The tree lies off the walked tracks entirely.
why_occupants_motive: A rope-and-lamp keeper lives in the trunk's first fork. The villages on all three lines pay her in food.
why_pressures: The tree is alive and growing. The trunk is growing over the walkway fixings. Every few years the keeper has to re-hang an arm higher.
why_would_change_if: When the tree dies, the villages would have to rebuild the junction from scratch as a piled platform. No record gives the rebuild's cost.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: connects three or more water settlements
vibe_silhouette: Three walkways converge on one huge trunk. A lamp hangs in the fork above them. The arms sit visibly at three different heights.
vibe_palette: The wet bark is black. The lamp is yellow. Pale scars mark where old fixings were cut out of the tree.
vibe_materials: Lashings go around the living wood. No fixings are driven into it. The keeper replaces the lashings on a schedule that she holds in her head.
vibe_signature_feature: The fixing scars form a vertical ladder of old cuts up the trunk. The scars record every time the walkways were re-hung.
vibe_condition: The junction is sound. It looks visibly temporary against a tree that keeps growing.
vibe_approach: The lamp is the landmark. The tree resolves out of the canopy only in the last hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Rope creaks. The keeper trims a lamp. Water moves around a trunk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The keeper's knowledge exists only in her head.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 466 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, nearPoint, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-ash-causeway (+1.30).
player_purpose_hook: One trunk in the water carries the walkways of three villages. Travellers cross here or pole a long way round.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at this position. The record sits on the Argonian marsh side of the region, where the two zones interleave. The catalogue files it with the north because its trade, its levies and its neighbours are northern. The place was moved to the Thorn-side walkway water that its prose describes. It had been plotted on the Stormhold side, three kilometres from any walkway network.

name: Ties-Four-Ways
why_founding: Four elevated walkways from four villages meet over open water here. No village would let the junction sit on the ground of another village. The four villages built it on a platform on piles in the middle of a lake.
why_site_advantages: The water is deep enough that no bank claims it. It is shallow enough to drive piles. The site is equidistant from all four villages to within a few hundred paces.
why_occupants_motive: One stall keeper sells to all four villages. She pays no toll. She is from none of the four villages.
why_pressures: Each village maintains every plank on its own arm. The condition of the junction shows which of the four villages has kept up its arm.
why_would_change_if: The junction would collapse into four dead ends in the year that two villages stopped repairing their arms. One village has already slipped.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: connects three or more water settlements
vibe_silhouette: A cross of raised walkways meets on an octagonal platform in open water. One awning stands on the platform. Nothing else stands there.
vibe_palette: The timber is weathered grey in four visibly different shades. The water is black. The single awning is red.
vibe_materials: The walkway timber is lashed and pegged. Each arm follows the habits of its own village. The arms meet badly in the middle.
vibe_signature_feature: The four arms do not match. They differ in width, rail height and repair standard. All four butt against one octagon.
vibe_condition: Three arms are sound. One arm is springy. The octagon is the best-kept thing on the lake.
vibe_approach: The awning shows from a long way over flat water. It is not clear until late which arm the other party is using.
vibe_senses: Boards sound in four different tones underfoot. Water lies beneath the boards. The stallholder greets each of the four villages in the same way.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Four communities all use this neutral ground. A meeting can be arranged there. A meeting can also be ambushed there.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 163 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, route.
player_purpose_hook: A pile-driven junction joins four walkways. It is equidistant from four villages. The villages argue the tolls in the middle.
siting_note: The culture raster reads hist-heartland at this position. The record sits on the Argonian marsh side of the region, where the two zones interleave. The catalogue files it with the north because its trade, its levies and its neighbours are northern.

name: Thorn Rat Gallery
why_founding: An Imperial warden worked penal labour into these galleries for crystal. The warden promised limited freedom. The warden died in office. The galleries are still worked.
why_site_advantages: The galleries are the deepest reachable level of the undercity, below the licensed diggings. The seams that the licensed diggers will not risk still run there.
why_occupants_motive: The people down here work an Owing. The Owing has been transferred so many times that the name of the original creditor is lost.
why_pressures: The gallery floods on an unpredictable schedule. The licensed diggers above now post the tide days at the shaft head.
why_would_change_if: The galleries would empty in a day if the Owing ledgers above them were voided.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: below or beside a carceral site
vibe_silhouette: A single hoist shaft goes down into the dark. Below it lie galleries with no headroom.
vibe_palette: The galleries are black and lamp-yellow. Wet Ayleid white shows where a lamp catches carving.
vibe_materials: Spoil has reduced the Ayleid galleries to crawl-ways. Timber props hold them. Nothing is built in them. The galleries are narrowed.
vibe_signature_feature: The flood tally is scratched by the hoist. It records days since the last flood and days between floods. The people below keep the tally.
vibe_condition: The galleries are structurally appalling. They work because the licensed diggers above do not have to look at them.
vibe_mood: The air is stale. Fury lies under the patience.
vibe_approach: Only the hoist frame shows above ground. It looks like the equipment of the diggings.
vibe_senses: Water moves somewhere below. A hoist rope creaks. People breathe in a confined space.
quest_hooks_opportunity: People who are not counted in the city work the lowest gallery of the undercity. Then the gallery floods.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 1053 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-high-wrappings (+0.76).
player_purpose_hook: The gallery is the deepest reachable level of the undercity, below the licensed diggings. People who are not counted work it.

name: Waits-For-The-Promise
why_founding: The An-Xileel promised a clean province and a return of ground. The camp holds families from three villages that the Xit-Xaht took. The families camp on the boundary of land that was theirs. They wait for the promise to be kept.
why_site_advantages: The site is the boundary itself. The camp sits on the old line. Others work the ground behind the camp.
why_occupants_motive: No family here will move, because moving would lose the argument. Every family present has a claim, a witness and a name. No court will hear any of the claims.
why_pressures: It is the fifth year of the camp. The families have built a mud oven and a well. They read those as a defeat.
why_would_change_if: The camp would end on the day that the An-Xileel gave a ruling either way. The families fear the ruling more than the wait.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Umbriel corridor
vibe_silhouette: A line of shelters is strung along a boundary bank in single file. All of the shelters face the same way. A mud oven and a well stand at one end.
vibe_palette: The shelters are grey canvas and reed. The worked ground on the other side of the bank is vivid green.
vibe_materials: The shelters are reed and canvas. The families rebuilt their one mud oven twice.
vibe_signature_feature: Every shelter faces the ground that its family lost.
vibe_condition: Five years of temporary.
vibe_mood: The mood is stubborn and exhausted. The families are close to done waiting.
vibe_approach: The bank path runs the length of the camp. Every shelter turns side-on to the path.
vibe_senses: A well rope creaks. Children play on a boundary bank. Conversation stops at close range.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The families hold a land claim with witnesses and a name but no court. The An-Xileel's promise sits on the ground. The families are one bad week from turning the camp into a raid.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: TA03 · tier-2; LD40 · tier-3; PP06 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 930 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-pilots-rest (+0.40).
player_purpose_hook: A camp sits on the old boundary line. Others work the ground behind the camp.

name: Waits-For-The-Trial
why_founding: Hissmir's Trials cannot admit all of the waiting pilgrims at once. The pilgrims who are not admitted camp on the last dry ground before the village. Some of them camp there for a week. A few stay for a whole season.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the last firm ground on the pilgrim path. Water and wood are at hand. The village is visible from the camp, two hundred metres off.
why_occupants_motive: The pilgrims keep an order of arrival. Most of them are Hist-less and unwilling to go home. The Root Stewards do not recognise the order. The pilgrims in the camp obey it anyway.
why_pressures: The waiting order governs the camp. The pilgrims enforce it. They have little else left.
why_would_change_if: The camp would empty overnight if the Stewards refused a new arrival. The Stewards cannot refuse. For that reason the camp keeps growing.
siting_prefs_water_relation: water and firm ground on a pilgrim route
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the last stop before a sacred destination
vibe_silhouette: Forty low shelters stand in rows on a dry shoulder of ground. A numbered stake stands at the head of each row. The village is lit on the ridge above.
vibe_palette: The shelter canvas is brown and grey. The cook-fires are orange. The pale stone of the xanmeer up the hill catches the last light.
vibe_materials: The pilgrims built the camp from whatever they arrived carrying. The materials are canvas and reed. There is one Dunmer travelling tent. A great deal of borrowed rope ties the camp together.
vibe_signature_feature: The stake board holds a numbered order of arrival. The pilgrims keep the board themselves. They write it in four scripts.
vibe_condition: The camp is semi-permanent. It is less so every year. Three of the shelters have chimneys.
vibe_mood: The mood in the camp is hopeful and tense. The pilgrims organised the camp out of necessity.
vibe_approach: The path comes up from below. The camp stands between the path and the village.
vibe_senses: Four languages are spoken in the camp. The cooks feed a lot of people. When the xanmeer's bell rings, the whole camp counts the strokes.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Places in the queue for the Trials can be bought, given away or jumped. A Hist-less community has a grievance but has nowhere to take it.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 428 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The pilgrims camp in sight of the village. The village has not yet called them up.

name: Went-Down-Slowly
why_founding: Went-Down-Slowly stands on drying peat beside an upland tarn in the border mountains. Five houses went into the ground over about a decade. The peat beneath them compacted slowly. The households kept re-levelling the floors until the doors would no longer open.
why_site_advantages: When the houses were built, this was the best-drained ground in the district. The ground was drying peat, which is why it sank.
why_occupants_motive: The last household left while the roof was still intact. The walls then stood at an angle of eleven degrees.
why_pressures: The subsidence has not stopped. The site is measurably lower each decade. The hollow now holds water for half the year.
why_would_change_if: The site would be a pond within two generations. The people of the nearby villages have already stopped using its name.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: above workings or burning peat
vibe_silhouette: Five roofs sit at wrong angles in a shallow saucer of ground. The door lintels stand at knee height. One chimney is still upright.
vibe_palette: The peat is brown-black. The thatch has gone grey-green. Standing water in the low corner reflects a sky that should not be visible from inside a house.
vibe_materials: The houses are ordinary mud-and-reed buildings. Their floors were repeatedly re-levelled inside. The interiors hold a stack of four floors. Each floor is flatter than the walls around it.
vibe_signature_feature: The floors show the re-levellings. A section cut anywhere shows the floors one on top of another.
vibe_condition: Standing, tilted, going down.
vibe_approach: The saucer cannot be seen from anywhere but its rim. From the rim, all five roofs lie below.
vibe_senses: Water lies where a floor should be. Wind blows through a door that is now a slot. The thatch moves.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The floors of one house form a diary of a resident who refused to leave.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 853 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The site was the best-drained ground in the district, which is why it sank. The houses are still standing, as level as when they went down.
siting_note: The owner promoted this place from the reserve on 2026-09-04. It fills an off-route D3 gap at (2144, 345). The aim is to have more fights off the road and fewer on it.

name: Wolk Market
why_founding: A market grew where the Tear road out of Morrowind meets the marsh tracks and the poled water routes from the north villages. Its name is the name of the ruin off the road to the east, shortened. The local villages did not want a town named after Boethiah. No set of directions worked without the landmark either.
