why_site_advantages: The market stands on firm ground at the hinge of the three roads. It lies above the flooding that closes the road on either side for two months a year. Spring water suffices for a market. It is not enough to tempt a port builder.
why_occupants_motive: The market takes a cut of the goods moving between the interior, the border city and the smugglers' port. On every market day, three sets of weights are argued into one here.
why_pressures: The vicecanons want the market fees. The river brokers want the warehousing. The market has spent forty years keeping both out.
why_would_change_if: Armies would fight over the market in the week that any of the three roads mattered militarily. The town has three walls and no fourth.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a road convergence on a spring, above the flood line
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the hinge of a district; several villages depend on it; the shunned ruin lies half a morning's walk off the road to the east
vibe_silhouette: The town is square, with three gates and no fourth wall. The market square is laid out in three wedges.
vibe_palette: The town is dust ochre. The awnings show colours from three different regions. The dust of three roads lies on all of it.
vibe_materials: The town is built of mud-brick and reed. An interior-style uxith stands on the west side. Stormhold terrace stone forms the north gate. Three building habits meet along one street.
vibe_signature_feature: Goods from each road are sold in their own third of the square. Mixing the goods is a fine. The market-warden levies the fine cheerfully.
vibe_condition: The town is well kept and is expanding westward. It is entirely unfortified.
vibe_mood: The townsfolk are cosmopolitan by northern standards and sharp about weights. They are superstitious about the eastern road.
vibe_approach: All three roads run straight at the town. The market bell carries further than the roofs are visible. The eastern road is the quiet one, because of what lies half a morning up it.
vibe_senses: Three dialects are spoken. Guar and porters move through the streets. A market bell hangs at each of the three gates. The bells are rung out of step on purpose.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The market is the northern road hinge. It is a three-way market where a courier line can be picked up or lost. A Marsh Charter factor has authority over weights and therefore over disputes.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LV06 · tier-3; LV07 · tier-3; LV08 · tier-3; LV09 · tier-3; LV10 · tier-3; LV11 · tier-3; LV12 · tier-3; LV13 · tier-3; LV14 · tier-3; LV15 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 86 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The market is the district's hinge. It is a three-wedge market where road, track and water meet. The shunned ruin stands in plain sight beside it.

name: Zuuk
why_founding: Zuuk was a Kothringi settlement. It died in 2E 561, one year into the Flu. The name of its founder is still on it.
why_site_advantages: Zuuk stands on a firm bank on the Shadowfen channels. The ground is good. Every boat that passes sees the settlement standing empty.
why_occupants_motive: Zuuk has no residents. The people of the neighbouring villages route their boats past without stopping. They have done so for three hundred years.
why_pressures: Zuuk is the best unclaimed landing in the district. The taboo keeps it unclaimed.
why_would_change_if: Settlers would resettle Zuuk within a decade if the north ever grew enough to need the ground.
siting_prefs_water_relation: coastal and riverine — they were sea-going
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the west and centre, where the Kothringi lived
vibe_silhouette: A stone landing has a name cut into it. Behind the landing stands a settlement whose walls are standing and whose roofs are gone.
vibe_palette: The stone is silver-grey. The doorways are black. Green growth reaches the doorsteps and stops.
vibe_materials: The walls are Kothringi coursed stone. It is finer stone than the surrounding villages use. No Argonian repair appears anywhere.
vibe_signature_feature: The founder's name is cut at the landing. It is still legible and uneffaced.
vibe_condition: Untouched after three centuries.
vibe_approach: From the channel, the landing steps show first. The name is cut at the eye height of a boat passenger.
vibe_senses: Water laps on the stone steps. Wind blows through the roofless rooms. No boats stop here.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Kothringi work stands on the best ground on the road. Every villager gives a different reason for leaving the ground empty.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 883 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Kothringi work stands on good ground that the neighbouring villages will not take. It stands in plain sight of passing boats.

name: The Held Breath
why_founding: The Held Breath is a maintained air pocket on a flooded root route. Divers keep the pocket in repair so that the crossing is survivable.
why_site_advantages: The pocket lies at the midpoint of the longest flooded branch in the region.
why_occupants_motive: The pocket is unstaffed. Passers-by maintain it under an interior custom. Anyone who uses the shelter repairs it before leaving.
why_pressures: The seal leaks. The pocket is smaller each decade. The Waykeepers who could reseal it will not work outside a paid line.
why_would_change_if: If the pocket were lost, the flooded route would become impassable. Every crossing would then go by the long root gallery. That route takes a day longer and is a band of danger worse.
traversal_fallback: The fallback is to walk the surface route. The walk takes two days over D5 ground.
vibe_silhouette: The pocket shows nothing from outside. Divers find it by diving.
vibe_palette: The root-brown walls are lit by a single carried lamp. Silver bubbles pin under the ceiling. The tally scars are pale against the dark bark. A dropped flower has gone black at the dive line.
vibe_materials: The seal is old resin that was poured thin and is cracking at the rim. The bubble ceiling is bare root with no lashing at all. The tally marks are cut, not painted. There are four hundred of them. The dry stores are wedged into a natural root shelf.
vibe_signature_feature: A dry bubble the size of a room lies thirty metres down a flooded gallery. A tally is cut into the root, with one mark for each rest taken.
vibe_condition: The seal is thinner every year. The Waykeepers have not been paid to reseal it.
vibe_approach: The dive to the pocket is one held breath from the last air.
vibe_senses: Divers hold their breath. They hear the pop of a fresh air pocket breaking the surface. Cold water presses at the ankles even when the chest is dry. The ceiling drips on a slow count. Divers use the count to time the next dive.
why_site_won: islet in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 377 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: A room of dry air lies thirty metres down a flooded root gallery. Four hundred marks in the wall record one rest each.

name: Alten Markmont
why_founding: Alten Markmont is a trading station that faces outsiders. It was built where the southern water route met the Helstrom approach. The alten- prefix marks it as never Argonian.
why_site_advantages: The station has a landing on deep-enough water. It lies at the last point at which outsiders were tolerated.
why_occupants_motive: A skeleton staff of two factors runs the station. Those who shelter in the warehouses also stay there. A company that no longer trades here pays the two factors a retainer. The company holds that a lapsed post is cheaper to hold than to re-license.
why_pressures: The interior tolerates the station but does not need it. The trade that the station was built for stopped. The warehouses now shelter people whom the factors are not allowed to register.
why_would_change_if: A single busy season would refill the station. The Helstrom assembly has decided that there will not be one.
vibe_silhouette: A company mark hangs on the wall of a building that is far too large for its occupancy.
vibe_palette: The quay stone is weathered grey. Faded company red shows on peeling paint. Brown floodwater laps the loading step. Dust lies pale on the empty shelving.
vibe_materials: An Imperial company crew raised the dressed stone quay walls. The warehouse timber is squared and jointed, with no local lashing. The roof shingle was imported once and has never been matched since. Iron strapping is rusting loose at the hinges.
vibe_signature_feature: Imperial warehouse frontage stands over a quay that the marsh has taken back to the knee. The frontage was never blended with a single Argonian building.
vibe_condition: Two factors keep the ledgers. The roof goes unrepaired.
vibe_mood: The station is commercial architecture without a trade. Dry rot affects the roof beams.
vibe_approach: The stone shows through the reeds a long way before the buildings resolve.
vibe_senses: Damp paper and old ledger dust hang in the warehouse air. Standing water slaps at the loading step. Canvas awnings hang slack in still air. A bell hangs unrung between convoys.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Three parties hold paper on stock that has not moved for a century. A quest can decide whose paper the marsh honours.
why_site_won: summit in firm lowland (danger band 4), 696 m from the nearest route; won on nearPoint, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: An Imperial warehouse quarter has been taken back to the knee by the marsh. The stock still sits on the racks. The stock has gone unclaimed since the Imperial factor stopped coming.
siting_note: The site is bound to the southern channel that its founding names. An outsiders' landing has to be on navigable water. The unconstrained plot left the site 260 m dry of the nearest channel.

name: Thousand-Chimes
why_founding: Thousand-Chimes is a craft village that makes bone and tin chimes. Half the province listens to its Hist through those chimes.
why_site_advantages: The village stands beside a hero Hist whose wind is reliable. The makers tune each chime against the tree that will hang it.
why_occupants_motive: The chime-makers hold a tuning that is a religious qualification, not a trade skill. The tree-minders examine and license the tuning. A maker who loses the qualification loses the craft and the village at once.
why_pressures: Cheap cast chimes from the cities undercut the makers. The makers say that the cast chimes mistranslate the trees. The tree-minders have declined to rule on that for six years.
why_would_change_if: A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority. The coastal foundries would then take the province's trade within a decade.
vibe_silhouette: Chimes, clacking looms and forge smoke announce the village before it comes into view.
vibe_palette: The chime metal is brass and bone. Forge-smoke grey lies against the green canopy. Resin catches gold in the tuning bowls. Dye batches stain the bark.
vibe_materials: Chime frames are racked by pitch in the tuning shed. The forge roofs are shingled and are patched where sparks have caught. The benches are worn pale at the grip from years of filing. The licensing tree is strung with sample chimes at every reachable branch.
vibe_signature_feature: A tuning field holds two hundred hung frames. The makers walk through the field in silence to test a batch.
vibe_condition: The village is kept exact under the tree-minders' licence. Nothing is left loose.
vibe_approach: The sound carries a kilometre. At closer range, the sound resolves into a village.
vibe_senses: Hammer taps on tin sound between long silences. Hot metal and cut sap smell in the same breath. The tuning field rings as a batch is walked past. Bone dust grits underfoot near the workbenches.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can pull a tuning qualification, restore one or prove a chime false.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH05 · tier-3; LH23 · tier-3; LH26 · tier-3; LH27 · tier-3; LH28 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 248 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: Two hundred hung frames stand in a field. The makers will tune a chime to a named tree, if they are given the name.

name: The Under-Ring
why_founding: The Barsaebic Ayleid works predate the works of the interior tribes. The Barsaebic Ayleid works go down into the ground and do not rise above it.
why_site_advantages: The Ayleids built rings underground. The rings fill from beneath every wet season. The rings drain again afterwards.
why_occupants_motive: No speaking creature lives in the Under-Ring. The lower rings are dry. Animals den in the lower rings.
why_pressures: Antiquarians want to enter the Under-Ring. The interior tribes have no stake either way. Two licensed parties went down. Neither licensed party came back up.
why_would_change_if: A dig licence from any authority would open the Under-Ring. The Helstrom assembly would then decide whether Ayleid stone falls under the Duskfall taboo.
vibe_silhouette: White stone arches and columns stand here. White is otherwise absent from the colours of the province.
vibe_palette: White stone rings sink into black flood water. Pale lichen crusts the risers. Lamplight shows sharply against the dark stone. No green grows below the first ring.
vibe_materials: The walls are dressed white stone laid in courses that no local hand cut. The welkynd settings were picked clean of their stones long ago. The floor drainage channels were cut by a different people than the builders of the walls. Roots have found every seam and split it wider.
vibe_signature_feature: Ayleid stonework stands here. Argonian root grows through the welkynd settings.
vibe_condition: No living hand maintains the Under-Ring. The rings drain and refill on their own.
vibe_mood: The Under-Ring feels alien. No interior tribe claims an ancestor in it.
vibe_approach: A ring of white stone teeth shows above the mud.
vibe_senses: Cold stone air rises out of the stair. Standing water slaps the lower rings on a slow tide. Grave-goods dust catches at the back of the throat. A call down the stair comes back with no echo.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 435 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: Ayleid stone has Argonian root growing through its light-settings. The works go down into water and do not rise into the air.

name: Long-Stride
why_founding: The keepers bred lizard-steeds on this rise for two generations. A wet season flooded the schooling paddock. The flood let the breeding stock loose.
why_site_advantages: The rise is firm and the paddock ground is soft. That ground once suited training. It now suits a wamasu that has denned in the flooded pens.
why_occupants_motive: A wamasu took over the paddock. The water is good and undisturbed, so the wamasu stays.
why_pressures: Porters once bought steeds here. Porters now route wide around the pens. The loss of this supply has driven up steed prices on every interior road.
why_would_change_if: Killing or driving off the wamasu would leave the pens open for breeding again. No keeper has tried this since the keepers scattered.
vibe_silhouette: The pen rails have collapsed. A burrow mouth lies where the schooling paddock used to be.
vibe_palette: The water of the flooded pens is the colour of tea. The drowned rail-wood is grey. One strand of breeding-tag cord is still red.
vibe_materials: The training rails were built for lizard-steeds. The rails are now underwater and a wamasu holds them. The soft mud of the schooling paddock kept its shape under the flood. The posts are snapped at the waterline where the herd broke out.
vibe_signature_feature: The laid-pole schooling runs are still visible under the water. The runs are now the approach lanes of the wamasu.
vibe_condition: The pens have not been repaired since the flood took them.
vibe_approach: The herd smell is gone from the pens. The paddock mud is still churned.
vibe_senses: A wake moves under still water before the wamasu is seen. The paddock mud smells of old dung gone sweet with rot. The rails creak when the current pushes them.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 59 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The breeding pens once supplied every porter route in the interior. A wamasu now dens in the flooded pens.

name: The Staying Stone
why_founding: The Staying Stone is a shrine where offerings are made to hold back the flood. Four villages maintain the shrine jointly.
why_site_advantages: The shrine stands at the pinch point where the flood enters this basin.
why_occupants_motive: The shrine has no residents. Four villages take turns keeping it. The turn order is older than any current naheesh of the four villages.
why_pressures: The offerings have not held back the floods for three years. The villages blame each other. They blame chiefly the village whose turn fell in the worst year.
why_would_change_if: One more bad year and the villages will abandon the shrine or rebuild it bigger. Either decision breaks the four-village compact. The compact is joint institution of the district.
vibe_silhouette: Offerings are heaped facing a body of water or a den. Open water lies behind the offerings.
vibe_palette: The floodwater is brown against green banks. The offerings are pale on dark stone. The tin chime frames catch grey light. Moss climbs the ledges nearest the water.
vibe_materials: Stone ledges are set four abreast, one per village. The roof beams have been gone since the last storm and the frame stands bare. Each village replaces the rope ties only in its own turn. Paint is renewed yearly over the old marks.
vibe_signature_feature: The shrine has four offering ledges, one per village. The state of each ledge shows whether its village has kept its turn.
vibe_condition: Each village patches the shrine only when its turn falls due.
vibe_approach: A stone stands in the water. Fresh and rotted offerings lie side by side on it.
vibe_senses: Standing water lies underfoot at every tide. The oldest offerings rot. The newest offerings smell sweet. Cold stone chills wet feet. Gulls work the shallows for scraps.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can find out which of the four villages has stopped keeping its turn.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 290 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: Four villages share the ledges here. The rot on each ledge shows which village has stopped keeping its turn.

name: Keeps-the-Egg
why_founding: The Hist of the tribe was killed in the Imperial century. The tribe recovered the Mnemic Egg. The tribe organised itself around keeping the Egg.
why_site_advantages: The tribe did not move. The dead trunk is still the centre of the village. The Egg is kept inside the trunk.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe keeps a memory. No member of the tribe can currently read the memory.
why_pressures: Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg. One of the three has publicly offered to buy it. If the tribe refused the offer, it would be seen to be hoarding the Egg.
why_would_change_if: The archivists of the main quest could read the Egg. Reading the Egg would resolve or destroy the tribe. Each claimant tribe has decided which outcome it wants.
vibe_silhouette: A dead trunk still stands at the centre of the village. The villagers kept the trunk and did not clear it.
vibe_palette: Bone-pale heartwood scaffolding stands against grey bark. The chamber of the Egg is lit orange from inside. Dust lies thick on the log shelf. The iron on the staff of the naheesh is dulled.
vibe_materials: The dead trunk is propped with green-cut props. Sap seeps from the driven ends of the props. The chamber of the Egg is walled with fitted bark tile with no gaps. The scaffold ladders are lashed fresh each season. The ladders are left rough underfoot.
vibe_signature_feature: The dead trunk stands in the middle of the village. The villagers scaffold and maintain the trunk like a building. The Egg is housed in a chamber cut into the heartwood of the trunk.
vibe_condition: The scaffold has been rebuilt sound. The trunk itself is past saving.
vibe_mood: The villagers keep their grief as a standing duty.
vibe_approach: A grey trunk with a lit doorway in it shows under the canopy. The trunk is visible from the water.
vibe_senses: The trunk creaks on a slow rhythm. Everyone in the village has stopped hearing the creak. Dust off old bark catches in the throat near the chamber door. Low argument carries from the hut of the naheesh on days when a claimant tribe visits.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can open the reliquary. A quest can arbitrate the three claims. A quest can read what is inside the Egg.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH29 · tier-3; LH30 · tier-3; LH31 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 23 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: The village is built around a dead trunk that the villagers refuse to leave. The villagers keep a Mnemic Egg. Three other tribes have claimed the Egg.

name: The Lit Fen
why_founding: The Lit Fen is a fen. Its water lights at night from the fall of Hist-flower.
why_site_advantages: The fen is still water directly downstream of the grove of a hero Hist.
why_occupants_motive: The fen is unkept. The villages come once a year. The night is fixed by the Tsoko stones. The villages come in numbers because of what is in the deep channel.
why_pressures: The fen lights only while the tree above flowers. This year the light came late and stopped early.
why_would_change_if: If the tree failed, the fen would go out. The district would see the fen go dark weeks before any sign appeared in the grove.
vibe_silhouette: At night the light itself is the landmark. It is visible from further away than any daytime cue in this province.
vibe_palette: The black canopy water burns red after dark. The banks are grey and unlit by day. The drifted flower petals bleach at the waterline. A paler current runs along the line of the channel.
vibe_materials: The fen has no structure beyond root shelf and silt bank. A single old shrine post is driven at the shallow end. A fallen limb is wedged across the water as a crossing. Bare mud is banked where the last flood pushed it.
vibe_signature_feature: The water is red-lit under a black canopy after dark. The light is brighter or dimmer with the flowering of the tree upstream.
vibe_condition: The fen is unkept between visits. The villages tend it once a year on the fixed night.
vibe_mood: The fen is beautiful. The deep channel is not safe.
vibe_approach: The ground glows beyond a root bank.
vibe_senses: Heat lasts long after sundown. Petals rot sweet at the waterline. The surface flickers when something shifts beneath it. For long stretches the main sound is dripping root.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: After dark the water burns red under a black canopy. The light shows the shape moving under the water.

name: The Raw Hold
why_founding: A Blackguard crew hides in the interior. The crew is found at this place and at no other.
why_site_advantages: The Raw Hold lies deep in the interior and off every route. It has a single boat exit.
why_occupants_motive: The crew are criminals who keep no ledger and have no discipline. Most of them are three generations out of Blackrose. They cannot work in any place where their descent is known.
why_pressures: The crew cannot resupply. They are starting to raid the villages on which they depend. Raiding a village that supplies a crew has ended other crews in the same way.
why_would_change_if: A retaliation by the villages would finish the crew. The interior tribes have already agreed among themselves which village would lead it.
vibe_silhouette: The camp is well built and has a guarded approach. The camp shows no smoke.
vibe_palette: The hull-black timber shows green stain. Rust bleeds down the old iron. Brown water lies at the keel line. No lamp is lit past the second rib.
vibe_materials: The ribs of a beached barge are re-roofed in cut frond. The deck planks were pulled from the hold below and reused. The salvaged nails are driven crooked. A single gangplank is rigged to lift on a signal.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp is built inside the ribs of a beached river barge. The crew dragged the barge up a creek and never dragged it back.
vibe_condition: The crew patch the camp irregularly. They repair nothing properly.
vibe_approach: A boat hull sits well above the waterline, up a creek.
vibe_senses: The hull creaks as the tide turns. Oil and old fish smell rises from the bilge. Talk is cut short when an unfamiliar boat is heard. Cold iron is under the hand at every rail.
why_site_won: island in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A Blackguard crew lives in the ribs of a barge. The crew could not drag the barge back to the water. The crew have one boat and no friends.

name: Many-Ways
why_founding: Many-Ways is a village that grew as a junction of walkways. It did not grow around a centre.
why_site_advantages: Four routes over soft ground have to meet here. No other place suits them. The junction is the whole capital of the village.
why_occupants_motive: Walkway-keepers live here. The keepers charge for maintenance. They argue about who owes what.
why_pressures: The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns. The keepers have begun charging tolls. The tribes on the arms consider the tolls extortion.
why_would_change_if: Losing one arm of the junction would strand the route of a whole tribe. That tribe has started surveying its own alternative. The tribe would sooner build the alternative than keep paying.
vibe_silhouette: The line of the walkway curves away into the vegetation.
vibe_palette: Reed-green water throws light up under the decking. The cane-pale boards are worn dark at the crossing. Red paint is fresh only on the newest post. Brown mud shows at low tide.
vibe_materials: The decking runs out in four directions from one central span. The keepers replace the cane lashings arm by arm as they can afford it. The shrine hangs on ropes under the crossing. The shrine is a separate structure from the crossing. A toll box is bolted to each of the four approaches.
vibe_signature_feature: The village has no square. Its centre is a five-way walkway junction. A shrine hangs under the deck where the routes cross.
vibe_condition: The keepers maintain the walkways arm by arm. They maintain the arm of whichever tribe has paid that season.
vibe_approach: Decking can be seen among the reeds. The village begins at the first boards.
vibe_senses: The boards drum underfoot where four lines of traffic cross. Fish and cut cane scent the air. Poles knock against the pilings at the mooring. Voices are raised over the toll boxes most evenings.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can audit the repair ledger of the keepers. A quest can cost the junction an arm.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH32 · tier-3; LH33 · tier-3; LH34 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in tidal delta (danger band 3), 239 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Four walkway routes have to meet somewhere. The shrine hung under the deck where they cross is the nearest thing to a town square.

name: The Pulled Field
why_founding: The Pulled Field is a grave-pole field. Looters pulled the poles from the ground. The poles had been holding something down. That something has now risen.
why_site_advantages: The field is the burial ground of an old village. No living village stands near it now.
why_occupants_motive: Bog blights live in the field. The grave-singers send their apprentices here to train. They do this without announcing it.
why_pressures: Looters still pull the poles because the goods buried under them are real. The looters are the heirs of the village that abandoned the field.
why_would_change_if: Restaking the field would settle the matter. It would also settle the question of who owns the grave goods. No local family has offered to pay for the work.
vibe_silhouette: Driven poles fill the field. One pole is down. A pahnjee rack has been left to sag.
vibe_palette: The grave-poles are pale against the black mud. Cord bands on them still hold their paint. The empty holes are darker than the ground around them.
vibe_materials: The original binders drove the poles straight and deep. Looters' rope marks scar every pulled post. The holes are undisturbed below the pull line.
vibe_signature_feature: Pulled poles lie beside their own holes. Each pole is still wrapped in knotted cord and paint bands. The bands name the person who lies under the pole.
vibe_condition: Looters pull poles faster than any family replaces them.
vibe_mood: The burial ground is no longer holding.
vibe_approach: Holes lie in rows across a field.
vibe_senses: The ground gives underfoot where a pole used to anchor it. Wet cord and old paint smell faintly of tallow. Loose poles rattle as they knock together in the wind.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 4), 330 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: Looters pulled the grave-poles. What the poles held down has risen. The cord and paint still name each grave.

name: The Carriers' Rest
why_founding: The Carriers' Rest is a staging post on the bone route. Carriers bring the bones of Argonians who died away from the Hist back to the dirt.
why_site_advantages: The water route meets the interior walking route here. It is the last point where a bundle can be re-wrapped and re-labelled before the walk. A cold store is cut into the rise under the racks. Unclaimed bundles have been stacked in the store since the office opened.
why_occupants_motive: Carriers live here. Carrying is a recognised and feared profession. The family pays the carriers. The village does not pay them. The carriers' loyalty therefore runs to the dead.
why_pressures: The 4E produced more distant dead than the route can carry.
why_would_change_if: A backlog is already visible in the racks. A second season of backlog would force the carriers to choose which families' dead go first. The families do not want the carriers to hold that power.
vibe_silhouette: A rack of wrapped bundles stands under a roof. Each bundle is labelled with a village name.
vibe_palette: Pale wrapped bundles lie under a dark roof. Chalk marks cover the delivery board. Brown river water lies below the cellar door. The racks are grey bark.
vibe_materials: The racks are built to a standard bundle length. They are not built to a person's length. The cellar door is cut straight into the bank and shored with timber. Numbered tags are carved fresh for each arrival. The roof is kept sound because the cargo cannot get wet.
vibe_signature_feature: Numbered racks hold wrapped bone bundles. The bundles wait for a carrier who is going the right way. A delivery board stands in the yard like the board of a freight office.
vibe_condition: The carriers keep the racks full. The carriers sweep the yard daily.
vibe_approach: The full racks stand at the front of the yard.
vibe_senses: Dry cold rises from the cellar store. Resin seals the wrappings. Rope pulleys creak as they lower a bundle. Talk is kept to names and numbers.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 27 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, route.
player_purpose_hook: The Carriers' Rest works as a freight office for the dead. Racks of wrapped bone wait for a carrier who is going the right way. Carriers take work off the delivery board. The priest signs a carrier's name to each bundle.

name: The Eaten Meer
why_founding: The Eaten Meer is a xanmeer that the forest has taken. Root has replaced stone in about half of the structure.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer went undefended on soft ground. The roots therefore won.
why_occupants_motive: Whatever creature suits a warm dry hollow lives here. Twice a year the tenders from the clan-tended meer visit. They come to see what stone becoming root looks like.
why_pressures: The structure is still settling and floors give way. Treasure-hunting outfits price it as unworkable. The tribes have stopped arguing about it.
why_would_change_if: The xanmeer is becoming root. The heretics of the restarted work cite this against their own project.
vibe_silhouette: Nothing shows the xanmeer from outside. Its shape reads only from the interior.
vibe_palette: Grey quarried stone goes root-black where the wood has taken it. A slick green skin coats the wet floor joints. Pale fungus climbs the collapsed side. Dull ochre grave goods lie half-buried in silt.
vibe_materials: Root growth has displaced cut stone blocks into a slow rockfall that never finishes falling. Hollow root chambers grew where a cut-stone chamber used to be. Old mortar has crumbled to grit underfoot. No hand has added anything recent.
vibe_signature_feature: Stone wall and root wall can be told apart by touch. One corridor changes from stone to root at its midpoint.
vibe_condition: The structure is still settling. The floors go soft a little further each year.
vibe_mood: Cold stone and warm root share one building.
vibe_approach: A hill has a doorway in it.
vibe_senses: The floor gives slightly underfoot where root has replaced stone. Cold stone air lies on one side of a corridor. Warm root air lies on the other. A scraping sound comes from somewhere below. The scraping stops when the footsteps above it stop.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 337 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The xanmeer is half stone and half root. The floors are still settling and give way each year.

name: The Choked Mouth
why_founding: The Choked Mouth is an older root tower that collapsed. The fall took the tower's line with it.
why_site_advantages: The tower stands on the route it used to serve. It is still a landmark.
why_occupants_motive: The tower is unoccupied. A shrine at the base still gets offerings. Waykeepers leave most of them. They leave them on the outward leg of a journey. They do not leave them on the inward leg.
why_pressures: The line beyond the tower has been unreachable for a century. The villages it once served have reorganised their trade around Helstrom.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the tunnel would reopen the line. The Waykeepers last costed the work a hundred years ago.
vibe_silhouette: A bulbed root tower has gone crooked. Its top third lies beside it.
vibe_palette: Bone-pale fallen bulk stands against open canopy. A mud-brown mouth opens at the broken end. Totem paint on the stub has faded. Moss climbs the underside where the tower lies.
vibe_materials: The tower's bulbed shell is cracked along its old growth rings. A shaft is still lined with root that kept growing after the fall. Dressed footing stones lie half-buried where the base once stood. A shrine post at the base is kept fresh with offerings.
vibe_signature_feature: The tower's top lies at full length like a felled column. Its mouth is still open at the broken end. The mouth goes nowhere.
vibe_condition: The Waykeepers have written the tower off. It falls further each season.
vibe_mood: The tower is a landmark that no longer serves a route.
vibe_approach: A pale horizontal shape lies in a [view/scene] with no horizontals.
vibe_senses: Dust sifts down the broken shaft. Sap has gone stale in the split wood. The fallen bulk settles with small cracks. A stillness lies over the wide clearing round it.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 80 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A fallen rootworm tower lies at full length like a felled column. Its mouth is open at the broken end. The mouth leads down a shaft that the Waykeepers have written off.

name: The Open Mouth
why_founding: The Open Mouth is a working rootworm-line exit. The root layer vents to the surface here.
why_site_advantages: The exit stands on a firm rise. The root tower could push through the rise without flooding.
why_occupants_motive: Waykeepers and the porters who meet the line here use the exit. Neither party can price the other out. The line needs both.
why_pressures: It is the working exit on this side of the basin. The Waykeepers ration seats on the line. They take payment in favours as often as in coin.
why_would_change_if: A collapse would strand the whole eastern line. The fallen tower two days north shows the result a century later.
vibe_silhouette: A bulbed tower of fused root stands above the canopy. The tower is swollen near the top.
vibe_palette: The pale root-grey trunk stands against dark canopy. Warm haze hangs over the vent mouth. Brown sap streaks the bark. One lamp swings at the hoist.
vibe_materials: The tower is fused root swollen near the crown. A hoist frame is bolted straight into living bark. A chalked timetable is rubbed clean and rewritten weekly. Porters' loads have worn the ramps smooth.
vibe_signature_feature: A bulbed root tower vents warm air. A hoist is rigged over the mouth at its foot. A timetable board is posted as approximate.
vibe_condition: The Waykeepers keep the exit working, largely on favours.
vibe_approach: The warm plume is visible from two kilometres away on a cold morning.
vibe_senses: Warm exhaled air breaks the surface chill. Turned soil and resin scent the vent mouth. The hoist chain strikes the hour. Waiting porters bargain in low voices under the hiss of the vent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: FAST root.east_line
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ05 · tier-0; LH21 · tier-3; RW-line · tier-2
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 90 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The Open Mouth is a working rootworm exit. A hoist stands over the mouth. A timetable is posted as approximate. The Waykeepers ration the seats.

name: Ash-Fence
why_founding: Ash-Fence is a village that was burned in the century of uprisings. The village was never rebuilt.
why_site_advantages: The village stood on the firm ground of this reach. The burners came because of that ground. The ground has stayed empty since.
why_occupants_motive: No village lives here. A bone-carriers' camp visits the site.
why_pressures: The neighbouring tribes disagree about who burned the village. One tribe says the Legion under Mallicius did it. Another tribe says a rival tribe used the burning as cover.
why_would_change_if: A settled account would let a tribe rebuild. The firm ground here holds a village of two hundred. The district has no other such ground to spare.
vibe_silhouette: A smoke seep and dead ground come first. Then structures charred into shapes appear.
vibe_palette: Black stumps stand in green floodwater. Ash-grey ground lies between the piles. Red flowers push up along the old burn line. Char shows through wherever the green has not yet covered it.
vibe_materials: Pile stumps are burned to a uniform char height. Grave-poles were driven into the footprint after the fire. They were not driven around it. A root cellar that the fire never reached has a hatch that is still sound. Wattle fencing has collapsed to a black tangle at the perimeter.
vibe_signature_feature: Charred pile stumps stand in a rectangle. The driven grave-poles were planted afterwards. The grave-poles stand inside the burnt footprint.
vibe_condition: Nothing has been rebuilt since the fire. The cellar hatch is kept shut.
vibe_approach: Black stumps stand on bare ash. Green water stands beyond them.
vibe_senses: Wet ash lies underfoot where the ground stays damp. Scavenger tracks cross the burnt clearing. A scorched smell has not left the timber. Standing water has gone still over the lowest stumps.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 280 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform.
player_purpose_hook: Charred pile stumps stand in a rectangle. Grave-poles are planted inside the burnt footprint. A root cellar that the fire missed lies under them.

name: The High Root
why_founding: The High Root is an aerial root that bridged two hammocks. The villagers made the root walkable. They did not cut it down.
why_site_advantages: The root runs twenty metres up. It crosses ground that floods completely.
why_occupants_motive: The crossing is unstaffed. The nearest village maintains the rope line. The alternative is a half-day round the flooded ground. The villagers' fish spoils in that time.
why_pressures: The root is alive and slowly moving. The villagers have re-rigged the rope line three times to follow it.
why_would_change_if: The root will eventually be too steep to walk. Every dry season the village argues about whether to build a walkway before then.
vibe_silhouette: A living root bridge spans two crowns up. It is visible only from directly beneath.
vibe_palette: Canopy shadow lies overhead. Pale scarred bark shows where the rope line grips. One strip of hand-line is dyed for grip against the dark wood.
vibe_materials: A single living root is walked as a footpath. The root is still thickening under the boards. The villagers re-rigged the hand-line three times to follow the root's drift. Old lashings are left in place beside the newest ones as a record.
vibe_signature_feature: A living root is walked like a bridge. The hand-line is lashed on in a way that does not girdle the root. The old lashings are left hanging as a date record.
vibe_condition: The villagers re-rig the line whenever the root moves enough to matter.
vibe_approach: From below the root reads as a shadow across the sky. From the hammock end it is walkable.
vibe_senses: The whole crossing sways faintly with the tree's own movement. A long drop of open air lies on both sides. Wet bark and standing water smell far below.
why_site_won: ravine in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 49 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, route.
player_purpose_hook: A living root is walked like a bridge twenty metres above ground that floods completely. Every year's old lashing is left hanging beside the new one.

name: The Basin Line
why_founding: The Basin Line is a rope crossing. An expedition rigged it. The expedition did not come back for it.
why_site_advantages: The rope spans a root gully. The Archon–Gideon road swings wide around the gully. The crossing saves an hour.
why_occupants_motive: The crossing is no longer used. The expedition's gear is still cached at the far anchor. The cache lies in a root hollow that something else claimed after the expedition left.
why_pressures: The rope is old. The only way to test the rope is to use it. The guides price a client's insistence on crossing it accordingly.
why_would_change_if: "Re-rigging the rope would open the route again. It would also put the dead treasure-hunters' camp [name the actual consequence] of the basin guides' shelter."
vibe_silhouette: A slack rope line crosses a gap. One end is still tied. The other end is in the water.
vibe_palette: Pale rope hangs against dark canopy. A green gap lies where the gorge drops away. A note gone brown with damp is pinned at the anchor tree.
vibe_materials: Two ropes are strung one over the other. The older rope is left frayed in place. The line has scarred the anchor tree where it cuts into the bark. A cache bag is lashed high out of reach. Boards are missing where feet have worn them away.
vibe_signature_feature: Two ropes hang here, one older than the other. A note hangs at the anchor tree. The writer of the note intended to return.
vibe_condition: The crossing has been unmaintained since the riggers left.
vibe_mood: The crossing is unmaintained. The far anchor is the dangerous end.
vibe_approach: The anchor tree is found first. The crossing is found second.
vibe_senses: The rope hums under weight. Damp bark and turned soil smell from something moving below. A cold draught rises out of the gap. Silence breaks only when the rope creaks.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Two ropes cross a whitewater reach. An expedition's cache lies at the far anchor. The cache is in a hollow that is not empty.

name: The Stepped Roof
why_founding: The Stepped Roof is a xanmeer. Its stepped terraces can be climbed from the outside.
why_site_advantages: The stone stands above the flood. The interior is intact and sealed.
why_occupants_motive: Nothing lives on the roof. Plenty lives below it. The creatures under the broken slab are the hazard.
why_pressures: The route up is easier than the route down. Gear that climbers abandoned piles up on the terrace, because they did not carry it back down.
why_would_change_if: A ruling by the tending tribe that climbing counts as entering would change it. The heretic-stone dispute could force that ruling.
vibe_silhouette: A visible route runs up the structure. The route is not a stair.
vibe_palette: Grey stone terraces are streaked white with old bird droppings. Personal effects glint where climbers abandoned them. A black slab hole opens at the fourth terrace. Green moss covers every shaded step.
vibe_materials: The stepped stone terraces are worn smooth at the tread and rough at the riser. The collapsed roof slab lies in three broken sections that the tribes have not cleared. Abandoned rope and packstraps are snagged on the upper courses. The sealed ground doors show no recent tool marks.
vibe_signature_feature: The building is entered from the top. The ground-level openings are sealed. The breach is a collapsed roof slab four terraces up.
vibe_condition: Traffic alone keeps the climb passable. The tribes do not maintain it.
vibe_approach: The terraces rise above the canopy. From a long way off they look like a staircase.
vibe_senses: Wind blows across the open terraces, after the still air below the canopy. Loose grit scrapes under a boot. A colder draught rises out of the broken slab hole.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 176 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Every ground-level door is sealed. The way in is over four terraces and down through a broken roof slab.

name: The Ripple Stack
why_founding: The pinnacled mountains of Middle Argonia come apart at a ripple. The Ripple Stack stands close enough to a route that climbers keep trying to climb it.
why_site_advantages: The Ripple Stack is a xanmeer stub bound in root. It stands clear of the canopy on its own debris mound. The region has almost no long sightlines. The stack is one of the few things that can be seen from a distance.
why_occupants_motive: The stack is unoccupied. Two climbers' caches remain on the route. A quantity of abandoned gear also remains on the route.
why_pressures: The debris fan at the base holds old falls and one from this season. The route was marked. A climber then deliberately unmarked it.
why_would_change_if: The stack will fall. The debris fan at the base shows roughly how often it sheds first.
vibe_silhouette: A leaning stack of root-bound ruin blocks stands here. The stack sheds a little every season.
vibe_palette: Root-bound ruin block leans grey against the green canopy. A dark lightning scorch runs down one face. Dull ochre lichen grows on the shaded side. The crown is bare, with no bloom to show for the season.
vibe_materials: The dressed xanmeer block is wrapped and split by root growth. Old climbing pitons are rusted fast into the stone. A debris fan of fresh and old rockfall is banked at the base. Scrubbed paint marks show where a route was once chalked.
vibe_signature_feature: A climbing route is marked in totem-paint. The climber who came back down alive scrubbed the marks out.
vibe_condition: Climbers climb the stack against every warning. Only weather maintains it.
vibe_approach: The stack is visible for a kilometre, which is rare here. Rockfall is audible from the same distance.
vibe_senses: Grit sifts loose underfoot on every ledge. A rumble carries up through the stone before anything drops. Resin-sharp air lies where the canopy thins near the top. Birdcalls thin out toward the summit.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 406 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: A ruin stack stands clear of the canopy. It sheds rock every season. Climbers have scrubbed out the paint marks of earlier routes.

name: The Quiet Camp
why_founding: The Quiet Camp is an Unbound Root staging camp. The cult stages work on a nearby tree there.
why_site_advantages: The camp is close enough to the target root line. It is also far enough from any village.
why_occupants_motive: Cultists stage there for work on a root line. Their doctrine is that a tree severed from the collective can be spoken to alone.
why_pressures: The nearest village has noticed the traffic and has stayed quiet. The cult pays the two households who noticed first.
why_would_change_if: Exposure moves the cultists deeper. The gallery cell they supply would then lose its method-testing site. A season's work would still remain to do.
vibe_silhouette: Masks or snare-fields show before the tents.
vibe_palette: Root-grey canvas stands against dark green. Mud is tracked up from the boat landing. No smoke rises by day. One pale mask hangs against dark bark.
vibe_materials: Tents are pitched off a living root that is used only as an anchor. The cultists sweep and relay the matting each morning. A cutting frame is staged and aimed at the target tree. Snare cord is coiled and sorted by length.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp holds no trophies and no disorder. The cultists sweep the camp every morning.
vibe_condition: The camp is cleaner than any working camp has cause to be.
vibe_mood: The camp is sober and ideological. The cultists are dangerous without swagger.
vibe_approach: The cultists' path is found before the camp. The path is swept.
vibe_senses: The cultists exchange signals and do not speak. Oiled steel is wrapped under canvas. Boots are wiped before the swept path is crossed. Talk stops at the sound of a paddle nearby.
quest_hooks_opportunity: main-quest cult staging site
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 544 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: The Unbound Root are staging here to cut a tree. Their cutting frame is aimed at it.

name: Cut-and-Carried
why_founding: A tribe whose tree died carried a root fragment two days' walk and replanted it. The villagers did the work on the Lilmoth precedent.
why_site_advantages: The tribe chose new ground for the cutting's sake. The ground has spring water and shelter. It has no old roots to compete with the cutting.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe raises a tree the way others raise a clutch. A tending rota has replaced every office that the old tree supported.
why_pressures: The cutting speaks faintly and only to two villagers. Both are young. Neither of them wanted the standing.
why_would_change_if: If the cutting failed, the tribe would have no standing left. The Hist-less refuge two days away has offered to receive them. They find the offer unbearable.
vibe_silhouette: The tallest thing in the village is a stump. The villagers cut and carried away the crown. They left the trunk standing as a marker.
vibe_palette: Pale new leaf on the sapling stands against the older grove's dark canopy. The cage-wicker is gold where the withy is fresh. Spring water runs clear over pale sand. A red thread is tied at the cage's rim.
vibe_materials: The villagers rebuild the cage each year in unweathered withy over the winter frame. The sapling roots are mulched in hist-leaf that was carried from the old grove. Walkway decking is pegged straight into fresh sill timber. The Mnemic Egg is housed in its own small hut of new bamboo.
vibe_signature_feature: A sapling stands under a woven cage. The whole village re-weaves the cage every year. The dead tree's Mnemic Egg is housed beside it in its own hut.
vibe_condition: The work is young throughout. Little of it is worn yet.
vibe_approach: The cage is the tallest thing in the village, at two and a half metres.
vibe_senses: Spring water runs under the decking, cold against warm air. The sap smells sharp and green but not sweet. The tending rota talks quietly at the cage each morning. Damp bamboo still smells of the cut.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can trace what is killing the carried sapling back along the two days' walk.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH35 · tier-3; LH36 · tier-3; MQ19 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 152 m from the nearest route; no free 'spring-head' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: A tribe carried a cutting of their dead tree two days' walk and replanted it. The sapling stands under a cage that the whole village re-weaves every year.

name: The Milking Shed
why_founding: The Milking Shed is a daril operation. The operation needs live venomous stock, constant heat and no neighbours.
why_site_advantages: The shed has deep interior warmth and total isolation. The ground is too poor to interest any tribe.
why_occupants_motive: Fermenters work here. They are half chemists and half snake-keepers.
why_pressures: The product ruins people in four cities. The fermenters know their buyers by name. One buyer is now buying more than the cities can consume.
why_would_change_if: A raid would move the trade and would not end it. The stock is the asset. The stock walks away.
vibe_silhouette: The shed is hidden at range. Up close, gas bladders hang from it like fruit.
vibe_palette: Earthenware racks stand lamp-dim. Gas bladders are the colour of old fruit. Venom-stained decking has gone dark.
vibe_materials: Split root-wood decking is pegged to the living sills below. Woven matting is kept dry over the venom stores. Earthenware jars are tuned so that each rings a different note.
vibe_signature_feature: Racks hold live milking stock in tuned earthenware. Each vessel rings a different note when tapped. The keeper checks the stock by ear.
vibe_condition: The fermenter runs the shed alone. The fermenter keeps everyone else out.
vibe_approach: The sound of the racks being played is audible before the shed comes into view.
vibe_senses: The racks give off a sour fermenting smell that catches at the back of the throat. The gas bladders hiss low. Damp heat is trapped under a closed roof.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 620 m from the nearest route; no free 'box-canyon' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: Racks of live venomous stock stand in tuned jars. The keeper checks them by ear. The cellar's owners admit no visitors.
singular_claim: The countBand is [1,1]. The place needs isolation, warmth and live stock. The deep interior supplies all three.

name: The Sunk Well
why_founding: The Sunk Well is a xanmeer's ceremonial well shaft. It is flooded through to the lower halls.
why_site_advantages: The shaft is vertical. It is cut in stone that has not moved in an age.
why_occupants_motive: Nothing living is in the shaft. The shaft is the entrance to something that lives. Divers work it in pairs. Enough divers have come out alone that pairing is now a rule.
why_pressures: The water is rising. The entrance ledge is nearly submerged. Within a few years the dive will not be possible at all.
why_would_change_if: A dry season opens two more chambers. It would also bring every treasure outfit in the interior to a ruin. The tenders consider the ruin consecrated.
vibe_silhouette: A dark opening lies in water. Worked stone often rings the opening.
vibe_palette: Black water narrows to a green disc of daylight above. Pale stone is smoothed at the rim. Handholds catch what light reaches them.
vibe_materials: The dressed stone shaft is cut true. Its face is unrepaired across the same span. Handholds are carved below the waterline for the dive and not for the walk. The rising water has [use literal: eroded/worn/consumed] back the entrance ledge.
vibe_signature_feature: Carved handholds spiral down the inside of the shaft below the waterline. The shaft was cut to be climbed wet.
vibe_condition: The unrepaired stone still holds its cut after an age underwater.
vibe_approach: A square hole of black water lies in a stone floor, in daylight.
vibe_senses: "Cold water presses on the ears at depth. The shaft's own echo [use literal: absorbed/submerged/flooded] every sound. Slick algae lies underfoot on the stone. No air current moves once a diver is submerged."
why_site_won: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 303 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: A ceremonial well has handholds carved below the waterline. The way leads into a xanmeer's flooded lower halls.

name: The Bared Flat
why_founding: The Bared Flat is a shallow bed that empties in the dry season. The emptying exposes what has been lost in it.
why_site_advantages: The flat is a wide shallow basin with a seasonal outlet.
why_occupants_motive: Scavengers work the flat in season. It is empty out of season. The same four families come each year. They treat the window as inherited property.
why_pressures: The exposure window is short and competitive. Last year two of the families arrived early and drained a channel to widen it.
why_would_change_if: A wetter cycle would close the window entirely. Four households have built their year around that income.
vibe_silhouette: A cracked flat lies where there was water. Things stand up out of it.
vibe_palette: Cracked brown mud is plated like old leather. Wreck timber is bleached grey where the water has left it. Dropped cargo rusts orange at the edges. Standing puddles hold a flat grey sky.
vibe_materials: The mudflat is unworked. The families dug drainage channels that cut it. Wreck hulls are half-buried and rotted through on the sun side only. Dropped cargo is scattered, with wood swollen and metal seized. No shelter is built here because the season is too short.
vibe_signature_feature: In the dry weeks the flat is a floor of exposed wrecks, dropped cargo and older things. The families argue every year over who may take what.
vibe_condition: The families pick the flat over each year while the window is open.
vibe_approach: The flat is a lake one month and a field of objects the next.
vibe_senses: Mud cracks underfoot with a sound like breaking crockery. Drying silt smells sharp and mineral. Heat comes off the exposed flat. No shade stands anywhere on it.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 240 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: For a few weeks a year the water goes. The bed becomes a floor of wrecks and dropped cargo. The families argue on the spot over who may take what.

name: The Sap Wallow
why_founding: The Sap Wallow is a natural sap pool that is used for sanctioned communion. The nearest tree-minder licenses its use.
why_site_advantages: A hero Hist's roots surface in a hollow and fill it.
why_occupants_motive: A tender controls dose and turn. The tree-minder appoints the tender. The tender answers to the grove and not to the users.
why_pressures: Unlicensed users come at night. The tender knows and mostly allows it. The tender calculates that a policed wallow becomes a starblossom hollow.
why_would_change_if: Overuse would produce another Miredance. Miredance is two days away. The tender cites it against the users who want the dose raised.
vibe_silhouette: A fenced amber pool has a single shelter over its deep end. No path leads away from the pool.
vibe_palette: The amber-warm pool is ringed in green shade. Pale stone dose-cups sit on their ledge. Red flower heads drift at the rim. Steam ribbons up where the water runs hottest.
vibe_materials: The sap-fed pool is banked in shaped root. The tribe adds one graft each generation. A cane fence marks the licensed edge. A single frond shelter roofs the deep end. Worn stone steps lead down into the warmth.
vibe_signature_feature: The water is warm amber at blood heat. A queue of stone dose-cups sits on a ledge, sized from a thimble to a bowl. The tender sets which cup a bather is given.
vibe_condition: The tender watches the pool day and night. The tender patches it by hand each season.
vibe_approach: The heat carries first. The smell follows.
vibe_senses: Sweet resin thickens the air near the surface. Blood-warm water laps at bare skin. The tender's low counting voice marks doses. Distant chimes sound the licensed hour.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 297 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.umpholo-mission (+0.66).
player_purpose_hook: The pool is sap-warm water at blood heat. A row of dose cups runs from a thimble to a bowl. The tender decides which cup a bather is given.

name: Starblossom Hollow
why_founding: Starblossom Hollow is a wallow that is used for the other kind of dreaming. The users have received no permission from any tree.
why_site_advantages: The hollow is cold. Starblossom grows thickly there.
why_occupants_motive: The wallow is unlicensed. Users come here. One man from the licensed wallow sells to them. He is not supposed to be here at all.
why_pressures: The tree-minders regard the hollow as the theft of a rite. Twice they have asked the assembly to name it. Naming it would make it prosecutable.
why_would_change_if: A crackdown would move the hollow. It would not end it. The plant grows in every cold hollow in the district. The hollows have not been counted.
vibe_silhouette: "After dark the hollow is lit blue-white. The flowers grow nowhere else throughout the region."
vibe_palette: Blue-white starblossom stands against black water. The green canopy fades to grey at the rim. The root-wood is bleached pale where feet cross it. One lamp is kept low for the sleepers.
vibe_materials: Raised beds are cut into the hollow floor and are edged with root. Sleeping mats are staked to low platforms. A watcher's lean-to is roofed in frond. Collecting bowls are set under the flower stems.
vibe_signature_feature: Starblossom is farmed here in careful beds. The farmers insist that they are not farmers. The beds are laid out as a constellation.
vibe_condition: The farmers run the hollow carefully. The beds are laid out as a constellation.
vibe_approach: Blue-white flowering stands in a [view/scene] that is otherwise red-flowered.
vibe_senses: The sweetness is thick enough to taste at the back of the throat. The sleepers breathe slowly on the mats. Cold settles over the water after dark. A single bell is struck when a sleeper wakes wrong.
why_site_won: island in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 570 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on remote, parent, culture-clump; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.pilgrim-camp-sap-road (+1.32).
player_purpose_hook: Starblossom is farmed in constellation beds by people who insist that they are not farmers. They sell to visitors. They watch any visitor who looks at the beds too long.

name: The Pull
why_founding: The Pull is a narrows. The wet-season flow becomes lethal there for a fortnight.
why_site_advantages: The narrows is the crossing on this reach, at the pinch.
why_occupants_motive: The narrows has no residents. The nearest village posts a watch in season, which is unpaid. The rota falls mostly on the two poorest households.
why_pressures: The watch lapses in some years. It lapses in the years when the village's men work the porter relay.
why_would_change_if: A bridge would solve the danger. Four villages would use a bridge. Each village holds that the crossing benefits the others more, so none of the four has paid for one.
vibe_silhouette: The water's surface is visibly wrong at the pinch.
vibe_palette: Brown current folds over itself at the pinch. The fatal mark on the depth stake is painted stark red. Pale waterlogged drift timber lies along both banks. The water shows no reflection where it moves fastest.
vibe_materials: A stake is driven at the narrows. The villagers recut its paint marks after each drowning. Drift timber and packed silt are banked where the current turns. A swimmer who got clear left a small cairn of stones. The pinch has no built crossing, no rail and no bridge.
vibe_signature_feature: A depth-and-flow stake has the fatal mark painted on it. The dates of the last four drownings are cut beside the mark.
vibe_condition: The stake resurfaces each year. The crossing is unfixed.
vibe_approach: The stake is visible from both banks. The current reads as slack water until the pinch.
vibe_senses: The pull of the current is audible before it is visible. Still air holds the smell of standing water on either side of the pinch. The water turns suddenly cold at the centre of the channel. The stake creaks against the flow.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 729 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: A depth stake has the fatal mark painted on it. The dates of the last four drownings are cut beside it. The nearest village posts a watch through the season.

name: The Unmade Work
why_founding: The Unmade Work is a xanmeer. Its own builders took it apart at the Duskfall. They did not abandon it.
why_site_advantages: The builders carried the stone away. What remains is the plan of the building and not the building.
why_occupants_motive: The site is untended. The heretic-stone village quarries it. The village is condemned for that. The condemnation has not stopped a single cart.
why_pressures: The site is the clearest physical evidence of the renunciation. The restarted work is quarrying it away.
why_would_change_if: Rebuilding on the site would settle the Duskfall argument in public. The Helstrom assembly has avoided visiting for eleven years.
vibe_silhouette: Dressed stone lies in stacks. A foundation has no building on it.
vibe_palette: The foundation stone is bare and grey. Straight lines are cut into bare earth. No colour marks the place where the walls used to stand.
vibe_materials: A full xanmeer footprint has every block quarried away. Fresh cart ruts are worn into the clearing floor. Root grows loose through joints that once held mortar.
vibe_signature_feature: A full-size floor plan of a xanmeer is left in the ground. Every block has been removed.
vibe_condition: The heretic-stone village quarries the site away steadily.
vibe_mood: The unmaking was deliberate. The site is tidier than a ruin.
vibe_approach: Flat ground has straight lines in it. No walls stand.
vibe_senses: The flat open ground has no wall to return a sound. Turned earth and quarry dust scent the air. Wind carries further because no walls break it.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can read the full-size floor plan. A quest can also work out what the builders were unmaking.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 469 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: A xanmeer was taken apart by its own builders, block by block. It left a full-size floor plan in the ground. It also left a foundation vault, which the builders left full.

name: The Interrupted Flight
why_founding: A man came out of the sky here, at speed. It happened roughly two hundred years after the same thing happened near Seyda Neen.
why_site_advantages: The site has no advantage. No road and no village lies within an hour of the ferns where he landed.
why_occupants_motive: He was not going anywhere near here. The letter in his satchel is addressed to a teacher in the tradition. The letter says that he has read the great experimenter's notes and corrected the error. In the letter he writes that the descent is the easy part.
why_pressures: Scavengers, water and the season threaten the site. The satchel is oiled leather. The scrolls in it still work.
why_would_change_if: A finder takes the scrolls. Whether the letter goes with them decides whether his teacher ever hears.
traversal_fallback: No route leads to the site. Travellers arrive only by being lost.
vibe_silhouette: The site is invisible from more than a few paces off. A break in the ferns has the shape of a man.
vibe_palette: The ferns are broken pale where the body fell. Brown leather has gone dark with damp. Scroll paper greys at the torn edge.
vibe_materials: A robe of fine cloth is split at the seams. A satchel is sealed well enough to keep the scrolls dry. Soft ground took the shape of the fall and kept it. No marker or grave-goods have been added since.
vibe_signature_feature: A crater a body deep lies in soft ground. A satchel beside it holds his jump scrolls. The scrolls are still usable.
vibe_condition: The site is untouched since the fall. The ferns are slowly closing over it.
vibe_approach: No path leads to the crater. Travellers find it by walking into it.
vibe_senses: Crushed fern gives off a green sap smell. Still air lies undisturbed by any path in or out. Paper rustles dry when wind finds the crater. No birdsong sounds directly over the site.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 817 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on remote, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A man came out of the sky here and did not survive the landing. The scrolls in his satchel are undamaged.

name: The Fenlord's Reach
why_founding: The Fenlord's Reach is an Ayleid fenlord's tomb. The marsh has kept the ground around it sealed.
why_site_advantages: The tomb lies in a deep basin with no route and no neighbours. The marsh has kept the seal wet. The stone has therefore not moved.
why_occupants_motive: The occupants of the tomb lie undisturbed since before the Duskfall. They are unrelated to what the interior tribes recognise as dead.
why_pressures: The tomb is intact. Two antiquarian parties are known to have entered. The second party went looking for the first.
why_would_change_if: Only a breach of the drainage would change it. The drainage has held for an age.
vibe_silhouette: A low formal stone entrance is framed by carving. The ground hides the entrance well.
vibe_palette: Black stone is carved in low relief that has gone soft with age. The crocodile skulls on the gate posts are bone-white. Grave goods lie dull gold under standing water. Moss climbs the door frame in one thin green line.
vibe_materials: The dressed Ayleid stone is jointed without mortar. The seams are still tight. The original drainage channel is still cut and running. It is unrepaired because it has never needed repair. Grave goods lie untouched as they were interred. No later hand has added anything.
vibe_signature_feature: The approach is flooded. The drainage of the tomb still works after an age.
vibe_condition: The tomb was sealed and undisturbed until two antiquarian parties entered. One party did not return.
vibe_mood: The work is Ayleid. It is older than any Argonian claim on this ground.
vibe_approach: Travellers find the tomb from a document and not from the ground.
vibe_senses: Standing water drips on a beat that never varies. Cold stone air carries no trace of the swamp's heat. A low structural groan sounds somewhere in the deeper chambers.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 357 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: The marsh has kept an Ayleid tomb sealed since before the Duskfall. Its own drainage still works.

name: One-Rise
why_founding: Six households live on ground that stays dry for two kilometres round in the wet season.
why_site_advantages: One-Rise is a single flood-high rise. The households occupy all of it.
why_occupants_motive: Farmers live here who cannot expand and will not leave. They work back-swamp rice. The rice exists only because the rise splits the flood.
why_pressures: Every neighbour wants shelter on the rise in the wet season. The households cannot house them. The neighbours remember the refusals longer than the floods.
why_would_change_if: A wetter decade would make the rise a refuge camp and not a hamlet. The households already know which of them would have to go.
vibe_silhouette: Structures stand on the high ground. They stand alone in a flat view.
vibe_palette: Green lies over standing brown water. The root-wood has gone silver with wet. Sap-gold runs in one bright line. Red flowers grow on the high ground. None grow below the flood mark.
vibe_materials: A shell of trained root stands here. Its floor is a single flattened buttress. The builders used hardwood pegs and withy, with no metal. The structure is unroofed since the last blow and is not yet re-shingled. Totems of wood, mud and plumage stand at the approach.
vibe_signature_feature: The rise is fully built to its edge. The wet-season waterline is painted on every wall at chest height.
vibe_condition: The households maintain the hamlet just enough and no more.
vibe_mood: The hamlet is cramped and self-sufficient. It is unwelcoming in wet months.
vibe_approach: In the wet season the rise is an island. The village is as large as the island.
vibe_senses: The boards spring underfoot at every step. Chimes rattle on a frame set above the flood mark. Wet bark and cut root smell like a woodyard in rain. No birds sound within earshot.
player_purpose_hook: Six households live on the last dry ground for two kilometres. The wet-season waterline is painted on every wall at chest height.

name: Greenspring
why_founding: Greenspring was founded beside the Panther Race. The founders chose springs whose water can be drunk unboiled. Unboiled drinking water is rare in this region. The tribe's Hist grows over the spring.
why_site_advantages: Greenspring stands on firm ground. Clean water rises from the spring. A lip of boulders rings the spring. The spring is a short walk from the road. The spring is a short walk from the river landing.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe serves travellers bound for Helstrom. The tribe has made itself indispensable to those travellers. The tribe charges nothing for water. The tribe charges a great deal for beds and rope.
why_pressures: Salt is reaching the spring water from upstream. The Hist has begun to sicken. The village blames the salt works for the salt in the water. Traffic for Helstrom brings cult couriers, tappers and the Veiled Reed's factors. The tribe does not wish to host those visitors.
why_would_change_if: If the spring soured, the village would have to move to find fresh water. Travellers bound for Helstrom would then lose their surest clean water.
vibe_silhouette: A sick crown leans over the spring. Huts stand round the spring.
vibe_palette: A pool of clear water lies under the Hist. The green crown of the Hist thins to open sky above. Painted urns stand along the yards. Brown churned mud lies at the landing.
vibe_materials: A tent stands beside the spring. The village has mud-walled pods and huts on mud pads. Beached canoes and a plank boat lie on the bank at the landing. The landing has no plank stage.
vibe_signature_feature: Visitors drink water from the clear pool under the Hist without ceremony. Visitors are expected to taste the water before they speak.
vibe_condition: The yards that are used daily are well kept. The ground that lies a step off the path is threadbare.
vibe_approach: On the way up from the landing, black river water gives way to a small clear pool under the Hist. Frond smoke from the cookfires reaches the landing before the houses are in sight.
vibe_senses: Visitors taste cold mineral water before a word is spoken. The landing smells of wet rope and boat tar. Voices barter over bed and rope prices. Frond smoke drifts from the cookfires at dusk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can settle the spring's use in writing. A quest can also foul the spring.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MR01 · tier-2; LH07 · tier-3; LH37 · tier-3; LH38 · tier-3; LH51 · tier-3
