watch_reason: A Hist village keeps no watch. Its disputes go to the tree-minder and the elders. The region's assessor sits in Helstrom.

name: The Far Shelter
why_founding: The Far Shelter is the second night's shelter on the basin crossing. The guides keep the shelter stocked themselves.
why_site_advantages: The shelter stands on defensible dry ground, an islet in deep marsh. The ground lies at the right distance along the crossing.
why_occupants_motive: Travellers crossing the basin use the shelter. A caretaker stays there in season. The guides pay the caretaker by a joint levy. The guides have not collected the levy in full since they agreed it.
why_pressures: Travellers take stores from the shelter and do not replace them. The guides have started marking the crates. The marks show whose clients took the stores.
why_would_change_if: An unstocked shelter costs lives. The guides at the gate camp price the second night higher than the first. They price it higher because of the risk of an unstocked shelter.
vibe_silhouette: The shelter is hard-roofed and stands on the last dry ground. A bell frame and a distance board stand beside it.
vibe_palette: Pale palisade timber stands against dark canopy. Ink on the ledger board is black on grey wood. Embers glow red in the banked fire pit. The chalked distance marker has gone white.
vibe_materials: The palisade is made of driven stakes lashed twice over. A bell frame stands beside the gate. A ledger post carries the season's tally sheets, which are nailed up. Sleeping shelves run along the inner wall.
vibe_signature_feature: A stock ledger records every taking with a signature. Unsigned takings are listed separately. Each unsigned taking is listed with a description of the taker.
vibe_condition: The guides restocked the shelter hard this year. The shelter had two seasons of shortfall before this year.
vibe_mood: The mood is relieved and short of stores.
vibe_approach: A palisade ring encloses a fire pit. The shelter stands on the first rise since the gate.
vibe_senses: Fire smoke hangs under the palisade roofline. Stakes settle and creak through the night. Parties compare crossings in low voices. Bedding is still damp come morning.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can audit the stores. A quest can arrive to find the stores gone.
why_site_won: islet in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 411 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The Far Shelter is the second night's shelter on the basin crossing. The guides stock it themselves. A ledger records who took what and who did not sign.

name: Gate-Side Camp
why_founding: Basin guides wait for hire at this camp outside the Helstrom gate.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands just outside the gate, 50 m west of the west basin gate. Inside the gate is the city's own ground. Guides loitering inside the gate are not welcome in the city.
why_occupants_motive: The guides price by the day and by the route. A guide will refuse a route outright and will not negotiate it.
why_pressures: Guides die in the basin. The camp's roster is shorter than it was. The basin has not got worse. Traffic has got heavier and less experienced.
why_would_change_if: The deep-basin expedition needs a hiring on a large scale. That hiring would empty the camp of its competent guides for a season.
vibe_silhouette: The hiring camp stands close against the Helstrom gate line. The camp is all frontage and has no depth.
vibe_palette: Cook-fire orange stands against Helstrom's grey wall. Route-board ink is faded where hands touch it most. Root-brown mud is packed hard by traffic. Red appears on the newest guide's tally mark and nowhere else.
vibe_materials: Tents are pitched hard against the gate ditch. The camp allows no permanent structure. A hire board is nailed up and repainted route by route. Cook fires are ringed in cut stone taken from the road verge. Bedding rolls are stacked ready for guides between hires.
vibe_signature_feature: A hire board lists routes with a price and a survival rate beside each. The survival rates are honest. A guide caught softening a rate loses the board.
vibe_condition: The guides rebuild the camp each season. Nothing in the camp is meant to last.
vibe_approach: Fires burn immediately outside a city that has no suburbs.
vibe_senses: Woodsmoke lies thick over the camp at dusk. Low bargaining voices run through the evening. The causeway's hum carries up from the gate. Boots and packs lie piled wet from the last route back.
quest_hooks_opportunity: MQ27 expedition guide hire
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ23 · tier-0; MQ27 · tier-0; LH06 · tier-3; LQ05 · tier-3
why_site_won: dry ground 50 m west of Helstrom's basin gate, 5 m above the marsh, outside every district of the city; sited there because the camp's name and its quest text place it at that gate.
player_purpose_hook: Basin guides wait for hire outside the Helstrom gate. A board lists routes priced beside their survival rates.

name: The Roost
why_founding: The Roost is a dead standing grove. Hackwings have used the grove for generations.
why_site_advantages: The grove is dead timber with clear flight lines. A roost needs clear flight lines.
why_occupants_motive: A flock of hackwings lives in the grove. The flock has used the grove for so long that the beast-keepers' grandparents complained about the same birds.
why_pressures: The hackwings take from the beast-keepers' young stock. The beast-keepers want the hackwings gone. The tribe that owns the grove takes hackwing feathers for its rites. That tribe refuses a cull.
why_would_change_if: Culling the roost would end a real nuisance. A cull would cost the owning tribe its feather source. The tribe recognises that feather source as legitimate.
vibe_silhouette: The circling birds mark the roost. They are visible from two ridges off.
vibe_palette: Dead grey timber stands against green canopy. Droppings whiten every branch. Black wings turn overhead.
vibe_materials: The grove is a standing dead grove that no builder has touched. The birds snapped the flight-line branches clean themselves. The roost has no repair of any kind.
vibe_signature_feature: Two hundred birds leave at first light in one movement. The departure is visible from four kilometres away.
vibe_condition: The grove is left to the birds. No cull has ever stuck.
vibe_approach: The dead grove is grey against green from a long way off.
vibe_senses: A wall of screeching rises at dawn when the flock lifts. The reek of guano lies thick under the grove. Feathers lie underfoot on every approach.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can move a roost that has begun taking from the road. The dawn line of the flock is predictable.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 27 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform.
player_purpose_hook: Two hundred birds leave in one movement at first light. The beast-keepers below have wanted them culled for three generations.

name: Crown of the First Line
why_founding: The place is the ancestor terrace of a tribe. The tribe buries its dead high because the ground drowns.
why_site_advantages: The oldest terrace sits on a hollow crown. The chambers inside the trunk hold the first line's dead. The crown stands on firm ground in firm lowland, not on a summit.
why_occupants_motive: Grave-singers visit the crown. The tribe permits no household on the crown. The tribe counts residence on the crown as trespass on its own ancestors.
why_pressures: Bone-thieves and antiquarians come to the crown. The tribe patrols in answer. The patrol is now a standing duty. The patrol takes four adults out of the fields.
why_would_change_if: The tribe would read a flood reaching the crown as a judgement. A Nisswo has twice told the tribe a flood is coming.
vibe_silhouette: Cut terraces step up a wooded dome. The terraces show as a shape change in the island's profile.
vibe_palette: Green terraces step up against brown floodwater below. A streak of gold sap catches light on one limb. Totem paint is weathered to rust.
vibe_materials: Platforms are cut into the living crown. The tribe re-pegs the platforms each generation. The builders use no metal. Hardwood pegs are driven fresh where old ones have worked loose. The grave-singer renews the totems at the base by hand.
vibe_signature_feature: Terraced burial platforms rise through the canopy. The oldest dead lie highest. The newest dead lie at the entry level.
vibe_condition: A standing patrol keeps the crown. The tribe can barely spare the patrol.
vibe_approach: The climb passes eight generations of terraces.
vibe_senses: Breath comes short by the fourth terrace. Still air holds the smell of old sap. Wind blows only at the highest platform. No insect sound reaches this high up.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 338 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: Burial terraces stack up through the canopy. The oldest dead lie highest. Grave-singers visit the crown. No household is permitted on it.

name: Green-Moss Hammock
why_founding: Green-Moss Hammock is a village on a raised hammock. The hammock has never flooded in memory.
why_site_advantages: The hammock has big timber, dry storage and its own spring.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe is rich in dry storage in a region that has almost none. The tribe is richer still in the obligations that storing other people's grain creates.
why_pressures: The village stores other villages' seed grain. The village has begun charging in labour and no longer in kind. Two of the four villages have started sending their grain further afield.
why_would_change_if: A theft or a rot in the store would ruin four villages at once. The tribe can insure against that loss only by holding more grain.
vibe_silhouette: A dome of taller trees stands above the marsh canopy.
vibe_palette: New-cut staddle posts show pale grain. A full granary interior shows deep gold through a propped door. Moss is soft green on every shaded roof. Dark stored grain lies heaped in sacks.
vibe_materials: Granaries stand on staddle posts to keep the store dry through the wet. Walls are woven withy, which is replaced only where a post has rotted. Roofs are thick frond laid to shed rain and to keep out light. The spring is boxed in stone. The village has kept the spring clear for generations.
vibe_signature_feature: Half the buildings are granaries on staddle posts. The village's standing is measured in how much of other people's food it holds.
vibe_condition: The village keeps the roofs sound. Four villages' winters depend on the roof holding.
vibe_mood: The mood is solid, careful and conscious of obligation.
vibe_approach: Big timber stands above the canopy line. Storehouses stand under the canopy.
vibe_senses: Dry grain-dust hangs in the air near the storehouses. A laden staddle post creaks as it settles under weight. Low counting voices check the stored grain against a tally-stick.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can turn on a double receipt. A quest can turn on a pledged household.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH39 · tier-3; LH40 · tier-3; LH41 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 4), 120 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The village holds other villages' grain. Half its buildings are granaries on staddle posts.

name: The Bled Tree
why_founding: The Bled Tree is a tribal Hist. An outside operation tapped it industrially during the Imperial century. The tapping has never been allowed to close.
why_site_advantages: The tree stands 47.2 m from swamp water and 715 m from the nearest route. The tapping crew chose the tree and still work it.
why_occupants_motive: The tapping crew are not local. A village has to watch the tapping. The crew work under a concession issued by an authority. That authority has not existed for a century.
why_pressures: The village feels every cut. The crew is armed and licensed by a lapsed authority. The crew sells to the same city fence as the sap poachers.
why_would_change_if: Ending the tapping would leave the village owing a debt. Ending it would put the fence's whole interior supply on the poachers alone.
vibe_silhouette: The crown thins from the top down. Cup-lines and ladder scars run up the trunk.
vibe_palette: The canopy thins yellow-green at the crown. Spiral cup-lines are pale against dark bark. Orange-red flowers drop before they open. A black sap slick pools at the sump.
vibe_materials: Split-cane ladders are lashed stage over stage up the trunk. Fired-clay collecting cups are set at every cut. A sap sump is dug and lined with stone. The village strung a chime frame between the pipes.
vibe_signature_feature: Stage-mounted taps spiral up the trunk. A sap sump lies at the base. The village hung its own offering chimes between the pipes.
vibe_condition: The crew works the tree on a lapsed licence. The village keeps up the offerings.
vibe_mood: The work is orderly. The village watches it.
vibe_approach: The sump smell carries across the swamp before the stage comes into view.
vibe_senses: Raw sap turns sharp in the heat. Ladder rungs creak under the crew's boots. An argument carries from the sump most afternoons. Tenders strike the offering chimes but cannot stop the work.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can end the tapping. A quest can make the dead authority's concession good.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 715 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: Taps spiral up a tribal Hist stage by stage. A sap sump lies at its foot. The tree is still worked. The village hangs its offering chimes between the pipes.

name: Helstrom
why_founding: Survivors of the Battle of Argonia withdrew to Helstrom. They retreated to ground that outsiders could not follow. The grove's tree-minders sheltered them.
why_site_advantages: Helstrom stands on spring-fed firm ground inside the Hist forest. Every interior route ends at Helstrom.
why_occupants_motive: An assembly of interior naheesh and tree-minders administers Helstrom. The assembly receives and redistributes goods. It does not rule. Its authority ends where a tribe stops sending a delegate.
why_pressures: The grove is the city. A blight, a fire or an Unbound Root cutting would destroy grove and city at once. Helstrom is safe inside the grove. Escorts are lost in the marsh at its gates every season.
why_would_change_if: If the interior tribes stopped sending delegates, Helstrom would be a grove with a market in it. Convocation attendance is already falling. The attendance count is public.
vibe_silhouette: Helstrom has no wall and no tower. The city grew out of a grove. Its crown-line steps down in living tiers from the grove crown to the market terraces. The tiers stand above the Onkobra reach, east of the city. The city is lit amber from inside after dark.
vibe_palette: Canopy-dark green is banded with lantern-amber. Red flowers mass across the grove crown. Black heart-mud lies in the lower lanes. One pale band marks where the river reach opens.
vibe_materials: Builders trained root across centuries into stair and gallery. Hot sap is poured into every structural joint and left standing proud. Chime lines are strung the length of every tier.
vibe_signature_feature: No wall can be seen from a distance. The grove canopy is the fortification. The gates open straight onto deep basin marsh. The escorts turn back at the gates.
vibe_condition: The residents replace the structures continuously.
vibe_approach: The last ridge of the escorted channel gives a long sightline. The grove crown stands over the canopy.
vibe_senses: Chimes sound together in patterns. Only residents read the chime patterns. Smoke and cooking fish layer by height.

why_site_won: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'helstrom' (world/sources/anchors); the anchor pixel is the city gate on the main road. The record sits at the solved city centre (cityLayout, owner rule 2026-09-18).
player_purpose_hook: Helstrom is the interior's capital and has no wall. Its chime lines carry signals that only residents read.
siting_note: The danger raster reads band 5 at the anchor. The rootland outside the gates is the worst ground in the province. The grove itself is the safest place in the region. The record carries D1 and not the band.

name: The Restarted Work
why_founding: A tribe decided that the Duskfall renunciation of stone was a mistake. The tribe began building with stone again.
why_site_advantages: The site holds an unfinished xanmeer terrace. The terrace stone was cut and abandoned mid-build. The tribe did not have to quarry it.
why_occupants_motive: The builders believe that permanence is owed to their descendants. Their naheesh says so publicly. The convocation has refused the naheesh a place twice for it.
why_pressures: Every neighbouring tribe treats the villagers as heretics. The Nisswo also object to the village. The village trades normally anyway. The same neighbours buy its cut stone.
why_would_change_if: Completion would force the interior to decide whether the taboo is law. The assembly at Helstrom has no procedure for such a ruling.
vibe_silhouette: Fresh-cut stone courses rise at the village. Argonians cut stone here, which the Duskfall taboo forbids.
vibe_palette: The new stone is pale against the weathered grey of the old courses. Mortar dust hangs white in the light. Moss grows only on the older half of each wall. Red paint shows where the join runs.
vibe_materials: New courses are laid rough over dressed Merethic stone. The join is left bare on purpose. Scaffolding of lashed cane stands against the finished wall. Mortar is mixed on site and cures in open troughs. The chime frame is built from offcut stone, not wood.
vibe_signature_feature: Fresh Argonian courses are laid on Merethic stone. The join between new and old stays visible on purpose. The new work is rougher than the old. The builders show the join deliberately.
vibe_condition: Two factions are rebuilding the work. The two factions keep undoing each other's work.
vibe_approach: Straight edges show on the skyline. Straight edges are rare in the interior.
vibe_senses: Chisel strikes can be heard across the clearing through the day. Stone dust catches at the back of the throat. Mortar smells wet and mineral over the usual mud and sap. The masons argue over a bad course within earshot of the gate.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can defend the masons or unmake the work.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH42 · tier-3; LH43 · tier-3; LH44 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 377 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: A tribe has started laying new courses on Merethic stone. The join between new and old is left visible. Every neighbouring tribe treats the villagers as heretics.
singular_claim: The place has countBand [1,1]. The taboo can only be broken where the abandoned stone already stands. The Duskfall horizon runs through the interior.

name: The Set-Aside Hut
why_founding: A tribal exile lives at the distance fixed by their sentence.
why_site_advantages: The site is the measured edge of the territory of the exile's tribe. A totem marks the edge. The exile may not pass the totem.
why_occupants_motive: One exile serves a term with an end date. The exile intends to reach the end date. The exile cuts a tally of the remaining days into the far face of the totem.
why_pressures: The exile's family leaves food at the totem. The family does not cross the totem. The youngest family member crossed it twice this season.
why_would_change_if: The sentence ends in four years. The exile is counting the days. The village that sentenced the exile has changed naheesh twice since then. The village may not honour the sentence.
vibe_silhouette: One hut stands on a rise. The ground around the hut is cleared for a full field of view.
vibe_palette: The hut is pale against the cleared ground. The boundary totem is dark with tally cuts. A single food ledge is bare of offerings today.
vibe_materials: The hut walls are living root that one pair of hands ties back each season. The totem carries a private tally on its far face. A cleared sightline is kept open on every side.
vibe_signature_feature: A food ledge stands at the boundary totem. A tally of the remaining days is carved on the totem's far side. Only the exile can see the tally.
vibe_condition: The exile keeps the hut alone. The exile counts down their own sentence.
vibe_approach: The totem is the first thing reached on the approach. The hut lies beyond the totem.
vibe_senses: Only wind can be heard through the cleared field of view. No neighbours are within earshot. Woodsmoke rises from a single fire. The totem's carved face is cold to the touch.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 631 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, region.
player_purpose_hook: An exile lives as far out as their sentence specifies. The remaining days are cut into the far side of the boundary totem.

name: The Talker
why_founding: A person went into the basin and stayed.
why_site_advantages: The hut stands on shallow marsh at the water's edge. The site has water and no neighbours. In the basin, that makes the site survivable.
why_occupants_motive: One person lives here in communion with something. The something may be a tree.
why_pressures: The occupant is harder to talk to each year. The occupant now speaks in the cadence of the sap-touched village. The occupant has never visited the sap-touched village.
why_would_change_if: The occupant will die here. The occupant's knowledge of the basin's routes is worth more than the caches that the occupant can name.
vibe_silhouette: One hut stands beside a churned pool. Every post is marked with red paint.
vibe_palette: Every post is marked with red paint against silvered wood. A churned brown pool lies at the door. Light is dim through the frond roof.
vibe_materials: The posts are cut only where needed. The rest of the tree is left standing. One pair of hands has patched the roof over thirty years. Carved lettering covers the walls from end to end inside. The lettering is unfinished.
vibe_signature_feature: One continuous carved sentence covers the whole interior of the hut. The sentence has been carved for thirty years. It has not reached a full stop.
vibe_condition: The occupant keeps the hut alone. The hut is tidy only where the occupant's hands still reach.
vibe_approach: Smoke rises from ground where a hearth is not expected.
vibe_senses: Smoke rises from a fire kept lit for no obvious reason. The same hand strikes one chime over and over. The pool smells stagnant at the door. Muttering can be heard before the hut is in sight.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 5), 356 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-firm-ground' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: One carved sentence covers the inside of the hut. The occupant has added to it for thirty years.

name: Needle-Crown, the Agaceph Hist
why_founding: The tree is one of the oldest of the deep basin. The Agaceph are its people and its shape.
why_site_advantages: The grove stands on an island in deep marsh. It has landings on three channels.
why_occupants_motive: The offices of tree-minder, sap-speaker and root-herald are all hereditary. One family holds all three offices. The neighbouring tribes have noticed this.
why_pressures: Pilgrims arrive without being asked. The Agaceph cannot refuse them. Pilgrims camp at the sap road a half-day out. They arrive faster than the Agaceph can feed them.
why_would_change_if: Withdrawal would end the Agaceph tribe as a culture. It would also close the district's fastest route, which runs through the Agaceph's three landings.
vibe_silhouette: One needle-fine crown stands a full canopy-height above the rest. The crown is red-lit after dark.
vibe_palette: The needle-fine crown shows red against the night sky. Gold sap runs in one unbroken line down the bark. Scaled gloor skin catches light in rainbow bands. Pale wood shows at the cleared pole-landing.
vibe_materials: The tree is left entirely as it grew. No surface is cut anywhere but at the landing. The pole-landing is kept clear by hand and is never allowed to close over. Regard-marks of withy are tied a hand's width apart, with one added per year. Nothing is built or propped against the trunk.
vibe_signature_feature: The tree's gloor produces needle-faced, rainbow-scaled people. The pole-landing is kept clear. The rest of the tree is left as it grew.
vibe_condition: Every regard-mark is replaced on schedule. The tree itself is untouched.
vibe_mood: The mood is formal. The people are hard on strangers who cannot be read by scale.
vibe_approach: The crown breaks the canopy. The crown glows red at night. It can be seen from four kilometres away across black water.
vibe_senses: A fast, high root-hum sounds unlike that of any other tree in the district. Needle-fine chime notes are pitched above ordinary hearing. Pilgrims keep their voices deliberately low near the trunk.
why_site_won: island in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 359 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, parent.
player_purpose_hook: A very old tree has needle-faced, rainbow-scaled people. Every Agaceph within a day's walk looks like a cousin of the tree.

name: First-Rain Trunk
why_founding: Interior recitation names this as the tree that stood at the first rain after the Duskfall.
why_site_advantages: The grove stands in still, open water in deep marsh. The fire that took the tree's northern half never reached the grove.
why_occupants_motive: A very small vigil of tenders expects to see the tree die. The tenders have refused every offer of help that came with a condition attached.
why_pressures: The tree is dying slowly. No cutting from it has taken. That includes the cutting given to the cut-and-carried tribe, which could not raise it.
why_would_change_if: The tree's death would produce a Mnemic Egg larger than the interior has seen before. Several factions want the egg. One faction has a camp within a day of the grove.
vibe_silhouette: The trunk is so broad that the path bends around it. The crown is lost in the layer above.
vibe_palette: Half the crown is dead grey. The other half is still deep green. The buttress roots are pale as scoured bone. Amber is sealed thick in the old root joints. One Hist flower hangs far out of reach overhead.
vibe_materials: Buttress roots serve as floor and bench. No tool has worked them. A single ancient chime frame has been strung over three generations. A ring of driven grave-poles stands at the drip-line. The tree is left unroofed and unwalled, as it grew.
vibe_signature_feature: The tree is the oldest trunk that the interior tribes will name. It is half dead standing wood and half alive.
vibe_condition: Keepers tend the tree and expect to outlive it. The keepers refuse all conditional help.
vibe_approach: The dead half shows as a grey spar above the canopy. It shows long before the green does.
vibe_senses: A low hum is felt through the chest more than it is heard. Sap thickens slowly in the dying limbs. The tenders talk quietly of what comes after. Birds are absent from the whole drip-line.
why_site_won: open water in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 510 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: Interior recitation names this as the tree that stood at the first rain after the Duskfall. Its tenders expect to outlive it.

name: No-Tree Camp
why_founding: The Hist-less settled here. They could not stay in the cities. The tribes would not admit them.
why_site_advantages: The ground is unclaimed. No tree's roots reach it.
why_occupants_motive: The people have no communion, no naming rite and no soul-return. They organise all three for themselves. They do it badly and in public. Each attempt sets a precedent.
why_pressures: The interior tribes regard the Hist-less as a thing that should not exist. The League of Open Water regards them as a cause. The League's coastal money is beginning to arrive.
why_would_change_if: If a tree accepted them, the settlement would dissolve. Some of them do not want that. The argument splits the camp every winter.
vibe_silhouette: The village has no tree and no stake-field. That reads as wrong to any Argonian raised near a tree.
vibe_palette: Firelight falls over ground with no crown above it. Green shade is doubled on still water. A bone-white peeled root forms the naming post. One red flower is planted.
vibe_materials: Trained root is braced over cut canopy timber for a frame raised without a Hist at its centre. Wattle infill is lashed panel by panel. The naming post is carved and recarved each season. A register is kept under oiled cloth.
vibe_signature_feature: A naming ground stands where the tree should be. It has a post, a register and a witness roster.
vibe_condition: The camp was built fast. It is kept up by argument as much as by repair.
vibe_approach: Firelight shows on ground where the interior says no firelight should be.
vibe_senses: It is quiet where a chime line should be sounding. The ground is dry and firm, which is uncommon this deep in the interior. Argument can be heard from the naming post most evenings. Woodsmoke lacks the usual resin note.
quest_hooks_opportunity: LW01 is a hook for the League of Open Water.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 144 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A naming ground stands with no tree at its centre. It does by register and witness what a Hist does by nature. The camp takes in anyone who has no tree.

name: Low-Crown, the Paatru Hist
why_founding: An old tree grew wide, not tall. The ground was too soft to hold a crown.
why_site_advantages: The grove stands at a spring head in tropical jungle. Soft mire surrounds it. The mire turns back carts, horses and outsiders.
why_occupants_motive: The Paatru regard height as a discourtesy. They build no higher than the tree's lowest branch. They apply the rule to visitors' tents.
why_pressures: The Paatru are physically unlike their neighbours. Their neighbours treat them accordingly. The Paatru trade through the walkway junction. They never trade in person.
why_would_change_if: If the mire dried, raiders could walk into the village. The village would then fall. The mire is the whole defence.
vibe_silhouette: A wide low crown spreads flat over a whole clearing. It is more roof than tree.
vibe_palette: Flat green light lies under the low crown. Amber sap is beaded at child height along the bark. Red bloom clusters thick at head height. Pale brown churned mud lies at every threshold.
vibe_materials: Benches are trained from the crown's own low limbs and polished smooth by use. Frond thatch is woven into gaps where the canopy thins. Passers-by redo the withy lashings each wet season. Totems are planted at every path into the crown's shade.
vibe_signature_feature: The tree is squat, wide and low. Its toad-like people build under its skirts. They do not build around its trunk.
vibe_condition: The village is kept low and close by design. It is patched constantly and never rebuilt.
vibe_approach: The canopy has no break at all. Visitors find the grove by the smell of its sap. Roofs appear under the leaf line.
vibe_senses: Warm damp air is trapped under the spreading canopy. Toad-croak is heard beneath low chimes, which sound more like drum-thuds. Sap and wet mud mix underfoot. No open sky is visible anywhere beneath the crown.
why_site_won: spring head in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 258 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A squat wide tree has toad-like people living under its skirts. Carts and outsiders cannot cross the soft ground around it. The crown sits below the level of the mire path.

name: High-Flower, the Sarpa Hist
why_founding: The Sarpa tend this tree from the canopy. They have tended it for nine recorded generations.
why_site_advantages: The grove stands on plain shallow-marsh ground above the flood. The air above is clear for launching.
why_occupants_motive: The winged Sarpa consider the ground a burial place. Their trade, their courts and their hatching all happen above the ground.
why_pressures: The climb is the approach. The tribe has twice refused to cut a stair for the tree-minders' benefit.
why_would_change_if: Losing the crown platforms in a storm would suspend the rite for a generation. The timber to rebuild them has to come from the hammock village two days away.
vibe_silhouette: A high thin crown carries flowers only at the highest point. Wings can reach the flowers.
vibe_palette: The trunk is bare grey below. Red flowers are massed high where only wings can reach them. White glare shines at the crown.
vibe_materials: Flint-vine ladders are strung for wings, not feet. Crown platforms are rebuilt from timber carried two days by the hammock village. A stake ring at ground level is left for the dead alone.
vibe_signature_feature: The Sarpa are winged, so they tend the tree from above. The working life of the grove happens on the crown platforms. The ground below is left to the dead.
vibe_condition: The Sarpa rebuild the platforms one by one after every storm. The rebuilding is required by Sarpa doctrine.
vibe_mood: The mood is vertiginous. The place is unwelcoming to the flightless.
vibe_approach: The approach passes under bare trunk. The settlement is overhead, reached by climbing.
vibe_senses: Silence holds at the roots. Voices come only from above. A thin sap smell thickens near the crown. The ground at the base is unworn by any path.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 117 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, parent.
player_purpose_hook: The working life of this grove happens on the crown platforms. The ground under it is left to the dead. The climb is the only approach for the flightless.

name: The Kept Line
why_founding: The Kept Line is a tribe that has watched one thing for generations. The watch is now the whole identity of the tribe.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on plain ground in shallow marsh, 49 m from a channel. From there the villagers patrol the sealed xanmeer place.hist-heartland.sealed-xanmeer-living. The wardens turn visitors back from the xanmeer.
why_occupants_motive: The wardens are hereditary. Each warden inherits a post, not a trade. The tribe feeds the wardens in exchange for the watch.
why_pressures: No living warden knows what lies inside the xanmeer that the wardens guard. Each of the last three generations of wardens privately reached a different conclusion.
why_would_change_if: Opening the xanmeer would end the tribe's reason to exist. The wardens fight an antiquarian harder than they fight a looter.
vibe_silhouette: The village is a gate with a cleared approach. Nothing along the approach offers a welcome to a visitor.
vibe_palette: The water is grey and the landing is bare. No colour flies at the gate. Spear-heads catch the sun as it crosses the clearing.
vibe_materials: The gatehouse roof is a bent canopy limb that is rooted at both ends. Every household mends the stockade to one uniform pattern. The stone of the sealed xanmeer behind the fence is left untouched.
vibe_signature_feature: Every adult carries the same inherited spear pattern. The villagers recite a watch-roster on the storytelling ground. They do not recite a history.
vibe_condition: The village is kept to a fixed standard, generation after generation.
vibe_approach: A warden calls a challenge from cover at eight hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Birdsong is absent close to the gate. A challenge is called from cover before any face is seen. The air smells of oiled spearheads. Long stretches pass with nothing said.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can get a name struck from the watch roster. A quest can also get past the watch.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH45 · tier-3; LH46 · tier-3; PP07 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 351 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, parent.
player_purpose_hook: The entire history of the village is a watch roster. The villagers guard a sealed xanmeer that no visitor may approach.

name: Medusa Wood
why_founding: Medusa Wood is a stand of drowned forest at the edge of the deepest basin water. The tribes give the stand a name in recitation. The tribes do not enter it.
why_site_advantages: The wood lies above the deepest standing water in the interior. The drowned forest beneath the wood has not rotted.
why_occupants_motive: Something lives down there. No two recitations describe it the same way. The recitations name the water. They cite no witness.
why_pressures: The stories are older than the name. The drowned timber is the finest known to the coast dredgers.
why_would_change_if: Little would change the wood. The dredging outfits on the coast have begun asking what it would be worth to lift a stand of unrotted forest.
vibe_silhouette: Grey trunks stand in the water. All of the trunks lean the same way.
vibe_palette: Grey drowned trunks lean uniformly under still black water. Pale light swims through the submerged canopy. Wreck cargo shows dull bronze on the silted floor. Past the treeline the surface shows no colour.
vibe_materials: The standing timber drowned whole and never rotted. The bark is still keyed tight to the wood. Wreck cargo lies among the roots, with the crates burst and spilled. Only the drowned forest stands down here. No built structure stands there. The silt is undisturbed except where a boat has passed.
vibe_signature_feature: A submerged forest still stands upright. The canopy of the forest lies at swimming depth.
vibe_condition: The wood is unrotted and has stayed unchanged for longer than the tribes have names for it.
vibe_mood: The wood is deep and still. The tribes name it in recitation.
vibe_approach: Seen from a boat, bare grey trunk tips break the surface in a grid. The grid is plainly a forest.
vibe_senses: Underwater the wood is totally quiet, with no current and no fish sound. The cold deepens with each metre of depth. Above the surface, the hull noise of a boat carries too far.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 378 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: A drowned forest still stands upright, with its canopy at swimming depth. The recitations give the water a name.

name: The Lost City
why_founding: The Lost City was built before the Duskfall around the graft called the Root of Accord. The city was unmade from the map. It was not destroyed.
why_site_advantages: The city lies in the deepest ground of the basin. The nearest route is 500.6 m away. The root layer is densest here. The density was grown here.
why_occupants_motive: The city has no inhabitants. A cult expedition and guardians are present. Whatever the Accord left tending itself has done the same work for an age.
why_pressures: The Unbound Root is trying to reach the city. The Eye is the key.
why_would_change_if: Only the Eye changes the city.
vibe_silhouette: Terraced massing rises unbroken out of black water. No path leads to it. No path goes round it.
vibe_palette: Black floodwater laps at pale terraced stone. A thin green glow is held only at the sealed entry. Amber lies long dead in the veins of the stone. Colour fades a few steps past the light.
vibe_materials: The city is xanmeer block that was cut and dressed at city scale. No lashed or woven work appears anywhere in it. Root has grown through the stonework and holds old collapses together. A single frontage opens only to the Eye. Silt has sealed every lower course for centuries.
vibe_signature_feature: A whole terraced city lies under root and water. The forest that grew over the civic streets roofs them.
vibe_condition: The city is sealed. It is not ruined. Contents lie in the places where the Accord set them.
vibe_mood: The city is quiet. It is larger than the Helstrom grove.
vibe_approach: Crossing the basin takes days, with fixed shelters along the way. The frontage then opens only to the Eye.
vibe_senses: Cold rises off ground that ought to hold warmth. An echo returns where the interior swallows sound everywhere else. The standing water tastes of old minerals. A distant working sound comes from guardians that are never seen.
quest_hooks_opportunity: LOC dungeon.lost_city · BOSS lost_city.last_warden · LOC lost_city.root_sanctuary
why_site_won: enclosed clearing in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 501 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: A terraced city lies under root and water. The forest that grew over the streets roofs them. The graft at the centre, the Root of Accord, is still inside.
reconciliation: The city is sited in the deep basin beyond Helstrom. Builders must confirm that no neighbouring place claims the same ground.

name: The Wading Ground
why_founding: The Wading Ground is a marsh giant's range. The tribes route around it without discussion.
why_site_advantages: The water is deep enough that the giant can stand upright in it. The shallows give the giant feeding ground.
why_occupants_motive: One giant lives here, with the birds that follow it. The tribes have mapped its hunting pattern closely. They route around it without a guide.
why_pressures: The range of the giant is expanding toward a walkway route. The walkway village has begun asking whether killing a giant is the offence that the tree-minders say it is.
why_would_change_if: Moving the walkway costs a season's labour. The tribe that uses the arm least would have to fund the move.
vibe_silhouette: A cleared path runs through vegetation at a wrong height. A totem line stands before the path.
vibe_palette: Clear brown water pales to green above. A wide track flattens red flowers into the mud. Pale bone catches light at head height. Grey churn lines the banks.
vibe_materials: No built structure stands here. The weight of the giant has cut channels through the reed beds. A single depth stick is driven into the bank and left there. A totem line marks the safe route around the giant.
vibe_signature_feature: The feeding paths of the giant are permanent channels cut through the reed beds. The newest channel points at the walkway.
vibe_condition: The ground is unmanaged. The channels widen a little more each season.
vibe_approach: The channels are readable from the walkway before the giant is in sight.
vibe_senses: The ground trembles faintly before the giant comes into view. Wading birds lift off ahead of it. Reed stems snap out of sight. Standing water goes still again once the giant has passed.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 418 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: The range of the giant can be mapped from the channels that it has trodden through the reeds. The newest channel points at the walkway.

name: The Counting Field
why_founding: The Counting Field is a Knahaten Flu mass grave. It serves the villages that emptied along this reach.
why_site_advantages: The ground is flat. It was left unwanted afterwards.
why_occupants_motive: A memorial keeper from the nearest village tends the field. The post carries no pay. The keeper is exempt from every other village duty.
why_pressures: The count on the stone is disputed. The stone has been recut twice, each time upward. A different tribe paid for each recut.
why_would_change_if: A recount would restart the argument. A recount would also have to include the Kothringi names. The grave-singers have cut no such stake.
vibe_silhouette: The field is marked ground with no settlement. The field has no burial furniture of the normal kind.
vibe_palette: Pale grey stakes stand in even rows over flat ground. Silt-white water beyond the field catches green light. Charcoal streaks have weathered into three blank stakes. Mud at the low edge of the field is dull brown.
vibe_materials: Driven stakes carry a village name and a cut number. Some of the stakes have been recut twice. Open ground is kept clear of the surrounding root growth. A low wattle fence marks the edge of the field. Nothing is built inside the field. Only the stakes stand here. No shrine structure stands here.
vibe_signature_feature: There is one stake for every village. There is not one stake for every person. Each stake carries the village name and its final count. Three stakes carry no count at all.
vibe_condition: Stakes are recut when a tribe pays for it. Otherwise the stakes are left as they stand.
vibe_mood: The field feels administrative. The count is disputed.
vibe_approach: Stakes stand at regular intervals. The field looks unlike an ordinary grave field.
vibe_senses: Insects are loud over the open field, where no canopy shades it. Recut names smell of damp stone-dust. Wind carries further here than in the enclosed swamp. The ground is firm and dry underfoot, unlike the land around it.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 400 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: There is one stake per village. There is not one stake per person. Each stake carries its final count. Three stakes carry no count at all.

name: The Chukka-Sei Ground
why_founding: The Chukka-Sei Ground is where the young of the interior are given their adult name.
why_site_advantages: The site is a stretch of bad water and root. A prepared adolescent can survive it.
why_occupants_motive: Trial-keepers set the route each year. A trial-keeper who is asked for the reason answers that the route is swum. What makes the route a trial is in the water. The route is put back after every year's running.
why_pressures: The trial kills a participant every few years. The last death was an Agaceph boy, in the dry season two years ago. Families whose clutch is not running that year support the trial more readily.
why_would_change_if: A death in the wrong family would force a change. The Agaceph tree-minders have a candidate in the coming season.
vibe_silhouette: The ground is a marked course in bad water. The course has an observation point.
vibe_palette: A pale finish-post stands alone. Bad water is dark beneath the surface. No other marker stands anywhere on the course.
vibe_materials: No built structure stands here. Root and current carry the course entirely. A single carved post at the finish has names cut deep. The trial-keepers reset the water after each trial.
vibe_signature_feature: The route is unmarked. One post at the finish is cut with the names given here. Some years have no name cut.
vibe_condition: The trial-keepers reset the course before every year's clutch.
vibe_approach: The finish post is easy to find. The route itself is unmarked.
vibe_senses: Heat does not lift once the sun goes down. Wet root smells like a timber yard after rain.
why_site_won: spring head in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 380 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, parent, remote.
player_purpose_hook: Adolescents go into bad water alone and come out with an adult name. The finish post carries every name given here since it was cut.

name: Kaal-Meen's Stone
why_founding: A guide died bringing a party out of the basin. Her clients paid for the stone.
why_site_advantages: The stone stands where she stopped. Guides walked that ground that year.
why_occupants_motive: The stone has no resident keeper. Passing guides touch it. Each season the gate camp reads its roster against her name to count the losses of the year.
why_pressures: The walking line has shifted east. Fewer guides make the detour to touch the stone each season.
why_would_change_if: The root country will swallow the stone. The guides have discussed moving it and have refused.
vibe_silhouette: A dressed upright stone with an inscription stands out against the vegetation.
vibe_palette: Pale dressed stone stands against root-country green. The gold lettering is worn thin. Fresh red petals lie over the browned petals of last season.
vibe_materials: The stone was quarried, cut and lettered outside the province. It was carried in whole. Root has grown around the base without disturbing the cut. Passing guides add stones one at a time to a small cairn.
vibe_signature_feature: Outsiders paid for the stone. It is Imperial-cut, in Cyrodiilic letters, in the middle of the interior.
vibe_condition: Whichever guide still makes the detour tends the stone.
vibe_mood: The stone carries a foreign grief that is small and private.
vibe_approach: Straight-cut stone stands in root country.
vibe_senses: The ground underfoot is warm even in shade. A frog-pipe is practised somewhere out of sight. The stone is cold against the surrounding heat. The place is quiet enough for a name spoken aloud to be heard.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 285 m from the nearest route; its choice #6 landform; won on route, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: An Imperial-cut stone in Cyrodiilic letters stands in the middle of the interior. The clients whom a guide died bringing out paid for it.

name: The Slow Ground
why_founding: Xanmeer footings sank into the mud here. The roots took the stone up again. A miregaunt walks the ground over the footings.
why_site_advantages: The mud is deep with hard courses under it. The miregaunt has footing there where a person has none.
why_occupants_motive: The miregaunt keeps a circuit of about four hundred paces. It has not been seen off that ground.
why_pressures: Reed cutters worked this stand for three generations. They now cut a poorer stand a mile north. They say so loudly at market.
why_would_change_if: Killing the miregaunt opens the good reed stand again.
vibe_silhouette: Reed stretches to the horizon. One shape stands taller than the reed and moves.
vibe_palette: Grey-green reed runs to the horizon. Wet stone shows pale where the mud has slumped. One dark shape moves taller than the reed line. Brown standing water lies between the stems.
vibe_materials: Dressed footing stone is sunk unevenly into the soft ground. Reed has grown thick over the buried courses. The slumped ring of stone marks how far the mud has moved in three generations. Nothing is repaired here. The reed cutters have cut nothing here since they left.
vibe_signature_feature: Dressed stone lies at the surface in a rough ring. The ring shows how far the mud has slumped.
vibe_condition: The reed cutters abandoned the ground. They left it as it stood.
vibe_approach: Cut reed lies at the edge, and then reed that has been left standing begins.
vibe_senses: Wet suction pulls underfoot with every step off the firm patches. Reed stalks tick against each other in a wind that is not felt at ground level. A heavy, regular footfall carries through the standing water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The reed cutters will pay in labour. They will not pay in coin. Labour is worth more to the households rebuilding the walkway.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 399 m from the nearest route; no free 'hollow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: One miregaunt walks a fixed circuit. It stands between the reed cutters and the best stand that they know.

name: The Ward
why_founding: A miregaunt has stood on the dry approach to Xal-Ussep. The wardens' line has known the ruin behind it for as long as the miregaunt has stood there. The miregaunt holds the approach.
why_site_advantages: The site is the dry approach to a sealed xanmeer. The place is firm ground in tropical jungle, 82.3 m from swamp water.
why_occupants_motive: One miregaunt holds the approach and is part of the land. The miregaunt returns when it is killed. It does not follow anyone beyond the approach that it holds.
why_pressures: Nothing pressures the miregaunt. Its toll is paid in lives. Hereditary wardens live on the ridge above the approach. The wardens regard the miregaunt as an ally that they did not have to feed.
why_would_change_if: The miregaunt comes back after it is killed. The cavity relic that the miregaunt carries goes to whoever kills it.
vibe_silhouette: The approach looks like ground where the vegetation has been rearranged. The vegetation on the approach has been broken, not cleared.
vibe_palette: Green light skims the silt-white shallows. Root-wood has gone silver where the wet has bleached it. Old amber is crusted in the shade. A red flower stays still in the reflection.
vibe_materials: The approach ground is unworked. The vegetation on the approach is broken, not cleared. Weathered grey stone shows through the cut root. A single old totem marks the edge and has never been replaced. A debris band of gear lies sorted roughly by age.
vibe_signature_feature: Gear from those who failed to pass lies where they fell. The debris lies in a hundred-metre band sorted by age. The newest debris lies at the near edge.
vibe_condition: No warden manages the approach. The miregaunt that already guards it is the only keeper of the approach.
vibe_approach: The debris field is graded by age. The debris lies well before the miregaunt that made it.
vibe_senses: Peat shifts underfoot with every step forward. Smoke drifts somewhere under the canopy. Its source is unclear. Standing water settles nearby with a low creak. The stillness breaks when the miregaunt moves.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The miregaunt returns when it is killed. A quest can use it as a door, a hazard or a renewable prize.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 350 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform.
player_purpose_hook: Gear from those who failed to get past lies where they fell. The debris lies in a hundred-metre band sorted by age, with the newest nearest. The way in is behind the miregaunt.

name: The Held Mist
why_founding: A hollow holds its own mist year-round. The air in the hollow does not move.
why_site_advantages: The hollow stands on plain firm ground in tropical jungle, 5.5 m from swamp water. A cold spring lies at the bottom of the hollow. Closed canopy covers the hollow.
why_occupants_motive: Whatever is in the hollow closes on visitors before it is seen. The guides route round the hollow. The guides charge clients as though they had crossed it.
why_pressures: People go into the hollow and come out somewhere else. They lose hours in the mist. Two of the district's wisp-lure stories probably describe this place by mistake.
why_would_change_if: The mist is weather. The guides say so. The guides' clients do not believe them.
vibe_silhouette: A standing mist body is visible from above. The mist fills this one hollow but not its neighbours.
vibe_palette: Grey mist lies over black water. Canopy green fades out past the rim. The bowl itself is drained of colour. A rope's pale line disappears downward.
vibe_materials: A single step is cut into living root. The step was made once and regretted. A rope anchor is tied off at the rim. Old paint marks on the last dry tree show the way out.
vibe_signature_feature: Visibility inside the mist is under four metres in any weather. Local practice is to enter on a rope that is tied off outside.
vibe_condition: The hollow is left as it is. No repair has held for a season here.
vibe_mood: The hollow disorients visitors. Sounds from it carry far before it comes into view.
vibe_approach: The mist edge is a hard vertical line. A hand pushed into the mist disappears.
vibe_senses: Cold rises off the spring at the bottom. Sound arrives from a direction with nothing in it. Sight is gone within a few strides of the edge. Footsteps are lost past the mist line.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 238 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: Visibility is under four metres in any weather. A cold spring lies at the bottom of the hollow. Something down there hunts by sound.

name: Waits-For-The-Second-Man
why_founding: A tribeless Naga band worked the plantation roads until the roads emptied. The band moved to the footpaths. Couriers still use the footpaths.
why_site_advantages: The camp lies on a thorn bank over a path. The path is narrow enough that a party has to walk it in single file.
why_occupants_motive: The band takes the second walker in a line. The band lets the first walker pass. A party sees the loss only when it stops to count.
why_pressures: The nearest village now sends its couriers in fives. That leaves the band four more meals a day to win.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the bank shortens the courier run by a day.
vibe_silhouette: The camp is invisible from the path. From above, four sleeping hollows are scraped in the thorn. A cold fire trench lies beside the hollows.
vibe_palette: Thorn grey-green closes overhead. Boots have rubbed the path below red-brown and worn it thin. No fire glows anywhere after dark. Stolen packs and cloth scraps are the only bright colour in the scrape.
vibe_materials: Sleeping hollows are scraped into bare earth under the thorn. Stolen packs are stacked for cover as much as for loot. A cold fire trench has been unused since the last watch. Everything built here can be abandoned in a minute.
vibe_signature_feature: The path below is worn to one boot width. The narrow wear runs for sixty paces.
vibe_condition: Raiders strike the camp within the hour of an attack. The band rebuilds wherever the thorn allows.
vibe_approach: The path runs directly beneath the bank.
vibe_senses: Thorn scrapes in the dark overhead. The single-file wear on the path shows where a party has to bunch. A courier's chime carries up from the track ahead of the courier. The air holds no trace of smoke.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The band keeps a cache of letters. The letters are worth more to their senders than the coin is to the band.
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 360 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A thorn bank lies over a single-file path. The band takes the second walker in the line.

name: The Tenders' Village
why_founding: The village exists to service the grave-pole fields of six neighbouring tribes.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on firm ground with landings. It is central to the fields that it serves. It lies downwind of all the fields.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers are grave-singers and pole-binders. The six tribes pay them in food. The six tribes do not invite them to the feasts. None of the six tribes accepts the villagers' children as marriage partners.
why_pressures: Bog blights rise when a pole is pulled. Poles are pulled more often since Umbriel. The village is turning work away. The tribes blame the village for risings that it could not reach.
why_would_change_if: If a neighbouring tribe learned to bind its own poles, the village would starve. The binding is taught by demonstration. The binding is never described.
vibe_silhouette: Cairn-rows step up the rise above the roofs. The village has more markers than houses.
vibe_palette: The cairn rows are pale above the low roofs. The water below is grey. Painted cord bands are the brightest colour in the village.
vibe_materials: Root has been trained into wall and floor over generations of binding. Racks of finished grave-poles stand along every house front. Cane lashing fills gaps where withy ran short.
vibe_signature_feature: The binding sheds run the length of the village. Every house front is a rack of finished poles waiting for collection. Each pole is wrapped in cord and painted in bands. The bands carry a life story.
vibe_condition: Villagers repair the village quickly and roughly. They rarely bring a repair to a finished state.
vibe_approach: The rattle of the racks in the wind carries further than the village does.
vibe_senses: Poles rattle in the wind before the village comes into view. A sweet smell of rot comes off the fields upwind. Little birdsong is heard this close to the graves.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An uncollected pole names a family. A quest can chase the pole to that family.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH09 · tier-3; LH47 · tier-3; LH48 · tier-3; PP12 · tier-3; province system · tier-1
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 292 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: Every house front is a rack of finished grave-poles waiting for collection. Each pole is bound in cord that carries a dead person's life story. The binding is done for six neighbouring tribes.

name: The Lightless Village
why_founding: The villagers stopped using fire and lamps generations ago. The village reorganised itself around not being seen.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh, 17.3 m from deep marsh water. No gorge site was left in the zone, so the ground is plain. The densest closed canopy in the interior covers the village. Noon and midnight differ little under that canopy.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers' eyes have adapted to the dark. Their etiquette is entirely acoustic. They trade by leaving goods and counted taps. They do not trade by meeting.
why_pressures: Something in the surrounding darkness caused the villagers to live without light. That thing is still out there. The youngest generation has begun to doubt the rule. The elders expect the young to learn otherwise.
why_would_change_if: A single lamp carried in would be an act of violence. The guides charge extra to explain that to clients before they arrive.
vibe_silhouette: No light and no smoke show where a village clearly stands.
vibe_palette: Unbroken dark lies where a settlement plainly stands. Faint blue smoke lies flat under the canopy. No other colour is visible.
vibe_materials: Houses are built on a canopy-timber spine. No window is cut in any house. Chime-lines are strung head-high between posts to guide by touch. Goods are left on a step and are not handed over.
vibe_signature_feature: No flame is used anywhere in the settlement. Chime-lines strung head-high give the direction. Villagers lead visitors by the wrist.
vibe_condition: Villagers keep the village as it has always been kept. They keep it without a flame.
vibe_approach: Villagers meet visitors in the dark. The meeting happens before the village is in sight.
vibe_senses: The ground moves faintly with the weight of the tree. Chime notes pass hand to hand across the dark. Sour leaf-litter lies underfoot. A hand takes the visitor's wrist before a voice is heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can foul the chime-lines. A quest can cut the chime-lines. A quest can follow the chime-lines somewhere unlit.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: DQ05 · tier-3; LH49 · tier-3; LH50 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 20 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'gorge' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: No flame is lit anywhere in the village. Villagers lead visitors by the wrist along the chime-lines.
singular_claim: The countBand is [1,1]. The closed interior canopy is where lightlessness is survivable and necessary.

name: Nine-Trunks
why_founding: A village grew where nine root-joined trunks stand in one ring. By the Hist's reckoning the ring is one tree. By the tribes' reckoning the ring is nine trees.
why_site_advantages: The ring encloses firm ground. The ring serves as its own stockade.
why_occupants_motive: A tribe hosts the convocation's overflow. The tribe has grown rich on hosting it. It rents pitch-rights to delegations that cannot fit at the Tsoko camp.
why_pressures: Hosting a province's delegations one month a year has made the tribe arrogant the other eleven. Two neighbouring tribes now choose to camp at Greenspring on principle.
why_would_change_if: A convocation held elsewhere would halve the village. Attendance is counted publicly at the Root Talk ground. The falling attendance already shows in the village's rents.
vibe_silhouette: Nine trunks grow from one root. The ring reads as a stockade from any angle.
vibe_palette: Nine grey trunks cast one shared shadow. Pitch-canvas gold marks the delegation tents. Peat-dark ground is trodden bare inside the ring. Chime-metal glints where it has been taken down and stacked.
vibe_materials: Houses are framed between the trunks. Bark and root grown between the trunks serve as walls. The houses have no timber of their own. The ring itself is untouched except for pitch-rights markers driven at its base. Delegation shelters are borrowed canvas that is struck and re-pitched by the month. Nothing here shows age. The village is rebuilt for show each convocation.
vibe_signature_feature: Houses stand between the nine trunks. The trunks are the houses' corner posts. No building here has four walls of its own.
vibe_condition: Villagers keep the village immaculate for one month. They neglect it the other eleven.
vibe_approach: The ring reads as a single mass from outside. It opens once entered.
vibe_senses: Raised bargaining voices come from the pitch-rights ground. Canvas snaps loose in a wind that the trunks otherwise block. The smell of too many cook-fires fills the space.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can turn on pitch-rights. A quest can turn on what the delegations carry.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH37 · tier-3; LH51 · tier-3; LH52 · tier-3; LH53 · tier-3; MQ19 · tier-3
why_site_won: Pinned by the Part 6 meso siting (world/sources/blueprints/place.hist-heartland.nine-trunks.json): A firm-lowland knoll 149 m from the plot: 4.77 m above the water table, ground slope 2.6 deg and 2.17 m of relief across the whole 66 m ring, so eight of the nine trunks sit on a plinth or a pad and the elder trunk needs a dug-in flare. Poleable water 32 m west with the shoreline 40 m off, so the ring encloses firm ground rather than standing in it; the Archon-Gideon road passes 160 m south-west, which is the catalogue's road discovery; flood band 0 and no wet-season inundation.
player_purpose_hook: Nine root-joined trunks stand in a ring. Houses are built between the trunks. The village rents pitch to convocation delegations.

name: The Turning House
why_founding: The Nisswo keep a rest house on the Helstrom pilgrim road.
why_site_advantages: The rest house lies one day's walk from the gate. It is deliberately the last stop.
why_occupants_motive: Nisswo preach at whoever stops. They feed visitors either way. The feeding is the doctrine's proof. The preaching is the price.
why_pressures: The Hist establishment and the Sithis preachers disagree politely about the interior's soul. The politeness holds because Helstrom's assembly would have to act if it broke.
why_would_change_if: A closure would leave the last day of the road unsheltered. Pilgrims would arrive at the gate camp. The guides would charge them for it.
vibe_silhouette: The house is swept and maintained. The road's other shelters sag.
vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow glow lights the near wall. Peat-brown floorboards are worn springy underfoot. Black-burned sap marks stain the roof beams. A red Hist flower hangs high above the doorway.
vibe_materials: Root is trained just enough to leave a path clear through it. Cane-and-vine binding is renewed at every visit. Bone chimes hang at the threshold to greet arrivals. The sermon is painted in soot ink around the inside of the roof ring.
vibe_signature_feature: The sermon is painted around the inside of the roof. Visitors read the sermon lying down.
vibe_condition: The Nisswo keep the house swept and freshly painted. They leave the road's other shelters to sag.
vibe_approach: Lamplight shows on the road at the hour the walking parties arrive.
vibe_senses: Cooking smoke is thick under a low roof. Walking parties arrive after dark with audible footsteps. A Nisswo's voice is pitched to carry to the last bench. Quiet returns fast once the meal is served.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can commission a sermon here. A quest can erase a sermon here. A quest can dispute a sermon here.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 91 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: A Nisswo rest house stands one day short of the gate. The sermon is painted round the inside of the roof. Visitors read the sermon lying down.

name: The Singer's House
why_founding: A grave-singer lives apart from the villages that the grave-singer serves. Custom and preference both keep the grave-singer apart.
why_site_advantages: The house stands between five villages. None of the five villages claims or maintains the ground.
why_occupants_motive: A grave-singer lives here. An apprentice who does not want the job lives here too.
why_pressures: Staking work has increased since Umbriel. It is more than one singer can do. The necropolis village a day away has offered to take the circuit. The five villages cannot afford that offer.
why_would_change_if: If the apprentice left, five villages' dead would be stranded. The apprentice has family at the Hist-less refuge. She has been asking about the refuge.
vibe_silhouette: One dwelling stands set apart, downwind of the village. It has a drying rack and a pole store.
vibe_palette: The water is grey and the banks are green. A pale mourning mat lies at the threshold. Dried red flowers hang by the door.
vibe_materials: Root-wood is cut only where needed. The rest of the frame is left living. A drying rack holds staking cloth. Blank grave-poles are racked under cover. One finished pole is propped unclaimed by the door.
vibe_signature_feature: A wall of blank poles waits to be bound. One finished pole is propped by the door. That pole has waited eleven years for a family to collect it.
vibe_condition: One household keeps the house. The five villages will not fund repairs.
vibe_approach: The house stands off every village's ground. It stands on the path between the villages.
vibe_senses: Drying reed cloth smells over the marsh smell. Carving sounds run through most of the day. Five villages' chime lines carry faintly from here. Damp wood smells near the water's edge.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The finished pole names a family. The pole has waited eleven years. A quest can find that family.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 150 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: A wall of blank poles stands at the house. One finished grave-pole stands by the door. It has waited eleven years for a family to come for it.

name: The Minder's House
why_founding: The Minder's House is a tree-minder's house. The tree chooses its site. The village does not choose the site.
why_site_advantages: The house stands within sight of the tree. It also stands within earshot of the tree. The tree-minder's post requires both at all times.
why_occupants_motive: A tree-minder lives in the house. A second tender sits in whenever the first listens. The arrangement costs the grove two adults' labour. The grove never waives the arrangement.
why_pressures: The two-tender rule is the grove's answer to what exclusive communion did at Lilmoth. The minder here trained under a person who was at Lilmoth.
why_would_change_if: The grove would remove a minder who listened alone. The whole district would hear of the removal by nightfall.
vibe_silhouette: One dwelling stands set apart, within sight of the tree. A chime frame stands taller than the roof.
vibe_palette: Tea-dark water lies under close green shade. Red clay shows raw where the bank has slumped. A single red flower is kept in a cup on the sill. Pale fungus shelves up the nearby trunks.
vibe_materials: The decking is split root-wood pegged to living sills. The one-room house has two built-in beds, two built-in chairs and two built-in lamps. Storm damage to the roof shingling has been patched. The patching is not yet finished. Totems are set along the path that runs from the house to the tree.
vibe_signature_feature: The house has two beds, two chairs and two lamps. The builders made solitary communion physically awkward.
vibe_condition: The roof is patched when it needs it. The sills are kept sound throughout.
vibe_mood: The mood is vigilant. The house is short of privacy.
vibe_approach: A single house faces the tree. Its back is to the village.
vibe_senses: The floor shifts with the tree's own sway. Insect hum is thick against the wattle walls. A damp mineral smell rises off the mud below the sills. No birdsong carries this close to the tree.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can involve catching a solitary communion. A quest can also involve defending a solitary communion.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 39 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: The house has two of every fitting. The fittings make solitary communion awkward. The house stands within earshot of the tree. Its occupant is not allowed to leave the tree's earshot.

name: Tsoko Camp
why_founding: Tsoko Camp is the delegation camp used during the convocation month. The camp stands empty for the rest of the year.
why_site_advantages: The camp lies four hundred metres from the convocation ground. It stands on the convocation ground's landings.
why_occupants_motive: Delegations occupy the camp in season. Each delegation brings its own cook and its own water. Each delegation has its own account of why its pitch is where it is.
why_pressures: Precedence disputes about pitch positions are an annual institution. The nine-trunks village rents out an overflow pitch. The overflow pitch has begun to outrank the camp's own back rows.
why_would_change_if: A tribe losing its pitch is a real political event. Two pitches have gone unclaimed for three years. No reallocation has been agreed.
vibe_silhouette: The cleared ground is far larger than its shelters. Fire scars from a season ring the ground.
vibe_palette: Numbered posts stand pale in an empty clearing. Tribal signs are worn faint on the wood. Grass overgrows the least-visited pitches.
vibe_materials: Pitch markers are cut once and left standing all year. Shelters are dismantled and stacked above flood height for eleven months. Landing posts are anchored in living root.
vibe_signature_feature: Permanent pitch markers are cut with tribal signs. The markers stand empty eleven months a year. Grass has grown over the less-attended pitches.
vibe_condition: The camp is struck down for eleven months. The delegations rebuild it fast for the convocation.
vibe_approach: The camp is an empty field of numbered posts.
vibe_senses: The open field has no fire and no cooking smell. Wet grass is all that covers the ground. Wind crosses the field unbroken by any tent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can read from the pitches which delegations did not come this season.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 268 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Pitch markers cut with tribal signs stand empty eleven months a year. Grass has grown over the pitches of delegations that stopped coming.

name: The Sap Road Camp
why_founding: The Sap Road Camp serves people who walk to a hero Hist to grieve.
why_site_advantages: The camp has the last water before the grove.
why_occupants_motive: Mourners use the camp in rotation. The mourners mostly do not talk to each other. They leave the camp stocked for the next arrivals. Little else passes between them.
why_pressures: Predators have learned that this camp is quiet and slow. The Agaceph grove will not post a watch. A watched mourning is not a mourning.
why_would_change_if: A killing here would close the road for a season. The Agaceph grove would then receive its mourners by water. The grove does not want those landings used.
vibe_silhouette: The camp is strung out along the road and follows it. Cup-lines are stacked at one end.
vibe_palette: Black water lies under deep shade. Pale peeled root shows at the edge of the camp. Old travel clothes grey on the wall.
vibe_materials: A washing stage is built out over the water for mourners before the grove. Each party that passes rebuilds the chime frame fresh. Gear is stacked and left ready for the next arrivals.
vibe_signature_feature: Mourners clean themselves at a washing stage before they approach the tree. The discarded travel clothes of years hang as a wall.
vibe_condition: Whoever passes through rebuilds the camp each season. Nothing is repaired in the meantime.
vibe_approach: The clothing wall is visible before the camp.
vibe_senses: Chill lifts off the black water at dusk. Voices are kept to what is needed. Damp cloth dries on the wall. The road is quiet once the camp empties.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 353 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'relaxed-score'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.dream-wallow-starblossom (+1.32).
player_purpose_hook: The camp has the last water before the grove. It has a washing stage. The discarded travel clothes of years hang as a wall.

name: The Counting Tower
why_founding: The Counting Tower is a ladder tower built to see over the canopy. The canopy closes over every other vantage.
why_site_advantages: The tower stands on the tallest hammock timber for kilometres.
why_occupants_motive: A watcher from the nearest village serves on rotation. The watcher counts smoke and boats. The watcher reports both counts to the naheesh.
why_pressures: From the ground there is only canopy. The reports from the tower are the district's distant information. The naheesh acts on the tower's reports the same day.
why_would_change_if: If the tree died, the region would lose its sole sightline. The vista ledge that would replace it is a day away. The vista ledge is closing over.
vibe_silhouette: The tower breaks through the canopy. At night, lanterns burn at three heights.
