vibe_palette: Grey timber ladder stages rise pale against the green canopy. Three lantern heights burn amber after dark. A chalked slate shows white at the platform rail. Sap glints on the collecting cups below.
vibe_materials: Six ladder stages are built from the tallest hammock timber available. Rungs are replaced individually as they wear. The platform floor is planked and railed. Whoever is on rotation resurfaces the platform floor. The slate is chalked and wiped. Forty years of entries have been scraped clean and restarted. No metal is used except the lantern fittings.
vibe_signature_feature: Six ladder stages climb a single tree to a platform. The platform has a horizon on it. A slate there records what was seen and when.
vibe_condition: The tower is well-found. The naheesh depends on it daily.
vibe_mood: The mood is functional. The tower is built for the view.
vibe_approach: The tower is invisible until a visitor reaches the trunk itself.
vibe_senses: The ladder sways slightly with every climbing step. Wind at the platform does not reach the ground. A counting voice recites smoke and boat counts under its breath.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 268 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Six ladder stages climb one tree. The slate at the top records what was seen and when. The record on the slate goes back forty years.

name: The Tapping Camp
why_founding: The Tapping Camp holds illicit sap-tappers. They work trees that the tree-minders do not visit.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands between three unattended wild Hist. It stands 17.3 m from the open sea, in coastal lagoon and salt marsh. A boat can get out from the camp.
why_occupants_motive: The tappers sell to a city fence. The tappers are fully aware of what they are doing. They work only wild Hist. No tribe has standing to complain about wild Hist.
why_pressures: The tree-minders have put a bounty on the tappers. The bounty is paid in licence-renewal favour. The tappers of the licensed stage hunt the poachers.
why_would_change_if: One arrest would name the fence. The arrest would unroll the whole trade. The tapped-tree crew use the same buyer under a lapsed concession.
vibe_silhouette: A drying line holds things that should not be dried.
vibe_palette: Green shade lies over the water. Rot-brown thatch drips onto stacked crates. Thin pale sap runs in open pans. A red Hist flower is held high out of reach.
vibe_materials: Root buttress walls are filled in with hide and cut frond. Grass-rope binding is doubled against the damp. Bark-shingle roofing is laid straight over sap seams. Crocodile skulls are nailed above the gate as a warning mark.
vibe_signature_feature: Sap barrels are branded with a city merchant's mark. The barrels are already stencilled for a buyer.
vibe_condition: Outlaws run the camp efficiently. They keep it just tidy enough to move fast.
vibe_approach: The smell of raw sap marks a place where no work should be.
vibe_senses: Raw sap sours where no licence permits the work. Boots sink soft on a floor that gives with the tree's own sway. Tappers argue in low voices over the buyer's price. No chime sounds anywhere in the camp.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 405 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, remote, route.
player_purpose_hook: Sap barrels are already branded with a city merchant's mark. The barrels are stencilled for the buyer. The tappers defend the camp themselves.

name: The Poling Relay
why_founding: The Poling Relay is a relay yard. Interior porters hand off loads there between poling stages.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands where the polable water ends. The walking route begins at the yard.
why_occupants_motive: Porters work at the yard. A yard-keeper takes a cut of each load. The yard-keeper holds the covered store between the water and the walking route.
why_pressures: The yard-keeper's cut is the region's standing grievance. The lizard-steed breeders quote prices that assume the cut.
why_would_change_if: A second yard would break the monopoly. The firm ground for a second yard belongs to the village. That village takes the keeper's rent.
vibe_silhouette: The yard holds stacked loads. Boats and carts are absent from it.
vibe_palette: Green water darkens to brown. Pale loam is threaded with root hair. Amber is set hard in old joints. Blue smoke banks low under the canopy.
vibe_materials: A transfer stage is timbered where the polable water ends. A tariff table is cut directly into the wood. Storage racks are built over older repairs. A covered store stands between the water and the track.
vibe_signature_feature: A load-transfer stage has the tariff cut into the timber. Beside the tariff is a longer list of exemptions.
vibe_condition: The stage sags on the loading side. It is shored there and nowhere else.
vibe_approach: Stacked cargo stands in the middle of nowhere.
vibe_senses: Porters bargain over stacked loads. Resin and turned mud smell at the edge of the yard. The tally-keeper counts loads against a chime frame. Water from the rapid laps the stage all day.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can turn on a weighing. A quest can turn on an Owing. A quest can turn on a hire that went wrong.
why_site_won: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 416 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: Polable water ends here and walking begins. Porters are hired at the stage. The tariff is cut into the timber. A longer list of exemptions stands beside the tariff.

name: The Kept Refuge
why_founding: The Kept Refuge is a shelter maintained on ground that the tribes avoid. The tribes keep it against the day they have to run again. The tribes ran in 4E 48.
why_site_advantages: The refuge stands high and dry. It is deliberately remote. It has one maintained approach.
why_occupants_motive: Two caretakers serve the refuge on an unenvied rotation. The funding tribes draw the caretakers by lot. Each caretaker serves a year. The tribes accept no exemption.
why_pressures: The caretakers rotate the stores. The register of the year the refuge was full is read aloud. The reading happens every Sun's Dusk. Fewer tribes attend the reading each year.
why_would_change_if: Using the refuge would mean that something terrible had happened again. Two funding tribes have let their shares lapse. Neither tribe has said so at the reading.
vibe_silhouette: A maintained structure stands on ground that has every reason to be empty.
vibe_palette: Tea-dark water lies under the canopy's shade. Sap runs treacle-dark into the collecting cups by the door. Churned pale mud marks the one maintained approach. Faded red paint shows on the entry posts.
vibe_materials: A canopy limb is bent down and rooted at both ends. The limb is roofed across the span. Hardwood pegs and withy hold the building together, with no metal. Bark shingle is laid fresh over the store-room roof. Stores are stacked to a marked capacity. The caretakers keep the stores up despite low use.
vibe_signature_feature: A capacity mark on the wall reads 'four hundred and eleven, Sun's Dusk 4E 48'. The caretakers still keep stores for that many.
vibe_condition: The refuge is kept up on a rota. The repairs are small and recent.
vibe_mood: The mood is prepared. The refuge is short of attendance.
vibe_approach: A maintained roof is reached by the one cleared path.
vibe_senses: Heavy wet heat does not lift after dark. A counting voice reads aloud each Sun's Dusk. Otherwise the refuge is silent. The sweet-sour smell of green rot is held under the roof. No straight edge appears anywhere in the building's line.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can recount the stores. The stores are held against a forty-year-old survey. The recount must happen before the next flight needs the stores.
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 215 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route.
player_purpose_hook: A capacity mark on the wall reads four hundred and eleven, Sun's Dusk 4E 48. The stores are still kept for that many.
singular_claim: The countBand is [1,1]. The place is a province-wide refuge of last resort. It is sited in the interior it serves.
reconciliation: The lore associates 'the Refuge' with Deepmire. Zone ownership is to be confirmed before Part 3.

name: The Fallen Nine
why_founding: The gallery began as a trunk root that died. The dead root gave way and collapsed.
why_site_advantages: The gallery lies on a route that people still use. People still dig at the fall because the route passes it.
why_occupants_motive: The gallery is unoccupied. The bone-carriers come once a year. Four families' dead lie under the fall. The dead cannot be recovered and returned to their families.
why_pressures: The route now goes the long way around the fall. The detour costs a day. The porter relay charges for that day.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the fall would restore the route. It would also settle four families' claims. It would cost the relay yard a quarter of its traffic.
vibe_silhouette: The entrance is a slumped sinkhole lip. Old rope is still tied off at the edge. There is no safe way down.
vibe_palette: The passage is black past the entry. The old rope is pale against dark root. Green shows only where light still reaches the mouth.
vibe_materials: Nothing is built here. Packed silt lies over collapsed root and drift timber. The sinkhole lip is slumped, with rope still tied off at the edge. A porter train's load is still buried under two metres of fallen root.
vibe_signature_feature: The gallery collapsed with a porter train inside it. The salvage is still where it fell. It lies behind two metres of root.
vibe_condition: The fall is untouched since it happened. People dig at it only from the outside.
vibe_mood: The place is a collapse with a burial inside it.
vibe_approach: The mouth is slumped. Fern has grown across the old path.
vibe_senses: The air past the entry sits still and close. A cold mineral smell comes off the deep mud. No sound carries back from where the tunnel closed.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 99 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, parent.
player_purpose_hook: A porter train is still under two metres of fallen root with its load. People are still digging toward it.

name: The Severed Branch
why_founding: A cult cell took the gallery. The roots here reach a tree that the cell intends to sever.
why_site_advantages: The gallery is isolated and deep. It connects directly to the cell's target.
why_occupants_motive: Cultists are testing a method of severing. They work from notes that came out of the staging camp. They go back to the staging camp with their results.
why_pressures: The tree above the gallery is beginning to withdraw. The village does not know why the tree is withdrawing. The villagers have begun consulting a tree-minder. The tree-minder will recognise the pattern.
why_would_change_if: Discovery would make the cell move. The cell would lose its notes. The notes are the written account of how a severing is actually attempted.
vibe_silhouette: The entrance is a grave-cut into the bank. The cut is too wide for one body. The approach marks are scrubbed off.
vibe_palette: The root is brown and lit only by carried lamps. Sap has gone dark and stiff along the cut marks. Grey silt dries at the entrance.
vibe_materials: The root walls are cut in a deliberate repeating pattern. The pattern is unlike any natural growth. A single step is cut into the bank for access. Notes are kept dry on a shelf inside.
vibe_signature_feature: An Unbound Root cell has cut the root walls in a deliberate repeating pattern. The cell's notes explain the cuts.
vibe_condition: The cell keeps the entrance deliberately hidden. The cell scrubs the entrance clean of tracks.
vibe_approach: The approach marks at the mouth are scrubbed off.
vibe_senses: Chime notes at the entrance are pitched oddly to test anyone approaching. The smell of rot thickens near the mouth. Low argument is audible from within when work is under way. No natural light reaches past the first turn.
quest_hooks_opportunity: main-quest severance evidence
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 398 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, region, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The root walls are cut in a deliberate pattern. The cell's working notes lie on a shelf beside the walls.

name: The Long Throat
why_founding: The gallery is a single enormous trunk root. The root runs toward the basin.
why_site_advantages: The gallery is the dry way toward the deep basin.
why_occupants_motive: No staff work inside the gallery. A guide camp sits at each end. The two camps keep a tally of everyone entering. The tally tells the far end who to expect.
why_pressures: A party cannot get back past whatever enters behind it. The guides move parties through in one direction only. The guides wait out the day if the tally is wrong.
why_would_change_if: A branch collapse would turn the passage into a trap. A collapse would also cut the basin's deep ground off entirely.
vibe_silhouette: The entrance is a stair-throat of worn root steps going down a ravine wall. The first verse of the counting song is cut beside it.
vibe_palette: The passage is black and lit only by carried lamp. Grey silt dries in cracked plates along one stretch. The first counting verse is cut pale into stone at the mouth. The passage has no other colour for three kilometres.
vibe_materials: The passage is unworked root. No wall is built or repaired along its length. A traveller who reached the end left a single stake-cairn at one point. The counting verse is cut shallow into the stone lip at the entrance. That verse is the single mark made by any hand here. The root is otherwise as it grew.
vibe_signature_feature: The gallery runs three kilometres without a side chamber or a branch. Travellers count paces aloud.
vibe_condition: The gallery is unchanged since it formed. It is unbuilt along its whole length.
vibe_mood: The passage is monotonous. It is long enough to be frightening.
vibe_approach: The mouth lies in a ravine wall. The first verse of the counting song is cut beside it.
vibe_senses: The low ceiling flattens the sound of footsteps. Every traveller murmurs a paced counting song along the passage. The air stays still for the whole length of the gallery.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 562 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The root run is three kilometres long. It has no junction and no side chamber. Travellers count paces aloud. Guides teach them the chant before they set off.

name: The Drowned Stair
why_founding: A root branch grew downhill into the water table.
why_site_advantages: The gallery short-cuts a full day of surface travel. Only a courier who can hold their breath can use it.
why_occupants_motive: The gallery is uninhabited. Divers use it, mostly couriers. A message that takes a day on the surface takes an afternoon. The dive takes four held breaths.
why_pressures: The water rises in the wet season. The rising water drowns the last two landings. For half the year the shortcut is a full dive. The couriers charge double in that half.
why_would_change_if: A dry decade would make the gallery an ordinary road. A dry decade would end a courier trade. Three villages depend on that trade for news.
traversal_fallback: The fallback is to go by boat around the surface route. The boat route takes one day longer.
vibe_silhouette: No part of the gallery is above water. A diver finds the stair by feel. The entrance is made swimming.
vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow light fades to black in the depths. Grey drift-timber is wedged along the walls. The smooth-worn root carries no sap anywhere. Pale marks are cut fresh at each landing.
vibe_materials: The floor and ceiling are both root. Water carves the rest between them. The landing steps are cut and worn smooth by hundreds of passing feet. Grave-poles are driven at the rim. None of them is recent. No lashed or built work lies below the waterline.
vibe_signature_feature: The gallery descends in flooded steps. Each step is a held breath longer than the last. The marks of who got how far are cut at each landing.
vibe_condition: The gallery is passable only in the dry season. The rest of the year it is drowned two landings deep.
vibe_mood: The place is a dive with a tally cut at every landing.
vibe_approach: The mouth lies at water level. Divers enter it swimming.
vibe_senses: Warm air rises strangely from underground. Divers hold their breath four times before the far landing. Sap has gone sour where the root has been cut. Sound is swallowed entirely below the surface.
why_site_won: cove in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 353 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, route; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: A courier is through in an afternoon on four held breaths. The surface route takes a day. The marks of who got how far are cut at each landing.

name: The Underway
why_founding: The gallery is the trunk root under Helstrom. The Waykeepers opened it and keep it as a road. The surface route crosses the deep basin.
why_site_advantages: The gallery goes where no boat can go. No road will be built where it goes.
why_occupants_motive: Waykeepers maintain the passage only as far as their contract runs. They post the paid limit in cut marks at the second junction.
why_pressures: Beyond the second junction the passage is not maintained. People still go beyond it. The Waykeepers have stopped recovering bodies past the second junction. The Waykeepers have not told the assembly.
why_would_change_if: Losing the Waykeepers would close the interior's overland link entirely. Helstrom's escorted water traffic could not absorb the difference.
vibe_silhouette: The entrance is a worked gate in the root wall at the Helstrom line. The gate is lit and guarded. Traffic queues at the gate.
vibe_palette: The passage is black past the lamp's reach. Mud is churned underfoot. Amber is set hard in the root joints. Passing walkers leave red flowers in wall niches.
vibe_materials: The tunnel's own walls are root, black silt and old bone. A maintained gate stands at the Helstrom mouth. Cut marks post the paid limit at the second junction. A traveller who found the way out left a stake-cairn.
vibe_signature_feature: The Waykeepers maintain the floor and hang lights as far as the second junction. The Waykeepers' contract ends at the second junction.
vibe_condition: The floor is laid and lit to the paid limit. Beyond the paid limit there is root and water.
vibe_mood: The passage is comfortable underground. It is unlike the rest of the region.
vibe_approach: The mouth is a worn root mouth at the Helstrom gate. A keeper's post stands there. A written notice states how far the maintenance goes.
vibe_senses: Trapped air presses close and still. Insects sound inside the walls. A rot-sweet smell hangs past the second junction. The passage has no straight line anywhere.
quest_hooks_opportunity: FAST root.helstrom_hub
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 221 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: The gallery is a semi-public road under the marsh. It is floored and lit to the second junction. Past the Waykeepers' cut limit mark the floor is root and water.
siting_note: The gallery's identity is the trunk root under Helstrom. It is bound to Helstrom. An unconstrained plot put it 2.4 km north, by the Stormhold road. The siting binds it back to the city. The siting change is the Round 4 network-role bind.

name: The Kept Light
why_founding: The gallery lies under a hammock that dropped its levee. The water came in from the back and stayed.
why_site_advantages: The run holds chest-deep still water in the dark. One dry shelf lies at the far end. Two mouths open at opposite ends of the run.
why_occupants_motive: Wisps hold a light over the deepest cut. A wader is in leech water before it is halfway to the light.
why_pressures: Two polers from the eastern hamlets have gone in after the light this year. Their rafts are still tied at the root mouth.
why_would_change_if: Cutting the old levee back open would drain the run to ankle depth. The wisps would go when the run drains.
vibe_silhouette: The entrance is a root mouth at water level. Two empty rafts are tied to it.
vibe_palette: Black water lies under one small blue light deep in the run. Brown root walls close overhead. Pale poling gear lies abandoned on the rafts. No colour shows anywhere the light does not reach.
vibe_materials: Living and drowned root together form the gallery walls. Two rafts are tied at the mouth with their poling gear still aboard. A dry shelf at the far end is the only footing in the run. The gallery itself is the sole structure. Nothing else is built here.
vibe_signature_feature: The light sits over a cut where the floor drops away.
vibe_condition: The gallery holds. The levee behind it does not hold.
vibe_approach: The drip carries before the mouth is in sight.
vibe_senses: Dripping water carries far down the flooded run. Standing water has gone sour where the leeches breed. Root creaks as the tide shifts outside. Cold settles fast once the mouth is out of sight.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Recovering the two polers or their gear is a quest opportunity. It gives the eastern hamlets a reason to owe a favour to the person who recovers them.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 574 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'hollow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A blue light is held over deep water. Two empty rafts are tied at the mouth.

name: Lantern Hollow
why_founding: Growers took over the root gallery. They needed dark, damp and constant temperature.
why_site_advantages: The root layer provides dark, damp and constant temperature for free.
why_occupants_motive: The growers are underground by preference. They rarely surface. They sell glowing fungus to every village in the district. They sell through a single agent.
why_pressures: Something else uses the deeper branches. The growers have stopped going to the deeper branches. Their best beds are out of production. The price of the fungus is up.
why_would_change_if: A collapse would end the interior's light supply. The nightbound village uses none of the fungus.
vibe_silhouette: The entrance is a hollow trunk. A fungus-drying rack stands outside it. A tended path leads to it.
vibe_palette: The fungus-lit walls glow pale green. A drying rack shows pale against dark root-brown. Mud-grey banks lie at the entrance.
vibe_materials: The growers fitted out the hollow trunk with drying racks themselves. Fungus beds are cut directly into the root walls. Daily traffic has worn the tended path smooth.
vibe_signature_feature: A small community colonised the gallery. They farm luminous fungus on the root walls. They sell light to the villages above.
vibe_condition: The growers who live there keep the gallery in daily repair.
vibe_approach: A tended path leads to the mouth. A fungus-drying rack stands outside the mouth.
vibe_senses: The warmth is damp and constant, unlike the surface. A faint mushroom smell hangs over standing water. Chimes sound distant down the gallery. Each chime is a little out of tune with the last.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can move the growers' jarred light past the assembly's licences.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 466 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Growers have colonised the gallery. They farm luminous fungus on the root walls. They sell light to every village above them.

name: The Root Talk Ground
why_founding: The Root Talk is an occasional convocation held at Helstrom. The convocation falls in the month of Hist-Tsoko.
why_site_advantages: The ground is an enclosed clearing at the grove's edge. Enclosed clearings like this are rare. The clearing holds every interior delegation and their landings.
why_occupants_motive: The ground stands empty for eleven months in twelve. In the twelfth month the naheesh and tree-minders of the interior sit here. The seating is set by a precedence order that is kept at Helstrom.
why_pressures: Attendance at the Root Talk is falling. The empty places are counted publicly. Two tribes have stopped coming. The two tribes have not been asked why in six years.
why_would_change_if: A convocation that failed to reach alignment would end the institution. The residents of the Hist-less refuge are waiting for that end. The heretic builders are waiting for that end as well.
vibe_silhouette: The ground is very large and cleared. It has permanent stone or root seating, but it has no buildings.
vibe_palette: The pale root is worn to a shine underfoot. Green shade lies overhead. A single red flower is shed and left where it falls.
vibe_materials: Root is trained flat over generations into floor and seating. None of the root is cut. One chime frame stands at the north end. A standing rule forbids building here.
vibe_signature_feature: Generations have worn the root seating into shape. Each tribe's delegation mark is cut where that tribe has sat since the seating was trained. The recently unclaimed marks are obvious.
vibe_condition: The ground is not repaired by hand. Its upkeep comes from growth and custom.
vibe_approach: A worn path runs from the Helstrom gate. The path is a highway for one month a year. The path is a green tunnel for the rest of the year.
vibe_senses: The floor hums when many feet cross the ground at once. The ground is quiet for eleven months of the year. Resin scent from the grove drifts in from the edge. One voice speaks at a time during the convocation.
quest_hooks_opportunity: SCENE root_talk.convocation · LOC many_root.council_grove · LOC many_root.finale_venue
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MR08 · tier-2; LH02 · tier-3; LH04 · tier-3; LH10 · tier-3; LH24 · tier-3; LH53 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 378 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: Each tribe's mark is cut into the root floor. Each tribe has sat on its mark for nine generations. Two of the marks have been unclaimed for six years.
singular_claim: The place has a countBand of [1,1]. The lore fixes the convocation at Helstrom.

name: The Emptied Bore
why_founding: A rootworm dug this bore. The worm died in the bore. The bore was then abandoned.
why_site_advantages: The tunnel is dry, wide and straight. Dry shelter is extremely rare here.
why_occupants_motive: Whatever creature is living in a free tunnel occupies the bore. The occupant changes every season. No village has claimed the bore.
why_pressures: Travellers want to use the bore as shelter. Something is usually in it already. The bore has killed more travellers than the weather ever drove into it.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the bore would give the region a dry way-shelter. The guides have costed the work twice. The guides cannot agree who would own the bore afterwards.
vibe_silhouette: The bore mouth is old and oval where it has slumped. Ferns grow across the opening.
vibe_palette: The mouth is round and dark, fringed with fern. The tunnel walls are brown-black and smoothed to a shine. Pale worm bone fills the last chamber. Old cut marks have gone hard and dark with age.
vibe_materials: The bore is unlined. The worm cut the bore itself. The bore has never been reinforced. Ferns grow unchecked across the collapsed mouth. The worm's skeleton fills the last forty metres. The skeleton is untouched since the worm died there. No shelter work has been added since.
vibe_signature_feature: The worm's skeleton fills the last chamber that it dug. The tunnel stops at that chamber.
vibe_condition: The mouth is slumped shut. Clearing it has not been agreed.
vibe_approach: The bore is a perfectly round dry hole in a bank. It is too neat to be natural.
vibe_senses: Cold air pools at the tunnel floor even in the dry season. Old fern fronds rattle dryly at the entrance. A faint carrion smell never quite clears from the last chamber.
why_site_won: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 264 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, culture-clump; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.umbriel-stripped-quiet (+1.07).
player_purpose_hook: The tunnel is dry, wide and straight. The worm's skeleton fills the last forty metres of it.

name: The Working Burrow
why_founding: A wild rootworm dug this burrow off a trunk root. The Waykeepers watch the burrow. A wild worm can open or close a line.
why_site_advantages: The burrow lies where soft ground meets the root layer. The worm can turn at that point.
why_occupants_motive: A rootworm lives in the burrow. A small scavenger population lives off the worm's spoil. The Waykeepers read this ecology well. They can predict where the worm will turn.
why_pressures: The Waykeepers want the worm moved. The local tribe considers it sacred. The dispute has been at the convocation twice. The convocation gave no ruling.
why_would_change_if: Driving the worm off would open a shorter root line. It would also start an argument that would reach Helstrom.
vibe_silhouette: The burrow mouth is ringed with cut root. The mouth is wider than a gallery. The spoil ridge is still fresh.
vibe_palette: Wet root walls show a lamp-yellow sheen. Freshly turned spoil ridges are pale. Thin sap beads along the tunnel cuts. A single red flower lies crushed flat at the mouth.
vibe_materials: The burrow floor is root that a moving body has packed hard. Water shapes the rest of the burrow. A spoil ridge of turned earth lies loose at the mouth. A stone-and-pole cairn stands where the last person got out. No built structure stands inside.
vibe_signature_feature: Fresh spoil heaps lie outside the mouth. The mouth is wider than any maintained gallery. The rim of the mouth is worn smooth.
vibe_condition: The Waykeepers and the tribe dispute the burrow. It is left as the worm made it.
vibe_mood: The worm is felt through the ground before it is heard.
vibe_approach: The ground shakes at irregular intervals. The shaking begins a long way off.
vibe_senses: The ground trembles before any sound arrives. Turned earth and torn root fill the air. Sap sours where the fresh cuts leak. There is no dry footing near the mouth.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 383 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, danger, parent.
player_purpose_hook: Fresh spoil lies outside a mouth that is wider than any maintained gallery. The worm that dug it can open a line or close one.

name: The Helstrom Line-Head
why_founding: The station is the hub of the rootworm network (root-node.helstrom).
why_site_advantages: The station stands at the Helstrom gate. The trunk roots converge there.
why_occupants_motive: Waykeepers run the station. They run a semi-public service and a restricted one. A paying passenger is not told that the restricted network exists. The register has two columns.
why_pressures: The restricted network is a favour. It is not a service. The Waykeepers guard it as a favour. The tribes of the interior have begun to resent a road whose inside they may not see.
why_would_change_if: Losing the Waykeepers' cooperation closes the interior. The Waykeepers know this. They price accordingly.
vibe_silhouette: The station is a loading platform over a root hollow. The hollow is hidden beneath the platform.
vibe_palette: Green shade lies over tea-dark water. No sap shows on the worked timber. Mud is churned at the loading platform. One red flower is painted on the boarding post.
vibe_materials: The platform is built over the berth below, in a root hollow. Builders used hardwood pegs and withy binding. No metal is used. A boarding stage has a public register. A second, restricted gate stands beside it.
vibe_signature_feature: A worm-berth stands in the root wall. It has a boarding stage and a passenger register. A second gate carries the restricted sign. Most travellers never pass that gate.
vibe_condition: The station was re-lashed this season. The restricted gate is kept separately.
vibe_approach: The station is reached from inside the Underway. It is not reached from the surface.
vibe_senses: A departure chime sounds once as a worm gate opens. Smoke is held low under the platform roof. Register pages turn while names are checked. The restricted side is completely quiet.
quest_hooks_opportunity: FAST rootworm.helstrom
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ23 · tier-0; TG06 · tier-2; LH03 · tier-3; LH12 · tier-3; LH15 · tier-3; LQ07 · tier-3; RW-line · tier-2
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 5), 136 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, bound.
player_purpose_hook: The station is the hub of the rootworm lines. It has a boarding stage and a passenger register. It has a second gate that most travellers never pass.
reconciliation: The place replaces placeholder station 'helstrom' in the compiled root-transit graph.

name: The Bleeding House
why_founding: A Daedric-worked facility was built in the interior. It harvests a Hist industrially. It follows the Haj Uxith pattern.
why_site_advantages: The facility stands on a tree. It does not stand on ground. The building is a machine that wraps around a trunk.
why_occupants_motive: The bargain left something there. That something still works the machine on a schedule. No tribe has authorised anyone to enter the building for six hundred years.
why_pressures: The tree is still alive. It is still connected. Its anguish is felt down the root line. The Agaceph sap-speaker can name the direction of the anguish. The sap-speaker has refused three times.
why_would_change_if: Ending the facility would be the largest thing that the interior has done in a century. The convocation rarely reaches agreement. It would agree to reward this act.
vibe_silhouette: The facility is industrial apparatus on a Hist. The manufacture is not from Tamriel.
vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow light catches wet black stone. Sap-channels stain every wall dark red-brown. One steady red glow shows. It is not a flower. Grey silt coats every floor.
vibe_materials: Dressed stone is fused with worked daedric metal. It is the only metal for a hundred miles. Sap-channels are cut straight into the floor and still run. Root has grown into the machinery. The root died where it touched the machinery. Portable fittings were stripped out long ago. The fixed apparatus was left standing.
vibe_signature_feature: The apparatus is still running, unattended. The sap that it collects has gone the wrong colour.
vibe_condition: The apparatus runs unattended. It has run to its schedule for six centuries.
vibe_approach: The root-hum in this region carries a wrong note for kilometres. The source is found last.
vibe_senses: Warm air rises off the tree-body and carries its sap-scent. A mechanical drip keeps time too evenly to be natural. Sap turns sour and then metallic near the collecting vats. There is no chime and no birdcall. The only sound is the machine's own working.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 449 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, remote, region.
player_purpose_hook: A Daedric machine is wrapped round a living Hist. The machine still runs to its schedule. It has stood unattended for six hundred years.
singular_claim: The place has a countBand of [1,1]. An enslaved-Hist facility only makes sense inside the Hist forest.
complexity_justification: The place is a signature D5 site. It has geometry, dressing and a single occupant stratum.

name: The Licensed Stage
why_founding: Tappers tap sap under licence to the tree-minders' rule. The rule allows one stage, one season, one tree.
why_site_advantages: The assembly designated the tree for tapping.
why_occupants_motive: Tappers work here. Their licence is their livelihood. They police poachers themselves. An unpoliced district loses its licences entirely.
why_pressures: The licence is renewed annually. The objection comes most reliably from the tribe whose tree carried the stage the previous year.
why_would_change_if: A lost licence would be worth violence. The last holder to lose one now sells to the same city fence as the poachers.
vibe_silhouette: Tap lines and vessels hang on a great tree. A track is worn to the tree from one direction only.
vibe_palette: Sap-dark tap lines show against pale bark. A weathered licence is hung to catch the light. One worn track leads to the stage.
vibe_materials: A single tapping stage is built to the assembly's own rule. The licence is nailed up, countersigned and weathered. Hardwood pegs and withy hold the stage together. The stage uses no metal.
vibe_signature_feature: The licence is nailed to a single tapping stage. The licence is weathered and countersigned. It is hung to be readable from the water.
vibe_condition: The stage is kept correct. The licence depends on the stage.
vibe_approach: The stage is correctly placed, as one stage on a healthy tree.
vibe_senses: The air is still over the tapping platform. Sap smells sweet where it has just been cut. Wear on the boards is concentrated in the same few footfalls.
why_site_won: Pinned by the Part 6 meso siting (world/sources/blueprints/place.hist-heartland.sap-tapping-licensed.json): The bank above the head of reach 118. Anchor ground 31.20 m, flood band 0, buildable 59% of the 150 m disc; every parcel stands dry: stage 30.67 m, stair 31.38 m, cart 31.20 m, mule line 31.27 m, hut 32.65 m, licence board 30.81 m. Road 526 m to the south-west. Canopy closure 1.00; concealment 0.74. The camp keeps this bank. Its landing stands elsewhere. The water at the foot of the camp is an 882 m2 pocket bounded x 3327-3433, z 4453-4507, connected to nothing, on a reach that falls 6.3% over 463 m, so a canoe floating there can go nowhere. The berth moved 357 m on bearing 201 to (3309.4, 4815.0), the head of the tide, which the recipe's satellite slot already asks for at 200 to 400 m. See dossier licensed-stage-layby.
player_purpose_hook: The rule allows one stage, one season, one tree. The licence is nailed up, weathered and countersigned. It is readable from the water.

name: Miredance
why_founding: The sap-touched left together in one season. They walked out in the slow shared rhythm that they had kept for years.
why_site_advantages: The root system of the overflow pool had hollowed a gallery beneath the huts. The dancers only ever lived on top of the gallery.
why_occupants_motive: No household is kept here now. Creatures that came for the standing water moved into the root galleries. The creatures have not been driven out.
why_pressures: The tap-lines above ground still run when sap flows from the tree. They feed the pool. Whatever lives below is drawn to the pool.
why_would_change_if: If the overflow dried, the gallery would dry with it. The gallery would lose whatever nests there now.
vibe_silhouette: Sagging tap-line staging stands over a black root-mouth. The huts used to stand where the staging is.
vibe_palette: Green shade has gone to black mould over standing water. Sap dried black over the old tap cuts. No other colour is left.
vibe_materials: Grafted limbs collapsed where the joints gave way. Tap-lines still sag above the pool. Drums hang at the stage, split with damp.
vibe_signature_feature: The drums are still hung at the tap-lines. The drums are split and swollen with damp.
vibe_condition: The site is abandoned above ground. The gallery below is undisturbed.
vibe_approach: The drums used to carry before the huts came into view. Now the drums are heard only at the root-mouth.
vibe_senses: Cold air rises out of the root-mouth below. A drumbeat is heard only at the mouth and never above. Standing sap has gone sour. The frog-pipe is not heard anywhere near the pool.
why_site_won: enclosed clearing in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 488 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The sap-touched left here in one season. Something else has since taken the hollow root gallery under the huts.
singular_claim: The place has a countBand of [1,1]. It requires a hero Hist's overflow. Only the heartland has an overflow to spare.

name: Xal-Ussep
why_founding: Xal-Ussep is a xanmeer that was sealed with its tribe's Hist inside it. The Hist has been alone since the Duskfall.
why_site_advantages: Xal-Ussep stands on firm ground in tropical jungle, 7.8 m from swamp water. The xanmeer was never opened.
why_occupants_motive: Only the Hist tree lives inside Xal-Ussep. The tree has not touched the collective since the Duskfall. The tree may not know that the Duskfall has ended.
why_pressures: A whole tribe watches Xal-Ussep. None of its members has ever been inside. The watch post holds that tribe together now.
why_would_change_if: Opening Xal-Ussep would release or kill a Hist that has been isolated for an age. It is the nearest thing to a test of whether a tree can be cut off from the collective and live.
vibe_silhouette: Xal-Ussep is a small, entirely intact stepped meer. It has a single stair-throat. Warm air comes out of the stair-throat.
vibe_palette: The stone is dressed grey and is unweathered by the centuries. A single bright green thread of root runs through a crack in the wall. Gold light with no fire source shows deep inside the stair. Dark unlit chambers lie beyond the seal.
vibe_materials: The quarried stone was sealed at every joint on the day the meer was shut. No joint has been reopened since. A living trunk has grown against the inside of the chamber ceiling. A root pushes three metres through the outer wall. The stone doors are still seated true. No repair has ever been made, because none has been needed.
vibe_signature_feature: A living Hist is sealed inside the stone. The trunk has grown into the chamber's ceiling. A root has come out through the wall. Three metres of tree are visible from outside.
vibe_condition: Xal-Ussep has been sealed since the Duskfall. It has never been opened or repaired.
vibe_mood: The meer is sealed and warm. A presence inside answers a visitor.
vibe_approach: The root through the wall shows that Xal-Ussep is not an empty ruin.
vibe_senses: Warm air breathes steadily out of a stair that should hold no heat. A low resonant hum is felt through the stone floor before it is heard. Total silence holds here, where every other xanmeer carries some sound.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can reach the sealed Hist or keep it sealed. A quest can also bring the questing party before the watch for trying.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 456 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: A living Hist has been sealed inside stone since the Duskfall. Three metres of its root come out through the wall.
reconciliation: Xal-Ussep is among the 2–3 living sealed Hist allowed province-wide. Its neighbours must claim at most two more living sealed Hist.

name: The Coiling Reach
why_founding: The Coiling Reach is a reach where the big snakes den in the root banks.
why_site_advantages: The root banks are warm and sit above the flood line. Those are the conditions that snakes need for a den.
why_occupants_motive: Giant snakes live here. Hunters take them for hide. The daril fermentary sets the hunting season. The snakes do not set it.
why_pressures: Snake hide is worth enough that hunters keep coming and keep dying. The daril fermentary buys venom from the same reach. A bad year hits both the hide trade and the venom trade.
why_would_change_if: Overhunting would clear the reach of snakes in a decade. The daril fermentary has begun keeping its own stock against that day.
vibe_silhouette: Shed skins hang at a size that halts an approach.
vibe_palette: Green fades to blue-grey in standing mist. Pale shed skins drape high in the branches. The amber has long since drained from the buckets. A red flower lies flattened in a drag mark.
vibe_materials: Repeated denning has warmed and hollowed the root banks. The turning of heavy coils has polished the floor smooth. The hunters' rope stands are lashed to the nearest firm trunk. A single old totem marks the edge of the range.
vibe_signature_feature: Sloughed skins hang in the branches. Hunters left them there as range markers.
vibe_condition: Hunters work the reach every season for hide. At other times the snakes hold the reach as they please.
vibe_approach: The skins first.
vibe_senses: Musk and dry skin hang thick in the warm air. Leaf litter ferments underfoot, sweet and sharp. A long hiss carries further than any bird call. The stillness breaks when a coil shifts.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 32 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, danger.
player_purpose_hook: Sloughed skins hang in the branches as range markers. The skins show the size that the snakes reach.

name: The Swallow
why_founding: The root mat over an old channel void gave way here in a single night. The marsh has not filled the hollow.
why_site_advantages: The collapse has stayed open. The ground is firm enough to hold a rim. It does not slump into the hollow.
why_occupants_motive: A creature in the hollow hunts by dropping. The rim is fenced. The fence stakes point outward.
why_pressures: The tribes fence the rim. Something breaks the fence from the inside every year. The fence has been rebuilt eleven times.
why_would_change_if: A second collapse would open the hollow into the root layer below. The Waykeepers' second junction lies directly beneath it.
vibe_silhouette: The Swallow shows as a rim with a change in vegetation around it.
vibe_palette: Green thins to black at the rim. The loam is dark and laced with pale hair-roots. Amber is crusted old at the edges. Charcoal streaks mark the pale wood.
vibe_materials: The rim is fenced with driven stakes that face outward. A rope ladder is rigged and cut short at four metres. A single totem stands at the fence line and has not been renewed for years.
vibe_signature_feature: The rim is fenced. A rope ladder is rigged and then cut off at four metres.
vibe_condition: The fence has been rebuilt eleven times. Each rebuild came from the same side.
vibe_approach: The fence is found first. The hollow is visible only from the rim.
vibe_senses: Cold rises from the black drop below. Birdsong is absent right at the rim. Leaf litter ferments thick enough to taste. The footing is uncertain on ground that has slumped before.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 510 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The rim is fenced. A rope ladder is rigged and then cut off at four metres. The fence stakes point outward.

name: Sleeps-In-The-Ring
why_founding: The tribe kept a hundred-year vigil over a hist that had gone to sleep. The village was built in a ring around a xanmeer that is older than the vigil.
why_site_advantages: Sleeps-In-The-Ring stands on firm ground, 5.5 m from a lagoon. The rise was defensible and dry. The tribe did not ask what lay under the rise.
why_occupants_motive: A presence that slept under the xanmeer woke enough to be noticed. The village had waited ninety years for its own tree to wake. The villagers left in a single night, when something else woke instead.
why_pressures: The hatchery pool goes unswept. The stair-throat down into the xanmeer has been open since the village was left.
why_would_change_if: The presence that woke below must sleep again or be killed. Only then could the tribe live in the ring again.
vibe_silhouette: A ring of collapsed roofs surrounds a stair-throat. The stair-throat is sunk into old xanmeer stone.
vibe_palette: Tea-black water has gone grey under thin canopy. Amber sap has dried hard and dark on the collapsed roofs. Pale xanmeer stone shows at the stair mouth. There is no red anywhere in the ring.
vibe_materials: Root-braided walls have fallen in on each other around the ring. Xanmeer stone is exposed at the stair. Hands older than the vigil dressed the stone. Sap-resin caulk has cracked open at every seam. The hatchery pool still holds water. Its rim is unrepaired.
vibe_signature_feature: The hatchery pool is still full. Its sweeping stopped in the middle of a pattern.
vibe_condition: The ring collapsed decades back. The stair below stays clear.
vibe_mood: The place is still. The stair below is open.
vibe_approach: The village's noise carries further than its size explains. The noise drops away as the ring is approached.
vibe_senses: Cold air rises steadily out of the open stair. Boards give underfoot wherever they still hold. The village's noise carries further than its size explains, then drops away. There is no birdcall and no chime anywhere in the ring.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 637 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The hatchery pool is still swept in a half-finished pattern. The stair-throat under the ring has been open since the night when the villagers left.

name: The Hollow House
why_founding: One household lives in a xanmeer antechamber because the antechamber was empty and dry.
why_site_advantages: The stone floor is dry and above the flood. Dry floors are the scarce good in the region.
why_occupants_motive: The household is a family with no tribe. The family does not intend to explain itself. The family trades at the walkway junction. The family has never been to the village that tends the ruin.
why_pressures: The tribe that tends the xanmeer knows about the family and has not decided what to do. Evicting the family would mean admitting that the antechamber was habitable.
why_would_change_if: A decision either way ends the arrangement. A ruling that squatting is trespass would apply equally to the fort-dwelling tribe two days east.
vibe_silhouette: A wisp of hearth smoke comes out of a ruin. The tending tribe has closed that ruin.
vibe_palette: Hearth smoke shows pale against dark stone. A carved niche is undamaged. Brown floodwater mirrors the walls.
vibe_materials: A cooking hearth is fitted into a carved offering niche without cutting the niche. The xanmeer stonework is structurally untouched. A different hand cut the doorway. The doorway is now pegged with a chime frame.
vibe_signature_feature: A cooking hearth is built into a carved offering niche. The carving is carefully undamaged.
vibe_condition: One family keeps the house tidy. The family has no claim to the ground.
vibe_approach: Smoke comes out of a ruin that should be empty.
vibe_senses: Smoke rises from a closed ruin where none should. The stone floor stays dry when everything around it floods. The household keeps quiet enough to be missed at a glance.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 76 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: One household cooks in a carved offering niche without damaging the carving. The household trades with whoever passes the door.

name: The Standing Thing
why_founding: What the Standing Thing is and who made it are unknown. The local tribes tell four incompatible stories about it.
why_site_advantages: Vegetation has grown around the Standing Thing without touching it.
why_occupants_motive: None of the four tribes has ever posted a custodian. A presence below the stone has kept the two-metre circle clear without help.
why_pressures: Two of the four stories are politically useful and are being pushed. One story makes the stone Ayleid, which would open a dig. Another story makes it pre-Duskfall Argonian, which would close a dig for good.
why_would_change_if: An authoritative answer would disappoint three of the four stories. The Helstrom assembly has declined to hear the question three times.
vibe_silhouette: The object is unmistakably made. It is unmistakably wrong for its surroundings.
vibe_palette: Worked grey stone stands against a quarter-mile of reed. A single red flower lies on the stone. Churned mud lies at the circle's edge.
vibe_materials: A single dressed stone stands, unlike anything quarried nearby. A scatter of totems lies at the rim and has been untouched since the last flood. There is no roof, no wall and no second stone.
vibe_signature_feature: Vegetation stops dead at a two-metre radius around the stone. It has done so since the grave-singers began keeping the count.
vibe_condition: The stone is unclaimed and untended. It holds only as long as the next season allows.
vibe_mood: The stone is unexplained. The circle stays clear.
vibe_approach: A circle of bare earth lies in country that grows over a cut in a season.
vibe_senses: Ground is bare here, where growth returns to any other cut within a season. An old chime frame is left unclaimed. Ash mixed with sap lies at the circle's edge. No sound carries from directly overhead.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can settle one of the four incompatible stories. A quest can also leave all four standing.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 653 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: The ground stays bare two metres out. It has been so since the grave-singers began counting. A stair leads down inside the circle.

name: Two-Poles
why_founding: Two-Poles is a hamlet-turned-village on a shallow flat. The flat floods to the floor twice a year. The village is rebuilt each time.
why_site_advantages: The shallow flat has good fishing and no competition.
why_occupants_motive: The families have decided that the rebuild is cheaper than moving. They have made the rebuild a rite. It takes three days with the whole village present.
why_pressures: The floods are getting deeper. The piles are getting longer. The timber now comes from the hammock village, which charges for it.
why_would_change_if: Two bad years running would end the village. The households have not agreed where they would go. The firm ground nearby is a rise that is already fully occupied.
vibe_silhouette: Two mooring poles stand well out from a short pile line. They are visible before the village is.
vibe_palette: Two bare mooring poles stand pale against brown water. Root-scarred pile stumps from earlier villages ring the current one. Fish-scale silver shows on the drying racks. Red flower petals darken on wet boards.
vibe_materials: Piles are driven fresh after every flood. The shortest stumps from four earlier rebuilds stay standing as markers. Walls are split cane lashed with new withy each season. Roofs are re-thatched from reed cut at the flat itself. Nothing here is older than the last flood, by design.
vibe_signature_feature: Pile stumps from four earlier villages stand around the current one in the shallows. The stumps read like a diagram of the village's own history.
vibe_condition: The village is rebuilt as a rite. Each flood brings three days of work.
vibe_approach: The old stumps read as a ruin from the water. The living village is behind them.
vibe_senses: Fish and wet cane scent every board. The whole structure rocks gently underfoot with the current. A frog-pipe is practised somewhere under the piles.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can go down into what each of the four earlier villages left.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH54 · tier-3; LH55 · tier-3; LH56 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 380 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: Pile stumps from four earlier villages stand around the current one in the shallows. The village is rebuilt in three days after every flood.

name: Ux-Aneet
why_founding: Ux-Aneet is a working village on the channel that carries Helstrom's traffic.
why_site_advantages: The channel edge has a bed firm enough to pile. The bank is high enough for landing.
why_occupants_motive: Polers and provisioners live in Ux-Aneet. They live off passing convoys. Helstrom's escort schedule sets their margins.
why_pressures: The convoys are escorted and often pass without stopping. The escorts prefer Greenspring, which has cleaner water. Greenspring's tribe flatters the escorts.
why_would_change_if: A change in the escorted route would empty Ux-Aneet in two years. The village has begun courting the pilgrim traffic as a hedge.
vibe_silhouette: A long low deck follows one channel bend. All the huts stand on the outside of the curve.
vibe_palette: Brown channel water reflects green overhang. Pale root-wood decking is worn silvery at the edges. Red flower petals are trodden soft into the boards. White bone charms hang at eye height.
vibe_materials: Stilt piles of root are grown deliberately round the older frame. Withy lashing is renewed on every joint each wet season. The patched frond roofing has not been repaired since the last storm. Forty tin chimes hang, with a single chime to each door.
vibe_signature_feature: Every house has its own landing ladder. Every house has its own toll board. The toll boards disagree with each other.
vibe_condition: Working polers keep the village solid. It is defended mostly by being hard to reach.
vibe_approach: From the water, a line of ladders runs down the channel at head height.
vibe_senses: Brackish water slaps the pilings underneath. Boat poles knock against tie-rails at the landing. Forty small chimes ring at once in a gust. Bargaining voices are pitched over toll prices.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can turn on a carrier who is charged four ways at four landings.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LH57 · tier-3; LH58 · tier-3; LH59 · tier-3
why_site_won: open water in interior swamp (danger band 5), 520 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region.
player_purpose_hook: Every house on the bend has its own landing ladder and toll board. Prices are agreed before a boat is tied.

name: The Tsoko Stones
why_founding: The Tsoko Stones are the reckoning by which the interior learns that Hist-Tsoko has come. The convocation is called from that reckoning.
why_site_advantages: The stones stand in a clearing. The clearing has a sightline to a gap in the canopy. The gap admits the light that the reading needs.
why_occupants_motive: Two readers keep the reckoning and the assembly at Helstrom appoints both readers. The two readers must agree. The agreement rule was added after one reader's error moved a convocation by a month.
why_pressures: The canopy has grown and the sightline is closing. The reading is disputed. The tribes that dispute the reading are the ones that would prefer not to attend.
why_would_change_if: A failed reading would postpone the convocation. Cutting the canopy to save the sightline is itself a contested act.
vibe_silhouette: The place is a formal stone arrangement on open ground. The open ground lies exposed to the sky.
vibe_palette: The forest around the clearing is black-green. A lit gap in the canopy opens overhead. Root-wood is silvered with wet. The worked stone is pale and kept bare of growth. White bone is set at eye height.
vibe_materials: The readers clear the worked stone by hand each season. Axes cut a corridor through the canopy and keep it open. A chime hangs at the approach and has been left untuned since the last dispute.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone ring has its sightline through a maintained gap in the canopy. The Tsoko Stones are the sole place in the interior where trees are cut to keep a view of the sky.
vibe_condition: The gap in the canopy narrows faster than the readers can reach agreement about it.
vibe_approach: A corridor is cut through the forest. A stone stands at the end of the corridor.
vibe_senses: Cold air settles on the open ground after dark and two readers argue at the clearing's edge. Trees cut back too often give thin, watery sap. Silence holds directly under the sightline.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can turn on a reading that has stopped matching the season.
why_site_won: summit in firm lowland (danger band 5), 151 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, route.
player_purpose_hook: The convocation is called from what comes through the gap in the canopy. The canopy is closing the gap and the two readers disagree.
singular_claim: countBand is [1,1]. The convocation calendar is a single province-wide institution. The calendar belongs at its convocation.

name: The Topmost Chamber
why_founding: A xanmeer subsided into a lake. One chamber stayed above water.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer sank straight down. Its top terrace is a dry island.
why_occupants_motive: Divers work the xanmeer. The living treasure-hunters' outfit, a day away, finances the divers on shares.
why_pressures: Below the first chamber the work needs breath and light. The outfit has lost two divers because it will not admit that the second chamber is beyond its divers.
why_would_change_if: A drawdown year would open two more chambers. The opened chambers would start a rush to loot them. The pilgrims who keep the rota of the pilgrim-tended terrace would have no standing to stop the rush.
vibe_silhouette: From outside, the place is a terrace corner breaking the surface. From above the water it can also be a geometric shadow under the surface.
vibe_palette: The stone shows no colour until lamplight falls on it. Amber is crusted pale on the dry room's sill. Black leaf-litter is banked in the dry corner. Green water light rises through the open doorway below.
vibe_materials: Burnt root-wood framing is black on the outside and sound inside. Grass-rope lashings are doubled and left fraying. Sap was poured hot into the joints long ago and still stands proud of the surface, but paint marks are redone yearly where carving would have gone.
vibe_signature_feature: One dry room has a doorway that goes straight down into clear water. In good light the whole drowned building is visible below.
vibe_condition: One room stays dry by luck. Water has taken the rest.
vibe_approach: The place is a stone box standing alone in a lake.
vibe_senses: The air is still and held tight in the dry room and smoke smell stays under the canopy outside all day. Cold rises through the open doorway from the water below. The drowned structure shows no straight line anywhere.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 263 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, danger.
player_purpose_hook: The doorway of the dry room goes straight down into clear water. The outfit working the xanmeer has lost two divers below the first chamber.

name: Xal-Irasotl
why_founding: Xal-Irasotl is the xanmeer of the tribe that still lives beside it. The tribe has maintained it as a monument since the Duskfall.
why_site_advantages: Xal-Irasotl stands on the tribe's own ground. That ground is why the xanmeer survived.
why_occupants_motive: Tenders sweep and repair the xanmeer. The tenders turn looters away from it. The tenders keep a duty roster that is the tribe's oldest continuous institution.
why_pressures: Treasure hunters do not accept that maintenance means ownership. The living outfit nearby has twice offered the tribe a share to look away.
why_would_change_if: A generation that stopped tending would turn the xanmeer into a dungeon. That is what happened to the subsumed meer, two days west.
vibe_silhouette: The terraced massing is kept clear of growth to the top course. The approach is swept. Every door stands shut.
vibe_palette: The terraces are swept grey stone. Cut stone shows pale against green banks. Fresh offerings lie at every level.
vibe_materials: The terraced stonework is kept clear of growth to the top course and every stair has been maintained under a duty roster since the Duskfall. Grave-poles stand in an unbroken line. The nearest water, a sloped-rapid reach, lies 131.6 m away.
vibe_signature_feature: Swept steps and offerings lie on every terrace. Every stone is in place.
vibe_condition: The place is swept and maintained under the tribe's oldest roster.
vibe_mood: The mood is reverent. Trespass here is a real offence.
vibe_approach: The approach is swept stone. It comes after a week of mud.
vibe_senses: Swept stone lies underfoot after a week of surrounding mud. Sound is deadened at the site more than in the marsh around it. Smoke from tending fires is held under the canopy.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 50 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The ruin is visibly maintained. The tribe beside it keeps a sweeping roster that is older than any other institution of the tribe.
reconciliation: Lore sources place Xal Irasotl near Hutan-Tzel/Rockguard. The agent that owns that village must be confirmed.

name: The Swept Terrace
why_founding: The Swept Terrace is a xanmeer with no surviving tribe. Pilgrims on the way to Helstrom keep it.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer stands near the pilgrim route to Helstrom. The route lies 110.4 m away.
why_occupants_motive: The xanmeer has no owner. Strangers keep a rota and will never meet each other. Each stranger does a half-day's work because the last one did.
why_pressures: The rota is slipping. The lower terraces are going back to the marsh. This follows the falling pilgrim traffic, which the sap road camp also reports.
why_would_change_if: A tribe claiming the xanmeer would end the arrangement. The tribe would probably improve the building. No tribe will claim it, because the claim implies that the dead here are theirs.
vibe_silhouette: The place is a stepped meer. The vegetation is cut back only on the pilgrim face. The rest is overgrown.
vibe_palette: The pale meer stone is swept clean on one face. Green marsh reclaims the rest. A red flower is shut in the morning.
vibe_materials: Charred timber is still solid under the blackened face. Whoever passes replaces cord lashings at every joint. A door jamb is carved with three hundred years of names.
vibe_signature_feature: Successive pilgrims carved a tending rota down one door jamb. Three hundred years of names stand in a column.
vibe_condition: The place is kept only as far as the rota still reaches. The kept area thins each year.
vibe_approach: The approach is half-swept. The upper terraces are clean. The lower terraces are green.
vibe_senses: Heat holds through the night on the swept terraces. The mineral smell of deep mud rises from the lower steps. No chime frame is fixed to the swept face and footsteps are the sole sound underfoot.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can restore a stage that was cut out of the carved rota.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 110 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform.
player_purpose_hook: Three hundred years of pilgrims have carved their tending rota down one door jamb. The names of the last twenty years are thinner.

name: The Cut Circle
why_founding: The hall is a stilt hall built for a village that did not grow. People who wanted a room where two hundred could sit uncounted took it over.
why_site_advantages: The hall stands on piles at the lagoon's edge over deep still water. One pile-walk leads in from the land. The hall is wide enough to seat a congregation but has no door onto a street.
why_occupants_motive: The Unbound Root preach here openly. They preach to people who arrive believing something milder than what will be asked of them.
why_pressures: Preaching in public is how the cult recruits. It is also how the cult will eventually be found. The congregation is not the cell, but most of the congregation does not know this.
why_would_change_if: One arrest in the middle of a sermon empties the hall for good. Two hundred people would then have to say what they heard.
vibe_silhouette: The place is one long hall on piles over open water. The hall is lit from inside. A single causeway runs out to it.
vibe_palette: The timber is unpainted grey and warm lamplight slats through split cane walls. Black open water lies beneath the floor. The cut root lies pale the length of the hall.
vibe_materials: The hall is unornamented pile and plank construction with split cane walls left free of paint and carving, built for a village that never grew into it. Two hundred people sitting in the same places each sermon wear the floor smooth. The congregation replaces the cut root each season and never otherwise marks it.
vibe_signature_feature: The cut root lies the length of the hall where an altar would stand. The congregation replaces it each season.
vibe_condition: The hall is kept plain and clean. The cult never lets it show the congregation's size.
vibe_mood: The room is full. It goes quiet when the door opens.
vibe_approach: The causeway is the sole approach. The watch counts each arrival along it.
vibe_senses: Lamp smoke is thick under the low roof. Footsteps sound on the causeway's boards as the watch tallies who enters. The breathing of two hundred people fills a room built for far fewer.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Two hundred people half-agree with the cult. The man who runs the cult is in the room among them.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 585 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The cult's own sermon is open to anyone arriving as a believer. The Collector preaches at the front, unmasked.

name: The Last Camp
why_founding: The Last Camp is an expedition camp. Its expedition did not return from the xanmeer that it was working.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands three hundred metres from a sealed xanmeer. It stands on dry ground. The second expedition will camp here too.
why_occupants_motive: The dead expedition and its notes remain in the camp.
why_pressures: The notes are accurate up to the point where they stop. The living outfit has been trying to buy the notes from whoever brings them out.
why_would_change_if: A second expedition using the notes would get further. The last page of the notes warns against doing so, in the writer's own hand.
vibe_silhouette: The camp is still standing. The tents are grey. A spoil heap has gone green.
vibe_palette: Silt-white light filters green over the canvas, which has gone grey. Pale root-wood crates are stacked and dry. No sap lies near the tents and red paint has faded on the marker posts.
vibe_materials: Burnt root-wood staking is driven into firm ground. The tents are oiled cloth, still pitched taut. A spoil heap of dug earth has gone green with moss and grave-poles are set in a line at the water's edge.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp is intact, stocked and undisturbed. The parties that were sent to recover it did not return.
vibe_condition: The dead expedition closed the camp up properly. It has stood untouched since.
vibe_approach: Tents still stand a season after they should have been struck.
vibe_senses: Canvas stirs in a wind that never quite stops. Damp paper and ink smell rises from ledgers that were left open. Smoke is long cold in a dead firepit and the stillness does not match that of a working camp.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 574 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent.
player_purpose_hook: The camp is stocked, closed up properly and never reopened. The notes inside are accurate up to the page where they stop.

name: Fortune's Own
why_founding: Fortune's Own is a working treasure-hunting outfit. Its licence comes from no authority that the interior recognises.
why_site_advantages: The camp is central to three unopened sites. It stands on a channel that takes a boat out.
why_occupants_motive: The hunters hire, trade, cheat or race whoever else is looking, depending on the day. Backers on the coast finance the hunters. The hunters answer to no tribe in the interior.
why_pressures: The tended-xanmeer tribes consider the hunters criminals and are correct. The outfit's answer has been to work drowned sites, where no tribe has a tender.
why_would_change_if: A big find would break the outfit up in an argument. Two of the six hunters already have a buyer of their own on the coast.
vibe_silhouette: The camp has no economic reason to be where it is. The reason is visible in a fresh spoil heap.
vibe_palette: Brown floodwater doubles the green above it. Grey silt dries into cracked plates. Tool handles are dark and glassy with resin from handling and no red flowers grow near the diggings.
vibe_materials: Cut poles and bent saplings are lashed for one season's stay and fresh withy is laid over older bindings. Matting is kept dry for sleeping only. A find board is chalked with sites and crossings-out.
vibe_signature_feature: A find board lists three sites, two crossed out. Beside it stands a running tally of shares owed. Two of the four partners dispute the tally.
vibe_condition: The camp is usable and no better. It is built for one dig at a time.
vibe_approach: Visitors arrive by boat. An awning stands over the landing. An argument is audible from the water.
vibe_senses: An argument over shares carries from the water. Cut root and sawdust smell rises after rain and talk breaks off while the hunters check a passing boat. No chime hangs in camp and none of the party can tune a chime.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 5), 157 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: The outfit will hire, race or sell the same map twice, depending on the day. The find board has three sites on it, two of them crossed out.

name: Nothing-Left
why_founding: Nothing-Left was a village under Umbriel's track in 4E 48. Umbriel took the organic matter. The buildings were left.
why_site_advantages: The village stood under the track that Umbriel took.
why_occupants_motive: The village is unpeopled. The dead did not stay there. The walking village in the deep swamp differs on this. The local theology is mostly about why.
why_pressures: The neighbouring villages will not use the ground or the timber. The timber is good, seasoned and standing. The neighbouring villages have taken no plank.
why_would_change_if: The village stays unbuilt. The heretic builders asked about the stone footings. Four tribes refused them at once.
vibe_silhouette: The village stands intact with no bodies in it.
vibe_palette: The water is clear brown, paling to green above. Grey drift-timber stands stacked untouched at the fence line. Amber pools hard in the root joints. Faded red paint marks the posts.
vibe_materials: The frames are burnt root-wood, black outside and still sound inside. Split cane lashings are left in place, unused. The layered frond roofing should have rotted and has not. Xanmeer stone offcuts are stacked by the fence, unquarried.
vibe_signature_feature: The village is complete and undamaged. It holds no organic material at all, with no thatch, no rope, no bodies and no plants inside the fence line. A century has passed since Umbriel came.
vibe_condition: The village has stood untouched for a century. The timber is good and has not been taken.
vibe_mood: The village feels sterile. The ground inside the fence is dead.
vibe_approach: The village looks inhabited from a distance.
vibe_senses: Root-hum carries clearer than it should through the empty structures. Insect noise is loud against the silent wattle walls. The sweet-sour rot smell is absent where it should be strongest. Footsteps give back too sharply off the stripped ground.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 344 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.rootworm-burrow-dead (+1.07).
player_purpose_hook: The village looks inhabited from the water. Inside the fence there is no thatch, no rope and no bodies. A century has passed since Umbriel came.

name: Umpholo
why_founding: Umpholo is a Maran mission. Its priests died of swamp rot within a month of arriving. The last book was gone by 3E 399.
why_site_advantages: The mission stands on a stone outcrop. The outcrop is why a shell of the mission survives.
why_occupants_motive: The mission has stood empty for two centuries. The interior tribes will not use the outcrop. They hold that stone that killed foreigners will kill them too.
why_pressures: The mission decays into the marsh at a measurable rate. Antiquarians from Gideon have begun asking for the last book. The last book left in 3E 399 and has not been traced.
why_would_change_if: A claim on the mission would change it. The squatters two days west have noticed that the stone building is unheld.
vibe_silhouette: The compound has an intact gate. The path to the compound shows no wear.
vibe_palette: The walls are chalk-pale plaster. The open canopy lets in too much light. The altar is bare of colour.
vibe_materials: The compound is Imperial timber frame and lime plaster. It sinks unevenly into marsh ground. The roof timbers are long gone. The altar is left standing. No Argonian work stands anywhere on the compound.
vibe_signature_feature: The chapel is empty and stone. It has decayed for two hundred years. The roof timbers are gone and the altar is in place. A tree grows where the congregation stood.
vibe_condition: The mission has been left to rot for two centuries. No tribe has claimed it.
vibe_approach: Straight Imperial masonry runs through the trees.
vibe_senses: A dry rot smell is out of place in wet country. The boards give a hollow echo with no earth packed behind them. An unnatural quiet lies where roots have not taken hold.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 76 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.dream-wallow-sap-pool (+0.66).
