player_purpose_hook: The last book left in 3E 399. Antiquarians in Gideon are still asking after it. The chapel it left is half decayed.
singular_claim: The singular claim is countBand [1,1]. Umpholo is the interior mission named in the lore. Umpholo is the type's only instance.

name: The Shut Vault
why_founding: The vault holds the dead who may not be staked. They are heretics, the Hist-less and one whole tribe.
why_site_advantages: The vault is dry stone, sealed. It lies well away from any village.
why_occupants_motive: A keeper holds the register but not the key. That way no single person can be pressured into opening the vault.
why_pressures: Families want their dead moved out. The register says no. The register's authority rests on an assembly ruling. The register-keeper cannot now produce that ruling.
why_would_change_if: A ruling on the register would empty half of it. The Hist-less refuge has offered to receive the dead whom the register denies. That offer would make the refuge a burial authority.
vibe_silhouette: The vault is a sealed low structure. It has no offerings and no path.
vibe_palette: The entrance is green, giving way to black inside. The gold beading is worn thin on the door limb. A red flower is shut at the threshold.
vibe_materials: Root grows around the sealed doorway and is trained to hold it shut. Crocodile skulls are fixed to the gate posts. A register box is built into the wall beside the door.
vibe_signature_feature: Urns stand shelved by category of offence. The urns are not shelved by family. The offence is written on each urn.
vibe_condition: One keeper's authority keeps the vault sealed. That authority has not been challenged so far.
vibe_approach: The approach is a single door in a hillside. A register box stands beside the door.
vibe_senses: The air is still and holds no smell of offering. Damp leaves rot somewhere unseen inside. The stone at the threshold is cold even at midday. Apart from the register-keeper's own footsteps, the place is silent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can overturn one shelving. A quest can add another shelving.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 567 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: Urns are shelved by category of offence. The offence is written on each urn. The shelving includes one whole tribe.

name: The Break
why_founding: An old storm's blowdown left one ledge with a view over the canopy.
why_site_advantages: The ledge is the single highest exposed point in the district.
why_occupants_motive: The ledge has no occupants. Guides bring clients here to take a bearing. The guides charge for it.
why_pressures: The forest is closing the gap. The view has ten years left. The guides argue about whether cutting to keep it open is theirs to do.
why_would_change_if: When the gap closes, the district's only orientation point is the counting tower. The counting tower belongs to a village. The counting tower is not for hire.
vibe_silhouette: The ledge is a break in the canopy or a rim edge. It shows as light from below.
vibe_palette: A narrow band of gold light shows where the canopy has broken. Leaf-litter is black underfoot. Thin pale sap weeps from storm-split wood. The Helstrom crown burns red on the far horizon.
vibe_materials: The ledge has no structure at all. It is just the blowdown and bare root exposed by the fall. An earlier climber left a single stake-cairn marking the safe line up. Storm-split timber lies where it fell and slowly closes the gap it made. Nothing here has been cut or cleared, only climbed.
vibe_signature_feature: The ledge gives a ground-level view over the interior canopy. The Helstrom grove crown is visible from the ledge. One hero Hist is visible beyond the grove crown.
vibe_condition: The gap closes a little more each year. The forest heals over it.
vibe_mood: The ledge feels open. The gap is closing.
vibe_approach: The approach is a short hard climb out of closed forest into open sky.
vibe_senses: Open wind blows after the stillness of the forest floor below. The blowdown smells of split, weeping wood. A long silence lies here, with no bird call carrying this high.
why_site_won: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 4), 30 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The canopy breaks here for perhaps ten more years. Helstrom's grove crown shows over the break, red at night.

name: The Sealed Cistern
why_founding: The Sealed Cistern is a xanmeer cistern. Its builders sealed it on purpose. What was in the cistern is still inside.
why_site_advantages: The cistern lies below the water table. It sits in stone that has held.
why_occupants_motive: A voriplasm is held behind the seal. The people who cut the seal wrote in a language that is no longer read.
why_pressures: The seal is stone and will hold. The warnings cut into the seal have outlasted the language. Antiquarians are the people who can read the warnings. They are also the people most likely to break the seal.
why_would_change_if: The seal need not be broken. The breached cistern in the deep swamp shows the result of the other choice. The result of that breach has stood for twelve years.
vibe_silhouette: The cistern shows as a doorway. A residue line crosses the doorway at knee height. The doorway is dark past the residue line.
vibe_palette: The stone is black and fades into grey daylight at the threshold. Churned brown mud pools at the sill. No sap shows on the bare rock. A red Hist flower shows high through the gap above.
vibe_materials: There is no built work at the site. Living root and fallen limbs lie sorted by standing water. A stone seal is cut with three inscriptions of different ages. Grave-poles are driven at the rim. None of them is recent. Centuries of damp have worn the bare rock walls smooth.
vibe_signature_feature: The seal carries the same warning in three scripts of different ages. Each generation that found the seal added its own script. No generation trusted the last script.
vibe_condition: The seal has not been opened since the third script was added. The seal's own weight holds it shut.
vibe_mood: The cistern is sealed. The door carries three warnings.
vibe_approach: The approach ends at a blank stone face. The face carries three inscriptions. The face has no door.
vibe_senses: Cold mineral air pools at the sill. A residue line marks where water once stood higher. Total silence lies below the seal line. Grit settles faintly from the stone above.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 256 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: One seal carries three scripts of different ages. All three scripts say the same thing. The door has not been opened since the third script was cut.

name: Still-Waiting
why_founding: The vigil families kept faith for a hundred and fifty years. A sickness went through the settlement in one wet season. The sickness took most of the vigil families.
why_site_advantages: The enclosed clearing once gave the vigil dry ground. The same clearing leaves the root warren below it dark and undisturbed.
why_occupants_motive: No household keeps Still-Waiting now. Something moved into the collapsed cellars after the houses emptied. It came up through the root-mouth.
why_pressures: Tally stones are still stacked at the swept ground. They have been uncounted since the year the sickness came.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the warren would allow the tally to be finished. The tally-keeper has not entered the warren.
vibe_silhouette: Sunken roofs mark the village. A root-mouth stands where the swept ground used to be.
vibe_palette: Grey rot lies over the sunken roofing. Root has gone black at the collapsed cellars. One fleck of bone shows pale in the leaf litter.
vibe_materials: Root growth has pulled down the cane walls. Old grass-rope ties are still knotted on fallen posts. Tally stones are stacked in sets of ten at the swept ground.
vibe_signature_feature: The tally stones are stacked in sets of ten. The stacks stop mid-count at the year of the sickness.
vibe_condition: The tally has been uncounted since the sickness took the households.
vibe_mood: The village is quiet. The houses are empty.
vibe_approach: The swept ground shows under the leaf litter before the roofline does.
vibe_senses: Root smell hangs over standing rot. No birds sing this close to the warren mouth. Leaf litter shifts somewhere below the roofline. The swept ground stays readable before the ruin does.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 395 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: The vigil lasted a hundred and fifty years. A sickness ended the vigil in one wet season. Something has since come up through the root-mouth into the cellars.
singular_claim: Still-Waiting has countBand [1,1]. One plague-abandoned village is a tragedy. Several would be a movement. The An-Xileel withdrawal order was a single event.

name: High Crossing
why_founding: Four walkway routes are forced to meet. They meet above ground that floods to chest height.
why_site_advantages: High Crossing is the single place where the four alignments can share a footing.
why_occupants_motive: A keeper collects for maintenance and sells rope. The keeper knows the true condition of all four arms. The tribes that pay him do not know it.
why_pressures: Four tribes use High Crossing. Two of the tribes pay for it. The branching village a day away has the same problem. That village has started coordinating rates.
why_would_change_if: If one arm fails, the traffic of an entire tribe is rerouted. The Paatru are the tribe most likely to be affected. The Paatru have no alternative that does not cross their own mire.
vibe_silhouette: The walkway lines converge. They can be seen across open marsh.
vibe_palette: Silt-white water catches green light below the deck. Pale sand shows at the channel turn. A gold bead of sap hangs on the underside of a limb. No red shows on this tree.
vibe_materials: Root is braided tight into the deck's frame like basketwork. Flint-vine cord lashes every joint. Sap-rubber gaskets seal the small store box. A maintenance ledger is nailed to the central post.
vibe_signature_feature: The four-way deck stands at head height. A maintenance ledger is nailed to the post. The ledger lists who paid and who did not.
vibe_condition: The keeper shores up the deck only at the points that the ledger lists as needing it.
vibe_approach: Four walkway lines converge over open marsh.
vibe_senses: The deck is audible before it comes into view. Insect noise is thick against the braided walls. Sap sours at the cut edges nearby. The surrounding green absorbs the crossing's echo quickly.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can buy the keeper's knowledge of the four arms. A quest can test that knowledge.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MR06 · tier-2; LH32 · tier-3; LH34 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 64 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Four routes meet at head height. They meet over ground that floods to the chest. The ledger on the post lists who paid and who did not.

name: The Charged Pond
why_founding: The Charged Pond is a wamasu nesting pond. The tribes avoid it. The guar herds avoid it.
why_site_advantages: The pond holds still, deep, isolated water. That kind of water suits nesting.
why_occupants_motive: A breeding pair and a season's eggs live here. Buyers in the coastal egg trade would pay a fortune for the eggs. No interior guide will lead a party here.
why_pressures: The water is lethal to swim while the wamasu are in it. The route past has to go round. The detour runs through the marsh giant's expanding range.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the pond opens a two-hour shortcut. Clearing it ends a species' nest site. The offering-shrine keepers hold that the flood-staying rite depends on the pair being there.
vibe_silhouette: Dead standing trees show lightning scarring. The fish have left the pond.
vibe_palette: Dead lightning-scarred trunks stand pale against brown water. A ring of dead fish floats pale at the surface. No red shows anywhere near the pond.
vibe_materials: There is no structure of any kind. Bare root and flood debris pile at the upstream edge. A single depth stick stands in the bank. The pond is still because of the nesting pair's presence.
vibe_signature_feature: Dead fish float in a ring at the radius of the discharge. The ring is renewed daily.
vibe_condition: The pond is not visited, by rule as much as by fear.
vibe_approach: The dead ring is visible before the animals are.
vibe_senses: The water sits unnaturally still until something moves under it. The ring of dead fish gives off a sweet rot smell. The smell is renewed daily. The heavy silence is broken by surface ripples alone.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 302 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: Dead fish float in a ring at the radius of the discharge. The ring is renewed daily. Past the ring the route is two hours shorter.

name: The Struck Ground
why_founding: The Struck Ground is a shallow pan of warm standing water. The pan lies on black mud and has no outfall. Adult wamasu have wallowed in it since before the nearest village kept a count.
why_site_advantages: The banks are soft. The water is deep enough to wallow. From the middle of the pan the tree line is clearly visible.
why_occupants_motive: Three grown wamasu hold the water. They drive off whatever comes to drink. They drive off each other's young.
why_pressures: The village two hours east lost a lizard-steed at the pan last dry season. Its hunters now walk round by the reed cut. The detour costs them half a morning.
why_would_change_if: Killing the big male opens the water again. Another adult moves into the pan before the year is out.
vibe_silhouette: The pan is flat and brown with three long backs in it. Dead trees stand round the rim. The water killed their roots.
vibe_palette: The water is flat and brown. Grey standing deadwood lines the rim. Pale wamasu bellies turn in the shallows.
vibe_materials: Soft black mud lies underfoot for two hundred paces before open water. Drowned timber rings the pan. A lizard-steed's saddle lies abandoned on the bank.
vibe_signature_feature: The air over the pan smells burnt on a still day.
vibe_condition: The ground is unbuilt. Wallowing has produced its present form.
vibe_approach: The ground softens for two hundred paces before the water shows.
vibe_senses: Flies work the mudline. A crack and a burnt smell come when a wamasu shifts its bulk. Warm still air lies over the pan. No birdcall sounds over the open water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A village that wants its drinking pan back must decide which of the three wamasu it can afford to leave alive.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 339 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Three grown wamasu share one warm pan. Charged bone is worth carrying out.

name: The Root Fall
why_founding: A spring bursts out of the root layer. It falls into a chamber behind the curtain.
why_site_advantages: The fall has twenty metres of vertical relief. Such relief is rare in this country.
why_occupants_motive: The chamber is used by whatever needs a dry room behind water. In this district it has held a cult cell, a smuggler and something else. The village downstream describes that something only as an animal.
why_pressures: The village downstream knows a chamber lies behind the fall. The villagers stopped counting who came back two naheesh ago.
why_would_change_if: A dry season halves the curtain. The halved curtain exposes the entrance. Whoever uses the chamber then has to move.
vibe_silhouette: The fall itself is a visible cue. The chamber is not visible.
vibe_palette: Grey-brown mud curls dry at the chamber edge. A single bright line of gold sap runs down the root wall. A red Hist flower grows high in the canopy above the fall. Black water pounds pale where it breaks.
vibe_materials: Living root lines the chamber walls. The chamber has no stone lining. The root is warm to the touch. A previous visitor left one rope tied off and never retrieved it. Raw mud is packed into the gaps where the root does not meet flush. Nothing here has been shaped, only used.
vibe_signature_feature: The fall comes out of a living root. It does not come out of rock. The chamber behind it is lined with the same root. The chamber is warm and dry.
vibe_condition: New rope hangs beside work three lifetimes old. The chamber has not been claimed by any occupant.
vibe_mood: The chamber is a hidden room in country with almost no rock.
vibe_approach: The noise carries two kilometres through closed canopy.
vibe_senses: The roar of falling water carries for two kilometres through closed canopy. Still warm air fills the chamber. Cold spray fills the chamber's mouth. Wet mud underfoot smells of minerals.
why_site_won: cliff bench in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 157 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The fall comes out of a living root. It does not come out of rock. The chamber behind it is warm, dry and root-lined.

name: The Panther Race
why_founding: The Panther fork drops through a root-choked reach. The reach is the Panther Race.
why_site_advantages: The Panther Race is fast water. The province is otherwise a province of still water.
why_occupants_motive: The reach is empty of fish. A portage crew works beside the reach. The crew charges by the hull. The crew holds a registered salvage claim on the reach. The interior tribes do not fish the reach.
why_pressures: Boats are lost at the Panther Race regularly. The portage crew profits from the losses. The people of Greenspring downstream receive the wreckage and the survivors. They resent both.
why_would_change_if: A cleared channel would end the portage trade. It would also put laden craft no more than a day from Helstrom's approach. The escort service has costed that outcome and favours it.
vibe_silhouette: The sound is heard from a long way upstream. White water follows the sound.
vibe_palette: Clear brown water breaks white over submerged root. Pale root-wood decking stands at the portage stand. Gold beads of sap hang on the underside of a spanning limb. Red flower colour has gone orange with age.
vibe_materials: Raw root-wood staging is driven at the portage landing. One abandoned rope is still tied off at the bank. A totem marks the crew's claimed stretch. The totem is unrenewed. Loose stone ballast is piled to steady the landing.
vibe_signature_feature: Roots make the rapids, not rock. The whole reach is a lattice of submerged root.
vibe_condition: A licensed crew works the reach. The crew maintains the landing only well enough to keep the toll running.
vibe_approach: The Panther Race is heard from the last quiet bend.
vibe_senses: White water roars from a long bend upstream. Wet spray is cold even in the heat. The portage crew calls prices over the noise. Birds are absent from the loudest stretch.
why_site_won: gorge in firm lowland (danger band 4), 192 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, route, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The rapids are made of submerged root. They are not made of rock. A boat's crew must read the lattice before committing the boat. The portage crew charges by the hull.

name: The Turned Tree
why_founding: The Turned Tree is a wild Hist with no tribe. It went wrong on its own. It stands in unkept ground.
why_site_advantages: The tree stands in a deep basin. No route passes it. It has no neighbours who would notice it for decades.
why_occupants_motive: No tribe speaks for the tree. The nearest villages maintain a totem line and stay outside it. They re-cut the line outward each year as the ring widens.
why_pressures: The flowering ring is wider each year. The watchers of the counting tower have recorded the rate for three generations.
why_would_change_if: A tribe that adopted the tree would most likely be destroyed. The Hist-less refuge has debated adopting it twice.
vibe_silhouette: The crown has grown wrong. Its limbs turn back on themselves. No chimes hang anywhere near it.
vibe_palette: Green shade doubles on still water. Gold beads hang under a turned limb. Algae covers every flat surface. One red flower is held still in the reflection.
vibe_materials: There is no built structure. The tree's own root serves as floor and wall. Crocodile skulls are set along the totem line. Trunks double back on themselves where the growth turned.
vibe_signature_feature: Inside the flowering ring the trunks are doubled. The leaves face away from the light.
vibe_condition: The villages re-cut the totem line outward every year as the ring spreads.
vibe_mood: The tree feels wrong. The reason cannot be named.
vibe_approach: The birdsong stops about two hundred metres out.
vibe_senses: Birdsong stops well short of the flowering ring. Heat rises off ground that stays warm through cold nights. Bark ticks as it dries in still air. Leaves on every limb turn from the light.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 483 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: The villages re-cut the totem line around the flowering ring outward each year. The animals inside the line do not leave.

name: The Sleeper Under Ash
why_founding: After the Duskfall, a Hist isolated itself from the collective. The isolated Hist sleeps. The Sleeper Under Ash grew from that Hist.
why_site_advantages: A burn scar never regrew around the tree. The tree stands alone in open ground.
why_occupants_motive: No keeper tends the tree. Pilgrims come to sit here and do not come to speak. Sitting here is a recognised alternative for pilgrims who were refused audience at a hero grove.
why_pressures: The sap-tappers know that the tree cannot object to being tapped. The poacher camp works this tree in preference to any tree that has a tribe. The tree-minders know this but cannot prove it.
why_would_change_if: If the Hist woke, three villages would have to renegotiate where they belong. Two of the villages pay the Agaceph grove for standing. Those two villages would no longer need that standing if the Hist woke.
vibe_silhouette: A great trunk stands under a mound of ash-grey moss. The trunk barely reads as a tree.
vibe_palette: Ash-grey moss lies thick over the trunk. The water is clear brown and pales to green beyond the scar. Old pale amber crusts the bark in thin lines. Red petals lie stuck flat to the wet wood.
vibe_materials: Root is shaped by permission only. One graft is allowed each generation. Withy binding is renewed over the older ties. None of the older ties is stripped away. Grass matting turns ash-grey where it has weathered longest. There is no built roof, only the open scar around the trunk.
vibe_signature_feature: A living tree stands in a century of ash. The sky is open because the canopy burned away.
vibe_condition: The place is kept up by the effort of one pilgrim at a time. Otherwise it is untended.
vibe_mood: The place is still and open to the sky.
vibe_approach: The canopy stops at the burn scar. The ground beyond it is open to the sky.
vibe_senses: The open sky is unfamiliar after the closed canopy elsewhere. A chime frame has gone green and its cord has perished silent. A cold mineral smell comes off the mud at the edge of the scar. No horizon breaks the flat burned ground.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 682 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: A living tree stands alone in a century of ash. Pilgrims who were refused audience at a hero grove come and sit here.

name: The Guide-Lights
why_founding: Travellers who follow the lights in this stretch of basin leave the route.
why_site_advantages: The basin lies between two safe rises. It lies on the line along which the guides walk.
why_occupants_motive: The lights lie along a line between two safe rises. What the lights are is unknown. Whether they follow that line by design has not been tested.
why_pressures: Guides tell their clients that the lights are real and that the clients should ignore them. Clients follow the lights anyway. Survivors reach the far shelter and live on its stock.
why_would_change_if: The guides price the crossing on the assumption that one client in twenty walks off the line. They make this assumption whatever the clients were told.
vibe_silhouette: At night the lights themselves form the silhouette.
vibe_palette: Clear brown water is lit green from above. A lone red flower grows out of reach at the bank. No lantern light shows where lantern light is expected.
vibe_materials: Living root banks the basin on both sides. One cut step goes down to the water. The person who cut it regretted it. A blaze is cut into the last dry tree to mark the true line.
vibe_signature_feature: The lights show the lantern rhythm of a guide, which is three short and one long. Every interior traveller is taught to trust that signal.
vibe_condition: The true line is kept clear only by the guides. They pass it on by word of mouth.
vibe_mood: The lights are a hazard that copies a signal.
vibe_approach: The correct signal shows in the wrong place.
vibe_senses: The air is still, then a light moves that no guide lit. The water shows its bottom clearly and looks deceptively shallow. No chime sounds anywhere along this stretch.
quest_hooks_opportunity: It can be proved in a quest that the lights copy the signal. The proof can be made before another party enters the basin.
why_site_won: water narrows in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 167 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The lights repeat the lantern signal of the guides, which is three short and one long. They show it from the wrong place.

name: The Made Ground
why_founding: The Hist grow Xal-Krona out of sap. Each making has a reason. The reason here was the Accord. The hollow was flooded with sap. The Hist made the Last Warden there. The remains in the basin are earlier attempts.
why_site_advantages: The basin is closed and is fed by deep roots. Sap collects there and does not drain away. Few places in the interior let a tree pool enough of its sap to make something of that size.
why_occupants_motive: The basin is unoccupied. The Warden has not been here in an age. The Warden waits in the Lost City, as it was made to do. What remains here are the makings that came before it.
why_pressures: The basin still fills each wet season. What it grows now is smaller, wrong and short-lived. The Unbound Root have found the place and read it as a recipe.
why_would_change_if: The making record here states what the Warden was made to test. If it is read first, it decides whether the Warden can be stood down or must be fought.
traversal_fallback: The fallback is the rim path around the basin. The rim path adds a day to the journey. The rim path stays out of the sap.
vibe_silhouette: A bowl of dead-still amber lies under a canopy that closes right over it. Pale ribs of something very large stand out of the surface at the low end.
vibe_palette: Amber pools waist-deep and is lit from below. The black-green canopy is sealed overhead. Red petals are scattered across the amber surface.
vibe_materials: Unbuilt sap-flooded root holds the shapes of failed makings. Bones are bleached pale where the sap has thinned around them. A ring of driven poles is set around the largest remains.
vibe_signature_feature: Three skeletons lie in the sap at the shallow end. Each skeleton is larger than the last. Each skeleton is unfinished. At the deep end an empty impression the size of a house is still bare of growth.
vibe_condition: The basin has been undisturbed since the last making failed here.
vibe_approach: The way goes down the deep throat and out into a basin. The air in the basin is so sweet that it is hard to breathe.
vibe_senses: A chord is felt through the chest and is not heard. The sap hangs thick enough in the air to taste on the tongue. No insect sound is heard anywhere in the basin. A cold draught eases off as the basin opens out.
quest_hooks_opportunity: LOC warden.making_ground · EVIDENCE accord.making_record
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 510 m from the nearest route; no free 'box-canyon' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: Three unfinished skeletons lie in the sap. Each is larger than the last. An empty impression the size of a house lies at the deep end.

name: The Meeruth Station
why_founding: The Meeruth Station is an Imperial-era river station. It stands on the last navigable reach of the Helstrom approach. It was abandoned when the concession lapsed.
why_site_advantages: The station has a stone quay, a walled yard and a magazine. All of them stand on firm ground that the marsh cannot rot.
why_occupants_motive: Squatters live here and leave when a claimant arrives. They have kept the magazine dry for twenty years.
why_pressures: The interior tribes and the Veiled Reed would both prefer that the station stayed unclaimed. Whoever holds a station on this reach controls the Helstrom approach outright.
why_would_change_if: A claimant with standing could hold the station. That would put a fortified quay between Helstrom and the coast.
vibe_silhouette: The station stands on the road and is visible from both approaches.
vibe_palette: Pale Imperial stone has gone grey with damp. The working quay is dark and slick at the waterline. Rust-red stains the hinges of the magazine door. Green shoots force through the old paving of the walled yard.
vibe_materials: The masonry shows three visible phases of Imperial work. Each phase is patched in a different hand. The magazine door is iron. Squatters have kept the magazine door oiled for twenty years. The quay stones are original and still level. The gate of the walled yard has stood open so long that its hinges have seized that way.
vibe_signature_feature: A walled river yard has a working quay. The stonework shows three phases of building.
vibe_condition: Squatters keep the station dry and orderly. They leave the moment a claimant arrives.
vibe_approach: The magazine roof shows from the water before the quay does. The gate is open and has been open for a century.
vibe_senses: Wet heat comes off the river and does not lift at night. Gulls and river birds work the exposed mudbanks below the quay. The magazine door smells of iron each time it swings.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The station is a reserve player-stronghold site, `stronghold.site`. The primary stronghold is pirate-freeholds.rockpoint. The ruling for this is decision 0041 §12b.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 106 m from the nearest route; no free 'river-mouth' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-repair'.
player_purpose_hook: A walled river yard has a working quay and a dry magazine. The gate has been open for a century.
reconciliation: This place is a candidate stronghold site. It is one site province-wide. It is reconciled against the xanmeer candidates of neighbouring agents before Part 3.
reconciliation_note: Player-stronghold candidate A (2026-09-02 reconciliation): the interior river station. Candidate B is place.pirate-freeholds.rockpoint. BOTH stay flagged; the A/B choice is an owner call queued for touchpoint (1) in decision 0041's Owner Q&A.

name: Xal-Thuun
why_founding: A tribe moved into the xanmeer of its ancestors during the Imperial century. The tribe never moved out.
why_site_advantages: Xal-Thuun has stone walls and working vakka mechanisms. These make it the strongest fortification in the interior.
why_occupants_motive: A tribe lives in a monument that it is meant solely to maintain. The tribe describes its residence as continuous tending.
why_pressures: Neighbouring tribes consider inhabiting the xanmeer to be close to the stone heresy. The mechanisms still kill people, mostly the young of the tribe. The deaths are recorded as falls.
why_would_change_if: A mechanism failure would open the strongest position in the region. The vakka stones that drive the mechanisms are the largest cache in the interior.
vibe_silhouette: The silhouette is terraced monumental massing. Smoke and washing lie on the terraces.
vibe_palette: The terraces are green-grey and are kept deliberately clear of growth. Amber lamplight shows in the stair mouths after dark. A single red flower grows on the lone tree that stands inside the walls. The stone underfoot is black and wet.
vibe_materials: The tribe maintains the xanmeer stone and does not replace it. Neighbouring tribes object to this. Trained root binds the newer additions to the old. Withy and flint-vine lash the hoardings in place. Working vakka mechanisms are set into the terrace walls.
vibe_signature_feature: Working xanmeer traps guard a doorway. Laundry hangs across the doorway.
vibe_condition: The tribe lives in the fort and maintains it daily. The tribe leaves its traps running. The traps are occasionally fatal.
vibe_approach: The terraces break the canopy. The smoke comes out of the terraces.
vibe_senses: The stone treads ring underfoot at every terrace. Laundry snaps in the wind across a trap doorway. A mechanism resets somewhere below with a distant clunk. Cooking smoke drifts out across the walls.
why_site_won: summit in firm lowland (danger band 5), 98 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, route.
player_purpose_hook: Working xanmeer traps guard a doorway with laundry hung across it. The tribe living inside describes that as maintenance.

name: Ashen Tower
why_founding: Ashen Tower is an Imperial signal tower on the rim. It was built to send signals to Fort Swampmoth by fire. The people who keep it lit have no claim on the tower or on the fort.
why_site_advantages: The tower stands on a ridge end. It has a line of sight to the fort and a line of sight down the road.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages pay the two watchers in food. The villages want warning of raids and do not want warning of armies.
why_pressures: The fire code that the watchers use was written for legions. The watchers have given several of its signals new meanings.
why_would_change_if: The tower would be abandoned if the villages decided that the Sul-Xan were finished.
siting_prefs_water_relation: commands a route or a channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower
vibe_silhouette: The tower is a round stone stump three storeys high. An iron basket stands on top. Ash spills down one side.
vibe_palette: Ash grey lies on grey stone. Rust shows on the iron. An orange point shows at night.
vibe_materials: The tower is built of Imperial rubble. Its timber floors are renewed in local wood. The iron fire-basket is of a kind that no fringe smith could make today.
vibe_signature_feature: The code board inside carries the fire signals of the Legion. The signals are annotated in Jel down the margin.
vibe_condition: The lower two storeys are sound. The top floor is new timber on old corbels.
vibe_approach: The ash streak down the stonework is visible from further off than the tower itself.
vibe_senses: Wind passes through the arrow slits. The basket ticks as it cools.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The fire code is being answered from a station that the code does not list.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 71 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The signal tower gives a view of the road belt from fort to fort. The runners charge for the climb.

name: Bog Iron Workings
why_founding: Bog iron forms in this ground. Nails, tyres and tools wear out fast on the road. The road crews buy replacement iron from the diggers here.
why_site_advantages: The seep is stagnant and rich in iron. The ore can be lifted from the mud in cakes.
why_occupants_motive: The diggers come from three villages for one season a year. They consider the work shameful.
why_pressures: The seep is being worked out. Each season's cakes are smaller and lie further from the path.
why_would_change_if: The workings would be abandoned without ceremony.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a road or a foreign settlement
vibe_silhouette: A squat clay furnace and its black charcoal bed stand on a bench. A small timber house stands west of the furnace. The seep lies below the bank.
vibe_palette: The charcoal is black. The furnace clay is grey. The peat water is dark.
vibe_materials: The clay furnace is rebuilt every season. The timber house stands on posts.
vibe_signature_feature: The furnace stands on a levelled floor above the seep. Its charcoal bed is spread before its mouth.
vibe_condition: The diggers rebuild the furnace every season. They break it open to get the bloom out.
vibe_approach: The seep shows through the ferns below the bench. It shows well before the workings do.
vibe_senses: The mud makes a sucking sound. A struck bloom gives a hollow ring. The air smells of sulphur.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The diggers have abandoned the deep end of the seep. They have not said why.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 88 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Iron lifts out of the mud here in cakes. The seasonal diggers allow a visitor to take what the visitor can carry.
watch_reason: Three diggers and their bloomery. No office keeps a watch here.

name: Bonded Shed
why_founding: Goods that are declared but not yet taxed must wait in a lockable place. Gideon's court is the lawful holder of those goods.
why_site_advantages: The shed stands on the waterside landing below Gideon. A cart can be sealed at the wharf. The seal can be opened in court.
why_occupants_motive: The bond-keeper's authority comes from the courthouse. The bond-keeper mentions this often.
why_pressures: Half the bond is Cyrodilic Collections crates. The other half is goods that the antiquities fences shipped instead. The labels on the crates do not always match.
why_would_change_if: If the courthouse ever stopped sitting, thieves would loot the shed in a night.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in Gideon's own belt, next to place.imperial-fringe.gideon
vibe_silhouette: The shed is long and windowless. It stands on stone piers. It has one door. The door carries a great many seals.
vibe_palette: The boards are tar black. The seals are wax red. The river is silver.
vibe_materials: The shed is Imperial timber frame on stone piers. Reed covers the roof above the tie beam. Local builders rebuilt the roof.
vibe_signature_feature: The clerk leaves every seal that was ever applied on the door. Wax covers the door like scales.
vibe_condition: The shed is sound. The shed has no decoration.
vibe_approach: The wharf runs up to the door. The shed has no windows.
vibe_senses: The shed smells of wax and river damp. A padlock the size of a fist hangs on the door.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Crates go astray between the field station and the bonded shed. One crate goes astray each month. The bond clerk also keeps the customs post on the Onkobra ford below the town. The clerk stops any traveller who carries goods worth 400 or more. Wading round the clerk is smuggling. Smuggling gets the smuggler's name entered in the Owing ledger.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 17 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, route, bound.
player_purpose_hook: Goods that Gideon has seized and not yet taxed sit in a locked shed on the wharf. One clerk keeps the seals.

name: Carries-Them-Home
why_founding: People who carry bones home need stages along the way. The western route is the longest carry in the province.
why_site_advantages: The Counted Dead lies within 700 m of the waystation. The next stage lies a day's carry away.
why_occupants_motive: The keepers house the carriers. The keepers take custody of the bones overnight.
why_pressures: Carriers bring more bones west than east. The carriers keep a tally of both.
why_would_change_if: If the Chainbreakers ever emptied White Rose, the waystation would be busier than the road itself.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a walked or poled route
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: between a carceral site and the interior
vibe_silhouette: Two houses stand forty paces apart. One house has a hearth. The other house has none.
vibe_palette: The palette is thatch gold and whitewash. The bone house is white clay to the eaves.
vibe_materials: The houses are mud and reed. The bone house is limewashed. The keepers' house is not limewashed.
vibe_signature_feature: Empty ground lies between the living house and the bone house. The keepers keep the forty paces clear.
vibe_condition: The keepers renew the limewash monthly. The waystation is kept beautifully.
vibe_mood: The mood is formal. The same rules apply to every carrier.
vibe_approach: Two roofs with a gap between them stand on an open path.
vibe_senses: Wind blows between the two houses. Talk is low. The carriers do not sing.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A bundle that should have gone west did not. The carriers need a person who can go and ask why.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 138 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, bound; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The keeper knows whose bones went west this month. The keeper also knows which bones did not arrive.

name: Burnt Field
why_founding: The Legion burned this ground. The villagers came back to it. The peat still smoulders.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on a patch inside the burn. The peat there burned out to mineral soil.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers stay to hold their claim. Raiders stay away from the smoke.
why_pressures: Sinkholes open without warning where the peat has burned out below. Two houses have gone into sinkholes.
why_would_change_if: The villagers would relocate when the underground fire reached their side of the scar. The fire spreads a little each year.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the burn country of the west
vibe_silhouette: Pale new houses stand on black ground. Thin smoke rises from the earth behind them in three places.
vibe_palette: The palette is charcoal black and ash white. First-year regrowth is a sharp green.
vibe_materials: The houses are mud and reed, all of it new. Every house stands on a new footing.
vibe_signature_feature: A smoulder map is scratched on the fire-watcher's door. The map marks where the ground is hot this year.
vibe_condition: Every house and fence is under nine years old. The fire destroyed what stood before.
vibe_approach: The ground colour changes a kilometre out. The smell of smoke arrives before the roofs.
vibe_senses: The air smells of peat smoke. The ground sounds hollow. Almost no insects live here.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An unseen person keeps the village hearth alight. The open question is who is owed the house.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 382 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, route.
player_purpose_hook: The Legion burned this village. The villagers came back. Accounts of why differ from household to household.

name: Cartwright's Cross
why_founding: A town grew where the Blackwood Road crosses the north track. Carts stop at a crossroads. The townspeople could therefore take dues at the crossing.
why_site_advantages: The town stands on a shelf of level ground at the crossing. A seasonal stream runs 66.3 m away. Avoiding the crossing costs a day's detour.
why_occupants_motive: Four families hold the four corners. The four families split the crossing dues. The arrangement is older than the courthouse.
why_pressures: Gideon claims the dues are unlawful. Gideon collects a tax on the town instead.
why_would_change_if: If the north track were ever bridged upstream, the town would decline sharply.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Blackwood Road, a day's cart west of Gideon
vibe_silhouette: Four two-storey corner houses face each other across a crossroads. The town fills in behind the houses.
vibe_palette: The palette is cart-grease black and ochre plaster. Each of the four corner houses is painted a different colour.
vibe_materials: The buildings are mud-brick and timber. Imperial road stone lies underfoot. Each corner has one tiled roof as a boast.
vibe_signature_feature: Each corner family repaints its house every year. Each family uses its own colour.
vibe_condition: The townsfolk repair buildings with any material that the last cart was carrying.
vibe_approach: Both roads run dead straight at the crossing. The crossing is visible from either arm.
vibe_senses: Iron tyres ring on stone. Smiths hammer. Four different bells sound.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Two parties collect the dues at this crossing. A quest can start by asking which set of coats is lawful.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LF71 · tier-3; LF72 · tier-3; LQ15 · tier-3; Reed track · tier-2
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 8 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: The crossroads lies west of Gideon. A cart has no way around it. The road's traffic stops here for a night.

name: Cassian's Holding
why_founding: A Nibenese family held this grant for five generations. The fields gave out. The family then walked off the grant.
why_site_advantages: The holding stands on a dry loam shoulder above the flood line. The barn was built to keep vermin and damp out of the stored goods.
why_occupants_motive: Sap-poachers use the staddle-stone barn to dry and cure the goods that they take. Goods in the barn are safe from the things that climb.
why_pressures: Gideon still lists the grant as occupied. The heir has not told the tower clerk otherwise.
why_would_change_if: The sap-poachers would be cleared out on the day a patrol rides the fringe road again.
siting_prefs_water_relation: tried to be dry and failed
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in Gideon's own belt, next to place.imperial-fringe.gideon
vibe_silhouette: A tiled farmhouse with a walled yard stands in fields that have gone back to reed. A barn stands up on mushroom stones.
vibe_palette: The terracotta has gone grey. The whitewash is flaking. Reed has overgrown the straight field lines.
vibe_materials: The farmhouse is Imperial stone and pantile. The field hands' quarters, fifty metres off, have collapsed to their footings.
vibe_signature_feature: The staddle-stone barn still stands clear of the ground on stone mushrooms. Drying hides hang in the barn in place of grain sacks.
vibe_condition: The roof is intact and the walls are sound. The yard is overgrown. The holding is better kept than it looks from the road.
vibe_mood: The mood is quiet. A sap-poacher in the barn listens.
vibe_approach: The straight field edges still show where the holding lies. The crops that they once framed are gone.
vibe_senses: The air smells of hide smoke. A dog's chain lies with no dog on it. Low voices come from the barn.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 64 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, bound.
player_purpose_hook: Cassian's people are long gone. The barn is still proof against damp and vermin. Sap-poachers use the barn to cure the goods that they steal.

name: Castle Giovesse
why_founding: Castle Giovesse is a Cyrodiilic ducal seat. It was raised within sight of Gideon's north gate. It was later used to hold an Empress.
why_site_advantages: The castle stands on a dry knoll above the flood line. The knoll has a clear line to the city gate.
why_occupants_motive: The caretaker families left when the well went bad. The families of Gideon tell their children not to go to the castle.
why_pressures: Roots grow in the vaulting. The north range has already gone. Treasure-hunters chip at the cell doors.
why_would_change_if: A Gideon family would reoccupy the castle the moment it wanted a stone house badly enough. Since the Duskfall, no Gideon family has wanted one.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: dominating ground nobody else wanted
vibe_silhouette: A broken square keep has one intact stair turret. The keep stands black against the evening from the city wall.
vibe_palette: The stone is bone-grey. Damp streaks the stone black. Fig roots are a violent green.
vibe_materials: The castle is Imperial ashlar with vault ribs. All the timber is gone.
vibe_signature_feature: Empress Tavia's cell is still identifiable. Its door hinges are still in the jamb.
vibe_condition: The castle is roofless and root-split. It is structurally treacherous above the first floor.
vibe_mood: The mood is aggrieved, because the house was made into a prison.
vibe_approach: A track runs through fig scrub. Then comes the ditch, then the gate arch. The ducal arms on the arch have been hacked flat.
vibe_senses: Wind blows in an empty stair. Bats roost in the castle. The air smells of wet stone dust.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Castle Giovesse is a haunted ruin in sight of Gideon. Tavia's cell is a quest hook.
why_site_won: summit in firm lowland (danger band 3), 172 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump-yielded, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2-region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: A ducal castle once held an exiled Empress. It has stood empty since the siege. Its lower floors are still barred from the inside.

name: Claywater Station
why_founding: Claywater Station is a mixed village where the road crosses the Claywater ford. An Imperial well and station house stand on one bank of the ford. An Argonian landing stands on the other bank. The landing is older than the station. Argonian polers worked the ford before the Imperials dug the well. A poler's canoe lies pulled up on the bank.
why_site_advantages: The ford is shallow and stony, so a walker can wade it and a cart cannot. Firm ground on each bank holds the well on one side and the landing on the other.
why_occupants_motive: Two communities share the village because neither can hold the other's half.
why_pressures: The Imperial-built well is failing. The Argonian half of the village will not help to repair the well in stone.
why_would_change_if: The village would become one community or two villages within a generation.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: day-travel spacing along a road
vibe_silhouette: A timber station house and a stone well stand on one bank of the ford. Low round mud huts stand on the other bank.
vibe_palette: The station half is wet stone grey and weathered timber. The landing half is mud brown and thatch gold. The two halves do not share a colour.
vibe_materials: The station half uses Imperial timber framing and well masonry. The landing half uses Argonian mud walls and thatch.
vibe_signature_feature: The ford divides the station half from the landing half. The two halves face each other over the water.
vibe_condition: The well is cracking. The mud half of the village was replastered last year.
vibe_approach: The station house roof shows first to an arriving traveller. Across the ford the huts sit low by the water.
vibe_senses: A bucket stands by the well. Water is poured at the well. Two languages are spoken, one from each bank.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Travellers are charged separately at the well and at the landing for the same stop. The poler's plank ferry is the only way a cart crosses the ford.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 20 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, nearPoint, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The village is the road's water point at the ford. It has a well, a landing and a plank ferry for carts.
siting_note: The village is bound to the western reach of the Blackwood Road, set in round 4. There the road runs within 40 m of open water. The old site stood up in the border mountains. The old site had no road and no channel.
watch_reason: A station house with no watch post; the Legion remnant's watch stands at the Broke Column on the same road.

name: Licensed Dig
why_founding: Cyrodilic Collections refounded at Gideon. The Collections immediately needed something to dig. The Collections licensed the nearest Ayleid ground.
why_site_advantages: The dig lies directly below Twyllbek's terrace. The ground is flat. Carts can reach Gideon from the dig.
why_occupants_motive: The Collections dig to return what they find. The Collections pay the local hands a daily wage.
why_pressures: The permit is Gideon's. The Collections did not ask the tribes with a claim on the ground.
why_would_change_if: The Gideon council could shut the dig down in a day. It would do so if it decided that dealing with the fences brought a better return.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always beside a ruin
vibe_silhouette: A white conservation tent stands over a pegged grid of trenches. The spoil heap is sorted into four sizes.
vibe_palette: Canvas white stands against spoil brown. Yellow string lines mark the grid.
vibe_materials: The dig uses canvas, rope and timber shoring. All of it is temporary.
vibe_signature_feature: The find table stands under the tent. Every object is drawn there before it is moved.
vibe_condition: Neat and expensively supplied.
vibe_mood: The mood is earnest. The villages resent the permit.
vibe_approach: The tent shows white against green for a kilometre either way. At dusk the tent glows.
vibe_senses: A hand bell is rung for finds. Under the bell, people argue in three languages.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Cyrodilic Collections works in the field here. The dig is a foreign presence in the fringe.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 326 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, route, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The place is a licensed dig. The Cyrodilic Collections foremen pay cash for finds. The foremen settle up the same day.

name: Comes-Back-Slowly
why_founding: Sap ruins Argonians. The fringe villages have nowhere to put a person coming off sap. A former user built a house, a short walk past the last houses of Gideon. Anyone relapsing has only a short walk to buy sap.
why_site_advantages: The house is a short walk past the last houses of Gideon. The house stands on good water. A hill stands between the house and the road. Road traffic does not hear what goes on inside.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper has been through sap withdrawal herself. The keeper takes no fee. The house is kept going with what the families of those inside bring. The families usually bring food, often very little.
why_pressures: Two sap traders on the Gideon road consider the house a commercial threat. The sap traders have said so. The villages would not forgive an attack on the house.
why_would_change_if: The house would close if the keeper died. The keeper has not trained a second keeper.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: just outside a settlement, near sap country
vibe_silhouette: The house is long and low, with too many small windows. A walled yard adjoins the house. A hill stands between the house and the road, so only the chimney shows from the road.
vibe_palette: The lime-wash is kept deliberately bright. The thatch is dark. The yard is pale swept sand.
vibe_materials: The house is ordinary village mud-and-reed. It is built long and not tall. All residents are on one floor and can be reached quickly.
vibe_signature_feature: The yard is swept sand, raked every morning. An unraked yard means a bad night inside.
vibe_condition: Poor materials, kept immaculately.
vibe_mood: The mood is steady. The keeper is brusque with visitors.
vibe_approach: Woodsmoke carries before the chimney shows. The house stays out of sight behind the hill as far as the gate.
vibe_senses: A rake moves over sand. A resident is sick in a back room. Strong bitter tea is brewed.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The house is a healer's answer, about 300 m from Gideon. A visitor can be treated here or a patient can be brought here. The house is the physical place attached to a sap-dependence thread.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 79 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, route, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The house takes sap-sick Argonians in and dries them out. A keeper who has been through it herself runs the house.

name: Dreams-In-Mud
why_founding: Dreams-In-Mud is a wallow of warm clay in a screened hollow. A hut stands beside the wallow. A keeper supplies the herbs. Visitors come for an answer that talking cannot produce. It is the nearest wallow of its kind to the Imperial road.
why_site_advantages: A warm clay seep lies in a hollow ringed by fig trees. The hollow is silent. The hollow is fully dark for eleven hours in every twenty-four.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper takes no payment for the wallow. The keeper charges heavily for the herbs. The keeper states the distinction plainly.
why_pressures: Nibenese visitors have started coming out from Gideon for it as a novelty. The keeper allows the visits. The neighbouring villages resent the visits. Two of those visitors left the hollow badly disturbed.
why_would_change_if: The villages themselves would shut the wallow if a Gideon citizen died here. The keeper knows that. The keeper takes Gideon visitors anyway.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a short walk from a village, out of its sight
vibe_silhouette: Seen from above, the hollow holds one hut. A fenced oval of grey clay lies in the hollow. A ring of fig trunks surrounds it, so close-set they read as a wall.
vibe_palette: The colours are warm grey clay and fig-bark brown. After dark there is no colour at all.
vibe_materials: One reed hut and a withy fence stand around the wallow. The wallow itself is worked ground.
vibe_signature_feature: The shape of the hollow shuts out the marsh noise. The sound drops away within six paces of the lip.
vibe_condition: The hut is patched. The keeper scrapes the wallow clean each month.
vibe_mood: The mood is hushed. The keeper is matter-of-fact about what the wallow does.
vibe_approach: The marsh goes quiet before the hollow appears. The last part of the path descends in a scramble.
vibe_senses: A visitor meets silence first. Then comes a clay smell. Then comes a bitter green smell from the hut.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The wallow is a vision scene with a physical venue. A visitor can undergo a rite here. The wallow is a fringe answer to a question that no NPC answers directly.
why_site_won: spring head in firm lowland (danger band 4), 181 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The place has a warm clay wallow and a keeper with the right herbs. Those who sleep in it report dreams they cannot explain.

name: Fenmarch
why_founding: The westernmost Hist stands at Fenmarch. The villagers built the village around the Hist.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on a firm hummock at the marsh's western limit. The tree was already ancient when the village came.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers stay because the tree is here.
why_pressures: Gideon took its disputed cutting from this tree. Gideon took the cutting without the village's consent.
why_would_change_if: The village would not move. Hist villages do not relocate.
siting_prefs_water_relation: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage
vibe_silhouette: A single vast pale-barked crown stands well above the marsh canopy. Roofs stand in a ring beneath the crown.
vibe_palette: The Hist bark is grey-white. The canopy is green and the thatch is gold. Amber uxith lamps burn at night.
vibe_materials: The houses are mud and reed. The uxith is a grown material.
vibe_signature_feature: Houses stand at the distance that the roots permit. The village plan follows the tree.
vibe_condition: The villagers constantly rebuild the edges of the village. The centre is unchanged.
vibe_approach: The crown breaks the canopy. The crown shows from a long way off.
vibe_senses: Wind blows in a crown far above. The uxith and frogs sound or show in the village. The village goes quiet at root talk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The westernmost Hist has chosen no speaker for two years. A quest can turn on who is permitted to ask the tree.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ15 · tier-0; LF73 · tier-3; LF74 · tier-3; LF75 · tier-3; LF56 · tier-3; LF76 · tier-3; LF77 · tier-3; LF78 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 225 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The westernmost Hist in Black Marsh stands in this village. The tree-minders decide who may approach it.

name: Fig Market
why_founding: The produce of the marsh and the manufactures of the road have to change hands somewhere. Neither the marsh nor the road controls that place.
why_site_advantages: Fig Market has a landing on the last navigable reach. Cart ground lies behind the landing. Boat and cart meet at the same quay.
why_occupants_motive: The town lives on the spread between marsh prices and road prices. The guild of brokers exists to keep that spread.
why_pressures: The authorities in Gideon want the market inside the city walls. They have tried twice. The brokers pay them not to try a third time.
why_would_change_if: The town would collapse into a village if the navigable reach silted a kilometre downstream.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a junction of navigable waters, or a road crossing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the hinge of a district; several villages depend on it
vibe_silhouette: A long covered market shed stands with a quay at one end. Fig trees stand down the middle of the street.
vibe_palette: The colours are fig-leaf green, sun-bleached awning and river brown. The market shed's tar roof is black.
vibe_materials: The platforms by the water are Argonian reed and mud on stilts. Mud-brick shops stand uphill. One tar-roofed communal shed serves the market.
vibe_signature_feature: The spread board posts today's buying and selling prices side by side.
vibe_condition: The town is crowded. The townsfolk extend it sideways every few years, to no plan.
vibe_approach: The tar roof is the biggest single surface for a kilometre. The roof shows over the trees from the water.
vibe_senses: Buyers and sellers haggle. Boats knock against the quay. Overripe figs smell strongly.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Fig Market is the fringe's produce market, where an interior cargo first becomes an Imperial price. A visitor can be hired into a weighing-and-grading dispute on either side. An An-Xileel buying agent operates here with no office and no denial.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LF33 · tier-3; LF34 · tier-3; LF35 · tier-3; LF36 · tier-3; LF37 · tier-3; LF38 · tier-3; LF39 · tier-3; LF40 · tier-3; LF41 · tier-3; LF42 · tier-3; tier-2 shared
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 27 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: Marsh produce and road manufactures change hands here under the brokers' guild, not Gideon's law. Goods the city will not licence are on the spread board.

name: Fort Greenditch
why_founding: Fort Greenditch is the second of the road forts. The Empire built it to hold the marsh side of the frontier. The garrison left it empty with the other forts at the Oblivion Crisis.
why_site_advantages: The fort stands on a low spur over the marsh edge. The spur is good against an army but useless against water.
why_occupants_motive: The ditch flooded and took the ground floor with it. The cost of pumping the ditch dry was once priced. Then the plan was dropped.
why_pressures: Something has been using the gatehouse. The villagers have stopped cutting reed on that side.
why_would_change_if: The fort would be as valuable as Swampmoth if the ditch were drained. Draining the ditch is a two-season job.
siting_prefs_water_relation: commands something that no longer matters
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a dead road
vibe_silhouette: A square fort stands in its own moat. The moat reflects the fort perfectly. Reeds grow inside the walls.
vibe_palette: The ditch water is green. The wall is grey. The reeds inside the courtyard are gold.
vibe_materials: The fort is built of Imperial fort masonry. The timber floors are gone. Reeds have colonised the parade.
vibe_signature_feature: From the causeway, the fort and its reflection are the same size.
vibe_condition: The walls are sound. The internal ranges are drowned or rotted.
vibe_mood: The mood is quiet. The reeds have overgrown the courtyard.
vibe_approach: The wall shows over the reeds from a long way off. Then the water in front of the wall shows.
vibe_senses: Frogs call inside the walls. Wind passes through the empty embrasures. Something splashes out on the ditch.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The garrison's pay chest is still under the flooded ground floor.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 22 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, nearPoint, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The place is an emptied road fort with a flooded ground floor. Something makes use of the dry half.

name: Fort Swampmoth
why_founding: The Third Empire built Fort Swampmoth to hold the province's land approach. Rumour says the fort was emptied when the Legions were recalled at the Oblivion Crisis.
why_site_advantages: The fort commands the border road where it leaves the ridge for the flood plain. A cart cannot pass the fort unseen.
why_occupants_motive: An outfit moved in two centuries ago. The outfit charges for passage and calls it upkeep. The outfit has a written claim and produces it on request.
why_pressures: The council of Gideon would prefer the tolls to be its own. The Marsh Charter's people regard it as an insult that toll-takers hold a foreign fort.
why_would_change_if: The fort would change hands entirely if the road moved. It would also change hands if the council ever paid to garrison it properly.
siting_prefs_water_relation: commands a road or a crossing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a road between the border and a city
vibe_silhouette: A square Imperial keep and curtain wall stand on a ridge nose. Moss climbs to the string course. The banners on the fort are the toll company's.
vibe_palette: The colours are basalt grey, rust and red road clay. Green rises up the north face.
vibe_materials: The fort is Imperial fort masonry. The toll company has added timber hoardings. A wattle stock pen stands where the parade ground was.
vibe_signature_feature: The Imperial eagle still stands over the gate. The toll company has not troubled to chisel it off.
vibe_condition: The fort is structurally sound. People with no masons repaired it in wood.
vibe_mood: The mood is officious and mercenary. The men know they are not soldiers.
vibe_approach: The road bends. The wall is simply there. The wall is higher than any wall since Leyawiin.
vibe_senses: Chain and windlass clank. The toll bell rings. Goats graze in the ditch.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Fort Swampmoth is held, but not by the Empire. The fort offers border content and carries a Marsh Charter hook.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 93 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on nearPoint, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A toll company in Legion colours holds the Empire's last fort on the land road into the province. The toll company decides who passes.

name: Gideon
why_founding: Gideon was founded where the Blackwood Road out of Leyawiin crosses the low saddle. The saddle lies in the western border belt. The saddle is the province's land door.
why_site_advantages: The barrier gap measures 46 m. Ridges of 60-87 m flank the gap. Firm lowland and drinkable spring water lie on the marsh side. A pond lies 77 m from the gate. The town's clay is dug from the pond.
why_occupants_motive: A civic council sits in the old Governor's Mansion. The council keeps the courthouse and archive working. The people of the city still recognise paper as the authority. Money from Leyawiin trade pays for the council.
why_pressures: The monsoon closes the road for months. The archive's writs are honoured nowhere east of the Onkobra. Cyrodilic Collections and the antiquities fences fight over the same crates.
why_would_change_if: Gideon would fail if the Blackwood Road silted permanently. It would also fail if the disputed Hist cutting in the city gardens took root. That would make Gideon an Argonian city.
siting_prefs_water_relation: river port on a road river
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the western terminus of every road in the province; Leyawiin two days out
vibe_silhouette: Low tiled roofs and a squat courthouse tower step up a saddle. One impossibly green crown stands in the gardens behind them.
vibe_palette: The colours are fired red clay, wet slate and Nibenese ochre. The grey-green of the marsh reaches the gate.
vibe_materials: Cyrodiilic dressed stone and timber stand below the eaves. The roofs are red pantile. Argonian reed and mud fill every quarter that the council does not show to visitors.
vibe_signature_feature: The Records Court is a stone archive. Its ground floor floods every monsoon. The province's history is kept on the first floor and up a ladder.
vibe_condition: The city is maintained but patched with local materials. The masonry is Imperial with wattle repairs.
vibe_mood: The mood is bureaucratic. Documents are still stamped and filed at the courthouse.
vibe_approach: From the west, the road climbs out of the Blackwood trees. The town appears in the notch, roofs first. From the east, the town is a wall of pale stone at the end of the marsh.
vibe_senses: Wet paper and clay dust smell strongly. The courthouse bell rings. Guar carts pass. Frogs call from the gardens pond at dusk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Cyrodilic Collections refounded at Gideon, in the unbuilt-museum-site district. Gideon is a wintertide rootworm migration stop with a frontier courthouse and archive.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ20 · tier-0; MQ32 · tier-0; MR03 · tier-2; SS06 · tier-2; LF01 · tier-3; LF02 · tier-3; LF03 · tier-3; LF04 · tier-3; LF05 · tier-3; LF06 · tier-3; LF07 · tier-3; LF08 · tier-3; LF09 · tier-3; LF10 · tier-3; LF11 · tier-3; LF12 · tier-3; LF13 · tier-3; LF14 · tier-3; LF15 · tier-3; LF16 · tier-3; LF17 · tier-3; LF18 · tier-3; LF19 · tier-3; LF20 · tier-3; LF21 · tier-3; LF22 · tier-3; LF23 · tier-3; LF24 · tier-3; LF25 · tier-3; LF26 · tier-3; LF27 · tier-3; LF28 · tier-3; LF29 · tier-3; LF30 · tier-3; LF31 · tier-3; LF32 · tier-3
why_site_won: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'gideon' (world/sources/anchors); the anchor pixel is the city gate on the main road. The record sits at the solved city centre (cityLayout, owner rule 2026-09-18).
player_purpose_hook: Gideon is the frontier city, with courts, markets and a magistracy. The magistracy hires outsiders.
complexity_justification: Gideon is a major city. It has districts, a walled records core, a foreign quarter and a seasonal root terminus. Placement complexity stays Morrowind-level, with kit assemblies on a graded saddle. The district count justifies the budget.

name: Wintertide Stop
why_founding: The rootworms migrate south to Gideon in wintertide and not otherwise. The stop exists only while the rootworms are here.
why_site_advantages: A root-layer breach lies in the clay bank outside the city. The worms come up there under a mat of hist root. Red clay marks the breach.
why_occupants_motive: The waykeepers keep the marks and the etiquette. Gideon's carters keep the freight rates.
why_pressures: Gideon's council keeps trying to make the stop year-round. The stop has yet to run outside wintertide.
why_would_change_if: The stop would end for good if the potters cut the bank back past the breach.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: nodes on the root network; not on any map
vibe_silhouette: Out of season the stop has a red-daubed post in a clay bank. It has a flattened waiting circle. A low root-hung mouth lies in the bank behind the circle.
vibe_palette: The colours are wet red clay and worm-translucent pink. The sky is wintertide grey.
vibe_materials: Daubed marks, mats and a rope rail stand against a bank of packed clay and old root. The waykeepers can strike the whole stop and carry it out in an hour.
vibe_signature_feature: The tally post is daubed red once for each arrival. The tally goes back three keepers.
vibe_condition: Unbuilt on purpose.
vibe_mood: The mood is expectant in wintertide. The stop is a bare field the rest of the year.
vibe_approach: Red daub marks on trees lead away from the road. The marks stop at a bank with a hole under the roots.
vibe_senses: In season the ground itself moves. The smell is turned compost and wet root.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The stop is a wintertide rootworm migration stop, seasonal only. It is the Waykeepers' fringe terminus. It is the order's sole seat where an outsider can buy passage. Elsewhere in the order, passage must be granted.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 74 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform.
player_purpose_hook: For the wintertide weeks only, a traveller can ride a rootworm north from here. The ride is in the dark and at a price.

name: Reckoning House
why_founding: The Synod inherited the Mages Guild's ambitions. The Synod sent an outstation to Gideon. The Synod can read the archive there.
why_site_advantages: The outstation stands inside Gideon's reach but outside its walls. The council leased the ground cheaply to keep the Synod at arm's length.
why_occupants_motive: The Synod adepts are here to inventory and to acquire.
why_pressures: The Whispers house across the marsh is here for the same reason. The two houses do not speak.
why_would_change_if: The authorities in Cyrodiil would recall the outstation the moment they decided the province was not worth the stipend.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in or near a northern city; rival to the Whispers
vibe_silhouette: A compact stone house has a flat leaded roof with instruments on it. The house is all straight lines and shut windows.
vibe_palette: The colours are cold grey stone, lead and brass. One window is lit blue at night.
vibe_materials: The house is built of imported dressed stone. Importing dressed stone is an offence here.
vibe_signature_feature: The roof instruments are turned to the sky. The sky is usually invisible in the province.
vibe_condition: The house is new and exact. It is already streaked green with damp that the builders did not anticipate.
vibe_mood: The mood is officious and foreign. The wards on the door are real.
vibe_approach: The flat roofline is wrong against every other roof for a kilometre.
vibe_senses: A ward hums. Brass sounds on stone. No local voices are heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Reckoning House commissions a survey. The villagers have refused that survey for two centuries.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 115 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, bound.
player_purpose_hook: The Synod buys readings and sells enchanting. The Synod races Gideon's own archive for the same books.

name: Giovesse Lines
why_founding: An unnamed army besieged Castle Giovesse, where Empress Tavia was held. The besiegers cut banks, ditches and battery positions. Those earthworks keep their shape, because earth here holds its shape better than stone.
why_site_advantages: The ground is firm and within bowshot of the castle's landward face. The besiegers had no choice about where to cut the lines.
why_occupants_motive: Scrub occupies the lines. In the dry months a herd shelters in the ditches.
why_pressures: The fringe's farmers have quarried the banks for road metal for two centuries. The profile of the banks is going. Gideon's records court objects but cannot enforce anything.
why_would_change_if: The lines would be a field within a lifetime at the current rate of quarrying.
siting_prefs_water_relation: dry ground with a view of the target
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with what it besieged
vibe_silhouette: Three long grass banks with ditches between them run in shallow zigzags across a field. The castle's broken face stands beyond.
vibe_palette: Grass covers bank and ditch alike. One raw ochre scar marks the last quarrying. The grey ruin stands beyond.
vibe_materials: The lines are dug and turfed earth. The earth has outlasted the masonry against which it was cut.
vibe_signature_feature: Six flat pads lie at the spacing of Imperial siege engines. The plan of the attack is readable from the pads.
vibe_condition: The earthworks are sharper than the masonry they face. Farmers are eating them away from the road end.
vibe_mood: The mood is quiet and tidy. The layout is military.
vibe_approach: From the road the lines read as agricultural ridges.
vibe_senses: Wind moves in long grass. Footsteps sound hollow in the ditches.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The lines are a legible battlefield that a visitor can read without being told. They are evidence of a siege that the archive records differently.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 93 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, culture-clump-yielded, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2-region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: An unnamed army besieged the castle. The besiegers left their ditches and their dead on the ground. The magazines under the banks are still full.

name: Glenbridge
why_founding: Pilgrims from all over Tamriel come to Glenbridge. They come to hear the Nisswo read a ruined Sithis xanmeer's decay as the god's sermon. A town grew to feed the pilgrims.
why_site_advantages: Glenbridge is a bridged glen on the last easy ground before the bog. The pilgrim road crosses there.
