why_occupants_motive: The Nisswo stay because the sermon is not finished until the stone is gone. The innkeepers stay because pilgrims eat.
why_pressures: Foreign pilgrims want the ruin preserved. The Nisswo find preservation blasphemous. Rectavius is still sealed below. The seal is two centuries older than the Nisswo who tends it.
why_would_change_if: The town would empty in a season if the xanmeer finally collapsed.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with a hero Hist, a Sithis temple or a trial ground
vibe_silhouette: A single stone-arched bridge crosses the glen. A market square lies beside the bridge. A half-eaten pyramid stands on the skyline above the roofs.
vibe_palette: The colours are warm ochre thatch and pale ruin stone. The Nisswo wear black cloth.
vibe_materials: The houses are built of local mud-and-wattle. One Imperial-built bridge crosses the glen. The rest of the stone in the glen belongs to the ruin.
vibe_signature_feature: The wager board in the square takes bets on which block falls next. The bets also name by when the block falls.
vibe_condition: The town is prosperous and well-swept. The town's income depends on the ruin above it.
vibe_approach: The road drops into the glen. The market is audible before the ruin above it is visible.
vibe_senses: Chanting sounds on the hour. Hammers sound somewhere out of sight. The air smells strongly of hot oil and river weed.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Glenbridge is the village around the ruined Sithis xanmeer. The Nisswo of the Turning Path live there.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LF43 · tier-3; LF44 · tier-3; LF45 · tier-3; LF46 · tier-3; LF47 · tier-3; LF48 · tier-3; LF49 · tier-3; LF50 · tier-3; LF51 · tier-3; LF52 · tier-3; NI-line · tier-2
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 593 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The pilgrim town has beds and guides. It also has a nightly argument about what the Nisswo actually said on the hill.

name: Sermon Xanmeer
why_founding: The xanmeer is a Merethic Sithis temple. The Nisswo deliberately left it to decay. They read its decay aloud as scripture.
why_site_advantages: The temple stands above Glenbridge on the glen's shoulder. The whole town can watch the sermon progress.
why_occupants_motive: The Nisswo read the decay. The Clutch below them leaves the fallen dust where it lies.
why_pressures: The voriplasm-sorcerer Rectavius is sealed in the lowest chamber. The seal is part of the structure that is being allowed to fail.
why_would_change_if: The seal would release Rectavius when the sermon reaches the bottom course.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a regional pilgrimage terminus
vibe_silhouette: A stepped pyramid is missing its top three courses. A black doorway at the base looks like a bite.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey-white and stained with green runnels. Black cloth hangs on the reading stand.
vibe_materials: The temple is built of Xanmeer tileset ashlar. Every stone is original and every joint is unrepaired.
vibe_signature_feature: The reading stand stands on the second terrace. Three centuries of elbows have worn it.
vibe_condition: The Nisswo let the temple fail on purpose. They leave every fallen block where it landed and number it.
vibe_approach: The path climbs from the market past numbered rubble. The numbers run down as the path rises.
vibe_senses: Grit falls. The reader's voice carries. A wet chemical smell comes from the doorway.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Rectavius lies sealed beneath in voriplasm. The decay sermon is the hook.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 547 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: The temple was left to decay on purpose. The Nisswo read its decay aloud as scripture.

name: Nine Bells Guar Holding
why_founding: The Blackwood Road's traffic ran on guar that were bred, broken and rested at the holding. The road trade ended. The holding lost the income that kept it.
why_site_advantages: The grazing is rough, too poor for crops and too dry for rice. Nine gates can be watched by a small band from one spot.
why_occupants_motive: Sap-poachers keep the pens. Stolen guar need somewhere to stand while a brand grows out, as in any other herd.
why_pressures: The bells still ring on schedule.
why_would_change_if: If Gideon sent more than a token patrol, poachers would be raided out within days.
siting_prefs_water_relation: tried to be dry and failed
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: strung along a road at Imperial spacing, not local spacing
vibe_silhouette: Rail pens stand on open grazing. A bell hangs on each of nine gates. One round sand ring has gone to weed.
vibe_palette: The colours are dust, hide-grey and hide-green. The rail timber is weathered.
vibe_materials: The holding has split-rail fence and a stone-footed byre. Every wall is low enough for the animals to see over. A visitor is spotted from the byre door.
vibe_signature_feature: The nine bells each ring a different note. The poachers use them now to signal each other, not the handlers.
vibe_condition: The fences are patched with green wood. They are not properly mended.
vibe_mood: The mood is watchful under the ordinary noise of animals.
vibe_approach: The bells carry long before a fence shows, as always. A stranger's call goes unanswered.
vibe_senses: Guar call. Bells ring. A whistle passes from gate to gate.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Neither lender nor borrower grazes the pledged herd. The bells are still rung at night.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 773 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent.
player_purpose_hook: The bells still ring. The herd in the pens is stolen. The men counting it are poachers.

name: Hangs-Above-The-Water
why_founding: When the gorge floods it fills to within a few metres of the rim. The people who work the gorge live on the wall. They live in cut chambers and built galleries above the worst water.
why_site_advantages: The rock is dry and at a constant temperature. The face has to be climbed to be reached.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers net the fish that the narrows concentrate. Boats that need a hand through the rapid pay for a pilot.
why_pressures: The galleries are reached by ladder and rope. Every year a villager falls. The village argues about cutting a stair. A stair would also let outsiders climb up to them.
why_would_change_if: The village would become an ordinary river village if the stair were cut.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: commands a stretch of river; the corridor's signature settlement
vibe_silhouette: A band of small square openings and timber balconies runs along a sheer wall. The galleries hang about twenty metres above the water. Rope ladders hang below the galleries like a fringe.
vibe_palette: The rock is wet grey. The openings are black. Drying nets are strung bright across the face.
vibe_materials: The chambers are rock-cut. Timber balconies and withy rails front them.
vibe_signature_feature: Every household's ladder is a different length. The households draw the ladders up at night. The face looks different at dusk and at dawn.
vibe_condition: The rock is old. The villagers renew the timber every year.
vibe_mood: The mood is vertiginous. The villagers watch the water below.
vibe_approach: From the water the village is overhead before it is visible. From the rim the balconies show. No path leads down to them from the rim.
vibe_senses: Water noise fills the gorge. A ladder knocks against rock. Voices arrive from directly above.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The settlement's front door is a climb. It is a traversal set piece that is also a home. A gorge pilot takes boats through the rapid, or refuses.
why_site_won: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 774 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The village hangs on a gorge wall and is reached by ladders. The galleries hang about twenty metres above the water.

name: Hearth House of the Burnt Field
why_founding: Villagers raised a hearth house on the edge of the old burn country. People arrive exhausted at that edge.
why_site_advantages: The house stands on the first ground with living trees on the eastern approach out of the burn.
why_occupants_motive: The burn-scar village downslope keeps the house out of pride. The villagers know what arriving hungry means.
why_pressures: The burn ground still supports almost nothing. Stocking the house costs the village more than it can spare.
why_would_change_if: The village would move the house further into the burn if anyone ever re-greened it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities
vibe_silhouette: A low house stands under the first three living trees. The black ground starts fifty metres behind the house.
vibe_palette: Charcoal black lies behind the house. Green lies ahead. Thatch gold lies between them.
vibe_materials: The house is built of mud, wattle and thatch. The hearth ring is fire-cracked stone salvaged from the burn.
vibe_signature_feature: The hearth stones were burnt in 1E 2828. They are making fire again.
vibe_condition: The village keeps the house up at real cost. The thatch is thinner than it should be.
vibe_mood: The mood is relieved. The bad ground stops here.
vibe_approach: Walking out of the burn, a traveller meets the first trees. The roof stands under the trees.
vibe_senses: Leaves rustle, which is startling after the silence. Water runs nearby. Wood is being split close at hand.
player_purpose_hook: The house offers the first roof and hot food on the eastern way out of the burn country. The house turns away no traveller.

name: Highwater
why_founding: People build on any dry rise in the flood plain. For four months a year the plain is water.
why_site_advantages: The hamlet stands on a knoll that the flood has yet to top in recorded memory. The knoll stands clear of the plain when the plain is water.
why_occupants_motive: In the wet season the households rent dry floor to their flooded neighbours. In the dry season they farm like everyone else.
why_pressures: The rise is small and there is no room to grow. The third generation is having to leave.
why_would_change_if: The hamlet would be abandoned after a flood that topped the knoll.
siting_prefs_water_relation: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: refuge for its neighbours in flood
vibe_silhouette: Eight houses crowd onto a knoll. The knoll stands above a sheet of floodwater for a third of the year. A cart ramp is cut up one side.
vibe_palette: In the dry season thatch gold stands on green. In the wet season thatch gold stands on brown water.
vibe_materials: The houses are built of mud, wattle and reed. They are packed so tightly that the eaves touch.
vibe_signature_feature: Flood posts stand on the slope. They mark each year's high water in a downward-drifting series.
vibe_condition: The hamlet is dense and well kept. It cannot expand.
vibe_approach: In the wet season the hamlet is a village floating on a plain of water. It can be read from a kilometre away.
vibe_senses: Neighbours live at close quarters. Water laps at the fourth post. A great many frogs call.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The dry-season wells taste of the drowned farmstead upstream. That gives a short investigation with a source to find.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 39 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The knoll is one that the flood has yet to top. In the wet months it holds the dry beds for an hour's walk in any direction.

name: Hollow Arch
why_founding: A stone bridge crosses the Onkobra at its narrowest reach near Gideon. The bridge has carried a toll since it was built.
why_site_advantages: A rock nose on each bank gives the stone arch its landings. The arch needs no piling.
why_occupants_motive: Gideon's council farms the toll out each year to the highest bidder. The toll rate changes every year.
why_pressures: The arch is hollow inside. The last toll farmer left the hollow unfilled. The current toll farmer has not filled it either.
why_would_change_if: If the toll rose above the cost of wet feet, travellers would bypass the bridge by the ford upstream.
siting_prefs_water_relation: spans a channel at its narrowest
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight
vibe_silhouette: One high stone arch spans green water. A toll house is built into the parapet.
vibe_palette: The stone is wet and grey. The water is black. The toll board is flaking white.
vibe_materials: The arch is made of Imperial voussoirs. The bridge house is built of the same stone and has a reed roof.
vibe_signature_feature: The rate board is rewritten every year. Each year a different hand writes over the last rate.
vibe_condition: The arch is sound on top. The east side is visibly failing at the springing.
vibe_approach: The road runs straight at the arch. The toll house sits under the parapet. The rate board comes into view before the toll-keeper does.
vibe_senses: Water runs under the stone. Coins sound at the toll house. A chain is drawn across the deck at night.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Hollow Arch toll house logs fewer arrivals than the Onkobra ferry logs crossings.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 17 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: A stone arch crosses the river at its narrows. A toll table stands on the arch. The crossing saves half a day.

name: Keeps-The-Lower-Water
why_founding: Gideon's hunting trade needs a keeper who lives on the ground that is hunted. The keeper says what may be taken and when.
why_site_advantages: The lodge stands on the river below the last village. Every boat going upstream passes the lodge door.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper licenses hunters and takes a share. The villages accept the licensing because the keeper also culls the predators that kill their stock.
why_pressures: Poachers work around the keeper. The keeper knows who the poachers are.
why_would_change_if: If the Gideon hunting trade collapsed, a village office would replace the lodge.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with a crossing, landing or light
vibe_silhouette: The lodge is a timber building on piles over the river bank. Skulls are fixed along the eaves, one for each year.
vibe_palette: The skulls are bone white on dark timber. The river is brown. The dog yard is dusty.
vibe_materials: The lodge is built of stilted timber and reed. The ornament on it is bone.
vibe_signature_feature: Each year the skull of one culled predator is added along the eaves. The oldest skull is at the far end.
vibe_condition: The lodge is well kept and heavily used. It smells of dogs.
vibe_mood: The lodge feels territorial. The keeper finds most visitors funny.
vibe_approach: The skull line can be read from the water at fifty metres.
vibe_senses: Dogs bark and move about the yard. The river runs past the lodge. A hide is scraped somewhere in the yard.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 23 m from the nearest route; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: The keeper says what may be hunted on the lower river. The keeper sends word downstream about anyone who ignores her.

name: Ladder-To-The-Light
why_founding: The fig canopy over the lower Onkobra is closed. A fringe village cannot see its own river through the canopy. Builders made a stack of platforms and ladders to put a lookout above the leaves. The platforms are now used for much more than the watch.
why_site_advantages: The site is a single very old fig with a straight bole. The fig stands on firm ground within sight of the road. It breaks the canopy by six metres.
why_occupants_motive: Three villages pay a lookout to sit up the tree in the flood season. The lookout watches which lanes are open. The rest of the year the village children have the tree.
why_pressures: Every platform is younger than the one below it. The bottom ladder is the oldest thing here. The tree is growing out of the fixings.
why_would_change_if: If the fig died, the site would be abandoned. No second tree of this height stands within two kilometres.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: placed where a viewshed pass shows a dead zone
vibe_silhouette: A great fig carries a spiral of eight timber platforms. A crow's nest stands above the leaf line. From a distance the tree looks as if it wears a staircase.
vibe_palette: The canopy is green-black. New lashings are pale on old grey timber. One lamp burns at the top after dark.
vibe_materials: The platforms are lashed timber and withy. Builders used no nails. Every platform is tied, so the tree can move.
vibe_signature_feature: The top platform breaks the canopy. From the top platform the river and the road are visible. Below the canopy only a wall of leaves shows.
vibe_condition: Repairs go on continuously from the top down. The lower ladders are the least sound.
vibe_mood: The place is practical. The sky is open at the top.
vibe_approach: The tree cannot be seen from any distance. Then it stands suddenly overhead. Boats steer by the lamp at night.
vibe_senses: The platforms creak and sway. Canopy insects are loud below. Only wind sounds above. The lookout rings a bell for open lanes.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tree is the fringe's one genuine viewpoint. A reveal there shows the region. A signal system serves three villages. The signal system can be silenced.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 182 m from the nearest route; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: Platforms are stacked up one old fig. The top platform gives a view of where the river goes.

name: Long Causeway
why_founding: The villages built the Long Causeway of lashed logs on driven piles. The causeway is low enough that a flood runs over it and does not take it away. The Imperial answer to the same water was an embankment.
why_site_advantages: The causeway crosses the widest shallow between the Gideon hinterland and the marsh edge. The bottom there takes a pile, but no bank would hold.
why_occupants_motive: Six villages each own a segment and maintain it. The causeway's quality changes every two hundred metres.
why_pressures: One village's segment is in dispute. That segment has the worst planks on the crossing.
why_would_change_if: The villages would go on replacing the causeway piecemeal forever.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: links two named places directly
vibe_silhouette: The causeway is a dark ribbon a hand's breadth above the water. It runs on until it disappears into haze.
vibe_palette: The timber is black and wet. The water is silver. Six slightly different timber colours show where the segments meet.
vibe_materials: The causeway uses lashed logs and plank decking on driven piles. Reed matting covers parts of the deck. Hand ropes are fitted only on the disputed segment.
vibe_signature_feature: Each village sets its totem at its own boundary. Six carvings stand along the causeway.
vibe_condition: The causeway is sound for most of its length. One stretch has lost piles and is knee-deep.
vibe_mood: Travel along the causeway is slow. Walkers are wet from the ankle down for a kilometre.
vibe_approach: The causeway runs flat to the horizon. Neither end is visible from the other.
vibe_senses: Water lies an inch below the planks. A bird colony nests half a kilometre off.
quest_hooks_opportunity: If the monsoon barrier can be opened in time, the causeway is the convoy's route.
why_site_won: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 4), 138 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'isthmus' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A log road is laid across the shallows on piles. In the wet months it is the dry way east.

name: Low-Water Fair
why_founding: When the water drops, the river bed becomes the widest flat surface in the marsh. Villages that otherwise meet by boat can meet on foot.
why_site_advantages: The site is a braided reach that dries to firm sand for eight weeks a year. The rest of the time the reach is four metres deep.
why_occupants_motive: Villagers come to settle marriages, debts and boundaries. They also come to trade.
why_pressures: A trader who miscalculates the rise loses the goods. That happens most years.
why_would_change_if: In a wet year the fair does not happen at all. There have been three wet years.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a landing, because most goods come by water
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: The fair stands on a dry river bed floored with pale sand. Mats are laid straight on the sand. Water still runs in one thread down the middle.
vibe_palette: The sand is bleached. The banks are wet green. The mats are dyed in every colour the villages have.
vibe_materials: The fair uses mats, poles and tethered boats hauled up the bank. No structure touches the river bed.
vibe_signature_feature: A stake stands at the level the water reached last year. The stake is absurdly high above the mats.
vibe_condition: Temporary. Kept immaculate.
vibe_approach: The fair lies down the bank. It sits below the level of the surrounding ground.
vibe_senses: Feet sound on sand. A single thread of water runs through the fair. Drums sound at dusk.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The seasonal fair is where the gate's untaxed goods surface.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 664 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.comes-back-slowly (+0.59).
player_purpose_hook: For eight weeks the river bed dries into the widest market floor in the west. Villages a week's walk apart trade on it.

name: Lower Onkobra Paddies
why_founding: Rice takes the flood that drowns the fringe's other crops. Gideon is fed from these terraces.
why_site_advantages: The site is a terraced flood plain with controllable inflow. The flood provides the irrigation. The sluice decides how much each terrace takes.
why_occupants_motive: The families here own the water. They do not own the land.
why_pressures: Imperial builders made the sluice. One gate has jammed open since the Oblivion Crisis. The lower terraces are permanently wet.
why_would_change_if: The paddies would be worth twice as much with a working gate.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a city's hinterland; owned
vibe_silhouette: Stepped pools of water mirror down a shallow slope. Each pool is a slightly different green. One stone sluice stands at the head.
vibe_palette: The paddies show twelve greens. Much sky is reflected in the water.
vibe_materials: The paddies use earth bunds and reed drying platforms. One Imperial stone sluice has an iron rack.
vibe_signature_feature: The jammed gate is propped and silted. Many offerings lie on it, like those at a shrine.
vibe_condition: The families maintain the earthworks well. The stonework cannot be repaired.
vibe_approach: The whole staircase of water shows from the low rise above it. The water flashes in the light.
vibe_senses: Water steps down the terraces. Bird-scarers sound. Frogs call at enormous volume after dark.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The crop is failing in a wedge. The wedge points straight back up at the mine.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 39 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; bound to river.352-503 within 200 m.
player_purpose_hook: Gideon's rice comes off these terraces. Disputes over the sluice decide how much each family harvests.

name: Lowmere
why_founding: The western lake's level swings four metres a year. Its people stopped building on the shore. They moored their houses out on the water.
why_site_advantages: The site is sheltered water behind a headland. The water is deep enough to keep the rafts off the mud. It is shallow enough to pole.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers stay out on the water. Gideon cannot evict a village that holds no land. The mooring-holder makes that point often.
why_pressures: Gideon's council has twice tried to tax the lake. Both times the village said it keeps no shore to tax.
why_would_change_if: If the sheltered moorings were lost, the villagers would come ashore.
siting_prefs_water_relation: moored on sheltered water, off the shore
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: has two or three fixed moorings keyed to the flood cycle
vibe_silhouette: Thirty low platforms are moored in a loose spiral. Each platform carries a reed house. The platforms sit a hand's breadth above black water.
vibe_palette: The reed is gold. The lake water is black. Every roof sits at a different angle.
vibe_materials: The platforms are lashed timber moored to driven piles. The houses are reed. Plank walkways are untied and relaid whenever a household falls out with its neighbour.
vibe_signature_feature: The platforms are moored in a spiral. The order is social. The oldest household sits at the centre.
vibe_condition: The villagers rebuild continuously. No platform is more than fifteen years old.
vibe_mood: The town is gossipy. The rafts are moored within earshot of each other.
vibe_approach: From the shore Lowmere is a low line of roofs on water. No land lies under it.
vibe_senses: Water runs under the floors. Timber knocks against piles. Conversation carries over three rafts.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A household's raft keeps drifting to the landing the town gave up. The town will pay to have the landing made usable again.
why_site_won: water narrows in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 1966 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Lowmere is a town moored out on the lake. The shore is under water half the year. The town has beds, boats and a harbourmaster with no harbour.

name: Marcian's Terrace
why_founding: A Nibenese surveyor called Marcian took a grant of upland shelf. Every lowland family had passed over the shelf. Imperial crops would grow on it. Two centuries later the village is Argonian. The village is still called after Marcian.
why_site_advantages: The shelf lies above the fever line and above the flood. The water on the shelf is clean. The nights are cold enough to keep grain.
why_occupants_motive: Terrace farmers sell dry grain into a province that mostly cannot grow it. The price they receive is enough to cover the carry down the stair.
why_pressures: Grain, salt and iron all come up the stair on porters' backs. In the dry months the villagers on the shelf live on stored water. Gideon's assessors tax upland grain as a luxury.
why_would_change_if: The village would empty in one generation if the cisterns failed. The cisterns are the oldest Imperial thing here.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a pass or an upland route; isolated
vibe_silhouette: Six stepped terraces of pale stone walling climb a green shelf. The houses stand along the top step.
vibe_palette: The walls are dry-stone grey. The upland grass is a hard yellow-green. The pantiles are terracotta.
vibe_materials: Dry-stone retaining walls stand under Nibenese pantile roofs. The houses where the tiles ran out have Argonian reed roofs.
vibe_signature_feature: Five Imperial-cut stone tanks lie under the top terrace. The tanks are still watertight.
vibe_condition: The buildings are old. The villagers patch them continuously and do not rebuild them.
vibe_mood: The villagers are thrifty. They are superior about the lowland.
vibe_approach: A stair path climbs to the village. The terraces open one at a time above the path. The last twenty minutes of the climb are in sight of the top step.
vibe_senses: Wind is heard and insects are not. Goat bells ring. Grain is turned on a stone floor.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The village sells dry grain that the lowland cannot make. It is an upland village that reads visibly non-Argonian in silhouette.
why_site_won: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 280 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Marcian's Terrace is a fringe village above both the fever line and the flood. It has clean water and cold nights.

name: Mile House of the Eagle
why_founding: The Mile House is a Legion road-house on the first stage west of Gideon. It stays open because travellers on the road still need a place to stop before the gate closes at dusk.
why_site_advantages: The site is the last firm, drained ground before the road drops to the flood plain. A walled yard is big enough for six carts.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper holds an inherited road-warrant. The warrant has not been renewed since the Legions left. The keeper produces it unprompted.
why_pressures: Fort Swampmoth's toll-takers stop at the Mile House too. The keeper cannot refuse them.
why_would_change_if: The Mile House would close the first year that the road did not carry carts.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road
vibe_silhouette: A long low tiled range stands beside a walled yard. Every other roofline on the ridge is round.
vibe_palette: A repainted door is Legion red. The stone is lichen grey. The cart tracks are ochre.
vibe_materials: The house is built of Imperial farmhouse masonry. A reed-thatched cart shelter has been added.
vibe_signature_feature: The milestone in the yard is still legible. It shows the distance to a city in another province.
vibe_condition: The house is sound and thriftily maintained. One range is shut up and used for hay.
vibe_mood: The house is sleepy and hospitable. It is still official on paper.
vibe_approach: The yard wall shows from a bend a good half-kilometre out. It is the last masonry before the notch.
vibe_senses: Cart axles creak. A dog barks. River fish fry and give off their smell.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A wheelwright's daughter vanished at noon on the road between the crossing and the Mile House.
why_site_won: ravine in upland hills (danger band 2), 195 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, nearPoint, region.
player_purpose_hook: The Mile House is a Legion road-house on the first stage west of the city. It still has a walled yard, a fire and a fixed rate for a bed.
siting_note: The place is bound to the Blackwood Road west of Gideon (round 4). The record's identity is a stage on that road. One march means the first stage of the road at province scale. One march is not a literal day.

name: Moonmarch Ground
why_founding: The road villages on the fringe keep the Argonian calendar on Imperial ground. For one month of the twelve the road villages between Gideon and the Onkobra empty out onto this flat. They hold Moonmarch there. During the other eleven months the flat is a field with post-holes in it.
why_site_advantages: The site is a wide dry flat that the monsoon does not reach. It lies close enough to three villages that the dancers walk home the same night. It lies far enough from Gideon that the magistracy does not attend.
why_occupants_motive: The ground-keeper's family holds the flat in order to keep it unbuilt. Their claim is older than the Imperial title that governs the flat.
why_pressures: Gideon's clerks have twice tried to license the gathering. Both times the villagers said there is no roof here to license. A Nibenese landowner has started grazing the flat out of season to establish use.
why_would_change_if: The ground would become a permanent fairground if a roof went up over it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: serves a settlement cluster
vibe_silhouette: For eleven months the ground is a flat field with a grid of post-holes and one stone. In the twelfth month a town of awnings stands there. The awnings are taller than the villages that came to it.
vibe_palette: The grass is yellow-green. Bare trodden earth shows the shape of last year's lanes. In season, dyed cloth from every village that comes hangs there.
vibe_materials: The moon-stone and the post-holes are the permanent part. Awnings, poles and cook-frames arrive on carts. They leave on the carts.
vibe_signature_feature: The post-holes hold the layout of a whole town in empty ground. They show which village pitches nearest the stone.
vibe_condition: The ground is empty. It is worn only where the lanes run.
vibe_mood: Off-season, the ground is empty. In season, it is very loud.
vibe_approach: The flat opens out beyond a low rise.
vibe_senses: Off-season, wind blows over grass. In season, three kinds of drum sound. Oil fries. A bell rings at moonrise.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Moonmarch is a festival that can be joined, missed or ruined. The ground holds a seasonal town that stands for one month a year.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 5 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.onkobra-field-station (+1.45).
player_purpose_hook: The road villages keep the Argonian calendar on Imperial ground for one month a year. Gideon's Imperial households are invited to Moonmarch.

name: Moonrack
why_founding: Folk alchemy here is a moon-timed craft. Calcining needs a level court that is laid out to the moons, not the sun.
why_site_advantages: The site is a flat upland shelf with an unobstructed eastern horizon. Such a horizon is rare below the rim.
why_occupants_motive: The two practitioners here sell reagents to Gideon. They refuse the apprentice who keeps coming back.
why_pressures: The alignment of the court is drifting out of true as the shelf slumps. The two practitioners argue about whether to move.
why_would_change_if: The court would be rebuilt entirely fifty metres east. It would not be adjusted.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a settlement, above canopy where possible
vibe_silhouette: A paved circle lies on an open shelf. A timber rack of shallow trays faces the eastern sky.
vibe_palette: The trays are ash white. The paving is slate. The glazed dishes are moon-blue.
vibe_materials: The court uses laid stone, fired clay dishes and a timber rack. The work is precise by the standards of the road villages.
vibe_signature_feature: The rack is angled and re-angled. Its post holes are drilled in a visible arc of past positions.
vibe_condition: The court is swept. It is out of true.
vibe_mood: The mood of the place is technical. The practitioners are superstitious about the things they measure.
vibe_approach: The shelf appears above the tree line. The rack breaks the skyline.
vibe_senses: Trays scrape. Wind blows on an open shelf. A mineral bitterness hangs in the air.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The calcinator court is the rival bid for Gideon's kiln contract.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 71 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: Moonrack is a calcining court laid out to the moons, not the sun. The alchemist will make what the Gideon apothecaries refuse.

name: Nine-Arch Stage
why_founding: A stage grew where the road crosses the flood plain on a nine-arched viaduct. The crossing takes longer than the daylight left.
why_site_advantages: The dry undercroft of the viaduct keeps the rain off. No other cover lies within two hours in either direction.
why_occupants_motive: The family here sells fuel and fodder. The family charges for the undercroft. The family does not own the undercroft.
why_pressures: Four arches have silted solid. Twice a decade the flood now goes over the road and not under it.
why_would_change_if: The stage would be abandoned if the viaduct failed. The stage family expects the viaduct to fail within their lifetimes.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road
vibe_silhouette: Nine arches stand on a dead-flat plain. Four of the arches are full of mud. The arches carry a road four metres above the water.
vibe_palette: The silt is grey. The mortar is weathered and pale. Green algae climbs to the flood line.
vibe_materials: The arches are Imperial cut stone. Reed lean-tos are wedged into the piers.
vibe_signature_feature: A flood scale is painted up the third pier. The family has repainted it higher three times.
vibe_condition: The road deck is sound. Floodwater is wearing away the piers below the deck.
vibe_approach: The arches can be read from a long way across the plain.
vibe_senses: Water drags at the silted arches. Swallows fly under the viaduct. Wind blows across the deck.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A pilgrim's pack arrives on the stage cart without the pilgrim.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 39 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: Nine-Arch Stage is the rain-proof stop. Two hours of open road lie on either side of it. The stage offers a fire under the arches and a cart out at dawn.

name: Ninefold
why_founding: Nine families of wheelwrights settled here. They rebuilt carts that the stone surface of the road had broken. The road stopped being paved before it was finished.
why_site_advantages: The site lies halfway between the fort and the marsh edge. It is on a widened length of the Gideon–Soulrest road. A gate there can stop a cart without blocking the ditch.
why_occupants_motive: A toll gang holds the workshops now. The gang charges for a road that stops two miles further east.
why_pressures: Fewer carts come through each season. The toll on each cart climbs.
why_would_change_if: Ninefold would empty if the road trade dried up entirely.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: day-travel spacing along a road
vibe_silhouette: Nine open-sided workshops stand around a rutted green. Their roofs sag. A gate is built across the road where there was none before.
vibe_palette: The sawdust is pale gone grey. The timber is brown. The iron tyres are rusted.
vibe_materials: The workshops are timber frames with failing reed roofs. The toll gate is the newest thing standing.
vibe_signature_feature: Failed wheels stand on edge and mark the village boundary. There are hundreds of them. Half of them are now sunk in the ground.
vibe_condition: The workshops are collapsing. The toll gang keeps the gate in good repair.
vibe_approach: The wheel fence still reads from the road for two hundred metres. The gate across the road is new.
vibe_senses: Iron rattles on the gate chain. Men wait at the gate. Nine silent workshops stand behind them.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 103 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Nine wheelwright workshops stand on a road stage left unfinished. A toll gang runs the gate now. The gang sets its own price.

name: Ninth Milestone House
why_founding: A family built the house against a Legion milestone. They found it easier to name themselves after the milestone than to name the place.
why_site_advantages: The site is nine miles from the gate. That is the distance a loaded porter covers before wanting to stop.
why_occupants_motive: Porters and pilgrims are the trade. The family sells water, shade and foot-binding.
why_pressures: The pilgrim traffic to Glenbridge has doubled. The well has not doubled. Deferred 2026-09-03 (Part 4 step 2): repetitive road-house fill within a kilometre of three others, held in reserve against the province record budget.
why_would_change_if: A bigger house would replace this one on the same spot. Every stop on this road grew that way.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: A single-storey house wraps around a Legion milestone. The milestone now holds up one corner of the porch.
vibe_palette: The walls are whitewashed. Dust lies over everything. The porch vine is deep green.
vibe_materials: The house is mud brick and reed. One Imperial stone predates everything else.
vibe_signature_feature: The milestone serves as the porch post. Two centuries of people leaning on it have polished its numeral.
vibe_condition: The house is modest and sound. The family constantly extends it by one room.
vibe_approach: The vine is visible from further away than the house.
vibe_senses: A well rope creaks. Travellers unwrap their feet. Bees hum in the vine.
player_purpose_hook: A family named themselves after a milestone. They trade every piece of road gossip between here and the gate.

name: Onkobra Clay Pits
why_founding: Red pottery is sold in Gideon. The pottery needs a red clay bank, a water source and a firing floor within a cart of the city.
why_site_advantages: A cut meander bank exposes the clay in a two-metre seam. The river carries away the waste. The river also brings the fuel.
why_occupants_motive: Four potting families work the pits in rotation. The families dispute the order of the rotation.
why_pressures: The river is undercutting the seam. The wintertide worm road comes up through a root breach in the same bank. The waykeepers want the bank left undisturbed.
why_would_change_if: The pits would move fifty metres upstream. The potting families have moved them three times before.
siting_prefs_water_relation: river clay; needs water and fuel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a navigable water for export
vibe_silhouette: A red gash cuts into a green bank. A field of pots dries in ranks. A squat stone furnace stands under a soot-blacked hood.
vibe_palette: The clay is signal red. The dust is pink. The furnace soot is black. The river is brown.
vibe_materials: The pits use raw clay, fired clay and reed drying racks. Fuel is stacked nearby. The stone furnace was paid for with Imperial money.
vibe_signature_feature: The seconds wall holds two centuries of failed pots. The potters pressed the pots into the flood bank as revetment.
vibe_condition: The pits are busy and muddy. The potters rebuild them every few years.
vibe_approach: The path turns. The whole bank is red.
vibe_senses: The clay is wet. Woodsmoke drifts off the fuel stacks. Potters tap pots for cracks. The pots ring.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The city's kiln contract is up. Two yards are bidding for it. One landing lies between the two yards.
why_site_won: local tie in firm lowland (danger band 2), 93 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; bound to river.352-503 within 200 m.
player_purpose_hook: Gideon's red clay comes out of this bank in a two-metre seam. It is dug and fired by people who owe the council for the privilege.

name: Onkobra Ferry
why_founding: The river below Gideon is too wide to bridge. It still has to be crossed.
why_site_advantages: A double bend slows the current to polling speed. Both banks shelve gently.
why_occupants_motive: The ferry family has held the crossing for four generations. The family treats the rope as its property.
why_pressures: The bonded warehouse opposite would prefer to load direct. That would cut the ferry family out.
why_would_change_if: The ferry would end when a bridge is built. The council proposes a bridge every decade.
siting_prefs_water_relation: across water too deep or wide to ford
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage
vibe_silhouette: A tarred plank raft runs on a rope. A slipway of laid brushwood leads to the raft. A shelter with one bench stands nearby.
vibe_palette: The tar is black. The river is brown. New brushwood is bright yellow.
vibe_materials: The ferry is built of plank and hemp. The shelter is reed on four poles.
vibe_signature_feature: The crossing order is chalked on the shelter wall. A traveller with a body to carry goes first.
vibe_condition: The ferry works hard and is patched. The ferry family replaces the rope twice a season.
vibe_approach: The road bends down through willow scrub. The water is suddenly a hundred metres wide.
vibe_senses: The rope creaks. Water laps on planks. The ferry bell rings once per crossing.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The ferry family's crossings outnumber the toll house's arrivals by three.
why_site_won: local tie in firm lowland (danger band 2), 8 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; bound to river.352-503 within 200 m.
player_purpose_hook: The ferry is the lower river's crossing. A punt, a ferryman and a queue wait there.

name: Onkobra Field Station
why_founding: Cyrodilic Collections needed somewhere to hold specimens between the licensed dig and the boat to Gideon. The licence for the station is pinned to its wall.
why_site_advantages: The station stands on the Onkobra bank where the current is slow enough to land a boat. The bank is high enough that the jars survive the monsoon.
why_occupants_motive: Two scholars and a local assistant live at the station. The assistant does the actual collecting. They stay because the licence is site-specific. Moving the licence would take two years.
why_pressures: The station is underfunded. One scholar is four years behind on her returns. The station sells duplicate specimens to pay for lamp oil. The assistant knows about the sales. The scholars think she does not know.
why_would_change_if: The station would close if the licence lapsed. The jars would end up in a Gideon tradehouse.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately near something interesting and far from help
vibe_silhouette: One long shuttered building stands on stilts with a jetty. From the water the rack of drying frames looks like a fence made of paper.
vibe_palette: The whitewash goes green at the base. The river is brown. After dark, lamp-light shines yellow through a hundred glass jars.
vibe_materials: The building is of Imperial plank-and-shutter construction. It stands on Argonian stilts.
vibe_signature_feature: An entire interior wall holds specimens in river-water. The labels on the specimens are in two hands. One of the hands stopped four years ago.
vibe_condition: The building is sound but shabby. All the repairs are local work on an Imperial frame.
vibe_mood: The mood of the station is earnest and tired. The returns that the scholars file are not honest.
vibe_approach: The lamps show on the water long before the building does.
vibe_senses: Preserving spirit and river mud smell strongly. A drying frame ticks. A scholar dictates a label aloud.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The station is a place to identify, sell or be paid for specimens outside a city. It is Cyrodilic Collections' fringe desk. The licence chain there makes a dig legal or illegal.
why_site_won: local tie in firm lowland (danger band 2), 52 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, nearPoint, region; bound to river.352-503 within 200 m.
player_purpose_hook: Specimens wait here for the boat to Gideon. The licence nailed to the wall does not cover half of what is in the crates.

name: Onkobra Kwama Mine
why_founding: Dunmer kwama husbandry is practised here at the far western end of its range. Buyers in Gideon take the eggs. Buyers in Leyawiin pay more for them. The workings changed hands in the 3E uprisings. Argonian mine hands took the kwama mines from their Dunmer owners. The Argonian owners keep the Dunmer husbandry technique going. The mine is owned by Argonians and not by Dunmer.
why_site_advantages: The site is a limestone shoulder above the Onkobra with dry galleries. It is the sole ground in the west that will hold a kwama colony.
why_occupants_motive: The mining family keeps the queen alive. The trade dies with her. The Owing hands work the mine because they were entered in a ledger.
why_pressures: Scribs get out. The colony has been pushed for two hundred years. The eggs are smaller than the ledgers say.
why_would_change_if: The mine would collapse in the year of the queen's death. The mine family's heir thinks that year is close.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a road for shipping
vibe_silhouette: A shed, a spoil heap and a black adit stand in a pale bluff. The bluff rises above brown water.
vibe_palette: The rock is chalk-pale. The spoil is ochre. Kwama chitin is a wet grey-green.
vibe_materials: The mine uses timber head-gear and an Imperial cart track. Underground, the galleries are unlined rock.
vibe_signature_feature: The queen's gallery is a domed dig with standing headroom. It is as warm as a byre.
vibe_condition: The mine is overworked and propped. The miners patch it with green timber.
vibe_approach: The road smells of the rendering shed a full minute before the adit shows.
vibe_senses: Chitin clicks underfoot. Water drips. The queen gives off a low continuous hum.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Mine water is reaching the paddies below in a widening wedge.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 356 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent.
player_purpose_hook: The mine is a site of Dunmer egg-mining at the far west of its range. It has dry galleries and a queen at the bottom. The eggs fetch a good price in the city.

name: Open-To-All
why_founding: The duty to shelter a comer is absolute. The people of the villages therefore maintain a house that is common property of no family.
why_site_advantages: The house stands at the saddle where four paths meet.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers keep the house by rota. The family whose month it is stocks the house. That family does not attend the house.
why_pressures: Foreigners keep trying to pay. Paying is an insult. The villagers forgive it as ignorance.
why_would_change_if: It would be a scandal if the house were ever found empty of fuel.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities
vibe_silhouette: A small round house stands on a bare saddle. The doorway has no door. A fire is laid, but it is unlit.
vibe_palette: The thatch is gold. The mud walls are ochre. The hearth is black.
vibe_materials: The walls are round mud-and-wattle. The roof is reed. A single stone hearth ring stands inside.
vibe_signature_feature: Fuel, water and dried fish are stocked by the hearth. They are ready for whoever comes.
vibe_condition: The house is immaculate. The newness of the thatch shows the rota.
vibe_approach: The house sits on the skyline of the saddle, small and pale. It has no gate and no wall.
vibe_senses: Wind blows in the doorway. Ash lies in the hearth. A deep quiet hangs over the saddle.
player_purpose_hook: The house is common property of no family. It is kept stocked for whoever arrives. The company is whoever is in it that night.

name: Hand-Read Halls
why_founding: The Orma were native to Black Marsh. The Orma were gone by the end of the Third Era. They built for people with no eyes. Orma work elsewhere has weathered past reading. These ridges can still be read by hand.
why_site_advantages: The site is a dry box canyon in the western hills. The canyon is enclosed and acoustically legible. The builders needed no more than that.
why_occupants_motive: The halls are unoccupied. Scholars have camped outside them for two seasons.
why_pressures: Every visitor brings a lamp. Lamplight makes the building unreadable.
why_would_change_if: A visitor who put the light out and followed the ridges by hand would reach the inner chamber of the halls.
vibe_silhouette: A doorway stands in a canyon wall. It has no lintel carving. No window opens anywhere above it. Two ridges run away from it into the dark.
vibe_palette: The halls are unrelieved dark. Dry pale stone shows at the mouth. Beyond the mouth everything is dark.
vibe_materials: The walls are dressed stone. Continuous guide-ridges run at hand height. Texture takes the place of ornament.
vibe_signature_feature: The ridges form a navigation system. It still works in total darkness.
vibe_condition: The halls are structurally sound. A lamp cannot read them at all.
vibe_mood: The halls feel enclosed. The Orma built them to be handled.
vibe_approach: Visitors meet the scholars' camp first. The camp has charts of an ornament scheme that does not exist.
vibe_senses: The chambers are proportioned for echo. Footsteps arrive back changed.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Hand-Read Halls is a ruin that is read by touch and sound. Sight does not read it. It is the province's single blind-architecture dungeon. Its Orma script can be reached only by rubbing and cannot be read by eye.
why_site_won: box canyon in upland hills (danger band 3), 806 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, region.
player_purpose_hook: The Orma built for people who could not see. These halls are read with the hands.
singular_claim: The place has countBand [1,1]. The sources say the Orma left almost nothing. A second site would contradict the source.

name: Red Cart Yard
why_founding: Freight changes carriers where the wheeled road ends and the marsh paths begin. A broker organises the change and takes a cut.
why_site_advantages: The yard is the last hard standing before the ground goes soft. Carts can go no further. Porters cannot start earlier.
why_occupants_motive: The yard master holds the porters' Owing entries. The labour cannot leave for a better yard.
why_pressures: Two porters have run this year. The yard master has posted their names.
why_would_change_if: The yard would lose its purpose if the causeway were ever built to cart standard.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a mandatory node between a boat lane and a land route
vibe_silhouette: A red-dust yard holds a load rack. A long open shed of hammocks stands beside it. No walls stand anywhere.
vibe_palette: The clay is red. The ropes are brown. The porters' issued sashes are pale blue.
vibe_materials: The yard has beaten earth, a timber load rack and reed shade. One lockable ledger box stands there.
vibe_signature_feature: The runaway board carries two painted names. The amount still owed is written under each name.
vibe_condition: The yard is hard-used and swept. The benches are backless on purpose.
vibe_approach: Cart noise stops. The road becomes a path.
vibe_senses: Hammock ropes creak. A tally is counted aloud. Dust hangs in the air.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A nine-man porter string failed to arrive. The carts were found parked and loaded.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 79 m from the nearest route; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The carts stop here and the porters take the loads onward. The brokers hire hands to carry the loads, or to see that a rival does not.

name: Red Daub Relay
why_founding: The province's letters move by running couriers. A run has to break where the ground changes.
why_site_advantages: The relay stands where the road path meets the marsh path. Red clay is daubed on the trees to mark it for people who cannot read.
why_occupants_motive: The runners hold the relay because the office is inherited. The office carries the right to refuse a letter.
why_pressures: The council wants the letters read. The runners will not read them.
why_would_change_if: If the running families agreed to be paid by the council instead of the senders, the relay would collapse.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay
vibe_silhouette: A post, a covered box on legs and a hammock frame stand at the relay. Red daub marks twelve trees around them.
vibe_palette: The clay marks are red. The bark is grey. The hammock is indigo.
vibe_materials: The relay has a waxed letter box and a reed shelter. Nothing there is lockable.
vibe_signature_feature: The refusal peg holds letters that the runners will not carry. The letters hang there for the sender to reclaim.
vibe_condition: Minimal, maintained daily.
vibe_approach: Travellers notice the daub marks first. The marks lead in to the relay.
vibe_senses: Cicadas sing. A runner leaves at a run.
player_purpose_hook: Letters leave this relay at a run. The runners carry letters out, or they repeat what was in the last one.

name: Reedcutters' Bridge
why_founding: The villagers built a timber bridge on the reed road. The deck is low on driven piles. The toll is paid in reed bundles, not coin.
why_site_advantages: The site is a slow, shallow reach. The bottom there takes a pile, so the crossing can be built by hand.
why_occupants_motive: The reed cutters maintain the bridge themselves. The toll is paid in cut reed. The cutters need reed but cannot carry it far.
why_pressures: Travellers who pay in coin are charged more. Foreigners think this is a joke.
why_would_change_if: If a tax-taker tried to farm the bridge, the cutters would pull it apart and carry it off in a night.
siting_prefs_water_relation: spans a channel at its narrowest
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight
vibe_silhouette: A dark timber deck lies almost flush on the water. Its piles are visible only from a boat.
vibe_palette: The reed is gold. The timber is black and wet. The water is tea-coloured.
vibe_materials: The bridge is lashed timber on driven piles. Reed fenders sit at both ends. The bridge has no metal.
vibe_signature_feature: The bundle post is where the toll is stacked as cut reed. The cutters restack it daily.
vibe_condition: The cutters constantly repair the bridge and do not rebuild it. No part of it is older than four years.
vibe_approach: Cut reed is stacked at the near end in every stage of drying. The smell reaches the path first.
vibe_senses: Reed rustles. Rope is wet. The planks underfoot were replaced this year.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The new tollkeeper wants coin. The bridge has been paid in reed bundles for four generations.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 42 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: A village bridge is tolled in reed bundles, not coin. Travellers who pay in coin are charged more.

name: Ridge Runners' Post
why_founding: The rim line north out of the fringe is faster than the road. No cart can use the rim line. Letters go that way and freight stays on the road.
why_site_advantages: The post stands on a saddle high enough that a runner can see the next saddle. Few saddles on the rim line manage that.
why_occupants_motive: Runners use the route because it halves the time to the north. Carters cannot use it because the last stretch is a scramble.
why_pressures: One bad section is washing out. The runners disagree about whether to report it.
why_would_change_if: If the runners stopped clearing the route, it would be lost in a season.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay
vibe_silhouette: A drystone wind shelter stands the height of a crouching person. A cairn stands beside it. Cloth is tied to the cairn.
vibe_palette: The rock is grey. The cloth has faded to no colour. Sky fills the view.
vibe_materials: The post uses dry stone and knotted cloth. That is the limit of what a runner will carry up.
vibe_signature_feature: Each runner ties one knot in passing. The cairn cloth reads as a tally.
vibe_condition: The post is weathered. The runners rebuild it after every storm.
vibe_approach: The path comes up out of a ravine. Two kilometres of view open at the top.
vibe_senses: Wind and cloth snapping.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A tamperer opens the sealed bag between stages. The tamperer then reseals it with a better seal.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 27 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The rim runners know the fast way north that no cart can use. They sell the route or run a message down it.

name: Rockgrove
why_founding: Rockgrove is a Sul-Xan holding in the Blackwood. The Sul-Xan stage raids from it. The raids take souls, not goods.
why_site_advantages: Ridge and thorn thicket screen the site on three sides. One ravine path gives access to the site. The noise of a camp is hidden by a stream.
why_occupants_motive: The Sul-Xan raid to feed soul-snares. The site persists because search parties cannot find it a second time.
why_pressures: Stonewastes' Four Winds hunt the Sul-Xan. The Empire's old bounty on jade masks is still quoted in Gideon. The Hist charge the Ca-Uxith with watching the xanmeer. The Ca-Uxith stone-talkers hold the ruins against the geyser field beneath the xanmeer.
why_would_change_if: The Sul-Xan would move after a serious defeat. Nothing here is fixed to the ground.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: within raiding distance of villages
vibe_silhouette: Empty ground runs up to the tree line. Past it, hide tents stand under a jade-green canopy. Poles hang with masks.
vibe_palette: Jade, blood-brown, deep shadow-green.
vibe_materials: The camp is built of hide, lashed poles and jade death masks. It has no permanent structure.
vibe_signature_feature: Soul-gems are strung on cord at head height. Raiders walk under them.
vibe_condition: The camp is temporary by design and filthy. The raiders keep the trophies in order.
vibe_approach: A raiders' path runs along a stream bed. Green tattoos show in the leaves at ten metres.
vibe_senses: Low chanting sounds. Flies buzz. Charged gems hum.
why_site_won: box canyon in firm lowland (danger band 3), 944 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: Rockgrove is a Sul-Xan staging ground for soul-taking raids. What the Sul-Xan have taken is still in the camp.

name: Rufio's Landing
why_founding: A Colovian family cut a fish landing into the lake wall. The water stays deep against the rock there. Three generations worked the landing. The last of them stopped coming down.
why_site_advantages: Deep water lies hard against a stone shelf. A boat can lie alongside without a jetty at any level the lake takes.
why_occupants_motive: The crocodiles keep the shelf. It is warm stone beside deep water. A slipway is already cut into it.
why_pressures: Lowmere's rafts need the deep channel past the shelf. The poling crews take a long way round. They lose an hour each way.
why_would_change_if: The landing would go back to work if the shelf were cleared. The cut stone is sound.
siting_prefs_water_relation: deep water against a stone shelf
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: within an hour's poling of the raft town it starves
vibe_silhouette: A cut stone shelf lies under a rock wall. A rotted boat rack is still bolted to it. No boat sits on the rack.
vibe_palette: The stone is wet and grey. The water is black. One strip of pale bone-dry rock lies at the top of the cut.
vibe_materials: The landing uses dressed Colovian kerbstone and iron ring bolts. A fish-drying frame has gone to sticks.
vibe_signature_feature: The slipway groove is worn into the rock and polished smooth. It is wide enough for a keel.
vibe_condition: The stonework is sound. The timber has gone.
vibe_approach: From the water the shelf looks like a usable landing. Then the shapes on the warm stone move.
vibe_senses: Flies buzz. Old fish smell strong. Water slaps under the cut.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Lowmere loses an hour of poling each way to this shelf. Clearing the shelf is a favour that the raft town can repay.
why_site_won: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 1445 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, landform.
player_purpose_hook: Rufio's Landing is a usable stone landing on the western lake. Crocodiles lying on the warm rock hold it.
interior_exterior_shell: The exterior shell is a cut stone shelf in the lake wall. The slipway is still in the shelf.
siting_note: The lair had a class with no way into it (round 4). The cut slipway now opens on the undercut where the crocodiles den. The landing can therefore be entered as a place. It is no longer seen as a dot on a cliff.

name: Sabinus' Claim
why_founding: The Niben crystal workings made two men rich a generation ago. Every year since, a Nibenese arrives on the fringe convinced that the seam runs east. Sabinus is the current one. He has a claim mark, a sample pile and about eleven weeks of food.
why_site_advantages: The site is a scree slope where the country rock is exposed without digging. It lies close enough to the road that a mule can reach it.
why_occupants_motive: Sabinus believes that the seam is here. His two hired locals are waiting to be paid. He has four weeks' coin left.
why_pressures: The sample pile is getting bigger and the food is getting smaller. Both are visible from the path.
why_would_change_if: The claim will be an abandoned camp by next season. Either Sabinus was wrong, or being right brings a hundred people and a licence.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a known extraction district
vibe_silhouette: Two tents stand on the scree. A spoil heap taller than either tent stands beside them. A peeled stake has a claim mark cut into it.
vibe_palette: The scree is grey-white. The canvas has gone brown. The fresh-cut wood of the claim stake is surprisingly bright.
vibe_materials: The camp uses Imperial canvas and imported tools. None of it is built. Sabinus carried it up and set it down among the scree.
vibe_signature_feature: The sample pile is sorted into rows by day. It holds eleven weeks of rows.
vibe_condition: The camp is getting worse week by week.
vibe_approach: The spoil heap is the first thing seen on the approach. It is far more work than two men should have done.
vibe_senses: A hammer strikes rock at a stubborn, unvarying rhythm. A cold wind blows. No cook-fire burns.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The claim can be shared, denounced to the licensing clerk or simply outlasted.
why_site_won: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 785 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Sabinus is another Nibenese prospector on the crystal scree. He is one season from ruin. He is certain that this time is different.

name: Saddle Fair
why_founding: Gideon's gate tax made it cheaper to trade outside the walls. The trade moved out.
why_site_advantages: The site is the flat saddle floor a kilometre west of the gate. It is drained. It is legally nowhere.
why_occupants_motive: Traders come because the fair has no tax. The council tolerates the fair because it can watch the whole field from the wall.
why_pressures: The council tries to enclose the fair every few years. Each time, the fair moves two hundred metres.
why_would_change_if: If the gate tax were dropped, the fair would be inside the city within a decade.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a landing, because most goods come by water
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: In season, two hundred striped awnings stand in a shallow bowl below the city wall. Out of season, worn rings mark the turf.
vibe_palette: The awning stripes are madder and indigo. The turf is grey-green. The city's tiles above are red.
vibe_materials: The fair uses market tents, hurdles and tethering lines. All of it is taken down within the week.
vibe_signature_feature: The pitch rings are bare circles in the grass. The same traders stand in them every year.
vibe_condition: The traders strike the ground bare between fairs. Law and preference both require it.
vibe_approach: The whole fair shows at once from the saddle lip.
vibe_senses: Auctioneers call. Guar low. Oil fries. Traders speak three languages.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Goods taxed at Gideon's gate are on sale untaxed a kilometre outside it.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 302 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Trade that will not pay Gideon's gate tax happens a kilometre outside it. The ground is legally nowhere.

name: Silver Mouth
why_founding: Silver Mouth is a Kothringi river town. It emptied inside one season in 2E 560 and has stood shut since.
why_site_advantages: The town stands at a river mouth on the lake. The Kothringi laid a stone quay. They built to last.
why_occupants_motive: The neighbouring villages regard the ground as still infectious. Three hundred years have passed.
why_pressures: The quay is the best landing on the lake. The taboo keeps it empty.
why_would_change_if: If a single respected voice said that the ground was clean, villagers would occupy the town.
siting_prefs_water_relation: coastal and riverine — they were sea-going
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the west and centre, where the Kothringi lived
vibe_silhouette: A stone quay stands at the lake. Three parallel streets of roofless houses run down into the lake.
vibe_palette: The stone is silver-grey. The lake is blue-black. No green grows on the paving.
vibe_materials: The town is built of Kothringi coursed stone. The stone is squarer and older than the Imperial work at Gideon.
vibe_signature_feature: The streets continue underwater. A diver can follow them.
vibe_condition: The houses are roofless. The walls stand to two storeys and are undisturbed.
vibe_approach: By boat the town appears all at once as a stone shore. A stone shore is rare in this province.
vibe_senses: Water lies in stone doorways. A hollow echo sounds. Unusually few birds call.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A dealer is selling grave silver with papers. He has not entered the site that the papers name.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 402 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, culture-clump, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Silver Mouth is a Kothringi river town that emptied in a single season. It has stood unentered since. The stone quay is still there.

name: Silver Cairns
why_founding: The Kothringi buried their dead under stone. This hillside holds the cairns of a whole community. The burials date from the last generation before the Flu.
why_site_advantages: The site is a stony hill shoulder. Cairn stone lay ready to hand there.
why_occupants_motive: The neighbouring villages leave the cairns undisturbed. Argonian custom has no use for a cairn.
why_pressures: Treasure-hunters take the glass beads from the cairns. The practice is old. Some cairns have been opened twice.
why_would_change_if: The cairns would be protected if the Gideon magistracy had standing over the graves of a dead people.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: beside a lost-peoples ruin
vibe_silhouette: Two hundred stone mounds stand on an open hillside. A third of the mounds are opened. Their stones have spilled downhill.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone and pale grass. Blue-green glass glints in the spoil.
vibe_materials: The mounds are dry-stacked local stone. The glass beads are the worked part of the site.
vibe_signature_feature: The opened cairns have spilled their stones downslope in fans. From a distance the hillside looks damaged.
vibe_condition: Two thirds of the cairns are intact. One third are robbed and left open.
vibe_mood: The ground is exposed. Thieves have worked it over.
vibe_approach: The mounds break the skyline as seen from the valley track.
vibe_senses: Wind blows over the stones. Glass grinds underfoot.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A Gideon silver dealer claims the cairns as the provenance of his stock. The dealer has not visited them.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 35 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-art-and-ash-place (+1.42).
player_purpose_hook: The cairns hold the burials of a whole community from the last generation before the Flu. Dealers in Gideon's antiquities trade know what the cairns are worth.

name: Sink Field
why_founding: The field lies on a clay pan that drains nowhere. It has been out of the estate's rotation for thirty years.
why_site_advantages: Warm shallow water lies over clay. Weed grows thick and frogs are numerous. Death hoppers breed in such conditions.
why_occupants_motive: The death hoppers hold the whole pan. They spread along the ditch when the water rises.
why_pressures: The estate's east ditch runs through the field. The ditch needs clearing every spring. Two men have been carried out of the field.
why_would_change_if: Cutting the pan open to the ditch would drain the field in a week. The death hoppers would then take the next low ground down the line.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a silted field ditch with no fall
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the edge of estate ground, off the walked tracks
vibe_silhouette: The field is flat and green, with water underfoot. A ditch bank runs through the middle.
vibe_palette: The colours are weed green and clay yellow at the ditch cut. Frog-back blue and red show in the shallows.
vibe_materials: The site holds clay, weed and a rotted sluice board. A culvert mouth opens under the bank.
vibe_signature_feature: The old culvert still runs under the field. The culvert is dry enough at the mouth for crawling.
vibe_condition: The field has been out of use for thirty years. It grows wetter every season.
vibe_approach: The ditch bank is the firm walking. It runs within hearing of the death hoppers.
vibe_senses: Frogs call by the thousand. Then all of them stop at once.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Draining the field is a job with a clear before and after. The estate is then obliged to admit whose ditch it is.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1088 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on nearPoint, landform, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The field is drowned and full of death hoppers. The culvert under it can be used to drain the field.

name: Slough Point
why_founding: The Empire put its census and excise station where the Blackwood Road first touches navigable water. Goods can be counted twice there.
why_site_advantages: The site is a firm bank at the head of a slow reach. Carts arrive and boats leave. Goods are weighed here between the two.
why_occupants_motive: The excise remains because the collectors live on it. The census remains because its ledgers are the proof to Gideon that a resident exists.
why_pressures: Sap, hides and grain now go by the rim paths. The town's takings fall every year.
why_would_change_if: The town would die if the road were abandoned. It would become rich again if a state ever taxed the marsh in earnest.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the province's border; one of only three or four
vibe_silhouette: The town has a weighbridge, a long bonded shed and a jetty. They are strung out along one street. The street has no middle.
vibe_palette: The colours are whitewashed lime going green, tar-black sheds and brown water.
vibe_materials: The older buildings are Imperial farmhouse timber and plaster. The later additions have Argonian reed roofs.
vibe_signature_feature: The census board stands outside the excise house. Names are still being added to it in three scripts.
vibe_condition: The town is shabby. It is over-built for the traffic it gets.
vibe_approach: The road widens into the town. The tar sheds stand at the near end.
vibe_senses: Tally sticks click and tar drips. A bell is rung for the ferry.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The hook concerns census and excise. It is a documented-identity hook.
why_site_won: open water in firm lowland (danger band 3), 875 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, navigable.
player_purpose_hook: Goods off the road are weighed, counted and written down here. Travellers are entered in the same book.

name: Customs Waiting Shed
why_founding: Slough Point's excise came with a census. In a province marked by the Knahaten Flu, a census brings an inspection shed.
why_site_advantages: The shed stands on the landing, before the weighbridge. Everything passing inland is looked at first.
why_occupants_motive: The inspectors keep the shed because the fee for release is theirs. No traveller has been detained in living memory.
why_pressures: The forms still contain questions about a plague. The plague ended two centuries ago. The forms are in a script that most travellers cannot read.
why_would_change_if: The shed would be repurposed as a store if the excise lapsed.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: at a legal port or border crossing
vibe_silhouette: The shed has slat sides and stands on the landing. Benches run down both walls. A smoking brazier stands in the middle.
vibe_palette: The colours are smoke-stained timber and brazier red. The green of the river shows through the slats.
vibe_materials: The shed is timber slats on a stone brazier plinth. An Imperial noticeboard hangs there and has never been updated.
vibe_signature_feature: The inspectors still issue an Imperial plague questionnaire. The questionnaire is in Cyrodiilic.
vibe_condition: The shed is sound and sooty. It holds more benches than travellers need.
vibe_approach: The shed is the first building off the jetty. The way inland passes through it.
vibe_senses: Smoke fills the shed. A stamp falls. The river slaps the piles.
player_purpose_hook: Travellers wait in the shed to be judged clean. Word gets out there about who is coming into the province.

name: Sour Orchard
why_founding: The site is an Archein fig orchard left standing when the quarters emptied. The trees still bear. The figs rot where they drop.
why_site_advantages: Dead limbs above open rows give the birds height. They also give the birds a clear drop.
why_occupants_motive: The flock feeds on what the fallen fruit brings up. It also stoops on anyone crossing the rows below.
why_pressures: The rows need to be walked again for the fig wood. The estate sells the fig wood in Gideon.
why_would_change_if: Culling the roost would free the wood for cutting. The flock would take the next orchard along the line.
siting_prefs_water_relation: an old irrigation ditch, half silted
