siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: within an hour of a derelict estate
vibe_silhouette: The fig rows are straight. Half of the trees are dead standing. Birds turn above the far end.
vibe_palette: The colours are fig green going black underfoot, grey dead wood and white bird lime on the rows.
vibe_materials: The site has fig wood and a ditch wall of dressed stone. A picking ladder still leans against a trunk.
vibe_signature_feature: The rows are still straight. The flight lines of the birds follow the rows.
vibe_condition: The orchard has been untended for a generation. The trees still bear heavily.
vibe_approach: The smell of fermenting fruit carries well beyond the rows.
vibe_senses: Flies swarm in numbers. Fruit bursts underfoot. A saw-edged call sounds overhead.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The estate offers cutting rights in trade for a cull. The cutting rights give a poor household a season's income.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 343 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, nearPoint, route.
player_purpose_hook: The dead fig orchard has birds that stoop down the rows. Payment from the estate is in cutting rights.

name: Stonefoot
why_founding: Upland Argonians terrace the hillside. These hills give the slope and the loose stone that terracing needs.
why_site_advantages: The site is a south-facing slope above the ravine head. Spring water rises at the top. Loose stone is available for building the terraces.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers stay because terraces are generational work. Abandoning them would waste four lifetimes.
why_pressures: Using stone for the terrace walls is a compromise. The lowland villages needle the villagers about it constantly.
why_would_change_if: The terraces and the village would both collapse if the spring at the top failed.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a pass or an upland route; isolated
vibe_silhouette: Twenty stone-walled terraces step up a hillside. A house stands at the end of every third terrace.
vibe_palette: The colours are dry-stone grey and terrace-crop green in bands. Brown earth lies between the bands.
vibe_materials: The lower walls are dry stone. The houses above are mud and reed.
vibe_signature_feature: The water ladder is a stone channel running down the terrace ends. A wooden gate stands at each level.
vibe_condition: The terraces are superbly maintained. A fallen terrace wall is a village emergency.
vibe_approach: The banding of the terraces shows from the valley floor at a kilometre.
vibe_senses: Water runs down the ladder. Goats graze. Villagers reset stone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Loads move off the terrace at night that the terrace does not grow. The trail leads to the smugglers' ledge.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 287 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Terraced hill farms stand above the ravine head. Spring water rises at the top. A bed above the whole valley is available.

name: Stonewastes
why_founding: Stonewastes is a bogland town grown around a xanmeer keep. Its people have used the keep without a break. The hereditary Four Winds have defended it since the first hut went up.
why_site_advantages: The stone walls already existed. They stand on the firm ground of a bog. Raiders cross the bog slowly.
why_occupants_motive: The Four Winds hold the keep by hereditary right. The Sul-Xan raiding out of the Blackwood is why the office has held.
why_pressures: Four hereditary captains share one gate. The captains do not agree. The Sul-Xan press harder each dry season.
why_would_change_if: The town would change utterly if the Four Winds ever accepted an outside charter. The Marsh Charter intends to ask them for one.
siting_prefs_water_relation: defensible approach, often a single crossing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the Blackwood bogland's only defended town; Glenbridge a day south
vibe_silhouette: A stepped stone keep rises out of low mud-and-thatch roofs. Four banner poles stand on the terrace, one per wind.
vibe_palette: The colours are bog-brown and grey-green stone. Four dyed banners are ochre, indigo, white and black.
vibe_materials: The keep is ancient xanmeer masonry. The villagers maintain it but do not imitate it. Their own building is mud, wattle and thatch.
vibe_signature_feature: The Four Winds' drill ground lies on the keep terrace. Drill has worn four wheel-shaped paths into the stone.
vibe_condition: The stone is impeccably kept. The mud and thatch are rebuilt when they rot.
vibe_mood: The town is martial and proud. Strangers are received courteously. They are asked their business twice.
vibe_approach: The causeway runs straight at the keep for four hundred metres. Wet ground lies on both sides. The whole length of the causeway is in view of the terrace.
vibe_senses: Drill counting sounds. Thatch is wet. A hollow drum is used as a gate signal.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The hook features a hist in the town centre. It features a xanmeer keep. It features the Four Winds as hereditary defenders.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: FG08 · tier-2; LF53 · tier-3; LF54 · tier-3; LF55 · tier-3; LF56 · tier-3; LF57 · tier-3; LF58 · tier-3; LF59 · tier-3; LF60 · tier-3; LF61 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 677 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.westfield-village (+1.27).
player_purpose_hook: A town lives inside a xanmeer keep. Its people have held the keep without a break. Four hereditary captains defend it.

name: Swampmoth Town
why_founding: The soldiers of a garrison eat, drink and buy. A town grows below the gate of a fort whether or not the garrison is legitimate.
why_site_advantages: The town stands on the apron of firm ground below the fort's wall. It lies inside the arc that the fort can protect.
why_occupants_motive: The townsfolk live off the toll company. In public the townsfolk say otherwise.
why_pressures: If the tolls fail, the townsfolk go hungry. The townsfolk support the company for that reason.
why_would_change_if: The town would survive as a road village at a third of its size. That is what the town was before.
siting_prefs_water_relation: at a crossing or a road
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with a fort, occupied or not
vibe_silhouette: One street of shuttered fronts runs under the fort wall. Every roof is lower than the curtain wall above it.
vibe_palette: Wall-shadow grey covers the street for half the day. Then hard light falls on painted shutters and rust.
vibe_materials: The town is built of mud-brick and timber, set tight against Imperial masonry. The buildings are not bonded to the masonry.
vibe_signature_feature: The townsfolk set their day by the shadow line on the street.
vibe_condition: The town is cramped and prosperous. The buildings stand too close to the wall to be safe.
vibe_approach: The road comes up under the fort. The town is a strip of roofs in the shadow of the fort.
vibe_senses: Boots sound on the stone above and a smithy rings. Shutters close when the company comes down.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The garrison town keeps Imperial military process at arm's length from Gideon's courts. A supply contract is worth corrupting. The quartermaster allows it. Billeting makes a place where a fugitive can be legally, uncomfortably, safe.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: FG05 · tier-2; LF62 · tier-3; LF63 · tier-3; LF64 · tier-3; LF65 · tier-3; LF66 · tier-3; LF67 · tier-3; LF68 · tier-3; LF69 · tier-3; LF70 · tier-3
why_site_won: local tie in upland hills (danger band 2), 298 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump-yielded, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2-region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: The town stands under the gate of the fort. The toll company pays for the well, the watch and the beer.

name: Takes-The-Field
why_founding: When an Owing is called in on land, men must go and take the field. The brokers hire men to do it.
why_site_advantages: The camp is set on the boundary of the fields that it holds.
why_occupants_motive: The brokers pay the men by the day. The men keep a household off ground that the household worked.
why_pressures: The villagers feed the camp but hate it. The brokers deny that the camp exists.
why_would_change_if: The camp would break up when the debt is bought out. Whoever chooses to pay can buy it out.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the edge of a worked field within sight of a village
vibe_silhouette: A rope line stretches across a field gate and a fire burns behind it. A table holds a writ that is weighted down.
vibe_palette: The colours are rice green, rope hemp and one red seal.
vibe_materials: The camp uses borrowed canvas and a borrowed table. It also has one very good lock.
vibe_signature_feature: The writ lies on the table in a case. The clerk produces it to any traveller who asks.
vibe_condition: The camp is temporary. The camp is in no hurry to end.
vibe_mood: The camp is legal and patient. It is widely hated.
vibe_approach: A rope crosses the field path short of the gate.
vibe_senses: Rice water smells and the clerk reads aloud. The fire of the household burns on the far verge.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The camp is supplied from inside Swampmoth Town. The supply runs on the account of the company.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 387 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route.
player_purpose_hook: A rope stretches across a field gate and a writ lies on a table. Men who are paid by the day keep a family off its own rice.

name: Abandoned Survey
why_founding: An Imperial survey party set out to run a level line from Gideon to the pass. The party stopped mid-line forty years ago. The camp is still where the party left it.
why_site_advantages: The site is a dry knoll on the line itself. The surveyors chose it for sightlines between stations. They did not choose it for shelter or water. No village has moved onto it.
why_occupants_motive: The surveyors walked out and left the tents pitched. The knoll has stayed unclaimed for forty years.
why_pressures: The canopy has closed over two of the survey stations. The third station is under water.
why_would_change_if: The line would start a road if it were ever finished. Forty years later, the villagers plan their journeys around the swamp.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: chained along a planned route
vibe_silhouette: Two collapsed tent frames and a tripod stand on a bare knoll. The scrub has not come back there. The tripod is still standing.
vibe_palette: The colours are bleached canvas rags and silvered wood. A level on its tripod has gone brass-green.
vibe_materials: Imperial survey kit rots in place. The kit includes canvas, brass, ranging rods and a chain in its case.
vibe_signature_feature: The tripod is still standing and still level. It was set for a sighting that was never taken.
vibe_condition: Forty years of decay have gone untouched. In this climate the decay is thorough but not total.
vibe_approach: The bare knoll shows first, where the scrub will not grow. The tripod shows on the climb.
vibe_senses: Canvas snaps in the wind. No bird sings on the knoll itself. The cut of the survey line sounds as a change in insect noise.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The field book explains why the survey stopped, in the surveyor's own hand. Three survey stations remain to find. One station is canopied, one is drowned and one is intact.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 20 m from the nearest route; no free 'summit' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: A survey camp stands with its instruments still set up. The party walked out unharried. The line that the party was measuring is still on the ground.
siting_note: The record was converted from a hostile record to a neutral one in the round-4 hostility rebalance. This neighbourhood already carried three route-side fights inside 250 m.

name: Makes-And-Burns
why_founding: Nisswo doctrine holds that a made thing must be unmade. Pilgrims on the sermon road need a place to do it.
why_site_advantages: The site is a gravel spit in a river bend. It is a flat working floor. The flood clears it entirely every year.
why_occupants_motive: Pilgrims make something here and destroy it. What stands on the spit is the work not yet unmade.
why_pressures: Collectors have started stealing pieces before the pilgrims can unmake them.
why_would_change_if: The site would be spoiled permanently if a piece from here were ever displayed in Gideon.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a Nisswo circuit
vibe_silhouette: A gravel spit is covered in half-finished sculpture. At one end lies a burn patch. The ash there is a foot deep.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey gravel and ash white. The pieces of the day add their own colours.
vibe_materials: Pieces are made of clay, reed, bone and river stone. All of it comes off the spit.
vibe_signature_feature: The ash end holds a year of destroyed work in one heap.
vibe_condition: Nothing standing is over a year old. Doctrine and the flood both ensure it.
vibe_approach: The colour of the pieces shows from upstream before their shapes do.
vibe_senses: The river runs over gravel. Pilgrims work clay. Pilgrims break a piece deliberately.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One piece of this season's work is wanted for keeping. Keeping it goes against the whole point of the site.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 27 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.silverhand-cairns (+1.42).
player_purpose_hook: Pilgrims unmake what they have made on this gravel spit. Visitors may bring a piece of their own to the burn patch.

name: The Back Kiln
why_founding: A disused potters' firing house stands outside the clay pits. It became the place where the night trade of Gideon happens out of sight.
why_site_advantages: The firing house is a stone shed with a dead furnace. It has one door and no windows. It holds heat and hides light. Daril ferments there and the road cannot smell it.
why_occupants_motive: An Owing broker keeps a fermentary running here. The broker pays the tower clerk to keep the site listed derelict.
why_pressures: The vats need constant tending. Whoever the broker trusts with that job knows enough to ruin him.
why_would_change_if: The council would burn the kiln out in the week it became embarrassing and stopped being useful.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a mooring is half the type
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter
vibe_silhouette: A low stone shed stands in a nettle field. Light leaks under one door. No smoke rises.
vibe_palette: The colours are soot black, ember orange and nettle green.
vibe_materials: The shed has stone walls, a cold furnace and its hood. Reed baffles cover the flue. Vats stand on the old firing floor.
vibe_signature_feature: The firing floor is now a ring of covered vats. A keeper's hand stirs each vat as a job.
vibe_condition: The building is structurally fine. It is left looking derelict from outside on purpose.
vibe_mood: The air inside is close and hot. It is sour with daril.
vibe_approach: There is no path. The trodden nettles show the way.
vibe_senses: Daril ferments in a closed room. Low voices murmur. A keeper counts stock aloud.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The kiln is the Night-Reed's fringe fence-den. It is where interior goods lose their provenance before reaching Gideon.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 361 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-old-office-house (+1.00).
player_purpose_hook: A dead firing house has one door and no windows. An Owing broker ferments daril there. The site is under a paid-off derelict listing.

name: The Black Tarn
why_founding: A deep cold tarn in a rim basin holds something old. The villagers have a rule about it. The rule predates their stories.
why_site_advantages: The tarn fills a drowned box canyon with sheer walls. It holds forty metres of cold water. It has one narrow outlet.
why_occupants_motive: No household stands here. The rule permits drinking at the outlet. The rule forbids drinking from the tarn.
why_pressures: Treasure-hunters ignore the rule roughly once a decade.
why_would_change_if: The site would not change. No rail or fence has gone up in living memory.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the apex hazard of its region; routes bend around it
vibe_silhouette: Black water lies in a stone bowl, absolutely still. A pale drinking step stands at the outlet.
vibe_palette: The colours are black, stone grey and one white line of outflow.
vibe_materials: A single cut step, worn hollow, is the only built work. There is no other building.
vibe_signature_feature: The drinking step is cut at the outlet. It lies well back from the tarn itself.
vibe_condition: The step and the bowl are as the last generation left them.
vibe_approach: The route is a climb into a bowl. The water of the tarn differs in colour from the water of the lake into which the tarn drains.
vibe_senses: The outflow runs. No birds sit on the water and no insects fly over it.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The hunting trade of Gideon will pay for proof of what takes boats off the tarn. The trade will also pay for the head of the creature.
why_site_won: box canyon in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 709 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: A drowned canyon holds forty metres of cold water. Drinking is permitted at the outlet. Drinking from the tarn is forbidden.

name: The Borrowed House
why_founding: An Imperial road villa emptied two centuries ago. One family has lived in three of its rooms for two generations.
why_site_advantages: The villa is dry and roofed. It stands off the road behind a hedge that has become a wall.
why_occupants_motive: The family lives here because it is free. They built a reed house inside the atrium. They do not live in the stone rooms.
why_pressures: Living in dead stone is a compromise. Their neighbours mention it. The reed house inside is the answer of the family.
why_would_change_if: The family would abandon the villa without regret when the roof went.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: inside any ruin type
vibe_silhouette: A villa's tiled roof rises over a hedge. Inside the courtyard stands a reed house with its own little roof.
vibe_palette: The colours are terracotta above, reed gold in the courtyard and hedge green on every side.
vibe_materials: The Imperial masonry serves as a shell. The actual dwelling inside is entirely reed and mud.
vibe_signature_feature: A complete reed house stands inside a colonnaded courtyard.
vibe_condition: The Imperial fabric is failing. The reed house is new.
vibe_approach: The hedge hides the villa entirely. A path leads in through a gap.
vibe_senses: Chickens roam the peristyle. Rain falls on tiles and then on reed, so two roofs sound at once.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The sealed cellar under a squatted ruin holds evidence. The eviction case lacks that evidence.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 280 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.treasure-hunters-camp-of-the-white-hill (+0.49).
player_purpose_hook: One family has lived in three rooms of an Imperial villa for two generations. The other twenty rooms are as their owners left them.

name: The Broke Column
why_founding: Part of the column on the border road deserted when the Legion was recalled about two centuries ago. The Legion never paid the deserters, who had not been paid at the recall. The men in the camp now are the deserters' sons and grandsons, who keep the duty roster and wear the colours as an inheritance.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on a small level bench beside a spring-fed upland tarn. The bench lies in the hills above the Mile House track and is out of sight of the Gideon road. The uphill side of the bench is covered by the hill above it.
why_occupants_motive: The men keep watches and wear the Legion colours. They take money from each traveller. They call it a levy.
why_pressures: Gideon's governor will not pay to clear the camp. The toll company's officers would use the men for their own ends.
why_would_change_if: If Gideon offered the men a pardon and a wage, they would disband.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a spring tarn at its back
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: off the Gideon road, within a walk of the Mile House
vibe_silhouette: Four Legion tents stand pitched in a dressed line. The ground is steep. The small bench is level.
vibe_palette: The palette is Imperial red faded to brown on the cloth, dull steel and churned mud.
vibe_materials: The tents are Legion issue canvas. The men use Legion issue tools. A palisade of sharpened poles surrounds the camp.
vibe_signature_feature: The duty roster is nailed to a tree. A clerk keeps the roster current in his own hand.
vibe_condition: Militarily tidy, but starving.
vibe_approach: The track narrows at a barricade below the tents. A man steps out at the barricade and asks for the levy in correct Legion phrasing.
vibe_senses: The camp smells of woodsmoke. The watch is called on the hour. The men speak little.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The serjeant parleys before he fights. The pardon question can be settled without clearing the camp.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: FG07 · tier-2; LF21 · tier-3; LQ15 · tier-3
why_site_won: spring head in upland hills (danger band 2), 165 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on nearPoint, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The camp is held by the sons and grandsons of a Legion column that was left unpaid at the recall. The camp stands on a bench above a track junction off the Gideon road, where the men take money from travellers and call it a levy.
watch_reason: The column's descendants keep the duty roster and stand watch at the barricade under the serjeant.

name: The Buried Spears
why_founding: The Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War. They buried their weapons and did not surrender them.
why_site_advantages: The weapons lie under a bank of dry sand above the flood line. Iron keeps there. The people who buried the weapons expected to come back.
why_occupants_motive: The people who buried the spears have not come back. The location is passed on as a story with directions in it.
why_pressures: The Owing brokers would pay for the location. The Marsh Charter would also pay, for opposite reasons.
why_would_change_if: The cache would be a serious political object the day it was dug up.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a battlefield or a village of the period
vibe_silhouette: A sand bank lies under three trees. One tree is carved at head height. Imperial surveyors read the mark as damage.
vibe_palette: The colours are pale sand, grey bark and leaf shadow.
vibe_materials: There is no building. The cache is bundled hide and pitch. The marker is a carving.
vibe_signature_feature: The carving is a Jel word for 'enough'.
vibe_condition: The site is undisturbed. The pitch has held.
vibe_mood: The site is ordinary. Nothing at the site marks it out.
vibe_approach: The site is invisible from the path. The directions come with the story.
vibe_senses: Wind stirs three trees. Sand moves under the wind.
quest_hooks_opportunity: People who expect a war that has not been declared are digging up the cache.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 28 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, culture-clump, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-hollow-under-the-figs (+1.06).
player_purpose_hook: The weapons of the Blackwater War were buried here and not surrendered. Dry sand keeps iron.

name: The Cold Forge
why_founding: Traffic on the western road runs on iron tyres. A smith in the west still works iron for that reason.
why_site_advantages: The forge stands beside the bog-iron workings. It lies downwind of the village. The neighbours insisted on that.
why_occupants_motive: The smith is Imperial-trained and Argonian-born.
why_pressures: Most of the smith's neighbours regard working metal as a moral error. They still bring him their tyres.
why_would_change_if: The forge would close once the road stopped carrying carts.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a road, in a port, or hidden
vibe_silhouette: A stone-built forge with a tall chimney stands alone in cleared ground. No house stands nearer than a kilometre.
vibe_palette: The colours are charcoal black, forge orange and the scoured pale of cleared ground.
vibe_materials: The forge is built of cut stone and iron. Both materials are distrusted here.
vibe_signature_feature: An offering shelf stands outside the door. Neighbours leave work and payment there without entering.
vibe_condition: The forge is in excellent condition. The roof and the bellows are unpatched.
vibe_approach: The chimney smoke shows first. Charcoal can be smelled a long way out.
vibe_senses: Hammer strikes anvil, arriving in pairs. The bellows blow. Hot metal is quenched.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Work is accepted at the forge only from a customer who can name the use of the metal.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 394 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The smith will touch bog iron, which the Gideon shops refuse. He mends a tyre or a blade and gives his opinion of the customer's gear.

name: The Cold Lights
why_founding: A cold spring feeds one arm of the lake. Whatever lives in the water lights when it is disturbed.
why_site_advantages: The arm is a dead end with no current. The bloom is not flushed out.
why_occupants_motive: The raft village steers by the bloom. The villagers will not put a hand in the water after dark.
why_pressures: The glow is dimmer than it was. The village argues about whether the spring or the lake is the cause.
why_would_change_if: The raft village would lose its night navigation if the glow failed.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: known and visited; a destination, not a secret
vibe_silhouette: Black water lights blue-green where a paddle touches it. The glow stays in the wake for a few seconds.
vibe_palette: After dark the colours are black and one blue-green.
vibe_materials: One pole marks the arm's mouth. There is no building.
vibe_signature_feature: The glow marks a swimmer's track for a few seconds afterwards.
vibe_condition: The glow is measurably dimmer up close than it was.
vibe_approach: By day the arm is unremarkable.
vibe_senses: Almost silent.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Whatever lights the lake arm has begun coming up the ditches into Fenmarch.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 142 m from the nearest route; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: The lake arm is a dead end where the water lights when it is disturbed. The raft village will not swim in it after dark.

name: The Cordon Stones
why_founding: A line of marker stones was set across the western approaches during the Knahaten Flu. The stones mark which side of the line held the living.
why_site_advantages: The line follows the natural contour where the ground firms up. A fleeing population would take that line anyway.
why_occupants_motive: No stone has been moved in three hundred years. Villages still do not build across the line.
why_pressures: Root-heave is losing the stones one by one. There is no record of where they stood.
why_would_change_if: The cordon would be forgotten entirely in another century.
siting_prefs_water_relation: uses water as part of the line where it can
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: encircles a plague-abandoned village or a cairn field
vibe_silhouette: Waist-high stones stand every hundred paces along a contour. The line runs out of sight in both directions.
vibe_palette: The colours are lichen orange on grey. Grass grows to the knee.
vibe_materials: The stones are local, undressed and set upright.
vibe_signature_feature: Two stones stand closer together where a path crosses. A rubbed hollow lies between them.
vibe_condition: The stones are weathered. Several have fallen. One stone was recently re-erected.
vibe_mood: The mood is sober. The line runs for miles.
vibe_approach: Travellers cross the line without noticing. The next stone shows a hundred paces along the contour.
vibe_senses: Wind blows and grass rustles. Footsteps sound for a long time.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The cordon has stood unlifted for two centuries. The stones themselves turn travellers back.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 39 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Waist-high stones run for miles along a contour. No village will build across the line.

name: Counts-The-Dead
why_founding: The Flu killed faster than the dead could be carried home. The western road villages made one ground and counted the dead into it.
why_site_advantages: The ground lies a day's carry from the marsh edge, beside the road. A carrier taking bones west has somewhere to stop before the last stage. The ground was cut and not dug. The earliest counts are kept in a chamber under it. The chamber has gone unswept for a century.
why_occupants_motive: The bone-carrier's office is hereditary here. The current holder keeps the count in her head, in her ledger and in the number of poles driven.
why_pressures: The count is still rising. Owing deaths and burn-country deaths are added to it.
why_would_change_if: The ground would close if a court ever ruled that the road's dead had somewhere else to go.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village
vibe_silhouette: A field holds thousands of thin driven poles. The poles lean at every angle. A cairn stands at the head of each block of a hundred.
vibe_palette: The colours are weathered pole grey, pale cut wood where a pole is new and black soil.
vibe_materials: The built work is driven poles and stacked-stone cairns. A woven totem stands at the road end. There is one reed shelter.
vibe_signature_feature: The field grows towards the road. The newest poles stand nearest the road.
vibe_condition: The field is continuously maintained. The oldest poles at the far end have rotted to stumps.
vibe_mood: The field is vast. Each pole stands for one person.
vibe_approach: The stakes appear beside the road gradually. The field's size is not apparent from the road.
vibe_senses: Thousands of poles knock wood on wood in the wind.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A bundle booked for the western road was counted into the mass grave instead.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 55 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, route.
player_purpose_hook: The Flu's dead were counted into this ground because they could not be carried home. A pole goes in for each dead person. The tally is still kept.

name: Drowned Furrow
why_founding: The farm was a second grant. A family worked it who ploughed the way they had at home and drained nothing.
why_site_advantages: The site was superb for eight months a year. It lay under half a metre of water for four months. Then came a season in which the water did not go back down.
why_occupants_motive: The grant-holders are long gone. Whatever moved into the flooded rooms has the sills and doorframes to itself.
why_pressures: The roof is the last dry surface left. The tiles are coming off it.
why_would_change_if: The farm would be walkable again only if the channel that flooded it silted shut.
siting_prefs_water_relation: tried to be dry and failed
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: strung along a road at Imperial spacing, not local spacing
vibe_silhouette: A tiled roof stands in a sheet of water. The fields show as pale ridges under the surface.
vibe_palette: The sky is reflected everywhere. Terracotta shows above the water. Drowned grass is a sick yellow.
vibe_materials: Imperial masonry stands in water to sill height. It goes green below the waterline.
vibe_signature_feature: The plough ridges lie three centimetres below the surface. They are still perfectly parallel. Whatever swims there uses them as a route.
vibe_condition: The building is weathertight above the water. It rots below the water.
vibe_approach: From the bank it still looks like an ordinary empty farm. It has not been dry in two years.
vibe_senses: Water laps in a doorway. Something breaks the surface and goes under again. No birds fly indoors.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The drowned farmstead upstream is what Highwater's wells are tasting.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 869 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: The marsh finally drowned the farmhouse for good. The roof holds the last air above water. Something ambushes from the rooms below the roof.
siting_note: The place was moved to the valley floor at the channel that flooded it in round 4. The old site was a dry mountain shoulder with no water to cause a drowning.

name: The Drowned Mule
why_founding: A carters' house stands at the wet end of the road. It is named for the animal that the flood took in the year of its opening.
why_site_advantages: The house is the last building on firm ground before the drowning gate. Carters stop here because there is nowhere else.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper survives on the wet season. In the wet season the road closes and forty carters are stuck for a week.
why_pressures: In a dry year the people of the house nearly starve. The keeper prays for floods and says so.
why_would_change_if: The house would relocate if the barrier moved. The sign would go with it.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: A wide low house has a stilted floor. A stone stable stands beside it. The sign is carved as a mule underwater.
vibe_palette: The colours are smoke-brown timber and flood-stain grey on the stable. One bright repainted sign stands out.
vibe_materials: The house has an Argonian stilt frame. An Imperial stone stable is bolted onto the end.
vibe_signature_feature: Flood lines are scored inside the common room. Each line carries a year. The highest line is above the door.
vibe_condition: Sturdy and damp.
vibe_mood: The house is crowded and idle. The guests cannot travel onward.
vibe_approach: The road runs out into water. The house stands on the last dry metre with its lamps lit.
vibe_senses: Rain falls and guests play cards. Wet tack steams by the fire.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 181 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: The house is the last building on firm ground before the road drowns. Every carter stops here.

name: The Drowning Gate
why_founding: The western road closes every monsoon at this point.
why_site_advantages: The site is the road's lowest point. The plain drains across the road there, so the water arrives here first.
why_occupants_motive: Gideon pays two families to swing the barrier. The families also argue with anyone who wants it opened anyway.
why_pressures: Every wet season a driver goes round the barrier and drowns. The tally board records how many.
why_would_change_if: The gate would be unnecessary if the Empire's raised causeway had ever been finished. Its drowned embankment runs alongside.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a road that has a wet-season alternative
vibe_silhouette: A painted pole barrier stands across an empty road. Water lies on both sides for half the year. Open plain lies beyond.
vibe_palette: The colours are warning ochre and black bands, brown floodwater and grey sky.
vibe_materials: The built work is one Imperial gauge post, a timber boom and a reed hut on stilts.
vibe_signature_feature: The tally board lists a name and a year. It lists one for every person who went round the barrier.
vibe_condition: Crude. Repainted every year.
vibe_approach: In the dry season the barrier stands in a field. In the wet season the road is under water.
vibe_senses: Rain falls on water. The boom creaks. Frogs call at a volume that makes conversation hard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The barrier must be opened early for a convoy. The flood would otherwise strand the convoy.
why_site_won: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 4), 104 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The monsoon shuts the Blackwood Road at this point. Once the barrier is down the road stays shut for months.
siting_note: The place is bound to the Blackwood Road's lowest crossing of the western plain, set in round 4. The record's identity is the point where the western road shuts. That road runs west of Gideon.

name: The Eight Steps
why_founding: The upper water drops through eight ledges in a kilometre. Boats stop below the ledges. Portage starts there.
why_site_advantages: The reach is confined, with rock ledges. A loaded boat cannot run the ledges.
why_occupants_motive: The portage families live above and below the reach. Both families claim the whole reach.
why_pressures: A boatman runs the reach every year on a bet. Roughly every third one dies.
why_would_change_if: The reach would be passable if a proper portage path were cut. That is a season's work. Neither portage family will pay for it on the other's bank.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: forces every boat route to stop; a portage or a ferry always answers it
vibe_silhouette: Eight white steps lie in a green-black river between rock walls. A worn path scrambles beside them.
vibe_palette: The colours are white and black rock. The green is so dark that it reads as black in shade.
vibe_materials: The built work is the portage path, driven poles and a cairn at the worst step.
vibe_signature_feature: The fourth step is the dangerous one. Driven poles mark it on both banks. A cairn stands above the eddy.
vibe_condition: The path is eroding. The poles are renewed.
vibe_approach: The water is audible long before the track arrives. The sound changes at each step.
vibe_senses: White noise sounds at eight different pitches. Wet rock lies underfoot.
why_site_won: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 368 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route.
player_purpose_hook: Eight rock ledges fall in a kilometre of river. Boats stop and cargo walks. The portage crews charge by the load.

name: Drowned Embankment
why_founding: An Imperial scheme set out to raise the road above the flood. It began with foreign engineering and no local hydrology.
why_site_advantages: The embankment runs dead straight across the plain. It dammed the drainage that it crossed.
why_occupants_motive: The villages downstream have been cutting gaps in the embankment for two hundred years.
why_pressures: Each cut gap makes the next flood worse somewhere else. The arguments about which gap to close are inherited.
why_would_change_if: The embankment would be a fine road if it were rebuilt with culverts. The unfinished culvert line was intended for that.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the line of an abandoned Imperial road
vibe_silhouette: A perfectly straight green ridge crosses a plain. Seven deliberate gaps break it.
vibe_palette: The colours are grass green on the bank. Black standing water lies on one side. Dry cracked mud lies on the other.
vibe_materials: The embankment is rammed earth over an Imperial stone core. The core is exposed where the gaps were cut.
vibe_signature_feature: Deep water lies on the upstream face. Dry cracked mud lies on the downstream face. This holds along the whole length of the embankment.
vibe_condition: The embankment was abandoned mid-build. The last two hundred metres are only staked out.
vibe_mood: The mood is bleak. The villages downstream still tell the story as a joke.
vibe_approach: From anywhere on the plain it reads as a horizon line. Closer up it is a bank with gaps cut through it.
vibe_senses: Wind blows over grass. Water slaps flatly on one side only.
why_site_won: gorge in firm lowland (danger band 4), 27 m from the nearest route; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A dead straight Imperial embankment dammed the drainage that it was built to beat. Its culvert chambers are dry and occupied.

name: The Empty Steading
why_founding: A family built a river station. They left for Leyawiin in the last bad flood. They did not return.
why_site_advantages: The site is a firm bank at a channel junction. It has its own landing, a walled yard and a well.
why_occupants_motive: The house stands empty. The neighbours agree that it can be claimed. They do not agree on who should claim it.
why_pressures: Two villages and the Owing brokers all have a colourable claim. The question has been open four years.
why_would_change_if: The question would settle the moment a credible claimant moved in and made the case.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one per region packet, near but not in a settlement
vibe_silhouette: A walled yard has a sound roof. The landing has two rotted piles. A door stands open.
vibe_palette: The colours are weathered timber and yard-weed green. The well head is clean stone and still works.
vibe_materials: The house is Argonian stilt-and-mud on a stone footing. It is well founded and empty.
vibe_signature_feature: The door has stood open four years. Closing it would be a claim.
vibe_condition: The house is sound. It deteriorates as unoccupied buildings do.
vibe_approach: From the channel it shows as a roofline with no smoke.
vibe_senses: Wind blows through an open door. The well rope knocks.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Three separate offices must sign before the steading changes hands. A deed, a well and a landing go to whoever finishes the paperwork.
player_purpose_hook: A river station has a walled yard, a well and its own landing. Its family left in the last bad flood. Whoever clears it can have it.

name: The Fig and Ledger
why_founding: Court business makes people wait. A keeper opened a wine house for them.
why_site_advantages: The house stands directly outside Gideon's courthouse gate. It stands in the shade of the one old fig on the street.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper sells information as readily as wine. The keeper has never been caught selling it twice.
why_pressures: Advocates and fences drink in the same room by unspoken arrangement. The arrangement holds until a customer is drunk.
why_would_change_if: The house would close if the courthouse ever stopped sitting. The trade is adjournments.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: A narrow two-storey house stands here. A fig grows out of the pavement and through the balcony.
vibe_palette: The colours are wine-red shutters and fig green. Courthouse grey lies opposite.
vibe_materials: The house is Imperial townhouse masonry with reed awnings. Its floor is Onkobra tiles. A craftsman paid in wine laid the tiles.
vibe_signature_feature: The adjournment board hangs by the door. It lists which cases were put off today.
vibe_condition: The front is well kept. The back is structurally optimistic.
vibe_approach: The house is the first door past the court gate.
vibe_senses: Customers argue and cups clink. Figs drop on the awning.
player_purpose_hook: The wine house stands outside the courthouse gate. Everyone waiting on a judgement says more than they should.

name: Fig Camp
why_founding: Gideon buys hide and meat from the poachers. He does not ask which village's ground was the origin of the animals.
why_site_advantages: The camp lies in a dense fig thicket at the head of a ravine. The thicket blocks every sightline from outside. Water is to hand. The camp has three ways out.
why_occupants_motive: The poachers are village men who work the camp for a second season's income. They would be recognised in daylight.
why_pressures: The village whose ground the poachers work has begun to set its own watch.
why_would_change_if: The camp would fold immediately if Gideon's market ever asked for provenance.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: just outside a village's watched ground
vibe_silhouette: Drying racks are strung between the fig trunks. A fire trench is dug so that the smoke spreads. There are no tents at all.
vibe_palette: The colours are fig green and meat red. Smoke grey is held down under the canopy.
vibe_materials: The camp is made of rope, racks and a dug fire trench. The poachers can leave all of it behind in five minutes.
vibe_signature_feature: The smoke trench is dug and baffled. The fire cannot be seen from above or smelled downhill.
vibe_condition: The poachers reuse the camp every season. They clean it between times.
vibe_mood: The camp is practical. The poachers are ready to run.
vibe_approach: The path gives no cue. A drag trail leads to the camp.
vibe_senses: The poachers keep their dogs quiet. Flies buzz and smoke stays low.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The poachers sell whatever they take to Fig Market. Fig Market is two hours down the road.
why_site_won: box canyon in upland hills (danger band 3), 69 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: A poachers' camp stands at a ravine head with three ways out. The poachers sell hide and meat to a city that does not ask about its origin.

name: The Glass Scar
why_founding: A gate opened on the Blackwood frontier in 4E 5–7. The Argonians went through the gate and did not flee from it.
why_site_advantages: The scar sits where the gate stood. It lies on a bare shoulder of the rim above the burn country. Gates did not choose their ground.
why_occupants_motive: The villages leave the ground unworked. The ground has not grown back properly.
why_pressures: The Synod wants to survey the scar. The villages refuse to permit it. The argument is annual.
why_would_change_if: On any other ground in the fringe the scar would be overgrown by now.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near settlements that existed in 3E 433
vibe_silhouette: A circle of black fused ground is forty metres from rim to rim. A rim of offerings marks its edge. The ground inside is bare.
vibe_palette: The colours are obsidian black and offering-cloth red. The green stops dead at the rim.
vibe_materials: The ground is fused earth and glassy slag. The worked part is the offering line that the villages maintain.
vibe_signature_feature: A ring of small offerings sits on the rim. The villages renew the offerings. The offerings mark where people will step and where they will not.
vibe_condition: Unchanged in two centuries.
vibe_mood: The site is silent and avoided. The villagers respect it more than they fear it.
vibe_approach: The colour break shows from a hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Insects do not live inside the circle.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Synod wants the scar surveyed. The villages refuse.
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 1272 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The Argonians went through the gate and did not flee from it. What came back out is still on this flat.

name: Hackwing Scarp
why_founding: A rim scarp has south-facing ledges and thermals. Hackwings have used it as a colony for as long as the villages have stood below it.
why_site_advantages: Broken cliff ledges lie above a warm slope. The birds have used the ledges long enough to whiten the rock.
why_occupants_motive: The birds are here for the updraught.
why_pressures: Lambing season and hatching season coincide.
why_would_change_if: The scarp would stay as it is. The colony is older than the villages.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: downwind of a lair, a battlefield or a midden
vibe_silhouette: A cliff face is streaked white for eighty metres. Birds turn above it all day.
vibe_palette: The colours are guano white on red-grey rock. A mass of dark wings moves above it.
vibe_materials: There is no building. One old rope anchor remains, left by an egg-taker.
vibe_signature_feature: The white streaking is renewed every season.
vibe_condition: Unchanging.
vibe_approach: The scarp is visible from the valley for two kilometres.
vibe_senses: Shrieking is continuous and wind blows. The updraught carries a smell down the slope.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The hackwings of the roost have learned the sermon road's timetable. That turns a pilgrimage into a running fight.
why_site_won: gorge in border mountains (danger band 3), 1300 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: A hackwing colony nests on warm cliff ledges. The nests are worth money.

name: Hollow Pass Station
why_founding: The rim path from Gideon to the north crosses one saddle. A person caught by weather on the saddle will die. A station therefore stands on it.
why_site_advantages: The station stands on the lee side of the saddle. It lies in a natural hollow that breaks the wind from three directions.
why_occupants_motive: Two keepers hold the station on a season's rota from the villages below. They are paid in food and standing.
why_pressures: Couriers and smugglers use the path more each year. The station is provisioned for neither.
why_would_change_if: The station would be abandoned in the year that the rim path lost its traffic to a safer road.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the only crossings of the rim; each one is strategically singular
vibe_silhouette: A low turf-roofed building stands in a hollow. A horn on a post stands at the crest of the saddle above it.
vibe_palette: The colours are turf green on the roof and stone grey. Cloud sits above the crest most days.
vibe_materials: The station is dry stone with a turf roof. From above it is invisible. From below it is a green lump.
vibe_signature_feature: The horn stands on the post at the crest. The keepers sound it when weather comes over.
vibe_condition: The station is thick-walled and sound. It is buried in its own hollow.
vibe_mood: The keepers are hospitable. They are obsessed with the weather.
vibe_approach: From the crest the station shows roof-first, down in its hollow.
vibe_senses: Wind stops abruptly on the drop into the hollow. A horn sounds and a fire burns.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The shelter's arrivals book records four departures against three arrivals.
why_site_won: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 1350 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region.
player_purpose_hook: The shelter stands in the saddle hollow on the stretch of rim path where the weather kills. A rota keeper keeps it. The keeper holds travellers back in the wrong hour.

name: The Hollow Under the Figs
why_founding: The province has almost no rock. Its caves are root galleries. The fig-root mats of the fringe form the westernmost of these galleries.
why_site_advantages: The root layer runs over a drained hollow. The roots hold up a roof. The ground beneath the roots has gone.
why_occupants_motive: The Hollow has no keeper. The poachers who live below use its mouth. The poachers stop at the second chamber.
why_pressures: The roots are alive and moving. They move on a timescale of years. The shape of the gallery changes as they move.
why_would_change_if: The Hollow would close on itself within a decade if the figs above it were felled.
siting_prefs_water_relation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect, so that connection is the map
vibe_silhouette: The Hollow is a dark mouth under a fig root buttress. The roof of the passage is made entirely of living wood.
vibe_palette: The colours are root brown and black interior. Green light shows only at the mouth.
vibe_materials: The Hollow has no masonry anywhere. The roof and the walls are living root.
vibe_signature_feature: The floor is bare drained earth. The ceiling above it is visibly growing.
vibe_condition: The Hollow is alive. Passages that were open last year are closing.
vibe_approach: The mouth is behind a root buttress. The mouth faces away from the path.
vibe_senses: Roots creak and water drips. Something further in stops moving when the walking stops.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The root gallery has opened into Fig Market's storage pits.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 564 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on nearPoint, hinterland, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-buried-spears (+1.06).
player_purpose_hook: The province has almost no rock. Its caves are root galleries. This gallery is the westernmost. Something has moved into it.

name: Keeps-The-Terrace
why_founding: The Kept Terrace is a Merethic xanmeer. It stands at the western edge of the province. The nearest village tends it as a monument.
why_site_advantages: The terrace stands on a rise above the flood. The flood has yet to reach the terrace.
why_occupants_motive: The village keeps the terrace swept as its office. Entering the xanmeer to loot is a serious offence. The village states this plainly.
why_pressures: Gideon's antiquities trade lies two days away. The trade gets closer every year.
why_would_change_if: The keepers would seal the xanmeer the first time a theft succeeded.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it
vibe_silhouette: A stepped pyramid rises clear of the tree canopy. The pyramid is swept. Cut vegetation is stacked neatly at its base.
vibe_palette: The stone is pale grey. The terrace shadows are sharp and black. The canopy below is green.
vibe_materials: The xanmeer is built of ashlar. The keepers maintain it with brooms and knives alone. No stone has been added.
vibe_signature_feature: Bare stone extends for a hundred paces. The country around it is green.
vibe_condition: Immaculate outside, untouched inside.
vibe_approach: It breaks the canopy.
vibe_senses: Brooms sweep stone. Wind blows at terrace height. Birds sing loudly in the canopy below.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A village sweeps the terrace nightly. The village says it stopped sweeping years ago.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 269 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The nearest village tends this xanmeer as a monument, not as a tomb. Visitors who ask first are told what not to touch.

name: High Scree Floor
why_founding: The province distrusts metal but still needs edges. This scree has been worked for stone tools since the Merethic.
why_site_advantages: The scree is of fine-grained stone. It lies below a rim cliff. It is the workable stone source for the whole west bank.
why_occupants_motive: Two families come up each dry season to work the scree. Their grandmothers worked it the same way.
why_pressures: Gideon's iron is cheaper and worse. The young buy it anyway.
why_would_change_if: The floor would go quiet within two generations. The floor itself would still be here.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a village or a hunting ground
vibe_silhouette: The floor is a flat apron of grey scree. Sitting hollows are worn into it. Flake debris glitters across the apron.
vibe_palette: The scree is grey on grey. A mica glitter shifts with the position of the viewer.
vibe_materials: The floor has no structure. A wind-break of stacked stone stands there. Thousands of years of flakes cover the ground.
vibe_signature_feature: Generations of knappers wore sitting hollows into the rock. The hollows are in the same four places.
vibe_condition: The knappers use the floor continuously. The floor is entirely unbuilt.
vibe_approach: The glitter is the cue to the floor. It shows only with the sun behind the walker.
vibe_senses: Stone is struck on stone with a ringing knock. Wind follows.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Village stonework is being sold in Gideon as Ayleid work.
why_site_won: oxbow in upland hills (danger band 3), 148 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-turned-out (+1.18).
player_purpose_hook: Stone tools have been struck on this scree since the Merethic. The knappers make an edge that cannot rust.

name: Onkobra Divers' Yard
why_founding: The lake holds a drowned Kothringi town. Three centuries of boats lie on top of the town. Argonians can dive down and look.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands on a shingle beach. Working depth is twenty metres out. It is the shortest swim to the good ground on the lake.
why_occupants_motive: The divers work the wrecks. They avoid the drowned town, which is prohibited ground.
why_pressures: Two of the younger divers have started working the town at night. The yard is dividing over it.
why_would_change_if: The yard would be rich and finished within five years if the prohibition broke.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: always paired with drowned ground it works
vibe_silhouette: The yard is a shingle beach. It has a boat rack and a sorting frame of dripping salvage. A line of rope dries there.
vibe_palette: The shingle is wet grey. Salvage shows green bronze. The rope is brown. The lake is silver.
vibe_materials: The racks and frames are timber. Every object on them came out of the water.
vibe_signature_feature: The sorting frame has a forbidden shelf. Kothringi stone-work would go there, but only if a diver admitted to bringing it up.
vibe_condition: The yard is working and wet. The water is slowly taking the yard.
vibe_mood: The mood is matter-of-fact. The yard is split down the middle.
vibe_approach: The drying line is visible from the water. It is visible for a good distance.
vibe_senses: Water drips. A bell rings when a diver surfaces late. The gulls here are not sea gulls.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1824 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, culture-clump, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: The diving yard lies on the shortest swim to a drowned Kothringi town. Divers are taken on for lung capacity alone.
siting_note: The yard moved onto the western lake shore in round 4. A diving yard needs working depth off the beach. The old site lacked that depth.

name: The Lamp at the Ford
why_founding: A house stands at an upland ford. The household keeps a lamp burning there all night. The ford is unmarked. People drowned there before the lamp was lit.
why_site_advantages: The ford is the sole crossing for two kilometres. The banks are steep enough to hide it.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper's family took on the lamp as a debt to a drowned cousin. The family has kept the lamp for eighty years.
why_pressures: Lamp oil is expensive here. The family is not rich. Guests are expected to understand this. The record was deferred on 2026-09-03 (Part 4 step 2). It is repetitive road-house fill within a kilometre of three others. It is held in reserve against the province record budget.
why_would_change_if: The lamp would go dark if the family fails. People would then start drowning at the ford again.
siting_prefs_water_relation: on a route, with a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: The house shows one lit window and a lamp on a pole. At night it is the sole light in a black valley.
vibe_palette: The colours are lamp yellow, wet slate and black water.
vibe_materials: The footings are local stone. The house is timber above. The reed roof is kept low against the valley wind.
vibe_signature_feature: The lamp pole is taller than the house. A counterweight lowers the pole in wind.
vibe_condition: Small, thickly built, spotless.
vibe_approach: The lamp is the cue. It works only within about six hundred metres. It shows the sightlines of this province in one object.
vibe_senses: Water runs over stones. A rope works the pole. A kettle sings.
player_purpose_hook: One house keeps one lamp burning all night over an unmarked ford. The lamp exists because of what happened before it was lit.

name: Last Post
why_founding: The Blackwood Road leaves the province through this cut. The Legion drew back to Leyawiin. The road villages then put their own keepers on the pole.
why_site_advantages: The post stands at the narrowest point of the road cut. Rock rises on either side. The gate needs almost no wall.
why_occupants_motive: The keepers are villagers on a rota. They check arrivals for disease and for slavers. They check for disease first.
why_pressures: The Leyawiin side of the cut is unmanned. The keepers find that insulting.
why_would_change_if: The post would become a real frontier in the year that Leyawiin posted a gate of its own on the far side of the cut.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: spaced along the border; gaps are the point
vibe_silhouette: The post is a barrier pole, a bench and a reed hut. Rock walls stand on both sides of the road. The road goes on without the post.
vibe_palette: The colours are rock grey and unpainted timber. The Cyrodiil side has a different green.
vibe_materials: The post is timber and reed. It stands on Imperial road stone.
vibe_signature_feature: The tongue bench is where every comer sits to be inspected. The habit is kept from the Knahaten Flu.
vibe_condition: Minimal, kept, unfortified.
vibe_approach: The cut narrows to a pole across the road. The light changes where the vegetation does.
vibe_senses: Wind funnels through the cut. The barrier counterweight creaks. Birds keep to the Cyrodiil side.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A pardon for the unpaid column would have to be registered at the border post.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 77 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'saddle' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, route.
player_purpose_hook: The gate stands on the Blackwood Road where it runs out towards Leyawiin. Villagers hold it. They carried on after the Legion stopped. Arrivals are looked over at the gate.
siting_note: The western gate is bound to the last 200 m of the Blackwood Road before the closed edge. The owner ruled this on 2026-09-04. If the plot cannot honour that, the record is cut. The record is not moved inland.

name: Leaning Watch
why_founding: Leaning Watch is the twin of another tower. It was built on a peat lens. The ground turned out not to be rock.
why_site_advantages: The tower has the same commanding view as its twin. It leans a further degree or so every decade.
why_occupants_motive: Children dare each other to climb it. A hermit sleeps in the base in winter.
why_pressures: The tower leans towards the road. Gideon's road office has been told twice.
why_would_change_if: The tower would come down entirely in one wet season. The villages have a wager on the year.
siting_prefs_water_relation: commands a route or a channel
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower
vibe_silhouette: The stone tower is out of plumb by a clear four degrees. Its top course is open to the sky.
vibe_palette: Green-black damp marks the low side. The high side is dry pale grey.
vibe_materials: The tower uses the same Imperial rubble as its twin. It stands on ground that could not hold it.
vibe_signature_feature: The lean itself is the feature. A plumb line that a surveyor left a century ago hangs inside.
vibe_condition: The tower is dangerous above the second floor. The danger is obvious.
vibe_approach: The lean is readable only at close range.
vibe_senses: Grit falls inside the shaft. Birds call. The tower creaks in wind.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The basket on the tower is lit on the nights that Stonewastes has a death.
why_site_won: headland in upland hills (danger band 3), 1102 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent.
player_purpose_hook: This signal tower was built on peat. The ground there is not rock. It leans a degree a decade. Its floors are not yet cleared.

name: Ledge of Tallies
why_founding: The province has one legal crossing into Cyrodiil. Everyone else goes over the rim.
why_site_advantages: The site is a cliff bench with a ravine below and a saddle above. A cave mouth in the face behind the bench is deep enough to hold a season's goods. Loads come down from one province on rope. They go up into the other province in the same way.
why_occupants_motive: The carriers are village men from both sides of the border. They have worked the same ledge for generations.
why_pressures: Fort Swampmoth's company prices the legal road very high. The ledge now carries more goods than the road does.
why_would_change_if: The ledge would be abandoned if the tolls ever dropped.
siting_prefs_water_relation: none; this is the dry route
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: beside a pass, out of sight of its post
vibe_silhouette: A rope bollard is pegged into the rock of the ledge. A hide-covered cache stands against the face. A dark cave mouth lies behind it.
vibe_palette: The colours are rock grey, rope brown and deep ravine shadow. A single strip of sky shows overhead.
vibe_materials: The fittings are pegged bollards, rope, hide covers and a plank stage over the drop. Every fixing is driven into a crack, because a crack is all this rock will hold.
vibe_signature_feature: Scratched marks beside the bollard make a tally. The tally holds one mark per load and is generations deep. The oldest marks are nearly worn away.
vibe_condition: The carriers maintain the ledge where it bears weight. They leave the rest untouched.
vibe_approach: The ledge cannot be seen from the ravine or from the saddle. The way in is a climb.
vibe_senses: Rope creaks under load. Rock falls from the face. Wind blows in the ravine.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tally marks name traders who deny the debts.
why_site_won: gorge in border mountains (danger band 3), 693 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: This is the illegal crossing. Goods are lowered to a cliff bench above a ravine, tallied into the cave behind the bench and lifted out on the other side.

name: The Marble Field
why_founding: Imperials buried their dead here for two centuries. Burial does not work in this province.
why_site_advantages: The field lies on a dry shoulder of the rim above the city. The Imperials chose it because they assumed dry ground stays dry.
why_occupants_motive: The Imperial families left and took the upkeep with them. Argonians will not tend a grave, because they have other arrangements for their dead.
why_pressures: The water table rose. A third of the plots have surfaced. The matter is not discussed in Gideon.
why_would_change_if: The field would be cleared if a Gideon contractor took the work.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: attached to a foreign settlement
vibe_silhouette: Pale stelae lean at every angle across the field. Half of them have fallen. The field lies on a knoll in sight of the city.
vibe_palette: The marble is grey-white. The ground is green. Black damp fills the lettering.
vibe_materials: The stelae are imported Nibenese marble. The marble was carted up from the Niben at private expense.
vibe_signature_feature: In some rows the boxes have surfaced from the ground. They lie where they surfaced.
vibe_condition: The field is collapsing and unvisited. It is not vandalised, because the locals will not touch it.
vibe_approach: The white of the stelae shows through the grass from the city road.
vibe_senses: Grass rustles. The city can be heard in the distance. Birds do not call here.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Plots paid for a century ago are being resold.
why_site_won: local tie in border mountains (danger band 3), 466 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region.
player_purpose_hook: The field holds two centuries of Imperial burials. It stands on a knoll that stopped being dry. The vaults at the bottom are open.

name: The Month Chapel
why_founding: The Chapel was a Maran mission on the western road. Its brothers died of swamp rot inside a month, which was the same fate as Umpholo. The Chapel stands on the road, not in the interior.
why_site_advantages: The Chapel was built on ground that the surveyors recorded as firm. The wet season cuts it off.
why_occupants_motive: The road villages route around the Chapel. The habit is a hundred and eighty years old.
why_pressures: Fig roots are destroying the Chapel. The rate can be measured year to year.
why_would_change_if: The Chapel would have been a village if it had been sited fifty metres higher. The locals draw a sermon out of that.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: The place lies far inland, on land that other settlers passed over.
vibe_silhouette: A stone apse stands in scrub with no nave left. A fig grows out of the altar.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey. The fig is green. The crypt stair is black and full of water.
vibe_materials: The masonry is Imperial chapel masonry. The timber went for firewood within a decade.
vibe_signature_feature: The last brother cut the brothers' names into the apse wall. His handwriting grows worse down the list.
vibe_condition: One wall stands. The rest is a footprint in the grass. The crypt is flooded.
vibe_mood: The mood is brief and futile. The list on the wall is short.
vibe_approach: The path bends away from the Chapel deliberately. Reaching the Chapel means leaving the path.
vibe_senses: Water sits in the crypt. Fig leaves lie over the floor.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One chapel and one priest must serve two calendars. The calendars are eleven days apart.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 33 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, route, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The Chapel was a Maran mission whose brothers all died inside a month. The altar is still set. The register runs to the last name.

name: Niben Crystal Workings
why_founding: Niben-crystal comes out of the Blackwood's hills. The enchanters' benches of two provinces will buy it.
why_site_advantages: The workings stand on a ravine wall. The water that cut the ravine exposed the seam there.
why_occupants_motive: A family works the seam. They sell to whichever side pays. They have no politics and say so.
why_pressures: The seam runs under the ravine floor, so the family works waist-deep in water. The work is ruining their health.
why_would_change_if: An outside concession would take over the workings if the family failed.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: supplies an artisan village's jewellers
vibe_silhouette: Timber staging is pinned to a ravine wall. A seam of glassy blue-green runs behind it.
vibe_palette: The crystal is blue-green. The rock is wet and black. The timber is dark with water.
vibe_materials: The staging is lashed timber with rope ladders. No post of it is founded on the ground.
vibe_signature_feature: The seam itself is the feature. It glints in the hour of direct light that the ravine gets.
vibe_condition: The family rebuilds the workings after every flood. Floods come annually.
vibe_mood: The mood is precarious. Everything is damp to the bone.
vibe_approach: The water is audible first. The seam glints for about an hour a day. At other times the place is invisible.
vibe_senses: Hammers tap on rock. Water runs. Timber shifts.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 817 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Niben-crystal lies in an exposed ravine seam. Enchanters in two provinces will buy it. The crystal cannot be taken from the workings easily.

name: Old Office House
why_founding: Some village offices are held by a household, not by a village. That household lives apart from both villages.
why_site_advantages: The house stands midway between four villages. The ground belongs to none of the four.
why_occupants_motive: The holder settles boundary and water disputes for all four villages. She lives apart from every one of them.
why_pressures: Her heir does not want the office. No other household will take it.
why_would_change_if: Without the office, the four villages would argue directly with each other.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: 200-600 m from the village it serves
vibe_silhouette: One house has four paths converging on it. A long bench outside the door faces the yard.
vibe_palette: The thatch is gold. The yard is packed earth. Four differently coloured paths arrive at the house.
vibe_materials: The house is ordinary mud and reed. The office requires it to be kept deliberately plain.
vibe_signature_feature: The four paths are worn to different depths. The deepest belongs to the village that argues most.
vibe_condition: Modest and immaculate.
vibe_approach: The converging paths are visible from any of the four approaches.
vibe_senses: A slow conversation goes on at the bench. A kettle sings. Visitors do not hurry.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Two claimants inherit the same house. Two bodies of law apply here. Both claim it.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 39 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-back-kiln (+1.00).
player_purpose_hook: A household holds an office that four villages share. The household lives apart from all four villages.

name: The Old Quarters
why_founding: The Old Quarters were the living quarters of a plantation. They form one long brick row, built for field hands when the crop still paid. The crop failed for good when the drainage silted.
why_site_advantages: The row sits on the dry line through this stretch of swamp. A crossing means walking its length.
why_occupants_motive: The sap-poachers who used the row moved on when the cutting moved. Travellers shelter in what the poachers left.
why_pressures: Locals still use the row as a footpath. The poachers let them through in daylight and rob them after dark.
why_would_change_if: The row would be abandoned again if the sap dried up. It would also be abandoned if a bigger gang drove the poachers out.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: near a road that stopped being used
vibe_silhouette: Twenty identical doorways stand in a row of roofless walls. The row runs dead straight into the trees.
vibe_palette: The render is grey. The doorways are black. Green covers the rest.
vibe_materials: The row is built of cheap Imperial brick. Its reed roofs are long gone. The overseer's end was stone.
vibe_signature_feature: Twenty identical openings stand in a row. A twenty-first has a lintel and a step. The poachers have hung a door there.
vibe_condition: The row is roofless, with walls to head height. The poachers patch it with poached hide and rope where they sleep.
vibe_mood: The mood is watched. Every doorway is a place to stand and wait.
vibe_approach: The path becomes a corridor of doorways without any transition.
vibe_senses: Footsteps echo between brick walls. Woodsmoke drifts from a hidden fire. Hide dries on a line strung across two doorways.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The row is a plantation's abandoned quarters. It was left empty when the drainage silted. The sap-poachers shelter in it.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 143 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.onkobra-clay-pits (+1.11).
player_purpose_hook: The sap-poachers have gone elsewhere. They left the long plantation row standing dry. The path through the swamp now runs under standing walls.
siting_note: The record was converted from hostile to neutral in the round-4 hostility rebalance. This neighbourhood already carried three route-side fights inside 250 m.

name: Pass Shelter
why_founding: The upland pass out of the fringe kills people in the wrong month. Wind-driven rain does it. There is no cover for two hours in either direction. The road authority built a hard shelter at the worst point and then stopped maintaining it.
why_site_advantages: The shelter has a rock back. No run-off channel lies above it. Every alternative on the pass is a stream bed in a storm.
why_occupants_motive: Whoever is caught out holds the shelter. In the bad months that means two or three parties share a fire, which they would not otherwise share.
why_pressures: The door is gone. The fire-store holds whatever the last party left. The tradition of leaving fuel holds, but only just.
why_would_change_if: The shelter would become a death trap. That happens the first winter the fuel tradition broke.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on an exposed stretch with no settlement
vibe_silhouette: A squat stone box stands against a rock face. Its slate roof is pitched almost flat. Its chimney is much too large for it.
vibe_palette: The slate is wet and the stone is black. A fire burns orange in a doorway with no door.
vibe_materials: The shelter is built of Imperial road-authority masonry. The next cut stone is ten kilometres away.
vibe_signature_feature: The name-book is a slate slab inside the shelter. Every party scratches its name and hour on it. The entries go back longer than the shelter has been maintained.
vibe_condition: The shelter is structurally sound. Only the roof is maintained.
vibe_mood: The mood is grim and functional. It is companionable when the shelter is full.
vibe_approach: The shelter is invisible until the last bend. People still die short of it.
vibe_senses: Wind changes note behind the rock. Wet wool smells strongly. A slate is scratched.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A forced-company scene puts two hostile parties at one fire. A written record shows who crossed the pass and when.
why_site_won: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 691 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The shelter has rock behind it. No run-off channel lies above it. It is somewhere to sit out the pass weather without being washed off the road.

name: The Quiet Pit
