why_founding: Argonians build no prisons. Debtors still have to be held at times under the Owing. The holding takes place in a pit. The holding is called 'waiting'.
why_site_advantages: The pit is a dry storage pit at the back of a broker's yard. It is roofed and grated. It is invisible from the road.
why_occupants_motive: The brokers hold debtors here for a day or two. They hold them until the Owing is transferred. The holding is legal.
why_pressures: A debtor was held for eleven days last year. The villagers still talk about it.
why_would_change_if: The pit would be filled in during the week that a court ruled that waiting is imprisonment.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: attached to a hard-owing estate or crossing
vibe_silhouette: A timber grate lies flush with a yard floor. A mat is pulled half over it.
vibe_palette: The yard is dust-coloured. It is dark below the grate. One bright patch of daylight falls on the pit floor.
vibe_materials: The pit has a timber grate and a mud-lined pit. The ladder is kept elsewhere.
vibe_signature_feature: The grate lies flush with the yard floor. People walk over it.
vibe_condition: The pit is serviceable. The brokers renew the mud lining every so often.
vibe_approach: No marker announces the pit. A villager has to point it out.
vibe_senses: Yard noise comes from above. A voice below is not shouting.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The debtor in the pit is being renegotiated over.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LF03 · tier-3; LF69 · tier-3; BC-line · tier-2
why_site_won: local tie in firm lowland (danger band 3), 80 m from the nearest route; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The Owing is a debt that is worked off and not paid. Argonians build no prisons, so the holding takes place in a roofed pit at the back of a broker's yard. The holding is called 'waiting'.

name: The Ravine Doors
why_founding: The rim rivers cut deep gorges. The flat ground in a gorge is on its walls. A community learned to live sideways on them.
why_site_advantages: The gorge wall has a natural bedding plane running along it at two levels. The shelf is the street.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers live here because the gorge is defensible against raiders. It is not defensible against the river. The river is predictable.
why_pressures: The lower shelf floods in a bad year. The upper shelf cannot hold the households of both shelves.
why_would_change_if: The village would move to the rim if the lower shelf were lost. It would lose half its people to the lowlands.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: commands a stretch of river; the corridor's signature settlement
vibe_silhouette: Two lines of doorways run in a rock wall, one above the other. Ladders link the lines. The river lies far below.
vibe_palette: The rock is grey-brown. The doorways are black. A strip of bright sky shows.
vibe_materials: The fronts are reed and timber built onto natural rock shelves. Barely a wall of the village is freestanding.
vibe_signature_feature: Movement through the village is vertical. The villagers pull the ladders up at night.
vibe_condition: The village is well built and constantly re-lashed. Cooking smoke blackens the rock above every door.
vibe_approach: From the gorge floor, cooking smoke comes out of a rock wall. There is no other cue.
vibe_senses: Voices come from directly above. The river runs continuously. Ladders knock against rock.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The ladders between the two shelves have been cut over an Owing.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 336 m from the nearest route; no free 'gorge' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, route.
player_purpose_hook: A community lives sideways on two shelves of a gorge wall. Porters carry loads that are too heavy for a traveller.

name: The Ring of Nine Wells
why_founding: The Ring is a Barsaebic Ayleid ring of well stones. Exiles who came east out of Cyrodiil built it. They set their wells where the ground was highest.
why_site_advantages: The Ring stands on a broad low dome of firm ground. Sightlines run between all nine positions.
why_occupants_motive: The local villages use the Ring as a meeting place. The villagers refuse to sleep in it.
why_pressures: Three wells still charge at dusk. Six wells do not. The Synod would like to know why.
why_would_change_if: The Ring would become a Synod compound. That happens the week that Gideon's council granted a lease.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in Ayleid country
vibe_silhouette: Nine white stumps stand in a wide circle on open ground. Three of them are faintly blue at dusk.
vibe_palette: The stone is bone white. Dusk adds blue. The grass is dry gold.
vibe_materials: The Ring is Barsaebic Ayleid dressed stone with welkynd fittings. No course has been added in four thousand years.
vibe_signature_feature: Three wells are live and six are dead. They are indistinguishable until the light goes.
vibe_condition: The stones are weathered to stumps. They are not inert.
vibe_mood: The ground is open. It feels strange for one hour at dusk.
vibe_approach: In daylight the whole Ring reads from outside it. At dusk only the three live stones show.
vibe_senses: A very low hum sounds near the live stones. Wind blows. The grass is laid flat in a circle.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Eight wells give water. The ninth gives back speech.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 1223 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, danger.
player_purpose_hook: Nine Ayleid well shafts stand on one low dome. Exiles sank them. Six of them are dead.

name: Rests-The-Walkers
why_founding: Nisswo travel on foot. The pilgrim road carries houses at half a day's interval.
why_site_advantages: The house stands half a day from Glenbridge. It stands where the road leaves the firm ground.
why_occupants_motive: The resident Nisswo hears the confessions of the road. The confessions are mostly about money.
why_pressures: The Imperial travellers on the road keep mistaking the house for an inn. The Nisswo feeds them anyway.
why_would_change_if: The pilgrims themselves would keep up the house if the Nisswo ever left.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: between villages on a preaching circuit
vibe_silhouette: A small house has a black-painted door. A bench outside faces the road.
vibe_palette: The door is black and the wall is ochre. Road dust covers the ground.
vibe_materials: The house is mud and reed. It is kept plain deliberately. The door is the painted part.
vibe_signature_feature: The bench is worn into two hollows. One hollow is for the Nisswo. The other is for whoever sits down.
vibe_condition: Plain and swept daily.
vibe_approach: The black door stands on a road of reed-brown ones. It reads at a hundred metres.
vibe_senses: A kettle sings. The road is audible. Long silences are not awkward.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The rest house has stopped receiving the walkers that it exists to receive.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: This is a walking priest's house on the pilgrim road. It offers a bed and a sermon about the end of the world.

name: Old Locks
why_founding: The Second Empire tried to make the Onkobra navigable to the uplands. It built a staircase of stone locks.
why_site_advantages: The locks stand at the reach where the river drops fastest.
why_occupants_motive: The villages downstream fish the pools that the ruined chambers formed.
why_pressures: The masonry is a millennium older than the Imperial work below. It is visibly better. The downstream headmen agree. They agree out of a Gideon clerk's hearing.
why_would_change_if: The locks would be worth rebuilding the day that upland freight paid for itself.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: under or beside later Imperial works
vibe_silhouette: Four stone chambers step up a wooded gorge. Each chamber is now a still green pool. A waterfall falls into each pool.
vibe_palette: The shade is deep green. The stone is wet and black. White water marks each step.
vibe_materials: The locks are Second Empire ashlar. The blocks are huge with tight joints. No mortar shows.
vibe_signature_feature: The gate recesses are still square. The pintles are still in them. The gates have been gone for a thousand years.
vibe_condition: The masonry is structurally superb. The ironwork is gone. Silt fills the chambers to half depth.
vibe_approach: There is no path. The route is up the river bed to the first chamber.
vibe_senses: Four waterfalls sound at different pitches. Water drips. Dressed stone echoes.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A failed lock floods Gideon's archive every wet season.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: A stone staircase of locks was built to make the river climb. It was abandoned unfinished. The chambers below the gates have not drained since.

name: The Second Hearth
why_founding: Argonians raised outside a Hist's reach built a hearth ring here. The ground was one where their gloor-faded skin drew no comment.
why_site_advantages: The site is close enough to Gideon for work. It is far enough that the settlers were not asked their business twice a day.
why_occupants_motive: The settlers rebuilt a mile off when the old ring flooded twice in one year. They left the first houses standing. They did not pull them down.
why_pressures: The new settlement will not send a party back for the timber. The speaker changes the subject when asked.
why_would_change_if: The houses would be stripped for materials. That happens once the fear of what dens there wore off.
siting_prefs_water_relation: wherever they were allowed to stop
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the edge of somewhere that refused them
vibe_silhouette: A ring of empty houses surrounds a bare central circle. A hearth used to stand in the circle. The roofs are failing one by one.
vibe_palette: Washed-out ochre has gone dark with damp. Pale scale-marks show on the doorframes. Weeds grow in the empty centre.
vibe_materials: The houses are standard mud-and-wattle round houses. Several have caved in at the back wall.
vibe_signature_feature: The hearth stone stands at the centre. It is cold and cracked. It is swept.
vibe_condition: Half the ring has collapsed. The other half holds a den.
vibe_approach: The gap in the middle still reads from the approach. It reads the same as when people lived here.
vibe_senses: Wind blows through open doorframes. Claw marks scar a threshold. No birdsong sounds nearby.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 116 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The Hist-less who built this hearth moved a mile off. The hearth flooded twice in a year. The settlers left the old houses standing for whatever moved in after them.

name: Sermon Road Camp
why_founding: Glenbridge cannot house a sermon crowd. The overflow camps a mile short. The pilgrims walk in at dawn.
why_site_advantages: The camp is a flat bench beside the pilgrim path. It has water and firewood. It has no landlord.
why_occupants_motive: Pilgrims camp here because arriving at dawn is considered better. The innkeepers price the difference.
why_pressures: Foreign pilgrims and Nisswo pilgrims camp at opposite ends of the meadow.
why_would_change_if: The camp would become a village if the sermon ever drew a permanent crowd. The people of Glenbridge would fight that.
siting_prefs_water_relation: water and firm ground on a pilgrim route
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the last stop before a sacred destination
vibe_silhouette: Sixty small fires burn in a meadow at dusk. They form two distinct clusters. A clear gap lies between the clusters.
vibe_palette: The fires are orange. The meadow is grey-green. Black Nisswo cloth fills one end. Every other colour fills the other end.
vibe_materials: The camp uses bedrolls, awnings and a shared water point. The ground is worn bare in the same two patches every year.
vibe_signature_feature: Forty metres of unused meadow separate the two camps.
vibe_condition: The camp is seasonal. Out of season the two bare patches remain.
vibe_mood: The pilgrims are devout and sociable. They are sectarian about pitches.
vibe_approach: The fires are visible from the road at dusk. In daylight the meadow is unremarkable.
vibe_senses: Two different chants sound at once. Kettles sing. A dawn stir starts in the dark.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The overflow camp has become a village. The shrine will not feed it.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 485 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform.
player_purpose_hook: The overflow camp lies a mile short of Glenbridge. It has water and firewood but no landlord. Pilgrim rumours reach it a day before they reach Glenbridge.

name: The Shaking House
why_founding: The marsh gives travellers fevers. The villages will not risk the fever cases. The sick are put somewhere apart and tended anyway.
why_site_advantages: The house stands downwind and downstream of the village. It has its own spit. Carriers bring clean water in to the house.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper is a survivor of swamp rot. The keeper cannot catch it again and knows it.
why_pressures: The villagers pay in food and never visit. The keeper's own family have not crossed the spit in nine years.
why_would_change_if: The house would be burned and rebuilt at a spot fifty metres away. That happens at the first sign of anything that the keeper does not recognise.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: 200-600 m outside an M3+ settlement
vibe_silhouette: A long low shed stands on a spit. A burning ground lies beside it. A bell hangs on a post at the water's edge.
vibe_palette: The inside is lime white. The outside is smoke grey. Brown water lies between the house and everything else.
vibe_materials: The house is limewashed wattle. The reed roof is renewed yearly. The burning floor is stone.
vibe_signature_feature: The bell post stands on the far bank. A shelf under it holds what the village leaves.
vibe_condition: The house is scrupulously clean. It is deliberately cheap to burn.
vibe_approach: The bell post shows first, on the near bank. The shed stands across the water from it.
vibe_senses: The bell rings. Coughing carries over water. Lime and woodsmoke scent the air.
player_purpose_hook: This is where the fever cases are put and tended anyway. The keeper treats arrivals. The keeper will not let them back on the road early.

name: Door-That-Stayed-Shut
why_founding: The Door-That-Stayed-Shut is a xanmeer. Its own people closed it deliberately. Its traps are still live. Its contents are undisturbed.
why_site_advantages: The site is low ground that has half-drowned. The sealed door stands at the level of the standing water. The terraces above the door are cut off for half the year.
why_occupants_motive: The nearest village knows the xanmeer is there. The villagers do not approach it.
why_pressures: Water is getting in below the seal. The water will eventually open the door from underneath.
why_would_change_if: The xanmeer would be open from below once the water finished the job.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it
vibe_silhouette: Stone terraces stand stacked out of reed and shallow water. A sealed door sits two hand-widths above the waterline.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey with a green-black waterline. Above the waterline the stone is dry pale grey.
vibe_materials: The xanmeer is built of ashlar. One vakka-stone seal plate closes the door.
vibe_signature_feature: The vakka-stone seal plate is unbroken.
vibe_condition: The stone above the water is preserved. The stone below the water is undermined.
vibe_approach: The terraces show above the reeds at about two hundred metres. The door does not show from that distance.
vibe_senses: Water laps against the stone. Striking the seal plate gives a hollow note. No sound comes from inside.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 627 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on nearPoint, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: The xanmeer's own people sealed it. Its traps are live and its contents lie where they were left. The door is now at water level.
siting_note: The record was moved to the drowned ground below Glenbridge in round 4. There the standing water reaches the sealed door that gives the record its name.

name: The Silent Halls
why_founding: The Silent Halls is a Merethic xanmeer. It was opened long ago. The Sul-Xan took it over. The Sul-Xan use its chambers to keep what their snares catch.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer lies in deep stone below the water table. The halls are cool, dark and very quiet.
why_occupants_motive: The Sul-Xan keep the xanmeer because a soul-store needs walls. The tribes do not contest it. The tribes will not enter a broken xanmeer.
why_pressures: The mechanism floor still works. The Sul-Xan do not understand the mechanisms. The Four Winds want the place burned.
why_would_change_if: The place would become a tended xanmeer again. That happens if a tribe with a claim takes it back and closes it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a district with other xanmeer, showing the range of states
vibe_silhouette: A low terrace, mostly buried, stands in the trees. It has one forced doorway. The lintel of the doorway is cracked and propped.
vibe_palette: The doorway is black and the stone is pale. Jade points of light show inside.
vibe_materials: The halls use xanmeer ashlar and vakka-stone fittings. Sul-Xan hide and cord are strung through the chambers.
vibe_signature_feature: The gem shelf holds hundreds of soul-gems. The soul-gems sit in niches made for the dead. Each soul-gem is lit from inside.
vibe_condition: The xanmeer is broken open and occupied. Half its mechanisms are still armed.
vibe_approach: The forest noise stops about thirty metres from the xanmeer.
vibe_senses: No insects are heard. Footsteps sound too loud. A faint singing comes from the gem shelf.
why_site_won: enclosed clearing in firm lowland (danger band 4), 114 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The Sul-Xan opened this xanmeer. They keep whatever their snares catch in the chambers below it.

name: The Snowline Cell
why_founding: The air above the marsh's ceiling is cold and dry. That air carries no disease. One order of ascetics winters there.
why_site_advantages: The cell stands on the highest saddle of the western rim. Snow lies on the saddle for a few weeks a year. The cells are cut back into the saddle rock. The older cells behind the occupied row have been sealed. The older cells were not cleared.
why_occupants_motive: Two ascetics winter here. They aim to prove that an Argonian can winter here. They mean the wintering as theology.
why_pressures: One of the two ascetics is dying of the cold. Both ascetics treat the dying as evidence.
why_would_change_if: The cell would be empty in a decade. A third ascetic would have to join to prevent that.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: the rim's signature dwelling; deliberately alone
vibe_silhouette: A drystone cell the size of a cart is built into a saddle wall. A fuel stack twice the cell's size stands beside it.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey. The snow is white for six weeks. The fuel stack is brown. The green province lies below.
vibe_materials: The cell is built of dry stone and hauled peat. It uses no reed and no mud.
vibe_signature_feature: The fuel stack is twice the size of the cell. It is the largest thing on the saddle.
vibe_condition: The cell is solid and tiny. The inside is immaculately dry.
vibe_mood: The ascetics are lucid and pleased with themselves.
vibe_approach: The climb takes five hours. From the saddle the marsh lies as a green floor below.
vibe_senses: Wind blows constantly. Peat smoke hangs in the air. The ascetics' teeth chatter. The ascetics find that funny.
why_site_won: ravine in upland hills (danger band 3), 137 m from the nearest route; won on route, hinterland, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Ascetics live above the marsh's ceiling in cold dry air. They will argue at length that disease is a choice.

name: The Standing Mist
why_founding: The Standing Mist forms in a cold-air hollow on the rim. The mist forms every night. The mist does not lift until midday.
why_site_advantages: The hollow is a box canyon with a spring in it. The water is cold and the air is still. There is no draught.
why_occupants_motive: Two villages graze the edges of the hollow. Neither village takes stock in before noon. Something takes stock in the dark.
why_pressures: Things are lost in the mist regularly. Two people were lost in the last decade.
why_would_change_if: The hollow would be ordinary ground if the spring failed.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: visible as a feature from a nearby high point
vibe_silhouette: A canyon mouth holds a flat white ceiling of mist. The mist is level as water. A path drops beneath it.
vibe_palette: The view is white, then grey. Beyond that, only what is close enough to see shows.
vibe_materials: The place has no building. Cairns stand inside the mist. Travellers who were trying to find their way out placed the cairns.
vibe_signature_feature: From above, the mist is a lake of white. The canyon walls stand out of it.
vibe_condition: Unchanged; the cairns accumulate.
vibe_mood: The mist is disorienting. Sound carries further than sight.
vibe_approach: The rim above overlooks the top of the mist.
vibe_senses: Sound arrives from the wrong direction. Water drips. A voice returns flat.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The mist does not move with the wind.
why_site_won: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 526 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The mist stands in the hollow until midday. A sink lies at the bottom of the hollow. Something living is in the white.

name: The Stone Drop
why_founding: The toll company needs an off-the-books place to leave goods it seizes. The company takes these goods on the Swampmoth road. The goods stay at the drop until a buyer is found.
why_site_advantages: The site is a scree bench above the fort road. The slope screens the bench from the road below. Two scrambles lead down from the bench onto the road.
why_occupants_motive: The men holding the bench are paid by the week. They sit on other people's goods. They are to be somewhere else when the fort asks.
why_pressures: Fort Swampmoth can see the smoke from a fire on the bench. For that reason the men keep no fire after dark. They are cold all winter.
why_would_change_if: The drop would be given up if the company were made to keep an honest weighbridge.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: above the road on which it preys, within sight of the fort from which it hides
vibe_silhouette: Three low shelters stand on a bench of loose stone. The shelters are roofed with scree-coloured canvas. They are invisible from the road below.
vibe_palette: The scene is grey on grey. One stack of seized bales in dyed cloth does not belong there.
vibe_materials: The shelters use canvas over cut poles. The stone walls are dry-laid from the scree itself. A strongbox was brought up on a mule.
vibe_signature_feature: The goods are stacked by owner. Each lot still carries its cart mark.
vibe_condition: The drop is cold and tidy. It is temporary by design.
vibe_mood: The men are bored. They will fight to avoid being identified.
vibe_approach: The scramble up gives the drop away. It is a boot-polished line in the scree. The top of the line holds no pasture.
vibe_senses: Stone shifts underfoot. There is no smoke. A mule complains somewhere below.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Every bale on the bench still carries the cart mark of its original owner.
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 325 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, nearPoint, route.
player_purpose_hook: This is the toll company's off-book store above the Swampmoth road. The goods are stacked by owner.
siting_note: The record is bound to the rim shoulder directly above the Fort Swampmoth path in round 4. The record exists because that shoulder overlooks the road. Two scrambles lead down onto the road.

name: Holds-The-Stone
why_founding: The Ca-Uxith were charged by their Hist with watching the Rockgrove xanmeer. The village stands beside the ruin for that reason. The tribe has held this ground as long as the charge has existed.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on the last firm shelf before the geyser field. The shelf is close enough to see the xanmeer's upper courses. The shelf is also far enough away that the ground does not vent under the houses.
why_occupants_motive: The stone-talkers do the actual work. They read the ruin's stone for the cracks that the geysers open. They pack the cracks with clay before the ruin comes apart.
why_pressures: The Sul-Xan keep a raid camp on the ruin that the Ca-Uxith are sworn to keep. The tribe has no means to remove the Sul-Xan. The geyser field is getting louder. The elders disagree about whose fault that is.
why_would_change_if: The charge would end if the xanmeer collapsed. The tribe would then have no reason to be here. Several of the young ones say so aloud.
siting_prefs_water_relation: upslope of a geyser field, on spring water that is drinkable and hot
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: within sight of place.imperial-fringe.rockgrove; no other neighbour within an hour
vibe_silhouette: A low village stands on a shelf. Drying racks of grey clay run along its edge. Behind the village, steam stands in columns. The steam columns do not move with the wind.
vibe_palette: The colours are steam white and packing-clay grey. Hot-spring rust-orange stains the rock. A red Hist flower grows well back from all of it.
vibe_materials: The houses are reed and mud with a great deal of worked clay. The tribe packs stone that it did not cut. The tribe quarries no stone of its own.
vibe_signature_feature: Every visible crack in the xanmeer opposite has a grey clay seam. A notch dates each seam.
vibe_condition: The village is modest and worn. The clay work is kept up.
vibe_mood: The villagers are dutiful and tired. The villages below send food.
vibe_approach: The steam gives the village away long before the roofs show. The guide who meets visitors walks a fixed line between the vents.
vibe_senses: Vents hiss on a slow rhythm. A sulphur smell lies under the cooking smell. A talker taps the stone to sound it.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Ca-Uxith are a canon Argonian counterparty to the Sul-Xan at Rockgrove. The stone-talkers practise a preservation craft that can be taught or can be defended on request. The geyser field is a live, worsening hazard next to a settlement.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LF56 · tier-3; LF76 · tier-3; LF77 · tier-3; LF78 · tier-3; tier-1 owned
player_purpose_hook: The Ca-Uxith were charged by their Hist with watching the Rockgrove xanmeer. Sul-Xan raiders are camped on the xanmeer now.

name: The Sunk Lane
why_founding: The burn country's peat burned out from below in places. The ground collapsed where the burnt roof failed.
why_site_advantages: A collapse opened within living memory. It cut across an old cart lane on the rim's peat bench. The carters had trusted that peat for generations.
why_occupants_motive: The lane ends at the hole. Ruts run to the lip on both sides.
why_pressures: The hole is still widening. The villages measure it with a stake each year.
why_would_change_if: The hole would swallow the last of the lane within a generation.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: rare — eleven found province-wide; every instance should be individually meaningful
vibe_silhouette: A cart lane stops at a hole that measures thirty metres from side to side. Black water lies at the bottom of the hole.
vibe_palette: The hole walls are brown and fringed with roots. The water is black. The cart ruts are ordinary.
vibe_materials: The place has no building. A line of stakes marks the rim's retreat. The line holds one stake per year.
vibe_signature_feature: Cart ruts run to the lip. The ruts start again on the far side.
vibe_condition: Actively enlarging.
vibe_approach: The lane is ordinary until the ground stops at ten metres. The ground stops with no warning.
vibe_senses: Water drips from roots. A dropped stone takes a long time to land.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 794 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.onkobra-clay-pits (+0.85).
player_purpose_hook: The peat burned out from underneath and took the road with it. The lane is still down there in the dark.

name: The Turned-Out
why_founding: An Owing can be called in against a household's land. The household is then put outside.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the verge of the road. It is within sight of the fields that the households worked. The brokers put the households out at that spot.
why_occupants_motive: The households stay in sight of the fields deliberately. Leaving would be taken as abandoning the claim.
why_pressures: It is the third winter of the camp. Two families have gone to Gideon and have not come back.
why_would_change_if: The camp would end tomorrow if the estate voided one ledger.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: immediately outside an estate village
vibe_silhouette: Six lean-tos of salvaged thatch stand on a road verge. All the lean-tos face the same way. They face the field that the households used to work.
vibe_palette: The camp is the colour of dust and salvaged straw. The fields beyond it are a too-neat green.
vibe_materials: The households reassembled their salvaged house materials badly. The thatch is better than the frames. The households carried the thatch with them.
vibe_signature_feature: Every shelter faces the fields. No door opens on the road.
vibe_condition: It is the third year of the camp. The camp is no longer temporary.
vibe_approach: The camp is on the road. Travellers pass within a few metres of it.
vibe_senses: The camp is very quiet. A hand mill turns. Children are being kept quiet.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The evicted household on the verge holds a deed. The estate steward will not read the deed.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 22 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-knapping-floor-of-the-high-scree (+1.18).
player_purpose_hook: Households were put out of their own fields for a called debt. They camp on the verge within sight of the fields.

name: The Two Lamps
why_founding: A hermit made himself unreachable at this spot. He then hung a lamp out for anyone who made the climb.
why_site_advantages: The site is a cliff bench forty metres up a ravine wall. One climb reaches it. There is no path.
why_occupants_motive: The hermit is here to be alone. The second lamp is for a person he expects. That person has not come.
why_pressures: The hermit is old. The climb is not getting easier. The villages below have begun to worry aloud.
why_would_change_if: The hut would become a shrine after the hermit's death. He knows that and dislikes it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design
vibe_silhouette: A hut is wedged on a ledge. Two lamps hang from a pole. One lamp is lit and one is not.
vibe_palette: The colours are rock grey and lamp yellow. The ravine below is black.
vibe_materials: The hut is built of stone and driftwood that was carried up over years. The roof is a single sheet from the boat of an unknown owner.
vibe_signature_feature: The second lamp is unlit. It is cleaned and filled.
vibe_condition: The hut is improbably sound. Every fixing is doubled. A replacement has to be carried up the wall.
vibe_approach: The visitor sees one lamp forty metres up a black wall. Wet rock lies above and below the lamp.
vibe_senses: Wind passes the ledge. Water drips. A very quiet voice speaks.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 227 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: A hermit made himself unreachable. He then hung a lamp out for climbers who got up anyway. Reaching him is a forty-metre climb.

name: Vellum Estate
why_founding: Vellum Estate is an Archein-era estate. It survived the end of slavery. It converted its slaves into Owing debtors on paper.
why_site_advantages: The estate holds good drained land on the river terrace. It is held in one block because no heir has yet divided it.
why_occupants_motive: The estate house holds the ledgers. Without the ledgers, the Owing lapses. The workers would then walk.
why_pressures: The Chainbreakers know the estate exists. The courthouse also knows. The ledgers are lawful.
why_would_change_if: The estate would dissolve overnight if a court voided inherited Owings.
siting_prefs_water_relation: controls a crossing or a landing
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: holds the crossing that its neighbours must use
vibe_silhouette: A pale estate house stands at the head of an avenue. Two long worker rows stand behind it at right angles.
vibe_palette: The house is bleached lime. The avenue is in shade. The worker rows are dun.
vibe_materials: The front of the house is Imperial estate masonry. The rear is mud and reed. The change happens along one line across the yard.
vibe_signature_feature: The strong room window is barred at ledger height. The rest of the house is shuttered.
vibe_condition: The house is well kept where the avenue shows it. The occupants patch the rows themselves.
vibe_approach: The avenue frames the house from four hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Cicadas sing. A bell rings for shift change. No children's voices sound near the house.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The estate's washed-out labourers are owed three seasons of wages. The house that owes them keeps immaculate books.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LF79 · tier-3; LF80 · tier-3; MQ11 · tier-3; province system · tier-1
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 71 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The estate survived the end of slavery by rewriting its slaves as debtors. It has the paperwork to prove that this was legal.

name: The White Throat
why_founding: A rim river drops twenty metres at this spot. The river has cut back into the rock. It left a room behind the water.
why_site_advantages: The undercut has standing headroom. It stays dry enough for storage.
why_occupants_motive: Smugglers and one hermit have both used the chamber. Each left different rubbish.
why_pressures: The flow of the fall doubles after rain. The chamber floods to knee height.
why_would_change_if: In a province with fewer waterfalls, the chamber would be a shrine. Here it is a good room.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only
vibe_silhouette: A curtain of white water hangs over a black slot. The slot is invisible from the path above.
vibe_palette: The water is white and the wet rock is black. Green light comes through the fall.
vibe_materials: One stacked stone shelf stands in the chamber. It is built above flood height.
vibe_signature_feature: Moving water lights the chamber green.
vibe_condition: The flood scours the chamber clean every year. Whatever is stored there was put there recently.
vibe_approach: The fall is audible for four hundred metres. The chamber is invisible until the last three metres of the approach.
vibe_senses: The water is so loud that speech is lost. Water drips. Breathing sounds amplified.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 760 m from the nearest route; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: A dry room lies behind the waterfall. People have kept things in it for longer than the village has stood.

name: White Hill Camp
why_founding: Antiquities are bought in Gideon. A camp stands above the graves that supply them.
why_site_advantages: The camp is just over the ridge from the cairn field. It is out of sight of the valley track. It is upwind of the smell of its own camp.
why_occupants_motive: The hunters are here for glass beads. The beads are small and light. A bead is worth a season's wages in Leyawiin.
why_pressures: The Collections dig offers better pay. Its staff ask questions. Two of this camp have already crossed over.
why_would_change_if: The camp would move to the next dead people in the month that the beads ran out.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: beside a notable ruin or hard-to-reach landform
vibe_silhouette: Four hide tents stand behind a ridge. A sorting mat lies beside them. A great deal of broken stone lies about with no buyer.
vibe_palette: The colours are hide brown, bead blue-green and ridge grey.
vibe_materials: The camp uses hide and poles. It also uses one stolen conservation tarpaulin. The hunters have not bothered to hide the tarpaulin.
vibe_signature_feature: The sorting mat has beads laid out by colour. The hunters push the bone aside with a boot.
vibe_condition: Filthy and well armed.
vibe_approach: Smoke rises over a ridge. It is seen from the cairn field.
vibe_senses: Stone is knapped open. Voices stay low. Flies buzz.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 596 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-borrowed-house (+0.49).
player_purpose_hook: Diggers camp over the cairn field. The camp is upwind and out of sight of the track. The diggers buy or rob depending on the hour.

name: Twyllbek Crown
why_founding: The Barsaebic compound at Twyllbek has one block with sound upper courses. The collapsed stair of the block has left the outside face climbable.
why_site_advantages: The block stands on the high corner of the compound. The height clears the scrub. From the block, the Blackwood road is visible for four kilometres.
why_occupants_motive: The block stands empty. Couriers use the top as a drop. The Collections surveyor climbs it twice a year. The surveyor measures the collapse.
why_pressures: The face can be climbed because it is failing. Two courses have gone in the last decade. The route changes each time.
why_would_change_if: The top would be unreachable if the face came down.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: a canopy-breaking landmark in dense country
vibe_silhouette: One square Ayleid block stands clear of a low ruin field. A stair-scar runs down one face. The top is open to the sky.
vibe_palette: The Barsaebic pale stone has gone lichen-orange on the weather face. The scrub is black. The top surface is bleached white.
vibe_materials: The block is Ayleid block-and-course work. The collapsed internal stair is now a set of holds on the outside.
vibe_signature_feature: The stair that used to run inside the block is climbed on its outer face.
vibe_condition: The block is failing at a measurable rate. The stakes of the Collections surveyor show how fast.
vibe_approach: The block reads as a stump from the road. It reads as a tower from the ruin field. The scale flips over the last two hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Wind blows at the top and none blows at the bottom. Grit lies under the hands. The road is audible from above.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The block is a pure climbing objective with a reveal at the top. The courier dead-drop can be watched or robbed.
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 1075 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, danger, parent.
player_purpose_hook: An Ayleid block still stands to its upper courses. It is the last of its field. The collapsed stair makes a climb to the top.

name: Twyllbek Ruins
why_founding: Twyllbek Ruins is a Barsaebic Ayleid compound from the exile centuries. It is close enough to Gideon that the antiquities trade of the city starts here.
why_site_advantages: The compound stands on a dry terrace over a spring. That is Ayleid siting logic. The diggers of Gideon keep coming back to the terrace.
why_occupants_motive: The diggers want stones with light in them. The Collections chapter wants the same stones back. Both are here most months.
why_pressures: Every season of digging takes more of the wall.
why_would_change_if: The ruin would be protected properly if the council of Gideon thought a ruin was worth a guard.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in the north and west, where the Barsaebic Ayleids went
vibe_silhouette: A white arcade fragment stands on a green terrace. It is geometric in the Ayleid way.
vibe_palette: The colours are bone white and moss. A live well stone gives a cold blue.
vibe_materials: The ruin is Barsaebic Ayleid masonry with welkynd fittings. Canvas and rope mark where the diggers work.
vibe_signature_feature: String lines and numbered pegs lie over a floor that already had a grid.
vibe_condition: The ruin is half-excavated. It is weather-damaged where excavation exposed it.
vibe_approach: The white shows through the trees from the Gideon track a good way off.
vibe_senses: Trowels scrape. Cold air rises from a well. Canvas snaps.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The dig licence sealed the ground doors. That leaves the roof as the remaining route.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MR03 · tier-2; LF05 · tier-3; LF28 · tier-3
why_site_won: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 570 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: This Barsaebic compound is the ground on which the antiquities trade of Gideon was built. It has been dug over for a century and is still not emptied.

name: Culvert Line
why_founding: The line was the correction to the embankment. Stone culverts were cut and dressed on site. They were then left where they were cut.
why_site_advantages: The stone was dressed where it was quarried. The quarry lay next to the line that the culverts were meant to serve.
why_occupants_motive: Road thieves live in the dressed culverts. A cut stone pipe is a dry room with two exits. The tribes quarrel over stone-taking. That quarrel keeps the villages off the line.
why_pressures: Building in dead stone is a moral error here after Duskfall. The blocks therefore sit where they were left.
why_would_change_if: The line would vanish in a decade if a village with a use for stone stood nearby.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: on the line of an abandoned Imperial road
vibe_silhouette: Sixty dressed stone rings lie in a line in long grass. The line ends in the middle of a field.
vibe_palette: Pale dressed stone stands against unmown green. Lichen grows on the top faces and nowhere else.
vibe_materials: The rings are cut Imperial voussoirs and ring segments. The tooling marks are still crisp.
vibe_signature_feature: Every block is chiselled with its position. The numbering ends at forty-one.
vibe_condition: The stone is untouched and unweathered underneath. The rings are sinking slowly.
vibe_approach: The grass is as tall as the rings. The visitor walks into the line before seeing it.
vibe_senses: Grass rustles. Cut stone lies under it.
why_site_won: waterfall in seasonal floodplain (danger band 5), 364 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: Culverts were cut, dressed and left unlaid in a line across the plain. They have been lived in ever since.

name: Vanin's Signal
why_founding: Vanin's Signal is one of the signal towers. The towers relayed word from the north gate along the hill line to the ducal seat.
why_site_advantages: The tower has dry footing above the flood. It has a view down four miles of cart road.
why_occupants_motive: A kaj-thux has denned in the fallen stair. The stair is dry. The stone of the stair stays warm well past dark because it keeps the day's heat.
why_pressures: Carters now go round by the ford. The detour adds an hour and a toll to the journey.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the den would make the platform usable ground again. The whole road would then be in view from it.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in sight of a cart road, out of shouting distance of any village
vibe_silhouette: Two thirds of a square tower stand on a knoll. The fallen third lies downhill in one piece.
vibe_palette: The ashlar is grey with orange lichen. The cart road below is red.
vibe_materials: The tower is built of dressed stone with an iron brazier ring. The timber floors have gone to powder.
vibe_signature_feature: The stair fell inward. The fall made a dry chamber under the rubble.
vibe_condition: The standing courses are sound. The slope under them is still moving.
vibe_approach: The tower is visible from the road for a mile. It was built to be visible.
vibe_senses: Wind blows through the arrow slits. A dry rustle sounds under the stair.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Whoever holds the platform sees the road traffic first. Several parties would pay for that view.
why_site_won: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 620 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, nearPoint, region.
player_purpose_hook: A signal tower has a snake in its fallen stair. Four miles of road are visible from the top.

name: Weighed Cart
why_founding: Gideon's council put a tower where the road forks for the clay pits. The pits' output is an export that the council can actually count.
why_site_advantages: The tower stands on a knoll that commands both forks. Every cart on either fork is seen and counted from it.
why_occupants_motive: The tower's clerk is paid on what he records. He records every axle.
why_pressures: The potters route half their carts round the tower by night. The clerk has written that up twice.
why_would_change_if: The tower would be pointless if the clay bank moved. The clay bank moves every generation.
siting_prefs_water_relation: commands a channel or a road
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: one of a chain; must see a neighbour or it is not a watch
vibe_silhouette: A squat two-storey stone tower has an external stair. A weigh beam juts from the first floor.
vibe_palette: The stone is soot-grey. Red clay dust reaches waist height on the wall and the door.
vibe_materials: The tower is built of Imperial rubble masonry and has a reed-roofed lean-to. One iron beam is the most valuable object for a kilometre.
vibe_signature_feature: The seizure shelf under the stair holds unclaimed pots. The pots go back decades.
vibe_condition: The tower is serviceable and grubby. It is over-stocked with confiscations.
vibe_approach: The tower is visible from the clay pits and from the fork. The beam stands out against the sky.
vibe_senses: The beam creaks. A tally is called out. Carts change gear on the slope.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tower's weigh beam reads heavy for some carts and not for others.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 151 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: Every cart off the clay road is weighed under this tower. The recorded weight sets the tax.

name: Westfield
why_founding: Argonian villagers took up field agriculture from their Imperial neighbours. They now grow it better than the Imperials do.
why_site_advantages: Westfield stands on temperate grassland on the saddle's western apron. It is the largest stretch of arable in the west.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers farm because grain sells in Gideon. In a bad year they ask whatever price they like.
why_pressures: The fields are held in common. The Imperial grants overlap the fields on paper. The field-holder has not tested the overlap in Gideon's court.
why_would_change_if: The villagers would fight, in court or otherwise, the first time another party tested the overlap.
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: in a city's agricultural hinterland
vibe_silhouette: Round mud houses with conical thatch sit in open grain fields.
vibe_palette: The colours are grain gold and thatch gold. The mud walls are ochre. The field-edge trees are dark green.
vibe_materials: The houses are Argonian mud-and-wattle round houses. A stilted granary stands among them. No boundary is straight.
vibe_signature_feature: The threshing floor is a beaten clay disc. It is bigger than any house in the village.
vibe_condition: The village is thriving and expanding. It is rebuilt on a rolling cycle. A quarter of it is new in any year.
vibe_mood: The villagers are confident and competitive with the Imperials next door.
vibe_approach: The fields start abruptly. The roofs stand lower than the grain.
vibe_senses: Threshing continues. A work song is sung. Grain dust hangs in the light.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The shared granary loses a measured amount each week. The seals stay intact.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: FG01 · tier-2; LF81 · tier-3; LF82 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 258 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.stonewastes (+1.27).
player_purpose_hook: Argonian villagers took field farming from their Imperial neighbours. They bake the best bread in the west.

name: Low Fen House
why_founding: The College of Whispers kept a house here. The College worked out of the magistracy's sight. It closed the posting and left the cellar as it stood.
why_site_advantages: The house is a stilt house over standing water. A pole-punt can reach it and there is no path. What the College left behind has gone undisturbed for years.
why_occupants_motive: No scholar has held the posting in years. The cellar workings were left running. The College did not shut them down.
why_pressures: The College was decanting something in the cellar. That work has kept going unminded since the last scholar left.
why_would_change_if: The College itself would reopen the house if it ever wanted to know what its workings became.
siting_prefs_water_relation: a quiet way out by water
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: inside a settlement, indistinguishable from it
vibe_silhouette: An ordinary reed stilt house has too many shutters. It stands alone on open water. No path leads to it.
vibe_palette: The reed is grey-gold gone black with rot. The water is dark. One green-glass window is still unbroken.
vibe_materials: The house uses local stilt construction. It was built that way to hide what lies underneath.
vibe_signature_feature: Barrels still hang slung below the platform. Some barrels are split open. The water around them is off-colour.
vibe_condition: The house above is collapsing. The cellar below it is intact.
vibe_mood: The house is quiet, though the working is still running.
vibe_approach: A punt reaches the house. From the water it looks like any other stilt house.
vibe_senses: Water laps under rotten boards. A low sound is heard that is not the wind. The smell of something still being made hangs in the air.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 31 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: The College of Whispers closed this house years ago. It left the cellar workings running. Something old still guards the workings.

name: Xi-Tsei
why_founding: A whole community was killed on this ground in 1E 2820. The Sul-Xan trace their grievance from the killing.
why_site_advantages: The ground is an open flat between two ridges. It is one of the few grounds in the Blackwood where an army can be made to stand and fight.
why_occupants_motive: The Sul-Xan come each year and leave marks. The Four Winds remove the marks.
why_pressures: Two peoples tend the same field against each other. The work of both is visible.
why_would_change_if: The ground would be settled again if both traditions lapsed.
siting_prefs_water_relation: where an army could deploy — rare here
siting_prefs_neighbour_relation: at a xanmeer, a crossing or a road
vibe_silhouette: A wide empty flat has grass growing in rows. No hand planted the rows. A single pole stands at the centre.
vibe_palette: The colours are straw-gold grass and rust in the soil. Grey ridges lie on either side.
vibe_materials: The ground has no architecture. It holds bone, corroded iron and jade chips. The pole is replaced yearly.
vibe_signature_feature: Painted jade tallies lie on the flat. Beside each tally is a scrubbed patch where it was removed.
vibe_condition: Only two rituals disturb the ground.
vibe_approach: The ridges draw closer together. The ground goes level and treeless.
vibe_senses: Only wind is heard. The pole's cords creak. Birds do not visit the flat itself.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The yearly count has been read out wrong for a generation.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 33 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: A whole community was killed on this ground in 1E 2820. Every Sul-Xan grievance since is traced from it.
siting_note: Lore:Xi-Tsei puts the site on the southern strip of Blackwood. That strip is administered as Cyrodiil. The record sites it inside the province here. The border there has moved more than once. The massacre is Argonian history wherever the line currently runs.

name: The Potentate's Works
why_founding: Versidue-Shaie was the Akaviri Potentate. His people left works in this basin while building the Rose. The works are not Cyrodilic in any detail.
why_site_advantages: The works stand on the quarry road between the Robbed City and the Rose. The stone for a single day's building was handled there.
why_occupants_motive: The works are empty. The stone-handling gear was designed for atronachs. The gear makes no sense for people.
why_pressures: These are the best surviving Akaviri civil works south of Gideon. The quarry crews who pass them call them old Imperial work.
why_would_change_if: An identification would bring outside scholars and their money into the district. The district wants neither.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey and dressed with unusual tooling. Green invasion covers the works.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone-handling yard has lifting sockets sized for something inhumanly strong. Akaviri tool-marks show on every dressed face.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest could establish the purpose of the lifting sockets. That would answer how the Rose went up in a day.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 233 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Threewater's crews call the works old Imperial. The working notes inside say how the Rose went up in a day.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: under or beside later Imperial works

name: Bell-Under-The-Cliff
why_founding: Bell-Under-The-Cliff is a karst chamber in the lake's limestone shore. It holds a bubble of air above the water line. It is entered from below.
why_site_advantages: The chamber lies three metres under the shore cliff. It opens into a dry chamber the size of a room.
why_occupants_motive: Whoever currently needs a hiding place uses the chamber as a cache. No search will find the cache.
why_pressures: The air is old. The chamber is silent enough to hear the lake through the rock.
why_would_change_if: A rise in lake level would flood the bell. It would drown whatever is in it.
vibe_silhouette: There is no exterior at all. A cliff-foot shore shows nothing. A dry room lies hidden three metres under it.
vibe_palette: The colours are wet limestone cream, black water and lamp gold.
vibe_materials: The chamber is a natural limestone dome. One natural stone shelf serves as a store. Oiled hide wrappings cover the goods. A single lamp lights the chamber. Nothing in it is built and nothing is fixed.
vibe_signature_feature: A dry limestone room is reached only by swimming down and up again. Dry goods are stacked on a natural shelf.
vibe_condition: The chamber is undisturbed and in constant use. The goods change and the room never does.
vibe_approach: The visitor swims down along the cliff foot and up again. The first sign of the chamber is the visitor's head breaking into air.
vibe_senses: Dead air rings like the inside of a bell. Drips fall on a long slow beat. Lamp-oil scents the air. Sacking is dry after cold water.
player_purpose_hook: The chamber lies three metres under the shore cliff. It opens into a dry chamber the size of a room.
deferred_why: The place was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The place is a lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: hidden; discovered by exploring water

name: The Running Post
why_founding: Three rivers and a lake mean that letters go by boat and arrive late. The runners exist because the causeway road is faster than the water.
why_site_advantages: The post stands at the junction of the causeway road and the lake shore. Fresh runners are always waiting.
why_occupants_motive: Runners are paid by the delivery. They race each other for the good routes.
why_pressures: Everything to and from the Rose passes through the post. Some of it is read.
why_would_change_if: A regular ferry timetable would make the runners obsolete on two of their three routes.
vibe_palette: The colours are chalk white, dust and running-leather brown.
vibe_signature_feature: A post carries a peg board of destinations. A bench holds waiting runners. A chalked record shows the day's best times.
player_purpose_hook: The post stands at the junction of the causeway road and the lake shore. Fresh runners are always waiting.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'courier-relay' runs 10 province-wide against a countBand of 7-9. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

name: The Counting Stones
why_founding: Nineteen dressed stones stand in the marsh. They stand in a line that points at nothing. They are older than the Lilmothiit city.
why_site_advantages: The stones stand on a firm ridge under the marsh. The ridge only becomes apparent when one walks the line.
why_occupants_motive: No people occupy the stones. Villages count them on passing and disagree about the total. That disagreement is a local joke with an edge to it.
why_pressures: Two stones have fallen. They were re-erected in the wrong sockets. No living person noticed.
why_would_change_if: Nothing explains the stones. Every proposed explanation has been wrong.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone, reed gold and flat water.
vibe_signature_feature: Nineteen worked standing stones run in a dead-straight line across the marsh. Two of them are subtly out of true. Their empty sockets lie beside them.
player_purpose_hook: The stones stand on a firm ridge under the marsh. The ridge only becomes apparent when one walks the line.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The region has 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The place is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately unrelated to its surroundings

name: The Cordon Hearth
why_founding: The Cordon Hearth is a kept fire on the southern approach. It is built against one of the cordon stones. The cordon stone was the sole marker on the road.
why_site_advantages: The Cordon Hearth stands at the midpoint of an eight-kilometre stretch of road that has no settlement along it.
why_occupants_motive: Rockspring households keep the hearth on a rota. They keep it badly in winter and well in the trading season.
why_pressures: Travellers who know the district avoid sleeping at the hearth. The plague cordon stone beside the hearth is the reason for this.
why_would_change_if: Moving the hearth two hundred metres would double its use. The Rockspring households will not move it.
vibe_palette: The palette is fire orange, cordon-stone grey and dark road.
vibe_signature_feature: The hearth house is built against a plague cordon marker. The cordon stone forms one wall of the house.
player_purpose_hook: A kept fire burns halfway along eight kilometres of empty road. The fire is built against a wall that is a plague cordon stone.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

name: The Fasting Hut
why_founding: An ascetic holds a rock ledge above the sinkhole. The ascetic says that the sound of the water going down is the point of living there.
why_site_advantages: The ledge is dry and lies above a sinkhole. A spring is within reach of the ledge. Reaching the ledge takes a deliberate approach.
why_occupants_motive: The ascetic eats the food that pilgrims bring. The ascetic answers questions and asks nothing in exchange.
why_pressures: The ascetic knows the basin's water routes better than anyone alive. The ascetic shares that information freely. The drag crew resents this deeply.
why_would_change_if: The ascetic's death would take the district's best hydrological knowledge with it.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey limestone, white water and thin smoke.
vibe_signature_feature: A ledge hut stands above a roaring sinkhole. The district's water routes are scratched into the rock face beside the door.
player_purpose_hook: The ledge is dry and lies above a sinkhole. A spring is within reach of the ledge. Reaching the ledge takes a deliberate approach.
deferred_why: The hut is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The type 'hermit-hut' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design

name: Basin Swallow
why_founding: Basin Swallow is a collapse in the marsh south of the city. An entire stream drains underground there.
why_site_advantages: Basin Swallow is a hole in the marsh south of the city. The water has not filled the hole.
why_occupants_motive: The rim is bare rock. Something lives below the first ledge.
why_pressures: Basin Swallow is almost certainly connected to the Blue Hole. To prove the link, a dyed float must come up in the lake. No crew has paid for the dye.
why_would_change_if: Proving the connection would open a route from the western hills into the lake floor.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey limestone, white falling water and a black throat.
vibe_signature_feature: A stream pours into an undercut in the wet rock under the ledge. The stream lands without a sound.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can send an outsider below the first ledge. The outsider must prove that the swallow and the Blue Hole are one system.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 440 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.flu-mass-grave (+0.29).
player_purpose_hook: A whole stream pours into this hole. The lake-divers argue about where the water emerges. Their guess is the Blue Hole.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: one of a handful of holes in the western feeder country; each one should be individually meaningful

name: The Gatehouse
why_founding: A family lives in the gatehouse of the abandoned cordon fort. The gatehouse has a roof and a door. The family has never been asked to leave.
why_site_advantages: Of the whole fort, the gatehouse is the part that is dry, defensible and small enough to heat.
why_occupants_motive: The family keeps the road. The family sells water to travellers. The family considers itself the caretakers of the fort.
why_pressures: Any faction that occupied the fort would have to deal with the family first.
why_would_change_if: A garrison would evict the family in an afternoon.
vibe_palette: The palette is lamp yellow in grey stone, painted board and road dust.
vibe_signature_feature: One lit window shows in the gatehouse of an otherwise dark fort. A water butt and a hand-painted price stand beside the road.
vibe_mood: The mood is small life in a large shell.
player_purpose_hook: Of the whole fort, the gatehouse is the part that is dry, defensible and small enough to heat.
deferred_why: The gatehouse is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The type 'squatted-ruin-home' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: inside any ruin type

name: The Standing Account
why_founding: The Standing Account is a tradehouse on the causeway road. The Rose's people and the city's people drink in the same room there. The shared room is the purpose of the tradehouse.
why_site_advantages: The tradehouse stands halfway along the road on firm ground. A landing lies behind it.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper runs a standing account for both sides. The keeper has never been robbed.
why_pressures: Everything said in the tradehouse reaches both the city and the Rose within a day.
why_would_change_if: A killing in the tradehouse would close the sole neutral room in the district.
vibe_palette: The palette is hearth glow, slate grey and worn plank.
vibe_signature_feature: The tradehouse has a long room with a hearth at each end. A slate of standing accounts hangs in the room in two columns.
player_purpose_hook: The tradehouse stands halfway along the road on firm ground. A landing lies behind it.
deferred_why: The tradehouse is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The zone holds 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The tradehouse is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

name: Blackrose
why_founding: The Lilmothiit built Blackrose in a lake where three rivers converge. The Empire rebuilt it after 1E 2837. Whoever holds the island core has held Blackrose since.
why_site_advantages: Murkwood's water comes in from the north-east. Oliis Bay's water comes in from the south. Eastern Blackwood's water comes in from the west. Bramman's concealed river runs out to Topal Bay. The lake is a wide fringe marsh with a hard island in it. The city stands on the island.
why_occupants_motive: The people of Blackrose live on toll and transit revenue. They also live on whatever comes out of the Rose. Most residents arrived on business and stayed.
why_pressures: The people of Blackrose raised an army against the Third Empire. A battlemage broke that army with one spell. They distrust magic more than they distrust outsiders.
why_would_change_if: Whoever took the island core would take the whole southern route network with it. The core has changed hands four times.
vibe_silhouette: Blackrose has a dark walled island core. A single spire of Lilmothiit footing is carried up in Imperial courses. The spire stands clear above a flat spread of boardwalk roofs. The boardwalk roofs reach to three gates on three rivers.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey lake water, dark wet stone, red-brown Argonian roofs and lamp reflections.
vibe_materials: The foundations are Lilmothiit blocks. Imperial dressed courses sit on top of them. Argonian roof and boardwalk carpentry covers both. The stone came out of the Lilmothiit city. All the timber is new.
vibe_signature_feature: A walled stone core stands on a lake island. Lilmothiit foundations lie under Imperial courses, under Argonian roofs. The rest of the city spreads over the water on boardwalks between three river gates.
vibe_condition: Blackrose has been repaired continuously for two thousand years. Fresh mortar fills old joints. New decking lies on old piles. The gate ironwork is four centuries old.
vibe_approach: The core is visible across open water from every river gate. It is lit, with its reflection under it.
vibe_senses: Gate bells sound across open water in answer to each other. Oars and toll-chains sound in the city. Wet stone and lamp oil scent the air. A flat lake sound runs under everything.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can set the city's clerks, founding houses and toll-farmers against each other. The dispute centres on a single page of the record.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR01 · tier-3; LR02 · tier-3; LR03 · tier-3; LR04 · tier-3; LR05 · tier-3; LR06 · tier-3; LR07 · tier-3; LR08 · tier-3; LR09 · tier-3; LR10 · tier-3; LR11 · tier-3; LR12 · tier-3; LR13 · tier-3; LR14 · tier-3; LR15 · tier-3; LR16 · tier-3; LR17 · tier-3; LR18 · tier-3; LR19 · tier-3; LR20 · tier-3; LR21 · tier-3; LR22 · tier-3; LR23 · tier-3; LR24 · tier-3; LR25 · tier-3; LR26 · tier-3; LR27 · tier-3; LR28 · tier-3; LR29 · tier-3; LR30 · tier-3; LR31 · tier-3; LR32 · tier-3; LR33 · tier-3; LR34 · tier-3; LR35 · tier-3; LR61 · tier-3; tier-0; LR56 · tier-3; LR57 · tier-3; LR58 · tier-3; LR59 · tier-3; LR60 · tier-3; RS04 · tier-2
why_site_won: Reseated (2026-09-20): Blackrose is an island city in the lake. The committed dot at 2123.0, 6215.0 stands on the shore, 304.0 m from the island. No other ground inside body.1284-3448 is fully enclosed: the island is 149 cells, rows 1750-1765 by columns 633-647 of the entity raster. Its centroid is 2343.0, 6424.8, dry ground 17 m from the owner-approved anchor at 2359.5, 6415.0.
player_purpose_hook: Every road and every river in the south ends at the same island. A toll is charged at Blackrose on all of it.
complexity_justification: Blackrose is a major city. It has a walled island core over Lilmothiit foundations. It has stilt and boardwalk districts spread across a lake. It has three river gates.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: lake hub; a notorious prison a day's march north
siting_prefs_preferences_density_gradien: city core; dense over water, thin on land
footprint_why: island city; spreads over the lake and onto the shore, owner 2026-09-23

name: Speaks-Below-The-Water
why_founding: Blackrose's Hist stands in the lake outside the city. The lake rose over it.
why_site_advantages: The Hist grew on the island's old shore. Three centuries of raised lake level put six metres of water over its crown.
why_occupants_motive: Tenders dive to the Hist. The city has no other Hist tree. The city has not planted a second. A second tree would be taken as a judgement on this one.
why_pressures: An underwater Hist cannot be communed with in any of the usual ways. The tenders have improvised a practice of their own. No village upriver recognises that practice.
why_would_change_if: Lowering the lake would expose the Hist. The tenders disagree about whether exposure would save it or kill it.
vibe_silhouette: A green shadow the size of a village lies six metres down. Weighted offering lines run from a small surface platform straight into the shadow.
vibe_palette: The palette is green underwater light, dark bark and silver surface.
vibe_materials: The Hist is living drowned hardwood with an intact canopy. The surface platform is lashed timber. The weighted offering lines are cord, shell and tin. Nothing is fixed to the tree.
vibe_signature_feature: A great tree stands whole and alive underwater. Its canopy is a green shadow six metres down. Weighted offering lines run from a boat platform on the surface.
vibe_condition: The tree is alive, undamaged and wholly submerged. The tenders rebuild the platform every few years.
vibe_approach: Visitors are poled out to a small platform in open water. Bare lake lies on every side. The canopy shows as a shadow under the boat.
vibe_senses: Above the water, the platform creaks and the lines run. Below, green light comes through leaves that should be in air. The root-hum carries up through the water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can put the speakers who tend the drowned Hist against the city. The city wants a landing stage on top of the Hist.
why_site_won: open water in seasonal floodplain (danger band 2), 61 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on submerged, danger, parent; bound to body.1290-3508 within 30 m; needs 3 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The city's tree is alive six metres under the lake. The tenders go down to it on weighted lines.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in Blackrose's own lake, tended from the city shore

name: Blackrose Prison
why_founding: Potentate Versidue-Shaie's battlemage Pelladil Direnni built the prison. He built it from the rubble of the Lilmothiit city. An army of stone atronachs built it in a single day. The prison is named for the city. Its stone came from that city.
why_site_advantages: The prison stands surrounded by marsh and is reached by one causeway. That is the Imperial siting rule for this province. The ground outside is quiet country. The danger lies behind the gate and below it.
why_occupants_motive: Families born in the prison for three generations hold it as their inheritance. Exiles and outlaws live there too. The families resent the word prison. They argue that the place has not been a prison for generations.
why_pressures: Umbriel left something in the lower levels. The stair has been bricked up for two generations to hold it below. The Chainbreakers want the place opened. Blackrose's toll clerks want the toll that is taken at the prison on the south road.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the lower levels would make the Rose a genuine settlement. The city's toll clerks and Third-Born Xeekh both know this.
vibe_silhouette: The prison is a blunt single-day fortress. It has flat curtain walls and flat towers. The blocks lie at whatever angle they came out of the rubble. Washing lines strung across the yard soften the walls.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey re-cut stone, ochre carving fragments, a black stairwell and domestic colour in the yard.
vibe_materials: The walls use reused Lilmothiit stone throughout. Vulpine carving survives at random angles in the courses. The gate furniture is Imperial iron. Inside the yard, three generations of domestic Argonian carpentry stand. The carpentry stands free of the walls.
vibe_signature_feature: A single-day fortress is built of reused Lilmothiit stone. The blocks still carry vulpine carving laid in at random angles. Washing lines are strung across a parade yard. A sealed stair leads to the lower levels.
vibe_condition: The fortification is unbreached and unrepaired because it needs no repair. The interior is wholly domesticated. One stairwell was bricked and mortared two generations ago.
vibe_mood: The mood is domestic, with a sealed stair in it.
vibe_approach: One causeway crosses open marsh to the prison. The causeway is watched along its whole length.
vibe_senses: Children play in a parade yard. The wall is so thick that the yard noise stops at it. Cold comes off the sealed stairwell in the corner of a warm yard. The yard smells of cooking and washing, with goats.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can force a choice between the prison-born families, the Chainbreakers and the city. The city farms the causeway toll.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ09 · tier-0; LR15 · tier-3; LR18 · tier-3; LR24 · tier-3; LR36 · tier-3; LR42 · tier-3
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 181 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Three generations have been born inside these walls. The stair in the corner of their yard has been bricked up for two of them.
complexity_justification: The prison is a fortress-prison attested in the sources. Three occupancies are stacked in it: prison-born families, outlaws and Umbriel's dead below. It has a defended approach. It is the zone's largest single authored site.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a day's march from a city that pretends it is not there

name: The Refused Vault
why_founding: The Refused Vault holds the ashes of those whom the basin's villages refused to stake. They are blasphemers and oath-breakers. Latterly they include the Rose's unclaimed dead.
why_site_advantages: The vault is cut into the limestone above the flood. It lies deliberately far from any burial ground.
why_occupants_motive: A keeper accepts the urns. The keeper cuts the refusal word into each urn.
why_pressures: The Chainbreakers argue that the prison dead were refused here for the wrong reason. The Chainbreakers want the prison dead removed.
why_would_change_if: A ruling that the prison dead may be staked would empty half the vault.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey rock, terracotta urn and lamp shadow.
vibe_signature_feature: A rock-cut vault holds stacked urns. Each urn carries a single word explaining the refusal. A growing section has the same word on every urn.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can ask what a burial ground owes to the urns that it refused.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 74 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, nearPoint, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Each urn carries the word that got it refused. Lately the same word is on all the new urns.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately outside a village's normal ground

name: The Cold Bloom
why_founding: The Cold Bloom is a bloomery working the basin's bog iron. It was abandoned when the charcoal ran out. The ore did not run out.
why_site_advantages: The bloomery stands beside the ore beds. There is water close at hand for the bellows. Woodland for charcoal once stood nearby.
why_occupants_motive: The bloomery stands empty. The furnace stack stands. The slag heap is the highest ground for two kilometres.
why_pressures: The ore is still there. The charcoal is still missing. The arithmetic has not changed.
why_would_change_if: A charcoal supply from the eastern forest would restart the bloomery tomorrow.
vibe_palette: The palette is slag black-purple, rust and reed gold.
