vibe_signature_feature: A furnace stack stands alone on a slag heap. The slag heap has become the local high point. The last bloom is still in the hearth.
player_purpose_hook: The bloomery stands beside the ore beds. There is water close at hand for the bellows. Woodland for charcoal once stood nearby.
deferred_why: The bloomery is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The type 'bog-iron-bloomery' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: near a road or a foreign settlement

name: Bramman's Head
why_founding: Bramman's Head is the inland end of the concealed Bramman river. A First-Era fleet sailed up the river from the coast. Bramman's water meets the Blackrose lakes at the head.
why_site_advantages: The head is a screened lagoon. The lagoon is deep enough for a laden hull. The bank is firm enough for transhipment.
why_occupants_motive: A small permanent crew keeps the head open. The crew charges for the last mile of the route. The route appears on no chart.
why_pressures: Blackrose's toll authority has walked within two hundred paces of the head. The toll authority followed a fisher's footpath but did not find the river mouth. The river mouth lies out in the mangrove screen.
why_would_change_if: Charting the river would make Blackrose a sea port. Charting the river would also destroy the pilots at both ends.
vibe_silhouette: The head is a blind lagoon screened by mangrove. A cut stone bank lies at the back of the lagoon. The stone bank cannot be seen from outside the screen.
vibe_palette: The palette is black water, green screen and old iron.
vibe_materials: The mooring bank is old cut stone. Its iron rings are a thousand years old. Every ring carries a fresh rope. Market tents and scaffold shears are struck between uses. No fixed building stands above the bank.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone-cut mooring bank lies in a blind lagoon. Its iron rings are a thousand years old. A fresh rope hangs on every ring.
vibe_condition: The stonework is a thousand years old and perfect. Whatever stands above the stonework can be struck in an hour.
vibe_mood: Bramman's Head is an old smuggling landing that is still worked.
vibe_approach: The approach runs through a screen of mangrove into a lagoon. The lagoon holds a working quay. The quay appears on no chart in Blackrose.
vibe_senses: Bay noise cuts off inside the screen. Rope creaks on old iron. Crews tally goods quietly. The water is black and still.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can ask why the crew of a landing all took other work in the same week.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR48 · tier-3; RS-line · tier-2; LR53 · tier-3; LR54 · tier-3; LR55 · tier-3
why_site_won: river mouth in tidal delta (danger band 2), 350 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on nearPoint, parent, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; needs 1.2 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Bramman's Head is the inland end of an uncharted river. A thousand-year-old iron ring holds each rope on the bank.
siting_note: The record's positionM is (1806.8, 6434.9). The positionM outranks the siting note. The siting note gave the earlier figure (1941, 6295) as the inland head of the Bramman channel. The region list was widened to the lake and fringe-marsh classes that the head meets. The widening follows the founding line and leaves the head on its water.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on Bramman's river where it meets the lake system, within sight of the Lake road's last stage

name: The Floating Road
why_founding: The land route to the Rose crosses four kilometres of marsh. The marsh is too soft for a stone causeway. The road is carried on lashed log piles driven into the mud.
why_site_advantages: The marsh is deep and soft with a stable water level. The water is shallow enough for piles to be driven along the whole crossing.
why_occupants_motive: Vaunting maintains the causeway, section by numbered section. Vaunting depends on the causeway for its existence.
why_pressures: The deck is narrow and cannot be defended. The causeway is the only way that the Rose is supplied.
why_would_change_if: Cutting three sections would isolate the Rose completely. Several parties have considered cutting three sections.
vibe_palette: The palette is wet dark timber, marsh olive and painted section numbers.
vibe_signature_feature: The causeway is a plank road on lashed log piles. Painted numbers mark it along its whole length. Wet-season sections stand on taller piles. Dry-season sections are left low.
vibe_approach: The whole crossing is visible from either end. Anyone crossing is visible for all of it.
player_purpose_hook: The causeway is four kilometres of plank on piles. Its sections are numbered one by one. It is the only land way into the Rose.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The province holds 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The record is tier-2 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: links two named places directly

name: The Lit Pool
why_founding: The Lit Pool is a spring-fed pool in a limestone cave. The pool's water glows year-round. The villages of the basin have used it as a light source for centuries.
why_site_advantages: A cave mouth opens in the hillside at the foot of the western hills. A permanently full clear pool lies a short way inside.
why_occupants_motive: Lamp-jelly gatherers take a fixed quantity from the pool. An agreement that predates the city sets the quantity.
why_pressures: The quotas of two villages overlap. The villages argue about the quotas every year as a ritual.
why_would_change_if: A drop in the spring would end the glow. It would also end an argument of great age.
vibe_palette: The palette is blue-green glow, wet limestone and black cave.
vibe_signature_feature: The pool lights the whole chamber blue-green from below. A stone post stands at the waterline. The post carries the quota tallies of the two villages, notched into it.
vibe_approach: The approach is a plain cave mouth in the hillside. A plank landing and a boat chain lie below the mouth. Nothing outside the mouth shows what is inside.
player_purpose_hook: A cave mouth has a plank landing. A pool inside lights the rock from below.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'bioluminescent-water' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-5. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

name: Open House
why_founding: The Blackrose Chainbreakers run the shelter. It houses people who have come out of the Rose, an Owing or a toll pit. Those people have nowhere else that will take them. The Freed Rows in the north send word but no supplies.
why_site_advantages: The shelter stands outside the toll line. It stands on water with two exits. It has no fixed sign.
why_occupants_motive: The Chainbreakers offer board, work and legal help at the shelter. This is the practical programme of the Chainbreakers in the south.
why_pressures: Two of the powers that the Chainbreakers oppose fund half their neighbours. The shelter is watched constantly.
why_would_change_if: A single violent incident here would let the city close the shelter lawfully.
vibe_silhouette: The shelter is a rambling low water-house. It has grown sideways, not up. It has more doors than windows. It carries no sign of any kind.
vibe_palette: The palette is patched timber, lamp gold and tag-bone white.
vibe_materials: The walls are mud-mother plaster and patched shack-kit over a stilt frame. Market canvas covers the yard. A wall of hung bone-tags stands in the house. Every material is second-hand.
vibe_signature_feature: The water-house has more doors than rooms. A work-board lists paid tasks. A wall holds bone-tags returned from the Rose.
vibe_condition: The house was extended again this season. A new room goes up whenever a group arrives.
vibe_approach: The shelter is reached by water from two directions. It has no sign and no landing stage. Arrivals are told which door to use.
vibe_senses: Arrivals come constantly. The tag wall clicks in the draught. The kitchen cooks for more people than are expected. Lamp oil scents the air. Names are given only by those who offer them.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can put the shelter one incident away from lawful closure. It can offer a chance to prevent or provoke that incident.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: BC03 · tier-2; LR31 · tier-3; LR61 · tier-3; PP05 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 241 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Anyone who gets inside is fed and put on the work-board. The door has to be pointed out first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: within a day of a hard owing district, out of its sight

name: The Chain Towers
why_founding: Three low towers form a chain linking the city to the Rose causeway. The towers let a signal cross the marsh in minutes.
why_site_advantages: The towers stand on the only three rises with mutual sightlines. The sightlines cross four kilometres of flat marsh.
why_occupants_motive: The toll families man the towers. They use the chain for commercial news far more often than for alarms.
why_pressures: The towers are in plain view of the Rose. The signals can be read perfectly well from the Rose.
why_would_change_if: A single lost tower breaks the chain. It also breaks the early warning of the city.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey stone, marsh olive and lamp shutter black.
vibe_signature_feature: Three squat towers stand in a line across flat marsh. Each tower is visible from the next. Each holds shuttered signal lamps and nothing else.
player_purpose_hook: The towers stand on the only three rises with mutual sightlines. The sightlines cross four kilometres of flat marsh.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The province holds 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The record is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower

name: The Reading Ledge
why_founding: The Reading Ledge is a cliff bench on the western hills. The entire lake is visible from it. All three river mouths and the causeway of the Rose are visible at once.
why_site_advantages: It is the only ground above the basin with a clear line over the whole basin.
why_occupants_motive: The signal watch of the city uses the ledge. The toll families use the ledge. Everyone planning anything uses the ledge.
why_pressures: Whoever holds the ledge sees every movement in the basin. They see it a full hour before the city does.
why_would_change_if: Nothing changes the value of the ledge. The ledge has been fought over twice.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey rock, silver lake and green marsh.
vibe_signature_feature: A rock bench lies above the whole basin. A wind-shelter of piled stone stands on it. A scratched diagram of the three river mouths covers the back wall.
player_purpose_hook: It is the only ground above the basin with a clear line over the whole basin.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'vista-ledge' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: placed where the visibility raster shows a dead zone

name: Cordon Two, Under-Stores
why_founding: Every cordon post on the Flu line had a ration store cut into the bank behind it. The stores outlived the posts by about nine centuries. The cellars stay dry.
why_site_advantages: The cellars are dry and vaulted, in a levee bank. They lie above every recorded flood. They lie on a line of stones that the council has not voted to lift.
why_occupants_motive: The collectors of the Owing keep distrained goods here between the taking and the auction. The stores were built for that. The law does not allow it.
why_pressures: Each lot in the cellars belongs to an owner who is still alive.
why_would_change_if: Opening the cellars to their owners would break the whole practice of the Owing in the south.
vibe_silhouette: A brick arch stands in a grass bank. A cart track is worn to the arch. The bank is bare for a kilometre in either direction.
vibe_palette: The palette is bank green, brick red and cellar dark.
vibe_materials: The cellar has imperial brick vaulting cut into the levee. The original store racking is still in place. A new door of new timber hangs in nine-century brick.
vibe_signature_feature: A cordon ration cellar is still racked to the plan of the Empire. It is filled with the furniture of other people. Each lot is tagged and dated.
vibe_condition: The cellar is structurally perfect. Three different authorities use it continuously for the same purpose.
vibe_approach: A cart track leaves the cordon line at right angles.
vibe_senses: Cold dry air comes out of the arch. A collector reads a tally aloud. Furniture is stacked in a place built for grain.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can set two lawful claims against each other. The claims concern racked goods whose owners are mostly dead.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR04 · tier-3; LR40 · tier-3; PP05 · tier-3; BC-line · tier-2
why_site_won: Reseated (2026-09-23): Moved outside the Blackrose disc after the 2026-09-20 island reseat: the dot sat 2566.9, 6388.9, less than 275 m from the new centre, the city disc plus its own footprint; the nearest standable ground within 60 degrees of its bearing from the new centre is 2712.0, 6443.4 (369.5 m from the centre, 155.0 m move).
player_purpose_hook: The Owing distrains goods from the lake villages to Blackrose. The goods are racked in the cellars, tagged and dated. The people of Never-Sold have spent a year trying to read the tags.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the marked cordon line, within a kilometre of a cordon stone

name: The Long Sleep
why_founding: The Long Sleep is a daril house in a city. The city has a large transient population of people recently released from somewhere.
why_site_advantages: The den stands on the water's edge under a boardwalk. It is entered from below at low water.
why_occupants_motive: Daril from the eastern marsh is sold by the hour at the den. Customers are not asked where they have been.
why_pressures: The withdrawal house draws its custom from the den. The two houses have an arrangement that is never described.
why_would_change_if: A supply interruption from the fermentary would empty the den in a week.
vibe_palette: The palette is green underlight, hammock canvas and smoke.
vibe_signature_feature: The den is a low room under a boardwalk. Hammocks hang in three tiers. A water-level door opens only at half tide.
player_purpose_hook: The den stands on the water's edge under a boardwalk. It is entered from below at low water.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'vice-den' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-5. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

name: Yeller's Holding
why_founding: Yeller's Holding is an estate whose owning family died out in the rebellion. Its tenants, the city and a claimant from Cyrodiil have all claimed it since.
why_site_advantages: The ground is good and drained, on the western feeder. It has a landing and a mill.
why_occupants_motive: The tenants farm the estate. They pay rent into an escrow held by the arbiter.
why_pressures: The escrow is now a substantial sum. At least two parties want the case settled for that reason alone.
why_would_change_if: A ruling in any direction would end a hundred-year arrangement. The arrangement currently works.
vibe_palette: The palette is shuttered grey house, working green fields and mill white.
vibe_signature_feature: The great house is sealed and shuttered. A fully working farm surrounds it. A rent chest stands in the parlour of the arbiter eight kilometres away.
player_purpose_hook: The ground is good and drained, on the western feeder. It has a landing and a mill.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'estate-village' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: holds the crossing its neighbours must use

name: Bare Lake
why_founding: The shallow north-eastern arm of the lake empties for six weeks every dry season. The emptied arm exposes a wide lake bed. The bed lies a metre under water for the rest of the year.
why_site_advantages: The site is a wide flat arm of the lake that is barely a metre deep. The outlet of the arm drops below its sill in the dry season.
why_occupants_motive: Longmont and Rockspring both use the drawdown, which is a local event. The shore villages walk out onto the bed while the water is low. They take whatever the year has dropped there.
why_pressures: The driven poles of a drowned burial ground stand out of the bed during the drawdown. Villagers argue every year about what may be taken from the bed.
why_would_change_if: A wetter cycle would end the drawdown. The annual custom of walking the bed would end with it.
vibe_silhouette: For six weeks a year the lake bed is a cracked grey plain. Drowned fence lines and bleached poles stand out of the plain. For the rest of the year the place is four square kilometres of open water.
vibe_palette: The palette is cracked grey mud, bleached pole and bright sky.
vibe_materials: The lake bed is cracked clay. Drowned fence timber lies on the bed. Lost cargo lies among the timber. Rows of bleached driven poles stand over the old graves. Market stalls are pitched on the bed itself for six weeks.
vibe_signature_feature: Half the district walks the cracked lake bed. Drowned fence lines, lost cargo and rows of driven burial poles emerge for six weeks a year.
vibe_condition: The place exists for six weeks a year. The refill takes back whatever the drawdown exposed.
vibe_mood: The mood is that of a market festival held over a burial ground.
vibe_approach: During the drawdown, travellers reach the bed on foot from the shore villages. For the rest of the year, they reach it by boat.
vibe_senses: The feet of a whole district cross the dry lake bed. Stalls stand on the bed. The air smells of a lake bottom in the sun. A hush falls wherever the poles stand.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can use the six-week drawdown as a deadline. The refill takes back whatever the bed exposed.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 313 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, nearPoint, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: For six weeks a year, traders hold a market on the lake bed. For the rest of the year the bed is a dive site.
siting_note: The site was moved 150 m west onto zone ground. The old position read mercantile-coast on the culture raster. The arm lies north-east of the city and not south of it.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: the lake's north-eastern arm, walked from Longmont and the city

name: The Drowned Gallery
why_founding: The Empire tried to drain the approach to the Rose with a gallery driven under the levee. Gangs small enough to fit the gallery worked it. The lake came in through the face of the gallery. The gallery has been full of water since that day.
why_site_advantages: The gallery lies under the levee, below the water table. Its head shaft is still open in the lake bed.
why_occupants_motive: The gallery holds no breathing creature. The lake-divers know the shaft. They work the wrecks and leave the gallery alone.
why_pressures: The gallery runs toward the foundations of the Rose. The necromancers who dig from the landward side know of it.
why_would_change_if: Pumping the gallery out would give three separate parties a dry way under the prison.
vibe_silhouette: A square timbered shaft mouth opens in a flat lake bed. The shoring is still square. The shaft goes straight down into the dark.
vibe_palette: The palette is silt brown at the mouth, black below and pale timber.
vibe_materials: The gallery shoring is Imperial waterlogged hardwood in perfect preservation. Rail and barrow iron lie on the floor. The floor has had no plank laid on it since the lake came through the face.
vibe_signature_feature: The drowned Imperial drainage gallery keeps its shoring square. Its barrows are still on the rail. The face stands where the lake came through it.
vibe_condition: The water that flooded the gallery preserved it. Every timber is sound. Every tool lies where it was dropped.
vibe_approach: The gallery is a square hole in an otherwise featureless lake bed. Divers find it from a diver's chart or not at all.
vibe_senses: The water is cold and has no current. Silt hangs where it is disturbed. The timber looks new by lamp. The gallery runs further than a single breath-hold allows.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can hire an outsider to dive where the divers of Longmont refuse to go. The fate of the last diver hired is part of the quest.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 349 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A drowned Imperial gallery runs under the levee toward the foundations of the Rose. Barrows are still on the rail.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: between the lake shore and the prison, touching neither

name: The Windlass Reckoning
why_founding: The western feeder has a sill of rock and old log-jam two hundred metres long. A laden hull cannot pass the sill. Crews drag hulls around it.
why_site_advantages: A low saddle beside the narrows lets crews lay a greased timber slipway on a workable gradient.
why_occupants_motive: A drag crew with a windlass works the slipway and is paid by the hull. The crew also controls who goes upstream and when.
why_pressures: The crew holds a total monopoly. The crew does minimal maintenance on the slipway.
why_would_change_if: Cutting the sill would open the western route. Cutting the sill would also end the crew.
vibe_silhouette: A greased timber ramp is cut over a low saddle. A windlass frame stands at the crest. Hull-shapes queue out of sight at both ends.
vibe_palette: The palette is grease black, pale timber and white water below.
vibe_materials: Greased hardwood skids lie on a laid stone bed. The hand-windlass is oak and iron. Scaffold shear-legs and roller stock stand at the slipway.
vibe_signature_feature: A greased timber slipway crosses the saddle. A hand-windlass stands at the top. A queue of hulls waits at both ends.
vibe_condition: The slipway is heavily worked and constantly re-greased. Crews replace the skids twice a year. The stone bed is Imperial work and is untouched.
vibe_approach: The whitewater and the windlass are audible together. The length of the queue sets the length of the wait.
vibe_senses: Hulls drag on grease. The windlass pawl clicks. Whitewater sounds below, out of sight. The air smells of tallow and hot timber. Crews wait for their turn.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tally of the windlass crew counts loads that the books of The Water Reckoning omit.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 165 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.wisp-lure-basin (+0.86).
player_purpose_hook: A greased slipway and a hand-windlass stand here. A crew works them and sets the order of the queue.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a mandatory node on a boat lane

name: The Stair Rapids
why_founding: The western feeder drops through a limestone stair of six ledges. The stair is the reason the portage exists.
why_site_advantages: The site is a confined rock reach. It has six clean drops in three hundred metres.
why_occupants_motive: The rapids have no residents. Drag-crew apprentices run them empty as a rite. The run occasionally kills an apprentice.
why_pressures: The rapids mark the boundary between the economy of the basin and the economy of eastern Blackwood. The boundary is fixed and cannot be negotiated.
why_would_change_if: Cutting one ledge would let empty hulls run the rapids. That change would halve the portage trade.
vibe_palette: The palette is white water, grey limestone and green overhead.
vibe_signature_feature: Six clean limestone drops stand in a row. A worn path runs beside them. A name is cut beside each drop.
player_purpose_hook: The site is a confined rock reach. It has six clean drops in three hundred metres.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The rebalance holds 70 records against a budget of 17-21. The record is a tier-4 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: forces every boat route to stop; a portage or a ferry always answers it

name: The Counting Ground
why_founding: Blackrose buried the Knahaten dead of three peoples here. It buried them in the order in which they died. It made no distinction between the peoples.
why_site_advantages: The site is a gravel terrace above the flood. The terrace is dry enough to take that many graves at once.
why_occupants_motive: Argonian grave-singers keep a memorial rota here. Grave-Singer Ossu is among them.
why_pressures: Two of the three peoples buried here are extinct. The Argonian villages keep the memorial rota.
why_would_change_if: Separating the burials by people is impossible. The villages would refuse to attempt it.
vibe_palette: The palette is gravel grey, two pale stakes and wide sky.
vibe_signature_feature: A single continuous grave trench runs four hundred metres. One stake stands at each end. Bare gravel lies between the stakes.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can make the city account for the tally stones in public.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR07 · tier-3; LR26 · tier-3; LR32 · tier-3; PP18 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 44 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.basin-sinkhole (+0.29).
player_purpose_hook: Three peoples lie buried in the order in which they died. They lie in one trench four hundred metres long. A stake stands at each end of the trench.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

name: Holding Fields, Cordon Three
why_founding: Lilmothiit refugees fled the Knahaten Flu in Murkmire. They went inland toward Blackrose. The records give no account of what became of them. Blackrose stopped them at this place.
why_site_advantages: The site is on the Lake road north of the city. It lies at the last narrows before the water. A cordon can be held there.
why_occupants_motive: The place has been empty since the Flu year. It was a village-sized pen with a fence, a gate and a ration store. It also had a burial ground larger than the village.
why_pressures: The fate of the Lilmothiit refugees is recorded here and in no other place. Blackrose has kept it out of its own accounts.
why_would_change_if: Published ration ledgers would make the founding families of the city answer for it.
vibe_silhouette: A rectangular fence enclosure stands here. A burial ground four times its size lies beyond it.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey weathered fence, sour green ground and white bone.
vibe_materials: The fence is weathered grey timber. The gate furniture is on the outside of the fence. A ration store is built into the wall. Mud-mother houses stand inside. The graves carry no stakes.
vibe_signature_feature: A fenced village-sized enclosure stands here. The gate furniture is on the outside of the fence. A ration store is built into the wall. The burial ground is four times the size of the enclosure.
vibe_condition: The fence has weathered for sixteen centuries and still stands. The fence is falling on its own. The villages within a day of it leave it standing.
vibe_approach: The fence line is visible from the road. The gate furniture is on its outer side.
vibe_senses: Birds are silent inside the fence. Wind moves through the palings. The ground smells sour. The burial field is bare of carving throughout.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can put the ration ledgers of the cordon into outside hands. Several parties want the ledgers left unread.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The ration ledgers are still in the store. The histories of Blackrose omit the cordon.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Lake road out of Blackrose, deliberately just out of reach of its neighbours

name: The Singing Ponds
why_founding: A farm breeds frogs selected for their call and not for their meat. The chime-and-instrument trade of the province pays better than the food trade.
why_site_advantages: The site is a terrace of warm shallow ponds fed by a spring seep. Each pond is tuned to a different stock.
why_occupants_motive: Tone-selected stock takes six generations to fix. It sells at a high price to instrument villages.
why_pressures: A wild frog that gets into the ponds ruins a lineage. A lineage cannot be rebuilt within one lifetime.
why_would_change_if: A flood that connected the ponds to the lake would end the whole programme in a night.
vibe_palette: The palette is green pond, pale wall and dusk violet.
vibe_signature_feature: Six walled ponds stand in a row. Each pond sounds a different pitch at dusk. A listening bench stands between them.
player_purpose_hook: The site is a terrace of warm shallow ponds fed by a spring seep. Each pond is tuned to a different stock.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The rebalance holds 70 records against a budget of 17-21. The record is a tier-3 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: supplies a named artisan village

name: The Gar Pens
why_founding: Keepers pen gar on the lake edge. They keep the gar for meat, hide and channel-clearing hire.
why_site_advantages: The site is a gateable inlet with reliable flow-through. A hard bank gives the keepers firm footing for their work.
why_occupants_motive: The hire trade is the profitable part. The city pays to have its channels cleared before the trading season.
why_pressures: The pens lie two hundred metres from the water row.
why_would_change_if: A single escape into the market would end the trade permanently.
vibe_palette: The palette is dark water, gantry timber and silver flank.
vibe_signature_feature: A gated inlet has feeding gantries. A hire board lists channels by name and price.
player_purpose_hook: The site is a gateable inlet with reliable flow-through. A hard bank gives the keepers firm footing for their work.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The rebalance holds 70 records against a budget of 17-21. The record is a tier-4 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: attached to a village or a city canal system

name: Cassia's Ground
why_founding: An Imperial grant lies on the western firm lowland. The same family has farmed it continuously since before the rebellion.
why_site_advantages: The site is the best drained firm ground in the basin. It lies above the flood and beside the road.
why_occupants_motive: The family has survived by being useful to whoever holds the city. The family has not taken a side.
why_pressures: The neutrality of the family is two centuries old. Their neighbours regard it as cowardice.
why_would_change_if: A forced choice in any future dispute would break the arrangement that has kept the family there.
vibe_palette: The palette is lime render, red tile and green field.
vibe_signature_feature: A Nibenese farmhouse stands in perfect repair. An Argonian stilt granary stands beside it. Both are maintained to the same standard.
player_purpose_hook: The site is the best drained firm ground in the basin. It lies above the flood and beside the road.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The rebalance holds 70 records against a budget of 17-21. The record is a tier-4 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: strung along a road at Imperial spacing, not local spacing

name: The Last Survey
why_founding: An Imperial survey camp surveyed a canal. The canal would have joined the lake to Oliis Bay. The Empire abandoned the camp mid-season when the province was lost.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the saddle that the canal would have crossed. The saddle is still the only viable line.
why_occupants_motive: The camp has no residents. The surveyors carried the instruments away. They left the pegs and the levelling book.
why_pressures: The book proves the canal was feasible. That is a politically significant fact in a basin that lives on portage tolls.
why_would_change_if: Producing the book to a party with money would threaten the drag crew, the toll families and Vaunting.
vibe_palette: The palette is weathered peg white, grass and rust tin.
vibe_signature_feature: A line of surveyor's pegs runs four kilometres over a saddle. A rotted camp stands at its midpoint. A levelling book lies in a tin box.
player_purpose_hook: The camp stands on the saddle that the canal would have crossed. The saddle is still the only viable line.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The rebalance holds 70 records against a budget of 17-21. The record is a tier-4 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: chained along a planned route

name: Fort Cordon
why_founding: Fort Cordon was built to hold the central narrows of the Flu cordon. Long after the cordon, the Empire kept the fort in commission. The Empire left the fort intact when it withdrew.
why_site_advantages: Fort Cordon commands the narrows. It also commands the road, where the narrows and the road run together.
why_occupants_motive: Fort Cordon stands empty and roofed. Whoever is strongest on the road occupies it from time to time.
why_pressures: Fort Cordon is the best building in the basin outside the city. No faction has held it for more than a season.
why_would_change_if: Permanent occupation of Fort Cordon by one faction would give that faction the Lake road.
vibe_palette: The palette is lime render, rust and cold hearth black.
vibe_signature_feature: Fort Cordon is a small Imperial fort. It is still roofed, but its gate is missing. The courtyard holds fire scars from three different parties.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can commission a clearance of Fort Cordon. The city's patrols avoid the fort and say little about it.
why_site_won: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 280 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.feeder-portage (+2.00).
player_purpose_hook: The Empire left the armoury in place at Fort Cordon. This season the fort is held by the strongest band of travellers on the road.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a dead road

name: Ash-Hand
why_founding: Ash-Hand was a Kothringi village on the Blackrose river terrace. The Knahaten Flu emptied the village in a single season.
why_site_advantages: Ash-Hand stands on a river terrace with a landing. The ground is good. Rockspring's families refuse to put a house on it.
why_occupants_motive: Ash-Hand is unoccupied. The Argonian villages nearby keep its boundary marked.
why_pressures: Half the province's demography dates from the Flu. Ash-Hand is one of the villages that the Flu emptied.
why_would_change_if: Proof that the ground is safe would bring a village back to Ash-Hand.
vibe_silhouette: Ash-Hand is a terrace of low plastered shells above the landing. The walls stand to head height and the roofs are gone. All the doorways face away from the river.
vibe_palette: The palette is pale plaster, black doorway and bright river.
vibe_materials: The houses are lime plaster over rubble. They stand on older dressed footings that the villagers reused. The storage pits still have lids. Silver offering-wire is wound round every lintel.
vibe_signature_feature: The houses are roofless and plastered. Silver wire is still wound round the lintels. The flu-year's stores lie lidded in the pits under the houses.
vibe_condition: Ash-Hand is preserved because the Argonian villages and Rockspring's families avoid touching it. The walls stand to head height and the roofs are gone. The flu-year's stores lie untouched in the pits.
vibe_approach: Ash-Hand has the best landing on this stretch of river. An unused ruin stands above the landing.
vibe_senses: The river is bright and loud below the ruins. The ruins are silent and smell of plaster dust. The storage pits still smell of grain.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can establish whose bones the town has been crushing for road metal.
why_site_won: headland in firm lowland (danger band 4), 431 m from the nearest route; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The flu-year's grain is still lidded in the pits under the houses.
siting_note: Ash-Hand was moved into the empty marsh quarter north-west of the lake. It lies 352 m from any route, in danger band 4. Four other fights stood within 250 m of it on the western feeder. The siting of a Flu-emptied Kothringi town calls for empty ground around it.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in the west and centre, where the Kothringi lived

name: Spine
why_founding: Spine is a village built as one continuous boardwalk from the shore into the lake. Households extended it a house at a time for three centuries.
why_site_advantages: A shallow shelf runs eight hundred metres out from the shore before it drops.
why_occupants_motive: Position along the spine marks seniority. The oldest households live at the shore end. The newest households live over deep water.
why_pressures: The far end of Spine now stands over the drop. Each new house costs more and is less safe than the last.
why_would_change_if: A storm surge would take the outer third of Spine. The loss would reset the whole social order of the village.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey deck, bright new timber at the end and dark water beneath.
vibe_signature_feature: One boardwalk runs straight out into the lake. Houses stand down both sides. The houses get newer, poorer and more precarious toward the far end.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can compare what the polers of Spine carry by day with what they carry unlit at night.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR53 · tier-3; LR54 · tier-3; LR55 · tier-3
player_purpose_hook: Households at the shore end of Spine are the oldest. The outer houses are the newest and the poorest.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: often the only dry route through its stretch

name: The Barge Yard
why_founding: Three centuries of laden barges have sunk in this lake, mostly in the same two places. The boat families of Longmont worked those wrecks first and built the yard.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands on the shore nearest the deep hole where the wrecks concentrate. It has a crane frame and a drying floor.
why_occupants_motive: Crews dive for cargo, not hulls. The toll families buy the recovered goods at a discount that they set themselves.
why_pressures: Some of the sunk cargo was insured and some was smuggled. The paperwork for both is still in the city.
why_would_change_if: A rise in the lake would put the wrecks out of free-diving range entirely.
vibe_palette: The palette is black waterlogged timber, lake grey and chart ochre.
vibe_signature_feature: The yard has a drying floor of lake-blackened trade goods. A crane frame stands over the water. A chart of sinkings is painted on the shed wall.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can start with a finished hull gone from the yard. Its papers are still on the bench.
why_site_won: saddle in firm lowland (danger band 1), 82 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, submerged, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; bound to body.1290-3508 within 150 m; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The crews who work the wrecks painted a chart of every sinking in the lake on the shed wall.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: always paired with drowned ground it works

name: Under-Longmont
why_founding: Under-Longmont is the village that Longmont replaced. The lake level rose across the fourteenth century of the Third Era. The households rebuilt the old settlement a kilometre up the shore.
why_site_advantages: Under-Longmont stands complete in five to eight metres of clear cold lake water. The households walked a kilometre up the shore and left the roofs in place.
why_occupants_motive: Under-Longmont has no living occupant. The households of Longmont still know which house down there was theirs.
why_pressures: Diving on a family's own drowned house is acceptable. Diving on another family's drowned house is not acceptable. The Longmont households enforce the rule.
why_would_change_if: A drop in lake level would expose Under-Longmont. The exposure would force a decision about who owns what.
vibe_palette: The palette is clear green water, silt-grey timber and pale driven poles.
vibe_signature_feature: A complete village stands upright underwater with its roofs intact. Its street is legible. The driven poles of the burial ground stand in rows at the end of the street.
vibe_approach: On a still day, roof-ridges show as dark lines under the surface from a boat.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can send a dive after a document that the living village needs from the drowned one.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MR09 · tier-2; LR34 · tier-3; LR56 · tier-3
player_purpose_hook: The households of Longmont still name their own drowned houses. Diving on a neighbour's house is not allowed.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: below a living settlement, or beside one that watched it go

name: The North Stage
why_founding: The lake is too wide to walk round on the Murkwood side. The city licensed a stage on the east shore. The city put its boats on the Lilmoth lane.
why_site_advantages: The stage has a firm shelving shore on the lane that the Lilmoth boats already run. The ground has standing for a stone slip.
why_occupants_motive: The North Stage is a city concession. Its boats leave on schedule.
why_pressures: The stage carries the Murkwood-side traffic. The board of the concession does not itemise that traffic.
why_would_change_if: A crossing further north would bypass the count of the city entirely.
vibe_palette: The palette is stone slip grey, sail brown and open lake.
vibe_signature_feature: A sail-and-pole ferry runs between two stages. Each end has a proper stone slip. The passenger board lists cargo types, not names.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can ask who decided that a scheduled crossing should stop counting a certain kind of cargo.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR06 · tier-3; LR57 · tier-3; PP01 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 179 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, nearPoint; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The scheduled crossing has a stone slip at each end. It replaces a day's walk round the shore.
siting_note: The North Stage is bound to the Blackrose-Lilmoth boat lane. The record cut the claims that the north road ended here and that a nine-hundred-metre narrows lies here. Neither claim holds on the ground, so the stage stays.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a station on the Blackrose–Lilmoth boat lane; has a paired stage

name: The Cluster
why_founding: Households who wanted no landlord and no toll built rafts and lashed them together. They moored the cluster in the middle of the lake.
why_site_advantages: The cluster floats in deep still water with good anchorage. No shoreline claim is attached to that water.
why_occupants_motive: The lake bottom has no owner. The whole legal position of the cluster is that it does not touch anything.
why_pressures: The city has argued for two generations about whether a lashed raft is a building.
why_would_change_if: A ruling that the cluster is a building would make it taxable and probably demolishable.
vibe_palette: The palette is weathered raft timber, garden green and open water.
vibe_signature_feature: Thirty rafts are lashed into an irregular floating block. Gardens grow on the outer rafts. A common fire raft sits at the centre.
player_purpose_hook: The cluster floats in deep still water with good anchorage. No shoreline claim is attached to that water.
deferred_why: The Cluster is deferred in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'raft-village' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 2-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: has two or three fixed moorings keyed to the flood cycle

name: The Water Row
why_founding: The Water Row is a market held on the water. Blackrose has almost no level dry ground where a market can be held.
why_site_advantages: The Water Row lies in a sheltered arm of the lake. Boats can raft up ten deep there without fouling the channel.
why_occupants_motive: Sellers moor and buyers pole between them. The shape of the market changes every day and its position never does.
why_pressures: The city cannot tax what it cannot count. The city has tried to count the Water Row for eighty years.
why_would_change_if: A fixed stall row on land would be taxable, so none is ever built there.
vibe_palette: The palette is hull colour, produce green and grey lake.
vibe_signature_feature: Two hundred boats are rafted into rows on open water. A poled aisle runs between the rows. A bell starts and ends the trading.
player_purpose_hook: The Water Row lies in a sheltered arm of the lake. Boats can raft up ten deep there without fouling the channel.
deferred_why: The Water Row is deferred in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The rebalance holds 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The Water Row is a tier-3 density fill on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement

name: Lake Meer
why_founding: Lake Meer is a xanmeer that stood on the old floor of the lake before the water rose. It is now entirely submerged and entirely intact.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer lies 3.6 metres down in cold clear water. Its terraces step up toward the surface.
why_occupants_motive: Fish live in the xanmeer. Silt seals its doorways at the base. The doorways stay open at the third terrace.
why_pressures: Lake Meer is the deepest reachable structure in the south. The divers who work it treat it as a different profession from lake salvage.
why_would_change_if: A silt slump would close the open terrace and seal the xanmeer entirely.
vibe_silhouette: From a boat, a dark mass resolves into a stepped pyramid. Its base is lost in silt.
vibe_palette: The palette is deep green-blue, pale stone and silver fish.
vibe_materials: The xanmeer is xanmeer stone throughout. Current scours the upper terraces clean. Silt covers the lower terraces. Nothing has been added to it.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone pyramid stands whole on the lake floor. Silt buries its lower terraces and the upper terraces are clean. Fish hold station in every doorway.
vibe_condition: The xanmeer is whole and unlooted. The cold water has kept it so.
vibe_approach: A dark mass under the boat resolves into steps on the descent.
vibe_senses: The water is cold and clear. The diver feels the pressure change on the descent. Fish hold station in the doorways. No silt shows until the lower terraces.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can tie the lights of the xanmeer to something happening on the surface. Longmont blames that event on the weather.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 283 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, culture-clump; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The divers who work the sunk xanmeer count it a different trade from lake salvage. No stone has been taken off the xanmeer.
siting_note: Lake Meer lies in the western arm of the lake. The culture raster reads that arm as mercantile-coast hinterland. The xanmeer predates both cultures, so it stays on its own water. It is not moved inland.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in drowned country; often near a drowned village

name: The Book House
why_founding: The Blackguards' heirs of the Blackrose region run their business as a counting house. They inherited the Rose's ledger.
why_site_advantages: The Book House is an unremarkable water-house on a settled back channel. It has three exits. It has a clear view of the toll quay. The ground is safe and the Blackguards guard the house.
why_occupants_motive: The Blackguards broker debt and cargo. They buy silence. Their accounts are better than those of the city.
why_pressures: Their ledger is the most complete record of who owes what in the south. The city, the toll families and Never-Sold each want it for a different reason.
why_would_change_if: Losing the ledger would end the Blackguards. They keep 3 copies and let the city know it.
vibe_palette: The palette is ledger cream, lamp brown and black channel.
vibe_signature_feature: The Book House stands on a back channel. Its front room is a working counting office with proper books.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can make the ledger itself the prize. Three copies exist and there are 3 buyers for them.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'eviction-repair'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The front room is a working counting office. The Blackguards settle debts in the back room.
siting_note: The Book House stands on the western edge of the lake. The culture raster reads that edge as mercantile-coast. A book-keeping smuggler crew belongs on the seam between the water of the city and the water of the coast. The region list was widened to include the standing water beneath the house.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: answers to a reoccupied prison

name: Robbed City
why_founding: The Lilmothiit city lies under Blackrose. Blackrose was quarried out of that city. The Rose was built from the city's rubble in a single day.
why_site_advantages: The stone of a vanished city lies within a day of Blackrose. Blackrose needed that stone for building.
why_occupants_motive: The Lilmothiit left no inheritors because they died of the Knahaten Flu. Blackrose's own foundations are the remains of the Lilmothiit city.
why_pressures: Only a robbed-out ground plan is left of the city. Every carved block in Blackrose's district can be matched to a socket here.
why_would_change_if: A systematic survey could reconstruct the Lilmothiit city. The survey would work from the Blackrose buildings that hold its stolen blocks.
vibe_silhouette: The city is reduced to footings, robbing trenches and square sockets. They stretch to the horizon. One colonnade still stands because its blocks were too big for the sledges.
vibe_palette: The palette is pale foundation stone, black robbing trench and green lake edge.
vibe_materials: The foundations are pale dressed stone that was left in place. Black robbing trenches mark where the courses above were lifted. One unrobbed colonnade has blocks too large to move. Surviving carving is on the faces that were laid downward. The carving is vulpine throughout.
vibe_signature_feature: The city is reduced to its footings and robbing trenches. The sockets of lifted blocks are still square. The quarry gangs left one colonnade standing.
vibe_condition: The city was dismantled in a single campaign and has not been touched since. The robbing trenches are as sharp as when they were dug.
vibe_approach: The pattern in the grass reads as streets only after several minutes of walking over it.
vibe_senses: The ground rings differently underfoot where the footings run. Lake wind comes across the site unbroken. No stone stands above knee height.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can match robbed blocks back to their sockets. The matches put half of Blackrose's district frontages in question.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 88 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on nearPoint, region, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Any carved block in Blackrose's district can be traced to the socket here from which it was lifted.
siting_note: The record was moved 500 m north into the empty quarter. An earlier siting stood 330 m off any route. The plot is now 88.4 m from the nearest route. The robbed substratum was one of five fights in a 250 m radius. A picked-over lost city should not be a roadside stop.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: beneath and beside Blackrose itself

name: The Meer Camp
why_founding: A crew works the submerged xanmeer from a shore camp. The crew is in its third season and is running out of money.
why_site_advantages: The camp is on the nearest shore to the Lake Meer. The crew has a boat, a drying rack and a line of sight to its moored buoy.
why_occupants_motive: The crew dives deeper each season. The crew has started arguing about the depth in public.
why_pressures: A rival crew has moored a second buoy fifty metres from the first crew's buoy.
why_would_change_if: A serious find would turn the camp into a village. A death would end the camp.
vibe_palette: The palette is canvas, wet stone grey and lake blue.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp has a drying rack of recovered stone fragments. The camp has two boats. Two buoys float on the water. The crews do not discuss them.
player_purpose_hook: The camp is on the nearest shore to the Lake Meer. The crew has a boat, a drying rack and a line of sight to its moored buoy.
deferred_why: The camp is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'treasure-hunters-camp' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: beside a notable ruin or hard-to-reach landform

name: Longmont
why_founding: Longmont is a shore village on the approach to Blackrose, north-west of the city. It is the last stop before the city's toll gates.
why_site_advantages: Longmont stands on a long shallow flat on the lake shore. Boats can pole across the flat all year. The flat lies outside the city's wall line.
why_occupants_motive: Longmont's people break freight bound for Blackrose by land to boats. They are not the city and charge less than it.
why_pressures: Blackrose has twice tried to bring Longmont inside its toll regime. Both times the village stopped handling freight.
why_would_change_if: Absorption into the city's toll regime would move the whole trade to Rockspring in one season.
vibe_silhouette: The village is one horizontal line a kilometre long. The line is the same height from end to end. A continuous loading deck runs under it. No vertical accent breaks it.
vibe_palette: The palette is pale stilt timber, silver flat and red-brown thatch.
vibe_materials: The village uses pale stilt timber, cane decking and reed thatch. Argonian lamps stand at fixed intervals. The same kit repeats from end to end.
vibe_signature_feature: Longmont is a single village street a kilometre long on stilts over a shallow flat. A loading deck runs its entire length.
vibe_condition: The village is uniformly maintained. The deck is replaced in sections on a rota. The rota shows in the timber colour.
vibe_approach: From the lake the village reads as a single unbroken line on the water. It takes ten minutes to pole along its length.
vibe_senses: Sound travels the length of the street and arrives late. The village sounds of poling, freight and a bell relayed door to door. Wet timber and lake weed scent the air.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can set Longmont against the ferry concession. The crossing in dispute is one that the village is not allowed to run.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR56 · tier-3; LR57 · tier-3; LR58 · tier-3
player_purpose_hook: A kilometre of stilt village breaks land freight to boats for less than the city charges.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: Blackrose's north-western neighbour on the same lake, not the coast

name: The Water Reckoning
why_founding: The Water Reckoning is a tower where the marsh drains toward the lake system. It stands on the water by Blackrose. The tower was put there to count hulls.
why_site_advantages: The tower stands on a rock spur. The water passes 11 m from it.
why_occupants_motive: The tower has two counters and a boom. The boom has not been lowered in thirty years. The Reckoning maintains the boom anyway.
why_pressures: Traffic off the western feeders is the hardest to count. That traffic is also the most valuable.
why_would_change_if: Lowering the boom would be an act of policy. Upstream would answer that act.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey tower, black chain and green river.
vibe_signature_feature: A chain boom lies slack across a river beside the tower. Its winch is greased and its links are free of rust.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can work the difference between what the Reckoning counts and what passes it.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LR02 · tier-3; LR08 · tier-3; LR54 · tier-3; Reed track · tier-2; LR45 · tier-3; LR59 · tier-3; LR60 · tier-3; RS04 · tier-3
why_site_won: Reseated (2026-09-23): Gate guard at the causeway's shore end on the Soulrest road (the Blackrose city pass in the place loop refines it): the first dry ground on route.road.soulrest-blackrose past 45 m from the Blackrose centre that clears the drowned Hist's footprint is 2267.4, 6377.9.
player_purpose_hook: A chain boom lies slack across the channel. It is greased and free of rust.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: one of a chain; must see a neighbour or it is not a watch

name: The Trodden Ground
why_founding: The Trodden Ground is a marsh giant's range on the marsh north of the city. Paths mark the range. People have walked the paths for two centuries.
why_site_advantages: The site is a wide shallow marsh with reed stands. It holds no human settlement. It lies on the Murkwood side of the lake.
why_occupants_motive: The marsh giant is the sole occupant. One giant has walked the same circuit for two centuries.
why_pressures: The paths are the fastest route toward the Murkwood verge. Guides use the paths anyway.
why_would_change_if: Little will move the giant. It has walked this circuit longer than the city has stood.
vibe_palette: Reed gold, black trodden mud and wide sky dominate the ground.
vibe_signature_feature: Deep firm trackways are trodden through the marsh in a repeating circuit. Reed is flattened in beds at three points on the circuit.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest could hire out a clearance for a giant sitting across a drove line. A quest could also hire out a diversion for a giant sitting across a drove line.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 5), 360 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Firm trackways cross eight square kilometres of marsh. The giant that still walks them trod the trackways.
siting_note: The place is kept on the Murkwood side of the lake (culture raster: naga-kur-deeps). The range is defined by having no settlement in it. The lair has a wallow-mouth den, which the 'trodden ground' implies, so the lair can be entered.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a protected territory, mapped by totems

name: Murkwood Verge
why_founding: The forest that ever moves was last placed south-east of Blackrose. Only the Conclave of Baal at Stormhold can find it. The Conclave reads the Elder Scrolls with an old tablet.
why_site_advantages: The verge is a stretch of coast marsh south-east of the city. The tree line falls in a different place on every survey. The ground itself is ordinary. The danger comes with the forest.
why_occupants_motive: Medusas and fellrunners came in with the trees.
why_pressures: The verge is where the forest stands now. Villages within a day of it keep a tally of where it has stood before.
why_would_change_if: The forest will stand somewhere else. The villages date its previous positions from the stump-fields.
vibe_silhouette: A wall of black-green forest stands straight up out of flat marsh. There is no transition between marsh and forest. A kilometre behind it, grey bleached stumps stand in ankle-deep water. The stump field marks where the tree line used to be.
vibe_palette: The palette is black-green canopy wall, grey bleached stumps and white mist.
vibe_materials: On the marsh side stand market tents and totem posts. The nearest tent is a hundred metres back. No cut timber comes out of the trees. The forest stands intact.
vibe_signature_feature: A wall of forest stands across open marsh with no transition. The bleached stumps of the previous tree line lie a kilometre behind it.
vibe_condition: The verge itself is unaltered. The bleached stump-field behind it records that the forest stood elsewhere.
vibe_approach: The verge is approached across open marsh. The forest edge is a line, not a gradient.
vibe_senses: The marsh is noisy on one side of the line and silent on the other. The line between them is a step wide. The smell of leaf-mould and a draught of cold air come from the trees.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 292 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, parent, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.blasphemer-urn-vault (+0.73).
player_purpose_hook: The villages keep a tally of where the moving forest has stood. This is where it stands this year.
siting_note: The verge is deliberately on the naga-kur-deeps frontier. The verge marks the edge of Blackrose's basin. Beyond that line the basin is no longer Blackrose's.
reconciliation_note: Contestable CONFIRMED here (2026-09-02 reconciliation). The flag suspected a mercantile-coast double-claim; there is none. The record stands south-east of Blackrose (positionM 2591.0,6676.2 against Blackrose 2343.0,6424.8: 350 m south-east), which is this region, so the record stays where it is built. Its 'moves' property is expressed as the verge plus an absent state, not as a second record elsewhere.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: has two or more authored verge locations and an absent state, exactly as the drifting village does

name: The Blue Hole
why_founding: The Blue Hole is a karst shaft in the lake floor. It drops well below the lake bed and connects to something else.
why_site_advantages: The shaft is a vertical hole nine metres wide in a flat lake bottom. A cold current comes out of it.
why_occupants_motive: The shaft is unworked. Two lake-divers have gone down it and one came back.
why_pressures: The current reverses seasonally. The source of the current fills and empties.
why_would_change_if: Mapping where the shaft surfaces would alter the basin's hydrology. It would also open a route.
vibe_palette: The palette is lake green above, blue-black below and a silt curtain.
vibe_signature_feature: A perfectly round hole sits in a flat lake floor. Colder, clearer water rises out of it. No bottom is in sight.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can pay for a through-dive. The dive would prove the shaft reaches the western feeder country.
why_site_won: local tie in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 27 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; bound to body.1290-3508 within 80 m; needs 1 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A karst shaft nine metres wide lies in the lake floor. Cold water rises out of it and no bottom is in sight.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: the only entrance to a submerged place

name: The Quiet Excavation
why_founding: Diggers are tunnelling toward the Rose's lower levels from outside the walls. The work is recent and unlicensed.
why_site_advantages: The dig stands on a spoil-hidden rise in the marsh. The rise is 275.5 m from the Blackrose centre and 210 m from the prison. It lies on the alignment of the flooded tunnel.
why_occupants_motive: The diggers know what Umbriel left in the lower levels. They are digging for it.
why_pressures: The Rose's families have not noticed the dig. The Chainbreakers have noticed it. The Chainbreakers have not agreed what to do.
why_would_change_if: Breaking into the lower levels from outside would release what the bricked stair contains.
vibe_palette: The palette is wet spoil black, lamp green and marsh grey.
vibe_signature_feature: A shored shaft stands under a spoil-covered awning. An alignment string runs dead straight from it toward the prison. The prison is about 210 m away.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can follow fresh grave-goods in the city market back to a shaft aimed at the Rose.
why_site_won: Reseated (2026-09-23): Moved outside the Blackrose disc after the 2026-09-20 island reseat: the dot sat 2179.7, 6561.0, less than 275 m from the new centre, the city disc plus its own footprint; the nearest standable ground within 60 degrees of its bearing from the new centre is 2131.4, 6601.3 (275.5 m from the centre, 62.9 m move).
