name: The Red Pit
why_founding: The basin's red clay is the best in the south. Every roof tile and storage jar for fifty kilometres is fired at this pit.
why_site_advantages: The pit is a clay bank at a river bend. Fuel comes down the river and the product goes out on it.
why_occupants_motive: Families work three firing floors in rotation. Those families have never done anything else.
why_pressures: The pit face is undercutting the river bend. It will eventually collapse the firing floors.
why_would_change_if: A bank collapse would move the whole industry to a worse clay.
vibe_palette: The palette is red clay, wood-smoke grey and orange tile.
vibe_signature_feature: A red clay cliff has three stone-hooded firing floors at its foot. Fuel is stacked in walls behind the floors. Drying racks of green tile lie in an orange field.
player_purpose_hook: Every tile roof for fifty kilometres was dried on these racks. The bank on which they stand is eroding into the river.
deferred_why: The pit is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance (70 records against a 17-21 budget). It is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a navigable water for export

name: The Standing Debt
why_founding: An estate on the western feeder evicted households for owed labour. The households camp on the estate boundary because leaving forfeits their claim.
why_site_advantages: The camp is on the estate boundary, in sight of the households' fields. It is within reach of Vaunting's market.
why_occupants_motive: The camp is how the households hold their claim. Vaunting feeds the households because feeding them is cheaper than the alternative.
why_pressures: The estate's owners are waiting the households out. The Chainbreakers have started paying their market debts. That payment changes the arithmetic.
why_would_change_if: A Chainbreaker purchase of the debt would end the eviction. It would also set a precedent.
vibe_palette: The palette is mud, salvage timber and crop green beyond.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp is strung along a field boundary. Each household carried its door-post from its old house. Each door-post is re-set facing the household's own fields.
player_purpose_hook: The camp is on the estate boundary, in sight of the households' fields. It is within reach of Vaunting's market.
deferred_why: The camp is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. Type 'owing-eviction-camp' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: immediately outside an estate village

name: The Cordon
why_founding: Blackrose held this line during the Flu. Stones mark the line every hundred paces from the hills to the water.
why_site_advantages: The line follows the narrows. Six kilometres of stone blocks the basin there.
why_occupants_motive: Blackrose has not enforced the line since the Flu. Every stone is still standing.
why_pressures: Villages on the far side of the line still describe themselves as outside. The Flu was about nine centuries ago, between 2E 560 and 4E 201.
why_would_change_if: Removing the stones would need a council vote. No council member has put that vote on the roll.
vibe_palette: The palette is weathered stone, grass and distant water.
vibe_signature_feature: A line of hundred-pace marker stones runs six kilometres across country. Each stone is cut with the same three words.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 55 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Six kilometres of hundred-pace marker stones are all still standing. Each stone is cut with the same three words.
siting_note: The line runs east of Blackrose toward the coast hinterland. The culture raster reads mercantile-coast on the line's far side. The record depends on that reading. The villages beyond the stones still call themselves outside. The line was kept in place and given its surviving gate.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: encircles a plague-abandoned village or a cairn field

name: Third Generation
why_founding: Prison-born households left the Rose. The households cannot join any village because they have grown up without a Hist.
why_site_advantages: The settlement stands on an island in the coast marsh. The island lies two hours off the causeway and is defensible. No group has claimed the island.
why_occupants_motive: The households are building a community with no tree and no clan. No village recognises the households' funeral rite.
why_pressures: The households will not return to the Rose. No village will give the households shelter. Hissmir is weeks away. The households have not made the journey to Hissmir.
why_would_change_if: If a village sponsored the households into tree-access, the settlement would dissolve in a single season.
vibe_silhouette: The settlement is new and stands around a carefully finished empty enclosure. The settlement has the shape of a hist-village. Bare swept earth fills the middle of the enclosure.
vibe_palette: The palette is raw new timber, bare earth and marsh grey.
vibe_materials: The buildings are raw new timber throughout. The plaster is unweathered. The tree-enclosure is built of dressed stakes and is unplanted.
vibe_signature_feature: A carefully built empty tree-enclosure stands at the settlement's centre. The households wait for a cutting that no village has agreed to give.
vibe_condition: The settlement is newly built to an old standard. The enclosure is finished better than the houses.
vibe_approach: The settlement lies two hours off the causeway by water. The enclosure is the first thing visible from the landing.
vibe_senses: The wood is new. The households sweep the enclosure daily. Three generations of accents are heard in one place. Root-hum is not felt anywhere in the settlement.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest could carry a citizenship petition. The petition forces Blackrose to name what the Rose is.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 186 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, bound; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A finished tree-enclosure stands empty and is swept every day. The households wait on a cutting from a village that has not agreed to send one.
siting_note: The settlement lies west of the lake. The culture raster calls the ground mercantile-coast. The refuge exists to stand apart from Blackrose, so the edge of Blackrose's cultural reach suits the record.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the edge of somewhere that refused them

name: The Verge Camp
why_founding: Two villages from the north-east marsh moved out. The Murkwood verge stood closer than any living villager had seen it. The villagers camped at the ferry.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands at the north stage. The north stage is as far as the villagers' boats could carry them in one journey.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers wait to see if the verge advances again. The villagers have waited nine years.
why_pressures: The city will not settle the villagers. The villagers will not go back. The holders of the ferry concession are wary of the camp.
why_would_change_if: If the verge retreated, the camp would be empty in a week. If the verge advanced, the ferry would empty.
vibe_palette: The palette is hull colour, tarpaulin and grey slip stone.
vibe_signature_feature: The boats of two villages are drawn up in two separate lines above the ferry slip. The villagers have built houses on the boats and not beside them.
player_purpose_hook: The camp stands at the north stage. The north stage is as far as the villagers' boats could carry them in one journey.
deferred_why: The camp is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The province holds 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The camp is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: just outside a settlement that has not taken them in

name: Welloc's Lines
why_founding: The city threw up the lines when Blackrose rebelled against the Third Empire and raised an army. The garrison abandoned the lines when Empress Morihatha's battlemage Welloc broke the rebellion with a spell. Welloc laid no siege.
why_site_advantages: The lines stand on dry ground that commands all three approaches. The lines are competent and complete. The lines were never used in a siege.
why_occupants_motive: A licensed digging crew works along the ditch. The crew works for the pay chest that was never issued. The crew resents visitors who have had the same idea.
why_pressures: The citizens of Blackrose remember raising an army. They see the lines every day. A crew with a permit takes the lines apart one spit of earth at a time.
why_would_change_if: The lines will stay as they are. Only the crew's digging changes the lines.
vibe_silhouette: The ditch-and-bank profiles are sharp and geometric. The profiles lie across open grass in a textbook figure. The profiles are unblunted and have no breach.
vibe_palette: The palette is grass green, ditch shadow and grey sky.
vibe_materials: The lines are cut turf and rammed earth only. A few stockade stumps stand at the gate positions. The system holds no iron.
vibe_signature_feature: The siege lines are complete and unused. The ditch profiles are sharp and unfought. No arrowheads have been dug out of the lines.
vibe_condition: The lines are complete and unfought. Grass has softened the lines. The profiles stay sharp where a siege would have flattened them.
vibe_mood: The earthworks are unused and carry new spoil heaps.
vibe_approach: From the ground the ditch system reads as terracing. A walker crosses the ditch before recognising it.
vibe_senses: Wind crosses the grass. Footfalls sound hollow on the counterscarp. The ground holds no bone and no burnt earth.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest could establish that the garrison that reported the rebel lines dug them.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 124 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The siege lines were dug for a battle that did not happen. A licensed crew digs along the ditch for a pay chest that was never issued.
siting_note: The record changed from a hostile claim-gang delve to a wary licensed dig in the round 4 hostility rebalance. The place was one of sixteen fights within 250 m of the city's roads. The place stands at D1. The province already has twice Morrowind's fight density.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: always paired with what it besieged

name: The Raising Stone
why_founding: The city raised the stone for the army it raised. The inscription on the stone does not state what happened to the army.
why_site_advantages: The stone stands at the west gate. Every arriving trader reads the stone.
why_occupants_motive: The toll families maintain the stone. The toll families paid for the stone.
why_pressures: Three separate later inscriptions have been added to the stone. One inscription has been chiselled off.
why_would_change_if: A fourth inscription that named Welloc would be a political act.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey stone, cut shadow and one erasure.
vibe_signature_feature: A gate stone lists an army's muster by district. A scraped blank marks where a name used to be.
player_purpose_hook: The stone stands at the west gate. Every arriving trader reads the stone.
deferred_why: The stone is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The province holds 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The stone is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

name: The Arbiter's House
why_founding: A retired city arbiter keeps the case books. The arbiter settles disputes from a private house. More disputes are settled at the house than at the courthouse in session.
why_site_advantages: The house stands on the shore between Blackrose's gate and the lake landings. Both parties to a dispute can reach it. Neither party sets foot on the other's ground.
why_occupants_motive: The arbiter arbitrates for a fee that is set by the parties' means. The parties honour the rulings. Refusing a ruling is socially fatal.
why_pressures: The arbiter's case books contain the actual origins of the toll compact. Both sides know this.
why_would_change_if: If the arbiter died without a successor, disputes would return to the city's courts. The return of disputes to the courts would end a decade of quiet settlements.
vibe_palette: The palette is pale plaster, book brown and lake light.
vibe_signature_feature: The house is a modest lake house. A public bench stands outside the house. A queue forms on hearing days. A wall of case books shows through the window.
player_purpose_hook: A retired arbiter settles disputes at a private house. The house stands on the shore between Blackrose's gate and the lake landings.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The province holds 70 records against a budget of 17-21. The record is a tier-3 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: 200-600 m from the village it serves

name: Rockspring
why_founding: Rockspring is a village south-west of Blackrose. The village stands along a natural levee. A hard spring on the levee runs clear when the flats are brown.
why_site_advantages: The levee crest stands a metre above every recorded flood. A rock spring rises on the crest.
why_occupants_motive: The spring is the village's main asset. In a bad year the villagers sell water to boat crews by the cup.
why_pressures: The villagers want a share of Blackrose's lake-landing freight trade. The feeder is too shallow for laden hulls.
why_would_change_if: A dredged feeder would make Rockspring the western freight village. The dredged feeder would end Blackrose's monopoly on that trade.
vibe_silhouette: The village is a single-file line of thatch along the levee crest. The line is one house deep. Every door faces the water. One squat spring house stands at the middle of the line.
vibe_palette: The palette is levee green, thatch and clear spring silver against brown flood.
vibe_materials: Houses on the levee use mud-mother plaster over withy. Roofs are reed thatch. Stock fencing is wattle. The spring house is the hamlet's one stone building. The stone of the spring house is undressed.
vibe_signature_feature: A single-file village is strung along the crest of a natural levee. The spring house stands at the centre of the village. Every door faces the water.
vibe_condition: The village is sound. The whole village maintains the levee. Each household maintains its own house, unevenly.
vibe_mood: The village is strung out along the levee.
vibe_approach: In flood the levee carries the whole road. The hamlet sits on the levee. The road runs the length of the village.
vibe_senses: Clean water runs loudly at the spring. Every other water in the basin is silent and brown. Hens, wet clay and woodsmoke are present. Woodsmoke goes straight along the levee.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest could set a lawful lease against the water of a village.

siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: refuge for its neighbours in flood

why_pressures: The fee is the most resented transaction in the south. Both sides need the fee to continue.
why_would_change_if: If the families of the Rose refused to release the dead, the arrangement would end. The Chainbreakers and the families would then be in open conflict.

name: Rose Lower Levels
why_founding: The Rose's lowest levels flooded when the marsh submerged the foundations. Umbriel left something in the levels in 4E 48. What Umbriel left is still in the flooded levels.
why_site_advantages: The levels lie below the water table. A stair seals the levels. The prison-born families bricked up the stair two generations ago.
why_occupants_motive: The undead occupy the levels behind a bricked stair. The prison-born families bricked the stair and have not opened it. The families above say the stair leads to a flooded cellar. The brick has held for two generations.
why_pressures: The Chainbreakers' bone claims include people who died in the lower levels. The families' claim to legitimacy depends on the stair staying shut.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the lower levels would make the Rose a settlement. The clearing would end the Rose's reputation. The families would prefer the stair stayed bricked.
vibe_silhouette: A bricked stair-head stands in the corner of a working prison yard. The mortar is newer than the wall. The stair-head has no door. The stair-head is cold to the hand in a warm yard.
vibe_palette: The palette is black water, wet Imperial stone and lamp yellow at the head.
vibe_materials: The stair and vaulting below are Imperial. Above, the brick and mortar are two generations newer. Prison-born families laid the brick with the materials they had.
vibe_signature_feature: A bricked stair-head stands in a working prison yard. Water is audible behind the brick. The mortar is two generations newer than the wall around the stair-head.
vibe_condition: The stair is deliberately sealed. The structure is sound. The levels are occupied behind the brick.
vibe_approach: The stair-head lies inside an inhabited prison yard. Residents tell visitors to keep away from the corner.
vibe_senses: Water is audible behind the brick in a dry yard. Cold air comes through the seam. The ordinary domestic noise of the yard goes on around the stair-head.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest could make opening or holding the bricked stair the decision. The families and the Chainbreakers would be on opposite sides.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 345 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, region, danger.
player_purpose_hook: Behind the bricked stair the Rose continues downward under the water table. Umbriel's dead are still standing in the lower levels.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: links two known places by a wet route

name: Outworks, Cordon One
why_founding: The Empire dug holding pits and a ditch line outside the Rose's walls. Arrivals were processed in the pits before the gate was opened.
why_site_advantages: The ground is firm on the causeway side of the marsh. It lies close enough to the Rose for a chained line to be marched to the yard. It lies far enough from the Rose that the yard never saw the line.
why_occupants_motive: A raw Blackguard crew found roofed stone pits with locking floors already dug. The crew uses the pits for their original purpose.
why_pressures: The prison-born families refuse to police ground. They will not be associated with the prison on that ground. The townspeople of Vaunting say the outworks are the prison's business.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the crew out would give the Chainbreakers a receiving house. The house would lie within sight of the causeway.

vibe_materials: The pits are Imperial pit stone with iron floor-grates. The original numbering is cut into every lintel. The crew's additions are all timber and rope.
vibe_signature_feature: Six numbered stone pits stand in a ditched enclosure. The Empire's numbering is still legible. The crew replaced every lock within the last year.
vibe_condition: The stonework is sound and twelve centuries old. The locks are new.

name: Vaunting
why_founding: The Rose had to be fed for twelve centuries. The Empire built the supply town to feed the Rose. The town outlived the Empire. The town also outlived the prison's official function.
why_site_advantages: The town stands on the causeway road at the last firm ground before the marsh. The town has a barge landing and a walled magazine.
why_occupants_motive: The townspeople of Vaunting still supply the Rose, now on commercial terms. That arrangement is the entire economy of the town.
why_pressures: Half the town descends from prison staff. Half descends from released prisoners. The two halves intermarry. The townspeople still make the distinction.
why_would_change_if: Emptying the Rose would end the town within a decade.

vibe_materials: The ranges and magazine use Imperial lime render and red pantile. Argonians added reed lean-tos and mud-mother garden walls behind the ranges. The additions do not pass through the original walls.
vibe_signature_feature: Vaunting is an Imperial garrison town. The barrack rows are converted to houses. The magazine is still locked. The townspeople chalk the prison's ration tally on the magazine door every week.
vibe_condition: The institutional fabric is maintained beyond any civilian need. The domestic fabric is patched. The magazine is still locked and still sound.
vibe_mood: Vaunting is a military town that is still working.
vibe_approach: From the causeway road the barrack ranges read as a fort. Washing strung between the ranges is the exception.
vibe_senses: Townspeople write the weekly chalk tally on the magazine door. Barges move on the water. Civilian feet cross the drill-yard flagstones. The air carries render dust.

siting_note: The place was converted from a hostile clearable delve to a guarded cellar under a working counting-house. The conversion came in the round 4 hostility rebalance.
