name: Three Gates
why_founding: The economy of Blackrose rests on transit and tolls. The toll town sits at the western confluence outside the city walls. The Bramman channel, the three-gate channel and the portage water meet at that confluence.
why_site_advantages: The three western waters meet at this confluence. A hull from any western feeder must pass the quay to reach the lake.
why_occupants_motive: Families of an Argonian toll-holding compact hold the toll. The compact predates the current city government. The compact has outlasted three city governments.
why_pressures: The western freight families pay the toll under protest. Eastern traffic goes round by Threewater.
why_would_change_if: If the compact were lost, the city would gain direct control of its own revenue for the first time.
vibe_silhouette: Three gated water channels converge on one stone counting-quay. Three tariff boards stand above the roofline like sails.
vibe_palette: The stone is wet, the tariff boards are painted and the water is dark.
vibe_materials: The quay and gate piers are dressed stone. This is Imperial work that Argonians hold. The remaining structures use bridge timber and painted board. The counting house is stone.
vibe_signature_feature: Three gated water channels converge on one stone counting-quay. Three separate tariff boards in three scripts stand over one set of accounts.
vibe_condition: The toll is maintained ruthlessly. The gates work and the boards are repainted. The counting house of the compact is the best-kept building in the region.
vibe_approach: All three rivers arrive at the same quay.
vibe_senses: Three streams of traffic arrive and one queue leaves. Chain and windlass sound at the gates. Clerks scratch three sets of accounts that are kept as one.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can expose three gate books that agree too well to have been kept separately.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: RS04 · tier-2; LR45 · tier-3; LR59 · tier-3; LR60 · tier-3; Reed track · tier-2
player_purpose_hook: Three western channels meet at one counting-quay. The quay has three tariff boards and one set of accounts.
siting_note: The place is bound to the western confluence at (1607, 6520). The Bramman and three-gate channels meet at that confluence. The identity of the place is a toll that the western freight must pass. The claim was narrowed from the whole basin to those waters. The record was moved onto the junction that it names in the round 4 network-role pass.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the western boat lanes at their meeting point

name: Given Field
why_founding: Welloc's vampiric cloud displaced the rebels' strength and skill to their opponents on this field. The Blackrose army broke in under a minute.
why_site_advantages: The rebels chose this open ground south of the city for their muster.
why_occupants_motive: The field is unclaimed by any faction. Grave-singers refuse to work the field. Ossu grave-singers are among those who refuse. The grave-singers say that the dead on the field were emptied. The grave-singers hold that no rite exists for such a death.
why_pressures: The people of Blackrose distrust battlemages. The distrust dates from this field. The distrust is now civic policy.
why_would_change_if: A grave-singer who was willing to drive burial poles over this field would end a two-century-old civic wound.
vibe_silhouette: The field is flat and open. The grass grows in the shape of an army. The shape is legible only from a position slightly above the field.
vibe_palette: The grass is pale, the rust is a mass and the light is flat.
vibe_materials: Grass grows over a mass of rust. The field has no burial poles and no cairn. About two centuries later, the rust still lies where it fell.
vibe_signature_feature: The grass grows in the shape of a formation. No burial pole is driven into the field.
vibe_condition: The field is undisturbed. It has had no burial and no salvage. The formation is still legible in the sward.
vibe_approach: From the ridge track the pattern in the grass resolves into a formation.
vibe_senses: Wind blows, the light is flat and insects hum. The grass changes underfoot from soft to a mass that is not soil. Scavenger birds do not fly over the field.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can reopen a field that the city recorded as a victory. The quest would act on behalf of a person who was present on the field.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 219 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: About two centuries of rebel iron still lie in the grass. No grave-singer will drive a pole in the field.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: at a xanmeer, a crossing or a road

name: The Sealed Vault
why_founding: A vault lies under a ruined works. The people who found what had grown in it sealed it. They nailed the door shut.
why_site_advantages: The vault is a stone undercroft with one door and no other opening.
why_occupants_motive: The voriplasm lives in the vault. It has been sealed in the vault for two hundred years.
why_pressures: The note of the sealing party is still nailed to the door. The note names the contents of the vault.
why_would_change_if: If the vault were opened, a creature would be released. The province has a specific and unhappy history with that creature.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey and the board weathered.
vibe_signature_feature: Rusted iron bands hold the vault's old wooden door. A board is nailed to the door. The message on the board is legible after two hundred years.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can establish what has been fed to the sealed vault. The same quest can establish on whose orders it was fed.
why_site_won: water narrows in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 439 m from the nearest route; won on bound, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The party that sealed the door nailed a board to the door. The board says what is inside the vault. The board is still legible.
watch_reason: A sealed vault with no people.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: inside a xanmeer, an Ayleid ruin or a flooded cellar

name: Threewater
why_founding: The eastern feeder from Oliis Bay and the Lilmoth road meet the lake system at this site. A market grew for traders who were unwilling to pay the Blackrose gate toll.
why_site_advantages: The town stands at a river junction on the Lilmoth side. It has firm banks on three sides. The water carries laden hulls in every season but the driest.
why_occupants_motive: The town exists to be cheaper than Blackrose. The whole civic life of the town is organised around staying cheaper.
why_pressures: Blackrose has twice sent 'inspectors'. The townspeople have twice paid them and continued.
why_would_change_if: An enforced toll in the town would collapse the market back into the city in two years or less.
vibe_silhouette: A flat grid of open-sided shed roofs runs along a river junction. The outline has no wall, gate or tower.
vibe_palette: The colours are those of shed timber, grain sack and brown river.
vibe_materials: Frames are bamboo and mud-mother with shed roofing over open sides. The stalls use market canvas and plank scales. One landmark scale-house stands in the town. The town has no defensible building.
vibe_signature_feature: A grid of open-sided trading sheds runs along a river junction. Each shed has its own scale. The town has no wall or gate.
vibe_condition: The sheds are cheap and constantly rebuilt. A shed lasts three seasons.
vibe_approach: The town has no edge. The sheds begin along the river bank.
vibe_senses: Traders weigh goods all day, with a hundred scales and a hundred arguments. Grain dust and river smell hang in the air. No gate-bell rings in the town.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can compare the charter, the price board and the roads of Threewater. The three do not agree.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LQ25 · tier-3; LR44 · tier-3; LR45 · tier-3; LR46 · tier-3; LR47 · tier-3; LR48 · tier-3; LR49 · tier-3; LR50 · tier-3; LR51 · tier-3; LR52 · tier-3
player_purpose_hook: Traders in Threewater sell the same goods as Blackrose. The town stands at a river junction nearer the sea and has a cheaper toll.
siting_note: The town is plotted east of Blackrose on the junction of the eastern channel and the Prison road. Earlier prose called it the western feeder market, which contradicted its ground. The prose was corrected and the town was not moved. The junction that the town needs exists at this position. The western confluence is already the Three Gates toll. The culture raster reads mercantile-coast at this position. Traders in the town deal with the coast to undercut the city.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: the eastern feeder's junction, a half-day downstream of Blackrose

name: The Lantern Fen
why_founding: The Lantern Fen lies off any track. Lights move there at night in the pattern of a lit causeway.
why_site_advantages: The fen lies on the Murkwood frontier. The nearest route is 380.1 m away. The lights serve as a lure only in ground where walkers have no reason to go.
why_occupants_motive: Something unknown makes the lights. It has made them for as long as the floating road has stood.
why_pressures: Carters who walk at night have followed the lights off the road. Vaunting posts a lamp-keeper in the bad months.
why_would_change_if: A properly lit causeway would end the deaths. It would cost Vaunting money that Vaunting does not have.
vibe_palette: The lights are pale blue-green. The fen is black. Real lamps shine in the distance.
vibe_signature_feature: A line of soft lights crosses open fen. The lights are spaced like the causeway's own lamps. The lights move very slowly.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can make the fen lights a hazard to night travellers.
why_site_won: water narrows in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 380 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.feeder-portage (+0.86).
player_purpose_hook: The lights across the fen are spaced like the causeway lamps. Carters who walk at night have followed the lights off the road.
siting_note: The place is left on the Murkwood frontier, where the culture raster reads naga-kur-deeps. The lure works only where there is no reason to walk. The prose claim that it sat on the Rose approach was cut. The nearest track is 266 m away.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a route people travel at night

name: The Old Span
why_founding: A pre-Imperial stone span crosses the eastern feeder. It is older than the city. It still carries the road. A charge is still levied for the crossing.
why_site_advantages: The span is the only crossing of the eastern feeder within eight kilometres that needs no boat.
why_occupants_motive: One of the toll families holds the span. The claim of the family rests on continuous collection. It rests on no grant.
why_pressures: The Blackrose council disputes the claim annually. The council pays the toll monthly.
why_would_change_if: A collapse would sever the eastern road. All traffic would then use the water and the gates of the city.
vibe_palette: The ancient stone is grey and fitted. The timber is new and the water is brown.
vibe_signature_feature: A single low xanmeer-built span of fitted stone crosses the feeder. A modern timber toll house is grafted onto one end.
player_purpose_hook: The span is the only crossing of the eastern feeder within eight kilometres that needs no boat.
deferred_why: The record was parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The province has 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The record is a tier-2 density fill on the most over-dense ground of the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight

name: The Wrong Name
why_founding: A ruin in the Blackrose basin has been attributed to the Yespest by three separate authorities. The ruin is not Yespest at all.
why_site_advantages: The ruin stands on the western feeder where Kothringi, Yespest and Lilmothiit ground all overlap. That overlap is how the mistake was made.
why_occupants_motive: The site has no residents. Two rival scholarly parties maintain incompatible notice-boards at the entrance.
why_pressures: The building itself shows the correct attribution. A visitor who compares it with the Robbed City can read it.
why_would_change_if: A correct identification would embarrass an institution. It would also change who has a claim on the site.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey, the moss is green and the brass plaques are green with age.
vibe_signature_feature: A ruin has two competing carved attribution plaques at its entrance, both wrong. The right answer shows in the masonry twenty paces from the entrance.
player_purpose_hook: The ruin stands on the western feeder where Kothringi, Yespest and Lilmothiit ground all overlap. That overlap is how the mistake was made.
deferred_why: The record was parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance. The province has 70 records against a 17-21 budget. The record is a tier-2 density fill on the most over-dense ground of the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: near a settlement that tells the story wrong

name: The Alessian Hull
why_founding: A First-Era warship from the fleet that chased Red Bramman was lost on the reef. It settled upright in eleven metres of water.
why_site_advantages: The water is deep enough that the hull is intact. The stern is shallow enough for a single-breath dive.
why_occupants_motive: Four Soulrest families dispute the ownership. The dispute has not been settled by any court.
why_pressures: Two centuries of salvage have stripped the deck. Silt fills the hold up to the coamings.
why_would_change_if: One good season of settled water would let a diving team open the whole hold.
vibe_palette: The water is green, the timber black and the sand white.
vibe_signature_feature: A ram-bowed hull stands upright on the bottom with its ribs open. It is visible from the surface on a calm day.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can fund and survive the first cut into the shut hold. Four claimants watch as the salvage is raised.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 23 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; needs 8 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A First-Era warship sits upright in eleven metres of water. Its holds are still shut.
deferred_why: The record was parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'wreck' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6. The surplus is paid first out of the over-band types.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Southern Sea approach the wreckers work; inside 2 km of Whitebone Reef

name: Alten Meerhleel
why_founding: Alten Meerhleel is an outsider-facing port south-west of Lilmoth. It is below city scale. An Argonian raft-quarter and an outsiders' warehouse row front the same water. Lilmoth lay destroyed for a century and a half. During that time the bay's outside trade came to Meerhleel. Enough of that trade stayed that the quay outgrew the village.
why_site_advantages: Slow deep water lies inside the bar. A laden hull can lie off in the deep water and be worked by lighters. Firm ground behind the quay carries a warehouse row. The 'alten-' in the name means outsiders.
why_occupants_motive: Lightermen, Argonian raft-quarter families and factors from four ports live here. The customs presence is one clerk and an unstaffed tariff shed. Traders value the port for the absence of inspection.
why_pressures: Lilmoth is rebuilt, so the two ports are now direct rivals. Meerhleel's advantage is that no questions are asked there. Corimont is the province's real free port. Questions are not asked there either. Corimont lies behind a harbour wall.
why_would_change_if: If Lilmoth's council dropped its tariffs, Soulrest factors would have no reason to sail to Meerhleel. A real harbour at Lilmoth would serve their needs.
vibe_silhouette: A straight warehouse gable-line and two masts stand on one side of the landing. A low uneven raft-quarter with no roofline stands on the other side. The landing stage lies between them.
vibe_palette: The palette is sun-bleached deck timber, painted price boards and brown estuary water.
vibe_materials: Two kits share the landing stage. The warehouse row uses sawn plank, ridge-tile and iron strap. The raft-quarter uses lashed plank platforms on piles, with reed and cane. No frame, post or tile crosses the stage in either direction.
vibe_signature_feature: Two building grammars stand on one waterfront. A lashed Argonian plank quarter is moored to its piles. It stands beside a straight-gabled outsiders' warehouse row. The landing stage joins the two.
vibe_condition: The port is prospering and patched. The warehouse row is maintained to the day. The raft-quarter is rebuilt continuously and looks worse for the work.
vibe_approach: From the water, the masts and a warehouse gable read together. They show before the plank quarter does.
vibe_senses: The sounds are cargo hooks, tallying and arguments in two languages. The smells are tar, bilge and unswept spice. At slack water the estuary smells brown.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest tests a port in which no questions are asked. The port's own quay has been robbed.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM29 · tier-3; LM64 · tier-3; LM65 · tier-3; LM66 · tier-3; LM67 · tier-3; LM68 · tier-3; LM69 · tier-3; LM70 · tier-3; LM71 · tier-3; LM72 · tier-3; LM73 · tier-3; RS-line · tier-2
why_site_won: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'natural-harbour' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, navigable; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Foreigners can buy and sell here without Lilmoth's permission.
reconciliation_note: Retyped from neutral-free-port (2026-09-02 reconciliation). That singular type is anchored in the lore on Alten Corimont — named freehold, captain of the port, nailed price list — which keeps it; the lore gives Meerhleel only 'a port built to trade with outsiders', which port-town covers honestly at the same M4 scale. ID unchanged.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately equidistant from two customs regimes

name: Ashfield
why_founding: A Colovian family founded the estate on ash-enriched lowland left by the Great Burn. The family bought out the smallholders. They put in a single plantation.
why_site_advantages: The ground is dry and firm. Deep burn ash lies on it. The coast road runs at the field edge.
why_occupants_motive: The estate lacks a tenant. The house is empty. The fields have gone to scrub grass and bramble.
why_pressures: The roof timbers are failing one by one. A pack has denned under the old threshing floor.
why_would_change_if: A new tenant with the coin to clear the ground could reopen the fields.
vibe_silhouette: The site is a low horizontal, the province's only open field-horizon. Scrub has made it ragged. One marker stone still stands at the road junction.
vibe_palette: Black soil is going green with weed. Dead stubble is pale. Every metal fitting has rust.
vibe_materials: The walls are rammed black earth. The wattle hurdles are rotted. Farmstead timber sags on rendered-stone footings.
vibe_signature_feature: Roofed yard buildings stand over fields uncut for years. Charcoal still turns up in every collapsed furrow.
vibe_condition: The house range is derelict. The yard buildings are sound. Field fencing is down throughout the estate.
vibe_mood: The estate is empty and going back to scrub.
vibe_approach: The canopy still ends abruptly and sky opens above. Bramble now breaks the field lines.
vibe_senses: Wind moves through the dead stubble and bramble. A smell of char rises when a furrow is disturbed. The pack is the only thing that moves.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest is to clear the den under the threshing floor. The work must be done before the roof timbers finish failing.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1109 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.pilgrim-xanmeer (+1.27).
player_purpose_hook: Ashfield is an abandoned Colovian plantation on good soil. It is still roofed in places. A pack holds the yard.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in a city's agricultural hinterland

name: Ashfield Hearth
why_founding: Ashfield Hearth is a village-kept fire and dry floor on the road. Villagers maintain it by rota. The coast road kills travellers who are caught out.
why_site_advantages: It stands where the road leaves firm ground for the salt marsh.
why_occupants_motive: Ashfield's households keep the hearth in turn. Each guest who uses it must leave fuel.
why_pressures: Travellers routinely take fuel without leaving any. The rota is failing gradually.
why_would_change_if: A season of unkept fires would end a two-hundred-year custom.
vibe_palette: Ember orange, reed brown.
vibe_signature_feature: The hearth is a single shuttered room. It holds a banked fire and a fuel stack. A tally board records who last filled the fuel stack.
player_purpose_hook: A banked fire and a dry floor stand where the road leaves firm ground. Guests leave fuel. If a guest does not, the villagers remember it.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The province has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. This is tier-4 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

name: Ashroot
why_founding: Ashroot is the nearest Hist village to Soulrest. Argonian households remain in the burn country because the Hist is here.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on a rise that the peat fire did not cross. The tree's roots draw on water below the depth of the burn.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers kept the tree alive through the Burn. They date the village's own history from that season.
why_pressures: The jungle edge here kills travellers who walk it alone. The villagers give this warning at the gate.
why_would_change_if: Losing the tree would disperse the village into the city within a generation.
vibe_silhouette: One blue-flowered crown stands alone above a field of white dead stumps. A bright water channel rings the crown.
vibe_palette: The palette is blue blossom, black ash and green channel.
vibe_materials: Walls use mud-mother plaster and roofs use reed throughout. Wattle fire-breaks and Argonian lamp-cages stand in the village. Every post is new timber cut from outside the burn.
vibe_signature_feature: A blue-flowered Hist stands alone in a district of dead white stumps. A low water channel rings it. The villagers dug the channel to keep fire out of the crown.
vibe_condition: The village is deliberately new. Every structure has been rebuilt since the burn. Buildings are kept clear of the dead stumps. The villagers refuse to remove the stumps.
vibe_approach: The dead stumps read first as a white field. The living crown shows only from among the stumps.
vibe_senses: Water runs in the fire channel day and night. Chime-frames sound. The scent of blossom is out of place over ash. Charcoal lies underfoot throughout the village.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest is to carry the gate warning to people who ignored it. Another is to mend the sheltering rite that is failing.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ15 · tier-0; LM45 · tier-3; LM74 · tier-3; LM75 · tier-3; LM76 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 151 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Ashroot has the last Hist between Soulrest and the burn country. The villagers shelter travellers.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: within 2500 m of Soulrest, in the burn country behind the city

name: Sees-No-Root
why_founding: The village's Hist died with its mnemic egg unrecovered. The villagers organise their offices and rites around the loss.
why_site_advantages: The ground is unchanged and good. Villages that lose a Hist usually disperse. This village remained.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers maintain the empty enclosure and the grave offices. They recite aloud the memories once held by the crown.
why_pressures: The children are leaving for Lilmoth. The recitation takes six days. Fewer villagers can perform it each year.
why_would_change_if: A recovered egg would restore the village at a stroke. Treasure-hunters across Murkmire know that the reward stands.
vibe_silhouette: The village has a hole in its middle. A walled empty circle stands where the crown should be. The roofline dips toward it on four sides.
vibe_palette: The palette is wall moss, bare earth circle and lamp gold.
vibe_materials: Houses use mud-mother plaster and reed. One enclosure wall is of carefully laid stakes. A single hardwood recitation bench is worn to a shine.
vibe_signature_feature: An empty walled tree-enclosure faces a worn smooth recitation bench. Every evening a villager speaks the whole village's memory to a stump-socket.
vibe_condition: The village is well kept. The villagers maintain the empty enclosure more carefully than any house.
vibe_approach: The village looks ordinary from every direction. Inside the ring of houses, the enclosure that the houses face becomes visible.
vibe_senses: One voice recites at the same hour each evening. The rest of the village stays quiet for the recitation. The enclosure wall has wet moss. The root-hum is absent from the village.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest is to find speakers for the recitation. Another is to find the mnemic egg around which the village organised its life.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MR05 · tier-2; LM24 · tier-3; LM31 · tier-3; LM77 · tier-3; LM78 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 509 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The village lost its tree and remains inhabited. The villagers pay well for news of the egg.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: neighbours argue about whether to admit them

name: Murkmire Pulled Field
why_founding: The grave-poles of a burial ground were pulled out by persons unknown. The bog blight came up afterwards.
why_site_advantages: The site is an old village burial ground on soft peat. Soft peat is the condition that the blight requires.
why_occupants_motive: The field belongs to no household. The blight keeps to the field. The villagers fenced the field by common consent.
why_pressures: The pulled poles lie where they were dropped. The grave-warden cannot match each pole to its grave.
why_would_change_if: Driving the poles back in the right order would end the blight. A grave-singer must enter the field to do it.
vibe_palette: The palette is peat black, bleached wood and sick green.
vibe_signature_feature: The field holds plain driven grave-poles. Half of the poles are pulled and lie like scattered kindling. The ground shifts under no weight.
vibe_approach: A fenced wattle boundary has pahnjees hung on it. Beyond the boundary, peat gives under the boot.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest is to drive the pulled poles back in the order set down by the register. The field is awake on every side.
why_site_won: open water in interior swamp (danger band 4), 446 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on nearPoint, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The field is a grave-field with half its poles pulled. The ground still shifts.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: at or beside a grave-pole field

name: The Carrying House
why_founding: Argonians who die in stone prisons can still return if their bones are brought to the dirt. A halfway house for the bones had to be built.
why_site_advantages: The house stands on the burn-country track between White Rose and the coast road. It is one day's carry from either.
why_occupants_motive: Carriers rest, re-wrap and re-label bundles here. The keeper records every name that passes through the house and where it is going.
why_pressures: The register is longer than the number of bodies that have actually reached a Hist.
why_would_change_if: If White Rose were emptied, the house would become a memorial. It would cease to be a service.
vibe_palette: The palette is reed brown, bleached cloth and lamp-black ink.
vibe_signature_feature: The house is a low open-sided hall of racks. Each rack holds a wrapped bundle. Each bundle carries a written name and a destination village.
player_purpose_hook: The house is a rack-hall of wrapped dead waiting to be carried home. The keeper's register names every one.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'bone-repatriation-waystation' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The over-band types pay out the surplus first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: between a carceral site and the interior

name: Tideward Stage
why_founding: The coast road crosses the river south of Soulrest. The river is too deep to ford and too wide to bridge cheaply.
why_site_advantages: The crossing is a narrows with firm banks on both sides. Slack water lasts an hour either side of the turn.
why_occupants_motive: The ferry family also hire out as guides upriver. The guiding pays better than the ferry.
why_pressures: Guides are hired to go upriver far more often than the traffic justifies. The eldest daughter names a different reach each time she is asked to say which reach.
why_would_change_if: A bridge here would end both trades. People have proposed a bridge three times.
vibe_palette: The palette is river brown, rope grey and green bank.
vibe_signature_feature: A rope-guided flat punt serves the crossing. A hiring board lists the upriver reaches by hours. The board gives no names for them.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest is to hire the ferry family upriver. The trip reveals the sights that the ferry family take Soulrest factors to see.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 161 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The ferry family crosses passengers for coin. They also go upriver for considerably more.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The province has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'ferry-stage' stays active at 'oliis-ferry-stage'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage

name: Bramman's Screen
why_founding: The site is the seaward mouth, in dense mangrove, of a narrow winding river. Red Bramman escaped the Alessian navy by that river.
why_site_advantages: Four channel mouths open off the same bay. This one carries water at the top of the tide for about ninety minutes.
why_occupants_motive: The pilots who know the run sell the knowledge. A wrong channel strands a hull until the next tide.
why_pressures: The route is worth something only while it stays unmarked. A scheduled ferry service on the route would end that.
why_would_change_if: A silt pulse could close the channel or open a second. Either change would end the pilots' monopoly.
vibe_silhouette: The site has no silhouette. Four identical black mangrove mouths stand in an unbroken wall of root. They are indistinguishable until the water drops.
vibe_palette: The palette is black water, root brown and green tunnel light.
vibe_materials: The materials are living mangrove root, a sand sill, one cut tide-mark and a few unpainted marker withies. One stake platform inside the true channel is the built work here.
vibe_signature_feature: Four identical mangrove mouths open off the bay. One of them is false-bottomed with a sand sill. A tide-mark is cut into a root. The tide-mark is legible only at slack water.
vibe_condition: The site is untouched by design. A built marker would advertise the channel.
vibe_approach: From the bay the site looks like solid mangrove until the tide reaches the right point. Then one mouth is darker than the others.
vibe_senses: Water sucks through the roots at the turn of the tide. Insects sound and no human sound is heard. At the mouth of the right channel the smell changes from salt to tannin.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest is to run the navigable mouth inside its ninety minutes. Another is to prevent the channel being marked.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM40 · tier-3; LM49 · tier-3; RS-line · tier-2
why_site_won: isthmus in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 85 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Four channel mouths open off the bay. One is navigable for ninety minutes at the top of the tide.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a shortcut that halves a journey, on a schedule

name: Bright-Throat Village
why_founding: The Bright-Throat tribe brokers alliances between tribes and works fine crafts. The village stands on the mangrove wall above Oliis Bay. The tribe has brokered the settlements that followed each of the region's catastrophes.
why_site_advantages: The village is a platform village that stands clear of the tide on the mangrove wall. One stair leads down to a beach landing. The whole approach to Lilmoth can be seen from the dry and defensible site.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers pursue diplomacy and craft. Other tribes come to Bright-Throat because of its Listening-Tree and its chimes. The Bright-Throat tribe does not go to the other tribes.
why_pressures: Every trading party on Oliis Bay wants Bright-Throat's endorsement. Keeping neutral is expensive for the tribe.
why_would_change_if: Taking a side in the Lilmoth–An-Xileel quarrel would cost the tribe its role as broker. The tribe is known for that role.
vibe_silhouette: Long lashed platforms stand on mangrove trunks and rise in three levels up the wall. Dyed cloth hangs on every rail. One stair goes down to the sand.
vibe_palette: The rock is warm ochre. The chime frames are painted. The bay below is blue.
vibe_materials: The houses are built of shack-kit plank and cane and stand on a dry rock bench with no stilts and no mud. The rock shelf is the floor and the walkways are lashed. Bone and tin hang from the painted hardwood chime frames.
vibe_signature_feature: Houses stand on a cliff bench. Tuned bone and tin chimes hang from the houses. The chimes can be heard over the water well before the houses are visible.
vibe_condition: The village is dry, sound and comfortable. Little rots on the bench. The carpentry is the best work in Murkmire.
vibe_approach: From the water the stair is seen first, then the platforms above it. From inland the top deck is underfoot before the village is seen.
vibe_senses: Tuned chimes can be heard half a mile over water. Wind blows off the bay. The dry rock stays warm. Cooking smoke rises in a straight line.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An endorsement from Bright-Throat can be bought, earned or exposed. The whole bay treats Bright-Throat as neutral.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM83 · tier-3; LM90 · tier-3; LQ31 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla (+1.31).
player_purpose_hook: The Bright-Throat tribe will broker for an outsider. The other bay villages will not broker for an outsider.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: commands the bay approach to Lilmoth; one stair to the water

name: The Ash Cairns
why_founding: The dead of the western end of the Great Burn lie in the cairns. They lie where they were found. There were too many dead to carry.
why_site_advantages: The site is a rise at the edge of the ash plain. It was the first ground that did not burn.
why_occupants_motive: Grave-singers still come to the cairns. They keep the count and recite it. The count is not a round number.
why_pressures: Poles will not stand in ash. The dead here are marked in stone. The mourners who come resent the compromise.
why_would_change_if: The place does not change. That is the purpose of the cairns.
vibe_palette: The stone is grey. The ash is white. One tree is green.
vibe_signature_feature: Two hundred low stone cairns stand in rows on the edge of an ash plain. Each cairn has a plain grave-pole laid flat across it. The poles are not driven into the ground.
player_purpose_hook: Two hundred cairns stand on the edge of the ash plain. Grave-singers still come to count them.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'mass-grave-memorial' stays active at 'slaughter-memorial'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

name: The Overpass
why_founding: The roots and branches of two great trees meet forty feet above a channel. The channel is too dangerous to swim. The crossing was obvious to the villagers.
why_site_advantages: The canopy touches across the channel here. Six kilometres separate this crossing from the next such crossing.
why_occupants_motive: The villages on both banks maintain the crossing. They renew the lashings every dry season.
why_pressures: The channel below is home to the crocodile stock. The crocodiles make the crossing necessary.
why_would_change_if: Losing either tree would end the crossing. Every journey between the banks would then take a day longer.
vibe_palette: The canopy is green. The lashing is pale. The water below is dark.
vibe_signature_feature: A living root-and-branch bridge has lashed handlines. It stands forty feet above the water. Crocodiles are visible in the water.
vibe_mood: The crossing is exhilarating. The people who live here find it routine.
player_purpose_hook: A living root bridge stands forty feet over water that crocodiles occupy. The alternative to the bridge is swimming.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'canopy-crossing' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a shortcut between two routes

name: Chasepoint
why_founding: Chasepoint is an Imperial road stage that the Legion built. The wreck-salvage families of the coast keep the stage now. Soulrest is the nearest town, a short walk away. Lore names Chasepoint as the neighbour east of Soulrest.
why_site_advantages: Chasepoint stands on the last firm ground before the coast road turns inland. The sea lies to the south, out of sight of the stage. Wreckage from the Southern Sea comes ashore on the coast to the south.
why_occupants_motive: Salvage rights at Chasepoint are hereditary. The families guard these rights closely. They dry recovered rope and cordage in the stage's old stable.
why_pressures: No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries. Two families each claim the keeper's office. The roof is Argonian reed thatch on Imperial walls.
why_would_change_if: A revived coast road with paid stage-keepers would make Chasepoint a proper town again.
vibe_silhouette: The Imperial way-station has a straight ridge and an Argonian reed roof. A square yard wall stands beside it.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey plaster, rubble stone and bleached driftwood.
vibe_materials: The walls are Imperial grey plaster over a rubble core. Argonian reed thatch covers them. The families call the thatched roof a bodge. The yard stacks are ships' timber cut in other provinces.
vibe_signature_feature: An Imperial way-station has an Argonian reed roof. Its yard holds stacks of ships' timber cut in other provinces.
vibe_condition: The stage is sound but scavenged. The pantiles are gone. The families replaced the roof with local reed. The rest of the building is Imperial and holds.
vibe_approach: The square yard wall shows through the scrub from the road bend. The reed roof shows that Argonians hold the building now.
vibe_senses: Road traffic passes on the track. The sea lies south, two fields away, out of sight. The plaster is wet. The timber stacks smell of tar.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A salvage lot can be traced to its ship. The ship's owners do not know it sank.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM38 · tier-3; LM56 · tier-3; LM57 · tier-3; LM62 · tier-3; LQ29 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 27 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.hammock-village-murkmire (+0.77).
player_purpose_hook: Chasepoint is a wreck-salvage settlement at the road bend. A salvage stall sells goods recovered from wrecks in the past week.
watch_reason: An unclaimed wreckers' station where the families answer for themselves. No office stands here.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: day-travel spacing along a road

name: The Chime Line
why_founding: The chime-makers of Bright-Throat built a signal line from their craft. A line of tuned frames runs along the bay. Short messages sent along the line travel faster than any boat.
why_site_advantages: The frames stand on the ridge and headland points. The wind there is reliable. The next frame is audible from each point.
why_occupants_motive: Lilmoth and Bright-Throat jointly pay the keepers. This arrangement is not repeated at any other place.
why_pressures: The code is limited to about forty phrases. The fishing families have learned to hear the code. Privacy is impossible.
why_would_change_if: A silent season comes from no wind or a broken frame. The whole warning system of the bay falls silent.
vibe_palette: The colours are bone white, tin grey and sky.
vibe_signature_feature: A tall tuned bone-and-tin chime frame stands on a headland. The next frame is just visible and audible on the right wind.
player_purpose_hook: A message passes along the tuned frames of the bay faster than any hull can sail. The code has forty phrases. Everyone on the coast can hear the phrases.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'courier-relay' runs 10 province-wide against a countBand of 7-9. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

name: The Cinder Hermit
why_founding: The hermit is an exile from Ashfield. The hermit took the ash plain because pursuers stop at the ash line.
why_site_advantages: The home is a void in the ash crust with a roof over it. It is warm and dry. It is effectively invisible.
why_occupants_motive: The hermit avoids all company. The hermit trades knowledge of where the ground is safe for food.
why_pressures: The ground under the hut is not stable. The hermit knows where the ground gives.
why_would_change_if: A collapse would kill the hermit. The district would lose its only map of the voids.
vibe_palette: A fire is the only light.
vibe_signature_feature: A roof at ground level covers a burnt-out peat void. Cane markers stand across the plain in a pattern. Only the hermit can read the pattern.
player_purpose_hook: A hermit lives under the ash crust and knows which ground will hold. The hermit gives that knowledge for food.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'hermit-hut' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design

name: Cinderhome
why_founding: The Great Burn's peat network runs underground from Stormhold to Soulrest. The village sat on top of the peat network when the ground caught fire.
why_site_advantages: The village stood on a good dry rise. The rise was dry because burning peat lay under it.
why_occupants_motive: A handful of caretaker families live at the edge of the village. They keep the hearths cold as a matter of principle.
why_pressures: The peat is still smouldering somewhere under the district. Where it will surface next is guesswork.
why_would_change_if: A new vent under the caretakers' hamlet would move them permanently.
vibe_palette: The colours are ash grey, ember orange at night and dead white stumps.
vibe_signature_feature: House platforms stand over a collapsed ground surface that is still warm. Smoke rises from a crack that lies half a mile distant.
player_purpose_hook: The village stood on a good dry rise.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'burn-scar-village' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in the burn country of the west

name: The Night Cut
why_founding: The Night Cut is the unlicensed version of the licensed xanmeer trade. The crew of the Night Cut work a xanmeer that has no tending clan left to object.
why_site_advantages: The site is two hours from the nearest channel. It is screened. The crew cut the route to the site themselves. No other route leads there.
why_occupants_motive: A buyer pays the crew by lot, not by wage. The crew know the buyer only through a factor.
why_pressures: The crew have hit something with a live mechanism. The crew have not told the buyer.
why_would_change_if: A single fatality would scatter the crew. The cut would be left open.
vibe_palette: The colours are wet spoil black, lamp yellow and green cover.
vibe_signature_feature: A spoil heap lies hidden under cut vegetation. A shored shaft stands beside it. A crate of finds is already packed and bears a Lilmoth shipping mark.
vibe_mood: The mood is furtive. The crew work a week of short nights.
player_purpose_hook: An unlicensed shaft leads into a xanmeer that lies two hours from any channel. A crate is already marked for Lilmoth.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Umbriel corridor, or at an unwatched ruin

name: The Sermon House
why_founding: The Sermon House is a rest house on the coast road. It is kept for travelling Nisswo. The road between Soulrest and the interior has no other shelter.
why_site_advantages: The house stands half a day from either end of an empty stretch. It stands on the dry side of the road. It has its own well.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper feeds whoever arrives. The keeper preaches at the guests while they eat. The keeper does not negotiate on either.
why_pressures: Travellers who want a bed without a sermon continue along the road. They sleep badly.
why_would_change_if: A second rest house nearby would empty the house at once. The keeper knows this.
vibe_palette: The colours are reed brown, lamp yellow and a black doorway.
vibe_signature_feature: The house is a single long room. The road runs past its open front. The preaching bench stands where every visitor must pass it.
vibe_mood: The welcome is warm and cannot be declined.
player_purpose_hook: A bed, a meal and a sermon that cannot be avoided are offered at the house. It stands halfway along an empty road.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'nisswo-rest-house' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: between villages on a preaching circuit

name: Fourth Stage
why_founding: Fourth Stage was an Imperial road stage counted from Soulrest. People still call it by its number two centuries after the count stopped mattering.
why_site_advantages: The stage stands on a dry rise with a well. It lies an Imperial day's march from the last stage.
why_occupants_motive: An Argonian family keeps the stage. The family rebuilt the roof in reed. The family still uses the Imperial numbering.
why_pressures: The well is the only good water for six miles. In a dry season more people camp at the stage than the rota can feed.
why_would_change_if: A failed well would end the stage. It would shift the road's rhythm entirely.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone, reed gold and dust.
vibe_signature_feature: An Imperial milestone stands outside a reed-roofed stone shell. The number on the milestone has been recut by hand.
vibe_mood: The family maintains the stage out of habit.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A character can settle whether an Imperial rate, two centuries dead, is still honoured when the road's only good water is bought.
why_site_won: isthmus in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 22 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A well, a roof and a meal are available at the stage on the coast road. The Legion set the price two centuries ago.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is a tier-4 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road

name: The Halfway
why_founding: The Halfway is the only roofed building on the long empty stretch of the coast road east of Soulrest.
why_site_advantages: It stands half a day's walk from each end. It stands on the first dry ground past the salt marsh.
why_occupants_motive: The house exists because the alternative is sleeping in the marsh. The keeper prices accordingly.
why_pressures: Salvage families on the edge of banditry use the house as a meeting room. The keeper does not object.
why_would_change_if: A second stage house would halve the trade of The Halfway. It would halve the house's usefulness.
vibe_palette: Smoke brown, mud, firelight.
vibe_signature_feature: The house is one long low room. The road's mud is tracked to the doorway. A strongbox is chained to the hearth.
player_purpose_hook: A roof is available at the house on a stretch of coast road that has no other. The keeper prices accordingly. Salvage families meet in the back.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'tradehouse' stays active at 'soulrest-quay-tradehouse'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

name: The Paid Arch
why_founding: The Paid Arch is an Imperial stone arch that carries the coast road. A local family has collected tolls at the arch since the Legion stopped.
why_site_advantages: The arch crosses a tidal creek, so travellers do not need a boat. The next crossing is four miles up the creek.
why_occupants_motive: The family's toll is small and consistent. It has no legal basis. The family spends the toll on maintenance that genuinely takes place.
why_pressures: Soulrest's council wants the toll revenue. The council cannot take the revenue.
why_would_change_if: If the arch collapsed, the family, the toll and the road would end in one night.
vibe_silhouette: The Paid Arch is one clean semicircular arch. A lopsided reed shelter is built out from its upstream parapet.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey ashlar, reed roof and tidal brown.
vibe_materials: The arch is Imperial ashlar. It is kept pointed. The shelter is Argonian reed-and-pole work. The shelter is lashed to iron rings that were meant for another purpose.
vibe_signature_feature: A single Imperial arch stands in perfect repair. An Argonian toll shelter is built onto its parapet.
vibe_condition: The arch is in better repair than the Imperial work on either side. Livelihoods depend on the arch.
vibe_approach: The road drops to the arch between reed banks. The arch appears whole and unexpected at eye level.
vibe_senses: Water runs through the arch on the ebb. The toll-keeper rings a hand-bell. The air smells of tidal mud. Cart iron rings on stone.
player_purpose_hook: Travellers can pay the family at the arch. The alternative is to wade a tidal creek four miles off the route.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight

name: Cold Light
why_founding: Imperial harbour works lit the Topal approach for four centuries. The oil contract ended with the province.
why_site_advantages: Cold Light stands on the highest headland on the bay approach. Few structures in the province break the canopy line. This tower is one of them.
why_occupants_motive: The lighthouse is unmanned. A Soulrest chandler still bills the council for lamp oil that he does not deliver.
why_pressures: The lantern glass is gone. The stair is sound. Whoever relights the lantern decides who profits from the bar.
why_would_change_if: Relighting the lantern would end the false light on the Long Bar. It would also make the Soulrest approach safe.
vibe_silhouette: The tower is a squat cylinder with a dark glazed head. It stands on the highest headland and breaks the canopy line. The lantern is unlit.
vibe_palette: The palette is lime render gone green, rust streaks and a black basalt plinth.
vibe_materials: The tower is lime render over basalt rubble. It has an iron lantern frame and salt-pitted bronze. The tower has stayed free of reed, cane and lashing for two hundred years.
vibe_signature_feature: Cold Light is a squat Imperial tower with a dead lantern room. It has the longest sightline on the south-west coast.
vibe_condition: The tower is structurally sound and its lantern is dead. The glazing is half gone. The lamp gear is looted. The stair is intact from the foot to the lantern room.
vibe_approach: From the sea approach the tower shows for four miles as a pale mark on a green headland. From the land it cannot be seen until a visitor is at its base.
vibe_senses: Wind is rare here, but it blows at the tower. The sea breaks on the rocks at the foot of the headland. The lantern room smells of rust. Loose glazing clicks.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest opportunity is to relight the lantern. The person who relights it decides who profits from the bar.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 88 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'headland' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: From the dead lighthouse the whole bay approach can be seen. The view includes the sites that the wreckers use.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: one per hazardous approach

name: The Collections Bond
why_founding: The Collections Bond is Cyrodilic Collections' Lilmoth store. It holds antiquities that the company has shipped abroad. It also holds antiquities that the company never had permission to ship.
why_site_advantages: The building is one of the intact Imperial buildings near the wall. It is dry and defensible. It has a water gate for crates.
why_occupants_motive: A resident agent and two guards staff the store. The store's catalogue does not match the shelves.
why_pressures: Half the tribes of Murkmire have a claim on something in the store. Cyrodilic Collections knows the list of claims.
why_would_change_if: A repatriation ruling by the council would empty the store. The ruling would set a precedent across the province.
vibe_palette: The palette is crate pine, brass seal and lamp shadow.
vibe_signature_feature: The store has Imperial vaulted storerooms of crated antiquities. Each crate is stencilled with a find-site that the local villages can read.
player_purpose_hook: The store holds crated antiquities behind an Imperial water gate. Its catalogue does not match the shelves.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'bonded-warehouse' runs 7 province-wide against a countBand of 4-6. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: attached to a port or a wharf

name: The Murkmire Field Station
why_founding: The Murkmire Field Station is Cyrodilic Collections' forward station for the Murkmire xanmeer survey. It is a foreign presence that the Argonians contest by argument and not by fighting.
why_site_advantages: The station is central to four xanmeers. It stands on firm ground with a boat landing and a defensible single approach.
why_occupants_motive: Surveyors and a local guide contingent live at the station. The guides set most of the actual rules. The two sides argue permanently about which finds may be lifted.
why_pressures: The guides have a veto in practice and none on paper. The paperwork is starting to matter.
why_would_change_if: A single unauthorised lift would end the guides' cooperation. The station would end at the same moment.
vibe_palette: The palette is canvas cream, drawing ink and green shade.
vibe_signature_feature: A stilted survey hut holds a drafting table under a canvas fly. A rack of numbered finds stands beside it. The guides count the finds every evening.
player_purpose_hook: Surveyors and guides count each night which finds may be lifted. Work is available for either side of that argument.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The province has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately near something interesting and far from help

name: The Snapping Pens
why_founding: Crocodiles are farmed at the Snapping Pens for hide and meat. They are chiefly sold to villages that want a defended water approach.
why_site_advantages: The creek can be gated at both ends. Tidal flushing keeps the pens clean.
why_occupants_motive: Breeding stock is the valuable part. A village that buys a pair has bought a wall.
why_pressures: Escapes are frequent and deniable. Escapes are very bad for the neighbours.
why_would_change_if: An escape into Lilmoth's approach channels would end the trade by decree.
vibe_palette: The palette is brown water, grey hide and bleached stake.
vibe_signature_feature: A gated creek is divided into numbered pens by stake fences. Feeding platforms stand above each pen. The platforms are open at the edges.
player_purpose_hook: Breeding stock is sold to villages that want a defended channel. The feeding platforms are open at the edges.
