name: The Drowned Byre
why_founding: A herd of water-adapted guar is pastured on submerged weed meadows. The byre stands where the fodder is.
why_site_advantages: The byre stands on a shallow weed flat in two metres of clear water. The firm bottom lets the animals stand.
why_occupants_motive: The herders swim their rounds. The stock is worth more than any dry-land herd in the district. The stock grazes at no cost to the herders.
why_pressures: If a ripper-eel gets into the flat, the herders lose a season's calves.
why_would_change_if: Silting of the flat would kill the weed. It would end the whole practice.
vibe_palette: The palette is clear green water, pale weed and wet grey hide.
vibe_signature_feature: Feeding racks and a stock pen stand in open water. The herd's backs break the surface as they graze the bottom.
player_purpose_hook: A guar herd grazes the bottom in two metres of clear water. The herders swim their rounds.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'guar-byre' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: serves a coastal settlement's transport

name: The Clutch Camp
why_founding: The Clutch Camp works the wamasu and crocodile nesting grounds for eggs. The eggs are worth more than the animals.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands between three nesting grounds. It is screened from view. A fast water route leads out to Alten Meerhleel.
why_occupants_motive: Egg money is very good. The risk comes entirely from the animals and not from any law.
why_pressures: Taking wamasu eggs draws the adult. The adult curses the water for a hundred paces.
why_would_change_if: If a single wamasu followed the poachers home, the camp would end.
vibe_palette: The palette is straw gold, netting grey and green shade.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp consists of packed straw crates under netting. Eggs of three different species are sorted by size. The poachers keep a very careful fire.
player_purpose_hook: The camp holds three nesting grounds' worth of eggs under netting. A fast water route leads out to Alten Meerhleel.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'poacher-camp' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: just outside a village's watched ground

name: Fort Ninth Legion
why_founding: Fort Ninth Legion was built for the Expeditionary Force, which was sent to quell the 3E 427 uprisings. The Legion abandoned it when the province was lost six years later.
why_site_advantages: The fort stands on the rise that commands the road from the plantations to the port. The uprising used that road.
why_occupants_motive: The fort is collapsed and roofless. A poacher crew winters in the gatehouse.
why_pressures: The tribes emptied the fort's armoury. Some of the weapons that the tribes took are still in circulation.
why_would_change_if: If a faction refortified the fort, it would immediately become a regional power.
vibe_palette: The palette is rubble grey, thorn green and rust.
vibe_signature_feature: The Legion fort's walls are down. The gatehouse still stands. The eagle above the arch is uncut.
player_purpose_hook: A Legion fort has its walls down and its gatehouse standing. A poacher crew winters in the arch.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'abandoned-fort' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 2-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a dead road

name: The Wet Camp
why_founding: The Wet Camp holds households from two villages. Their ground flooded permanently three seasons ago. The households are still awaiting resettlement.
why_site_advantages: The camp is on the nearest dry rise to their lost fields. It is within reach of the fair.
why_occupants_motive: The households intend to go back. The water remains.
why_pressures: The council of Soulrest refuses to grant land. The inland villages refuse to absorb the households. The camp is becoming permanent architecture.
why_would_change_if: A land grant would turn the camp into a village overnight. That is why the council of Soulrest has withheld the grant.
vibe_palette: The palette is tarpaulin grey, salvaged plank and mud.
vibe_signature_feature: Shelters that started as tents have acquired plank walls. They stand in two distinct village layouts side by side.
player_purpose_hook: Two villages camp on a rise in sight of their drowned fields. They wait for a land grant that the council of Soulrest withholds.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The province has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is tier-4 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: just outside a settlement that has not taken them in

name: Ushjek
why_founding: Ushjek is a village that keeps gar as other villages keep guar. The gar are penned and bred. They clear the channels of every other creature that lives there.
why_site_advantages: Ushjek has a network of gateable channels with reliable flow. Gar-keeping requires such channels. Few other places have them.
why_occupants_motive: A gar-cleared channel is a safe channel. Villages pay Ushjek for the service. The fish are the by-product.
why_pressures: A gar loose in a paddy is a catastrophe. One gar got out three seasons ago.
why_would_change_if: A single loss of control would end the trade. It would end the village's welcome everywhere.
vibe_palette: The palette is dark water, pale gate timber and silver fish.
vibe_signature_feature: The village's streets are gated water channels. Every gate has a keeper's pole and a counting board.
player_purpose_hook: Penned gar clear the channels. The cleared channels are hired out by the gate. One gar got out three seasons ago.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The province has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: supplies mounts or protection to a district

name: Lights-From-Under
why_founding: Lights-From-Under is a still fen where the water plants light from below all year. The pilgrim route runs through the fen at night because of the light.
why_site_advantages: The fen is a shallow, warm, flow-free basin. The glow requires those conditions. They are rare. A drowned channel runs out of the basin under the weed. The strongest glow comes from the channel's mouth. The gatherers stay clear of the channel.
why_occupants_motive: Gatherers take the plants for lamp-jelly. Pilgrims cross at night because the glow shows the route.
why_pressures: Harvesting dims the glow. The villages ration the take by an argument that they restage each season.
why_would_change_if: Over-harvest would end both the trade and the route in the same season.
vibe_silhouette: The fen has an open, unbuilt surface. The glow forms a shifting green ceiling of light that is cast onto the underside of the canopy.
vibe_palette: The palette is green-blue glow, black canopy and silhouettes.
vibe_materials: The fen is water and little else. It holds a few pole-stages and stake markers for the safe lanes. Argonian lamp-cages are kept deliberately unlit.
vibe_signature_feature: Standing water is lit green-blue from beneath. Poling canoes throw shadows upward onto the canopy.
vibe_condition: The fen is unbuilt and heavily used. The lanes are worn into the weed.
vibe_approach: After dark the glow shows through the trees from a distance of about two hundred metres.
vibe_senses: The fen is as bright as day underfoot. It is almost silent. Poles drip. Frogs call. Harvesters keep their voices low.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest opportunity is to arbitrate the harvest ration. Another is to read the new pattern in the water.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 167 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The water glows from below all night. Pilgrims cross the fen after dark.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

name: The Gold Concession
why_founding: Gold was one of Soulrest's two exports. The tribes halted the gold trade in 3E 427. The Gold Concession is the place where the gold came out of the ground.
why_site_advantages: A quartz reef lies in the low hills behind the burn country. The reef is close enough to the port that ore can be barged down to it.
why_occupants_motive: The concession has no workers. It has a survey office, a stamping floor and three adits. The three adits still run wet.
why_pressures: Gold is left in the ground. The staff of the Soulrest office know this. No local family will put its name on a reopening.
why_would_change_if: An outside company with its own guards would restart the 3E 427 argument.
vibe_palette: The palette is quartz white, rust and deep shade green.
vibe_signature_feature: A stamping floor stands with its timbers up and its iron gone. Cold air flows from three adit mouths into a hot forest.
player_purpose_hook: The concession has three wet adits and a stamping floor with the iron gone. Gold is left in the ground. No local will go first.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'derelict-concession' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: behind a coastal ex-capital, on a dead haul road

name: The Watch Camp
why_founding: The Watch Camp is a guides' camp on the jungle route north of Lilmoth. It is kept because parties that cross without a guide have failed to arrive.
why_site_advantages: The camp is a defensible island of firm ground. It lies at the halfway point of a two-day crossing.
why_occupants_motive: Guides sell the crossing. They do not sell the camp. The camp exists so that the guides survive selling the crossing.
why_pressures: The eastern causeway failed. Traffic was pushed onto this line. The danger of the route has risen.
why_would_change_if: A repaired causeway would empty this camp and this route entirely.
vibe_palette: The palette is thorn grey, fire orange and black jungle.
vibe_signature_feature: A ring of thorn surrounds the camp. A raised sleeping platform stands above head height. The fire pits are placed to light the approaches. They do not light the camp.
player_purpose_hook: The crossing is hired at this camp. The alternative is a two-day jungle route that a traveller makes privately.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'guide-camp' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a guided route, day-travel spacing

name: The Plate Yard
why_founding: Haj-mota shell is the province's best shield and roof material. Lilmoth is where the shell is worked at scale.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands on the shore road. It has a boiling pit and a soaking tank. The strand is within a morning's haul.
why_occupants_motive: Shell is bought at the yard by weight and sold by curve. The skill of the yard's workers is to know which plate becomes what.
why_pressures: Supply depends on a moult season that the yard cannot time. Two thin years would close the yard.
why_would_change_if: A shift in the basking ground would move the entire shell trade east.
vibe_palette: The palette is shell brown-grey, black liquor and bone white.
vibe_signature_feature: Curved shell plates are stacked by size against a wall. A soaking tank of black liquor stands in the yard. A shieldwright's bench stands under the same roof.
player_purpose_hook: Shell plate is sorted by curve. A soaking tank of black liquor and a shieldwright's bench stand under one roof.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The rebalance counts 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is tier-4 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: supplies a village's defence

name: Four-Hands Crown
why_founding: Four-Hands Crown is a raised hammock's crown that is given over to the ancestors of the surrounding villages. It stays dry in the worst floods on the villages' record.
why_site_advantages: It is the highest dry ground in a wide floodplain. Every village that can reach it uses it as a burial terrace.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages bury here. Each village has its own sector. The sector boundaries are the oldest agreed lines in the district.
why_pressures: The hammock is running out of terrace. No village will yield any of its sector.
why_would_change_if: A flood high enough to reach the crown would be read as a judgement on all four villages.
vibe_silhouette: A green crown sits on a low rise. Kerb lines quarter the rise. The tops of driven poles stand out of it. The poles are set four different ways.
vibe_palette: The palette is green crown, pale wood and the brown flood plain below.
vibe_materials: The materials are low dry-laid stone kerbs, plain driven hardwood poles, cairns, ritual totems and cut turf. There is no dwelling material.
vibe_signature_feature: A tree-crowned rise is terraced into four quarters by low stone kerbs. The poles of each quarter are driven and dressed to the rule of a different village.
vibe_condition: The crown is crowded. Four villages maintain it to four standards. The change shows along every kerb line.
vibe_approach: In the wet season the rise reads as a green crown in a brown floodplain. It is visible from about a kilometre away.
vibe_senses: Poles are trimmed and driven at the working shelter. Wind moves in the crown trees. Cut earth smells. Offerings go sour in the heat.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Something is working at the far terrace. Four villages refuse to yield ground for a search.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 89 m from the nearest route; no free 'island' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Four villages bury on this single dry crown. Something has been digging at the far end.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: within 1500 m of Xul-Vaat, on the hammock chain whose dead it holds

name: Tzelvei
why_founding: Tzelvei is a village on a wooded hammock. It can be reached only by water. A sickness went through the households in a single wet season.
why_site_advantages: The site is a dry wooded rise in permanent marsh. It is hard to reach and is now harder to keep undisturbed.
why_occupants_motive: The village is empty. The hammocks that fed it are silent. The huts stand as they were left.
why_pressures: Bodies and stores were never moved out of the village. A swarm has taken the granary huts. Something larger dens under the canoe notch.
why_would_change_if: A cleared and blessed hammock could be resettled. No village has offered to settle it.
vibe_silhouette: A stand of unbroken old canopy has a single notch of pale mud at its edge. The canoe rack is rotted and half sunk.
vibe_palette: The palette is deep canopy shade, water silver going brown and thatch gone black with mould.
vibe_materials: The round-hut walls are cracked mud-mother plaster over withy. The palm and reed roofs have fallen in on themselves.
vibe_signature_feature: Hammocks are still slung inside the huts. The hammocks are empty. The fields beyond have gone to reed.
vibe_condition: The village is collapsing under its own weight. The canopy has closed in over the ground that the village cleared.
vibe_mood: The village is still. The huts are still furnished.
vibe_approach: From the water the village reads as a stand of trees. The notch and the wrecked canoes appear last.
vibe_senses: The shade is deep and holds no woodsmoke. Standing water drips. A low buzz gets louder near the granary huts.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 85 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.chasepoint (+0.77).
player_purpose_hook: A sickness emptied this hammock village. The hammocks and the stores were left where they stood.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a ring of satellite hammocks at poling distance; no land approach

name: Head of Tide
why_founding: A river rises just south of Soulrest and runs north-east into the interior. Head of Tide is the last point on the river that a sea-going hull can reach.
why_site_advantages: A gravel sill crosses the channel. The water is deep below the sill and is poling water above it. The banks are firm for transhipment.
why_occupants_motive: Porters break goods that are going inland into canoe loads here. The porters charge by the bale.
why_pressures: Whoever controls the sill controls the interior trade of the south-west. Four parties are contesting the sill.
why_would_change_if: Dredging the sill would destroy the transhipment trade. Dredging would make the city richer.
vibe_silhouette: A hard line crosses the river. Masts and hull-tops stand on one side of a gravel bar. A hundred canoe bows lie on the other side. The cranes of the portage yard stand on the bar between them.
vibe_palette: The palette is gravel grey, hull tar and cane green.
vibe_materials: The seaward bank has gravel, sawn transhipment staging and market tents. The upstream bank has lashed cane racks and pole-stages. The bar itself outlasts both banks.
vibe_signature_feature: Sea hulls are tied nose-to-tail below a gravel bar. A hundred canoes are drawn up above the bar. A portage yard stands on the bar between them.
vibe_condition: The place is worn hard. The banks of the bar are stripped to bare stone.
vibe_approach: Round the last bend, both fleets appear at once. They lie nose to nose across the bar.
vibe_senses: Hulls knock deeply below the bar. Cane rattles lightly above the bar. Porters shout tallies over wet gravel.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Four parties are contesting the sill. A side can be taken, or none.
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 57 m from the nearest route; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A carry into the interior can be hired here. Goods that have just come down the river can be bought here.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: the last point a sea-going hull reaches; within 3 km of Soulrest

name: The Hereguard Terraces
why_founding: The Hereguard Terraces are the engineered half of Hereguard. They have sluices, bunds and a controlled flood cycle. The work is Imperial-era work in Murkmire that still runs.
why_site_advantages: The gradient is gentle enough to terrace. The river is reliable enough to flood the terraces on schedule.
why_occupants_motive: A rota allocates the water. The rota is the most argued-about document in the district.
why_pressures: A single tenant who takes water out of turn ruins a terrace three levels down.
why_would_change_if: A bund failure in the wet season would take the whole staircase in one night.
vibe_palette: The palette is mirror silver, shoot green and mud brown.
vibe_signature_feature: A mile-long staircase of water has levels of different greens. Plank walkways run along every bund.
player_purpose_hook: The terraces are a mile of stepped water. The water rota for the terraces is the most argued-over in the district.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'paddy-works' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in a city's hinterland; owned

name: Hereguard Plantation
why_founding: Hereguard Plantation is a rice estate north of Lilmoth. It is one of the few places in Argonia where Bretons still live. Rice works here because rice wants the flood.
why_site_advantages: The estate stands on a river terrace that floods every year. The flood ruins any other crop and suits rice.
why_occupants_motive: A Breton family and Argonian tenant households live here. A share arrangement binds them. Both sides describe the arrangement differently.
why_pressures: Lilmoth depends on Hereguard rice. That dependence gives the tenants more hold over the family every year.
why_would_change_if: A tenant refusal at planting would starve the city. Both sides have made that calculation.
vibe_silhouette: A high slate gable, which is wrong for this coast, stands at the head of the terraces. The terraces are a mile of stepped water-mirrors.
vibe_palette: The palette is water-mirror paddy, green shoots and grey Breton slate.
vibe_materials: The house uses Breton dressed stone and slate. The terrace bunds are packed clay and stone. The worker village uses Argonian reed and cane. The house and the worker village stand three hundred metres apart. They share no wall or well.
vibe_signature_feature: A Breton stone house with a tiled roof stands at the head of a mile of terraced rice paddy. The paddy is worked entirely in Argonian fashion.
vibe_condition: Both halves are in good repair. They run on completely different maintenance regimes. The terraces are the older and better built.
vibe_mood: The estate is prosperous. Wages, water and rest are all negotiated.
vibe_approach: The paddy mirrors read first, stepping up in flat sheets. The house appears above them.
vibe_senses: Water steps between terraces all day. Frogs sound at the top of the paddy. Clay is wet. The house bell still divides the field day in two.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A credit book can be audited. A taint in the flood channel can be traced. Something fills the old cut early. It can be found.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM12 · tier-3; LM79 · tier-3; LM80 · tier-3; LM81 · tier-3; BC-line · tier-2
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 650 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Breton rice farmers pay in coin and hire outsiders. No other estate on this coast does so.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: holds the crossing that its neighbours must use

name: The Hestra Stone
why_founding: The Hestra Stone was raised for the Alessian sailors who were lost hunting Red Bramman. It stands on the headland from which the fleet entered the river.
why_site_advantages: The stone stands on the headland above Bramman's mouth. It faces water into which it cannot see.
why_occupants_motive: The stone is untended. The pilots of Screen-Watch use it as a navigation mark.
why_pressures: The inscription gives the name of the river. That is the most useful piece of public information about a hidden route.
why_would_change_if: Defacing the name of the river would be an act of policy.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey stone, orange lichen and green scrub.
vibe_signature_feature: A weathered Imperial pillar stands here. Its worn inscription is the sole written record that names Bramman's river.
player_purpose_hook: An Alessian memorial stands on the headland above Bramman's mouth. It faces water into which it cannot see.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The rebalance counts 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is tier-4 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: at or overlooking the event's site

name: Hestra's Lane
why_founding: Hestra's Lane is the shortest line between the Topal headlands. It is named for the Empress whose navy hunted Red Bramman down it.
why_site_advantages: A wind shadow lies behind the high islands. A sailing hull loses way there for an hour every afternoon.
why_occupants_motive: Khajiit and Argonian crews row. They do not sail. They choose when the lane is used.
why_pressures: The lane is on every pilot's chart. Captains still take it because going around costs a day.
why_would_change_if: A patrolled escort schedule out of Soulrest would price the risk away.
vibe_palette: The palette is mirror-flat pewter and black island silhouettes.
vibe_signature_feature: The water is glassy and sails hang slack. Low rowed craft appear from the island shadow.
player_purpose_hook: Dead wind lasts an hour behind the high islands every afternoon. Crews wait for hulls to sit in it.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The rebalance counts 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Archon-Lilmoth-Soulrest-Tear line

name: High Junction
why_founding: Four elevated walkways meet above the mangrove. The crossing platform where they meet has become a place in its own right.
why_site_advantages: Every walkway in the upper district meets at High Junction. The junction stands twelve metres above the water.
why_occupants_motive: A tea-seller works at the junction. A chime-relay peg board hangs there. The deck-keepers collect a toll that they have no right to collect.
why_pressures: The timbers of the junction carry more traffic than they were built to carry. The decks flex under a loaded porter.
why_would_change_if: A collapse of the junction would sever the upper network of the district into four dead ends.
vibe_silhouette: A dark platform-knot stands twelve metres up in the canopy. Four decks radiate from the platform. A rope-lift shaft hangs beneath the platform.
vibe_palette: The colours are canopy green, sun shafts and worn deck grey.
vibe_materials: The walkways are built of lashed timber, scaffold poles and cane decking. Argonian lamp-cages hang at the deck ends. No part of the structure touches the ground.
vibe_signature_feature: A crossing platform stands high in the canopy. Four decks radiate from the platform. A rope-lift shaft drops from the platform to the water.
vibe_condition: The junction is visibly overloaded. It has doubled props and sistered beams. One deck is closed by a rope across it.
vibe_mood: The mood is airy. Noise arrives loudly from four directions.
vibe_approach: From beneath, the junction shows as a knot of shadow and hanging rope. From any of the four decks, the junction appears where the canopy opens.
vibe_senses: The timbers creak audibly under load. The rope runs and the lift block make a steady sound. A tea brazier burns on the platform. Voices come from four directions and always sound overhead.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A broker pays for new timbers. The broker pays before the deck forces the decision.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 60 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Four walkways meet twelve metres above the water. Whoever runs the deck decides which walkway a traveller may use.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: connects three or more water settlements

name: Waits-For-A-Cutting
why_founding: The hist-less households of Lilmoth built and rebuilt this quarter for two generations. A Blackguards cell then took the quarter. The city did not contest the loss.
why_site_advantages: The quarter lies just outside the wall of Lilmoth. The city levies no tax on the ground and keeps no garrison there.
why_occupants_motive: A Blackguards cell holds the shells that the households abandoned. The cell runs a toll on porters who cross the swept circle.
why_pressures: The council of Lilmoth knows that the gang is there. Clearing the gang would take more guardsmen than the council keeps.
why_would_change_if: The council has not ordered a sweep of the gang. A sweep would change the quarter.
vibe_silhouette: A low ragged quarter surrounds a swept empty circle. The roofline forms a ring around bare ground.
vibe_palette: The dun mud-plaster has gone patchy and the cloth is torn. A bare green circle stays clear because the households kept it raked.
vibe_materials: Mud-mother plaster covers scavenged frames. Market canvas is cut for barricades. Wattle is propped up as a checkpoint.
vibe_signature_feature: The old swept circle is still raked at the centre. The gang now uses it as a muster ground.
vibe_condition: The gang uses improvised shelter as a stronghold. Little was built to last, but the gang patches what it needs.
vibe_approach: A traveller walks out of the gate and finds that the buildings continue. A watcher on a rooftop calls to the traveller.
vibe_senses: Low talk cuts off when a stranger approaches. Cooking smoke rises from too few fires. Boots sound on packed mud.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The toll that the cell runs on the swept circle can be broken, bought or replaced.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 88 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The old hist-less quarter lies outside the wall of Lilmoth. A Blackguards cell holds the quarter and runs tolls on the swept circle.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the edge of somewhere that would not admit them

name: New-Root
why_founding: The village was founded around a cutting taken after Umbriel. Households from three stripped villages founded it. The households were strangers to each other.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on a raised hammock above the flood, where the drainage is good. The founders chose the site for the sake of the cutting and not for their own.
why_occupants_motive: The village, its offices and its customs are a hundred and fifty years old at most. The villagers know how young they are.
why_pressures: The cutting is still young. If it fails, the memory of three villages fails with it.
why_would_change_if: If the tree reached maturity, the status of the village would be settled. It would end an argument with neighbouring villages about precedence.
vibe_palette: The colours are pale young bark, new timber and bright green.
vibe_signature_feature: A young Hist stands barely thicker than a person. It stands inside a stockade that is far larger than it needs. The villagers built the stockade for the tree that it will become.
player_purpose_hook: The village stands where the cutting was planted and not where the people would have chosen to live. The villagers have lived with that for four generations.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The province holds 140 records against a budget of 45-56. A stronger in-region 'hist-village' stays active at 'ashroot-village'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

name: Root-Sakka
why_founding: A Murkmire village had a tree that spoke clearly and often. The tree fell silent and the village emptied.
why_site_advantages: The village stood on a river terrace on the Keel-Sakka. The terrace has deep root-water and a defensible bend. The terrace is now overgrown.
why_occupants_motive: Every household has left. The root system beneath the old ring kept growing after the village was abandoned. The galleries under the ring are open.
why_pressures: A pack has denned in the outer galleries. A larger creature holds the deep chamber near the speaking-floor.
why_would_change_if: A new speaking Hist elsewhere would settle the argument that this village used to arbitrate.
vibe_silhouette: A closed ring of collapsed roofs faces inward at a dead tree. Root-mouths open in the ground around the tree.
vibe_palette: The colours are unchecked deep green canopy, rotted grey plank and black root-mouths.
vibe_materials: Mud-mother plaster crumbles off a hardwood frame. The white-worn planks of the speaking-floor are split and sunk into root growth.
vibe_signature_feature: Three root-mouths open into galleries under the old ring. Each root-mouth is wide enough to be entered on foot.
vibe_condition: The huts have rotted to timber and root. The galleries below are intact and growing.
vibe_approach: From the river the ring shows its overgrown, outward-facing backs. A gap marks the old entrance.
vibe_senses: Root-hum carries through the packed earth. Water drips. The air smells of wet timber and animal den.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A creature has started coming downriver from the outer galleries. A hunter can go into the galleries after it.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1169 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, landform, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The village went silent with its tree. The root galleries beneath the village are still open and still occupied.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

name: Keelhall
why_founding: A merchantman was driven ashore in a storm and never refloated. A shore family gathered round the wreck. The family roofed the hull over and did not dismantle it.
why_site_advantages: The hull lies high on the strand above the tide. A whole hull's worth of dry seasoned timber is already in place.
why_occupants_motive: A shore family charges for a dry night. The family sells salvaged fittings from the stern.
why_pressures: The hull is two hundred years old. The keel is going. The roof is reed and the walls are ship.
why_would_change_if: When the keel breaks, the hall becomes a boat-shaped ruin. The family then moves inland.
vibe_palette: The colours are silvered oak, reed gold and sand.
vibe_signature_feature: An upturned merchantman's hull lies on the strand. A reed roof covers it along its ribs. A plank porch is built against the bow. The doorway is cut through the bow.
player_purpose_hook: A storm-wrecked merchantman has a roof and serves as a home. The hall serves the cheapest hot meal on this coast.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'wreck' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6. The over-band types pay out the surplus first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a shipping approach or a hazard

name: The Quiet Tap
why_founding: An unlicensed sap camp works a wild Hist-kin stand well inside the jungle belt. The camp lies four hours past the last village that a warden visits.
why_site_advantages: The camp is four hours from the nearest village. The camp sits on an unclaimed stand. The barrels leave the camp by water.
why_occupants_motive: Sap sells for more in Lilmoth than hardwood or hide. The buyers do not ask about the source of the sap.
why_pressures: The tappers are not Argonian-local. The tappers do not know what they are doing to the stand.
why_would_change_if: If a village tree-minder discovered the camp, the camp would end violently.
vibe_palette: The colours are amber sap, iron black and deep green.
vibe_signature_feature: Tapped trunks carry crude iron spiles. Stacked barrels stand under a leaf roof. Every other tree in the stand is untouched.
player_purpose_hook: Barrels of unlicensed sap stand under a leaf roof. The nearest warden is four hours distant.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The province holds 140 records against a budget of 45-56. The record is tier-3 density fill on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: at an isolated or rogue Hist, far from a village

name: Chuxeth
why_founding: A tribe never left its xanmeer. The tribe holds the strongest fortification in southern Murkmire without having laid a stone.
why_site_advantages: The stone walls leave the xanmeer a single water approach. The old defences still stand. The road from Soulrest to Blackrose passes within sight of the walls but not through them.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe is polite and immovable. The tribe takes no interest in the politics of Lilmoth.
why_pressures: Every faction in the south has wanted the walls at some point. The defences still work. Every attempt on the walls has failed.
why_would_change_if: If the vakka mechanisms failed, the village would be ordinary overnight.
vibe_silhouette: A stepped stone pyramid stands above the canopy. Washing lines and roof-awnings soften every terrace.
vibe_palette: The colours are warm grey stone, bright cloth and black scorch marks.
vibe_materials: Xanmeer tileset stone is used throughout and stands uncut since it was laid. The Argonians added cane, cloth and reed as fittings only. The fittings are hung and lashed but never bonded.
vibe_signature_feature: A living village stands on the terraces of a stepped stone pyramid. Washing lines hang between carved lintels. A discharge-scarred causeway forms the approach.
vibe_condition: The pyramid is old and fully occupied. The stone is unrepaired because it needs no repair. The villagers replace the timber on the stone yearly.
vibe_mood: The mood is domestic. The walls inside have never fallen to a siege.
vibe_approach: A stone silhouette shows above the canopy. The silhouette can be seen from two directions before a traveller arrives.
vibe_senses: Voices carry off the stone, which happens nowhere else here. The defences crackle with discharge at night. Cooking smoke and dry stone dust fill the air.
why_site_won: summit in interior swamp (danger band 3), 341 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A tribe holds a stone fort that it did not build. The walls still work.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: dominates its immediate district

name: Xel-Nahkta
why_founding: A village refused every outside contact since 4E 48. The villagers enforced the refusal at the boundary. A fire took the huts behind the totem line.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on a defensible rise with a single approach. The rise is three days from Lilmoth. Water does not reach the rise.
why_occupants_motive: A Blackguards band moved into the burn scar. The village had chosen the rise for its single watchable approach.
why_pressures: The lookouts of the gang watch the same path as the old boundary speakers.
why_would_change_if: Driving the gang out would reopen the shortest route across the jungle belt. The village itself once blocked that route.
vibe_silhouette: A hard totem line stands rotted and leaning. A burn scar lies behind the line. Rebuilt lookout platforms rise above the old roofline.
vibe_palette: Ochre totem paint has faded to grey. The colours include charcoal black and dark timber patched with new wood.
vibe_materials: Burned mud-mother plaster and charred hardwood remain. One xanmeer-stone platform is still used as a meeting floor. Fresh stockade timber covers the old.
vibe_signature_feature: A totem boundary line still has old offerings tied to it. New spear-marks are cut fresh over the offerings.
vibe_condition: The core of the village is burned. The gang patches the perimeter.
vibe_approach: A single climbing path leads to the village. One totem line crosses the path. Lookouts stand above the burned roofs.
vibe_senses: A charcoal smell has not cleared. Cord and shell on the totem line rattle in the wind. Wet leaf lies underfoot.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1240 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.pilgrim-xanmeer (+0.55).
player_purpose_hook: A burned-out village refused every visitor for a century. A gang now holds the village and shoots arrivals on the same path.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: has an enemy; the enemy's ground is nearby

name: Ixtaxh Xanmeer
why_founding: The An-Xileel pumped the xanmeer out room by room. They held it dry with magicks. When the An-Xileel were gone the magicks lapsed and the silt returned.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer sits in standing water west of Lilmoth. Only the topmost chamber stands above the silt, as when it was first found.
why_occupants_motive: The xanmeer is untended. Divers go into it for what the An-Xileel abandoned. The water came back fast.
why_pressures: The lower rooms are silt and not water. A diver who enters them may fail to find the way back.
why_would_change_if: Another pumping effort would reopen the xanmeer. No faction is left with the will or the singing for it.
vibe_silhouette: One square of masonry stands in an empty sheet of water. A rusted iron gantry is still bolted across its lintel.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey silt water, wet stone and orange rust.
vibe_materials: Xanmeer stone lies below the silt. Iron pumping gear and its timber cradle sit above the stone. The iron is a thousand years newer than the stone and is more decayed.
vibe_signature_feature: One stone chamber stands clear of flat water. The pumping gear of a fanatical state party is still bolted to its lintel and rusting.
vibe_condition: The chamber is intact and the machinery is ruined. The party that came to drain the xanmeer left its gear where it stood.
vibe_mood: The mood is abandoned, with the work half done.
vibe_approach: A single square of masonry stands in an otherwise empty sheet of water.
vibe_senses: Flat water makes a low noise. Iron ticks as it heats. Rust and silt scent the air. Underwater is complete silence and the ordered edges of the stone descending.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A survey party can be followed into rooms that are silt and not water.
why_site_won: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 364 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on region, submerged, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The An-Xileel held this xanmeer pumped dry with magic. The silt is back and what they left is under it.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in drowned country; often near a drowned village

name: The Sakka Fall
why_founding: The Keel-Sakka river drops nine metres over a rock lip. The river has cut a chamber behind the fall.
why_site_advantages: The chamber behind the falling water is dry. The chamber is hidden and cool. The fall can be heard at a distance of half a kilometre.
why_occupants_motive: The chamber has no residents between visits. Visitors have used it as a shrine, a cache and a hiding place, in that order. Visitors will probably use it as a hiding place again.
why_pressures: The chamber floods when the river rises. People most want to hide in the chamber when the river is high.
why_would_change_if: If the river's course changed, the chamber would empty and be exposed.
vibe_palette: The palette is white water, black wet rock and green light.
vibe_signature_feature: A dry room lies behind a curtain of water. The room's back wall is covered in overlapping marks. The people who sheltered in the chamber left the marks.
vibe_mood: The falling water is loud enough to cover a shout.
player_purpose_hook: A dry room lies behind nine metres of falling water. Its back wall is marked by two centuries of people who hid in the room.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'waterfall-chamber' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only

name: Sakka Head
why_founding: Sakka Head is the furthest point that a loaded canoe can reach up the Keel-Sakka. A loaded canoe reaches it only in the wet season. In the dry season the head of navigation is two kilometres downstream.
why_site_advantages: A rock sill is a rapid in the wet season and a dry step in the dry season. A level bank beside the sill is used for stacking cargo.
why_occupants_motive: Porters take over cargo handling at Sakka Head. The porters' season depends on where the head of navigation lies each month.
why_pressures: The head of navigation moves, so the porters rebuild the porter yard twice a year. The porters refuse to build in stone.
why_would_change_if: Cutting the sill would push navigation four kilometres further upriver. That change would destroy the porters' trade.
vibe_palette: The palette is wet rock, stacked crates and brown flood water.
vibe_signature_feature: Two abandoned yards lie upstream of the stacking bank. The abandoned yards mark where the head of navigation stood in wetter years.
player_purpose_hook: Canoes stop at Sakka Head and porters take over the cargo. The head of navigation moves twice a year.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'head-of-navigation' stays active at 'head-of-tide'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node

name: Keel-Sakka Landing
why_founding: Keel-Sakka Landing is the first village up the Keel-Sakka river from Lilmoth. The rainforest road meets poling water at the landing.
why_site_advantages: The landing has a firm channel edge with deep water alongside. It lies on the road out of the north gate of Lilmoth.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers take the freight of Lilmoth off the road and put it on the river. They charge a fee for the change of medium.
why_pressures: The chime-relay of Bright-Throat reaches the landing. The writ of Lilmoth does not reach the landing. The families of the landing prefer this.
why_would_change_if: A cart road up the river would end the whole function of the village.
vibe_silhouette: The village is one long horizontal deck line on legs along a single bank. Canoe hulls are racked overhead like a second roof.
vibe_palette: The palette is green river, pale deck timber and red-brown thatch.
vibe_materials: The stilt-house frames are lashed hardwood. The decking is cane and the roofs are reed thatch. Argonian lamps stand at the deck edge. The loading deck is sawn timber and the rest is split.
vibe_signature_feature: A single line of stilt houses stands along one bank. A continuous loading deck runs under them. Canoes are racked overhead.
vibe_condition: The village is working and rough-repaired. The villagers replace the deck constantly. They replace the houses only when they fail.
vibe_approach: Walkers go along the deck into the village from the river road. They reach the deck before they enter any building.
vibe_senses: Freight is unloaded continuously. Poles and hulls knock together. The river runs under the floor. Fish dry on racks and cordage is wet.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A traveller can take a cargo above the last supplied bed. The cargo passes through the gap in the writ of Lilmoth.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM69 · tier-3; LM82 · tier-3; LM83 · tier-3; LM84 · tier-3
player_purpose_hook: The landing is the last supplied bed before the river turns to poling water. A traveller can hire a boat or a poler here.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: first village up the Keel-Sakka from Lilmoth, on the north-gate road, inside 3 km of the city

name: Black Fin Grove
why_founding: Black Fin Grove is kept for Keshu the Black Fin. Keshu the Black Fin is Murkmire's national hero.
why_site_advantages: The grove is a stand of old Hist-kin trees. The trees stand on ground where the story says Keshu mustered her force. A spring rises at the centre of the grove.
why_occupants_motive: Four villages keep the grove by rota. Each of the four villages claims the grove as its own.
why_pressures: The story of Keshu has four incompatible versions. The villages keep the rota so that they never have to settle which version is true.
why_would_change_if: A definitive account of the story would give the grove to one village. The other villages would then start a feud.
vibe_silhouette: The grove is a close stand of old tree crowns. One pale muster-stone shows at ground level through the trunks. Four offering racks stand so that no two are in the same view.
vibe_palette: The colours of the grove are deep shade, moss and four different cloth colours.
vibe_materials: The grove is made of living trees and moss. One dressed muster-stone stands among the trees. The four racks are of four different woods and four different cloths. No two racks touch. They share no structure.
vibe_signature_feature: A muster-stone stands at the centre of a grove of old trees. Four separate offering racks stand around the muster-stone. No rack is within reach of another.
vibe_condition: Four parties maintain the grove with reverence. The four parties will not share a rota. The four racks are immaculate. The path is neglected.
vibe_approach: Visitors find the grove where the light drops and the ground clears, since the path carries no marker.
vibe_senses: The shade is deep and cool. A spring runs at the centre. Four different incenses burn on separate air. Visitors keep their voices low.
why_site_won: enclosed clearing in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1218 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Murkmire's hero mustered her force at this grove. The keeper decides who may see what Keshu left.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a regional centre; routes converge on it

name: The Moorings
why_founding: Households could not get shore rights near Soulrest. They built on the water, where no landholder could charge them ground rent.
why_site_advantages: The inner lagoon is sheltered and holds two metres of still water. Mooring posts were already driven there for the salt trade.
why_occupants_motive: The households live rent-free in sight of the city. The mooring fee is a fraction of the cost of a shore plot.
why_pressures: The council has twice tried to tax the moorings. The council has twice failed to define a mooring.
why_would_change_if: A legal definition of a mooring as a dwelling would end the settlement.
vibe_palette: The colours of the moorings are wet timber, laundry colour and still green water.
vibe_signature_feature: Twenty platform houses are moored in a loose ring. Canoes use the gaps between the houses as streets.
player_purpose_hook: Twenty houses are moored beyond the reach of ground rent.
deferred_why: The Moorings are parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'raft-village' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 2-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: has two or three fixed moorings keyed to the flood cycle

name: Lighter Flotilla
why_founding: Lilmoth stands on firm ground near shallow water, so large ships cannot dock. Crews lighter goods ashore from the large ships. The lighter crews live aboard their boats at permanent moorings. The moorings lie beside the lighter quay, on the way out to the anchorage.
why_site_advantages: The moorings lie in sheltered estuary water off the east bank of Lilmoth's ground, beside the lighter quay. The moorings are out of the tariff line.
why_occupants_motive: The lighter crews control the link between deep-water hulls and the city. The crews know what that link is worth.
why_pressures: The council tried to license lightering. The attempt caused a two-week stoppage. Neither the council nor the crews want to repeat the stoppage.
why_would_change_if: A dredged deep-water channel would end the flotilla. The channel would also end the city's hold on its own trade.
vibe_silhouette: The flotilla is a timber pier off the east bank of Lilmoth's ground, with a line of masts along its south side. The tall trade ship lies alongside the pier head.
vibe_palette: The colours of the flotilla are tarred hulls, pale furled canvas and brown estuary water.
vibe_materials: A timber pier on piles runs out from the bank. Tarred working hulls lie bow-in along its south side, some with their sails furled on the yards. Plank ferries are moored singly along its north side. A short landing stage runs from the end of the Lilmoth track over the reed shallows to the pier foot.
vibe_signature_feature: Five working hulls are moored as houses along one timber pier. The market is held on four plank-ferry rafts on the other side of the pier. The Alten Meerhleel trade ship lies alongside the pier head. A lighter lies alongside the pier's north side.
vibe_condition: Every hull is afloat and in use. Few of the hulls would pass a sea survey. The moorings have not shifted in years.
vibe_approach: From the bank the flotilla looks like a moored fleet. A timber pier runs between the bows and the market rafts.
vibe_senses: Gangplanks and gear knock all night. Rigging creaks. Crews cook on deck. The air smells of tar, bilge and estuary.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A courier can carry the licensing offer between the council and the crews. The crews can stop the port.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: TG04 · tier-2; LM08 · tier-3; LM23 · tier-3
why_site_won: Reseated (pending: walk-12 re-site of the Lighter Flotilla, owner confirms in the walk-12 packet): The record pins the flotilla off Lilmoth's lighter quay. The first dot stood in a swamp pocket across water to the north, off Lilmoth's landmass. The new dot stands on the east coast of Lilmoth's own ground: a pier runs east from the bank into water 1 to 4 m deep, 50 m clear of the divers' yard, with the trade ship alongside the pier head beside the lighter quay.
plot_facts_landform: reseated (pending: walk-12 re-site of the Lighter Flotilla, owner confirms in the walk-12 packet)
player_purpose_hook: The crews who move every cargo in the bay live aboard these hulls. Their living comes from the tariff.
watch_reason: The flotilla speaker holds the Reed-Sail Compact's order aboard; the Compact assesses the Owing on this coast.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: trades with a shore settlement in which it does not live

name: Lilmoth
why_founding: The Slaughter of 4E 48 destroyed the old city of Lilmoth. Argonians rebuilt Lilmoth after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast. The rebuilt city is smaller and lower than the city that it replaced.
why_site_advantages: Lilmoth stands on firm ground at the head of the estuary, with shallow water about 128 m from its centre. The lighter quay runs out into the shallows. Big ships anchor out in Oliis Bay and lightermen bring their cargo ashore by lighter, a trade that supports the city.
why_occupants_motive: A reconstituted merchant council governs Lilmoth by tariff. The council refuses to appoint a ruler, because the last faction to hold sole power destroyed the city.
why_pressures: Lilmoth is hostile to the An-Xileel successor state. The merchants of the bay must trade through Lilmoth. The city stands over the mass grave of the drowned Imperial city.
why_would_change_if: Lilmoth has its own Hist tree, the third Hist. If the third Hist spoke to one faction alone, every institution in Lilmoth would fail. The world rules forbid the third Hist from favouring one faction.
vibe_silhouette: Lilmoth rises in three tiers of platform-decks and stilt-towers. It stands on firm ground near shallow water. Its skyline is all verticals and washing-lines, broken by one squat Imperial gate-tower that the rebuilders could not pull down.
vibe_palette: The timber is wet and grey, with a green cast of mould on the walls. Gold lamp-light shines in the upper walkways. Still black water lies beside the city and under the quay, with the drowned Imperial quarter under the floor.
vibe_materials: Argonian work covers the city above the waterline, built of lashed stilt timber and split-cane decking. The walls are mud-and-reed infill, the awnings are thatch and hide and the lamps hang in Argonian lamp-cages. Imperial ashlar survives only where the flood left it standing, with no new Argonian work built into it.
vibe_signature_feature: Ninety per cent of the city is Argonian stilt-and-platform work, which climbs high over the drowned Imperial villas. A wall encloses the city, Imperial on three sides and Argonian on the estuary side.
vibe_condition: Lilmoth is a rebuilt city in which every structure is newer than the ground beneath it. Bright deck timber sits over black Imperial masonry. The builders left the joins visible.
vibe_approach: From the bay, travellers see the lamp-tiers first, stacked above the quay. The north road comes down off a rise into the city, where the drowned quarter lies under the floor. Open water lies beside the city.
vibe_senses: Pole-thump and hull-knock sound under every walkway. The tariff bell rings over the quay. The air smells of tar, fish-oil and drying mould. At night the smell of wet stone rises from the drowned quarter under the floor.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Work is available on the quay, in the register and in the drowned city under the floorboards.
