why_site_won: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'lilmoth' (world/sources/anchors); the anchor pixel is the city gate on the main road. The record sits at the solved city centre (cityLayout, owner rule 2026-09-18).
player_purpose_hook: Southern cargo crosses the Lilmoth quay. The drowned city under the floorboards still holds people and goods.
complexity_justification: Lilmoth is a major city on stilts. It stands over the drowned Imperial city that came before it. It has two vertical layers. A wall circles the city. Argonians tend the city's Hist tree and have repopulated the slum. The build compiles from the blueprint schema.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: bay port with a second door (a floating port) across the water
siting_prefs_preferences_density_gradien: city core; the densest civil gradient in the south

name: The Beast Ground
why_founding: Livestock cannot go inside Lilmoth, a stilt city. The beast market sits outside the north gate on firm ground beyond the reach of the stilts.
why_site_advantages: The market ground is dry, level and fenced. Water lies on one side and the road on the other.
why_occupants_motive: Tribes sell guar, lizard-steeds, pen-bred crocodiles and hatchling stock. The tribes will not enter the city walls.
why_pressures: Half the sellers refuse city coin. The money-changers who solve that take a cut of every animal sold.
why_would_change_if: A city livestock tariff would move the market to Alten Meerhleel overnight.
vibe_palette: The colours of the ground are dust ochre, hide colours and red pen-paint.
vibe_signature_feature: A stockade of numbered pens stands on firm ground outside a city that has no firm ground. The market is loud from dawn and empty by dusk.
player_purpose_hook: Guar, lizard-steeds and pen-bred crocodile are sold outside the north gate. Half the sellers refuse city coin.
deferred_why: The Beast Ground is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. It is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement

name: The Cane Yard
why_founding: Lilmoth's crews lighter its cargo and pole the rest. More canoes are needed in Lilmoth than in any other place in the province. Boatwrights build the canoes at this yard.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands at the water's edge. It has a steam pit and a bending frame. Reed beds lie within poling distance.
why_occupants_motive: Families from three yards work one shore. They compete on hull shape and cooperate on materials.
why_pressures: Good cane comes from further away every year. The near beds are over-cut.
why_would_change_if: A reed-bed failure would raise the price of every hull in the bay.
vibe_palette: The colours of the yard are pale cane, black lacquer and white steam.
vibe_signature_feature: Rows of half-built hulls stand on trestles under one continuous open roof. The hulls are at every stage from bent frame to lacquered finish.
vibe_mood: Skilled work goes on all day, every day.
player_purpose_hook: Hulls stand at every stage from bent frame to lacquer. Three families compete for the order.
deferred_why: The Cane Yard is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'boatwright-yard' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: serves a port or a water-village cluster

name: Under-Yard
why_founding: Lilmoth stands on a drowned city. Salvage from beneath it is a licensed, taxed and respectable trade.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands on the quay directly above the deepest of the sunken villas. A stair leads down to a landing at water level.
why_occupants_motive: Crews work the drowned quarter by permit and in pairs. They hand each lot to the yard for valuation.
why_pressures: Some salvage belongs to families still living. The valuers at the yard rule on those claims daily.
why_would_change_if: A find of An-Xileel material would turn the trade into a political incident.
vibe_silhouette: A low open-sided valuation floor stands at the quay edge. A black stair-mouth goes straight down from it into the water.
vibe_palette: The colours of the yard are black mould, tarnished silver and green water light.
vibe_materials: The lower quay is stone. The upper quay is scaffold-and-canvas. Drip-racks and lot-tables are of scrubbed plank. Submerged Imperial masonry shows through the stair-mouth.
vibe_signature_feature: The valuation floor holds mould-blackened Imperial household goods. The goods are laid out in lots. The goods drip. A diving stair goes straight down into the drowned city.
vibe_condition: The yard is busy and grim. The same water has stained everything black to the same height.
vibe_approach: From the quay lane the yard looks like one more open shed. The tables inside come into view only on approach.
vibe_senses: Water drips constantly. The yard smells of mould from drowned houses. Their goods are brought up into daylight. Scrubbing brushes can be heard. A bell rings for each diver who surfaces.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A salvage agent can decide, lot by lot, which goods belong to the living family that lost the goods.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ13 · tier-0; LM01 · tier-3; LM16 · tier-3; LM26 · tier-3
why_site_won: open water in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 126 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, bound, nearPoint; needs 1 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Licensed divers work the drowned city. Divers buy air and sell salvage. Divers hear which villa is not yet stripped.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: always paired with drowned ground it works

name: The Weighing Room
why_founding: The merchant council's tariff is applied, argued and evaded here, one lot at a time.
why_site_advantages: The room stands on the lighter quay. It lies between the water stair and the warehouse row.
why_occupants_motive: Council clerks, lighter captains and brokers share one room. The council wants them in one room.
why_pressures: Law once restricted foreigners to the docks. The law lapsed, but the habit stayed.
why_would_change_if: A formal foreign quarter inside the wall would take half the room's business.
vibe_palette: The colours of the room are brass, chalk, wet plank and lamp gold.
vibe_signature_feature: A public scale stands under a lantern. The day's tariff is chalked beside the scale. Three separate sets of books are kept at the same table.
player_purpose_hook: The tariff is chalked on the wall. Three sets of books are kept at the same table.
deferred_why: The Weighing Room is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'tradehouse' stays active at 'soulrest-quay-tradehouse'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

name: Long Bar
why_founding: Long Bar is a shoal bar off the salvage coast. A false light has been shown there for longer than the Soulrest register shows.
why_site_advantages: The bar is two miles of breaking water on the Southern Sea approach. A beach lies behind the bar. Neither a road nor a village overlooks the beach.
why_occupants_motive: Salvage families stopped waiting for wrecks. They take quiet Southern Sea traders that no port reports missing.
why_pressures: Khajiit crews keep the same lane. They have begun to notice. The Soulrest harbour office would have to act if the wrecking were proved.
why_would_change_if: A working lighthouse on the headland would end the wrecking in one season.
vibe_silhouette: By day a stilted driftwood frame stands on an empty beach. By night a single light shows where a light should not be.
vibe_palette: The colours of the beach are black wet shingle, salt-white bone and tarred rope.
vibe_materials: The camp uses driftwood, salvaged spar and cordage. A stone-weighted pyre frame stands on the beach. Sorting lots are marked out in beach stone, which does not shift.
vibe_signature_feature: A driftwood pyre-frame stands on stilts above the tide line. A beach of sorted cargo is laid out in lots.
vibe_condition: The wreckers rebuild the camp after each wreck. They use the wreck's own timber.
vibe_approach: At night the camp shows as a light in the wrong place. By day the camp is unmarked.
vibe_senses: Surf breaks on the bar. Gulls call. The air smells of tar and salt-rot. The sorted cargo smells of the same sea. Every voice stays below the level of the surf.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An investigator can prove a century of wrecks deliberate. Once the proof is shown, the harbour office must move.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM36 · tier-3; LM62 · tier-3; LQ29 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 61 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'headland' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.mirtis-plantation (+0.82).
player_purpose_hook: A false light has been shown here for a century. The beach of sorted cargo is the proof.
reconciliation_note: Contestable CONFIRMED here (2026-09-02 reconciliation). wrecker-beach belongs to the Soulrest salvage coast — the lore's own economy for this stretch — and mercantile-coast is the only region file whose siting profile carries the ocean and breaking-bar landforms the type requires. No competing claim was found in any other file.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: off the shipping approach, out of sight of the coast road

name: The Talking Hut
why_founding: A survivor of a stripped village walked into the jungle in 4E 48 and never returned. A descendant of the survivor lives there now.
why_site_advantages: The hut lies deep enough in the jungle that arrivals are deliberate. It stands beside water under permanent canopy.
why_occupants_motive: The occupant talks continuously to a person who is not present. The occupant has done so for their whole life.
why_pressures: The occupant's talk includes an accurate description of the Umbriel shadow track. The occupant cannot have witnessed that track.
why_would_change_if: A written record of what the occupant says would be the best surviving account of 4E 48.
vibe_palette: The colours of the hut are green dark, pale sticks and a single fire.
vibe_signature_feature: Hundreds of carved tally-sticks hang on the hut. One voice carries a hundred paces through an otherwise empty forest.
player_purpose_hook: The hut is hung with tally-sticks. One voice talks to the racks. The voice describes a shadow track that it cannot have seen.
deferred_why: The Talking Hut is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'hermit-hut' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design

name: The Cut
why_founding: A Blackguard crew took a dead-end mangrove cut on Bramman's river. The crew uses the cut as a staging point for cargo that the pilots refuse to carry.
why_site_advantages: The cut is a blind channel with one entrance. It is deep enough to float a laden canoe. Mangroves screen it on every side.
why_occupants_motive: The crew wants the river to become a toll road. The crew is prepared to be patient.
why_pressures: Screen-Watch will not deal with the crew. The Rose's ledgered crews think this crew are amateurs.
why_would_change_if: A pilot family that turned informer would end the crew inside a month.
vibe_palette: The colours of the cut are wet black, tarpaulin grey and weapon-steel.
vibe_signature_feature: Netting is slung between mangroves over a canoe berth. A stack of unlabelled crates stays dry on a root platform.
player_purpose_hook: A Blackguard crew stages cargo up this dead-end cut. The crew posts a watch on the water.
deferred_why: The Cut is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'blackguard-hideout' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: answers to a reoccupied prison

name: The Standing Ward
why_founding: A miregaunt keeps the approach to a xanmeer. The xanmeer has gone unentered in living memory. The miregaunt has kept the approach since before the Imperial survey.
why_site_advantages: The ruin has a single dry approach. The only other way round the approach is swimming.
why_occupants_motive: The miregaunt is part of the land. It does not pursue and it does not negotiate. It comes back after it is driven off.
why_pressures: Something that the miregaunt protects or imprisons lies inside the ruin. That hidden thing is the reason to go past the miregaunt.
why_would_change_if: Killing the miregaunt changes the approach. Killing it does not change the door.
vibe_palette: Grey-green, moss, standing water.
vibe_signature_feature: A causeway approach has a single standing shape at its midpoint. Witnesses two centuries apart have described the shape identically.
player_purpose_hook: One standing shape stands at the midpoint of the dry approach. It does not pursue and it comes back.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The mercantile-coast has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: between a route and something worth reaching

name: Mirtis Plantation
why_founding: Mirtis Plantation is one of the plantations that the tribes destroyed in the 3E 427 uprisings. It was burned with its exports still in the yard.
why_site_advantages: The site is firm lowland with river access to Soulrest. The river access and firm ground made the plantation worth burning.
why_occupants_motive: The great house has not been reoccupied. The quarters behind it were dismantled for materials within a year.
why_pressures: The families who burned the plantation live four miles away. The families have not denied burning it.
why_would_change_if: A claimant with an Imperial deed and armed help could reopen the grievance.
vibe_palette: The palette is charcoal black, bright regrowth green and bleached render.
vibe_signature_feature: A fire-blackened colonnade stands in regrown scrub. The field boundaries stay legible from any rise.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A Colovian deed stands against the families who burned the house. The opportunity is to stand between the deed holder and those families.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 35 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.long-bar-wreckers (+0.82).
player_purpose_hook: A great house burnt in the uprisings was never reoccupied. Its export yard is as the fire left it.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The mercantile-coast has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is a tier-2 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in the ex-Imperial agricultural belt

name: Moonmarch
why_founding: Moonmarch is a Khajiit moon-sugar landing on the Murkmire coast. Moonmarch is the province gazetteer's only Khajiiti place-name.
why_site_advantages: The landing is sheltered and far enough east of Lilmoth to be outside its tariff. It is close enough to Lilmoth to sell into the town.
why_occupants_motive: Two families are left of a dozen. The sugar still lands in smaller amounts and less often.
why_pressures: Lilmoth's rebuilt council taxes trade that Moonmarch used to handle untaxed. The trade has moved to Alten Meerhleel.
why_would_change_if: A tariff rise at Lilmoth would refill Moonmarch in a single season.
vibe_silhouette: The roofline is low, flat, wide and arcaded in a foreign proportion. It was built for a desert and stands in a mangrove.
vibe_palette: The palette is faded ochre and lapis paint, sun-bleached timber and green rot. Green rot sits at the base of every wall.
vibe_materials: The buildings use rendered brick and painted timber arcading in the Elsweyr manner. Lapis and ochre paint and matting shades finish the buildings. The Khajiit have allowed no Argonian carpentry into the landing.
vibe_signature_feature: A Khajiit-built landing has low arcaded warehouses in the wrong climate. Three-quarters of the warehouses are empty. A moon-and-crescent is still painted over each door.
vibe_condition: Moonmarch is elegant and emptying. Three-quarters of the doors are shut. The Khajiit keep the paint up on the front range only. Green rot climbs the rear.
vibe_approach: The straight arcade line and its painted crescents read from the water as something imported entire.
vibe_senses: The empty arcades echo. The stores smell of moon-sugar sweetness. Rot sits at the base of every wall. Awning cloth moves in the sea breeze.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One opportunity is to follow the sugar trade north. The other is to save a place-name from an Imperial edition.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM67 · tier-3; LM68 · tier-3; LQ10 · tier-3
why_site_won: islet in firm lowland (danger band 2), 852 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Moonmarch is the province's one Khajiit landing. It offers moon-sugar and Southern Sea rumour. Traders at the landing ask no questions about cargo.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: too far inland for its own logistics

name: Mudfoot
why_founding: Mudfoot is a fishing and cockle village on the Topal tidal flat. It is close enough to Soulrest to sell cockles to the city daily.
why_site_advantages: The tide covers the cockle flat and uncovers it twice a day. Stilts keep the floors dry. The flat is walkable at low water.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers sell fresh cockles to the city and salted cockles to the coast road. The villagers stay off the council's books.
why_pressures: Buyers who all know each other set the city's price. The villagers answer by selling early and low.
why_would_change_if: A harbour road extension would turn Mudfoot into a suburb.
vibe_silhouette: The village stands on legs and its silhouette changes twice a day. At high water it stands in water. At low water it stands tall on a flat plain of mud.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey mud, silver water and reed-brown thatch.
vibe_materials: Houses use long-legged stilt frames of tarred hardwood, cane decking and reed thatch. Cockle rakes and drying racks hang under every floor.
vibe_signature_feature: The whole village stands on legs over a flat that is water at breakfast and mud at noon. Cockle rakes hang under every floor.
vibe_condition: The legs are black and shell-crusted up to the tide line. They are dry and sound above the tide line.
vibe_mood: The village is busy at each tide and quiet between tides.
vibe_approach: At high water the door is reached by boat. At low water two hundred metres of flat lead to the same door.
vibe_senses: Water comes first, then mud, then flies. The whole village works the flat with a rake-scrape. The air smells of shellfish and hot mud.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One opportunity is to prove that the buyers set the price before the boats land. The other is to find who is emptying the boats first.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM42 · tier-3; LM55 · tier-3; LM85 · tier-3; LM86 · tier-3; LQ24 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 352 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Mudfoot offers cockles, a dry floor and a walkable flat at low water. It has the cheapest bed on Topal Bay.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

name: The Wet-Road Hearth
why_founding: The Wet-Road Hearth is a kept fire on the road north from Lilmoth. It stands where the flood makes the road impassable without warning.
why_site_advantages: It stands on the highest point of a four-mile causeway. That point is above every recorded flood.
why_occupants_motive: The two villages at either end of the road keep the hearth. Both villages have lost people on this road.
why_pressures: In flood season the hearth holds twenty people for two days at a time. It is built for six.
why_would_change_if: A raised road would empty the hearth permanently.
vibe_palette: The palette is fire orange, wet stone and brown flood.
vibe_signature_feature: A single stone-floored room stands on a causeway high point. Flood heights and dates are cut into its doorpost. The cuts go back six generations.
player_purpose_hook: The hearth stands at the high point of a four-mile causeway. Flood heights are cut into the doorpost. It is built for six.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The mercantile-coast has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is a tier-4 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

name: The Toll That Isn't
why_founding: The Toll That Isn't is a seasonal camp on the north-gate road. It sits where a channel and a rock shoulder constrict the road.
why_site_advantages: A hundred metres of road have no bypass. Travellers have no sightline before they enter that stretch.
why_occupants_motive: The Naga call the payment a toll. The people of Lilmoth call it robbery. The rate is consistent and negotiated, which supports the Naga view.
why_pressures: Escorted convoys have begun refusing to pay. The Naga of the camp have not decided what to do about the refusals.
why_would_change_if: One killed merchant would turn a tolerated arrangement into a campaign.
vibe_palette: The palette is rope hemp, wet rock and fire orange.
vibe_signature_feature: A rope crosses a road between a channel and a rock. A fire and a tally stick stand beside the rope. Four people stand there and are not hiding.
player_purpose_hook: A rope crosses the road where there is no way round. The rate is negotiable. The road is not negotiable.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The mercantile-coast has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a route with traffic worth robbing

name: Xul-Hakka
why_founding: Xul-Hakka is a Naga village on the inner channels. It raided the Lilmoth road in the dry season and traded on the road in the wet season. That lasted until the households split from their tribe.
why_site_advantages: Deep channel water lies on three sides. A single poled approach leads into the village. The approach links the village to both the Lilmoth road and the estuary channels.
why_occupants_motive: Tribeless Naga hold the water court now. They price every load that moves along the bay-side track.
why_pressures: Lilmoth's council pays for road escorts. The escorts cut into the share of cargo that the camp can take without a fight.
why_would_change_if: A permanent armed escort would force the camp off the track entirely.
vibe_silhouette: A tight ring of steep dark roofs encloses the centre with no outward window. The ring stands over a single defended water court.
vibe_palette: The palette is dark timber, flaking painted scale-motifs and black water.
vibe_materials: Buildings use dark hardwood and bamboo on stilts. Mud-mother plaster covers the landward side only. Stockade poles cross the approach.
vibe_signature_feature: The water court is still used to stack whatever the camp takes off the track.
vibe_condition: The camp is kept functional and not kept well. Repairs are quick and rough.
vibe_approach: A single poled channel gives access. The court comes into view before the rest of the camp.
vibe_senses: Talk carries flat off the water in the enclosed court. Poles and hulls knock together. The air smells of cargo that was rained on elsewhere.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One opportunity is to break the toll. The other is to break the escort contract that has joined the toll without saying so.
why_site_won: islet in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1152 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, hinterland, culture-clump; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Tribeless Naga hold the old water court. They tax the bay-side track from the court.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: near the roads that its tribeless relatives work

name: Xul-Vaat
why_founding: Xul-Vaat is a village whose whole trade is the dead. Its households drive the poles, tend them, keep the register and repatriate for the whole southern coast.
why_site_advantages: The ground is firm peat able to hold a driven pole. The village is central to a dozen villages and set well apart from each.
why_occupants_motive: Every household holds a grave-office. Children learn the register before they learn to pole.
why_pressures: The village sits where the deep-marsh tribes begin. Its pole-drivers travel armed for that reason. The register is kept in duplicate for the same reason.
why_would_change_if: A refusal to accept more dead would force a dozen villages to solve the problem themselves.
vibe_silhouette: The village is small and its outline is enormous. Ordered ranks of pale driven poles run across the peat in every direction. The houses are lost among the poles.
vibe_palette: The palette is pale wood, peat black and red ochre.
vibe_materials: The village uses plain driven hardwood poles, which stand in their thousands. Cairns and ritual totems mark the row ends. Houses use mud-mother plaster, red ochre and wattle.
vibe_signature_feature: Ranks of driven grave-poles ring the village on every side. Each pole is numbered to a register. A visitor may ask to have the register read aloud.
vibe_condition: The poles are graded by age from bleached to raw. The age grades form visible rings out from the village.
vibe_approach: The poles run for ten minutes before the village appears in the middle of them.
vibe_senses: The grave-wrights trim and drive poles from dawn. Peat lies underfoot. The air smells of ochre and wood-dust. The register is read aloud to visitors, over and over.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The opportunity is to reconcile two copies of a register. The two copies no longer agree on who is buried.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: NI01 · tier-2; DQ07 · tier-3; LM25 · tier-3; LM60 · tier-3; LM87 · tier-3; province system · tier-1
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 3), 56 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, nearPoint, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The coast brings its dead to Xul-Vaat. The grave-wrights enter a body in the register for a price.
siting_note: Xul-Vaat is filed with the coast because its burial trade serves the coastal towns. The ground under Xul-Vaat is rootland deep marsh. Its neighbours upriver are Nagas.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: serves 6-12 villages that keep it at arm's length

name: Breathing-Stone
why_founding: Breathing-Stone is a maintained air chamber on the submerged route between the estuary and the inner channels. Divers built the bench in the chamber.
why_site_advantages: The chamber lies halfway along a flooded passage. The passage is too long to swim in one breath. The chamber is a natural dome that holds air.
why_occupants_motive: The divers who use the route keep the chamber. They keep a bench, a slate, a lamp bracket and a rule about leaving oil.
why_pressures: The air is finite and shared. The slate records who is currently below.
why_would_change_if: Losing the chamber would close the route to all but the strongest swimmers.
vibe_silhouette: The place has no exterior and is invisible from anywhere. A lamp-glow shows in a dome of black water. Swimmers find the chamber by touch along a guide rope.
vibe_palette: The palette is lamp gold on black water and wet grey stone.
vibe_materials: The chamber is a natural limestone dome. It holds one cut stone bench, an iron lamp bracket, an oil jar and a slate. The divers maintain the guide rope and leave the fittings as they are.
vibe_signature_feature: A dry stone bench stands in a domed air pocket underwater. It has a lamp bracket, an oil jar and a chalked list of names currently down.
vibe_condition: The chamber is kept up without an owner. The oil jar is full whenever a diver checks it. The reef cutters deny filling it.
vibe_approach: The chamber is reached only by swimming the flooded passage. The first sign of the chamber is light coming down through the water ahead.
vibe_senses: Breathing sounds amplified. Water drips. The air smells of lamp-oil. Dry air feels shockingly warm after cold water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: One opportunity is to find who stocked the bench for thirty years. The other is to find who wrote the last name on the slate.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM28 · tier-3; LM73 · tier-3; LQ23 · tier-3; PP09 · tier-3
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 204 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A bench and a dry breath lie halfway along a swim. Few swimmers can do the swim in one lungful.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: inside a drowned or flooded place

name: Walks-The-Mangrove
why_founding: Walks-The-Mangrove is a mangrove village that was built as a walkway first. Its houses were hung off the walkway after the walkway was built.
why_site_advantages: The mangrove belt is too soft for foundations. It is also too dense for boats. A raised deck is the form that works here.
why_occupants_motive: Every household maintains its own span of deck. The shape of the village shows which households keep their decks in repair.
why_pressures: Three spans are failing and their households have left. The remaining households build branches around the gaps and leave the spans unrepaired.
why_would_change_if: A concerted repair would reconnect the two halves of the village. Without repair, the two halves are drifting into separate villages.
vibe_silhouette: A branching dark walkway runs through the mangrove at chest height. Houses hang off the sides of the walkway. Two spurs end in open water.
vibe_palette: The colours are wet dark timber, mangrove green and tannin water.
vibe_materials: The decking is wet dark timber on driven piles. The handrails are lashed. Shack-kit houses are cantilevered off the walk. Argonian lamps stand at every junction.
vibe_signature_feature: A branching timber walkway runs through the mangrove with houses hung off its sides. Two dead-end spurs stop at rotten decking.
vibe_condition: The walkway is patched everywhere in three grades of repair. The grades run from sound decking to spans that are roped off.
vibe_approach: Visitors step onto the walk from a canoe. The village spreads sideways along the walk and not straight ahead.
vibe_senses: Every footstep sounds through the whole structure. Tannin water lies below the deck. Woodsmoke is in the air. Soft decking gives a hollow note underfoot.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A visitor can rebuild the failing spans. A visitor can also walk the deck after dark to see what uses it.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM88 · tier-3; LM89 · tier-3; LM90 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 66 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, bound; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The village is a two-mile walkway. The walkway is the dry way through the mangrove.
siting_note: The place is bound to the Estuary Stage, which its own siting preference names. When it was left unbound, it landed 4.2 km away in the saxhleel-coast zone. That placement gave a dependsOn edge over the sanity limit.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Oliis estuary crossing, within 2 km of the Estuary Stage

name: The Drake Hole
why_founding: The Drake Hole is a drowned sinkhole in the bay floor. The sinkhole is forty metres deep. A creature lives at the bottom of it.
why_site_advantages: The hole is deep, cold and permanent. The rest of the bay is shallow.
why_occupants_motive: The creature in the hole holds the attention of the fishers. The fishers work around the hole in a circle. The circle shows on any chart of their nets.
why_pressures: The hole lies directly on the natural lighterage line. Every hull on that line crosses the hole.
why_would_change_if: Bay crews will not attempt the hole.
vibe_palette: The colours are blue-black, a cold green rim and a silver bait shoal.
vibe_signature_feature: A circle of open water has no net set across it. A visible temperature line marks the rim of the circle. Beneath this circle lie forty metres of black water.
why_site_won: local tie in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 248 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, bound, region; bound to body.ocean within 60 m; needs 4 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A hole forty metres deep lies in the bay floor. The fishers do not name the hole at sea. A creature lives in the hole.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. That rebalance has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is tier-3 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a boat lane, so the bay traffic passes over it

name: Estuary Stage
why_founding: The estuary is half a mile wide at the road crossing. The ferry is older than the rebuilt city.
why_site_advantages: The crossing is a narrows with hard landings on both sides. Slack water comes twice a day.
why_occupants_motive: The council grants the ferry as a concession, farmed out annually to the highest bidder. The winning bidder sets the fare.
why_pressures: The fare rises every year. The boats do not improve.
why_would_change_if: A rival free crossing upstream would break the concession. The council would then lose its revenue from the concession.
vibe_silhouette: Two hard landings face each other across brown water. A fare board on a post is the tallest thing in sight.
vibe_palette: The colours are painted board red, brown estuary and grey plank.
vibe_materials: The landing ramps are stone-faced. The ferry is a plank swim-ferry. Rowboats also serve the crossing. Market tents stand on the waiting side. The fare board is painted plank that has been repainted five times.
vibe_signature_feature: A wide flat ferry carries a painted fare board. The board has been repainted over five times, each time higher.
vibe_condition: The landings and the ferry are maintained. The rest of the place is only tolerated.
vibe_approach: The road ends at the water. The fare board is read before the ferry is in sight.
vibe_senses: Waiting travellers make queue noise. Guar stand among the queue. The ferry is worked with a sweep-oar. An argument breaks out at the fare board on most crossings.
why_site_won: open water in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 163 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, nearPoint, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'eviction-repair'; needs 1.2 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The crossing saves a two-day walk round the estuary.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage

name: Oliis Pull
why_founding: Oliis Pull is where the whole ebb of the estuary squeezes past a rock spur. The current runs four knots for three hours at a stretch.
why_site_advantages: The narrows cannot be avoided on the river route. The alternative is a day's portage.
why_occupants_motive: Oliis Pull is uninhabited. Boat crews wait on the tide to pass it.
why_pressures: Loaded canoes are lost here every year. Boat crews treat the loss as weather.
why_would_change_if: Cutting the spur back would halve the current. The cut would cost more than the province has.
vibe_palette: The colours are a brown-white race, black rock and a bare mud beach.
vibe_signature_feature: A standing wave forms off a black rock spur. A waiting beach lies on the upstream side. Generations of boat crews sitting out the ebb have worn the beach bare.
player_purpose_hook: The current runs four knots past a black spur for three hours at a time. A boat crew can wait it out on the beach or take it loaded.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'drowning-narrows' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a boat lane; forces a portage or a wait

name: The Cut Reef
why_founding: The Cut Reef is harvested for lime, lacquer shell and building aggregate. It is not harvested for pearl. The stilts of Lilmoth need footings.
why_site_advantages: The reef is shallow enough to work by free-diving. It is close enough to barge the take straight to the city.
why_occupants_motive: Cutters take from the reef by permit from the council. Lilmoth licenses no other harvest in the bay.
why_pressures: The reef is visibly smaller than it was in living memory. The permit count of the council has not fallen.
why_would_change_if: Closing the reef would raise the cost of every new platform in Lilmoth.
vibe_palette: The colours are bleached coral white, blue water and a grey barge.
vibe_signature_feature: The reef is cut into steps like a quarry. Barge moorings lie over the deepest workings. A permit board stands on a post.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A diver can dive the worked steps that the cutters have abandoned.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 5 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The stilts of Lilmoth stand on lime cut from this reef. The cutters are short of divers.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. That rebalance has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The record is tier-4 density fill. It sits on the most over-dense ground in the province.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: worked from Lilmoth’s quay; within 2 km of the city, on the bay’s inner reef

name: Half-Day Flat
why_founding: Half-Day Flat is two miles of Oliis Bay flat. Travellers can walk it at low water and must sail it at high water. The difference between the two is ninety minutes.
why_site_advantages: The flat cuts hours off the coast route for a crew that reads the tide correctly. How much flat the ebb uncovers depends on the tidal amplitude of Oliis Bay. The uncovered distance is not fixed.
why_occupants_motive: Local carriers use the flat daily. Strangers use it once.
why_pressures: The tide reaches the flat from the rear. The tide moves faster than a person walks.
why_would_change_if: A marked causeway would make the flat safe. A marked causeway would also remove the reason to read the tide.
vibe_silhouette: The horizon is flat and made of whatever the ebb uncovers. A line of leaning withies crosses the flat. A bell post stands at each end.
vibe_palette: The colours are silver mud, grey sky and dark withy.
vibe_materials: The materials are mud and withy. The built work is two bell posts and the marker line. The footprint of the route is whatever the tide uncovers.
vibe_signature_feature: The tide uncovers the flat. Withies mark the flat and lean toward the source of the flood. A bell post at each end stops ringing when the water turns.
vibe_condition: The flat cannot bear any building, so it stays unbuilt. Carriers replace the withies after every spring tide.
vibe_approach: The flat opens out with the far bell post at the edge of vision. The near bell is already ringing.
vibe_senses: A bell at each end stops when the flood starts. Oystercatchers call over the flat. The flat makes a sucking sound underfoot. The wind is unbroken.
player_purpose_hook: A traveller who reads the tide right saves half a day. A traveller who reads it wrong is stranded two miles out on a flooding flat.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a shortcut that halves a journey, on a schedule

name: The Anchored Wreck
why_founding: The Anchored Wreck is a deep-water trader. It dragged its anchor in a blow and drove onto the bay flats. It still stands upright.
why_site_advantages: The wreck is grounded upright in two metres of water. It is visible across the whole anchorage.
why_occupants_motive: Lighter crews use the wreck as a marker. They also use it as a smoking shelter. The cargo went in the first week.
why_pressures: The wreck lies directly on the lighterage line. It settles further into the path of the lighter crews every year.
why_would_change_if: Breaking up the wreck would clear the line. Breaking it up would cost more than the council will pay.
vibe_palette: The colours are tarred hull black, grey mud and bright washing.
vibe_signature_feature: A full-rigged trading hull stands upright on a mudflat. Its masts are still up. Washing lines are rigged between the masts.
vibe_approach: The wreck is visible from every part of Oliis Bay.
player_purpose_hook: A trader stands upright on the bay flats. It can be boarded on foot at low water.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'wreck' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: inside sight of the Oliis bay traffic; walkable from the flat at low tide

name: The Ledger Camp
why_founding: Households were turned off their ground for owed labour. They camped at the edge of the ground. Leaving would forfeit their claim entirely.
why_site_advantages: The camp is on the boundary of the estate that evicted the households. It is in sight of their own fields.
why_occupants_motive: Staying is how the households keep their claim. Every day in the camp presses the argument.
why_pressures: The ledger house says the debt grows while the households camp. The households say the debt does not grow. The original ledger entry is illegible.
why_would_change_if: Producing the original ledger page would settle the dispute one way or the other.
vibe_palette: The colours are mud, salvaged thatch and green crop that extends beyond the shore.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp is laid out along a field boundary. The evicted households carried their door-posts from their old houses. They re-erected the door-posts facing the fields.
player_purpose_hook: Households camp on the boundary of the ground from which they were evicted. Leaving would forfeit their claim.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'owing-eviction-camp' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: immediately outside an estate village

name: Turns-The-Pilgrims
why_founding: Turns-The-Pilgrims is the last rest on the pilgrim route to the Teeth of Sithis. Nisswo of the Turning Path keeps the house.
why_site_advantages: The house is a day short of the temple. It stands on the only firm ground on the final approach.
why_occupants_motive: The house keepers house pilgrims free. They preach the decay-sermon at the pilgrims. Most pilgrims come for the sermon.
why_pressures: A rival reading of the sermon is preached three days back down the route.
why_would_change_if: A schism would split the route. A schism would split the house with it.
vibe_palette: The colours are rotting timber, lamp gold and black water.
vibe_signature_feature: The walls of the rest house are deliberately unrepaired. The decay of each year is marked and dated as part of the teaching.
player_purpose_hook: The house offers the last bed before the Teeth of Sithis. The bed is free. The decay-sermon is included.
deferred_why: The record is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'nisswo-rest-house' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: between villages on a preaching circuit

name: Xal-Meht
why_founding: Xal-Meht is a xanmeer with no surviving clan. Pilgrims on the way to the Teeth of Sithis tend it.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer stands on the pilgrim line. A spring flows at its foot. The spring is why the route goes this way.
why_occupants_motive: Pilgrims treat maintenance as devotion. Each party clears one terrace before continuing along the route.
why_pressures: Pilgrim tending is uneven. The unloved terraces are being lost.
why_would_change_if: A rerouted pilgrimage would leave the xanmeer to the forest within thirty years.
vibe_silhouette: The monument is stepped. One edge is hard and swept and the other is soft and green. The swept side is the side that the path overlooks.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone, moss green and pilgrim cloth colour.
vibe_materials: The monument is xanmeer stone with ornament courses. Moss is left standing on three faces. Pilgrim cloth is tied to the stair rails. No additions are bonded to the stone.
vibe_signature_feature: The stepped monument is half swept and half green. The swept terraces are those visible from the path.
vibe_condition: The pilgrims keep half the monument maintained on purpose. The line between the halves has not moved in living memory.
vibe_approach: The monument breaks the canopy line from the pilgrim path. It is one of the few reliable landmarks in Murkmire.
vibe_senses: Spring water runs at the foot. Pilgrims sweep. Cloth moves in the wind. The swept side is hot dry stone. Cold wet stone lies six feet away.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1005 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.insular-jungle-village (+0.55).
player_purpose_hook: The xanmeer has no clan left. Passing pilgrims keep it open. The lower rooms are not kept.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it

name: The Outside Barge
why_founding: Pusbottom's gaming tables moved onto the water when the council had started raiding buildings. The tables have stayed afloat since.
why_site_advantages: The barge is moored outside the wall line and is reachable only by boat. The barge can shift berth in an hour.
why_occupants_motive: The barge's business is dice, obligation-broking and buying debts.
why_pressures: The council knows precisely where the barge is. The council moves against it only when a council member loses badly.
why_would_change_if: A licensed gaming house inside the wall would close the barge. No councillor gains by proposing a licensed house.
vibe_palette: The colours are lamp red, black water and painted deck.
vibe_signature_feature: The barge is lantern-lit and a shallow-draught tender is kept alongside. A bell warns the tables.
vibe_mood: The mood is cheerful. The terms the barge offers are predatory.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A councillor owes a dice debt. The debt can be collected or buried before it becomes civic business.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ13 · tier-0; LM07 · tier-3; LM23 · tier-3; LQ09 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 260 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, bound; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The city's dice and debt tables are on the barge. The barge is moored outside the wall and is reachable only by boat.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'vice-den' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-5. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

name: Quin'rawl Anchorage
why_founding: Southern Sea crews anchor here, many of them Khajiit. The crews keep out of sight of Altmer and Maormer warships. No state looks at this cove.
why_site_advantages: The cove is a deep lagoon behind a headland and has two ways out. The bottom is sand holding ground. A freshwater run enters at the head of the cove.
why_occupants_motive: Half the hulls carry a Soulrest charter. All the hulls carry cargo that the charter does not mention.
why_pressures: Soulrest's council both licenses and disowns the crews. The arrangement is stable. The captains resent it.
why_would_change_if: A Dominion sweep of the Southern Sea would scatter the anchorage to the mangroves in a week.
vibe_silhouette: Six low mastless hull-lines lie in a cove under a dark headland. One properly rigged ship is anchored in the middle of them. The rigged ship looks entirely respectable.
vibe_palette: The colours are sailcloth ochre, wet sand and dark cliff green.
vibe_materials: The shore camp is sailcloth. Beached hulls serve as stores. Scaffold cargo-shears stand on the beach. Every structure on the beach is temporary.
vibe_signature_feature: Six low hulls are moored bow-and-stern in the cove. A shore camp of sailcloth stands on the beach. A chartered ship is anchored among the hulls.
vibe_condition: The anchorage is a camp. The whole camp can be off the beach in three hours.
vibe_approach: Neither entrance shows the anchorage until the headland is passed. Past the headland the whole cove is in view at once.
vibe_senses: The cove has rigging in the headland wind, dogs, roasting meat and tar. Fresh water runs at the head of the cove.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The licence-and-denial arrangement can be put in writing. It can be written for one side or the other.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: RS05 · tier-2; LM37 · tier-3; LM59 · tier-3; LQ11 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 280 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on hinterland, parent, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'relaxed-score'; needs 1.5 m of water; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Crews who keep clear of two navies anchor here. The crews trade off the beach.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: near a shipping lane it can reach and leave

name: Rockpark
why_founding: Pestilence, plague and a curse emptied Rockpark of every business and guild. No household returned. Rockpark's Hist died.
why_site_advantages: Rockpark stands on good firm ground. It lies on the upland road north-west out of Lilmoth.
why_occupants_motive: Rockpark is empty. The Unearthed Equipment Store still blocks the palace gate. The palace still holds what the royal family became.
why_pressures: Rockpark is a day's walk from a living city. It is stocked with five centuries of untouched goods. The taboo against entering holds.
why_would_change_if: A confirmed cure for whatever is in the palace would strip the town in a week.
vibe_silhouette: The town skyline is complete and has no smoke in it. Every roof stands and every chimney is cold. One collapsed store is jammed diagonally across the palace gate.
vibe_palette: The colours are dust grey, faded shop-paint and black doorways.
vibe_materials: The buildings are made of mud-mother plaster, bamboo frame, shack-kit and wattle. All the materials are five centuries weathered. No rebuilding has occurred in the village. The shop paint is original.
vibe_signature_feature: The whole town has its shop shutters closed. The stock is still on the shelves. A collapsed equipment store is jammed across the palace gate.
vibe_condition: Intact and unlooted.
vibe_approach: The road runs straight into the town. The road carries no mark of warning.
vibe_senses: The town is absolutely silent. Dust hangs in the air and doors move in the wind. The streets are empty of birds.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The plague town can be entered while stocked with five centuries of goods. Deeds to the goods are already being sold.
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 768 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Plague emptied Rockpark and no household came back. The houses were left furnished.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it

name: The Rockpark Stump
why_founding: Rockpark was never resettled because its Hist died. The Hist held the memory that the village kept in it.
why_site_advantages: The stump stands in the town's central enclosure, which is still walled. Pilgrims still sweep it. The pilgrims come and do not stay.
why_occupants_motive: The enclosure is uninhabited. Tree-minders from three villages visit annually. They take no cutting.
why_pressures: A dead Hist's mnemic egg is a theological emergency. The region's tree-minders keep passing the problem between them.
why_would_change_if: A cutting taking root here would change Murkmire's whole map of who is owed what.
vibe_palette: The colours are ash-grey wood, green wall moss and bright offering cloth.
vibe_signature_feature: A hollow grey stump stands inside a maintained wall. Visitors place offerings on its rim. The visitors then leave immediately.
player_purpose_hook: A hollow grey stump stands inside a swept wall. Three villages each send a tree-minder once a year.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'harmed-hist' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village

name: Under-Root
why_founding: The gallery is a walkable passage under a great root mass. It stays dry above the flood. People who wanted somewhere out of sight have occupied it for as long as the villages remember.
why_site_advantages: The gallery is two hundred metres of natural passage. It has three entrances and a permanent air flow.
why_occupants_motive: Whoever is currently in the gallery occupies it. The tenancy changes, but the fittings do not.
why_pressures: The gallery floods to chest height in the deep wet season. The flood comes on about a week's notice.
why_would_change_if: A root collapse would close the middle of the gallery. The collapse would split it into two dead ends.
vibe_silhouette: A living tunnel mouth opens at the base of a root buttress. Warm air flows from the mouth. Three worn approaches converge on it.
vibe_palette: The colours are root brown, soot black and green entrance light.
vibe_materials: Living root forms the wall, floor and ceiling. Three tenancies cut niches and hearth-scars at three heights. Lamp brackets are driven into wood, never stone.
vibe_signature_feature: The tunnel is living root. Three tenancies cut hearth-scars and shelf niches into it at three different heights.
vibe_condition: People have reoccupied the gallery continuously for centuries. Each tenancy's alterations cut across the last one's.
vibe_mood: The place is sheltered. It belongs to another owner.
vibe_approach: Warm air is felt on the path before the mouth comes into view.
vibe_senses: A permanent through-draught is warm at one end and cold at the other. The gallery smells of soot and sap. The root hums under bare feet.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A tenant is living in the gallery. The tenant can be reached before the wet season fills it.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 110 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, nearPoint, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The gallery is two hundred metres of dry passage under the roots. A tenant is living in it.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect; that connection is the map

name: Customs Suburb
why_founding: The suburb was the Imperial customs suburb outside Lilmoth's north gate. The An-Xileel looted it when they took the city from the Empire.
why_site_advantages: The suburb stands astride the north road. Every cargo had to pass along that road.
why_occupants_motive: The suburb is unrebuilt. Lilmoth's rebuilt council collects at the quay. The council prefers not to be reminded of the suburb.
why_pressures: The suburb's record room survived the fire. The records have not been read in two centuries.
why_would_change_if: The records would establish who owned what before 4E 48. Several families would prefer that this stayed unknown.
vibe_silhouette: A street of roofless Imperial gables runs ahead. The road still runs dead straight through them. One vaulted roof still stands at the end of the street.
vibe_palette: The colours are fire-black render, red brick core and green regrowth.
vibe_materials: The walls are fire-blacked render over a red brick core. Fallen pantile and iron window grilles remain. Every material is Imperial.
vibe_signature_feature: A burnt street of Imperial offices has the road still running through it. One vaulted record room still has its roof.
vibe_condition: The suburb is burnt and left. It is structurally dangerous and unrepaired. Two centuries of green growth are established inside every room.
vibe_approach: The north road runs straight down the middle of the suburb. The record room's roof is the only roof that reads as whole.
vibe_senses: Wind blows through open windows. Regrowth cracks the render. A wet ash smell remains in the render. Road noise comes from beyond the suburb.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The surviving record room can be read. Pages are being written into the record room.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 93 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, bound; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The Empire's customs quarter was looted in a night and never cleared. The cellars are still sealed.
siting_note: The place's identity is a role in the network. It is the customs suburb astride Lilmoth's north-gate road. It is bound to Lilmoth and that road, not sited on merit (round 4 network-role pass).
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: attached to a living settlement that does not talk about it

name: The Drying House
why_founding: Lilmoth's sap trade produced many people who could not stop using sap. The villages built the house to put them somewhere.
why_site_advantages: The house stands outside the city and upwind, with running water beside it. No sap is within a day's walk in any direction.
why_occupants_motive: Former sap users run the house. The treatment is time, water and work. No supply of sap is allowed in the house.
why_pressures: The city's dealers know precisely where the house is. One dealer funds the house. The keepers argue about the funding and take it.
why_would_change_if: Closing the illicit taps in the jungle would empty the house in five years.
vibe_palette: The colours are whitewash, rope hemp and running water.
vibe_signature_feature: A long dormitory hall has barred windows facing away from the city. A work yard of rope-making never stops.
player_purpose_hook: The house has a dormitory and a rope yard for people off the sap. One of the city's dealers pays for it.

name: Screen-Watch
why_founding: Screen-Watch is a village of the people who pilot Bramman's river. It stands inside the mangrove wall a mile above the river's mouth.
why_site_advantages: The village is invisible from the bay. Every house sits on the channel it watches. The mangrove serves as both wall and roof.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers live on piloting fees. A strict internal rule keeps any two families from teaching the same reach of the river.
why_pressures: Blackguards want the river opened as a road. Soulrest's council wants the river declared a customs matter. The villagers want the river to stay a rumour.
why_would_change_if: A public chart of the channel would end the piloting trade. The piloting trade keeps the village.
vibe_silhouette: The village has no silhouette. The mangrove wall is unbroken from the bay. The village exists entirely inside the wall.
vibe_palette: The colours are root black, leaf green and pale lashed cordage.
vibe_materials: Decking is cut between living trunks and is lashed to the trees with no nails. The walls are shack-kit and cane. Canoe slings hang from the structures.
vibe_signature_feature: Platforms are cut into the mangrove wall itself. The platforms are decked between living trunks. Poled canoes hang in slings above the tide.
vibe_condition: The village is kept invisible. It has no cut lines to the water and no smoke above the canopy. The decking is stained to match the root.
vibe_approach: The village has no line of approach. The first houses are overhead by the time they are reached.
vibe_senses: Bay noise is heard but not seen. Canoes creak in their slings. The air smells of leaf and root black-water. The villagers do not raise their voices.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The river can be kept a rumour. It can be opened as a road or handed to the customs office.

name: Shut-From-Within
why_founding: Its own people sealed the xanmeer when its Hist chamber was emptied. They sealed it so that whatever remains inside stays inside.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer is low and stands on a rise. It is unremarkable except for the door, which its own people closed from the inside.
why_occupants_motive: The xanmeer is untended and its traps are intact. The Hist chamber is not empty, whatever the sealers believed.
why_pressures: Two villages disagree about which of them did the sealing. That disagreement makes them disagree about who may open it.
why_would_change_if: An agreement between the two villages would open it legitimately. It has not been opened legitimately in centuries.
vibe_silhouette: A low stone step-mass barely clears the scrub. One dark vertical seam runs through it. The seam reads wrong from any angle.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone, ochre mortar and a black seam.
vibe_materials: The xanmeer has its original stone and ornament. One course of ochre mortar was laid by hand from the inside. The mortar is the later work.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone door is closed from the inside. The sealing crew's hand-marks remain in the mortar around it.
vibe_condition: The xanmeer is perfectly sound and completely closed. The hand-marks in the mortar are as sharp as the day they were pressed.
vibe_approach: The xanmeer is unremarkable from a distance. At close range the door was plainly closed from the wrong side.
vibe_senses: The seam gives off no draught. The air carries no water sound. Insects do not settle on that face of the stone.

player_purpose_hook: The door was shut from the inside. The mechanisms still work.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

name: The Shut Door
why_founding: The people of the Shut Door closed it themselves at some point after the Duskfall. It has never been reopened. The closing mechanisms were left live.
why_site_advantages: The Shut Door stands on a low rise in the burn country. It is far from any village. That distance makes its closure a decision and not an abandonment.
why_occupants_motive: The Shut Door is untended. Its vakka-stone defences still hold charge.
why_pressures: Two treasure crews have gone into the Shut Door in this generation. Neither crew came out. The lost crews protect the door more than the traps do.
why_would_change_if: A discharge of the vakka stones would open the whole complex at once.
vibe_palette: The colours are cold grey stone, scorch black and blue-white spark.
vibe_signature_feature: The door is perfectly fitted stone with no handle. A discharge scar fans across the terrace in front of the door.
player_purpose_hook: The door is fitted stone with no handle. A discharge scar crosses the terrace. Two crews went in and did not come out.

siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

name: The Slaughter Ground
why_founding: Lilmoth buried the dead of 4E 48 at the Slaughter Ground. The dead were the city's own residents. Lilmoth's tree and the party that served it killed them first.
why_site_advantages: The Slaughter Ground lies outside the rebuilt wall. It stands on firm ground large enough for the memorial. The mass grave under the city lies inside the wall.
why_occupants_motive: Keepers hold a rotating vigil at the memorial. The same rule governs the tree-minders, with no single faction and no single keeper.
why_pressures: The An-Xileel successor state denies that the city caused the deaths. Lilmoth's whole civic identity depends on that denial.
why_would_change_if: Reconciliation with the successor state would require abandoning the inscription.
vibe_silhouette: A long low wall runs across open ground. One tended tree stands behind the wall.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey stone, cut-shadow and one green tended tree.
vibe_materials: The wall is cut grey stone. The names on it are cut in three scripts. One section is deliberately left unfinished and blank. A wattle enclosure surrounds the wall. One tree is planted there.
vibe_signature_feature: Names are cut into a long low wall in three scripts. One section is left blank for the uncounted dead.
vibe_condition: The memorial is immaculate. Keepers re-cut the blank section clean every year. They do not fill it.
vibe_approach: From the gate road the wall looks like a low line. The city lies behind the wall.
vibe_senses: Visitors read the names aloud. The city can be heard over the wall but not seen. The grass is cut. Offerings lie at the wall.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The city council pays to keep the names weathered. The opportunity is to restore those names.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 252 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The Slaughter Ground holds Lilmoth's own dead of 4E 48. The city council would prefer that the stones went unread.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

name: The Smoulder Cuts
why_founding: Peat is the district's only fuel now that the timber is gone. Cutters cut peat at the edge of ground that is already burning underneath.
why_site_advantages: The peat is deep and dry. Cutters can cut it in the dry season. The cuts lie close enough to the coast road to sell the peat.
why_occupants_motive: Cutters work the cool face of the cut and race the fire. A cut worked out before the fire arrives makes a good year.
why_pressures: The fire moves underground at walking pace. The fire cannot be seen. Two cutters were lost last season.
why_would_change_if: Wet-season flooding could quench the whole seam. That would end both the danger and the fuel.
vibe_palette: The colours are chocolate peat brown, blue smoke and scorched orange.
vibe_signature_feature: Drying peats are stacked in neat rows. A haze of smoke rises from the ground fifty paces behind the rows.
player_purpose_hook: Cut peat dries in rows. Smoke comes out of the ground fifty paces behind the face.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in the burn country, or supplying a village's fires

name: Soulrest
why_founding: Soulrest was the Third-Era provincial capital. It stands at a sheltered deep-water landfall. Topal Bay meets the Southern Sea at that landfall.
why_site_advantages: A peninsula wraps the bay. A river mouth just south opens a route north-east into the interior. Islands screen the approach.
why_occupants_motive: Four powers hold pieces of Soulrest. They are a merchant council, an orphaned Imperial apparatus and interior tribes. The fourth power is the river interests who control Bramman's water.
why_pressures: The tribes burned Soulrest's gold-and-timber hinterland in 3E 427. The hinterland was never rebuilt. The capital moved elsewhere. The offices remain with little left to administer.
why_would_change_if: Soulrest would be a capital again if the mines reopened. It would also be a capital again if one of the four claimants finally won.
vibe_silhouette: A long low limestone palace roof stands on the peninsula spine. A customs campanile stands beside it. Argonian and Khajiit roofs form a ragged secondary skyline. Those roofs grow out of and over the Imperial roofs.
vibe_palette: Limestone is salt-bleached and timber is grey and weathered. Wet green mould covers the timber. Khajiit awnings add colour in the dock lanes.
vibe_materials: Two kits stand side by side with no blending between them. The administrative shell uses Imperial salt-cut limestone, pantile and iron-strapped doors. The town that grew through the shell uses lashed timber and reed thatch. The town also uses painted Khajiit awning cloth.
vibe_signature_feature: The Imperial administrative shell holds a palace, a courthouse and bonded stores. An Argonian and Khajiit town has grown through and over the shell.
vibe_condition: The buildings are structurally sound and hollow. Every roof is kept. Half the rooms are unused. Weeds grow in the ceremonial pavement, which is not swept.
vibe_approach: From the coast road the palace roof and the campanile come into view first, together. The harbour is visible only past the mole.
vibe_senses: Sea noise stops dead at the gate. Gulls call in the mole. Four languages are spoken in the dock lanes. Mould and old paper smell in the arcades. Spice smoke drifts from the Khajiit quarter.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Three defensible titles compete for the province's best harbour. The opportunity is to decide which title owns it.

name: Breaking Hard
why_founding: The Expeditionary Force's transports were cut up here for their iron. The breaking began when the Empire stopped paying for them.
why_site_advantages: The yard is a hard shingle slope inside the mole. Deep water lies at the foot of the slope. The slope has enough fall to lay a hull over.
why_occupants_motive: Breakers work the yard. They make more from Imperial fastenings than from the timber around them.
why_pressures: The supply of Imperial hulls is finite and nearly finished. The yard has started buying wrecks off the Long Bar. The yard asks no questions about those wrecks.
why_would_change_if: If Soulrest ever built ships again, the same slope would serve.
vibe_silhouette: Half a warship's ribcage stands in the shallows. It is higher than any hull still afloat in the harbour.
vibe_palette: The colours are iron-orange, tar black and sun-silvered oak.
vibe_materials: Frames are sun-silvered oak. Iron fastenings are stacked by size. Tar, scaffold shears and a shingle hard are in use. Sorted timber lots run the length of the beach.
vibe_signature_feature: Half a warship's ribcage stands in the shallows. Breakers unmake it plank by plank into sorted, stacked lots.
vibe_condition: The yard is perpetually mid-demolition. A hull has been coming apart here continuously for eighty years.
vibe_approach: From inside the mole the ribcage looks like a ship. The planks come off in the wrong direction for a repair.
vibe_senses: Adze and maul sound all day. Iron rings. Tar boils. Bilge water smells strong. Sawdust smells of somewhere else.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The last Imperial hull will be cut up. The opportunity is to decide what the yard becomes then.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ10 · tier-0; LM35 · tier-3; LM53 · tier-3

name: The Broken Bond

why_site_advantages: The bond stands on the quay behind the harbour office. It has its own water gate for lighters.
why_occupants_motive: Squatters live in the bond. A descendant of a bond-clerk still keeps the ledger. Anyone who needs dry floor space this month also stays there.
why_pressures: The ledger records cargo that no longer exists. The ledger lists families who wish that it did not.
why_would_change_if: A council audit would turn a curiosity into a scandal.
vibe_palette: The colours are damp brick, verdigris and ledger-paper cream.
vibe_signature_feature: Imperial iron doors were levered off their hinges. They are stacked neatly inside. The stacking looks as if the theft had been an official act.
player_purpose_hook: The Imperial bond store was opened by hand. Its iron doors are stacked neatly inside. Its ledger is still kept.

name: Soulrest Poling Relay
why_founding: The relay is a post where letters and small freight change from road carriage to poled canoe. The canoes serve the interior river.
why_site_advantages: The relay stands at the river's head of tide. The coast road first touches navigable water there.
why_occupants_motive: Polers work fixed reaches and hand over at the end of each. Each poler carries a letter no more than a day from home.
why_pressures: Three different interests read letters to the interior before they arrive. The senders write with that in mind.
why_would_change_if: A single through-carrier service would be faster. It would be trusted far less.
vibe_palette: The colours are wet cane, letter cream and river brown.
vibe_signature_feature: A rack of numbered canoes stands under a long roof. A board of destination pegs serves as the district's closest thing to a timetable.
player_purpose_hook: Road freight changes to poled canoe here. Three interests read the interior post before it arrives.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'courier-relay' runs 10 province-wide against a countBand of 7-9. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

name: The Divers' Yard

why_site_advantages: The yard stands on the inner harbour. It has a crane frame and a fresh-water rinse. The buyers' benches are thirty paces away.
why_occupants_motive: Diver crews sell by lot. The yard takes a share of each sale. The yard asks for no provenance.
why_pressures: Every lot on the bench is some owner's cargo. The harbour office periodically asks to see the books.
why_would_change_if: An enforced provenance rule would collapse the trade into the Long Bar's hands.
vibe_palette: The colours are rust, salt crust and wet rope.
vibe_signature_feature: Sorting tables stand under an open roof. They hold corroded ironwork and amphora bases. In an average week they also hold one item worth real money.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The harbour office seeks the yard's books. The opportunity is to produce, doctor or defend those books.

name: The Low Fair

why_site_advantages: The fair ground is level and dry beside the coast road. A river landing lies on one side. The city gate lies on the other side.
why_occupants_motive: The tribes do not enter the city. The council does not leave it. Both sides count that arrangement a success.
why_pressures: Both sides periodically try to move the fair to their own advantage. The fair has not moved in eighty years.
why_would_change_if: If the tribes ever entered the city freely, the fair would die. The arrangement would die with it.

name: The Governors' Ground
why_founding: Two centuries of Imperial administrators, officers and settlers are buried here. The graves lie outside Soulrest's wall. The burials follow consecrated Cyrodilic form.
why_site_advantages: The ground is firm and dry just outside the gate. It was chosen to lie outside Argonian burial country.
why_occupants_motive: A single hereditary sexton maintains the ground. The sexton's family has outlasted the government that hired it.
why_pressures: The last burial here was a hundred and forty years ago. The ground rent has not been paid since.
why_would_change_if: A council decision to build on the ground would be the moment Soulrest admits the Empire is gone.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey slab, moss green and raked white gravel.
vibe_signature_feature: Rows of Nibenese name-slabs sink at different angles in wet ground. The sexton keeps a swept gravel path perfectly clear.
player_purpose_hook: Two centuries of Imperial name-slabs sink at angles. One sexton outlasted the government.

name: Long Table
why_founding: Long Table is a quayside house in Soulrest. Cargo is contracted at Long Table. Crews are hired there. The council's tariffs are disputed there as well.
why_site_advantages: Long Table stands on the quay. It sits between the harbour office and the divers' yard.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper sells information at the same table as beer. The keeper treats information and beer as a single trade.
why_pressures: The port's factors and captains drink at Long Table. That makes it the least private room in the city.
why_would_change_if: A council monopoly on brokerage would empty Long Table of customers.

vibe_palette: The palette is beer amber, chalk white and wet-boot grey.
vibe_materials: The quay side has Imperial-frontage stonework, because this is the old town. Argonian fittings fill the inside. No structure crosses between the stonework and the fittings. A forty-foot table of scarfed plank stands inside.
vibe_signature_feature: A table forty feet long dominates the hall. The day's freight rates are chalked on the wall above it. The rates are written in three scripts.
vibe_condition: Long Table is hard-used and profitable. The table is scarred. The floor is worn to a channel from door to bar.
vibe_approach: Visitors hear the rate being argued from outside the door. The shutters stay open so that the argument carries.
vibe_senses: Three languages are spoken inside. Chalk on slate, beer and wet boots mark the room. The harbour shows through the open shutters.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A crew was hired at this table. Their ship sailed and did not make port. The quest is to track that crew.

name: The Sail-Count
why_founding: Staff at The Sail-Count count Southern Sea hulls from a headland. The tally sheets are written in Aldmeris.
