name: Ganthil's Rest
why_founding: Umbriel passed over this village in 4E 48, travelling from Lilmoth. Umbriel took the village with it. What stood up afterwards is still standing.
why_site_advantages: The village lies directly under the recorded track of Umbriel's shadow. The ground is good enough to hold a village. The ground is not worked now.
why_occupants_motive: The dead here do not leave the village bounds. The district lives alongside the village on that basis.
why_pressures: The village sits between two working villages. Every journey between them takes an extra half-day.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the village would restore a road. The road has been broken for a hundred and fifty years.
vibe_silhouette: The village outline is complete. Every door stands open. Every grave-pole is pulled out of the ground.
vibe_palette: The palette is bleached timber, grey figures and sour green ground.
vibe_materials: The timber is bleached and untended. The mud-mother plaster has gone chalky. Pulled hardwood poles lie where they fell. A raw new boundary ditch is cut around the whole village.
vibe_signature_feature: The village has its doors open. Its grave-poles are all pulled and lying on the ground. Figures keep to the paths. The figures do not cross the boundary ditch.
vibe_condition: The village is untouched since 4E 48. No timber has been taken.
vibe_approach: The boundary ditch is the warning. It was dug after the village was taken.
vibe_senses: No birds fly over the ground inside the ditch. No insects are present inside the ditch. The figures make no sound on the paths.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A carter tried to cut through the stripped village. The carter did not go around it. The quest is to follow the carter's attempt.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1128 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Umbriel took the village in a night. The houses stand furnished. Every door is open.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Umbriel corridor, a legible line across the province

name: Sixteen Doors
why_founding: Sixteen Doors is a second village on the same track as Ganthil's Rest. It was emptied and left clean. It has no dead, no damage and no explanation.
why_site_advantages: The ground is identical to its neighbour's. People avoid both villages, for different reasons.
why_occupants_motive: The village is empty. Its neighbours will not take its timber, even for a hearth.
why_pressures: The absence of horror here frightens people more than the horror next door.
why_would_change_if: A returning family could reoccupy the village tomorrow. No family has returned in a hundred and fifty years.
vibe_palette: The palette is silver-grey timber, green floor growth and flat light.
vibe_signature_feature: Sixteen sound houses stand with their doors open. Their contents are in place. No bones lie anywhere.
player_purpose_hook: Sixteen sound houses stand open with their contents in place. No bones lie anywhere.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'umbriel-stripped-village' stays active at 'stripped-village-north'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Umbriel corridor, a legible line across the province

name: The Swallowed Meer
why_founding: The xanmeer was left untended after the Burn. Regrowth got into the joints. Over two centuries the regrowth took the xanmeer apart.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer's terraces offer the sole climbing in a flat scrub district.
why_occupants_motive: A poacher crew uses the upper chamber. The lower chambers are full of roots and something else.
why_pressures: No clan claims or defends the xanmeer. Poachers are emptying it piece by piece.
why_would_change_if: A clan that claimed the xanmeer would immediately have to defend it.
vibe_palette: The palette is root grey, stone green and deep leaf shadow.
vibe_signature_feature: Its own vegetation is pulling the xanmeer apart. Root-buttresses stand where the stonework used to be.
player_purpose_hook: The forest has pulled this xanmeer apart over two centuries. Entry is where the roof gave way.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'broken-xanmeer' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in a district with other xanmeer, showing the range of states

name: The Sugar Barge
why_founding: The Sugar Barge is a Khajiit crew's dance barge. It is moored outside the harbour line. Its jurisdiction has never been settled.
why_site_advantages: The barge is moored beyond the mole. That is where the harbour office's authority stops and the council's begins. The barge sits in the gap between the two.
why_occupants_motive: The barge offers moon sugar, music and card games. None of these are illegal until an official decides where the barge is.
why_pressures: Every new wharfinger tries to define the mooring. Every wharfinger gives up.
why_would_change_if: A defined harbour limit would sink the whole business in a night.
vibe_palette: The palette is lantern gold on black water, with silk red.
vibe_signature_feature: The barge is hung with lanterns. A drum is going aboard. It is moored far enough out that a boat is needed to reach it.
player_purpose_hook: The barge offers sugar, drums and cards. It is moored in the gap between two jurisdictions. A boat is needed to reach it.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'vice-den' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-5. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

name: The Sugar Stack
why_founding: A Khajiit crew took the flat top of a sea stack as a transfer point. The Southern Sea's smugglers keep a low profile and hate harbours.
why_site_advantages: Deep water surrounds the stack on all sides. It has a single landable notch and a rock cistern. No inhabited shore has a sightline to it.
why_occupants_motive: Moon-sugar and untaxed cloth change hulls here. Neither ship enters a port.
why_pressures: The crew has to carry water up the stack. The crew is here for days at a time at most.
why_would_change_if: An Altmer patrol working the Southern Sea would empty the stack overnight.
vibe_palette: The palette is ochre canvas, wet black rock and white spray.
vibe_signature_feature: A tented platform is lashed to the crown of the sea stack. A block-and-tackle hangs over open water.
player_purpose_hook: The sugar crews use the flat-topped sea stack as a transfer point. The way up is the climb.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'sea-stack' stays active at 'wraxu-stacks'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a climbable stack on the Southern Sea lane, in sight of the Khajiit landing

name: Sunken Causeway
why_founding: The Sunken Causeway is an Imperial causeway across the salt marsh. It was built to carry ore carts. It was abandoned when the carts stopped.
why_site_advantages: The causeway runs straight across four kilometres of marsh. It is still the driest crossing.
why_occupants_motive: Travellers use the causeway as they cross. The causeway is not maintained.
why_pressures: Three spans are gone. Travellers swim, wade or jump the gaps depending on the tide.
why_would_change_if: Repairing the spans would restore the fastest route between Soulrest and the burn country.
vibe_silhouette: The causeway is a dead-straight grey line running out into the marsh. It stops three times before it reaches a destination.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey stone, salt-marsh olive and tide-line black.
vibe_materials: The road is Imperial ashlar courses on a rubble core. The iron cramps have corroded out. Travellers add lashed timber gap-bridges. The tide washes the timber bridges away yearly.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone road runs straight out into the salt marsh. Three drowned gaps cut it. The gaps dictate the crossing's tide timing.
vibe_condition: The roadbed is sound. Three spans are gone. Every attempt to bridge the gaps has been temporary. Each bridge has failed within a wet season.
vibe_approach: For a kilometre the causeway reads as a straight line in a landscape without any. The gaps do not show until a traveller reaches them.
vibe_senses: Footfall rings on stone, which is rare here. Wind crosses the marsh. Water runs at the gaps. The air smells of salt.
player_purpose_hook: The Imperial ore road lies under a metre of water. It is still the straightest line across the marsh.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: links two named places directly

name: Sunkfoot
why_founding: Sunkfoot is a shore hamlet. It subsided when the salt pans changed the drainage behind it. The sea came in over a decade.
why_site_advantages: The ground was firm before the subsidence. It is under water at every tide now.
why_occupants_motive: The hamlet is empty at low water. The villagers moved the grave-poles. They left some grave-poles standing in the hamlet.
why_pressures: The shore end is shallow enough to wade. The danger is inside the roofs. The water there is dark. It holds a drowned thing that did not stay drowned.
why_would_change_if: A second subsidence would take the salt pans too.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey-green water, black rotted timber and barnacle white.
vibe_signature_feature: Roof-ridges and a standing door frame break the surface at low tide. Fish swim in the house floors.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The way in is under the roofs at the spring tide. The drowned come back to their doors then.
why_site_won: The map point of a drowned village with an underwater entrance is on dry ground. The diver walks in from the bank. The old point lay in the sea at 4241.5, 6237.5, 0.12 m deep. The nearest dry cell to it is 4233.3, 6236.6, 8.3 m away, so the point is placed there.
player_purpose_hook: A whole hamlet went under in a decade. The roofs are still on it.
siting_note: The place is pinned 50 m west onto the coastal lagoon cell. The danger raster reads band 2 there. A drowned hamlet with an apex ambusher in it cannot sit on band-0 city apron.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'drowned-village' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: below or beside a living settlement that watched it go; within 2 km of the salt pans

name: Tapped-To-Death
why_founding: Tapped-To-Death is a second Hist in the burn country. An Imperial-era sap concession tapped the Hist under licence. The tapping never stopped.
why_site_advantages: The licence-holders could reach the Hist by cart. That cart access is why the concession chose it.
why_occupants_motive: The tapping outfit is long gone. The spiles are still in the trunk. A collector still takes the sap.
why_pressures: The village of Ashroot will not go near the Hist. The villagers will not say why in front of outsiders.
why_would_change_if: Pulling the spiles is a two-hour job. The job has been left undone for a hundred and sixty years.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey bark, iron black and amber sap.
vibe_signature_feature: A living Hist has forty iron spiles driven into it. The spiles stand in a surveyed grid. A numbered ceramic pot sits beneath each spile.
player_purpose_hook: Forty iron spiles are driven into a living Hist in a surveyed grid. The pots beneath the spiles are still being emptied.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'harmed-hist' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village

name: Teeba-Enoo Court
why_founding: The tribes tolerate Alten Meerhleel because of its Teeba-Enoo court. The port maintains the court. The port fields a team as the price of that tolerance.
why_site_advantages: The court is a floored court on the landward margin of the port. Tribal parties can come there without entering the trading water.
why_occupants_motive: The port fields a team and loses politely. The tribes take the result seriously. The trade continues.
why_pressures: A port team that won convincingly would create a diplomatic problem. The council would have to answer for that problem.
why_would_change_if: Ending the games would end the tribes' tolerance of the port.
vibe_silhouette: The court is a sunken rectangle. It has raised kerbs and banner poles at its corners. It is a hard shape in ground that has no other geometry.
vibe_palette: The palette is packed red clay, painted kerb stones and banner cloth.
vibe_materials: The court uses reused xanmeer kerb stone, a packed red clay floor, painted stone markers and banner cloth. Imperial material is absent from the court, though the port lies two hundred metres away.
vibe_signature_feature: A sunken stone-kerbed ball court stands beside a trading port. The court is better maintained than any building in the port.
vibe_condition: The keepers re-lay and roll the clay after every session.
vibe_mood: The mood is ceremonious. Play is scored to a fixed formal order.
vibe_approach: Parties approach the court from the landward side. They do this deliberately, so that every party stays out of the trading water.
vibe_senses: The ball makes a flat crack on the stone kerb. The air carries crowd noise, red dust and formal shouting in a set order.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A visitor can play a side in the ball game. The game buys the port its peace.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM29 · tier-3; LM64 · tier-3; RS-line · tier-2
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The ball game is paid for to keep the tribes friendly. Winning a place on a side opens doors.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: beside an outsider-facing settlement

name: The Teeth of Sithis
why_founding: The Teeth of Sithis is the largest Sithis temple in Murkmire. The Clutch of Nisswo tends the temple. The temple no longer serves its original purpose.
why_site_advantages: The temple stands at the end of a pilgrim route. It stands on the fringe marsh by the coast, 35 m from the open sea. Six black stone teeth stand in the shallows there. The temple was built to frame them.
why_occupants_motive: The Clutch maintain the temple precisely. They preach that the loss of its purpose is itself the teaching.
why_pressures: The temple's original purpose is lost. At least one faction claims to have found the purpose out.
why_would_change_if: A rediscovery of the temple's function would split the Clutch.
vibe_silhouette: A colonnade of black stone teeth rises straight out of flat water. The colonnade is scrubbed clean to the waterline and green below it.
vibe_palette: The palette is wet black stone, a white scrub-line and brown water.
vibe_materials: The temple is black stone, xanmeer construction on a natural formation, with ornament courses. The Clutch scrub the stone as ritual and make no repair or addition.
vibe_signature_feature: A colonnade of black stone teeth rises out of standing sea water. The Clutch keep the teeth scrubbed clean of algae to the waterline.
vibe_condition: The stone is immaculate to the waterline. The stone beneath the waterline is untouched.
vibe_approach: The temple comes into view at the last bend of the pilgrim water.
vibe_senses: Water laps on stone with no echo back. Scrubbing sounds carry across the water. Cold air comes off the stone even at noon. Silence lies where birds should call.
why_site_won: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 144 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, culture-clump, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The Teeth of Sithis is the largest Sithis temple in Murkmire. The Nisswo will take an outsider in for the right offering.
watch_reason: The Clutch of Nisswo keep a standing watch on the temple stair.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a regional pilgrimage terminus

name: Tempers-The-Young
why_founding: In Lilmoth people look to their elders, retired Shadowscales among them. Tempers-The-Young is the ground where those scales were trained.
why_site_advantages: The ground is an enclosed water-and-root ground an hour outside the city. It has three approaches and no sightline into it.
why_occupants_motive: Two retired scales keep the ground. They take the occasional sign-born child. Both practices are now illegal.
why_pressures: The Cheydinhal succession wants the tradition back. Lilmoth's council would prefer that the tradition did not exist near their walls.
why_would_change_if: A single public execution of a trainee here would force the council to act.
vibe_silhouette: The ground has no silhouette. It is a cleared water-ground screened on all three approaches. Its posts stand barely above the reed line.
vibe_palette: The palette is black water, wet root and dull steel.
vibe_materials: The ground uses weighted hardwood posts in black water and blinded screens of woven reed. A dry blade-rack hangs under a root. Stone-kerbed footing marks where the ground is worked.
vibe_signature_feature: A cleared water-ground has weighted posts and blinded approaches. A rack of blunted practice blades is kept dry under a root.
vibe_condition: The ground is hard-used and erased between uses. The keepers rake the ground and strike the racks.
vibe_approach: The ground has three approaches, all screened. A visitor is on the ground before it is visible.
vibe_senses: Blunt wood strikes wood. Water is disturbed and settles. Trainees count their breathing aloud. The air smells of wet root and dull steel.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A visitor can settle who takes the next Shadowscale intake. The rival claimant comes from Cheydinhal.
why_site_won: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 716 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, landform, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.keshu-grove (+0.45).
player_purpose_hook: Retired Shadowscales train people here. No other school in the south teaches it.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: near a hatchery and a major city, deliberately unremarkable

name: Tidewrack
why_founding: Tidewrack is a shore village on the tidal flat east of Lilmoth. The villagers live off what the bay leaves twice a day.
why_site_advantages: The village has two metres of tide over firm flats. The city's market lies within a morning's poling.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers live on cockles, crabs and salvage. Driven stakes divide the wrack line between households.
why_pressures: Lilmoth's growth means villagers buy more and are given less. The old sharing customs are visibly lapsing.
why_would_change_if: A bad shellfish year would put half the village into the city's slum quarter.
vibe_palette: The palette is mud silver, weed green and grey stilt timber.
vibe_signature_feature: Stake boundaries run straight out across the mudflat from each house. The stakes divide the tide line into private strips.
player_purpose_hook: The villagers live on cockles, crabs and wrack. Driven stakes divide the wrack between households. The city market lies a morning's poling away.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'stilt-village' stays active at 'keel-sakka-stilts'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

name: The Long Cut
why_founding: The Long Cut was the Empire's timber concession. It was Soulrest's second export. Crews felled timber along a graded haul road to the river.
why_site_advantages: The Long Cut is a straight graded cut through what was hardwood forest. It is still the driest walking line in the district.
why_occupants_motive: The Long Cut is unworked now. The haul road is the best inland path in the district.
why_pressures: The forest that the concession cut was the same peat forest that burned. The regrowth is scrub and not timber.
why_would_change_if: A hardwood forest does not regrow in two hundred years.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey deadwood, thorn green and red laterite.
vibe_signature_feature: A dead-straight overgrown haul road runs four miles into scrub. Rotted sleeper timbers are still in the road.
player_purpose_hook: The haul road runs four miles dead-straight through scrub. It is the driest inland walking in the district.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'derelict-concession' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: behind a coastal ex-capital, on a dead haul road

name: Ashen Hard
why_founding: Ashen Hard is a tidal hard on Topal Bay. Crews heave a hull down on the hard. They burn the hull clean of Topal Bay's shipworm.
why_site_advantages: The hard has a firm bottom. The tide range is four metres. A freshwater seep supplies the boiling coppers.
why_occupants_motive: Two families run the hard. They careen a stranger's boat. They ask no questions about the boat's last port.
why_pressures: Timber from the burn country is bad. Good keel stock now arrives by sea. The families resent buying keel stock by sea.
why_would_change_if: If the freshwater seep were lost, the whole trade would move a mile east.
vibe_palette: The palette is mud grey, pitch black and flame orange.
vibe_signature_feature: Boats lie over on their sides in the mud. Fires burn under the boats. The smell of pitch carries to the water.
player_purpose_hook: Two families burn the worm off a hull. They do not ask where the hull last berthed.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'boatwright-yard' runs 4 province-wide. Its countBand is 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: serves a port or a water-village cluster

name: Topal Pearl Beds
why_founding: Shellfish beds lie in the bay's clear inner water. Divers worked the beds since before the Empire. The Empire's officials have counted the beds since they arrived.
why_site_advantages: The water is five to nine metres deep over a firm shell bottom. The islands shelter the beds from the Southern Sea swell.
why_occupants_motive: Diving families work the beds in rotation. They fight over a bed's boundary. They never fight over a bed's rest year.
why_pressures: Soulrest buyers set the price. Working a bed out of turn causes a feud, not a crime.
why_would_change_if: Warming or a silt pulse off the burn country would kill a bed outright.
vibe_palette: The palette is turquoise shallows, nacre and wet grey shell.
vibe_signature_feature: Marker withies stand out of open water in a grid. The shuckers read the grid from the raft. A raft carries shucking baskets.
player_purpose_hook: The water is five to nine metres deep over a shell bottom. Withies mark the beds in a grid. A newcomer has to be taught the grid.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: worked from a coastal settlement or a flotilla

name: White Fields
why_founding: Salt is an export that the burning of the mines did not affect. The bay's shore is good ground for evaporation.
why_site_advantages: The shore is a wide, gently shelving salt-marsh. The dry season is long enough for salt to crystallise.
why_occupants_motive: Pan-holders pay Soulrest a share. They sell the rest to fish-curers along the whole south coast.
why_pressures: A wet-season overtop ruins a year's salt. Owed labour rebuilds the sea walls every spring.
why_would_change_if: If the Owing gangs stopped coming, the pans would silt in three years.
vibe_silhouette: Rectangles and bunds lie flat to the horizon. One shed-line breaks the flat.
vibe_palette: The palette is blinding white, black mud and pale sky.
vibe_materials: The works use black mud bunds and white salt crust. They also use cane sluice gates, a plank barrow-run and a single reed store shed. Almost no timber is used in the whole works.
vibe_signature_feature: Rectangles of white crust have black mud walls between them.
vibe_condition: Pan-holders work the pans hard in the dry season. The flood takes the pans in the wet season. The bunds are rebuilt from scratch every year.
vibe_approach: The white shows for two kilometres in the dry season. In the wet season the white is gone.
vibe_senses: The glare hurts the eyes. The crust cracks underfoot. Barrow wheels sound across the pans. The pans have no smell.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Owing rebuilds the sea walls each spring. A quest can end the Owing, enforce it or let a worker pay it off.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 202 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, hinterland, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The salters buy labour by the season. They sell salt in bulk.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: supplies a whole district's preservation

name: The Second Tender's House
why_founding: Lilmoth's rule says a second tender attends whenever the first tender listens. The rule created a second office. The office needed a house outside the Hist enclosure.
why_site_advantages: The house stands directly outside the Hist enclosure wall. It has a door onto the enclosure. It has a door onto the street.
why_occupants_motive: The rotating second tenders live in the house in turn. The house belongs to the office, not to the person.
why_pressures: The rota is the city's central political institution. Every faction has tried to influence the rota.
why_would_change_if: One tender holding the post permanently would recreate the condition that destroyed the city.
vibe_palette: The palette is pale plaster, duty-board chalk and green tree light.
vibe_signature_feature: The house has two doors. A duty board lists the next twelve tenders by name. The bed is never the same person's for long.
player_purpose_hook: The house belongs to the office that watches the tender who listens. The duty board lists twelve names.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: 200-600 m from the village it serves

name: The Rat Gallery
why_founding: Tunnel Rats are penal labour worked underground for a limited freedom. The Tunnel Rats dug the deep gallery under the gold concession.
why_site_advantages: The gallery lies below the water table. A single incline reaches it. The mine office had full control of the incline.
why_occupants_motive: The gallery has no living tenant. The bones are Argonian. The dead were never buried in the ground.
why_pressures: Half the gallery is flooded. The rest stands on rotten props. The bone-carriers want the dead out. The bone-carriers cannot reach the dead.
why_would_change_if: A dewatering effort would turn a grave into a recoverable one. The bone-carriers argue for dewatering.
vibe_palette: The water is black. The timber is wet. The lamplight is yellow.
vibe_signature_feature: A timbered incline drops into standing water. Tally marks are cut beside every side-gallery. Names are cut beside the tallies.
player_purpose_hook: Penal labour dug this gallery for limited freedom. The far end was never surveyed.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is a tier-2 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: below or beside White Rose Prison, on the workings it fed

name: The Cane Field
why_founding: The Expeditionary Force met the uprising in the open in 3E 427. The ground suited a legion.
why_site_advantages: The ground is flat, firm and treeless. The Imperials chose it. The tribes accepted it and have not given their reasons.
why_occupants_motive: Farmers work the field now. Ploughing still turns up mail links. The farmers stack the links at the field edge.
why_pressures: Two incompatible accounts of the day are told within a mile of each other.
why_would_change_if: The field stays a field. Farmers cut the cane every year.
vibe_palette: The palette is crop green, rust brown and black soil.
vibe_signature_feature: The field is an ordinary crop field. A cairn of ploughed-up armour fragments grows at its corner, year on year.
player_purpose_hook: A crop field has a cairn of ploughed-up mail growing at its corner. Two irreconcilable accounts of the day are told.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'battlefield-ground' runs 3 province-wide. Its countBand is 2-2. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: at a xanmeer, a crossing or a road

name: Varo's Holding
why_founding: Varo's Holding is an Imperial settler grant of the late Third Era. The grant was laid out to Nibenese practice. Stone will not hold in the ground.
why_site_advantages: The surveyors saw firm lowland in the dry season.
why_occupants_motive: The fourth generation still farms the holding. The family still refuses to rebuild in reed.
why_pressures: The house has sunk until the ground floor is a cellar. The family rebuilt the barn on stilts. The family does not discuss the contradiction.
why_would_change_if: One flood year would settle the argument.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey stone, green damp line and reed gold.

player_purpose_hook: A Nibenese stone farmhouse stands knee-deep in its own subsidence. A competent Argonian stilt barn stands next to it.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

name: The Villa Cellars
why_founding: The Imperial villas outside the rebuilt wall sank with their cellars intact. The cellars are connected.
why_site_advantages: A continuous flooded undercroft runs two hundred metres. Three collapsed floors give entry.
why_occupants_motive: Salvage crews work the near end under permit. The far end lies beyond the permit line. A creature lives in the far end.
why_pressures: The passage is head-height and silt-floored. The passage disorients a diver completely. Light fails after the second room.
why_would_change_if: A collapse at the middle would cut the far cellars off for good.
vibe_silhouette: Three collapsed floor-holes show in a green mound. The place itself lies entirely below the water and has no outline.
vibe_palette: The palette is silt brown, a red glimpse of mosaic and black water.
vibe_materials: The undercroft has Imperial brickwork and a floor mosaic under silt. One guide rope of foreign cordage hangs in it. The rope is older than the divers using it.
vibe_signature_feature: The undercroft is flooded and Imperial. Mosaic still lies on the floor under the silt. A diver tied a guide-rope there and did not come back for it.
vibe_condition: The structure is intact and wholly flooded. The mosaic is undamaged under the silt. The ceiling is unsound.
vibe_approach: Three holes open in the ground. All three are unmarked. A rope goes down one of them.
vibe_senses: Underwater, silt clouds at a fin-stroke. The rope runs through the diver's hand. The mosaic shows a red glimpse. Above the water, frogs call.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A diver's line runs past the second room, where the light stops. A quest can follow that line.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: TG02 · tier-2; TG08 · tier-2; LM02 · tier-3; LM26 · tier-3
why_site_won: ford in firm lowland (danger band 3), 882 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Two hundred metres of connected Imperial cellars lie under the water. The divers have not reached the end.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: links two known places by a wet route

name: Suvei-Tzel
why_founding: Suvei-Tzel makes vossa-satl and little else. It has done so long enough that the craft defines its marriages, calendar and politics.
why_site_advantages: The village stands beside the last stand of resonant hardwood in the district. The village has managed the stand for centuries.
why_occupants_motive: The instruments sell across the province. The village's real product is the tuning. Tuning is sold only in the village.
why_pressures: Bright-Throat's chime craft is fashionable and Suvei-Tzel's craft is not. Young makers are leaving for the cliffs.
why_would_change_if: Losing the hardwood stand would end the craft in a generation.
vibe_palette: The palette is warm wood, lacquer red and green stand.
vibe_signature_feature: Every house has a drying loft of shaped wood. The whole village is tuned each morning, audibly, at once.
player_purpose_hook: The village offers the only tuning worth buying in the province. The young makers are leaving the village.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a trade water; brokers between neighbours

name: Wallside
why_founding: Households pushed out of Lilmoth's tariff line built against the outside of the city wall. They built on platforms in the mangrove.
why_site_advantages: The wall is one side of every house. The mangrove forms the other three sides.
why_occupants_motive: The households live close enough to work in the city daily. They live far enough out to owe the city no rent.
why_pressures: The council periodically declares the platforms a fire risk. The council leaves the platforms standing.
why_would_change_if: A wall repair programme would demolish the platforms without any decision being taken.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey wall stone, raw plank and dark water.
vibe_signature_feature: Houses stand built onto the outside face of a city wall. Ladders climb to a postern. The council pretends the postern is sealed.
player_purpose_hook: Houses hang off the outside of Lilmoth's wall. Ladders climb to a postern that the council pretends is sealed.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region holds 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'mangrove-platform-village' stays active at 'screen-watch'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: deliberately not on any lane

name: Charge-In-The-Water
why_founding: Charge-In-The-Water is a wamasu nesting pond. The wamasu curses the water around it into convulsions. The convulsions kill.
why_site_advantages: The pond is still and isolated. A sand bank lies there. The animal returns to it. The pond lies off every through route.
why_occupants_motive: The adult wamasu holds the pond. Egg-poachers come anyway, from downstream, on foot.
why_pressures: The water within thirty metres is lethal while the adult is present. The adult is usually present.
why_would_change_if: A poached clutch would drive the adult out. That would free a whole channel network.
vibe_palette: The palette is blue-white flicker, black water and pale sand.
vibe_signature_feature: The pond has a hard sand nest bank. Dead fish rim the edges. The surface twitches with light before the nest-holder shows.
player_purpose_hook: Water within thirty metres convulses while the adult is on the bank. The adult is usually on the bank.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The type 'wamasu-pond' runs 4 province-wide. Its countBand is 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a district hazard; villages route around it

name: White Rose Prison
why_founding: White Rose Prison is one of the prisons that the Empire built after 1E 2837. The Imperial rule for this province was to use the marsh as a wall. It stands off the road that the Legion already held.
why_site_advantages: The ground is firm with marsh water on every side. A single causeway reaches it. It lies a short haul from the Soulrest road. Convicts came in along the road and ore went out along it.
why_occupants_motive: The prison holds no living occupant. Argonian dead fill it. They died away from their Hist. Their bones were never brought to the dirt.
why_pressures: The Blackrose Chainbreakers want the dead repatriated. The structure is sound enough that an outside party will eventually want it back.
why_would_change_if: Reoccupation by any armed party would make repatriation impossible. It would make the grievance permanent.
vibe_silhouette: A white rectangular block stands above the reed. The block is hard-edged and unweathered. The causeway is intact and the gate is open.
vibe_palette: The palette is lime white, marsh brown and black door-shadow.
vibe_materials: The walls are Imperial lime render over dressed stone. The gate furniture is iron. The tiled roof is complete. Scavengers have left the prison whole. Argonians have added nothing.
vibe_signature_feature: A white lime-rendered Imperial block stands above the marsh. It is structurally perfect and silent. Its causeway is intact and its gate is open.
vibe_condition: The render is sound. The gate is open. All the iron fittings are still in place.
vibe_approach: The prison shows white through the reeds from a long way off.
vibe_senses: The place is silent. Reeds grow around it. The causeway lies underfoot. Lime dust hangs in the air. The smell of occupation has gone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The cordon cellars were sealed with names still on the roll. A quest can open them.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: BC05 · tier-2; LM48 · tier-3; LM56 · tier-3
why_site_won: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 1027 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Marsh water lies on every side of the Imperial prison. The cordon cellars below the prison were never emptied.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: off the Helstrom–Blackrose causeway, in sight of nothing else

name: Whitebone Reef
why_founding: Whitebone Reef is a coral and shell reef across the mouth of Topal Bay. The reef lies a foot under water at high tide. The salvage trade exists because ships wreck on the reef.
why_site_advantages: The reef lies directly on the natural sailing line into Topal Bay.
why_occupants_motive: The reef belongs to no household. Three centuries of ship hulls lie on the reef.
why_pressures: Silt from the rivers of the burn country is killing the living head of the reef. The silt turns the reef head to rubble, which makes the reef more dangerous to ships.
why_would_change_if: A lit mark on the headland would make the reef harmless to shipping.
vibe_palette: The colours are white surf, dead coral grey and deep blue beyond the reef.
vibe_signature_feature: The reef shows as a white line of breaking water. Mast-stumps stand out of the line at intervals, like a fence.
vibe_mood: The reef looks pretty from a distance. The reef is dangerous to shipping.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The reef head is dying. Its depth at the tide is not yet charted. A quest can chart the reef head's depth before the pilots trust it.
player_purpose_hook: The reef lies a foot under water at high tide. Wrecks still lie on the reef.
siting_note: The reef was moved off the crowded Alessian-hull neighbourhood in the round 4 hostility rebalance. It now stands on the coastal lagoon named by its regionClasses.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on a shipping approach; explains the wrecks and the lights around it

name: The Witness Camp
why_founding: The Umbriel Witness Society keeps a standing camp on the shadow track. The society holds that the province is not clean until the society has accounted for every stripped place.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the track itself, between two stripped villages. The society chose the worst possible place on purpose.
why_occupants_motive: The society members record and count the stripped places. The members will not leave the camp. The council has not asked them to leave.
why_pressures: The society is old and small. More of its members each year were not born when it started.
why_would_change_if: Completing the survey would dissolve the society. Several members plainly dread that.
vibe_palette: The colours are canvas grey, ink black and sour green.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp is a permanent group of survey tents. A boarded map of the shadow track hangs under a canvas awning. Three different hands update the map.
player_purpose_hook: Survey tents stand on the shadow track on purpose. Three different hands update the map there.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. The place is a tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: on the Umbriel corridor

name: The Wraxu Frieze
why_founding: The Wraxu Frieze is a Sithite ground for making and unmaking. Local xanmeer carvings show the extinct wraxu birds. The Sithites copy the carvings in clay each year and destroy the copies.
why_site_advantages: A sheltered clay bank lies under a xanmeer face. The xanmeer face carries the original wraxu etchings.
why_occupants_motive: The Nisswo and their students make an exact copy of the frieze. They exhibit the copy for one night. They break the copy before dawn.
why_pressures: Outsiders keep trying to buy the copy. The Clutch keeps explaining that the destruction is the work.
why_would_change_if: A copy surviving a year would be a theological crisis. A person is trying to arrange a surviving copy.
vibe_silhouette: A carved stone face rises above a clay bank. Broken shards glitter on the bank for twenty metres in both directions.
vibe_palette: The colours are ochre clay, grey stone and feather-black shard.
vibe_materials: The original carving is xanmeer stone. Fired clay shards lie below it. Every copy made here is broken on purpose.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone frieze of extinct birds stands above a clay bank. The bank is littered with the broken shards of every copy ever made.
vibe_condition: The original carving is pristine. Every copy is destroyed. The shard bank grows every year.
vibe_approach: The shard bank crunches underfoot. The carving being copied is overhead.
vibe_senses: Shards shift underfoot with a sound like shell. Clay dust hangs in the air. A person works at the bank and breaks the result.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A sale of this year's clay work is under way. A quest can stop or complete the sale before the Clutch destroys the work.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The Sithites copy the extinct birds in clay each year and break them. The original carving is above the shard bank.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: near a Nisswo circuit

name: Wraxu Stacks
why_founding: The Wraxu Stacks are named for the extinct wraxu birds. Wraxu colonies once covered this coast. The birds that nest here now are not wraxu.
why_site_advantages: The stacks are vertical sea stacks off the islands. They are unclimbable from three sides. They are thick with guano and eggs.
why_occupants_motive: Egg-takers come twice a year by rope. They take the ledges in a fixed order.
why_pressures: The clans here know what happened to the wraxu. Their taking rules are stricter than any law written in Soulrest.
why_would_change_if: The clans hold that a single greedy season would empty the ledges for a generation.
vibe_silhouette: Two pale vertical stacks streaked white stand clear of the water. A wheeling cloud of birds hangs above them.
vibe_palette: The colours are guano white, black basalt and green sea.
vibe_materials: The stacks are black basalt covered in guano. Old iron rope anchors are driven into the rock. One rope ladder is taken away between seasons.
vibe_signature_feature: Two pale stacks are streaked white. The colony is loud enough to hear from a mile out. Old rope anchors are still driven into the rock.
vibe_condition: The rock is untouched. One set of rope anchors is maintained.
vibe_approach: The colony is audible from a mile out. The noise arrives long before the stacks appear out of the haze.
vibe_senses: This is the loudest place on the coast. The air smells of ammonia and of sea on rock. The noise stops dead in the lee of the stacks.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A licensed buyer wants eggs outside the taking rules. A quest can uphold the taking rules against the buyer, or break them.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 27 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, bound, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Egg-takers climb these stacks for a living. An unworked sea cave lies at the base of the stacks.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: off the islands that screen the Soulrest approach

name: Wraxu-Meht
why_founding: Local xanmeers were etched with the extinct wraxu birds. The coastal clans still maintain this xanmeer as a monument.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer is a stepped stone mass on firm ground above the flood. It is visible above the canopy. It is one of the district's few true landmarks.
why_occupants_motive: A clan rota clears the terraces and re-cuts the etchings. The clan forbids entry. Looting here is a serious offence. The clan says so.
why_pressures: Antiquarians want to go inside. The Soulrest council has been asked twice to compel access.
why_would_change_if: A single sanctioned excavation would end the tending. It would probably end the clan's standing.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey-green stone, cut-line shadow and swept sand.
vibe_signature_feature: The stone terraces are swept clean. Bird figures are cut deep into every riser. A sealed doorway is dusted daily.
vibe_approach: The stepped mass breaks the canopy line long before the site is reached.
player_purpose_hook: The terraces are swept. Wraxu birds are cut deep into every riser. A sealed doorway is dusted daily.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. The region has 140 records against a 45-56 budget. A stronger in-region 'tended-xanmeer' stays active at 'pilgrim-xanmeer'.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it

name: The Well Shaft
why_founding: The Well Shaft is a xanmeer's original water shaft. It is now the way into a complex whose surface entrances were sealed.
why_site_advantages: A vertical stone shaft drops eleven metres to a flooded gallery. A ledge at four metres gives a place to rest.
why_occupants_motive: The shaft belongs to no household. Two ropes from different decades hang in it.
why_pressures: A diver gets one breath down and one breath back. The gallery below has its own current.
why_would_change_if: A silt slump would close the shaft. It would seal the complex entirely.
vibe_palette: The colours are clear blue-black, cut stone grey and green rim growth.
vibe_signature_feature: The shaft is a perfectly circular cut in the stone, full of clear water. Carved handholds spiral down its inside face.
player_purpose_hook: The old water shaft is the only way into the xanmeer. The xanmeer's doors were sealed from inside.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'dive-shaft' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: the only entrance to a submerged place

name: The Sunken Shrine of Xhon-Mehl
why_founding: The shrine honours Xhon-Mehl the Fisher, Ancestral Organ Lord of Lilmoth. Xhon-Mehl is the drowned ancestor-god of the catch for the city of Lilmoth. The shrine is sunken.
why_site_advantages: The shrine lies in the estuary shallows off the old waterfront. The same subsidence that took the Imperial quarter submerged it.
why_occupants_motive: Fishers dive to the shrine before a long season. They leave an offering inside the shrine, not on it.
why_pressures: The city council would prefer the shrine on land, where it could be administered. The fishers prefer it in the estuary shallows.
why_would_change_if: Raising the shrine would be civic policy for the council. The fishers would take it as an insult.
vibe_palette: The colours are green underwater light, shell white and a black stone throat.
vibe_signature_feature: A carved fisher-lord's mouth opens underwater. Fresh offerings are wedged inside the mouth. Old offerings are fused to the stone by shell.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The council has ordered the god brought ashore. A quest can hold the offering season in the water against that order.
why_site_won: isthmus in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 295 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on nearPoint, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A drowned fisher-god lies in the shallows off the old waterfront. The offerings go inside the mouth.
deferred_why: The place is parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance. Type 'beast-offering-shrine' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3. The surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: between a village and a lair

name: Xinchei-Konu Monument
why_founding: Xinchei-Konu is a calendar of upright stone counters in the lowlands east of Lilmoth. It has a hereditary keeper and a jekka-wass. The monument is called a catalyst of change. The monument can alter the weather.
why_site_advantages: The monument stands in open lowland with a clean southern horizon. The instrument needs that horizon.
why_occupants_motive: The keeper's office is to keep the instrument unused. The keeper explains this to the scholars who arrive.
why_pressures: Every party with a weather problem eventually comes here. The keeper has refused emperors' agents and antiquarians alike.
why_would_change_if: A successful use of the instrument would be the largest single event in Argonia's recent history.
vibe_silhouette: A ring of upright counters stands on open ground under a wide unbroken southern sky. The keeper's rota keeps the ground clear of canopy.
vibe_palette: The colours are pale grey stone, cropped green and wide sky.
vibe_materials: The counters are pale dressed stone with ornament courses. The ground is cropped turf. One keeper's shelter of reed stands at the ring's edge. Every other structure is forbidden inside the ring.
vibe_signature_feature: The ring is made of aligned stone counters in open ground. Each counter face is carved with a different reckoning. One person keeps the ring clear of vegetation.
vibe_condition: The stones are unrepaired. One person cuts the sightlines back weekly.
vibe_mood: The place is precise. The keeper's rule leaves the instrument unused.
vibe_approach: A clean southern horizon opens before the stones come into view. That horizon is essential to the instrument.
vibe_senses: Wind blows with no leaves in it. The grass is cropped. One person cuts back growth endlessly. Sun heat comes off the stone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A quest can ask the keeper for weather. A quest can find who is buying her succession.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LM18 · tier-3; LM63 · tier-3; PP15 · tier-3
why_site_won: saddle in firm lowland (danger band 3), 895 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, region, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A working stone calendar has a hereditary keeper. The monument is held to turn the weather.
siting_prefs_preferences_neighbour_relat: above canopy; visible from a distance

name: The Poler's Breath
why_founding: The Poler's Breath is a maintained air pocket on the flooded shortcut under the narrows.
why_site_advantages: The pocket is the midpoint of a dive that cannot be made on one breath.
why_occupants_motive: The pocket is uninhabited. Two guiding families keep it up between them. The upkeep is charged into the crossing fee.
why_pressures: Silt is filling the pocket from below. The two families have argued for ten years over whose job the clearing is.
why_would_change_if: Losing the pocket would close the shortcut. It would add two hours to every crossing. The portage crews would take the traffic.
traversal_fallback: The fallback is to pole the surface route around the narrows. That route takes two hours.
vibe_silhouette: The pocket has no silhouette from outside. Divers find it by diving.
vibe_palette: The pocket is black until the lamp is lit. Then blue light shows doubled in still water. The undressed block is grey.
vibe_materials: The structure uses bog-oak posts, cane walls and bone lintels. Sinew and hide lashing binds it. Peat-tar fills the seams. Crocodile skulls stand on the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: A bell-shaped root chamber holds a bubble of air the size of a boat. The guides rig a pump-line to top up the bubble each season.
vibe_condition: sound, re-lashed last season
vibe_mood: The pocket is a rest stop, used thirty seconds at a time.
vibe_approach: The approach is a descent in the dark to a ceiling of air.
vibe_senses: The pump-line knocks on the roof of the bubble. Rot is held down under cold water. A lamp flame stands perfectly still.
why_site_won: The map point of the air-pocket station is on the bank at its entrance. The old point lay in the water at 2547.1, 4899.5, 1.56 m deep. The nearest dry cell to it is 2522.4, 4924.2, 34.9 m away. That is further than a bank usually lies from the water, because no land lay closer. The point is placed there.
player_purpose_hook: A room full of air lies halfway through a dive too long for one breath. The guides charge for it as part of the crossing fee.

name: The Unmaking Yard
why_founding: The Nisswo commission works of art at this ground. The Nisswo destroy each work when the sermon ends.
why_site_advantages: The yard is a clearing above the flood. The clearing has one landing. Patrons can attend, watch a work destroyed and leave the same night.
why_occupants_motive: A resident maker and a rotating congregation use the yard. The maker is paid to make well and then watch the work burn. The Nisswo do not commission a maker who flinches again.
why_pressures: Foreign collectors have begun buying works before their destruction. The Nisswo treat buying before destruction as heresy. The collectors pay in coastal coin. The congregation has learned to want coastal coin.
why_would_change_if: A single sale made public would split the congregation. A second, tolerant unmaking-yard would open on the coast.
vibe_silhouette: The debris field looks too deliberate to be wreckage.
vibe_palette: The yard is black above and blue below, with no green. Grey hide is stretched on the frames.
vibe_materials: The yard has no raised structure. Worked bone is set into the ground and left. Gut lashing is used and it stinks. Grave-cairns step up the bank, one course for each death.
vibe_signature_feature: A field of plinths holds the residue of destroyed works. Each plinth is labelled with what the work was. Each label also says how long the work lasted.
vibe_condition: The yard is clean and ordered. The yard is quiet for its size.
vibe_mood: The mood is unhurried. The burnings are scheduled.
vibe_approach: White plinths stand in black water. The newest plinth holds a work not yet destroyed.
vibe_senses: The pole shudders when it finds bone. Drum-signals carry flat across the water. Tar, burnt cane and ash are trodden into the landing.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 667 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The Nisswo commission works of art and destroy them as the sermon. Outsiders may pay for a commission.

name: Teeth-Pens
why_founding: The keepers bred crocodiles here for hide and meat. The penned ring itself serves as the cheapest wall in the swamp.
why_site_advantages: The creek is gated and once made good pens. The gated creek now works as a trap. Traffic in or out crosses the stock.
why_occupants_motive: The keepers are long gone. The crocodiles left in the pens have gone half-wild. They attack whatever wanders close.
why_pressures: The bridge over the pens is rotting at the centre span. The bridge is the last crossing left into what used to be the village.
why_would_change_if: Draining or breaching the pens would scatter the stock. The crocodiles would spread into the surrounding reaches for good.
vibe_silhouette: The pens and skull racks read as built structure before any hut does.
vibe_palette: The water is black with blue light under the surface. The silt is ash-grey. The racks are bone-pale.
vibe_materials: Bone plate cladding is rotted through in places. Hide thongs are perished and hang loose. Drum frames have collapsed at the landing.
vibe_signature_feature: Entry is across the bridge over the pens. The bridge is failing at the middle span.
vibe_condition: The village sags badly on one side. The pens themselves are undamaged.
vibe_approach: The smell reaches the water before the pens come into sight.
vibe_senses: Cold comes off the black water. A heavy splash sounds out past the lamplight. The water is dead, flat and sweetish.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 1098 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The village bred crocodiles and its pens are still full. The crocodiles have gone unfed by any keeper for years.

name: The Hunt Ledge
why_founding: Hunters pay at this shrine for what they are about to take.
why_site_advantages: The shrine stands at the head of the reach where every hunt starts. It sits where the reach forks. Every hunt must pass it before starting. Passing hunters keep the keeperless shrine observed.
why_occupants_motive: Hunters; no keeper.
why_pressures: The offerings have got smaller as the hunting has got worse. The hunters read the smaller offerings as poverty. The villages that eat what the hunters bring back read them as impiety.
why_would_change_if: An empty ledge would be read as the end of the hunting. If the ledge were swept clean, the reach would be declared closed for a season. Four villages would then go to the coast for protein. Those villages cannot afford that protein.
vibe_silhouette: Offerings are heaped facing a body of water or a den. The ground behind the offerings is unbuilt.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Cane bundles are yellowing. Blue glow shows only where the water is disturbed.
vibe_materials: The shrine uses cairns and driven poles. Cane is used only for the shelter. Vine cord is traded in from the interior and hoarded. The poles are plain and unpeeled. Stone cairns and feather totems stand behind the poles.
vibe_signature_feature: The ledge records takings as well as offerings. The hunting log is kept as a religious duty. It is the zone's best ecological record.
vibe_condition: New work stands next to work three lifetimes old. The ledge is patched so often that the original work is hard to find.
vibe_approach: A carved ledge stands over the water at the first bend.
vibe_senses: The air is perfectly still. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. Sulphur rises off disturbed mud. Nothing green shows in the light.
player_purpose_hook: The shrine stands at the head of the reach where every hunt starts.
deferred_why: The record is deferred as thin rite-dressing. The Kaju maturity ground stands beside it. The Kaju maturity ground carries the same hunt material better.

name: Since-The-Tree
why_founding: The village's Hist was killed during the Umbriel passage. The village has stayed put ever since.
why_site_advantages: The village ground is good. The villagers stay for the stump. The stump is a relic and a grave. No neighbouring village contests the stump.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers have no hatching, no naming and no soul-return. They keep the village going anyway.
why_pressures: Their young are Hist-less by birth. The province has no category for this generation. Neighbouring tribes trade with them but will not marry them. Each generation is smaller than the last.
why_would_change_if: Adoption by a neighbouring tree would dissolve them into another tribe. They have refused adoption twice. A hero Hist could hatch their young without taking their name. The elders have not yet put that question to a Hist.
vibe_silhouette: A dead trunk stands at the centre of the village. The villagers keep the trunk and have not cleared it.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. Pale bone is worked and stacked by size. The dead trunk shows no light.
vibe_materials: Bog-oak is salvaged black from the peat and worked wet. Cane-split cord is replaced constantly. Nothing is sealed, since the work is meant to leak. A line of plain poles stands behind the huts where the old field was. The villagers keep the poles upright.
vibe_signature_feature: The dead trunk was cut down. Its stump is now the village council table.
vibe_condition: New work stands next to work three lifetimes old.
vibe_approach: The villagers seat visitors at the stump table first.
vibe_senses: Mud closes over the foot at every step. Smoked hide and wet bone scent the air. The dead trunk creaks in a wind that the reeds do not feel.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The village carries the LW01 League of Open Water hook.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LN01 · tier-3; LN02 · tier-3; LN03 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 299 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, culture-clump, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.naga-village-settled (+1.25).
player_purpose_hook: The village's tree was killed during the Umbriel passage. The stump is now the village council table. Visitors are seated at the stump first.

name: The Under-Pool
why_founding: A pool lies in a root chamber. The pool lights blue when disturbed.
why_site_advantages: The chamber is closed. Flood cannot wash out the bloom in a closed chamber.
why_occupants_motive: The pool has no residents. The villages take children to see it once. The showing is a naming custom and not a spectacle. A child who has seen the blue is held to have been seen by the swamp in return.
why_pressures: Taking water from the pool kills the bloom for a season. People keep taking water from it. The takers are alchemists' agents from the coast. The villages will not police the takers. The coin is real and the bloom's death is slow.
why_would_change_if: Repeated harvesting would end the pool. Its end would end the naming custom. The next pool lies more than four days' poling away.
vibe_silhouette: At night the pool's light is visible from further than any daytime cue in this province.
vibe_palette: The water is black with thin blue light under the surface. Visitors notice the blue is thin. The black mud holds a print for a week.
vibe_materials: The chamber holds raw bog-oak and shell grit. Nothing is lashed. The pool has no marker. The polers say the lack of a marker is deliberate.
vibe_signature_feature: The bloom lights only where touched. The pool records a visitor's movement for about ten seconds behind them.
vibe_condition: The chamber is worn but sound. Everything load-bearing is new. The wear is all in the same places.
vibe_mood: The pool is the zone's one moment of straightforward wonder.
vibe_approach: The chamber is in total darkness until a hand enters the water.
vibe_senses: Warmth is held in the hide walls after dark. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The air smells of peat, cold and mineral. Silence lies where birds should be.
player_purpose_hook: The pool lies in a closed chamber. Flood cannot wash out the bloom there.
deferred_why: The record is deferred as the second bioluminescent-water record in a 2.5 km² zone. The blue-flood gallery already carries what the Under-Pool offers.

name: One-Spine
why_founding: The village is strung along a single walkway. The mire has no ground on which the village could spread.
why_site_advantages: The walkway is one firm alignment across two kilometres of mire.
why_occupants_motive: Households stand in a line, in an order that is also a social order. Position on the spine is inherited. A household's address is its rank. A household moves up the walkway only when a nearer neighbour dies without heirs.
why_pressures: The far end floods first. The poorest households live at the far end. The village repairs from the landing outward. The far end is repaired last in years when the repairs run out.
why_would_change_if: Extending the spine would cost more than the village earns in a decade. The far end has begun talking to the raft people about leaving entirely.
vibe_silhouette: The walkway line curves away into vegetation.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Drift bone and drift wood lie in the same line. Blue shows at the waterline and the village is dark above it.
vibe_materials: Hide and bone cover a trained-root core. The root is failing. Gut lashing holds and stinks. Peat-tar fills the seams. Totems of bone and plumage stand at every landing.
vibe_signature_feature: Status is positional along the walkway. The near end is dry and the far end floods. Every resident knows their place on the plank.
vibe_condition: The walkway is patched so often that the original work is hard to find. The wear is all in the same places.
vibe_mood: The village is linear and stratified. Gossip travels end to end in minutes.
vibe_approach: A single line of roofs stands on a single line of deck.
vibe_senses: The air is perfectly still. Paddle knock is the only sound. The water is dead, flat and sweetish. The smell of sap does not reach this deep in the swamp.
player_purpose_hook: The walkway is one firm alignment across two kilometres of mire.
deferred_why: The record is deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget after its executor pass. The budget is in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. It is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Nine-Stakes Field
why_founding: Nine-Stakes Field is a burial field of driven poles. The poles rose after a flood disturbed the burial ground. Nothing was stolen here.
why_site_advantages: The field lies on low ground beside a channel. The channel changed course.
why_occupants_motive: The blights here were raised by no fault of any stake-setter. No wrongdoer can be named. Local law makes the blights the village's debt.
why_pressures: The village that owns the field cannot afford to restake it. The stake-setters price their work by the night. The village pays in rice. The two rates have drifted far apart. The restaking stopped mid-field.
why_would_change_if: Restaking would settle the blights. The obstacle is labour, not danger. An outsider who supplies the labour buys a permanent claim on the village.
vibe_silhouette: Nine cairns stand in a line. A gap marks where a tenth cairn should be.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. Blue bioluminescence glows in the shallows. Olive weed is matted across the shallows.
vibe_materials: The field has no structure. The bottom is cold silt and the rim is fallen block. Peeled poles are pushed into the bank at a lean. The leaning poles form a warning line.
vibe_signature_feature: The poles still stand upright and plain. The water carried the dead out from under them.
vibe_condition: The stakes are sound. The ground under them is gone.
vibe_mood: The stake work was done correctly. The channel undid it.
vibe_approach: The stake field is intact. The ground around it has washed out.
vibe_senses: Stake tops knock together when the water moves. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The air smells of smoked hide and wet bone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The stake field drains into water that the seat village drinks. Whatever is wrong at the field shows up in the village's water.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LN04 · tier-3; PP12 · tier-3; province system · tier-1
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 1114 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The stakes still stand and are set correctly. The water carried the dead out from under them. The village has not found a rite that covers this.

name: The Old Cordon
why_founding: The Old Cordon is the burial line of a plague cordon. The buriers were foreign. The line was left unstaked.
why_site_advantages: The line is an Imperial-era cordon. It runs across the neck of the zone.
why_occupants_motive: A century of unstaked burial has produced whatever now lies here. The Legion dug the line and left. The ground has had no owner since.
why_pressures: The route that the cordon guarded is still in use. Each generation blames its accidents on the cowardice of the previous generation.
why_would_change_if: Staking the line would take a season. Staking would end a century of accidents. Staking would also settle publicly that the plague dead here were Argonian, not Kothringi.
vibe_silhouette: A stockade of pikes stands half-swallowed by the ground. It marks a cordon that the stake-readers stopped walking.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. The stake tops are bone-white. The rest is hide-brown and bone.
vibe_materials: The ground is unbuilt. Black water, bog-oak and bone lie sorted by the drawdown. A stripped drum frame stands at the landing.
vibe_signature_feature: Imperial burial trenches run deep and dead straight. They are cut to a pattern that the villages here do not know.
vibe_condition: The cordon is not kept at all. The trench line is still legible after a century.
vibe_mood: The Imperial work was left where it stopped.
vibe_approach: A dead-straight depression runs across the swamp for two kilometres.
vibe_senses: The air does not move at all. Reeds hiss with drums beneath. A rusted pike smells of wet iron.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The field was left off the season's bidding. The stake-setters who let it stand owe a reckoning.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 1014 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: An Imperial burial trench runs dead straight across two kilometres of swamp. It is cut deep, to a pattern that the villages here do not use. It is open at both ends.

name: The Carriers' Camp
why_founding: The Carriers' Camp is a seasonal camp of bone-carriers. The carriers gather the zone's distant dead. They then walk the dead inland.
why_site_advantages: The poling routes converge here. The walking route inland begins here. It is the last point where a laden carrier can be resupplied by boat.
why_occupants_motive: Carriers live here in season. Most carriers are repaying a family's unreturned dead. They earn no wages. The season is worked to exhaustion.
why_pressures: The Umbriel-era backlog of dead reaches this camp too. The stacks show it. Some bundles are labelled for villages that no longer exist.
why_would_change_if: A carriers' strike would leave a season's dead unreturned.
vibe_silhouette: Wrapped bundles lie on a rack. A small fire burns beside the rack.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. White shell grit lies at the landing. Blue shows at the waterline. The scene is dark above the waterline.
vibe_materials: The shelters are hide over paddles set as poles. A shelter can be struck in an hour. The lashings are sinew and hide. Tar and ash are worked into every lap. Carved frills are set as boundary markers.
vibe_signature_feature: Bundles are stacked by how many seasons they have waited. The oldest stack has been rewrapped so often that it is mostly wrapping.
vibe_condition: The camp is sound in season. One set of posts is not sound.
vibe_mood: The carriers do ordinary work among the dead.
vibe_approach: Visitors reach the stacks first. The smell of fresh wrapping cloth follows.
vibe_senses: Wet cloth slaps the rack. The air smells of tar and burnt cane. Nothing green shows in the light.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The rack is a register of who died where. One bundle came in last season labelled for a village. That village burned ten years ago.
player_purpose_hook: The carriers wait to carry the dead inland. The oldest bundle in the stack has been rewrapped so often that it is mostly wrapping.
siting_note: The place was cut on 2026-09-04 (round 4 network-role pass). Its identity is a junction: 'where the poling routes converge and the walking route inland begins, the last point a laden carrier can be resupplied by boat'. No such convergence exists in the Naga-Kur deeps. The plotted dot sat 361 m from any route and inside the mercantile-coast culture zone. Rewriting the junction camp as an ordinary camp would have removed the reason it existed, so it was cut rather than moved. Bone-carrying survives in the zone through the necropolis and burial sacred sites.

name: The Fallen Meer
why_founding: The Fallen Meer is a xanmeer that subsided and broke. It has been looted for two centuries.
why_site_advantages: Soft ground took one corner of the xanmeer. The rest followed.
why_occupants_motive: Squatters and scavengers occupy the ruin in rotation. Worse things occupy it too. Each rotation of squatters believes that the previous ones were too stupid to find the vault. The vault is the ruin's only renewable resource.
why_pressures: Nothing worth taking is left. People keep coming for it anyway. The tended xanmeer downstream now posts a watch. It never needed a watch before.
why_would_change_if: Nothing changes the ruin, because it is spent. A second subsided corner could open a floor that no visitor has yet reached.
vibe_silhouette: In the subsumed variant, the ruin gives no sign until a visitor is inside it. The reveal is the beat.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Blue light is bright enough for reading. Cairn stones are grey and stacked.
vibe_materials: Cane and hide have collapsed. The bog-oak posts still stand true. Gut lashing stinks and holds. Smoked hide is black and stiff. Crocodile skulls top the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: The looting is so complete that it is the interesting thing left. One doorway shows three distinct eras of tool marks.
vibe_condition: The frame survives. Everything soft has gone. It was burnt, then rained on for a century.
vibe_mood: The ruin is picked clean. It is a ruin of a ruin.
vibe_approach: A stone hill leans.
vibe_senses: The air does not move at all. The drum that should answer does not answer. Rot is held down under cold water. Dry ground lies more than a day away.
player_purpose_hook: Soft ground took one corner of the xanmeer. The rest followed.
deferred_why: The place was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The place is a lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Dead-Water Village
why_founding: Dead-Water Village is the seat of the Naga-Kur. The tribe was built for surviving the worst thing in the swamp. The village stands around the tree that made the tribe.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on a defensible rise in the inner swamps. Black water surrounds it on all sides. It has a single poling approach. That approach is the tribe's toll. Cargo bound for the eastern swamp is counted at the stage.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe organises its grave rite, watch and blight-craft around the dead not staying down.
why_pressures: The tribe built its discipline against Umbriel's legacy. The tribe has not stopped preparing. Their kin on the roads are tribeless. The reputation of the hold suffers for it.
why_would_change_if: If the blight pressure stopped, the tribe would have no reason for its discipline. The stake-setters would lose their trade. The night necropolis would lose its trade. Three subordinate villages would lose their trade.
vibe_silhouette: A blue-lit crown stands over a dark village.
vibe_palette: Black water reaches right up to the pile line. The shade is olive. A blue-flowering Hist lights the whole village from above.
vibe_materials: Cane and bog-oak sit on a trained-root core. The Hist itself put the root core there. Hide walls are smoked black. Bone lintels are cut from the tribe's own dead. The tribe states this honour to visitors. Stake-cairns step up the bank at the rear.
vibe_signature_feature: The Hist flowers blue where every other Hist flowers red. Its light is recognisable an hour out from the landing.
vibe_condition: Each post and roof has been replaced at least once. Doctrine requires the replacement.
vibe_mood: The village is organised like a garrison at every hour.
vibe_approach: Blue light shows on black water an hour out from the landing. The drums answer an approaching craft before a watcher shows.
