vibe_senses: Cold comes off black water on one side. Warmth comes off the hide walls on the other. The deep drum is answered by other villages. The air smells of smoked hide, bone-dust and cold peat.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tribe charges a toll on its single approach. The tribe keeps a grave discipline. A Hist has started flowering the wrong colour.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LN04 · tier-3; LN05 · tier-3; LN06 · tier-3; LN15 · tier-3
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 344 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, nearPoint, region.
player_purpose_hook: Dead-Water Village is the seat of the Naga-Kur. It stands under a Hist that flowers blue where the trees of the province flower red. Traffic east is counted at the landing before it passes.

name: Deepmire, the Refuge
why_founding: Deepmire is the shelter of last resort. It is a ridge eight metres over the flood. It is hard to reach. Even the tribes avoid it. The presence of Sithis is strong there. It holds pre-Duskfall xanmeers. It holds the skeletons of swamp leviathans. People go up only in an emergency. A few caretakers tend it.
why_site_advantages: Deepmire is high, dry, defensible ground. The province has almost none. A single approach can be walked. No approach can be poled.
why_occupants_motive: The caretakers do not live here. They keep the plateau fit for habitation. They turn the stores each season. They re-roof the shelters each season.
why_pressures: In 4E 48 the need did come. Murkmire's survivors fled onto the plateau while Umbriel passed overhead. The caretakers have fed that memory ever since. The Umbriel Witness Society wants the memorial catalogued. The Nisswo want it let go. The caretakers want it left as it is.
why_would_change_if: If the argument over the memorial is settled over the heads of the caretakers, the plateau stops being a refuge. It then becomes a destination.
traversal_fallback: No fallback route exists. The plateau is walked and climbed, or it is not reached.
vibe_silhouette: A flat-topped plateau stands clean out of the swamp. Two stepped xanmeer crowns break its rim. The white arc of a leviathan ribcage lies across the approach.
vibe_palette: Stone is grey and the grass is dry and pale. The swamp is black far below. The approach is bone-white. No blue light shows on the plateau.
vibe_materials: Cane and hide shelters have been struck and restruck for centuries without improvement. Dry-stone store huts stand here. The caretakers argue about the huts and keep them. Pre-Duskfall xanmeer stone is untouched since it was raised.
vibe_signature_feature: The Umbriel memorial is a line of shelters kept permanently ready. The stores are turned and the roofs are sound. The line stands as it did on the night in 4E 48.
vibe_condition: Deepmire is maintained to a standard that no other place in the deeps matches. It is used for perhaps a week a century.
vibe_approach: The approach is a day through leviathan bone country. A climb follows. No water route exists.
vibe_senses: The air is dry and the horizon long. The swamp below has neither. Wind replaces drums. The air smells of dust and old thatch. No insects make noise. The caretakers put this down to Sithis.
quest_hooks_opportunity: LOC deepmire.refuge · LOC deepmire.memorial_ground · LOC deepmire.caretakers_camp · LOC deepmire.document_cache · ROUTE deepmire.approach
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 202 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, danger, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Deepmire is one of the few dry plateaus in the province. It has been kept ready since the night in 4E 48. Travellers may shelter there. The caretakers permit no residence.

name: The Chimney
why_founding: The Chimney is a natural shaft. It runs from the swamp floor into the root layer.
why_site_advantages: A root gallery's roof gave way under standing water here. The shaft lies deep in the swamp. It is a long way from anywhere.
why_occupants_motive: The shaft is used in both directions. The villages date their worst years by what came up out of it.
why_pressures: Divers use the shaft as a shortcut. It does not reliably let them back. The guides charge double for naming it.
why_would_change_if: A collapse would seal the connection. It would add half a day to every stake-field circuit on this side of the zone.
vibe_silhouette: A dark opening lies in the water. Worked stone rings the opening. Root hangs from it like a beard.
vibe_palette: Blue bioluminescence serves as a lamp. The light is thin.
vibe_materials: The shaft has no worked construction. Black bog-oak sills have fallen from the roof. Silt lies across the floor. Root is thick enough to walk on where it crosses the shaft. A line of plain poles is driven at the rim. The village that lost the last diver drove the poles.
vibe_signature_feature: The shaft breathes with the season. Silt is drawn down it as the basin falls. Silt is blown back up when the monsoon refills the basin. The plume shows from the surface for a month either side.
vibe_condition: The shaft is holding. The next bad season decides its fate.
vibe_mood: The shaft draws and blows with the season.
vibe_approach: A silt plume rises out of the swamp floor for no visible reason.
vibe_senses: Cold comes up off black water. Two drums answer, a long way apart. Silt coats the tongue.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 548 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, nearPoint, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A silt plume rises out of the swamp floor for no visible reason. The shaft is the way down into the root layer. The plume is visible for a day's poling either side.

name: The Refilling Flat
why_founding: The Refilling Flat empties late and refills fast. The salvage window on the flat is short and dangerous.
why_site_advantages: The flat is a wide shallow. It has a narrow outlet.
why_occupants_motive: Salvagers work the flat for a short time. They are mostly heirs of the drowned village. The heirs work a claim that they cannot register. They will not abandon the claim.
why_pressures: The refill traps people every few years. A village fishes the outlet. That village has stopped reporting the bodies. A report would close the flat.
why_would_change_if: A wetter cycle would close the salvage window. It would also settle a three-family inheritance dispute. The flood would settle the dispute by drowning the evidence.
vibe_silhouette: The flat is cracked where there was water. Things stand up out of the flat.
vibe_palette: The water is black with blue light under the surface. The cairn stones are grey and stacked. Blue shows in the roots and nowhere else. No red appears anywhere, by custom and by tree.
vibe_materials: The materials are bone, peat and standing water. Teeth are the only worked thing here. One stake-cairn stands at the rim. The cairn is kept up by a person who has no name.
vibe_signature_feature: The refill comes as a visible front across the flat. The front moves at walking pace. The salvage rule is to leave as soon as the front can be seen. Salvagers do not wait until it reaches them.
vibe_condition: The works are dismantled for half the year. The parts are stacked above the flood. The works are re-made from scratch each year. The remade works are never quite the same.
vibe_mood: The hazard is timed, legible and fair.
vibe_approach: The flat is exposed mud. A line of water crosses the mud.
vibe_senses: Two drums answer each other a long way apart. The dead water smells flat and sweetish. No green shows in the light.
player_purpose_hook: The flat is a wide shallow with a narrow outlet.
deferred_why: The place was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The place is a lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Last Mooring
why_founding: The moving village chose this mooring for calm water. The calm water lies over the bone field. It was the calmest water in the district.
why_site_advantages: The still water suited the village's mooring for a season. The same still water now suits whatever feeds on the bone field. The bone field is very large.
why_occupants_motive: The creature that ended the quiet has held the mooring since. The village has not returned to reclaim the mooring.
why_pressures: Wrecked rafts and posts remain at the mooring. They are unlashed. They drift loose over the bones.
why_would_change_if: Hunters have not driven off whatever holds the bone field. The mooring-caller has not gone back to check.
vibe_silhouette: Broken piles and drifting posts stand over the bone field. The pale bone field shows through clear water.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. White bone is stacked deep below. Cold blue shows under the piles.
vibe_materials: The rafts are framed on cut bone. They are broken loose and waterlogged. Vine cord trails and is rotted. Smoked hide has gone to rag. No shelter is left standing that a body could enter.
vibe_signature_feature: The bone field is stacked deep. Its depth changes the colour of the water above it.
vibe_condition: The rafts are wrecked and scattered. The lashings have parted.
vibe_mood: Still water lies over a great deal of bone.
vibe_approach: The water goes pale before it goes deep. The bone shows through long before the wreck does.
vibe_senses: Cold water presses on a diver. Something heavy shifts below. The air smells of wet rag and bone dust.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Stock lifted from a stake store has to be landed somewhere. No counter works this water.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 1071 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, bound; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: This is the moving village's last mooring. The village tied up here for the calm water over the bone field.
singular_claim: The place has countBand [1,1]. The inner swamp's unreliable ground is the only thing that forces a village to be mobile.
complexity_justification: The place has two authored mooring locations. It has an empty-footprint state. The village is not a moving object.

name: Under-Piles
why_founding: Under-Piles is a stilt village. The village drowned when the channel changed. The water rose two metres in a season.
why_site_advantages: The village was correctly sited for the water level of its time. Local people cite it as the reason not to build on any firm-looking flat.
why_occupants_motive: Uninhabited. Fish; salvage divers.
why_pressures: The families who left live three villages away. They still claim the goods in the village. They have hired divers twice. The divers were hired to keep the dredgers from taking the goods.
why_would_change_if: A drawdown would expose the village. A drawdown would start a legal fight. Three villages would prefer to postpone that fight.
vibe_silhouette: Roof ridges and pile stumps break the water. More of them show every week of the drawdown.
vibe_palette: The water is still black with a slow blue drift. Blue light is bright enough for reading. White shell grit lies at the landing.
vibe_materials: Undressed block has slumped where the peat took it. Gut lashing has gone slack. Peat-tar fills the seams. A rank of plain poles is still driven along the drowned bank. Cairns and totems stand above the water line.
vibe_signature_feature: The houses are intact underwater. Their contents are in place. The rise was slow enough for the families to walk out.
vibe_condition: The village is submerged to the ridge line. Weed grows on the exposed thatch.
vibe_mood: A house interior lies underwater. The furniture is where it stood.
vibe_approach: Roof ridges lie in a line just under still black water. No current shows on the surface.
vibe_senses: Air stands dead in the pockets. Weed drags on a pile stump. A lamp finds no green.
why_site_won: The village's entrance is on the bank, at 2588.2, 5362.9, on the dry ground within 25 m of water body 1209-3032 that lies closest to 2596.4, 5387.6. That spot is 1.92 m deep. The entrance lies 26.0 m from it.
player_purpose_hook: The houses are still furnished under the water. The rise was slow enough that people walked away. They left the furniture standing.

name: The Gate Narrows
why_founding: The Gate Narrows is a flood-pulse pinch in deep marsh. The whole zone's outflow squeezes through it in the hours after rain.
why_site_advantages: The pinch is the single outlet of the inner swamp. It is held between two root walls, not rock.
why_occupants_motive: The narrows has no residents. The nearest village keeps a timing post. The village that most recently lost a boat mans the post.
why_pressures: Boats that mistime the pinch are lost. The village profits from salvage. The village therefore leaves the gauge post as it is. The villagers memorise the drawdown timings. They do not write the timings down.
why_would_change_if: A cut second channel would end the danger and the salvage income. The village has twice blocked the survey.
vibe_silhouette: The water's surface is visibly wrong at the pinch.
vibe_palette: The water is still black with a slow blue drift. Cold blue shows on the underside of the piles. Green shows only on the weed.
vibe_materials: The narrows has no built work. Silt, cane wrack and stripped debris lie scattered over the ground. Totems are set facing inward. Inward-facing totems are unusual.
vibe_signature_feature: A gauge post has the safe levels painted on it in four colours. A salvage board stands beside it. The board lists what the last mistiming produced.
vibe_condition: The post is hard-used. The wear is all in the same places.
vibe_mood: The narrows is a timed crossing with a salvage trade behind it.
vibe_approach: The gauge post is visible from both approaches. The noise starts an hour before the window closes.
vibe_senses: The air does not move at all. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. Silt boils up when the pulse starts.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A creature that hunts on a timetable can take the drawdown window. That would close a village's approach.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 562 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A painted gauge post gives the length of the window. The salvage board beside it lists what the last mistiming produced.

name: The Hire Stage
why_founding: The Hire Stage is where outsiders hire a poler. The inner swamp cannot be crossed without a poler.
why_site_advantages: The stage is the last point that can be reached without local knowledge.
why_occupants_motive: Polers, a broker and a price list work the stage. The price list is not the real price list. The broker has never poled. The broker takes a cut of each hire. The polers tolerate him because he deals with the foreigners.
why_pressures: Unguided travellers go in anyway. Their craft come back empty. Every loss justifies the next rise in the hire price.
why_would_change_if: A published chart would destroy the trade. No chart exists. Two surveyors have tried to make one. Both surveyors were poled home.
vibe_silhouette: A hut, a pole and a boat stand at the stage. The boat is clearly not a private one.
vibe_palette: The water is still black with a slow blue drift. The bog-oak is black and wet. Blue bioluminescence shows in the shallows.
vibe_materials: Cane bundles are pegged into bog-oak. Root is used only where root will grow. Vine cord is traded in from the interior and hoarded. Peat-tar fills the seams. Crocodile skulls sit on the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: A wall of recovered boat-nameplates hangs at the stage. The nameplates come from craft that went in without a poler. The wall serves as an advertisement.
vibe_condition: The stage is serviceable. It is not kept beyond that.
vibe_approach: The nameplate wall is the first thing at the landing. It runs the length of the hut.
vibe_senses: The air stands still over the stage. Paddle knock and the broker's voice carry. The air smells of smoked hide and wet bone. No dry ground lies within a day.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The stage offers a travel service. The service is poler hire into the deeps.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, culture-clump; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.refugee-camp-raid (+0.80).
player_purpose_hook: Beyond this landing the inner swamp is not crossed without a poler. The nameplates of craft that went in unguided hang along the hut.
siting_note: The stage sits outside the Naga-Kur culture raster on purpose. Its function is to be the last place an outsider can reach unguided. So it belongs on the boundary, not inside the culture raster.

name: Levee-Top
why_founding: Levee-Top is a hamlet built along the crest of an old natural levee.
why_site_advantages: The levee is the only linear dry ground in the zone.
why_occupants_motive: The hamlet's farmers work the back-swamp behind the levee. The back-swamp is the richest rice ground in the zone because it floods. So the hamlet farms what will destroy it.
why_pressures: A levee breach would take the hamlet and the fields together. The households nearest the weak point most oppose repairing it. Repair means a levy.
why_would_change_if: A breach is overdue. The villagers all know where it will happen. The village that would be flooded second has offered to pay for the work. That offer was refused.
vibe_silhouette: Structures stand on the only high ground in a flat view.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Blue light is bright enough for reading. The pole tops are bone-white.
vibe_materials: Bog-oak is salvaged black from the peat and worked wet. Cane-split cord is replaced constantly. Smoked hide is black and stiff. Plain poles are driven along the levee crown where the old field was.
vibe_signature_feature: Every house faces the same way, with its back to the swamp. The levee is one house wide.
vibe_condition: The levee is holding. The next bad season decides it. The hamlet is kept up. Small repairs show.
vibe_approach: A line of gables stands on a ridge in flat water.
vibe_senses: The hide walls hold warmth after dark. Two drums answer each other a long way apart. Rot is held down under cold water. No dry ground lies within a day.
player_purpose_hook: The levee is the only linear dry ground in the zone.
deferred_why: The place was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The place is a lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Sunk Corridor
why_founding: The Sunk Corridor is a xanmeer service corridor. It is now full of water to the ceiling.
why_site_advantages: The corridor connects two parts of a ruin. Those parts are otherwise a day apart. The far half carries no looters' marks.
why_occupants_motive: The corridor holds no den. The silt on the floor lies undisturbed.
why_pressures: The corridor is the sole link between the two basins. Its length is a hundred metres.
why_would_change_if: A drawdown year makes the corridor walkable. The tending clan means to be the first party to pass the corridor. The clan says so openly.
vibe_silhouette: Water goes into a structure and does not come out.
vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow falls on wet bone. Black water lies beyond. Blue glow shows only where the water is disturbed.
vibe_materials: The bone frame is still upright. The soft work has gone from the frame. Sinew and hide lashing have perished in the water.
vibe_signature_feature: A hundred metres of dead straight flooded corridor runs ahead. The far end is visible as a coin of light.
vibe_condition: The corridor is drowned and silted. The current works at the joints.
vibe_mood: The corridor is a straight swim on one breath.
vibe_approach: The swim takes one breath. The line is straight. The exit is visible.
vibe_senses: Cold comes up off the black water. Rot is held down under cold water. A lamp ring knocks on stone.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 137 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The corridor runs a hundred metres, dead straight and flooded. The far end is a coin of light. The far half carries no looters' marks.

name: The Polers' Camp
why_founding: The Polers' Camp is a night camp for poling guides. The guides use it while crossing the inner swamp.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on a rise at the midpoint of the longest crossing. The rise is high enough to sleep on and small enough to defend.
why_occupants_motive: Guides and their clients stay at the camp overnight only. A guide sleeps between his client and the water. A client who decides at midnight to find his own way must step over his guide.
why_pressures: The rise is small and the crossings have become busier. Arrival order decides who sleeps dry. The older guides arrive early on principle.
why_would_change_if: A second rise, built by hand, would change this. The guides are rivals. No village claims ground this far out.
vibe_silhouette: The camp sits in a place that a stranger would not have chosen.
vibe_palette: The water is black with blue light under the surface. The cairn stones are grey and stacked. Blue glow shows where the water is disturbed.
vibe_materials: The tools have bone handles. The camp has no built structure. Lashings are made of gut. Hide covers the roof and is weighted with cairn stone. Grave-cairns step up the bank, one course for each death.
vibe_signature_feature: A raised deck holds four craft and their crews. The guides enforce an arrival-order rule on each other.
vibe_condition: The camp is hard-used. The wear is all in the same places.
vibe_mood: The camp is crowded. Arrival order governs it.
vibe_approach: Lamps burn at water level. The camp is the first high ground since morning.
vibe_senses: The deck lifts underfoot as the boats pass. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. Disturbed mud gives off sulphur. The smell of sap does not reach this deep into the swamp.
why_site_won: islet in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 915 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Lamps burn at water level on the first high ground for a day's poling. Arrival order decides who sleeps dry.

name: The Founder's Crown
why_founding: The Founder's Crown is a single burial terrace for one clan's founder. A keeper maintains it above a swamp that buries nothing.
why_site_advantages: The crown is the highest ground within a day's poling. It stands above the flood line. It is the only ground in the zone where a burial stays where it was put.
why_occupants_motive: A keeper is appointed for life. The keeper alone may climb.
why_pressures: Two clans claim descent from the same founder. Both clans send keepers. The keepers have shared the terrace for six years without speaking.
why_would_change_if: A ruling on descent would empty one clan's claim entirely. Both clans have avoided asking any authority that is able to rule.
vibe_silhouette: Cut terraces step up a wooded dome. The dome shows as a shape change in the island's profile.
vibe_palette: The water is black with blue light under the surface. Blue bioluminescence glows in the shallows. Dredged block is undressed and grey.
vibe_materials: Nothing is raised above the ground. Worked bone is set into the ground and left. Hide thongs are wet-tied and shrunk on to the wood. Grave-cairns step up the bank, one course for each death.
vibe_signature_feature: Two keepers' huts stand at the base of one ladder. Rival clans built them. The huts are deliberately identical. The huts do not share a wall.
vibe_condition: Strangers who pass keep the terrace, so it is odd but never derelict. It is worn but sound. Everything load-bearing is new.
vibe_mood: The architecture of the place shows a genealogical dispute.
vibe_approach: One tree, two huts and one ladder mark the approach.
vibe_senses: Mud closes over the foot at every step. Reeds hiss and drums sound beneath them. Disturbed mud gives off sulphur. The birds are silent.
player_purpose_hook: The crown is the highest ground within a day's poling.
deferred_why: The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget after its executor pass. The budget is in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. This record is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Held Tree
why_founding: A crew holds a Hist. The crew feeds and tends it. The Hist's tribe is kept on the far bank.
why_site_advantages: The tree stands on a defensible rise. Twenty-five metres of black water separate the tree from the tribe that owns it. There is a single landing, on the crew's side.
why_occupants_motive: The crew says that it is protecting the Hist. The crew taps the tree. What the crew draws is worth more than the zone's season of bone and hide.
why_pressures: The tribe has camped within sight for eleven years. The surrounding villages depend on the standoff. While it holds, no rival tribe can claim the tree.
why_would_change_if: If either party breaks the standoff, it ends in violence. The tree is the likeliest casualty.
vibe_silhouette: A tree stands inside a cage of scaffold. The scaffold is newer than the tribe's camp across the water.
vibe_palette: The gloom is olive. Blue light is thin and flickers in the roots. Black water lies at the base. New pale timber marks where the scaffold went up.
vibe_materials: The scaffold is imported keeled timber bolted into living wood. Cane cladding covers the place where the crew sleep. Hide covers the tapping gear.
vibe_signature_feature: A tribe's whole village stands abandoned on one bank. The tribe lives in a camp on the other bank. The camp is in sight of the tribe's own tree and houses.
vibe_condition: The place is half kept and half deliberately spoiled.
vibe_mood: The standoff is an eleven-year siege. The siege is routine now.
vibe_approach: Two settlements face each other across twenty-five metres of water. One of the settlements is empty.
vibe_senses: A hum catches and restarts. The drums stopped when the scaffold went up. The sap smells metallic.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The standoff has lasted eleven years. Two people are held inside the fence. Neighbours profit while the standoff lasts.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 66 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A crew holds a tribe's Hist behind a scaffold and taps it. The tribe camps in sight of their own empty houses.

name: The Set-Out Hut
why_founding: A village put one person out for a killing. The exile lives where the village can see the hut.
why_site_advantages: The hut stands deliberately within sight of the village landing.
why_occupants_motive: One exile lives here and will not go further. The exile will not apologise. The exile fishes the village's water in full view. This is legally permitted and socially unbearable to the village. The fishing is the whole of the argument.
why_pressures: The village finds the visibility unbearable. That is the exile's aim. Two households now use the far landing to avoid the sight line.
why_would_change_if: An apology would end the dispute. The exile will not give one. A stranger who carries words in both directions could end it in an afternoon.
vibe_silhouette: A single hide roof stands on the far bank. The boat is kept pulled right up.
vibe_palette: The water is black with blue light under the surface. Blue shows at the waterline and the ground above it is dark. Black mud holds a print for a week. White grave-cairns step up the bank.
vibe_materials: The hut is cane and bog-oak. Dredged xanmeer block is reused undressed as footing. Vine cord is traded in from the interior and hoarded. The hut has no seal at all and is meant to leak. Totems of bone and plumage stand at every landing.
vibe_signature_feature: The hut faces the village across four hundred metres of open water. A lamp is lit in the hut every night that the village lights one.
vibe_condition: The hut was repaired in a hurry and has not yet been repaired properly. It is holding. The next bad season decides it.
vibe_mood: The exile keeps a grudge as a nightly performance.
vibe_approach: Two lights burn on one stretch of water, directly opposite each other.
vibe_senses: Mud closes over the foot at every step. Paddle knock is the only sound. The air smells of smoked hide and wet bone. The birds are silent.
player_purpose_hook: The hut stands deliberately within sight of the village landing.
deferred_why: The hermit-hut type is over-band at 9/6. This is the least motivated of the province's exiles.

name: The Horwalli Cut
why_founding: A vanished people built these waterworks. They managed this swamp and did not live with it.
why_site_advantages: The works stand at the zone's natural drainage pinch. Two channels are close enough there for cut stone to join them. The joining would pay for itself.
why_occupants_motive: The works have no staff. They run themselves, badly. The four villages downstream have built their calendars around its faults.
why_pressures: The half-working sluices still divert water. Two villages flood because of how the pre-Duskfall builders set the channels. Each village blames the other for failing to clear its own channel.
why_would_change_if: Repairing or breaking the works would redraw where the water goes. One village's rice ground would be made and another's drowned. Each village refuses to let the other order the repair.
vibe_silhouette: The water behaves too regularly. A straight channel, a level pool and a weir line show it.
vibe_palette: Black water runs in cut channels, straighter than water should. The lost peoples' stonework is grey. Blue light pools where the flow stalls.
vibe_materials: The channel stone is dressed and still watertight. Pre-Duskfall hands laid it. Dredgers dropped in bog-oak baulks later. Cane staging spans the deep cuts.
vibe_signature_feature: Sluices still open and close with the season, unattended. The villages downstream time their planting by them.
vibe_condition: The works have collapsed inward. The outline is still legible.
vibe_approach: Cut stone channels run dead straight through the swamp.
vibe_senses: The floor vibrates where water still moves under it. Water noise sounds in a place where the deeps have none. The peat is cold and mineral.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The sluices have no owner. They set the year of four villages. Repairing them decides whose ground floods.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 845 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on nearPoint, landform, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Sluices still open and close on the season, unattended. Four villages downstream set their planting by that schedule.
singular_claim: The singular claim has countBand [1,1]. The works belong at the drainage pinch of the province's wettest interior.

name: Asks-Later
why_founding: Asks-Later is a village that adopted a policy of striking first. Raiders hit it three times in one decade.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on an island with two approaches. Both approaches are watched. Four people can hold each approach. Four is the number that the village can spare.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers are not cruel. They are not taking chances.
why_pressures: The policy has killed traders. The villagers know it and have not changed it. The trade that used to stop here now passes to their rivals. The villagers call that the price.
why_would_change_if: One well-handled visit could change the policy. This is a social lock, not a combat one. The neighbouring settled Naga have failed to change it for a decade. They would resent whoever succeeds.
traversal_fallback: The approach can be resolved by talk as well as by force. The fallback traversal is social.
vibe_silhouette: A stake fence faces outward. A landing has the boats hauled clear.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. Blue shows at the waterline and the ground above it is dark. Dredged block is undressed and grey.
vibe_materials: Bog-oak is salvaged black from the peat and worked wet. Vine cord is traded in from the interior and hoarded. Tar and ash are paid into every lap. Plain driven poles stand inside the fence line. Cairns and totems are set among the poles.
vibe_signature_feature: A killing-ground of cleared water lies in front of the landing. The wreck of a trader's boat is left in it on purpose as a notice.
vibe_condition: New work stands next to work three lifetimes old. The effort of one person keeps the village. This is obvious.
vibe_approach: The cleared water is the warning. A visitor crosses half of it before any villager speaks.
vibe_senses: The deck lifts underfoot as the boats pass. The air smells of smoked hide and wet bone. The birds are silent.
player_purpose_hook: The village stands on an island with two approaches. Both approaches are watched.
deferred_why: The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget after its executor pass. The budget is in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. This record is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Pale Village
why_founding: The Pale Village is a Kothringi village. It emptied in the Knahaten Flu. It was never reoccupied.
why_site_advantages: The ground is good, which makes the emptiness conspicuous. It is the best unclaimed landing in the zone. It has been unclaimed for six centuries.
why_occupants_motive: The village has no occupants. The Kothringi are gone.
why_pressures: The Argonians refuse to take the ground. They cannot fully explain why. They explain that the dead here were not returned. No bone-carrier will act on that explanation.
why_would_change_if: Nothing will change the village's state. It is a memorial by default. The first outsider to build here would be tolerated. The Argonians would never speak to him.
vibe_silhouette: Stone and metal construction stands in a landscape that uses neither.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. Blue shows at the waterline and the ground above it is dark. The cairn stones are grey and stacked.
vibe_materials: The cane has perished off the frames. Bog-oak stands bare. Gut lashing stinks and holds. Hide covers the roof and is weighted with cairn stone. Drum frames stand at the landing, one large and one small.
vibe_signature_feature: The building style belongs to no local people. Silver-fittings and plank walls stand in a province of cane and mud. The village reads as visibly foreign and visibly old.
vibe_condition: The village was burnt, then rained on for a century. It was robbed long ago of anything portable.
vibe_mood: The place holds the silence of the flu in one spot.
vibe_approach: Straight plank gables stand half-standing in reed country.
vibe_senses: The air does not move at all. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The nearest dry ground is more than a day away.
player_purpose_hook: The ground is good, which makes the emptiness conspicuous.
deferred_why: The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget after its executor pass. The budget is in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. This record is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Feather Deep
why_founding: The Feather Deep is the deepest hole in the inner swamps. The tribes' recitation names the Feather Deep. Divers turn back at the lip of the hole.
why_site_advantages: The Feather Deep is a drowned sinkhole in the swamp floor. The sinkhole is far deeper than the channels around it. The root layer closes overhead across the zone. The root layer stops over the hole.
why_occupants_motive: The tribes' recitation names a creature in the hole, but does not describe it. The naming tribes hold that describing the creature invites it.
why_pressures: Divers who go for the treasure at the lip do not go past it. Divers have picked over the lip. The salvage below the lip has not been touched.
why_would_change_if: The Feather Deep is expected to remain as it is.
vibe_silhouette: Every local can name the landform. A warning is maintained at the edge of the landform.
vibe_palette: The scene is black above and blue below. Green appears nowhere in it. A disc of true black marks where the hole is.
vibe_materials: The site has no built work. The materials are peat, undressed block that fell from elsewhere and bone. Carved frills are pushed into the bank as a warning line.
vibe_signature_feature: From thirty metres off the water changes colour. The colour change is a disc of true black in olive water. The disc is visible from a boat.
vibe_condition: No work has been done here at all. The tribes renew the warning at the lip each season.
vibe_mood: The water is deep. The local tribes warn against it.
vibe_approach: The colour change is visible thirty metres away.
vibe_senses: The air stands still over the hole. Disturbed mud gives off sulphur. Green is absent from the light.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 812 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A disc of true black shows in olive water. The tribes' recitation names the Feather Deep, where divers turn back at the lip.

name: The Nine Ribs
why_founding: Swamp-leviathan skeletons litter Deepmire. The Nine Ribs is the largest of these skeletons. The bone-and-hide works grew up beside it. The bone is free and already dead.
why_site_advantages: The carcass lies beached in shallow water at a channel bend. Workers cut the carcass from boats. The ribs stayed standing while the rest of the carcass went.
why_occupants_motive: A handful of bone-cutters live here. One family lives in a shack that is roofed under the standing ribs.
why_pressures: The skull still carries the injury that killed the animal.
why_would_change_if: The bone runs out in a generation. The works has already begun arguing over the second skeleton downstream.
vibe_silhouette: The ribs arch clear above the canopy. The region has almost no long sightlines.
vibe_palette: The ribs are bone-white and stand out of black water for half a mile. Olive weed grows on the lower courses. Blue light collects inside the ribcages after dark.
vibe_materials: The shack uses cane and salvaged plank. The roof is set against the ribs. Cutters take worked bone from the field itself, by licence. Cane staging stands where the cutters work.
vibe_signature_feature: A house stands under the rib cage. Two standing ribs serve as its roof beams and windbreak. The bone itself is left uncut.
vibe_condition: The works is repaired in a hurry. The repairs are not yet done properly.
vibe_approach: The ribs can be seen from the water long before the works can.
vibe_senses: A pole shudders when it strikes bone under the mud. Bone clacks on bone in the wind across the whole field. The air smells of cold peat and old marrow.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Nine Ribs lie on ROUTE deepmire.approach, on the UW04 bone-country leg.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 1135 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, culture-clump, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A house stands under the rib cage, where the bone is left uncut. Other animals have taken shelter in the same ribs.
singular_claim: The sources put several skeletons of this size in Deepmire. This one is authored as a place with countBand [1,1]. The other skeletons are dressing.

name: The Burn Ground
why_founding: The Burn Ground is a pit where the tribes burned blight-risen dead and did not stake them. The burning came in a decade with too many dead to stake.
why_site_advantages: The pit lies downwind of everything. The ground is not farmed.
why_occupants_motive: A keeper maintains the fire ban. The tribes appoint the keeper jointly. The keeper always comes from elsewhere. No local family owns the decision.
why_pressures: Burning denied those dead any return. Their descendants argue about whether the burning was necessary. The bone-carriers refuse commissions from families whose dead burned here.
why_would_change_if: A ruling that the burning was wrong would require exhumation. Nothing is left to exhume. That is the doctrinal problem.
vibe_silhouette: The ground is marked, but it has no settlement. It lacks burial furniture of the normal kind.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Blue light doubles in still water. The cairn stones are grey and stacked. White grave-cairns step up the bank.
vibe_materials: The ground uses cairn and driven pole. Cane is used only for the shelter. Lashings are sinew and hide. Peat-tar fills the seams. Totems of bone and plumage stand at every landing.
vibe_signature_feature: Unused burial poles ring the pit rim, one per burned body. The poles are plain and driven point upward. The poles mark empty ground, since nothing lay below them.
vibe_condition: The ground is sound. The tribes have recently re-lashed it, visibly. It holds, but the next bad season decides it.
vibe_mood: The ground is an honest memorial to a shameful expedient.
vibe_approach: A ring of poles is driven the wrong way up. The ring is visible from a long distance. It has a single meaning.
vibe_senses: A pole shudders when it strikes bone. Two drums answer each other across a long distance. The water is dead: flat, sweetish and wrong. Water this black gives no echo.
player_purpose_hook: The pit lies downwind of everything. The ground is not farmed.
deferred_why: The Burn Ground is over-band: mass-grave-memorial stands at 8/4 province-wide. It is the weakest of the three deeps burial sites.

name: The Kaju Ground
why_founding: The deep-swamp young take an adult name through this trial. Each candidate makes one kill, alone, in water.
why_site_advantages: The reach reliably holds the right animal. The margins are shallow enough for the families to watch. The families cannot help from the margins.
why_occupants_motive: Trial-keepers work the ground. In season, the candidates' families wait at the bank.
why_pressures: The animal population is down. The trial is getting harder. Some read that as a judgement. Two families have sent their young to the coastal trials instead.
why_would_change_if: A failed season would force a change to the rite. The deep-swamp tribes would import animals before they admit the reach is finished.
vibe_silhouette: A marked course runs through dangerous ground. An observation point overlooks the course.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Hide is stretched grey on frames that stand here and there. Blue bioluminescence glows in the shallows.
vibe_materials: No structure is raised here. Worked bone is set into the ground and left. Hide thongs are wet-tied and shrunk tight. Totems of bone and plumage stand at each landing.
vibe_signature_feature: Skulls of every trial kill line the bank. Each skull is mounted with the taker's name. The recent row is shorter than the old one.
vibe_condition: The keepers maintain the skull mounts. They re-tie the frames each season.
vibe_approach: The skull line is visible from the water for four hundred metres.
vibe_senses: Drum-signals carry flat across the water. Rot is held down under cold water. Wet hide dries on the frames.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 567 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.raft-village-lashed (+1.15).
player_purpose_hook: The deep-swamp adult name is taken with one kill. The candidate makes the kill alone in the water, while the families watch from the shallows.

name: The Raid Stone
why_founding: The Raid Stone is a stone for a village's dead. It commemorates the worst raiding year anyone remembers.
why_site_advantages: The stone stands at the landing where the raiders came up.
why_occupants_motive: The stone has no residents. The village maintains it. Maintenance means recutting the names every generation. The argument restarts each time the names are recut.
why_pressures: The names of the raiders are cut on the back of the stone. Cutting raiders' names is not the custom. The raiders' descendants are the settled Naga two days upstream. The settled Naga know the stone is there.
why_would_change_if: Erasing the back would take a vote. The village will not hold that vote. The vote would fail. Everyone would then know it had failed.
vibe_silhouette: One standing stone rises from a bank. Cairns come closer to it year by year.
vibe_palette: The scene is black above and blue below. Green appears nowhere in it. The blue is thin here. Everyone notices. The stake tops are bone-white.
vibe_materials: Cut stone is kept clear of weed by hand. Nothing stands beside it. Carved frills mark the bank as a warning line.
vibe_signature_feature: The victims are named on the front of the stone. The named raiders are cut on the back. The stone is a memorial and an accusation. Readers have polished the back.
vibe_condition: The stone is patched so often that the original work is hard to find. One person plainly keeps it up.
vibe_approach: Visitors read the front first. They find the back only by walking round the stone.
vibe_senses: The hide walls hold warmth after dark. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The air smells of peat, cold and mineral. Birds are silent. Blue light fades as visitors enter.
player_purpose_hook: The stone stands at the landing where the raiders came up.
deferred_why: The Raid Stone is a low-value duplicate of the deeps' memorial vocabulary. The Burn Ground and the grave-cairn lines already carry that vocabulary.

name: The Open Ward
why_founding: A miregaunt holds a bearing in open water. Nothing built stands behind it.
why_site_advantages: The water is open and shallow, off any current route. A route ran past it once.
why_occupants_motive: One miregaunt guards something that no surveyor has found.
why_pressures: Probing under the silt has turned up no footing. The standing theory is that the ward outlived a Horwalli work.
why_would_change_if: The ward is expected to stay as it is. The miregaunt returns to the same stance on the same bearing after each disturbance. Scholars pay for that detail.
vibe_silhouette: The vegetation on the approach has been rearranged. It has not been cleared.
vibe_palette: The scene is black above and blue below. Green appears nowhere in it. Black mud holds a print for a week.
vibe_materials: The materials are raw bog-oak and shell grit, unlashed. Carved frills are pushed into the bank as a warning line.
vibe_signature_feature: Searchers have found no ruin and no cache. The miregaunt guards a patch of open water. It has held that station longer than the villages have stood.
vibe_condition: No structure here can wear. The ground is packed hard where the miregaunt walks.
vibe_mood: The miregaunt stands as a sentry who is posted over open water.
vibe_approach: The miregaunt can be seen from two channels away. It stands still in open water.
vibe_senses: The air is still over the flat. A paddle knocks, then all is quiet. The air smells of wet bone and cold mud.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The miregaunt returns to the same stance on the same bearing. A searcher could follow that direction.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 903 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, culture-clump, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The miregaunt has held this patch of open water since before the villages stood. A way down lies under the water.

name: The Left Camp
why_founding: The Left Camp was abandoned when the route it served silted up.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on a channel that no longer goes anywhere. That is why the cache has survived. Most thieves judge the cache not worth the cost of reaching it.
why_occupants_motive: The camp has no residents. The active camps know the cache is here and have twice sent crews. The crews fell out on the return over how to split the cache.
why_pressures: The takings are still cached here. The crew left suddenly.
why_would_change_if: The camp will stay as it is. The channel will not reopen. The silt that closed the channel is the only reason the site still holds anything.
vibe_silhouette: A fallen palisade line and a cold hearth ring mark the camp. The camp sits on a road bend that is no longer used.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Dredged block is undressed and grey. The blue is thin here. Everyone notices.
vibe_materials: Everything soft has gone from the bone frame that still stands upright. Hide thongs are wet-tied and shrunk tight. Hide covers the roof. Cairn stone weights it down. Plain poles are driven in pairs at the camp edge. Cairns and totems stand behind the poles.
vibe_signature_feature: The rope is still across the dead channel. No traffic worth a stop has come there in twenty years.
vibe_condition: The camp weathers in place. Nothing has been taken or added. The crew abandoned it within a season. The camp has been left untouched since.
vibe_mood: The camp's own gear and works remain standing after its business has ended.
vibe_approach: A rope stretches across dry reeds.
vibe_senses: A pole shudders when it strikes bone. Drum-signals carry flat across the water. The water lies flat, sweetish and stagnant. There is no red. Those raised here notice its absence elsewhere.
player_purpose_hook: The camp stands on a channel that no longer goes anywhere.
deferred_why: The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The Verify/wrap round rebalance applied. The Left Camp is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The North Cut Camp
why_founding: A tribeless Naga camp works the walked track. The track bends round a pond below the bench.
why_site_advantages: The camp sits at a blind bend. Walkers come into view below the bench before they can see the camp.
why_occupants_motive: The camp's Naga are tribeless. They take cargo and rarely kill. A robbed walker comes back next season. If a walker is killed, his tribe comes for the camp.
why_pressures: The settled tribes are blamed for the camp. Cut-Rope's raiders work the same tracks. Long-Water Hold has begun paying the camp not to work its stretch. The payment would ruin the hold if it were known.
why_would_change_if: A peace between the settled tribes and the tribeless would end the camp. Long-Water Hold would stop paying for quiet.
vibe_silhouette: A smoke plume rises above a cut bank. A watch platform stands over the bend of the track.
vibe_palette: Smoke-black dominates above. Dark peat and fern lie below. Hides are stretched on racks by the fire.
vibe_materials: The camp uses cane cut this week and lashed the same hour. Hide thongs are tied wet and left to shrink. The smoked hide is black and stiff. Four grave-cairns stand along the cairn way, one for each death.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp issues a scratched tally-stick receipt for what it takes.
vibe_condition: The camp is well-found. It is hard to reach on purpose.
vibe_approach: A cane gate stands between two totems where the path leaves the track. The watch overlooks the gate.
vibe_senses: A drum-signal carries flat across the pond. The air smells of tar and burnt cane. Hides smoke over the fire.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The camp sells quiet by the season. The buyers would be ruined if the sale were named.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 368 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A cane gate stands under a watch where the track bends. The camp issues a scratched tally-stick receipt for whatever it takes.
watch_reason: Tribeless Naga robbers recognise no law and assess no Owing. They meet a crime with violence.

name: The Reed Gate Camp
why_founding: The Reed Gate Camp is a second camp working the southern route. A group that fell out with the northern camp runs it.
why_site_advantages: The camp sits at a reed narrows with two exits. A boat that flees one exit is met at the other.
why_occupants_motive: The crew is worse than their northern rivals, by their own account.
why_pressures: The two camps are raiding each other's takings. The southern crew has started killing where the northern crew would not.
why_would_change_if: A merger or a war would resolve the feud. Either outcome doubles the pressure on the ferry stage that feeds both routes.
vibe_silhouette: A reed-gate is strung across the water. A low camp lies behind it, deliberately hard to see.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift in it. White shell grit lies at the landing. Cold blue shows on the underside of the piles.
vibe_materials: The camp uses bone-handled tools and has no permanent build. The cane-split cord is replaced constantly. The smoked hide is black and stiff. Carved frills are set as boundary markers.
vibe_signature_feature: The crew flies a tally-stick pattern copied from the northern camp. The copy is bad enough that northern polers spot it.
vibe_condition: The camp is solid where it is used daily. It is rotten a step off the path.
vibe_approach: The forged marks are visible on the gate poles.
vibe_senses: Cold comes up off the black water. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The dead water is flat and sweetish.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 373 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, route, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: A boat that flees one exit of the reed narrows is met at the other.
deferred_why: The place was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The place is a lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Deck Camp
why_founding: The Deck Camp is built under a boardwalk. It takes from foot traffic, not from boats.
why_site_advantages: The camp lies beneath a long walkway. It has no line of sight from either end.
why_occupants_motive: A small crew works by dropping through the deck. The crew must know which planks are loose. A villager in the village above must tell them.
why_pressures: The walkway village knows about the camp and takes a share. The village has begun to depend on the share in years when the reed cutting is poor.
why_would_change_if: Exposure of the share would end the village's standing in the region. The far end of the spine, the poor end where the loose planks are, would take the blame.
vibe_silhouette: The camp shows no plume at all. It is built underneath the walkway that it taxes.
vibe_palette: The water is black with blue light under the surface. The blue light is doubled in still water. White shell grit lies at the landing.
vibe_materials: Hide over paddles set as poles forms the tents, struck in an hour. Sinew and hide lashing holds the camp together. Hide covers the roof, weighted with cairn stone. Crocodile skulls sit on the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp lies entirely underneath the road that it robs. Walkers pass over the top of it. The deck boards above the camp's fire are scorched.
vibe_condition: The camp is sound. Its lashings are recently and visibly redone. Everything has been replaced at least once, as the camp's doctrine says it should be.
vibe_approach: The scorched boards are the tell for any walker who looks down.
vibe_senses: Warmth stays in the hide walls after dark. A drum-signal carries flat across the water. The air smells of tar and burnt cane. The air this deep in the swamp carries no sap smell.
player_purpose_hook: The camp lies beneath a long walkway. It has no line of sight from either end.
deferred_why: The place was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The place is a lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Cut-Rope
why_founding: Cut-Rope is a camp of tribeless Naga. The Naga once ran raids out along the routes. They have narrowed to a single camp that holds the water road itself.
why_site_advantages: The creek head still reaches three poling routes. It hides the boat sheds from any approach.
why_occupants_motive: The band prices the road by hull and cargo. The band answers to the raj-kaal who runs it.
why_pressures: Every fixed Naga village nearby has cut ties with the camp. The camp trades only with the coastal brokers who buy stolen cargo.
why_would_change_if: The raj-kaal's death would scatter the band inside a season. Two attempts on the raj-kaal have failed.
vibe_silhouette: A stake fence faces the water. Boat sheds behind it hold more craft than the camp has people.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. The camp is hide-brown and bone, with no other colours.
vibe_materials: Bone-frame huts stand under smoked hide. The gut lashing is rank and strong. Seams are sealed with tar and ash. Crocodile skulls sit on the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: Every boat in the sheds carries the same repainted mark. The mark was taken from a different owner each time.
vibe_condition: The camp is prosperous and badly finished. New goods are crammed into old houses.
vibe_approach: The shed roofs show through the reeds long before the fence does.
vibe_senses: Mud pulls at the foot with every step. Bone clacks in the wind. Rot lies under cold water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The band keeps receipts. The shed ledger names every owner that the band has robbed.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 233 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: The camp sits on the water road. It takes a cut from the laden craft that pass.

name: Long-Water Hold
why_founding: Long-Water Hold is the village of a settled Naga tribe. The tribe tends a Hist, villages and fields. The tribe quarrels with its own tribeless relatives.
why_site_advantages: The hold stands on firm ground on the main poling route of the inner swamp. Its landing is deep enough for laden craft.
why_occupants_motive: The people of the hold want the road trade. Tribeless kin who rob the road undermine that trade.
why_pressures: Outsiders arrive assuming that the hold's people are brigands. The hold pays the northern camp for quiet. The hold would win a war against the camp but could not afford it.
why_would_change_if: A settlement with the tribeless would change how the whole southern interior travels. It would cost the coastal escort trade its best market.
vibe_silhouette: The dwellings are markedly larger than ordinary ones. They stand on a long dry hold. Pens and drying racks stand among them. A drum frame stands at the centre.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black, with a slow blue drift in it. The black mud holds a print for a week. The blue is thin here.
vibe_materials: The posts are bog-oak, the walls are cane and the lintels are bone. The gut lashing is replaced each season. Smoked hide is black and stiff. Totems of bone and plumage stand at the landings.
vibe_signature_feature: Door heights, bench spans and cook pots are built to a larger scale. An ordinary-sized visitor stands about as high as a child of the hold.
vibe_condition: The buildings are sound. The big timbers are original.
vibe_mood: The hold is hospitable. It is built to a larger scale.
vibe_approach: A visitor notices the doorways before the people.
vibe_senses: The air is completely still. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. Disturbed mud smells of sulphur.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The hold pays its tribeless kin quiet money. The payments are hidden in a ledger. A visitor could be asked to audit the ledger.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LN07 · tier-3; LN08 · tier-3; PP16 · tier-3
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 116 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on danger, parent, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'.
player_purpose_hook: The doors and benches are a size too large for an ordinary visitor. The hold trades with whoever pays the toll.
siting_note: The hold is plotted on the boundary between the Naga-Kur and mercantile-coast cultures. It lies outside the zone interior. The hold's economy is selling quiet to the coastal escort trade. The trade needs the hold within reach of the coast road's market.

name: The Staking Village
why_founding: The Staking Village services the burial fields of the deep swamp. Its people drive and re-drive the poles of the fields. They work after dark, when the blights are readable.
why_site_advantages: The village is central to nine fields. It stands on a rise that stays dry. The rise has room to store stakes in quantity.
why_occupants_motive: The occupants are stake-setters. They work nights and sleep through the day.
why_pressures: Since Umbriel there is more work than there are setters. The backlog is measurable in risings. Villages bid against each other for a night's work. The poorest fields go unstaked.
why_would_change_if: Losing a generation of setters would let the fields go. The whole grave discipline of the Naga-Kur runs through the rota of this village.
vibe_silhouette: The graves of the village have the high ground.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black, with a slow blue drift in it. The cane bundles are yellowing. Cold blue shows on the underside of the piles.
vibe_materials: The posts are bog-oak, the walls are cane and the lintels are bone. The hide thongs are wet-tied and shrunk hard. Every building is left unsealed, because the buildings are meant to leak. Grave-cairns step up the bank, one course per death. Stacked pole-stock lies under every hut.
vibe_signature_feature: The village sleeps at noon. It is fully at work at midnight. Shielded lamps light it blue. The lamps do not carry far.
vibe_condition: well-found; hard to reach
vibe_mood: The village is nocturnal. Its people are unimpressed by the work.
vibe_approach: In daylight the village reads as abandoned.
vibe_senses: Lamp shields knock on a boat thwart. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. The air smells of tar and burnt cane.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The village serves nine fields. A bidding rota leaves the poorest fields unstaked. A night crew then fails to come back.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LN03 · tier-3; LN09 · tier-3; LN10 · tier-3; LN11 · tier-3; province system · tier-1
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 247 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: In daylight the village looks abandoned. The crews work the stake fields at midnight. They work then because the blights are readable.

name: The Egg Camp
why_founding: Egg-poachers work the nesting grounds of the zone. They work for a coastal buyer.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands between three nesting sites. It stands on a creek with a fast exit.
why_occupants_motive: The poachers take clutches that the villages are counting. A coastal buyer sells the eggs as a delicacy.
why_pressures: The villages treat egg-taking as they would treat child-taking. Villagers have staked two poachers alive. The poaching has not stopped.
why_would_change_if: One caught crew would end the trade for a season. It would give the villages a name to send to the coast. The buyer has paid to prevent it.
vibe_silhouette: A drying line stands in the camp. Crates are stacked in the open.
vibe_palette: The water is black, with blue light under the surface. Drift bone and drift wood lie in the same line. Blue shows in the roots and not in the water.
vibe_materials: The cane is cut this week and lashed the same hour. The hide thongs are tied wet and shrunk hard. Smoked hide is black and stiff. A few plain poles are driven at the landing. A cairn and a totem stand there that the poachers did not put there.
vibe_signature_feature: Packed clutches lie in wet moss crates. The crates are labelled by species and by buyer. One crate holds a species that the villages forbid taking.
vibe_condition: The camp was cut this season. It is not meant to last another.
vibe_approach: Crates are stacked in the open. They cannot be hidden and kept warm.
vibe_senses: Reeds hiss and drums sound under the hiss. The air is peat, cold and mineral. Wet moss and shell smell strongly.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 424 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Crates are stacked in the open because eggs must be kept warm. One crate is labelled with a species that no village here permits taking.

name: The Drag
why_founding: The Drag is a slipway. Craft are dragged past the narrows on it. Crews do not run the narrows.
why_site_advantages: It is the shortest firm crossing of the neck between two channels. The rollers have been here two centuries.
why_occupants_motive: A drag crew charges by the hull. The crew keeps the rollers greased with fish oil. It buys the oil from the drawdown village that competes with it.
why_pressures: The crew and the drawdown village compete for the same traffic. Each repeats the other's accidents to the traffic.
why_would_change_if: A cut channel would end both trades. The two rivals have twice sent a joint delegation against the survey.
vibe_silhouette: A worn, greased timber slipway climbs out of the water. White water runs beside it.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Blue glow shows only where the water is disturbed. Hide is stretched grey on frames. Black smoke stands low.
vibe_materials: Lashed cane sits over black bog-oak sills. The lashing is sinew and hide. Smoked hide is black and stiff. Crocodile skulls sit on the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: Two centuries of hulls have worn a polished groove in the bog-oak rollers. The crew charge by the depth that a keel sits in the groove.
vibe_condition: The slipway is kept up. Repairs are small and frequent.
vibe_mood: The mood is commercial. Prices are set by the hull.
vibe_approach: The groove is visible across the neck like a path.
vibe_senses: Rollers squeal under a laden hull. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The air smells of tar and burnt cane.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Two crews claim the right to move laden craft past the shallows. A season's trade depends on the claim.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: Two centuries of hulls have worn a groove in the bog-oak rollers. The crew price each haul by the depth that a keel sits in the groove.

name: The Lashing
why_founding: Households lashed their rafts together for the wet season. They did so in a backwater that was too poor for a neighbouring hold to claim.
why_site_advantages: The backwater is sheltered and has no owner. That water suited the lashing. It now suits whatever settled over the wreck after it went down.
why_occupants_motive: The households did not choose the place. The rafts sank still tied to each other. The wreck now draws creatures that feed on the drowned.
why_pressures: The lashing-master kept a knotted cord. The cord was the sole record of the mooring order. It went down with the rafts.
why_would_change_if: Nothing above the water marks where The Lashing sank. A diver would have to know already where to look.
vibe_silhouette: The waterline shows a clear surface. A raft-mass shape reads from below.
vibe_palette: The water is black, with blue light under the surface. The bottom is bone-pale. Cairn stones are grey and stacked.
vibe_materials: Bone plate and vine cord have gone slack and drift. Tar-and-ash lap-seams still hold the frames together underwater.
vibe_signature_feature: The rafts lie on the bottom still lashed. They keep the mooring order that the cord recorded.
vibe_condition: The wreck is intact below the waterline. It is stripped above the waterline.
vibe_approach: The surface reads as open backwater. The water goes dark fast over the wreck.
vibe_senses: Cold presses in on the dive. Bone plate clacks loose underwater. Light reaches only the first few strokes down.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The drowned raft village lies on the far field circuit. A missing night crew was last plausibly heading there.
why_site_won: The village is drowned and its entrance is underwater. The dry landing is on the bank at 2195.2, 4436.2, the land within 25 m of body 1208-2442 that lies closest to the old spot. The old spot sat at 2185.2, 4367.6, 68.6 m from that body. The landing is 69.3 m from it.
player_purpose_hook: A raft village sank still tied together in one night. Its knotted mooring-cord was lost with it.

name: The Raided Camp
why_founding: The camp is a village that ran from the raiding Naga two years ago.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the first defensible ground that the refugees reached. The ground has no owner. No tribe has had to decide what the refugees are.
why_occupants_motive: The occupants are waiting to hear whether their village still stands.
why_pressures: Two years have passed. The camp is becoming a settlement. The children have started calling it by a name. The adults refuse to use that name.
why_would_change_if: News either way ends the camp. A poler has seen the village. Two different parties have paid him to keep silent about what he saw.
vibe_silhouette: The shelters are pitched too close together. The ground is ground that the elder would not have chosen. A lookout stands on the single rise.
vibe_palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Hide-brown shelters crowd the one rise. The blue light is thin over the rise.
vibe_materials: Tools are bone-handled and everything is built to be temporary. Hide thongs are tied wet and shrunk hard. Tar and ash are paid into the laps. Crocodile skulls sit on the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: The camp follows the plan of the village that the refugees left. Tents stand house for house.
vibe_condition: The tents are two years old. They have been mended twice.
vibe_mood: The refugees have waited two years to hear.
vibe_approach: The camp is a tent village. Its street pattern is far too formal for a camp.
vibe_senses: Cold comes off black water at every hour. The air smells of smoke, wet hide and too many people. A lookout tries a horn twice a night.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 74 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.ferry-stage-guide-hire (+0.80).
player_purpose_hook: The tents are pitched in the street plan of the abandoned village. They stand house for house.

name: The Warren
why_founding: The Warren is a gallery beneath a burial ground.
why_site_advantages: The roots reach the graves. The burial ground feeds the gallery. The gallery undermines the burial ground.
why_occupants_motive: Bog blights live in the gallery in numbers. They work steadily upward. They stay below by day. The village above has held on that account.
why_pressures: The village above is driving a stake ring. It loses ground each year.
why_would_change_if: Clearing and restaking the gallery would put the Naga-Kur in a debt. No amount of trade buys that debt.
vibe_silhouette: The entrance is a burrow mouth widened from below.
vibe_palette: The colour is black. Blue shows only at the waterline. Olive weed is matted over the sills.
vibe_materials: Unworked black mud lies over stone. A roof of matted root covers it. Drift bone is laid along the high line. The polers say that the lack of a marker is deliberate.
vibe_signature_feature: The gallery is hollow root under a pulled pole field. Ramps that the swamp made itself lead through it. The risen went down into it. They followed the roots back toward the village.
vibe_condition: The gallery below is left unmaintained. The village re-drives the stake ring above each year.
vibe_mood: The blights of the burial ground live below it.
vibe_approach: A mouth opens in the middle of a pole field. Fresh plain poles are driven in a ring around it.
vibe_senses: The floor gives under the foot where the blight has been through it. Bone clacks on bone somewhere ahead. Rot is held down under cold water.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 1110 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: A mouth opens in the middle of a pole field. Fresh poles are driven in a ring around it. The risen went down and followed the roots back toward the village.

name: The Blue Flood
why_founding: The Blue Flood is a flooded branch of the root layer. It lies under the ground of the Naga-Kur.
why_site_advantages: It connects the village to three of its stake-fields. It does so without crossing open water.
why_occupants_motive: The Naga-Kur use the gallery and do not advertise it. They send their young through it once. The passage is part of the rite that names them.
why_pressures: The gallery is the escape route of the tribe and its secret. The pilgrim traffic to the tribe's tree now passes within a hundred metres of one of its mouths.
why_would_change_if: Discovery by raiders would change how the village is defended. The tribe would have to choose between sealing its own bolt-hole and holding it under arms.
vibe_silhouette: The surface shows an unbroken stretch of water. A blue glow rises through four feet of black water.
vibe_palette: The place is blue-lit and otherwise colourless. Blue light doubles in still water. Silt is the colour of ash.
vibe_materials: The place is left unbuilt. Black water, bog-oak and bone are sorted by the drawdown. Totems are set facing inward, which is unusual.
vibe_signature_feature: The flower fall of the Naga-Kur tree washes into the gallery. The flower fall lights it blue for its whole length. The gallery is a swimmable tunnel with its own light.
vibe_condition: Everything has been replaced at least once, as doctrine says it should be. It is patched so often that the original work is hard to find.
vibe_mood: The gallery is cold and luminous. It is navigable without a lamp.
vibe_approach: A submerged mouth lies under the village landing. Entry is by dive.
vibe_senses: Warmth stays in the hide walls after dark. The drum that should answer stays silent. Disturbed mud smells of sulphur. The light shows nothing green.
player_purpose_hook: The gallery connects the village to three of its stake-fields. It does so without crossing open water.
deferred_why: The place was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget (docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2) after its executor pass. The place is a lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Drowned Lanes
why_founding: Root growth followed three channels. The roots joined the three channels underground.
why_site_advantages: The Drowned Lanes are the fast route across the zone. The route can be used by a diver only.
why_occupants_motive: Nothing lives in the Drowned Lanes. The fish avoid the lanes. The guides treat the fish avoiding the lanes as the only reliable warning that the place gives.
why_pressures: Travellers take the wrong branch. Their bodies are found downstream. The branch that kills looks the most used. The used branch is the narrower one.
why_would_change_if: A silt fall would close the fatal branch. Closing the fatal branch would make the lanes safe. A silt fall would also add a day to the stake-setters' circuit. Opinions on a silt fall are not unanimous.
vibe_silhouette: A root mouth stands at water level. The lanes behind the mouth are flooded to chest height.
