vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow shows on wet bone, with black beyond. Bone-white stake tops show above the water. Blue shows at the waterline and the space above is dark. There is no red anywhere, by custom and by tree.
vibe_materials: The place is made of silt, cane wrack and whatever the water has stripped away. A drum frame stands at the landing with no drum in it.
vibe_signature_feature: A three-way flooded junction is the signature feature. The current chooses the swimmer's exit unless the swimmer can hold against it.
vibe_condition: The place is clean and ordered. It is slightly too quiet for its size. Strangers passing keep it, so it is odd but never derelict.
vibe_mood: The lanes form a one-way system. A swimmer must read the system before committing.
vibe_approach: Three mouths open onto the lanes. A swimmer can swim back out through a single mouth.
vibe_senses: Mud closes over the foot at every step. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. The air smells of tar and burnt cane. Nothing green shows in the light.
player_purpose_hook: The Drowned Lanes are the fast route across the zone. The route can be used by a diver only.
deferred_why: This region ran over its coverage-doc record budget in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2 after its executor pass. The record was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. It is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Root-Whisper Village
why_founding: The Barsaebic Ayleids destroyed the tribe here. The Ayleids harvested the tribe's souls into the Remnant of Argon. The Hist did not die but slept. While it slept it was called the Dreaming Tree. At the end of the Second Era the souls were returned. The village was re-founded on its own ground, below the xanmeer Vakka-Bok.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on East Deepmire ground that the tribe never left. A pre-Duskfall xanmeer stands above the village. The xanmeer can be seen from a distance and confines the approach to one line.
why_occupants_motive: The tribe was rebuilt out of returned souls. The tribe lives on the ground where it was killed. The tree stands at the centre of the village. The tribe exists because the tree survived.
why_pressures: The Hist is centuries old but speaks like a hatchling. Its own tree-minder treats it as convalescent. Cyrodilic Collections helped resurrect the tribe. Cyrodilic Collections still treats the village as its find.
why_would_change_if: If the Dreaming Tree failed a second time, there would be no second Remnant. The tribe organises its whole year around that risk.
traversal_fallback: The fallback is to pole the long way round the plateau foot. The detour takes a day.
vibe_silhouette: The village is low and stands on cleared ground. A stepped xanmeer stands at each end of the village. One tree stands between the two xanmeers. The tree is too small for its own trunk-scar.
vibe_palette: The shade is olive with unusually even blue light. Black water fills the cuts. Pale new cane stands against very old grey stone.
vibe_materials: The village is cane and bog-oak, raised new within living memory. It stands on the footprint of the old village. A trained-root core is at the centre, which the tree is still growing. Totems of bone and plumage stand at both xanmeer ends. The builders salvaged no stone from either xanmeer, deliberately.
vibe_signature_feature: The Dreaming Tree is a Hist with a hatchling's voice and an elder's trunk. The Hist speaks for two hours each day. The whole village times its day around those two hours.
vibe_condition: The work is new throughout. No timber here predates the return.
vibe_mood: The mood is careful. The village is ninety years old at most.
vibe_approach: The approach runs between the two xanmeers. The tribe keeps the line clear. Both xanmeers overlook an arrival.
vibe_senses: The ground under the tree is warm, but not beyond its shade. A single small chime is kept for the tree. The air smells of new-cut cane and wet stone. No drums sound at any hour.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The quest locations are LOC root_whisper.village and LOC root_whisper.dreaming_tree.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LN12 · tier-3; LN13 · tier-3; LN14 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 931 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump-yielded, bound, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2-region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The Hist has a hatchling's voice and an elder's trunk. The village was re-founded at the end of the Second Era. The Ayleids had harvested the villagers' souls. Those souls were returned.

name: The Shut Meer
why_founding: The Shut Meer is a xanmeer. Its vakka mechanisms still work.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer stands on a rise in black water. The building overlooks every approach.
why_occupants_motive: The defences hold the xanmeer. There are no squatters and no den.
why_pressures: Four expeditions have gone in over fifty years. No party has come back. The people of the nearest village keep the count. They charge a fee to recite it.
why_would_change_if: The xanmeer stays shut unless the mechanisms fail. The vakka stones that drive the mechanisms are worth more to a coastal broker than the contents.
vibe_silhouette: The building is a terraced mass. Its frontage is intact and unbroken. No path leads to it.
vibe_palette: The water is black until lamplight turns it blue. The dredged block is undressed and grey. Green shows only on the weed.
vibe_materials: The walls are dressed pre-Duskfall block. The block is unbroken and still tight at the joints. Carved frills are set as boundary markers at the landing.
vibe_signature_feature: The threshold is a debris field of four expeditions' equipment. The villagers keep a board at the landing. The board names all four parties.
vibe_condition: The building is intact. The frontage is unbroken.
vibe_mood: The building is shut. Fifty years of warning stand at the door.
vibe_approach: The board stands at the landing. The landing is well short of the first sight of the building.
vibe_senses: Cold comes up off the black water. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. Rot is held down under cold water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The tribe beside the xanmeer will permit a single entry. The party can bring out whatever a single trip can carry.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 1209 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, region, remote.
player_purpose_hook: The Shut Meer is a stepped stone xanmeer. Its old locking mechanisms still work. The building overlooks every approach to it.
deferred_why: This region ran over its coverage-doc record budget in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2 after its executor pass. The record was deferred in the verify/wrap round rebalance. It is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Adder Banks
why_founding: Moon adders den along a stretch of bank. The bank catches what little moonlight the zone gets.
why_site_advantages: The banks are open with a clear sky line. A clear sky line is rare in this zone.
why_occupants_motive: Adders live on the banks. Venom-takers work the adders for the daril trade. The takers work at moonrise. The adders come to the open bank at moonrise.
why_pressures: The takers are unlicensed. The people of the nearby village want a cut. They have begun burning the bank margin. The burning drives the adders onto the village's own ground.
why_would_change_if: A licence deal would make the banks a works site and end their use as a lair. The deal would put the daril trade of three regions behind one village's gate.
vibe_silhouette: Shed skins lie on the banks. The skins are of a size that halts most walkers.
vibe_palette: The black water breaks white where a pole passes. Cold blue shows on the underside of the piles. Bone-white stake tops show.
vibe_materials: No work stands here. The ground is peat, undressed block fallen from elsewhere and bone. Carved frills pushed into the bank form a warning line. One pole is left standing in the mud.
vibe_signature_feature: The adders come out on clear nights only. The site is empty and harmless about two nights in five.
vibe_condition: No work stands here beyond a warning line. The takers renew the warning line each season.
vibe_mood: The banks are dangerous only under a clear sky.
vibe_approach: The banks are bare and pale. They lie under an open sky.
vibe_senses: Shed skin drags under the boot. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. Disturbed mud smells of sulphur.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 179 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, culture-clump, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The bank is open and catches moonlight. The adders come out onto it on clear nights.
deferred_why: Adder venom (daril) is already sited at the fermentary and the Kaju ground. The bank itself is dressing.

name: The Black Eye
why_founding: The Black Eye is a collapse in the root layer. The collapse is drowned and lies in the middle of a reed flat.
why_site_advantages: The swamp has flooded this hole and left it unfilled. It is one of a handful of such holes in the province.
why_occupants_motive: Divers visit occasionally. The same three divers come each season. The divers take no passengers.
why_pressures: The hole goes into the root layer. A body put in here has twice surfaced two zones away.
why_would_change_if: A dry cycle would expose the rim. The exposed rim would make the hole enterable on foot.
vibe_silhouette: The rim is the visible feature. The vegetation changes around the rim.
vibe_palette: The scene is black, with blue only in the water. Olive weed is matted round the rim.
vibe_materials: No structure stands here. The bottom is cold silt and the rim is fallen block. A drum frame stands at the landing with no drum in it.
vibe_signature_feature: From the surface the Black Eye is a round hole in a reed flat. The reeds stop at its edge.
vibe_condition: The hole is unchanged. The rim has not moved in living memory.
vibe_mood: The hole is too round to be natural.
vibe_approach: The hole is invisible from more than a pace.
vibe_senses: Cold comes up off black water. Rot is held down under cold water. Reed stems knock at the rim.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 395 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: The Black Eye is a perfectly round hole of black water in a reed flat. The reeds stop dead at the edge as if cut.

name: The Emptying House
why_founding: The Emptying House is a Sithis temple in the deep swamp. The temple practises the doctrine at its least metaphorical.
why_site_advantages: Black water lies on all sides. No neighbour is close enough to object. The temple has one landing. The house itself overlooks the landing.
why_occupants_motive: Nisswo preach a sermon here. The coastal houses disown the sermon.
why_pressures: The interior tribes tolerate the temple and do not attend. The settled Naga forbid their young to go. The young attend in order to defy them.
why_would_change_if: A closure would need an authority that the deep swamp recognises. The coastal Nisswo who could claim that authority stay on the coast.
vibe_silhouette: Terraced stone stands above the canopy.
vibe_palette: Black water lies at the stair foot. Bone-white terraces rise above it. Blue glow is held in the lower chambers. Everything else is grey.
vibe_materials: The walls are dressed pre-Duskfall stone. The stone is kept swept and not repaired. Bone is set into the floor in courses. Fresh cane matting lies over stone left unwashed.
vibe_signature_feature: The sanctuary floor drains to a single hole. The hole lies under the altar stone.
vibe_condition: swept daily, unrepaired
vibe_approach: Stone terraces stand above the canopy. The stair comes down to one landing.
vibe_senses: Cold stone comes up through the feet in a country with no cold. A slow drum is kept up for the dead, all night, every night. The air smells of old blood and cold water.
why_site_won: open water in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 1086 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: The Nisswo here preach a sermon that the coastal houses disown. The sanctuary floor drains to a single hole under the altar stone.

name: The Block House
why_founding: A household lives in a dredged xanmeer block chamber. Haulers brought the chamber here as fill. The haulers left the chamber where it lay afterward.
why_site_advantages: The chamber is a dry stone box in a zone with almost no dry stone. It is the sole house here that does not need rebuilding every seven years.
why_occupants_motive: One family lives here. The family found the chamber and said nothing.
why_pressures: The chamber is stolen sacred material. Everyone pretends it is not. The tending clan two channels away pretends too. The tending clan has counted its blocks and knows that one is missing.
why_would_change_if: A tribal claim would evict the family tomorrow. The block would then have to be hauled back. Everyone avoids being responsible for organising the haul.
vibe_silhouette: One lit window shows in a block of undressed stone. The stone was never a house.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. White shell grit lies at the landing. Blue shows in the roots and nowhere else.
vibe_materials: Cane bundles are pegged into bog-oak. Root is used where root will grow. Sinew and hide lashing binds the work. There is no seal at all, because the house is meant to leak. Plain poles are driven in a short line where the old field was. The poles are left untended.
vibe_signature_feature: The house is a single carved chamber lying on its side. The family live with the floor carvings on their wall.
vibe_condition: The house is clean and ordered. It is slightly too quiet for its size. It is solid where used daily and rotten a step off the path.
vibe_approach: The house is a stone box in a reed bed. Its door is cut in the wrong face.
vibe_senses: Mud closes over the foot at every step. Paddle knock breaks the quiet. The air smells of peat, cold and mineral. There is no red. Everyone raised here notices its absence elsewhere.
player_purpose_hook: The house is a dry stone box in a zone with almost no dry stone.
deferred_why: The house is tier-4 dressing. The same beat reads better as a dressing row inside the Pale Village.

name: The Turning Stone
why_founding: The Turning Stone is a mechanism of unknown make. It stands in water and still moves.
why_site_advantages: The mechanism is bedded in the swamp floor. It lies at the Horwalli works' outfall. The location suggests a link between the mechanism and the works.
why_occupants_motive: The Turning Stone has no occupants. The nearest village sends one person each year to mark its new position. The duty was invented three generations ago. The villagers have never questioned the duty.
why_pressures: The stone turns a quarter-revolution each year. The villagers do not know what happens when the turning completes. The marks show that it has turned three quarters since the marking began.
why_would_change_if: No attempt to stop the turning has worked. The Horwalli works upstream stops and starts on roughly the same cycle. One keeper has noticed the match. The villagers do not believe the keeper.
vibe_silhouette: The mechanism is plainly made and does not belong in its surroundings.
vibe_palette: The water is black and the bottom is bone-pale. The cane bundles are yellowing. The blue light is doubled in the still water.
vibe_materials: Worked block stands upright, set by unnamed builders and left. The totems face inward, which is unusual.
vibe_signature_feature: The stone has moved a quarter-turn in the lifetime of the oldest person who watches it. The villages have started keeping a written record of the angle.
vibe_condition: The site is well-found and defended by being hard to reach. It sags on one side and is shored on that side only.
vibe_mood: The mood is patient and mechanical. The stone may be counting down.
vibe_approach: A stone drum stands in open water. A scratched scale runs around its base.
vibe_senses: The deck lifts underfoot as boats pass. The drum that should answer does not answer. Rot is held down under cold water. No dry ground lies within a day. The blue light thins on the approach.
player_purpose_hook: The mechanism is bedded in the swamp floor at the Horwalli works' outfall. The location suggests a link between the mechanism and the works.
deferred_why: Verify/wrap round rebalance ran this region over its coverage-doc record budget. The budget is set in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The record is lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Reed-Stand
why_founding: Reed-Stand is a reed-cutting village on a wide shallow flat. The villagers work with knives, racks and fires only.
why_site_advantages: Reed-Stand has the largest withy stand in the zone.
why_occupants_motive: The cutters supply thatch and cordage to four regions. Buyers pay in rice and salt. The zone grows neither rice nor salt.
why_pressures: The cutters cut the stand faster than it regrows. Coastal orders drive the cutting. The village cannot refuse the orders without losing the buyer for good.
why_would_change_if: A cutting ban would idle the village. The boardwalk villages' own withy cannot roof half the interior without Reed-Stand's supply.
vibe_silhouette: Drying racks and stacked bundles show across the shallows long before the huts do.
vibe_palette: The water is black with blue light under the surface. The cane bundles are yellowing. The blue light is thin here. Locals notice.
vibe_materials: Posts are bog-oak, walls are cane and lintels are bone. Gut lashing stinks and holds. Tar and ash are paid into every lap. Racks, retting frames and a bank of smoke-fires take up more of the village than the houses do.
vibe_signature_feature: The village is invisible from three sides. The reed is left standing tall around it. The cutters cut only the channel face.
vibe_condition: The site is well-found and defended by being hard to reach. Strangers who pass through keep it, so it is odd but never derelict.
vibe_approach: A visitor comes round the reed and the village is simply there.
vibe_senses: The air does not move at all. Two drums answer a long way apart. Rot is held down under cold water. No red shows. Locals notice its absence elsewhere.
player_purpose_hook: Reed-Stand has the largest withy stand in the zone.
deferred_why: Verify/wrap round rebalance ran this region over its coverage-doc record budget. The budget is set in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The record is lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Black-Piles
why_founding: Black-Piles is a stilt village on the drawdown reach of the inner swamp's outflow. The water there drops eight feet between seasons.
why_site_advantages: Water moves twice daily and flushes the channel. The channel holds the only clean water for kilometres.
why_occupants_motive: The fishers work the falling water and sleep through the rise. Their waking life runs out of step with their neighbours'.
why_pressures: The drawdown brings down unwanted things from upstream. These include bodies from the narrows and spoil from the dredgers. Once it brought a stake with its bindings cut.
why_would_change_if: A silted channel would end the flushing and the village. The dredging spoil upstream is silting the channel now. The village has said so. It cannot prove it.
vibe_silhouette: Black pile-tops form a slow curve. The deck line above them steps up twice.
vibe_palette: The scene is black above and blue below, with no green anywhere. The blue light is bright enough for reading. The cairn stones are grey and stacked.
vibe_materials: Posts are bog-oak, walls are cane and lintels are bone. Gut lashing stinks and holds. Smoked hide is black and stiff. Plain poles are driven along the bank above the tide, where the old field was.
vibe_signature_feature: The piles are black bog-oak and older than the houses on them. The village has been rebuilt four times on the same legs.
vibe_condition: Everything has been replaced at least once, as doctrine requires. The village is sound and recently, visibly re-lashed.
vibe_approach: The pile line reads as a fence across the channel.
vibe_senses: A pole shudders when it finds bone. Reed hiss sounds, with drums beneath it. The water is dead, flat and sweetish. The light has nothing green in it.
player_purpose_hook: Water moves twice daily and flushes the channel. The channel holds the only clean water for kilometres.
deferred_why: Verify/wrap round rebalance ran this region over its coverage-doc record budget. The budget is set in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The record is lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Xal-Kuur
why_founding: Xal-Kuur is a xanmeer entirely under the swamp. Its terraces are intact below the silt line.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer sank level, so the whole structure is preserved and enterable. Looters have stripped the region's other xanmeers from above, but they have not stripped Xal-Kuur.
why_occupants_motive: Nothing that breathes occupies Xal-Kuur. The tending villages take this as proof of consecration. The divers take it as proof of a sealed atmosphere.
why_pressures: The silt rises a hand's width a decade and will close the entrances. The dredging outfit two channels away has offered to clear them for a share.
why_would_change_if: A dredging would open the xanmeer. Three villages would count the dredging as sacrilege.
vibe_silhouette: A terrace corner breaks the surface. Otherwise a geometric shadow shows under the water.
vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow shows on wet bone, with black beyond. The pale bone is worked and stacked by size. The blue light is bright enough for reading.
vibe_materials: A bone frame still stands upright with everything soft gone from it. The lashing is sinew and hide. Smoked hide is black and stiff. Crocodile skulls sit on the pile heads.
vibe_signature_feature: The topmost terrace lies one metre under the water. At low water a visitor can walk a stone floor in ankle-deep swamp. The building falls away beneath the visitor's feet.
vibe_condition: The xanmeer is drowned and silted. It is slowly being taken apart by the current.
vibe_mood: Xal-Kuur is the underwater programme's centrepiece. It is a whole building, entirely submerged.
vibe_approach: A flat hard patch lies in soft ground. The patch is three hundred metres wide.
vibe_senses: Cold comes up off black water. The drum that should answer does not answer. Silence fills the place where birds should be.
player_purpose_hook: The xanmeer sank level, so the whole structure is preserved and can be entered.
deferred_why: Verify/wrap round rebalance ran this region over its coverage-doc record budget. The budget is set in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The record is lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Blue Terrace
why_founding: The Blue Terrace is a xanmeer tended by pilgrims. The pilgrims are coming to the Naga-Kur's tree.
why_site_advantages: The xanmeer lies on the pilgrim water route, at the last mooring.
why_occupants_motive: The Blue Terrace has no owner. A rota of strangers tends it. Each stranger tends it while waiting for the water. Each stranger counts the work as part of the pilgrimage.
why_pressures: The Naga-Kur consider the pilgrim traffic a nuisance and the tending a courtesy. They have never said which they would miss more.
why_would_change_if: A closure of the pilgrimage would end the tending in a decade. The ruin would then go the way of the broken meer upstream within two decades.
vibe_silhouette: Terraced massing rises above the canopy. The tenders keep the terraces clear of vegetation. It is the province's premier built landmark.
vibe_palette: The scene is black above and blue below, with no green anywhere. White shell grit lies at the landing. The blue light is doubled in still water.
vibe_materials: Cane and hide have collapsed, but the bog-oak posts are still true. Gut lashing stinks and holds. Hide over the roof is weighted with cairn stone. Plain poles are driven along the causeway, where the old field was.
vibe_signature_feature: Pilgrims leave a blue-glazed offering shard on each visit. After three centuries the lowest terrace is entirely paved in shards.
vibe_condition: The frame survives. Everything soft has gone. Robbers took everything portable long ago.
vibe_mood: People with no claim to the xanmeer keep it well.
vibe_approach: The blue terrace catches what light there is. It is visible from the water.
vibe_senses: The air does not move at all. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. Smoked hide and wet bone smell strongly. No red shows. Locals notice its absence elsewhere.
player_purpose_hook: The xanmeer lies on the pilgrim water route, at the last mooring.
deferred_why: Verify/wrap round rebalance ran this region over its coverage-doc record budget. The budget is set in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The record is lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Dredging Party
why_founding: The Dredging Party is an outfit that dredges drowned sites. The outfit does not enter the sites.
why_site_advantages: The camp lies between two drowned villages and a submerged xanmeer.
why_occupants_motive: The dredgers have realised that lifting the swamp floor beats diving it. Financiers on the coast fund them on a share. The villages never see the share.
why_pressures: The dredgers' spoil heaps are burying the ground that the villages fish. The drawdown village downstream has begun keeping a tally of what the falling water uncovers.
why_would_change_if: A ban would move the dredgers to another channel. Every village separately hopes for that outcome. No village will say so aloud.
vibe_silhouette: The camp has no economic reason to be where it is.
vibe_palette: The scene is black above and blue below, with no green anywhere. The dredged block is undressed and grey. Cold blue shows on the underside of the piles.
vibe_materials: Hide over paddles set as poles can be struck in an hour. Vine cord is traded in from the interior and hoarded. Tar and ash are paid into every lap. Grave-cairns step up the bank, one course for each death.
vibe_signature_feature: The spoil heaps have become the zone's newest islands. One of them already has a hut on it.
vibe_condition: Strangers who pass through keep the camp, so it is odd but never derelict. The used parts are tidy and the rest is rank.
vibe_mood: The mood is industrial and short-termist. The dredgers are reshaping the map unannounced.
vibe_approach: New islands lie where the maps show water.
vibe_senses: Two drums answer a long way apart. The air smells of cold, mineral peat. Silence fills the place where birds should be.
player_purpose_hook: The camp lies between two drowned villages and a submerged xanmeer.
deferred_why: Verify/wrap round rebalance ran this region over its coverage-doc record budget. The budget is set in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The record is lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Still-Walking Village
why_founding: The Still-Walking Village lies under the Umbriel track. Its dead did not lie down afterwards.
why_site_advantages: The village stands directly on the shadow's path. Before the shadow it was the best rice land in the zone.
why_occupants_motive: The village's own dead occupy it. The dead remain in their own houses.
why_pressures: The Naga-Kur built their discipline against this kind of enemy. They have contained the village. They have not cleared it.
why_would_change_if: Clearing the village would put the Naga-Kur permanently in debt to whoever did it. Clearing it would also free the rice ground. Four neighbouring villages have already divided the rice ground between them.
vibe_silhouette: The village has intact roofs and no bodies at all.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey-olive with the blue gone. The luminous weed died back here. The water is black. Bone-pale shows where the village stands.
vibe_materials: Cane and hide are left as they were, perished in place. The bog-oak posts are sound. The containment ring of pikes is a century and a half newer than the village.
vibe_signature_feature: The Naga-Kur have staked a containment ring around the whole village. They do not enter the village. They maintain and date the ring. They are slowly pushing the ring inward.
vibe_condition: The village is undisturbed and standing. The Naga-Kur have taken no pole from it in a hundred and fifty years.
vibe_approach: The ring stands a kilometre out from the village. A traveller crosses it before recognising it as a ring.
vibe_senses: Cold stands over the ground well out from the houses. Drums sound only from the containment camp a mile away. No smell of rot is present.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The Naga-Kur date and maintain the containment ring. The ring's record says what the village does at night.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 49 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: The Naga-Kur have staked a containment ring a kilometre out. They do not enter the village. They date the ring and push it slowly inward.

name: The Held Vault
why_founding: The Held Vault is a dry vault. It holds the ashes of the dead that the zone could not bury in water.
why_site_advantages: The vault is the most reliably dry chamber for kilometres in any direction. The vault was used because of that dryness.
why_occupants_motive: The vault is sealed. A keeper holds the register outside the vault. Families consult the register more often than they visit the vault. They come to check that a name is in the register.
why_pressures: The vault is full and no other dry chamber exists. Recent urns are stacked in the keeper's own hut. The villages have agreed to avoid naming that arrangement plainly.
why_would_change_if: A second vault would need dry ground. None exists. Dry ground could exist only if a clan gave up a hammock crown. No clan will give up a hammock crown for the denied dead.
vibe_silhouette: The vault is a sealed, low structure. It has no offerings and no path.
vibe_palette: Blue bioluminescence lights the place. There are no lamps. Black mud holds a print for a week. Cold blue light shows on the underside of the piles.
vibe_materials: Nothing is raised above the ground. Worked bone is set into the ground and left in place. The lashing is made of gut, which stinks and holds. Two drum frames stand at the landing, one large and one small.
vibe_signature_feature: The register outside lists more names than the vault can physically hold. The discrepancy has never been explained.
vibe_condition: The vault was repaired in a hurry and has not yet been repaired properly. It sags on one side. Shoring props up that side only.
vibe_mood: The place is administratively wrong. The keepers and families avoid investigating the wrongness.
vibe_approach: A sealed stone door closes the vault. A full ledger box stands beside the door.
vibe_senses: Reed hiss sounds over the place, with drums under it. The air smells of peat, cold and mineral. Red shows nowhere. People raised here notice the absence of red elsewhere.
player_purpose_hook: The vault is the most reliably dry chamber for kilometres in any direction. The vault was used because of that dryness.
deferred_why: The vault duplicates the burial function of the Staking Village. It does so at destination scale in a zone that is over its budget.

name: The Split Cistern
why_founding: The Split Cistern was a sealed cistern. A subsidence cracked it open twelve years ago.
why_site_advantages: The cistern lies under a xanmeer floor. The ground there is still moving. Any seal that is put back would have to be built to shift with the ground.
why_occupants_motive: Something was sealed in the cistern. The cistern no longer holds it.
why_pressures: The contents are spreading through the flooded lower halls and out into the swamp. Dredgers working two channels away have started finding it in their spoil.
why_would_change_if: Sealing the cistern again is possible. The tending clan has priced the work three times. Each price has been higher than the last. The clan lacks the nerve to do the work.
vibe_silhouette: A doorway stands with a residue line at knee height. Nothing is visible beyond the doorway.
vibe_palette: Lamp-yellow light falls on wet bone. Black lies beyond the light. Blue light is bright enough for reading. The bog-oak is black and wet.
vibe_materials: The place is made of silt, cane wrack and whatever the water has stripped away. It has no marker at all. The polers say the lack of a marker is deliberate.
vibe_signature_feature: The crack is a hand's width wide. Visitors have mapped the spread from the crack on the wall outside. The map works as a growth chart of something that should not be growing.
vibe_condition: The frame survives. Everything soft has gone.
vibe_approach: The growth chart is scratched on the wall outside. Visitors reach the chart before they reach the crack.
vibe_senses: The pole shudders when it finds bone. Two drums answer each other from a long way apart. Disturbed mud smells of sulphur. The black water gives back no echo.
player_purpose_hook: A hand's-width crack opens in a sealed cistern. Successive visitors have charted its spread on the wall outside.
deferral_note: On 2026-09-04 the place was deferred. It competes with sealed-xanmeer-vakka-deeps for the zone's last deep-interior xanmeer ground. The S4 complex wins that competition. The place is held in reserve.

name: The Standing Charge
why_founding: An adult wamasu holds a pond. The pond lies on the zone's main poling route.
why_site_advantages: The pond is deep still water a few hundred metres off the main poling line. The detour poles run past the pond for its whole length.
why_occupants_motive: One adult wamasu has been resident for years. The villages have begun leaving offerings at the bank in the old Shadowfen manner. The villages no longer treat the wamasu as vermin.
why_pressures: Traffic detours two hours around the pond. The detour is itself dangerous. It runs past the reed narrows where the southern camp works.
why_would_change_if: Killing the wamasu reopens the route. The tribes disagree about whether it should be killed. The offering-makers hold that a wamasu on a route is a toll.
vibe_silhouette: Dead standing trees show lightning scarring. The frogs have abandoned the pond.
vibe_palette: The water is still and black, with a slow blue drift in it. Olive weed is matted at the margins. White grave-cairns step up the bank.
vibe_materials: Unworked black mud lies over stone. Drift bone is laid along the high line. A drum frame stands at the landing with no drum in it.
vibe_signature_feature: Poles mark the detour for its whole length. The poles have stood so long that they have grown roots.
vibe_condition: The pole line has been patched so often that the original work is hard to find.
vibe_mood: The two-hour detour has been kept up for years.
vibe_approach: The pole line marks what lies ahead. The pole line shows it long before it becomes visible.
vibe_senses: Reed hiss sounds over the place, with drums under it. Drum-signal carries flat across the water. The air smells of smoked hide and wet bone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: An adult wamasu is a hunting hour with a charge in it. The wamasu lies across a village's crossing.
why_site_won: Pinned by the Part 6 meso siting (world/sources/blueprints/place.naga-kur-deeps.wamasu-pond-adult.json): The one closed body of standing water within 300 m of the plot: 962 m2, 38 x 38 m, water level 9.24 m, bank rim 9.37-10.59 m, bank slope p50 1.2 deg / p90 3.6 deg, 69 m from the plotted position, 156 m from the place's own poling lane, 278 m from the nearest road, canopy 0.63 against 0.82 at the plot. Not connected to the tidal system, so it is still and it can be held.
player_purpose_hook: A marked detour has poles that have stood long enough to grow roots. The poles route traffic around a wamasu. The wamasu has held the pond for years.

name: The Jam
why_founding: The Jam is a permanent logjam. The logjam has become a landform.
why_site_advantages: The jam sits where the channel narrows. Every flood adds to the pile.
why_occupants_motive: A portage crew lives at the jam. Something dens inside it. The arrangement works because the crew carry their loads over the top. The crew never cut into the jam.
why_pressures: The jam now holds back a head of water that has never been measured. Each wet season adds timber to the jam. The crew's living depends on the jam staying in place.
why_would_change_if: A breach would flood four villages downstream. The levee hamlet is among them. The levee hamlet's weak point lies directly in line with the jam.
vibe_silhouette: The sound of the jam carries from a long way upstream. White water follows the sound.
vibe_palette: Black water has blue light under the surface. White shell grit lies at the landing. Blue light is bright enough for reading.
vibe_materials: No work has been done here. The place is made of peat, undressed block from other sites and bone. Carved frills are pushed into the bank as a warning line. Bone is laid along the high-water line.
vibe_signature_feature: The jam is about eighty metres long. The jam is walkable and can be denned. The jam serves as a bridge, a lair and a dam. Every villager and crew member uses the jam. None of them trusts it.
vibe_condition: The jam is worn but sound. Everything load-bearing is new. The work is serviceable. The crew do not admire it.
vibe_mood: The jam looks structurally alarming. The locals treat it as completely routine.
vibe_approach: Water can be heard going through the jam from underneath.
vibe_senses: The deck lifts underfoot as boats pass. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The light holds nothing green.
player_purpose_hook: The jam sits where the channel narrows. Every flood adds to the pile.
deferred_why: The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget after its executor pass. The budget is in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The place is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore the place.

name: The Withdrawn Tree
why_founding: A wild Hist has cut itself off from the collective. The tribes know of two other cases.
why_site_advantages: The tree stands in deep swamp, away from any tribe and any witnesses. It has stood undisturbed long enough to be studied.
why_occupants_motive: No tribe speaks for the tree. The nearest village sends neither a minder nor an offering.
why_pressures: No work has been attempted on the tree. One sap-taster watches from the far bank. The sap-taster writes down what he sees.
why_would_change_if: Reconnection is possible in principle. No tree-minder has a method for it. The tribes that could try keep their distance.
vibe_silhouette: The tree has pulled its own crown in tight. The crown is small against the sky for the tree's girth.
vibe_palette: The tree is so dark that it looks like a hole in the canopy. Black water lies beneath it. Blue light fills the swamp except within thirty paces of the tree.
vibe_materials: No building and no lashing stand here. The ground under the tree is bare of even a cairn. The nearest stake line is set facing the tree.
vibe_signature_feature: The tree's flowers are dead white. They are neither the province's red nor the Naga-Kur's blue. The tribes see at a glance that the tree is alone.
vibe_condition: The tree is untended. The ground under it is bare.
vibe_mood: The place is silent. No tribe attends the tree.
vibe_approach: White light shows where blue light should be.
vibe_senses: No hum sounds inside the tree's shade. A strong hum sounds just outside the shade. Drums are forbidden within earshot. The air smells of wet bark and little else.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 710 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).
player_purpose_hook: White light shows where blue light should be. The tree has cut itself off from the rest of the Hist.

name: The Sunk Barge
why_founding: The Sunk Barge is an Imperial-era cargo barge. It went down in the narrows with its load aboard.
why_site_advantages: The barge sank in the deep of the bend. It has not shifted since. The hull is intact and the holds are still closed.
why_occupants_motive: Fish live in the wreck. Divers take a little cargo at a time. A wreck emptied all at once attracts attention.
why_pressures: The cargo is bonded goods. A company that no longer exists still owns the goods. Selling any of the cargo on the coast raises questions.
why_would_change_if: A dry cycle would expose the deck. That exposure would end the slow looting.
vibe_silhouette: A broken mast stands out of the bend.
vibe_palette: The scene is black above and blue below. Green shows nowhere. White shell grit lies where the bank shelves.
vibe_materials: The barge is keeled timber and iron of Imperial work. Silt reaches the gunwale. Drift bone is laid along the high line of the bank.
vibe_signature_feature: The barge's cargo seals are intact and still legible. Items taken off the barge carry the mark of a company a century dead.
vibe_condition: The barge is submerged to the deck line. Weed grows on the exposed timbers.
vibe_mood: The barge has been sunk a hundred years. It still counts as the property of its owners.
vibe_approach: A dark mass lies under the bend. It is visible from a boat in good light.
vibe_senses: Cold water presses on the diver. A paddle knocks, then all is quiet. The water is dead, flat and sweetish.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The barge's cargo seals are intact. Cargo lifted off the barge can be traced to whoever ends up holding it.
player_purpose_hook: The barge's cargo seals are intact and legible. Goods lifted from the barge carry the mark of a company a century dead.

name: Alten Corimont
why_founding: Alten Corimont is a river port east-southeast of the Hatching Pools. It grew into a town by being neutral about cargo. It sits on the back-channels between Stormhold and Thorn. A shallow-draft hull can reach its water. It lies far enough from either customs regime that both regimes use it.
why_site_advantages: The port stands on the last navigable water below the northern rim. An oxbow makes a natural basin. Firm banks suit warehousing. A rim road behind the port crosses to Morrowind without passing a post.
why_occupants_motive: A captain of the port governs by a nailed-up price list. Freeholder crews with no tribe and no tree live here. Dunmer factors work the Morrowind trade. Nord hands work off the northern hulls.
why_pressures: No Hist stands here. A crew lives by the price list and the depth of water. Stormhold's vicecanons want the trade but cannot reach it. Rockpoint downriver failed in trying to undercut the price list.
why_would_change_if: If Stormhold or Thorn made the port lawful, the trade would move elsewhere. If the river silted below the oxbow, the town would become a village in five years.
vibe_silhouette: A beached hull sits upright among the houses. The hull is too big for the street it ends. Warehouse gables stand behind the hull.
vibe_palette: Weathered grey timber covers the town. Tar is black. Crates stacked together carry Dunmer lacquer and Nord paint.
vibe_materials: The town is built out of other people's cargo. Builders used crate timber, ship planking and salvaged spars. Mud render covers walls where the crate timber ran out.
vibe_signature_feature: A price list is nailed up in public. The price list names contraband by grade. Each grade has a separate rate.
vibe_condition: prosperous and ramshackle
vibe_approach: From upriver, the hull's shape resolves out of the roofline. It does so long before the town itself is legible.
vibe_senses: Hulls work against the bank. Four languages are spoken. The air smells of tar and wet rope. Cooking from three cuisines fills the air at once.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The price list is a public document. A quest can move a grade on the price list. That change alters what is lawful in a morning.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: MQ05 · tier-0; LP01 · tier-3; LP02 · tier-3; LP03 · tier-3; LP04 · tier-3; LP05 · tier-3; LP06 · tier-3; LP07 · tier-3; LP08 · tier-3; LP09 · tier-3; LP11 · tier-3; LP13 · tier-3; LP17 · tier-3; LP20 · tier-3; LQ02 · tier-3
why_site_won: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'alten-corimont' (world/sources/anchors); the anchor pixel is the city gate on the main road. The record sits at the solved city centre (cityLayout, owner rule 2026-09-18).
player_purpose_hook: Alten Corimont is the free port. A board nailed up in public prices the passage. The board stands beside the cargo rates.
complexity_justification: The town is the zone's M4. The price list, the port captain, a beached hull hall and a two-culture waterfront form its whole organising institution. It has districts and a service economy. It needs no scripting beyond Morrowind level.

name: Rim Road Racks
why_founding: Carriers walk south with the dead. They need a stage a day out from the carrying house.
why_site_advantages: The ground at the camp is firm and dry. The camp lies on the southbound road and stands a day's walk from the house.
why_occupants_motive: Two or three carriers stay at the camp. They rest with their loads.
why_pressures: Other travellers do not camp within sight of the carriers. The carriers are content with that.
why_would_change_if: If the road were rerouted, the stage would move with it. The stage depends on its spacing along the road, not on the site.
vibe_silhouette: The camp is small. Its loads are racked, not stacked.
vibe_palette: grey cloth, small fire
vibe_materials: The camp has carrying frames, wrapping cloth and one fire.
vibe_signature_feature: The carriers rack the bundles off the ground on frames. They do this before anyone sits down.
vibe_condition: temporary and exact
vibe_approach: Visitors see the frames first. The frames show the purpose of the camp.
vibe_senses: The camp has one low conversation and a fire.
player_purpose_hook: The camp stands on firm dry ground on the southbound road. It lies a day's walk from the house.
deferred_why: The coverage critique S1/S2/S3 found that pirate-freeholds carried 53 records on 0.78 km2. The corrected budget for pirate-freeholds is 14-17 records. The zone is the most over-budget in the province. The record is deferred as surplus. The type 'bone-carriers-camp' is over its province count band, which allows 2 at most. The record falls outside established lore, quest-bearing records and tier 0-1. It belongs to neither an under-band vertical type nor an underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes the record if the ground turns out to want it.

name: Bundle Racks
why_founding: An Argonian who dies away from a Hist can go back if the bones are carried to the dirt. This zone has no Hist at all. Every death here starts a journey south.
why_site_advantages: The station stands on the trunk route. The southbound road and the river both leave the freeholds at that point.
why_occupants_motive: Bone-carriers take the dead of a town that cannot bury them. They charge a fee and are ashamed of it.
why_pressures: The racks are full from the wet season through to the dry. A town with no Hist buries its dead elsewhere.
why_would_change_if: If a Hist were planted at the free port, this house would close. The carriers would lose their trade.
vibe_silhouette: The house is long and low. Racked bundles sit under its eaves.
vibe_palette: The colours are bleached bone, wrapped grey cloth and dark timber.
vibe_materials: The materials are timber racks, wrapping cloth and carrying frames.
vibe_signature_feature: Racks hold wrapped bundles. Each bundle is labelled with a destination two weeks' travel south.
vibe_condition: orderly, full, quiet
vibe_mood: The mood is careful. Voices drop at the door.
vibe_approach: The resin used for wrapping smells strongly. The smell reaches well short of the buildings.
vibe_senses: The place has the sounds of cloth and cut cord. The house is silent inside.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A carrier counts vastei aloud. The carrier can teach it to a stranger who has just watched a clutch die.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LP04 · tier-3; LQ02 · tier-3; PP11 · tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 306 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Bundled bones sit on racks for travellers going upriver. The keeper pays carriers by the bundle.

name: The Hard
why_founding: Foreign keeled hulls come this far up the river. They must be laid over and scraped where the owner is not watching.
why_site_advantages: The bank inside the basin is firm and shelving. Its hard bottom takes a hull's weight at low water.
why_occupants_motive: The boatwrights build canoes well. They repair Nord hulls deliberately poorly. The owners pay for the repairs anyway.
why_pressures: Hull identities change here. The boatwrights plane a name off the board and paint a new one. The bench rate for the work is forty drakes.
why_would_change_if: If the free port were inspected, the hard would be the first thing to disappear.
vibe_silhouette: A keeled hull lies on its side on a mud bank. The hull is out of the water.
vibe_palette: The colours are tar black, raw plank gold and river brown.
vibe_materials: The materials are hull timber, a steaming pit and paint pots.
vibe_signature_feature: A stack of planed-off nameboards lies under a bench. A boatwright keeps them in case they are needed again.
vibe_condition: working, filthy
vibe_approach: The laid-over hull looks like a building. It looks like a hull only when it moves.
vibe_senses: The place has the sounds of scraping and the smell of hot pitch. Hammering stops when strangers arrive.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A hull turned over for scraping hides whatever was put under it.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 11 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: Hulls are laid over and scraped where the owner cannot see. The boatwrights change a boat's name for a price.
promoted_why: The place is the freehold's signature works. It is the friendly rest and service that the new delves need within 600 m. The rule is research §5.3 rule 2.

name: Short Rope
why_founding: The free port sells to whoever pays the list. It protects no hull once the hull leaves the basin. Crews that will not keep discipline do not stay.
why_site_advantages: The side-channel is blind and has a cut bank. It is out of sight of the port. It lies above the last mooring that the chartered hulls use.
why_occupants_motive: A Salt-Teeth crew works the channels between the port and the head of navigation. The crew keeps its prizes in the bank until they can be sold as salvage.
why_pressures: The hall-keepers tolerate the crew as long as the crew does not undercut the price list in public.
why_would_change_if: If the port set a rate for salvage, the crew would come in and pay that rate.
vibe_silhouette: Two low hulls nose into a cut bank. A shelf of roots overhangs them. The fires stay hidden from downriver.
vibe_palette: The colours are tar and wet root. Cargo colours are stacked where they do not belong.
vibe_materials: The materials are beached hulls and a plank stage. An undercut in the bank is shored with cargo timber.
vibe_signature_feature: A stack of bonded crates carries the seals of four different ports. All the seals are cut.
vibe_condition: The anchorage is makeshift. It has been in use for years.
vibe_mood: The mood is businesslike. Work comes first and drink after.
vibe_approach: The stage is heard working against the hulls. The hulls come out of the bank shadow only afterwards.
vibe_senses: The place has the smell of rope and tar. A voice counts out loud.
why_site_won: box canyon in firm lowland (danger band 3), 16 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region.
player_purpose_hook: A crew that will not pay the port's prices keeps its prizes in a hole in the bank. The crew has killed visitors who went near it.
siting_note: In round 4 the anchorage was moved. It had been plotted 543 m from any lane at 161 m elevation. That ground lay in the border mountains on dunmer-north culture ground. The anchorage is now bound to the lower reach inside the freeholds. It lies a bend below the chartered lay-by, out of the port's sight.

name: Chasecreek
why_founding: Chasecreek is a fishing hamlet on a rise. The creek surrounds the rise in flood. Boats wait out of the channel here when the free port is being watched. The hamlet has charged for that ever since.
why_site_advantages: The rise is firm ground well above the water. The creek behind it is deep enough to hold a hull. It is shallow enough to turn back a keeled hull.
why_occupants_motive: Fisher households live here. On about four nights a month they pole the rise as a lay-by. They charge for it.
why_pressures: The lay-by trade is worth more than the fish. The port road runs close. A waiting boat has to be kept out of sight.
why_would_change_if: If the free port's list covered waiting time, Chasecreek would be a fishing hamlet again.
vibe_silhouette: A dozen roofs stand on a rise above the creek. They form the highest roofline on this reach.
vibe_palette: The colours are reed gold and mud grey. Each household has one very good bought lamp.
vibe_materials: The houses are mud render and reed on a rise. A great deal of unexplained plank is built into them.
vibe_signature_feature: Every household owns one expensive object. The object is out of keeping with the rest of the room.
vibe_condition: The houses are modest outside. They are well found inside.
vibe_approach: The rise shows first. The road below it shows next. The creek beyond the houses shows last.
vibe_senses: The place has the sounds of reed and frogs. A boat arrives at the wrong hour.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The keeper sets the lay-by fee. The households split the fee.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 12 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, nearPoint.
player_purpose_hook: A fishing hamlet makes most of its money by hiding other people's boats from the port road.
siting_note: In round 4 Chasecreek was moved. 'A creek mouth deep enough to lie in' had been plotted 118 m from any water. It is now bound to the rise over the creek, east of the toll span. The water there is 36 m below the houses.

name: The Bad Stack
why_founding: The Bad Stack is a rotten limestone stack on the border rim. It stands beside the smugglers' traverse. The traverse is the reason that anyone is near it.
why_site_advantages: Climbing the stack shortcuts a day off the rim crossing. It is visible from most of the high ground on this side.
why_occupants_motive: The stack has no occupants. A freehold courier's kit lies on the second ledge. The rope above the kit is cut.
why_pressures: The traverse below the stack is used weekly. The scree fan reaches the path. Two of the four fixed lines have gone.
why_would_change_if: If the stack takes the traverse with it, the rim crossing moves twenty kilometres. The freeholds would lose their quiet door into Morrowind.
vibe_silhouette: A fissured stack stands above a switchback path. A fan of scree runs across the route.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey rim rock, orange lichen and weathered rope.
vibe_materials: The stack is rotten limestone. The fixed lines are cut. Every fixing on it is temporary.
vibe_signature_feature: Four rope anchors were driven at four different dates. Two of them hang with nothing on the end.
vibe_condition: The stack is failing. The schedule of its failure has not been written down.
vibe_mood: The stack is a shortcut that has stopped being one.
vibe_approach: The scree on the path shows the danger. The scree appears before the stack does.
vibe_senses: Loose stone shifts underfoot. Wind passes through the fissures. Rope slaps against rock.
player_purpose_hook: Climbing the stack shortcuts a day off the rim crossing. It is visible from most of the high ground on this side.

name: Sawn Seal
why_founding: The Company built a bonded store on the northern river when the trade was lawful. The free port opened it when trade failed.
why_site_advantages: It is the only cargo-bearing stone building in the zone. It stands on the basin's firm bank.
why_occupants_motive: The port captain's men live here. They store bonded goods in a store that is no longer bonded. They find that funny.
why_pressures: The seals were cut, not forged. The Company's manifest is still nailed inside. The manifest names a dead consignee.
why_would_change_if: If an Imperial claim were pressed, all the free port's warehousing would be legally stolen.
vibe_silhouette: A stone cargo hall stands among timber sheds. It was obviously built by other hands.
vibe_palette: The colours are Company red gone pink, grey stone and cargo colours.
vibe_materials: The hall is Imperial ashlar. Freehold timber lean-tos are bolted to it.
vibe_signature_feature: A saw cut clean through a Company seal. The sawn halves are nailed either side of the door as a joke.
vibe_condition: The hall is sound and over-used. It is extended in every direction.
vibe_approach: The hall's gable is dressed stone in a timber town.
vibe_senses: Cargo is moved at hours when cargo should not be moved.
player_purpose_hook: It is the only cargo-bearing stone building in the zone. It stands on the basin's firm bank.

name: Crosstrees
why_founding: The free port is built around a hull dragged up the bank sixty years ago. The masts were left standing because they proved useful. From the crosstrees both the roofs and the canopy are in sight. Every gable in the port stands lower than the crosstrees.
why_site_advantages: The beached hull sits on the highest firm ground in the basin. The canopy is cut back around it so that the lookout can work.
why_occupants_motive: The port's lookout watches for hulls coming up the channel. She takes no fee. People below pay her in beer for the early warning.
why_pressures: The rigging is sixty years past its rope. Whoever is free that week rebuilds the ladder every wet season.
why_would_change_if: If the hull goes over, the freehold loses its high ground. It would then post watchers on the water.
vibe_silhouette: Two masts stand over a roofline. A plank stage is lashed across them.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey timber and tarred rope. One strip of faded flag has stayed up since the hull came ashore.
vibe_materials: The materials are ship spars and lashed plank. The ladder is made of salvaged batten.
vibe_signature_feature: The stage at the crosstrees has three notches cut in the rail. Each notch stands for one of the channels that the lookout watches.
vibe_condition: old rigging, patched stage
vibe_mood: The mood is quiet. The port's noise sounds underneath it.
vibe_approach: The ladder starts behind the hull-hall. The hull-hall shelters it from the weather.
vibe_senses: Wind moves in slack rigging. The ladder creaks under a climber.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The lookout sells bearings. She takes payment in news from downriver.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 8 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, bound.
player_purpose_hook: The old hull's masts can be climbed. The lookout at the top names the reaches, the rim notch and the boat for the capital.
siting_note: This is a network-role bind from round 4. The record is the free port's own masthead lookout. It must stand on the port's ground. It had been plotted 361 m out. That also put its D1 tier on band-3 ground. It is now bound to Alten Corimont inside the port ring.

name: The Standing Slate
why_founding: The free port has one law, which is a price list. The house that runs Shells and Stones acts as the bank. People treat the debt slate as the law.
why_site_advantages: The house stands in the densest street of the free port. The hull hall is one door away.
why_occupants_motive: The house crew buy debts. They sell the debts on to the hiring yard.
why_pressures: Half the freeholders in town have debts recorded on the slate. For that reason the captain of the port treats the house carefully.
why_would_change_if: If the slate were burned, the whole informal credit system of the zone would go with it. The hiring yard would go with it too.
vibe_silhouette: The house has a low doorway with no sign. The doorway shows more light than any window near it.
vibe_palette: The palette is lamp red, chalk white and dark timber.
vibe_materials: The walls are crate timber. The house has one very good table and hung lamps.
vibe_signature_feature: A debt slate as high as a wall is chalked and re-chalked. It is the nearest thing that the zone has to a legal record.
vibe_condition: The house is worn but expensive in the places that matter.
vibe_mood: The house is the real seat of power in the town.
vibe_approach: The dice can be heard from the street.
vibe_senses: Dice rattle on wood. Chalk marks the slate. A debtor is told a number.
player_purpose_hook: The house stands in the densest street of the free port. The hull hall is one door away.

name: The Last Deep
why_founding: Above the free port the river shallows to a channel. A laden hull cannot use the channel. Cargo transfers to poled craft at this point. The limit moves every season.
why_site_advantages: The site is a confluence at -6.5 m relative depth. Three channels meet there. The deep water ends there.
why_occupants_motive: Transfer crews work here. A board-keeper keeps the season line. The season line is the most argued-about number in the district.
why_pressures: In a dry year the limit drops two kilometres. Half the freight costs in the district change when it drops.
why_would_change_if: If a dredge were run, the free port could take hulls upriver. The monopoly of Alten Corimont on transfer would end.
vibe_silhouette: The place has far more small craft than the shore behind them would suggest.
vibe_palette: The palette is river brown, pole-timber pale and cargo canvas grey.
vibe_materials: The place has transfer stages, poled craft and stacked cargo.
vibe_signature_feature: A navigable-limit board shows this season's line. Last season's line is still legible below it.
vibe_condition: muddy, busy, provisional
vibe_mood: Commercial argument is the way of life here.
vibe_approach: The boats thin out to nothing above the place.
vibe_senses: Poles scrape in gravel. Crews dispute draught.
player_purpose_hook: The site is a confluence at -6.5 m relative depth. Three channels meet there. The deep water ends there.
deferred_why: Coverage critique S1/S2/S3 found that pirate-freeholds had 53 records on 0.78 km2. The corrected budget for the zone is 14-17 records. Part 3 promotes the record if the site supports it.

name: The Hiring Yard
why_founding: Debts bought at the gambling house become owings. An owing is worked off in a gang. People who lost their ground are told at the yard where they will work.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands on hard standing beside the porter yard. It lies on the road out of the free port.
why_occupants_motive: Households whose owings the broker has called live here. The broker's clerk and his ledger are here too.
why_pressures: The yard has no chains. Leaving costs the balance on the ledger. The balance is read out in months.
why_would_change_if: If a Chainbreaker cell reached the yard, the labour supply of the free port would stop the same day.
vibe_silhouette: A line of shelters runs along a fence. A single roofed office stands at one end.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey canvas and mud. The office has one painted door.
vibe_materials: The shelters are salvaged canvas and crate timber. The office is the only proper building.
vibe_signature_feature: The office holds a ledger. The port halls and the gangs both treat the ledger as binding.
vibe_condition: The yard is twenty years old. It is built out of canvas.
vibe_mood: The yard is quiet. The waiting men watch the office door.
vibe_approach: The road out of town runs straight through the yard.
vibe_senses: A ledger is read aloud. The listeners give no reply.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: BC01 · tier-2; province system · tier-1; BC-line · tier-2
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 67 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.corimont-low-store (+0.53).
player_purpose_hook: The yard is where an owing turns into a work gang. The ledger is read aloud at the office door. The balance is counted in months.
promoted_why: Owner feedback and opening-hours research §6.1 require the Owing institution to exist as a live place. The Owing institution processes new arrivals in MQ01.

name: No-Tree
why_founding: The free port has no Hist. The camp on the edge of the town houses its Hist-less households. Some live there by choice. Some were left with nothing else.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the landward fringe of the town. The port does not administer the ground.
why_occupants_motive: Argonians with no tree awaiting their return live here. Outsiders who prefer that company live here too.
why_pressures: The people of the tribal villages upriver will not visit. Hissmir's reconnection rite is a two-week journey. The rite also means a hard conversation.
why_would_change_if: If a Hist cutting were successfully planted here, the free port would stop being a freehold and start being a town.
vibe_silhouette: The village has a swept empty circle where a tree should be.
vibe_palette: The palette is mud grey and undyed cloth. There is no amber anywhere.
vibe_materials: The buildings use mud render and crate timber. There are no ritual totems.
vibe_signature_feature: A planting circle is dug, edged and kept swept. It has been kept for sixty years. Bare dirt lies at its centre.
vibe_condition: solid and plain
vibe_mood: The camp is stubborn. The subject of the tree comes up every day.
vibe_approach: The gap in the middle shows before the houses do.
vibe_senses: There are no chimes. A visitor from upriver notices within a minute.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The people of a refuge with no tree must decide what a naming is worth without one.
why_site_won: land bridge in firm lowland (danger band 3), 419 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, parent, route.
player_purpose_hook: The village has an empty planting circle. The circle has been swept every day for sixty years. The keeper of the circle explains why it is kept.

name: The Low Store
why_founding: A bonded store was cut into the channel bank. The water then sat two feet lower. The water came back. The owner stopped paying the port. The doors were left to whoever wanted them.
why_site_advantages: The store is a dry-ish cellar under a wet bank. It is on the water, but out of sight of the quay.
why_occupants_motive: Three of the less useful dock hands sleep here between jobs. They take what floats past.
why_pressures: The store floods to the knee on a high river. It floods to the chest twice a year.
why_would_change_if: If the port enforced its own bond seals, the store would be emptied in a morning.
vibe_silhouette: A plank door stands in a mud bank. The door is half a metre above the water.
vibe_palette: The palette is silt brown and black water. One bright bolt of ruined cloth shows.
vibe_materials: The cut bank is shored with ship planking. A brick floor lies under the silt.
vibe_signature_feature: A bond seal is still nailed to the door frame. A knife has cut through the seal.
vibe_condition: flooded, occupied, not defended
vibe_mood: The store is damp. The tenants are not fighters.
vibe_approach: The bank steps down to the store. The doorway is visible from outside.
vibe_senses: Water slaps brick. Three people argue about a share.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The flooded store has three weak tenants. One bonded crate lies behind them.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.corimont-hiring-yard (+0.53).
player_purpose_hook: The store is flooded and lies under the bank. Three idlers live in it. They live on top of what the last owner left when he stopped paying the bond.

name: The Quay Room
why_founding: The social hall of the port is a beached hull. The port still needs a house that sells beds and locked doors.
why_site_advantages: The house stands on the basin front. The hull hall is one door away. The gambling house is two doors away.
why_occupants_motive: A keeper sells beds, stabling and discretion.
why_pressures: Four languages are spoken in one room. The guest book is worth more than the takings.
why_would_change_if: If the free port were made lawful, the guest book would become evidence. The keeper would burn it.
vibe_silhouette: A lit doorway stands between a mooring and a stable yard.
vibe_palette: The palette is lamp yellow and tar black. The walls are cargo crates.
vibe_materials: The house uses crate timber and ship plank. It has one bought Imperial door.
vibe_signature_feature: The guest book is kept in four scripts. Jel is not among the scripts. A private stair gives access that does not pass through the main room.
vibe_condition: prosperous, scuffed
vibe_mood: The house is loud. It holds four crews' worth of talk.
vibe_approach: The noise reaches the basin.
vibe_senses: Four languages are heard. Cooking smells drift through the rooms. A lock is turned upstairs.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Debts get settled here in cargo. The cargo is signed over without leaving the hold.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 145 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The house offers a bed and a door that locks. The keeper sells silence by the night.

name: The Old Pens
why_founding: House Dres took Argonians out of this river country for centuries. The pens used to hold and count them. The pens still stand on the bank. The barges loaded from that bank.
why_site_advantages: The site is a river landing with hard standing. It was sited for loading, not for living.
why_occupants_motive: The pens are empty above ground. Something has been getting into the flooded cells below. The traders of the free port keep their business off this bank. The Dunmer factors in town avoid the bank altogether.
why_pressures: The pens are not a subject for jokes at the market. They are not a subject for jokes on the barges.
why_would_change_if: If the Dunmer factors in town were formally associated with the pens, the trade of the freehold with Morrowind would end overnight.
vibe_silhouette: Stone pens and a loading ramp stand on an empty bank.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey stone, rust and bare hard standing.
vibe_materials: The pens use Dunmer-cut stone and iron rings. The ramp is graded for people.
vibe_signature_feature: The loading ramp is graded and railed for people, not cargo. Count-marks are still cut into the gatepost. A stair at the bottom of the ramp goes down into the holding cells.
vibe_condition: The pens are sound. They have been neither repaired nor demolished.
vibe_approach: The trunk road passes within thirty paces of the ramp.
vibe_senses: No birds are heard. No frogs are heard.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A hidden party is repairing the apparatus. They use money that the port cannot trace.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 117 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, nearPoint, culture-clump; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The Dres loading pens have count-marks still cut in the gatepost. Something lives in the cells below.

name: Andrano Hold
why_founding: Andrano Hold is a House holding left over from the Dres trade. It is now a Dunmer village on the wrong side of the border. Returning to Morrowind was the worse choice. The families stayed.
why_site_advantages: Andrano Hold stands on a defensible upland shelf on the pass road. The shelf has its own water. The hold has a walled core.
why_occupants_motive: Dunmer families settled here three centuries ago. The families work as factors for the free port. The river villages downriver hold the hold's trade against the families.
why_pressures: Andrano Hold holds the largest concentration of the zone's 22% Dunmer minority. The Dres pens stand on the river below the hold.
why_would_change_if: Morrowind could reassert a claim over the hold. The free port's northern trade would then become a diplomatic asset. It would no longer be a crime.
vibe_silhouette: Andrano Hold has a walled core. Its roof shapes are organic Velothi forms. The roofs look unmistakably foreign on this skyline.
vibe_palette: The palette is ash grey, lacquer red and black.
vibe_materials: The buildings use Velothi render and stone. The roofs use imported tile. A wall encloses the core.
vibe_signature_feature: The hold has an ancestor hall. People born on this side of the border have maintained the hall for three hundred years.
vibe_condition: solid and wealthy
vibe_mood: The hold feels closed. Its people watch the river below.
vibe_approach: The roof shapes read as wrong from a long way off.
vibe_senses: The people speak a different language. A bell sounds here, not a chime.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A Dunmer house on the wrong side of the border has to choose. It must choose between its ancestors and its neighbours.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: LP10 · tier-3; LP11 · tier-3; LP12 · tier-3; tier-2
why_site_won: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 470 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.
player_purpose_hook: The last Andrano still holds a Morrowind house on the wrong side of the border. The cellars have stayed unopened since the Dres trade ended.

name: Thin Levee
why_founding: The seasonal floodplain below the freeholds is the only ground in the zone that grows a surplus. People in the free port live on that surplus.
why_site_advantages: The floodplain has bunded flats. The river's annual rise can be let into the flats and held.
why_occupants_motive: Households here grow crops for the port's price list. The households are always slightly in the port's debt.
why_pressures: The households maintain the levee collectively. One household always does less.
why_would_change_if: The levee could fail in a bad year. The free port's traders would then buy grain from Morrowind through their own smugglers.

vibe_palette: The palette is water-sky silver, young green and levee ochre.

vibe_approach: The geometry of the bunds is visible from the road above.
vibe_senses: Water moves through the sluices. Frogs call. Wind blows over flat crop.

name: Five-Sixty Field
why_founding: The people who died in the Flu here were not Argonian. They had no Hist awaiting them. Whoever was still alive cairned them where they fell.
why_site_advantages: The field is firm dry ground above the village. Loose stone is close to hand.
why_occupants_motive: The field has no residents. Passing travellers re-stack the cairns. They have done so since the road was cut.
why_pressures: The field is the largest visible evidence in the zone that a whole people used to live here.
why_would_change_if: A scholar could count the cairns properly. The district's population history would then change.

vibe_signature_feature: The field has hundreds of cairns. One cairn has a date cut into it.

vibe_mood: The field is quiet. It is larger than it looked from below.
vibe_approach: The slope reads as scree. The pattern of cairns resolves as the visitor nears.

why_site_advantages: The shelter stands on ground upstream that no syndicate has claimed. The ground is defensible enough to discourage a broker's men.

vibe_approach: The residents challenge visitors before they arrive.
