name: Last Stage
why_founding: Word moves through this zone by memorised message. The port trades in information. The relay is the most valuable post on the trunk.
why_site_advantages: The relay stands on the trunk at a runner's stage from its neighbours. It has a bench and a landing.
why_occupants_motive: Runners staff the relay. They are paid twice for some messages. They know which messages those are.
why_pressures: A message in transit is worth knowing. Taking a message is the zone's only crime that is punished.
why_would_change_if: The port's traders could buy the relay outright. The freeholds would then lose their only independent channel.
vibe_silhouette: Last Stage is a small post. It has a bench and a rail of carved tokens.
vibe_palette: The palette is bleached timber and dark token wood.
vibe_materials: The post has carved tokens, a bench and a covered rest board.
vibe_signature_feature: The token rail has a lockable cover. No other courier post in the province has a lock.
vibe_condition: worn smooth
vibe_approach: Visitors find the bench first.
vibe_senses: One runner arrives out of breath. Then the runner leaves.
player_purpose_hook: The relay stands on the trunk at a runner's stage from its neighbours. It has a bench and a landing.
deferred_why: Coverage critique S1/S2/S3 found that pirate-freeholds had 53 records on 0.78 km2. The corrected budget for the zone is 14-17 records. Pirate-freeholds is the most over-budget zone in the province. Last Stage is deferred as surplus. The type 'courier-relay' is over its province count band of 9 max. The record is not lore-grounded. It carries no quest. It is not tier 0-1. It is not an instance of an under-band vertical or underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes the record if the ground proves to suit it.

name: The Open Ground
why_founding: The price list has to be applied somewhere. Traders apply it at the stall row under the board.
why_site_advantages: The market stands on level ground below the list board. It is one street up from the basin. It is clear of the wharf traffic.
why_occupants_motive: Traders work in septims and Dunmer coin. Barter is accepted at the next stall.
why_pressures: The board is a public document. It names contraband by grade. Stormhold's customs house publishes no such list.
why_would_change_if: The list could be withdrawn. The row would still meet. Traders would argue every price again.
vibe_silhouette: Permanent stall frames stand under one enormous nailed-up board.
vibe_palette: The palette is frame grey and board white. The awnings come from four provinces.
vibe_materials: The stalls use timber frames. The awnings are bought canvas. The goods come from four provinces.
vibe_signature_feature: A weights post carries four sets of weights. Three of the sets disagree.
vibe_condition: permanent frames, changing stock
vibe_approach: The board is the first thing legible from the water.
vibe_senses: Traders haggle in four languages and three currencies.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A forged grade on the board could move a cargo between lawful and contraband. The forgery would work before anyone checked.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 16 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, bound.
player_purpose_hook: The market sells four provinces' goods under one board. The board prices contraband by grade. The three currencies in use disagree.

name: Nine Mile
why_founding: A Naga band works the rim track up to the pass. The freeholds' cargo climbs the track unescorted. The nearest keeper sits four hours further up, at the pass station.
why_site_advantages: The camp has cover within a spear's throw of the track. The track cannot be left at that point.
why_occupants_motive: The band numbers eight or so. The band strikes camp after every taking.
why_pressures: Escorts are hired by the captains of the free port. They do not fight the band. Hiring escorts is cheaper than losing hands.
why_would_change_if: The pass station could keep a watch. The band would then move down to the river. It would take boats.
vibe_silhouette: The camp is hidden from the road. From the trees uphill it is a cleared circle. The circle holds no fire.
vibe_palette: The palette is dull hide, wet bone and dark green. The camp makes no smoke.
vibe_materials: The band uses hide shelters. It strikes and re-pitches the shelters daily. It uses bone-and-flint gear. Taken cargo stays in other people's crates.
vibe_signature_feature: The band keeps taken cargo in labelled heaps. The heaps are sorted by the place on the road where each was taken.
vibe_condition: The camp is recently made. It is ready to move.
vibe_mood: The band is patient. It is quick to strike camp.
vibe_approach: The band watches arrivals from cover for some minutes. Then the first spear shows.
vibe_senses: The camp has no dogs and no smoke. Then the whole band appears at once.
why_site_won: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 221 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A Naga band camps a spear's throw off the rim track. The climb is too steep there to leave the path.
siting_note: The camp was moved in round 4. Its constraint of at least 1.2 km from Alten Corimont is larger than the freeholds' own ground. The plot placed the camp 650 m outside the zone onto a 60-degree face. The constraint was relaxed to 500 m. The camp is bound to the climb below the pass station.
promoted_why: Hostility balance requires one honest ambush on the trunk road. The ambush is sited well clear of the start.

name: Bellet's
why_founding: Cargo from anywhere is accepted at the port, so sickness from anywhere arrives with it. The town has no temple. The sick come to the pest house.
why_site_advantages: The pest house stands downwind of the free port. It stands downstream of the free port. It stands on its own ground.
why_occupants_motive: Two keepers run the pest house. The keepers have no formal training. They use four hundred years of accumulated local practice.
why_pressures: The pest house is funded from the price list. The price list is the source of all public spending in the zone.
why_would_change_if: If the list stopped funding the pest house, the sick would lie in the port's own lodging houses after one month.
vibe_silhouette: The pest house is a long shed with open sides. It stands apart from everything.
vibe_palette: The palette is lime white, grey timber and green.
vibe_materials: The pest house uses lime-washed timber, reed screens and a boiling hearth.
vibe_signature_feature: A lime-washed board records what worked. The board has been kept for four hundred years. The keepers have never organised the board.
vibe_condition: clean and hard-used
vibe_mood: The keepers work briskly. The keepers do not pray over patients.
vibe_approach: The pest house stands alone downwind. Visitors smell the lime on approach.
vibe_senses: The sounds are boiling water, low voices and wind passing through the open sides.
player_purpose_hook: The pest house is a place in the freehold that takes in the sick. It does not ask what a patient can pay.
promoted_why: The pest house is the region's only sanctuary. It serves the rest cadence. Ring B needs a sanctuary.

name: The Chimney
why_founding: The province has almost no metalworking. The smithy is the province's sole forge. A free port that steals fastenings needs a place to reuse them.
why_site_advantages: The smithy stands beside the careening hard inside the port. The ground is dry and firm enough to stand a permanent forge.
why_occupants_motive: A Nord smith runs the forge. He came off a hull twenty years ago and stayed.
why_pressures: The smith's stock is other people's ship iron. The boatwrights buy the iron back. The boatwrights do not ask from which hull the iron came.
why_would_change_if: If the fastening supply were cut, the forge would go cold. The boatwrights would then lose their hulls.
vibe_silhouette: A stone chimney stands over reed and plank roofs.
vibe_palette: The palette is soot black, ember orange and grey stone.
vibe_materials: The smithy uses a stone forge, ship iron and charcoal.
vibe_signature_feature: A rack holds ship fastenings. The smith sorts the fastenings by the hull they came off. The smith names each hull.
vibe_condition: hot and sound
vibe_mood: The smithy is busy. The yard is in and out all day.
vibe_approach: One stone chimney stands over reed roofs.
vibe_senses: The sounds are hammers striking iron and burning charcoal. Hot scale lies about the forge.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 83 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The smithy is a forge in a province with almost no smithing. A Nord who came off a hull works the forge. The forge is stocked with salvaged ship iron.

name: The Dragway
why_founding: Everything that goes above the gorge has to come out of the water and go back into it. The haulers who drag it charge for the work.
why_site_advantages: The slipway stands on the sole bank with a gradient that a hauling gang can work. The bank lies immediately below the narrows.
why_occupants_motive: Six haulers run the slipway. The haulers keep a charge board and a monopoly.
why_pressures: Cargo is held at both ends of the slipway. Cargo is occasionally taxed twice.
why_would_change_if: If a second slip were cut, the price would halve. The haulers never cut a second slip.
vibe_silhouette: A greased timber ramp comes out of the water. The ramp lies beside white water.
vibe_palette: The palette is grease black, gold timber and spray.
vibe_materials: The slipway uses rollers, hauling lines and a charge board.
vibe_signature_feature: A charge board shows two prices. One price is for members of the port list. One price is for everyone else.
vibe_condition: worn to the grain
vibe_approach: The slip is the first built structure seen on approach.
vibe_senses: The sounds are turning rollers and straining rope. The narrows run underneath.
player_purpose_hook: The slipway stands on the sole bank with a gradient that a hauling gang can work. The bank lies immediately below the narrows.
deferred_why: The coverage critique S1/S2/S3 covers the pirate-freeholds zone. The pirate-freeholds zone carried 53 records on 0.78 km2. The corrected budget for the pirate-freeholds zone is 14-17 records. The pirate-freeholds zone is the most over-budget zone in the province. The record was deferred as surplus. The type 'portage-slipway' is over its province count band of 3 max. The record is not lore-grounded. It is not quest-bearing. It is not tier 0-1. It is not an instance of an under-band vertical/underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes the record if the ground turns out to want it.

name: The Grinder
why_founding: The gorge reach cannot be run. A logjam in the reach has built itself into a crossable structure. The logjam is made of dead trees.
why_site_advantages: The reach is a gorge pinch in firm lowland. Every flood's timber collects against the same rock.
why_occupants_motive: The jam has no residents. Four people usually work the jam for salvage.
why_pressures: The jam is unstable and walkable. The jam is the only dry crossing for two kilometres.
why_would_change_if: If a flood cleared the jam, both the crossing and the salvage would go in one night.
vibe_silhouette: A mass of bleached dead timber is wedged across a gorge. White water runs under the timber.
vibe_palette: The palette is bone-white timber, black wet rock and brown-white water.
vibe_materials: The jam is made of dead trees and wedged cargo. It has no built element at all.
vibe_signature_feature: A bridge is made entirely of drowned trees. The bridge was built by none of its users. All travellers use the bridge.
vibe_condition: The jam is unstable. The jam also bears load.
vibe_approach: The sound reaches visitors from upstream first.
vibe_senses: A continuous roar fills the gorge. Timber shifts under weight.
player_purpose_hook: The reach is a gorge pinch in firm lowland. Every flood's timber collects against the same rock.
deferred_why: The region ran over its coverage-doc record budget after its executor pass. The budget is in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The Verify/wrap round rebalance deferred this record. It is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: Long Water
why_founding: Half the crews on this water hold a charter from a sponsor. Asked whose, a captain names a port, not a man. Long Water is where the crews lie up between charters. The port halls count it as a berth.
why_site_advantages: Long Water is a long straight side-channel. It has deep water on one bank. It has room for four hulls. It has a clear run out in either direction.
why_occupants_motive: Crews rest and refit between charters. A broker sells passage to travellers. The travellers do not ask what else the hull carries.
why_pressures: One bad prize makes the port halls withdraw the berth. The crews that lose the berth end up at Short Rope.
why_would_change_if: If the League of Open Water chartered these crews properly, the freehold would have a navy.
vibe_silhouette: Four hulls lie on a long side-channel. Two of the hulls are careened over. No building stands on the bank.
vibe_palette: The palette is tar, bare timber and every crew's own paint on its own bow.
vibe_materials: Long Water uses hulls, stages between hulls and one plank walk to the bank.
vibe_signature_feature: No building stands on the bank. The crews do hiring on deck.
vibe_condition: Long Water is busy. The crews strike and move in a morning.
vibe_mood: The crews keep civil order by their own rules.
vibe_approach: The channel opens on four hulls. The watch on deck is already looking at the bank.
vibe_senses: The sounds are crews hammering and tar being applied to careened hulls. Four conversations stop when a stranger approaches.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 85 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: Four crews lie up between charters. The broker on the middle hull sells berths out.

name: Slack Bend
why_founding: The Kothringi held river country like this. The Knahaten Flu ended the Kothringi in 2E 560. Their village on the bend has stood empty since. The crews of the free port will not take the ground.
why_site_advantages: The bend is firm ground with a landing. A village would be built there today for the same reasons.
why_occupants_motive: The bend has no occupants. The free port's crews pass the bend without tying up. The older hands make a sign as they go.
why_pressures: The bend is the best unoccupied river frontage in the zone. It has been empty for six hundred years.
why_would_change_if: If a crew built here and lived out a season, the taboo would go.
vibe_silhouette: House platforms and a landing lie on a good bend. The posts are gone.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey stone footings, long grass and brown river.
vibe_materials: The ruin has stone footings and post holes. A people who built differently from Argonians made them.
vibe_signature_feature: A village-shaped clearing lies on the best ground for kilometres. A two-hundred-year-old tree grows in the middle of the square.
vibe_condition: reduced to footings, undisturbed
vibe_mood: The bend is empty. The ground is good.
vibe_approach: The good ground shows from the water before the footings do.
vibe_senses: The sounds are the river and the silence of crews who go quiet as they pass.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The best river frontage in the zone stands empty. Claiming it means finding a crew that will land.
why_site_won: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 3), 79 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on bound, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The bend is the best empty river frontage in the zone. No crew has tied up there in six hundred years.
promoted_why: Dungeon balance promoted the ruin. It is a standard delve with lore payoff on the water. It carries the region's Knahaten Flu layer.

name: The Drawdown
why_founding: The lake behind the freeholds drops four metres in the dry season. The drop exposes a flat of deep soft mud. People and things have sunk into the mud.
why_site_advantages: The flat is a shallow lake shelf. The shelf has a very large seasonal range.
why_occupants_motive: The flat is unoccupied. Scavengers work its edges when it is exposed.
why_pressures: What the drawdown reveals is worth having. The mud cannot bear the weight of a walker who tries to reach it.
why_would_change_if: If the lake level were stabilised, the sunken things would stay buried.
vibe_silhouette: In the dry season the flat is a cracked grey plain where a lake was.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey mud, salt crust and bleached wood.
vibe_materials: The materials are mud, exposed wreckage and stranded posts.
vibe_signature_feature: Boats, posts and at least one cart stand upright in the mud. They stand where they went down.
vibe_condition: The flat is seasonal. For six months of the year it is under water.
vibe_approach: A traveller who arrives in the wrong season finds water.
vibe_senses: cracking mud; nothing living
player_purpose_hook: The flat is a shallow lake shelf with a very large seasonal range.
deferred_why: The coverage critique S1/S2/S3 covers the pirate-freeholds zone. The pirate-freeholds zone carried 53 records on 0.78 km2. The corrected budget for the pirate-freeholds zone is 14-17 records. The pirate-freeholds zone is the most over-budget zone in the province. The record was deferred as surplus. The type 'drawdown-flat' is over its province count band of 4 max. The record is not lore-grounded. It is not quest-bearing. It is not tier 0-1. It is not an instance of an under-band vertical/underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes the record if the ground turns out to want it.

name: The Roll
why_founding: Keeping the channel of the free port open costs money. The cheapest way to keep it open is a dredging gang that owes money. The barge is where the gang lives. It is also where a new hand is read onto the roll.
why_site_advantages: The barge is moored off the port. It is close enough to work the channels. It is far enough away that the port does not have to look at it.
why_occupants_motive: The barge holds a broker's detail, a handful of overseers and thirty people who owe months. Two of the thirty are visibly washed out from years away from their Hist.
why_pressures: The ledger is read aloud at every intake, with the months added for food. Arguing costs months. The roll is heard out in silence.
why_would_change_if: If the port stopped paying for the dredging, the owings would be sold on to an estate upriver. The barge would then be broken up for planking.
vibe_silhouette: The barge is flat with a plank shed amidships. A crane frame stands at the bow.
vibe_palette: The palette is tar black, wet timber and the grey of dredged silt.
vibe_materials: The barge uses deck planks and plank partitions. Chain-and-basket dredging gear sits at the bow.
vibe_signature_feature: The roll is a board of names in a locked case. It is read out at the top of every shift.
vibe_condition: crowded and heavily worked
vibe_mood: The mood is orderly. Every hour on the barge is counted.
vibe_approach: reached by boat only
vibe_senses: Chain runs over a drum. A name is read out, then a number.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A new hand can buy their way off the ledger. A new hand can argue the ledger down or burn it.
why_site_won: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 3), 78 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, region, parent; needs 0.6 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: The place is a dredging barge moored off the port. Names and the debts of each hand are kept on a board in a locked case. The board is read out at the top of every shift.
siting_note: A new character is processed onto the roll here. The barge is held at D1 against a danger raster that reads band 3. The first 250 m of the opening ring has to be survivable. The source is docs/research/quests-and-cast/opening-hours-and-start-area.md §5, Ring A. The raster needs the ring carved into it at Part 6. The record is not retiered.

name: Gang Ground
why_founding: A gang that works a channel has to sleep on land. The gang's families follow it. The camp is forty years old. It is still named for the ground that the gang worked.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on a slope of firm ground between the Border road and the marsh. Its top terrace stays dry enough for a hatching shed.
why_occupants_motive: The occupants are families whose people are on the roll. They keep a life going a short walk from the roll.
why_pressures: The camp is a Hist a day upriver but has no claim on it. The families stay because the clutch is in the shed.
why_would_change_if: If the clutch is lost, the families go to a place that the ledger cannot reach.
vibe_silhouette: Low shelters step down a slope on levelled terraces. The hatching shed stands on the top terrace below the road. Below the camp, the gang's barge lies at its pier. The barge is a Bretic hull with a shed on the deck and a crane at the bow.
vibe_palette: The camp is mud and thatch. The hatching shed's lamp gives it warm amber at night.
vibe_materials: The materials are bamboo, reed thatch, hide over poles, packed earth and old ship timber.
vibe_signature_feature: The hatching shed is kept warmer and cleaner than the sleeping sheds. A nest of twig bundles and a carapace oven stand by the clutch.
vibe_condition: The camp is poor, but well kept. A timber stack, a chopping block, a hand cart and sacks stand about the camp. Cut planks and tools lie on the barge deck.
vibe_mood: The mood is domestic. The ledger is a walk away.
vibe_approach: The way in descends from the Border road to the hatching shed door. The yard way runs down the terraces from the hatching shed. The way down leads to the landing and the barge pier. A second way out climbs the two Hist roots on the west bank.
vibe_senses: The camp smells of cooking and wet reed. The hatching shed gives off a low continuous sound.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 20 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region.
player_purpose_hook: The gang's families live on this slope above the marsh. The warm shed at the top holds the gang's egg clutch. The families stay with the clutch.
siting_note: The camp is held at D1 with the barge for the same Ring A reason. The barge is place.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-barge.
watch_reason: The Dres remnant's overseers watch the yard and hold the gang to the Owing.

name: Ossic Line
why_founding: An unnamed party drew a line around the infected ground and marked it. The marks were maintained long after the reason ended.
why_site_advantages: The line follows the natural boundary of a ridge and a stream. It is the easiest line to hold.
why_occupants_motive: The line is unoccupied. The villages on either side re-cut the marks out of habit.
why_pressures: The line is absent from every map. Every local respects it absolutely.
why_would_change_if: If the line were formally lifted, two villages would have to agree where the boundary now is.
vibe_silhouette: A line of cut marks on trees and posts runs dead straight over a ridge.
vibe_palette: The palette is raw cut wood, weathered grey and green.
vibe_materials: The line uses blazed trees, cut posts and one painted stone at each end.
vibe_signature_feature: Blaze marks are re-cut annually. The trees were saplings when the line was drawn.
vibe_condition: maintained by habit
vibe_approach: A traveller crosses the line without noticing. The traveller then finds the next mark.
vibe_senses: The line is silent and odourless. Locals stop talking at it.
player_purpose_hook: The line follows the natural boundary of a ridge and a stream. It is the easiest line to hold.

The corrected budget for the pirate-freeholds zone is 14-17 records. The pirate-freeholds zone is the most over-budget zone in the province. The record was deferred as surplus. The type 'plague-cordon-line' is over its province count band of 3 max. The record is not lore-grounded. It is not quest-bearing. It is not tier 0-1. It is not an instance of an under-band vertical/underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes the record if the ground turns out to want it.

name: Tallyman's
why_founding: One person lives at the bottom of a ravine with no path. That person used to keep the port's ledger and cannot do so any more.
why_site_advantages: The site is deliberately awkward. It is a box canyon with a spring and one climb into it.
why_occupants_motive: One person lives here. Forty years of the free port's transactions are written from memory on the walls.
why_pressures: The hermit trades what they remember for a specific favour. The hermit refuses money. In this zone that refusal is a statement.
why_would_change_if: If the port read the wall, half the freeholds would be exposed.
vibe_silhouette: A thin smoke line rises out of a slot in the ground.
vibe_palette: The palette is rock grey, one fire and green at the bottom.
vibe_materials: The hut is built of ravine timber and stacked stone.
vibe_signature_feature: Forty years of the port's ledger are written on the ravine wall in charcoal. The hermit wrote it from memory.
vibe_condition: small, precise, obsessive
vibe_mood: The reward is a conversation. The conversation is worth more than loot.
vibe_approach: The route down is unmarked. A visitor has to find one.
vibe_senses: Water runs in the ravine. One voice sounds. It has not been used in weeks.
player_purpose_hook: The site is deliberately awkward. It is a box canyon with a spring and one climb into it.
deferred_why: The coverage critique S1/S2/S3 covers the pirate-freeholds zone. The pirate-freeholds zone carried 53 records on 0.78 km2. The corrected budget for the pirate-freeholds zone is 14-17 records. The pirate-freeholds zone is the most over-budget zone in the province. The record was deferred as surplus. The type 'hermit-hut' is over its province count band of 6 max. The record is not lore-grounded. It is not quest-bearing. It is not tier 0-1. It is not an instance of an under-band vertical/underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes the record if the ground turns out to want it.

name: Sixty Tun Salt
why_founding: A laden river hull failed to hold the line above the bar. The hull went down in the deep of the confluence.
why_site_advantages: The wreck lies in the confluence hole at -6.5 m. It is out of the current, but it lies under a lot of water.
why_occupants_motive: The wreck is unoccupied. The salvage yard has stripped the hull above the silt line.
why_pressures: The hold is under silt. The yard lost two hands working it in the dry season three years ago.
why_would_change_if: If the river dropped in a hard dry season, the hold would be reachable. The yard would then work it in a week.
vibe_silhouette: All the wreckage lies below the water. A shadow lies at the confluence.
vibe_palette: The palette is tea-brown water, black timber and silver silt.
vibe_materials: The materials are hull timber, silt and trapped cargo.
vibe_signature_feature: Cargo is still lashed in the hold under a metre of silt. The water is too dark for work.
vibe_condition: silted, intact
vibe_approach: A diver finds the wreck by diving the confluence hole below the salvage line.
vibe_senses: Current noise sounds above. Silence holds at the bottom.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The consignment is still aboard. A person willing to swim for it can take it.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 61 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; needs 6.5 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: Sixty tun of salt lies on the bottom of the confluence hole. It lies under a metre of silt.
promoted_why: The wreck is the region's only underwater-entrance delve for dungeon balance. The source is research §2 sub-target.

name: Gorrey's Fort
why_founding: An intact Imperial fort stands above the trunk road. It was abandoned two hundred years ago. An unnamed outfit has moved in and charges for passage.
why_site_advantages: The Legion built on this rise. Road and boat lane run together in the reach below. Neither the road nor the lane can go around the fort.
why_occupants_motive: The occupants are a toll-taking outfit with a bought claim. The outfit has thirty hired men and no legal standing.
why_pressures: The outfit is the free port's only rival for the road trade. The port would still prefer the outfit to the state.
why_would_change_if: If the state garrisoned the fort properly, the whole economy of the zone would be enclosed in a season.
vibe_silhouette: A square Imperial curtain wall carries the wrong banners.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey ashlar, faded eagle red and new banner colours.
vibe_materials: The walls are Imperial ashlar. Freehold timber additions are bolted through the parapets.
vibe_signature_feature: An Imperial eagle still stands over the gate. The eagle was left uncut. A banner hangs under it. The banner belongs to a house that the toll-takers cannot name.

why_occupants_motive: A keeper runs the house. The keeper takes coin, barter and, reluctantly, obligation.
why_pressures: Mile Twelve is the last place before the rim where a stranger is served without questions.
why_would_change_if: If the trunk were rerouted, the house would be worthless a year later.

name: The Trunk Span

why_site_advantages: Both banks are steep-cut. The site is where the Corimont-to-Stormhold road can span the channel and need not wade it.
why_occupants_motive: One to four toll-takers work the span. They work for a freehold syndicate that bought the span outright.
why_pressures: The Owing operates at this crossing, as at every tolled crossing on the road. The ledger is kept in the open.
why_would_change_if: If the free port bought the span outright, Stormhold's road trade would pay Alten Corimont directly.

vibe_approach: The barrier is visible from a long way along a straight road.
vibe_senses: Planks sound underfoot. A bored voice quotes a rate.
why_site_won: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 8 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, nearPoint, region.
player_purpose_hook: The road has to cross the span, which is owned outright. A tariff board lists goods in one column and people in another.

name: Nine Bends
why_founding: The gangs that work the lower channel are hired out of Alten Corimont. The tree that the gang families answer to stands nine bends upriver. The water there is still fresh enough to drink. The village grew where the tree is. The work has been a day downriver for sixty years.
why_site_advantages: The village has fresh water above the salt wedge. The bank is firm enough to carry buildings. Nine bends of river lie between the village and the port.
why_occupants_motive: A tribe keeps a tree. The tribe hires its own people out downriver. No other income reaches the village.
why_pressures: Every year more of the village's adults are on a downriver roll. The tree marks their absence and shows the strain.
why_would_change_if: If the tree withdraws, the village has no reason to stay nine bends from the work. The lower channel is left without a Hist that will speak to it.
vibe_silhouette: One broad low tree stands with the village built round its foot in a ring. The river bends away on both sides.
vibe_palette: The reed and fern are wet green. The trunk bark is dark and wet. The hatchery urns are painted clay. Their lids are fired clay plates.
vibe_materials: The buildings use cut reed, mud render and bundled cane. Earth tracks run between the houses. One wooden landing stage stands on the river.
vibe_signature_feature: A hatchery pool is cut into the bank. The tree's roots run down into the pool.
vibe_condition: The village has too few hands to keep it up.
vibe_mood: The village is quiet. It has too few people for its size.
vibe_approach: The tree's chimes carry a bend downstream of the village.
vibe_senses: The air smells of sap and wet reed. The tree makes a low sound.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The gang families answer to the tree. The tree stands a day upriver from the camp where their clutch is kept.

why_founding: Argonians who went north into Morrowind in the 4E came back. They would not settle in ordinary villages. They made their own holding on the border that they had crossed.

why_occupants_motive: The holding houses veterans and their children. They are armed and keep their own council.
why_pressures: Forty armed veterans live in a zone whose other factions hire muscle by the day. Requests to the veterans are put carefully.
why_would_change_if: If the port ever hired the veterans, the freeholds would become a power and cease to be a market.

vibe_palette: The holding shows stockade timber, trophy colours and a grey sky.

name: Archon
why_founding: Archon stands at a deep, sheltered lagoon mouth on the Padomaic where foreign hulls can land. The Second Empire and then the East Empire Company built a stone quay here. The Saxhleel town grew landward of the quay.
why_site_advantages: Archon has a lagoon with a landable stone shore. A road runs into the interior. The mangrove wall breaks here for more than a kilometre. It is the widest break on the east coast.
why_occupants_motive: The harbour population is Argonian-majority. They work the water as amphibians. They run the port authority out of dead Company offices. State customs also works here. A long-settled Dunmer merchant minority from the Morrowind trade lives here too.
why_pressures: The lawful port holds the working customs desk on this coast. Cargo that is meant to avoid duty goes round it. Half-chartered hulls land on the Oliis shore. Wreckers work the Padomaic beaches south of the city. The mangrove behind the city is D4 within a kilometre of the gate. The harbour authority says that the sealed Shadowscale sanctuary is not harbour ground.
why_would_change_if: If the Archon-Lilmoth-Soulrest-Tear line stopped running, Archon would change. If the harbour authority lost its claim to the Company buildings, Archon would change. In either case Archon would become a large fishing town in a month.
vibe_silhouette: Archon is a low town behind a long stone quay. Masts and a line of mooring columns show. No walls can be read at a distance.
vibe_palette: The stone is wet grey-green. The reed thatch is bleached. The timber is tarred. The bonded doors are dull Company red.
vibe_materials: The quay below is Imperial ashlar. The buildings above are Saxhleel reed-and-stilt. The two are stacked and are not blended.
vibe_signature_feature: A stone quay older than the town stands under it. A line of mooring columns runs out into water deeper than the present boats need.
vibe_condition: The town is working and patched. It is poorer than its architecture implies.
vibe_mood: The town is orderly. Clerks watch over it and guards are few.
vibe_approach: From the sea, masts show first. From the river road, the customs barrier comes before any roof.
vibe_senses: Gulls cry. Tally-calls sound in three languages. The air smells of tar and drying fish. Hulls knock hollowly on stone.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Cargo, passengers and writs all pass the customs desk. Archon is where a quest can start from a document and not from a person.

name: The Company Row

why_site_advantages: The Company Row stands on the stone quay. The Company laid footings there that carry a loaded cart.
why_occupants_motive: The harbour authority uses one corner. It has no lawful way into the rest.

vibe_approach: The row has the biggest gable on the quay front.
vibe_senses: The stone is cold. Old spice lingers. Rats move through the stores.

name: The Sunken Byre
why_founding: This coast breeds a strain of guar that breathes underwater. A port moves cargo across a shallow estuary. The drovers of the port pen the guar below the surface.
why_site_advantages: The byre stands on a sheltered shelf inside the estuary. The shelf lies three to six metres down. The bottom is firm enough to hold tethers.
why_occupants_motive: Two drover families work entirely submerged. By village standards the two families are rich.
why_pressures: Foreign buyers want the breeding stock but cannot legally take it. The stock is guarded underwater.
why_would_change_if: If the estuary silted or turned saline, the herd would move. If the herd moved, the byre type would disappear from the coast.
vibe_silhouette: Seen from above, the byre is a ring of posts. The ring shows no visible purpose.
vibe_palette: The light underwater is green-gold. Silt hangs in the water as haze. The post timber is pale.
vibe_materials: The byre is built of driven posts. The fencing is woven kelp. The feed store floats.
vibe_signature_feature: The byre is a working farmyard below the waterline. The feed store, the tack and the dung heap are submerged with it.
vibe_condition: well kept, invisible
vibe_approach: The byre is reached by swimming. No part of it shows from the surface.
vibe_senses: Sound is muffled underwater. The low calls of the herd carry oddly through the water.
quest_hooks_opportunity: The byre is a farmyard below the waterline. A drover will take an outsider down for a day's wage.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, hinterland, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.sealed-xanmeer-wall (+1.24).
player_purpose_hook: The byre is a working farmyard three metres under the estuary. The drovers herd the guar and do the whole job below the surface.

name: Reaches-The-Low-Branch
why_founding: A small Hist stands landward of the harbour. The salt does not reach it. Archon keeps it as the tree of the city.

why_occupants_motive: Tree-minders keep the Hist. Dockworkers touch it on the way out to the boats and again on their return. The Dunmer quarter does not touch it.
why_pressures: Salt intrusion is rising with the quay works. The tree is smaller than it was a century ago.
why_would_change_if: If the estuary silts or the harbour cuts a deeper channel, this Hist dies. Archon would then be a city with no tree of its own.
vibe_silhouette: One crown breaks a low roofline. The crown is taller than the roofs landward of the masts.
vibe_palette: The bark is pale. The leaves are dark and wet. Amber shows where sap runs.
vibe_materials: The tree is a living Hist. A ring of laid stone surrounds it. The city insists that the ring is not stone.
vibe_signature_feature: The Hist is small enough that an adult can reach its lowest branch.
vibe_condition: The minders tend the Hist anxiously. A prop holds up one side of the tree.
vibe_approach: The Hist is seen from the landward gate before any building.
vibe_senses: The air is sap-sweet. A chime hangs there that was hung by a grandmother. No birds sing in the air.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 82 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, bound.
player_purpose_hook: The Hist of the city stands ten minutes from the quay. Its minders keep their own account of the history of the city.

name: Estuary Light
why_founding: The approach to the lawful deep-water port of the province is strewn with reef. The approach must be lit. Without a light the port is worthless in the wet season.
why_site_advantages: The light stands on the outermost hard ground on the approach. The ground is built up clear of the mangrove. The tower stands square on the reef gap.
why_occupants_motive: A keeper family lives here, in its fourth generation. The harbour authority pays the keepers in fuel.
why_pressures: Fuel supply is the local dispute. A dark night on this reef is worth money to the wreckers south of the estuary.
why_would_change_if: If the fuel account lapsed, the tower would go dark. Wrecking on the reef would then increase.
vibe_silhouette: The tower is a stone drum on raised hard ground above the mangrove. It stands alone over the reef gap.
vibe_palette: The rock is wet and black. The tower is lime-white. One warm light burns.
vibe_materials: The tower is built of Imperial ashlar. The lamp is salvaged.
vibe_signature_feature: The keepers keep a wreck register. The register lists every hull lost on the reef and where it lies.
vibe_condition: sound, endlessly repointed

why_occupants_motive: A lookout keeps the tower. Three villages pay the lookout in food.
why_pressures: The tower is the only place for kilometres where a traveller can see where they are going.
why_would_change_if: If the tower fell, the three villages would lose their weather warning. They would also lose their smoke watch.
vibe_silhouette: A lashed tower breaks the canopy. The tower is climbed. It is not seen from afar.
vibe_palette: The palette is green below, grey sky above and pale ladder timber.
vibe_materials: The materials are lashed poles, ladder rungs and a plank crow's nest.
vibe_signature_feature: The tower is the highest reachable point for kilometres. It is made of rope and poles.
vibe_condition: sound but visibly temporary
vibe_approach: A traveller climbs the tower because it is there.
vibe_senses: Wind blows at the top. The canopy noise falls away.
player_purpose_hook: The tower stands on the tallest stable tree cluster on the walkway line.
deferred_why: This region ran over its coverage-doc record budget after its executor pass. The budget is in docs/research/phase11/phase11-critique/coverage-density.md S2. The verify/wrap round rebalance deferred this record. It is the lowest-value fine-tempo fill in an over-dense zone. It was chosen so that no type falls under-band. The record is intact. Part 3's homeless-batch review may restore it.

name: The Lit Water
why_founding: A lagoon arm blooms on certain tides. Bioluminescent organisms light the water from below. The villagers steer their boats by the light.
why_site_advantages: The water is still, warm and brackish. Exchange with the sea is restricted.
why_occupants_motive: Boat crews come out to see the bloom. Boat crews do not live on the water.
why_pressures: The bloom is a calendared event. It is not a permanent feature. For half the year the water is ordinary.
why_would_change_if: If the arm were opened to the sea, the bloom would stop. A navigation cue would be lost.
vibe_silhouette: In season the water itself is the landmark. The water is lit from below.
vibe_palette: cold blue-green on black
vibe_materials: The material is water. Anything that moves through the water disturbs it.
vibe_signature_feature: A boat's own wake glows behind it. Another wake also glows. That wake does not come from the boat.
vibe_condition: seasonal
vibe_mood: The mood is that of the province's single uncomplicated wonder.
vibe_approach: When a boat takes a night crossing, the glow starts.
vibe_senses: The scene is completely silent. The light is the only sign of it.
player_purpose_hook: The water is still, warm and brackish. Exchange with the sea is restricted.
deferred_why: Coverage critique S1/S2/S3 found that saxhleel-coast carried 99 records on 1.81 km2. The corrected budget for saxhleel-coast is 18-24 records. Saxhleel-coast is the most over-budget zone in the province. The record was deferred as surplus. The type 'bioluminescent-water' is over its province count band (5 max). The record is not lore-grounded, is not quest-bearing, is not tier 0-1 and is not an under-band vertical or underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes it if the ground allows it.

name: Eleven-Berth
why_founding: The shelter is a second shelter on the lagoon crossing. The crossing takes two hours. The squalls are shorter than two hours.
why_site_advantages: A low islet lies in the mangrove crossing. It has the only firm standing between the two shores.
why_occupants_motive: The shelter has no resident household. Boat crews shelter there from the weather.
why_pressures: The shelter floods in the worst storms. Every crew on the crossing makes the same joke about it.
why_would_change_if: If the shelter were raised a metre, it would be the safest place on the lagoon.
vibe_silhouette: A hut stands on an islet with nothing else on it.
vibe_palette: The palette is grey water, grey plank and one lamp.
vibe_materials: The materials are stone footings, plank walls and a mooring ring.
vibe_signature_feature: A high-water mark is chalked on the inside wall. The mark reaches above head height.
vibe_condition: damp always
vibe_approach: The hut is the only thing above water for a kilometre.
vibe_senses: Rain falls on planks. Hulls knock outside.
player_purpose_hook: The shelter has eleven berths. A bar closes across the door. It is the only dry floor on the lagoon crossing.

name: The Standing Corner
why_founding: The terraces were built dry. The water came up about two hundred years ago. Water now covers the top terrace to a depth of six metres.
why_site_advantages: The drowned lagoon is deep enough to cover six terraces. The water is clear enough to read the geometry from a boat above it.
why_occupants_motive: No household occupies the xanmeer. Divers who go down have brought back no account of what lives in it.
why_pressures: The xanmeer is a tended monument. The village cannot reach it to tend it.
why_would_change_if: If the water dropped a metre, the tribe would reclaim the xanmeer.
vibe_silhouette: One terrace corner breaks flat water. A geometric shadow lies under it.
vibe_palette: The palette is sun-bleached stone above, jade green below and black at the stair mouths.
vibe_materials: The materials are xanmeer stone, silt and trapped air.
vibe_signature_feature: Air is trapped at the chamber ceilings. The air is breathable at a depth of six metres.
vibe_condition: structurally intact, silted
vibe_mood: The water is still. Breath limits the dives.
vibe_approach: The corner reads as a rock. Then the shadow under it resolves into steps.
vibe_senses: Above the water, gulls cry and hulls slap. Below, a diver hears breath and settling silt.
why_site_won: open water in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 423 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on culture-clump, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; needs 6 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: The xanmeer has six terraces under still water. The entry is head-down through the top of a tower.

name: One-Chest
why_founding: A diver furnished a trapped air space inside a flooded structure. The diver keeps a lamp burning in it.
why_site_advantages: Water encloses the pocket on all sides. The way in is a dive of about 20 metres.
why_occupants_motive: One or two divers dive in to the pocket. What is inside may be no more than their belongings.
why_pressures: The hoard was chosen for being too heavy for a diver to carry out.
why_would_change_if: If the water level fell, the room would become an ordinary cellar.
vibe_silhouette: Nothing shows from outside. The pocket is found by diving.
vibe_palette: The palette is lamp yellow on wet stone.
vibe_materials: Dry goods are kept dry. A lamp burns.
vibe_signature_feature: The hoard was chosen for being too heavy for a diver to carry out.
vibe_condition: maintained by someone
vibe_approach: A diver finds the pocket by following bubbles or a rumour.
vibe_senses: dripping; a lamp guttering
why_site_won: cove in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 566 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The pocket is a dry room with a chest in it. It lies 20 metres down. The only way in is a held breath.
siting_note: The place is kept off the routes by a constraint. The published off-route gap list has no point inside the Saxhleel coast zone.
reconciliation_note: Retyped 2026-09-02 (Phase 11 repair, coverage critique S3): air-pocket-station was over band (4/3-3) and air-pocket-grotto under (2/4-4); this record's own content - a submerged entrance, a hoard too heavy for a swimmer to carry out, no surface expression - is the grotto recipe, not the staffed way-station one.

name: Three-Notch-One-Slash
why_founding: The village chose not to be found. It is cut into the mangrove wall. Only a traveller who knows which channel to take can reach it.
why_site_advantages: The mangrove is an unbroken green wall. The wall has one navigable cut, tidal and unmarked.
why_occupants_motive: The villagers are few and wary. They supply all their own needs.
why_pressures: The harbour authority does not know how many people live here. The villagers intend to keep it that way.
why_would_change_if: If an outsider read the channel markers, the entire defence of the village would be gone.
vibe_silhouette: Nothing shows of the village. The cue is a gap in an otherwise unbroken green wall.
vibe_palette: The palette is black water and every green there is. No built colour shows at all.
vibe_materials: The materials are cut-root landings, low platforms and woven screens.
vibe_signature_feature: Channel markers are cut into living roots. Only people of this village can read the markers.
vibe_condition: low, hidden, perfectly maintained
vibe_approach: The villagers lead a stranger into the wrong channel first, on purpose.
vibe_senses: Insects hum and water drips. Voices stop when a stranger arrives.
player_purpose_hook: The mangrove is an unbroken green wall. The wall has one navigable cut, tidal and unmarked.

name: Black-Cut Teeth
why_founding: Black-Cut Teeth lies where the mangrove wall meets open water. A shell bar has built up there. Villagers have farmed the shell bar for generations.
why_site_advantages: The reef is shallow and sheltered by the mangrove. The reef can be walked at the lowest tides. Children with baskets pick over the reef every day.
why_occupants_motive: Two villages work alternate lots on the reef. They hold to an agreement that neither village has written down.
why_pressures: A bad season would put the two villages in dispute over the lots.
why_would_change_if: If either village lost its boats, the other village would take the whole bar in under a month.
vibe_silhouette: Stakes and lot markers stand out of shallow water.
vibe_palette: The palette is olive water, black mangrove and pale shell.
vibe_materials: shell, stakes, woven baskets
vibe_signature_feature: The harvest lots are marked in the cutting patterns of the two villages. The two patterns alternate stripe by stripe.
vibe_condition: worked hard
vibe_approach: Visitors wade to the reef at low tide.
vibe_senses: Shell clatters underfoot. Mud sucks at the feet. Mangrove crabs move about the reef.
player_purpose_hook: The reef yields shellfish, crab and reef weed. Children gather them at low tide, because the children are too small to dive the lots.

name: Low-Water-Only
why_founding: Low-Water-Only is a second mangrove village on the seaward edge of the wall. It trades openly out of necessity.
why_site_advantages: The outer edge of the wall lets a boat lie alongside at any tide.
why_occupants_motive: The households sell shell and charcoal to Archon. They pretend not to know the hidden village.
why_pressures: Being visible costs the village. Every outsider comes to this village first.
why_would_change_if: If the hidden village were found, the hidden village's neighbours would blame this village. The whole social order of the wall would then break.
vibe_silhouette: Low platforms hang off the outer roots. A trade landing stands among them.
vibe_palette: The palette is olive and black with one bright trade awning.
vibe_materials: The village is built of root landings and woven platforms. A bought canvas awning covers the trade landing.
vibe_signature_feature: The only bought, imported object in the village is the awning. The awning covers the trade landing.
vibe_condition: worn, propped
vibe_approach: The awning is visible from the lane.
vibe_senses: Roots creak. The tide runs. Conversation is careful.
player_purpose_hook: The outer edge of the wall lets a boat lie alongside at any tide.

The place is deferred as surplus. The type 'mangrove-platform-village' is over its province count band (3 max). name: Salt-And-Nails
why_founding: A squall drove a hull into the mangrove wall. The roots caught the hull and hold it where it lies.
why_site_advantages: The roots hold the hull two metres above the mud at low water. The swamp built this structure.
why_occupants_motive: The wreck holds a hidden cache. The wreck has no lawful holder.
why_pressures: The wreck lies a kilometre inside the mangrove. Boat crews cannot drag it out.
why_would_change_if: If the channel shifted, the wreck would be underwater. It would then be a different POI entirely.
vibe_silhouette: A broken hull line sits at a wrong angle inside a green wall.
vibe_palette: The palette is black hull, olive root and brown water.
vibe_materials: Hull timber is laced through with living roots.
vibe_signature_feature: The mangrove has grown through the hull. The mangrove now holds the hull up.
vibe_condition: The roots break down the hull and support it at the same time.
vibe_approach: Visitors push through roots. The hull is suddenly there.
vibe_senses: The hull creaks.
player_purpose_hook: The roots hold the hull two metres above the mud at low water. The swamp built this structure.

name: Lands-It-After-Dark
why_founding: The customs desk at Archon is the working one on this coast. The Oliis run therefore has a last stop short of Archon. The stop is a channel mouth where a hull can lie a night. Crews break the cargo down there and send it in by canoe in daylight. The cargo is declared as something else.
why_site_advantages: The mangrove channel is deep enough for a keeled hull. The channel is screened from the lane. The lay-by lies a night's paddle from the Archon quay at most.
why_occupants_motive: The crews come half-chartered out of the Oliis coast. Their letters of marque cover the hull but not the hold. Factors in the city prefer their goods undated.
why_pressures: The harbour authority sweeps the channels twice a season. The harbour authority has yet to sweep this channel. The League of Open Water tolerates the trade. The League of Open Water taxes the trade privately.
why_would_change_if: If the customs at Archon stopped functioning, the lay-by would be pointless. The trade would then go straight to the quay.
vibe_silhouette: The lay-by cannot be seen from the lane. A hull's masthead shows above the mangrove to those who know to look.
vibe_palette: The palette is black water and green shade, lit by hooded lamps.
vibe_materials: A plank stack stands on piles. A walkway runs through the lay-by. No building stands that is worth burning.
vibe_signature_feature: A cargo stack stands under a mangrove roof. The cargo is already broken down into canoe loads. A plank hatch beneath the stack opens into a half-flooded cut.
vibe_condition: The lay-by is kept in order. The crews can be gone in an hour.
vibe_approach: Watchers on the water see visitors well before the place itself shows.
vibe_senses: The air smells of tar, bilge and wet rope. No cooking fire burns.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, bound, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: The lay-by is the last stop before the customs at Archon. Crews break the cargo down there and redeclare it. The broker hires carriers by the canoe load.
siting_note: The audit noted that the record names the Lilmoth-Archon lane but sits 281 m off it. The record works as written. Its hard constraint is that no sightline may run from that lane. The record is bound to Archon, because the customs desk makes the lay-by the last stop.

name: Lost-The-Ospreye
why_founding: The shipping lane keeps clear of the outer bar. The reef on the outer bar is still alive.
why_site_advantages: The water is clear over a healthy reef in the outer mangrove channels. The reef lies far enough out that the lot divers come once a season.
why_occupants_motive: No crew holds the reef. Divers come out for a day and go home.
why_pressures: The reef is the healthiest on the coast. No crew holds a claim on it.
why_would_change_if: If the harvest lots moved out here, the reef would look like the Gap in 15 years.
vibe_silhouette: Only a colour change in the water marks the reef above the surface.
vibe_palette: The palette is turquoise over rust and violet.
vibe_materials: The reef is living coral and sand. No built thing stands there.
vibe_signature_feature: The water is clear enough to see 30 metres.
vibe_condition: untouched
vibe_approach: Sailors find the reef by sailing off the lane.
vibe_senses: Above the water, wind blows. Below the water, a constant crackle sounds.
why_site_won: island in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 78 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; needs 1 m of water.
player_purpose_hook: Pearl beds lie under a living reef. A flooded cut in the reef wall can be reached only by Argonian lungs.

name: Sells-Their-Hours
why_founding: Households whose owing was called in are put off their ground. The evicted households camp at the edge of their former ground because the work is here. They have nowhere else to wait.
why_site_advantages: The camp stands on the margin of a licensed sap concession. It sits on jungle ground that the concession does not use.
why_occupants_motive: Families wait in the camp for a hiring day. A broker's clerk comes to the camp twice a week.
why_pressures: The families' former ground is a hundred metres away. Other hands work that ground. The jungle behind the camp is dangerous (D3).
why_would_change_if: A Chainbreaker cell could reach the camp. If a Chainbreaker cell reached the camp, the hiring queue would become an organised body.
vibe_silhouette: The shelters form a line along a boundary. Each shelter faces inward at the fields.
vibe_palette: The camp's colours are grey canvas and mud. Each family keeps one good cooking pot.
vibe_materials: The shelters are made of salvaged canvas and hurdles. Household goods are stacked outside the shelters.
vibe_signature_feature: Every shelter faces the ground that its household once worked. Every shelter has its door turned away from the camp.
vibe_condition: The camp has been settled far longer than a camp should be.
vibe_approach: The shelters can be seen from the boardwalk through the trees. The camp's people watch the boardwalk.
vibe_senses: children; adults not talking
quest_hooks_opportunity: The broker's hiring list is a document, so a quest can be won by altering who is on the list. The quest does not need a fight with the broker's clerk.
quest_hooks_tier_ownership: SX08 · tier-3; SX09 · tier-3; SX27 · tier-3; tier-3
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 323 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: Families camp in sight of the ground that their owing cost them. They wait on a broker who comes twice a week.
siting_note: The place is held at D3. The danger raster reads band 4 here. The camp sits on cleared concession margin. The band-4 reading belongs to the jungle around the camp, not the queue.

name: Shows-The-Wrong-Light
why_founding: Archon is the lawful landing on this coast. A hull that misses the estuary in weather looks for whatever light it can see. A shore gang keeps a fire burning above this beach.
why_site_advantages: The beach shelves south of the estuary. A bar lies offshore. No settlement is within sight of the fire.
why_occupants_motive: The occupants are landless coast households. They lost their fishing ground. They now work the cargo that comes ashore.
why_pressures: The harbour authority knows the beach exists but cannot prove which fire is which. The pilots of Portdun Mont lose a hull a season to the beach. The pilots want the fire burnt out.
why_would_change_if: If the estuary marks were kept properly lit, the gang would have no light to imitate. The gang would go back to fishing or go to Alten Corimont.
vibe_silhouette: A single fire burns above the beach. Dark shapes stand between the fire and the water.
vibe_palette: The colours are fire orange on wet black sand and salt-bleached timber.
vibe_materials: Wreck timber is reused for the shelters and the fire pole.
vibe_signature_feature: A fire basket stands on a pole. The basket is set where a pilot will take it for the estuary light.
vibe_condition: The camp is temporary by design. The shelters can be off the beach in an hour.
vibe_approach: The fire is visible from the water long before the camp is.
vibe_senses: The beach smells of smoke, tar, wet cordage and meat.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 242 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, bound, nearPoint; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.
player_purpose_hook: A shore gang keeps a false light above a shelving beach. The cargo stacked behind the light came off the last hull wrecked on the bar.

name: The Counted Lots
why_founding: Amphibious people with a port to sell into work a pearl bed. The beds were divided into numbered lots as soon as the trade began to pay.
why_site_advantages: The bed lies in clear water over a firm bed inside an offshore bar. The beds lie 6 to 8 m down, which is deeper than an outsider can casually work.
why_occupants_motive: Diver families hold numbered lots by inheritance. The families share the tenders moored over the lots.
why_pressures: The deep lots pay best. The deep lots kill divers. Both the pay and the deaths are entered in the tally book.
why_would_change_if: If foreigners learned to dive here, the lot system would collapse. The diver families teach their own.
vibe_silhouette: Marker buoys and a tender boat float over water with no bed in sight.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey-brown keg buoys, green water and silver shell.
vibe_materials: The works use keg buoys, grading baskets and stone lot cairns.
vibe_signature_feature: A diver keeps a tally of the lots worked. The deep lots are entered in a second hand.
vibe_condition: worked daily
vibe_mood: The divers are businesslike about a dangerous trade.
vibe_approach: The lots are found by spotting the tender boat.
vibe_senses: Rope creaks above the water. Shell clicks into a basket below.
quest_hooks_opportunity: A lot with no living heir has to be reassigned. The claimants settle the reassignment in the water.
why_site_won: Reseated (pending: builder recommendation np-pearl-lots-a 2026-10-04, owner confirms in the walk-12 packet): The record asks for clear water over a firm bed inside an offshore bar, 6 to 12 metres down, worked from a shore settlement that sells the catch. The first dot stood beside an inland swamp pool 1.2 m deep on a flat silt bed, 1.3 km from Portdun-Mont. The new dot stands over the ocean shelf east of Archon: 6 to 8 m of water over a flat bed 60 to 150 m off a low sand spit, with a bar 3 to 6 m deep beyond it, 600 m from Archon.
plot_facts_landform: reseated (pending: builder recommendation np-pearl-lots-a 2026-10-04, owner confirms in the walk-12 packet)
player_purpose_hook: Numbered pearl lots are held by inheritance. The tally book records the drownings as well as the takings.
watch_reason: A diving family's lots: no office, no watch.

name: Portdun Mont
why_founding: The village grew on the rise behind the pilots' watch. The village stands above the beach landing and below the ridge line.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on firm ground above the flood. It has a clear view down the whole estuary approach. A beach landing lies at the foot of the stair.
why_occupants_motive: Pilot families are paid to bring hulls through the approach. The pilot families remember when the fee was collected differently.
why_pressures: Archon's authority stops at the headland. The pilots' monopoly is customary and has no legal basis.
why_would_change_if: If the harbour authority licensed its own pilots, Portdun Mont would be a fishing hamlet in a year.
vibe_silhouette: Houses are stacked on a shelf against a rock face. The houses are lit from the seaward side only.
vibe_palette: The colours are wet black rock and salt-bleached timber. One red pilot flag flies in the village.
vibe_materials: The houses are timber on stone footings. Hauling gear stands at the stair head. A 200-step stair leads up from the landing.
vibe_signature_feature: The hauling gear stands at the stair head. Its beam is worn through where two centuries of loads came up.
vibe_condition: weathered hard, endlessly repaired
vibe_approach: The village is seen from the sea long before the land route finds it.
vibe_senses: The village smells and sounds of surf below, wind and creaking hauling rope.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Cargo and passengers reach the shelf by ladder and rope. A quest can turn on who controls the hauling gear.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 39 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent.
player_purpose_hook: Every hull bound for Archon takes a pilot at Portdun Mont first. The village hears the coast's news before the city does.

name: The Marque Cove
why_founding: The cove lies under the pilot headland. Privateers with two-century-old letters of marque still careen there. The letters have never been formally cancelled.
why_site_advantages: The cove has deep approach water hidden from the shipping lane by the headland. The cove has a beach that dries at low tide.
why_occupants_motive: The crews are lawful when it suits them. The crews never touch a hull that the harbour authority would have to notice.
why_pressures: Archon knows about the privateers and finds them convenient. One incident would end the arrangement.
why_would_change_if: If the Reed formally revoked the marques, the cove would become an outlaw anchorage. The whole coast's insurance would change.

vibe_palette: The colours are hull tar and wet sand. Four different flag colours are in use.
vibe_materials: The cove has beached timber, careening tackle and tented prize goods.
vibe_signature_feature: A case holds letters of marque dated 1E 2833. The same locker holds four flags for four occasions.
vibe_condition: The cove is in constant use. The cove is never built up.
vibe_approach: The tar fires can be smelled before the point is rounded.
vibe_senses: The cove smells of fire and tar. The crews sing. A hull is being scraped.
player_purpose_hook: The cove has deep approach water hidden from the shipping lane by the headland. The cove has a beach that dries at low tide.

name: Keeps-Its-Own-Cordon
why_founding: A village was put under cordon during a later outbreak. No release order was ever written. The cordon stands.
why_site_advantages: The village stands on an island in the lagoon. The island has one landing. The island was the obvious place to put people.
why_occupants_motive: The occupants are descendants of the quarantined. They have been free to leave for a century.
why_pressures: The villagers are healthy. No guard confines them. They still keep to the cordon line.
why_would_change_if: A release order, real or forged, would end the arrangement.
vibe_silhouette: A normal village stands behind an unguarded line of painted stakes.
vibe_palette: The village has ordinary village colours. One line of white-painted stakes marks the cordon.
vibe_materials: The village is built of mud render and thatch. Painted cordon stakes mark the line.
vibe_signature_feature: The people inside the cordon repaint the cordon line every year.
vibe_condition: well kept, entirely functional
vibe_mood: The villagers are ordinary. The villagers are careful about the line.
vibe_approach: Visitors cross the line unstopped. The villagers watch them cross.

name: Four-Hour Channel
why_founding: This is a mangrove channel. It floods deep enough for a laden boat only at the top of the tide.
why_site_advantages: A shallow sill lies in an otherwise navigable cut.
why_occupants_motive: Boat crews wait here. They argue about draught.
why_pressures: Missing the window costs six hours. The long way round is D4.
why_would_change_if: If the sill were dug out, the hidden villages behind it would lose their moat.
vibe_silhouette: A tide board stands on a post at the mouth of a cut.
vibe_palette: The water is brown. The mangrove wall is green. The board is chalked.
vibe_materials: The site has a chalk board, mooring rings and waiting boats.
vibe_signature_feature: The chalked tide board is updated before dawn every day. The person who updates it has never been seen.
vibe_condition: used constantly
vibe_approach: The boats waiting are found before the sill.
vibe_senses: hulls knocking, low conversation
player_purpose_hook: A shallow sill lies in an otherwise navigable cut.
deferred_why: Coverage critique S1/S2/S3 applies. saxhleel-coast carried 99 records on 1.81 km2 against a corrected budget of 18-24. It is the most over-budget zone in the province. The place is deferred as surplus. The type 'tide-timed-run' is over its province count band (5 max). The record is neither canon, quest-bearing, tier 0-1, nor an instance of an under-band vertical/underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes it if the ground proves suited to it.

name: The Two-Hour Flat
why_founding: A delta flat shortens the coast journey. It is crossable only while the basin's tidal amplitude leaves it dry. In practice that is a short morning.
why_site_advantages: The sand is firm under shallow water at low tide. A stake line laid generations ago marks the route.
why_occupants_motive: The delta carries no houses. Six people are usually waiting at the head.
why_pressures: The window is a different length every day. A tide board is chalked at the head before dawn.
why_would_change_if: If a causeway were ever built here, travel times across the whole district would change. The shelter would die.
vibe_silhouette: A line of stakes runs out into water.
vibe_palette: The sand is wet and silver. The water is grey. The stakes are black.
vibe_materials: The site has stakes, a tide board and a fire under a lean-to.
vibe_signature_feature: A tally of drownings is cut into the shelter post.
vibe_condition: The crossers renew the stake line every year.
vibe_approach: Travellers arrive at the head, then wait for the tide.
vibe_senses: Wind blows over the flats. The turning of the tide is audible.
why_site_won: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 283 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on culture-clump, landform, region.
player_purpose_hook: The sand is firm for two hours, twice a day. Outside that window the crossing is a running channel.

name: Keeps-The-Book Lots
why_founding: The province is full of drowned settlements. The trade of bringing things up, drying them out and selling them on rests on those settlements.
why_site_advantages: The yard stands on the bank directly above the drowned streets. Its drying frames face the prevailing wind.
why_occupants_motive: Five divers work the yard. They have mapped the drowned village better than anyone mapped it alive.
why_pressures: The divers hold a reserve of pieces that they will not sell. They know what the pieces are.
why_would_change_if: If Archon's antiquarians paid properly, the reserve would be gone in a week.
vibe_silhouette: Racks of drying frames hold things that have plainly been underwater a long time.
vibe_palette: Salt-white bloom covers everything. Rust and weathered timber are visible beneath it.
vibe_materials: The yard has frames, desalting tubs and weighted belts.
vibe_signature_feature: A lot book maps a drowned village street by street. Three generations have added to it in one hand.
vibe_condition: working, cluttered
vibe_approach: The frames read from the water before the sheds do.
vibe_senses: Water drips, brine stings and a desalting tub tocks.
player_purpose_hook: The yard stands on the bank directly above the drowned streets. Its drying frames face the prevailing wind.
deferred_why: Coverage critique S1/S2/S3 applies. saxhleel-coast carried 99 records on 1.81 km2 against a corrected budget of 18-24. It is the most over-budget zone in the province. The place is deferred as surplus. The type 'salvage-divers-yard' is over its province count band (5 max). The record is neither canon, quest-bearing, tier 0-1, nor an instance of an under-band vertical/underwater type. The record is intact and complete. Part 3 promotes it if the ground proves suited to it.

name: The Tide Streets
why_founding: The Tide Streets was a stilt village on subsiding delta ground. The water took the village street by street over sixty years. The last households moved to the rise behind the village.
why_site_advantages: The water over the street plan is shallow and clear. The street plan is intact. A boat crew can read the street plan at low tide.
why_occupants_motive: Salvagers work the shallow end of the drowned streets. The deeper streets lie beyond the reach of the salvagers.
why_pressures: Salvagers have picked the village over for a century. They have not yet worked the deep streets.
why_would_change_if: If the delta shifted again, silt would cover the whole street plan. The salvage trade here would then end.
vibe_silhouette: Roof ridges and pile stumps break the water surface. The set that is visible changes with the tide.
vibe_palette: The water is silt brown at the surface and green below. The doorways are black.
vibe_materials: The buildings are drowned stilt timber. The thatch is gone, but pile stumps remain.
vibe_signature_feature: A boat crew can see the whole street plan from the water. The successor village stands on the rise above the street plan.
vibe_condition: The village is drowned and picked over. The structures are soft.
vibe_mood: The mood is workaday. The salvagers do not linger.
vibe_approach: The successor village comes into view first. It stands on the rise above the drowned plan.
vibe_senses: Hulls knock against submerged posts.
quest_hooks_opportunity: Salvage law here gives the find to whichever crew reaches it first. A quest can set one boat crew against a rival crew on the same drowned street.
why_site_won: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 194 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on submerged, hinterland, culture-clump.
player_purpose_hook: A whole street plan lies under clear shallow water. The deep end of the plan has never been worked. A salvager who can read the layout sees where the deeper goods are trapped.

name: Four-Eight
why_founding: Umbriel crossed this coast in 4E 48. The villagers buried the bodies it left here. The graves lie away from any tree, because the burial site was chosen so that the Hist could not be blamed.
why_site_advantages: The site is a tidal flat above the village line. The ground could be opened quickly and in quantity.
why_occupants_motive: Bone-carriers still call here on the way south. The villagers keep clear of the mound.
why_pressures: The dead here were stripped of their belongings. No name-goods remain to carry home.
why_would_change_if: If a way were found to return even one of the dead, the Umbriel Witness Society would gain its first real relic.
vibe_silhouette: The mound is long and low, with markers along its spine. It is out of scale with the village near it.
vibe_palette: The colours are grey silt, bleached stakes and dark reed.
vibe_materials: earth, stakes, shell offerings
vibe_signature_feature: The mound is longer than the village that made it. No name is carved anywhere on it.
vibe_condition: The mound is settling. It is visibly sinking in places.
vibe_approach: The road bends around the mound without touching it.
vibe_senses: Reeds hiss. Wind sounds in the stakes.
why_site_won: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 347 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on culture-clump, route, region.
player_purpose_hook: A grave mound stands over the Umbriel dead of 4E 48. The mound has no name on it, but a cut in the ground can still be opened.

name: Reed-Stand Paid-Bed
why_founding: The largest village on the southern coast road has one house that takes money for a bed.
why_site_advantages: The house stands in the village, on the landing side.
why_occupants_motive: A household converted a boat-shed into the house. The household has never quite finished the conversion.
why_pressures: Half the village thinks charging for a bed is shameful.
why_would_change_if: If the village agreed with the objectors, the house would close. Travellers would then sleep on the deck.
vibe_silhouette: The building is a boat-shed with beds in it. A lamp hangs outside.
vibe_palette: The shed is grey. One window glows warm.
vibe_materials: shed timber, borrowed furniture
vibe_signature_feature: The roof still has the boat-shed doors. The doors still open.
vibe_condition: half-converted, permanently
vibe_approach: Villagers direct travellers to the house. Travellers do not find it unaided.
vibe_senses: Village noise comes through thin walls.
player_purpose_hook: A household converted a boat-shed into a house. The house stands in the village, on the landing side, where the household charges for a bed.
